The Eighth Adhyāya of the First Aṣṭaka

Sūkta 113 — "idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣām"

original p. 2

Anuvāda (Kannada): "Thus far the explanation of the meaning of the seventh Adhyāya has been given; now we begin the eighth Adhyāya. In the sixteenth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala seven sūktas have been completed. The sūkta which we now begin, idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ, is the eighth sūkta; it has twenty Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said 'idaṃ viṃśatir uṣasyaṃ dvitīyo 'rdharco rātreḥ'. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa, son of Aṅgiras; the metre Triṣṭubh; the deity Uṣas; the latter half of the first Ṛk is also addressed to Night. The sūkta has an application in the Prātaranuvāka mantras, for the recitation (pathana) at the time of the Uṣas-rite of Triṣṭubh Ṛks related to Uṣas — as shown by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra in the sūtra 'idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ pṛthū rathe iti sūkte' (Āśv. 4-14, as printed [?]). In the Prātaranuvāka mantras this sūkta is also applied to the Aśvina-śastra mantras."

सूक्त—११३ (Sūkta 113) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१६ ॥ सूक्त—११३ ॥ — Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 16; Sūkta 113. ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—१, २, ३, ४ ॥ — Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 8; Varga 1, 2, 3, 4. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 20. Ṛṣi: Kutsa Āṅgirasa. Devatā (as printed, small numerals, partly unclear [?]): the Ṛks 3–20 Uṣas; Ṛk 1 and the second half of the Ṛks given as "Uṣas and Rātri". Chandas: Triṣṭubh printed "paṅkti"?: the box reads chandaḥ—… [?]; the bhāṣya says Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.1)

इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा । यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवायँ एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥ १ ॥

idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā | yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya~ evā rātryuṣase yonimāraik ‖ 1 ‖

original p. 3

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.1) Reading note after viewing the Pada: the Saṃhitā's ārāik appears in the Pada as अरैक् (the second letter was doubtful here; it is clear in the Pada of Ṛk 2, p. 9, and of Ṛk 16, p. 75, so the doubt is removed); the Saṃhitā's savāya evā is the Pada's savāya | eva.

इदम् । श्रेष्ठम् । ज्योतिषाम् । ज्योतिः । आ । अगात् । चित्रः । प्रऽकेतः । अजनिष्ट । विऽभ्वा । यथा । प्रऽसूता । सवितुः । सवाय । एव । रात्री । उषसे । योनिम् । अरैक् ॥ १ ॥

idam | śreṣṭham | jyotiṣām | jyotiḥ | ā | agāt | citraḥ | pra 'ketaḥ | ajaniṣṭa | vi 'bhvā | yathā | pra 'sūtā | savituḥ | savāya | eva | rātrī | uṣase | yonim | araik ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.1)

ज्योतिषां ग्रहनक्षत्रादीनां द्योतमानानां मध्ये इदमुषोऽभिमानिनी ज्योतिः श्रेष्ठम् । प्रशस्यतमम् । अस्य कोऽतिशय इति चेत् उच्यते । नक्षत्रादिकं ज्योतिः स्वात्मानमेव प्रकाशयति नान्यत् । चन्द्रस्तु यद्यप्यन्यत्प्रकाशयति तथापि न विस्पष्टप्रकाशः । उषसं तु ज्योतिर्युगपदेव सर्वस्य जगतोऽन्धकारनिराकरणेन विशेषेण प्रकाशकम् । अतः प्रशस्ततममित्यर्थः । तादृशं ज्योतिरागात् । पूर्वस्यां दिश्यागमत् । आगते च तस्मिन् चित्रः चायनीयः प्रकेतः अन्धकारावृतस्य सर्वस्य पदार्थस्य प्रज्ञापकस्तदीयो रश्मिर्विभ्वा विभुर्व्याप्तः सन् अजनिष्ट । प्रादुरभूत् । किंच । यथा रात्रिः स्वयं सवितुः सूर्यप्रकाशात् प्रसूता उत्पन्ना । सूर्यो हस्तं गच्छन् रात्रिं जनयति । तस्मिन्नस्तमिते रात्रेरुत्पत्त्यभावात् । एवमेव रात्रिरपि उषसे सवाय उषसः उत्पत्तये तदर्थं योनिं स्थानं स्वकीयापरभागलक्षणमारैक् । अरेचितवती । कल्पितवतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । प्रसूता रात्रिः सवितुः सूर्यस्य सवाय प्रसवाय जन्मने यथा भवति एवं रात्रिरपि उषसः उज्जन्म तदर्थं योनिं स्वापरभागलक्षणं स्थानं कृतवती । अत्र निरुक्तम् । इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागात् चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञाततममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुः प्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्यैवं रात्र्युषसे योनिमरिचत् स्थानम् । नि. २-१९ । इति । श्रेष्ठम् । प्रशस्यस्य श्रः । पा. ५-३-६० । इति श्रादेशः । प्रकृत्यैकाच् । पा. ६-४-१६३ । इति प्रकृतिभावात्टेर्लोपाभावः । आगात् ।

jyotiṣāṃ grahanakṣatrādīnāṃ dyotamānānāṃ madhye idamuṣo 'bhimāninī jyotiḥ śreṣṭham | praśasyatamam | asya ko 'tiśaya iti cet ucyate | nakṣatrādikaṃ jyotiḥ svātmānameva prakāśayati nānyat | candrastu yadyapyanyatprakāśayati tathāpi na vispaṣṭaprakāśaḥ | uṣasaṃ tu jyotiryugapadeva sarvasya jagato 'ndhakāranirākaraṇena viśeṣeṇa prakāśakam | ataḥ praśastatamamityarthaḥ | tādṛśaṃ jyotirāgāt | pūrvasyāṃ diśyāgamat | āgate ca tasmin citraḥ cāyanīyaḥ praketaḥ andhakārāvṛtasya sarvasya padārthasya prajñāpakastadīyo raśmirvibhvā vibhurvyāptaḥ san ajaniṣṭa | prādurabhūt | kiṃca | yathā rātriḥ svayaṃ savituḥ sūryaprakāśāt prasūtā utpannā | sūryo hastaṃ gacchan rātriṃ janayati | tasminnastamite rātrerutpattyabhāvāt | evameva rātrirapi uṣase savāya uṣasaḥ utpattaye tadarthaṃ yoniṃ sthānaṃ svakīyāparabhāgalakṣaṇamāraik | arecitavatī | kalpitavatītyarthaḥ | yadvā | prasūtā rātriḥ savituḥ sūryasya savāya prasavāya janmane yathā bhavati evaṃ rātrirapi uṣasaḥ ujjanma tadarthaṃ yoniṃ svāparabhāgalakṣaṇaṃ sthānaṃ kṛtavatī | atra niruktam | idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāt citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātatamamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrirādityasyaivaṃ rātryuṣase yonimaricat sthānam | ni. 2-19 | iti | śreṣṭham | praśasyasya śraḥ | pā. 5-3-60 | iti śrādeśaḥ | prakṛtyaikāc | pā. 6-4-163 | iti prakṛtibhāvātṭerlopābhāvaḥ | āgāt |

Sense (mine): "Among the lights — planets, stars and the like, the shining ones — this light, the deity of Uṣas, is the best (śreṣṭha), the most praiseworthy. If one asks what its superiority is: the light of stars etc. illuminates only itself, not anything else; the moon too, though it illuminates other things, does not give a clear light; but the light of Uṣas, at one stroke, shows up the whole world especially by removing the darkness. Hence 'most praiseworthy'. Such a light has come, in the eastern quarter. And when it has come, a wonderful (citra), worshipful praketa — her ray, which makes known every object covered by darkness, pervading (vibhvā) — was born, appeared. Further: as Night, being herself born from the light of Savitṛ the Sun [—the Sun, going to his setting, produces Night; when he has set, Night has no birth otherwise—] so Night also, for the birth (savāya) of Uṣas, has prepared (āraik, 'emptied, arranged') a yoni (place) of her own, namely her latter part. Or: as Night, when born, is for the birth of Savitṛ the Sun, so Night has made for the birth of Uṣas the place, i.e. her own latter portion." Nirukta cited: "idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āgāt …" (Ni. 2-19 [?]) — a paraphrase of the Ṛk.

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): śreṣṭha — the superlative-suffix iṣṭhan with the substitution śra for praśasya (Pā. 5-3-60), and the grammatical point that the monosyllabic stem retains its natural form so the ṭi-elision does not occur (Pā. 6-4-163); āgāt — … (continues on the next page).

original p. 4

Grammatical tail of the bhāṣya, concluded (characterized, not transcribed; sūtra numbers partly illegible, none supplied): āgāt — root gam in the aorist, with the sic-elision after gā/sthā type roots and the ṭit-ending; ajaniṣṭa — jan in the sense "to appear", aorist; vibhvā — vi-sam-… bhū with the suffix ḍu (Pā. 3-2-180 as cited), and the instrumental ending replaced by ā by "supāṃ sulug…" (the rule of Vedic substitution), with the note that the yaṇ-substitution which the prohibition "bhūsudhiyoḥ" would block is permitted in the Veda; citra — final-accent point; praketaḥ — from kit, "to know"; prasūtā — sū in the sense "to give birth", past participle (niṣṭhā); savāya — the dative of sava (Pā. 6-?-? [?], "chandasi jana-sanavā vaktavyau" as the print has it [?]); eva — lengthened by "nipātasya ca" in the Saṃhitā; rātrī — feminine with ṅīp, plural/dual ending replaced by "rātreś cājasau"; āraik — root ric "to empty", aorist, with the Vedic "bahulaṃ chandasi" elision of the stem-vowel and the lightening of the penultimate (laghūpadha-guṇa) not applied by the rule ḥalaṅyābbhyaḥ… (as printed [?]); the long ai (ārāik) obtained by the vṛddhi — all noted briefly.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"jyotiṣām — among the planets, stars, etc.; idam — this (the Uṣas-[light]); śreṣṭham — most excellent; jyotiḥ — the mass of brilliance; āgāt — came up (in the eastern quarter); (it rose); citraḥ — wonderful; praketaḥ — (the rays) which make objects covered by darkness an object of sight; vibhvā — pervasively; ajaniṣṭa — was born; rātrī — Night; yathā — as; savituḥ — from the Sun; prasūtā — was born; evā — in the same manner (Night also); uṣase — for Uṣas; savāya — for the birth; yonim — the place of birth (the latter part of Night); āraik — prepared."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The mass of light — the most excellent among the planets, stars and the rest (namely that of Uṣas) — has risen in the eastern quarter. The wonderful rays of this Uṣas, which bring objects covered by darkness within sight, spread in all directions. Just as Night was born from the Sun, so Night makes for her own latter watch (yāma) a [seat] for the rising of the dawn."

English Translation (as printed)

This most excellent luminary of all luminaries has arrived; the wonderful and diffusive manifester (of all things) has been born; in like manner as night is the offspring of the sun, so she becomes the birth-place of the dawn.

original p. 5

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठमिदं ज्योतिः — इदं ज्योतिः प्रशस्यतमम् — the heading as printed (bold, with the Bhāṣya words "jyotiṣāṃ grahanakṣatrādīnāṃ dyotamānānāṃ madhye uṣa-ākhyaṃ jyotiḥ praśasyatamam"): the planets and stars shining in the atmosphere illuminate only themselves; there is no manifestation of other objects by them. Though the moon's light shows everything, objects are not well known by it. Because at Uṣas-time all things are seen plainly, the light of Uṣas is, to a very great extent, more excellent than the brilliance of the moon and the stars. Though the light of Uṣas is somewhat in the east, at that moment all the darkness in the world disappears. That is why [the commentators] explain "Uṣas's splendour is more excellent than the splendour of planets and stars" (śreṣṭhaṃ — praśasyatamam). The usage here "jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ" is for the sake of showing non-difference between the possessor of the property (dharmin, the luminary) and the property (dharma, the light) — a usage that occurs for this reason.

प्रकेतः — Praketaḥ. In the eleven names of knowledge (prajñā) the word ketuḥ is stated (Ni. 3-9 [as printed, numerals unclear?]). By the prefix pra, the sense is "excellent knowledge". Skandasvāmin, because ketu is said in the names of knowledge, explains praketaḥ as prakṛṣṭa-jñānam, "excellent knowledge" and gives the meaning, for the word citra, "worshipful": at the very moment when Uṣas rises, there is a light called knowledge, excellent, which makes everything worshipful appear before the eyes; so they have said the meaning "most praiseworthy light".

यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवाय एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् — The time after the Sun's setting is the time of Night's birth. From this it is established that Night is born from the Sun. In the same way, after the passing of the night, comes the time of Uṣas; therefore Night too is the cause of the birth of Uṣas — that is, as Night is born from the Sun, so Uṣas is born from Night: this is the intention. Or: as the rising of the Sun comes after Uṣas has risen, so that Uṣas is the cause of the rising (birth) of the Sun, so Night too is the cause of the birth of Uṣas — thus they have explained the meaning. These two meanings are the same in the two bhāṣyas (Sāyaṇa's and Skandasvāmin's).

original p. 6

Yāska explains this Ṛk in the following way:

इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरगमत् । चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञाततममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुः प्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्य । एवं रात्र्युषसे योनिमरिचत् स्थानम् । स्त्रीयोनिरभियुते एनां गर्भः ॥ [last words doubtful, [?]] (नि. २-१९)

idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotiragamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātatamamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrirādityasya | evaṃ rātryuṣase yonimaricat sthānam | strīyonirabhiyute enāṃ garbhaḥ ‖ [last words doubtful, [?]] (ni. 2-19)

"According to the saying 'rātreḥ paraḥ kālaḥ uṣa ity ucyate' ("the time after night is called Uṣas") [as quoted by the Kannada], the last portion of the night, that is the period before sunrise, is called Uṣas-time. The brilliance of this Uṣas-time, that is its light, is more excellent than all lights. In the world the Sun, the Moon and the stars are luminous. Of these the Sun's light is very sharp. The light of the stars lights only the stars themselves and does not light other objects: by the stars' light it is not possible to see other things. The Moon's light, though cool, is not much; so objects are not seen distinctly. But the light of Uṣas-time is neither fierce like the Sun's, nor cool like the Moon's, nor dim; it is able to show everything very well. Therefore it is said here that this Uṣas-light is extremely more excellent than the light of the Sun, Moon, stars and the rest. Moreover this light of Uṣas-time, at one time, in all regions, gives great delight to the hearts. Such an Uṣas-time's rise has now come. This is the explanation of the first half of the Ṛk."

"In the world, after the Sun sets, Night comes; after Night has passed, Uṣas-time; after Uṣas-time, the rising of the Sun. Since thus the one comes in a course after another, one is said to be the cause of the birth of the other. How: since Night follows the Sun's setting, the Sun is the cause of Night's birth; the Sun is therefore the cause of Night's birth. In the same way Uṣas-time is born from Night, and from Uṣas-time the Sun's rising comes. With just this intention it is described in this Ṛk: 'As Night was born of the Sun, so from Night Uṣas-time has appeared.'"

प्रकेतः — कित ज्ञाने । अन्धकारावृतस्य सर्वस्य पदार्थस्य प्रज्ञापकः । — "(rays) which, by their light, make visible those objects that cannot be seen in the dark." विभ्वा — विभुर्व्याप्तः । — "pervading, spread out." सवाय — उत्पत्तये । — "for birth, for rising." योनिः — उत्पत्तिस्थानम् । — "the place of birth; that which is the cause."

original p. 7

Grammar page, Kannada, on the words śreṣṭham (suffix iṣṭhan, the substitution śra for praśasya — Pā. 5-3-60 as printed; prakṛtyaikāc — Pā. 6-4-163 as printed; accent by jñityādir nityam [Pā. number not clearly read, [?]]), āgāt (iṇ "to go", aorist luṅ, tip; ito gā luṅi; gātisthāghupā… elision of sic; no augment), praketaḥ (kit jñāne, causative sense, ghañ suffix, guṇa; final-acute accent), ajaniṣṭa (jani prādurbhāve, luṅ, ta; cleḥ sic; ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ; ṣatva; tiṅ-atiṅaḥ nighāta accent), vibhvā (vi+bhū, viprasambhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām — Pā. 3-2-180 [?]; supāṃ sulug… ā-substitution; bhūsudhiyoḥ prohibition of yaṇ set aside by chandasy ubhayathā). ॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.2) Reading note after viewing the Pada: the Saṃhitā's ārāigu is the Pada's arāik + ūṃ iti; so the Saṃhitā's printed final gu stands for the Pada's k + the particle ū; and Ṛk 1's ārāik is the same form, which supports the doubtful arāik reading there.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.2)

श्वेत्येत्युषसो नामधेयम् । रुशती दीप्ता । श्वेत्या श्वेतवर्णोषा रुशद्वत्सा रुशद्दीप्तः सूर्यो वत्सो यस्याः सा तथोक्ता । यथा मातुः समीपे वत्सः संचरति । एवमुषसः समीपे सूर्यस्य नित्यमवस्थानात्तद्वत्त्वम् । अथवा यथा वत्सो मातुः स्तन्यं रसं पिबन्दरति [?] । एवमुषसोऽवश्यायाख्यं रसं पिबन्वत्स इत्युच्यते । तादृशी सत्यागात् । आगतवती । आगतायाः अस्याः उषसः कृष्णा कृष्णवर्णा रात्रिः सदनानि स्थानानि स्वकीयान्त्यार्धयामलक्षणान्यारैक् । अरेचितवती । कल्पितवतीत्यर्थः । ऊ इत्येतत्पदपूरणम् । अपि चैते रात्र्युषसौ समानबन्धू समानेनैकेन सूर्यात्मकेन बन्धुना सख्या युक्ते । यद्वा । सूर्येण सह [continues on the next page]

śvetyetyuṣaso nāmadheyam | ruśatī dīptā | śvetyā śvetavarṇoṣā ruśadvatsā ruśaddīptaḥ sūryo vatso yasyāḥ sā tathoktā | yathā mātuḥ samīpe vatsaḥ saṃcarati | evamuṣasaḥ samīpe sūryasya nityamavasthānāttadvattvam | athavā yathā vatso mātuḥ stanyaṃ rasaṃ pibandarati [?] | evamuṣaso 'vaśyāyākhyaṃ rasaṃ pibanvatsa ityucyate | tādṛśī satyāgāt | āgatavatī | āgatāyāḥ asyāḥ uṣasaḥ kṛṣṇā kṛṣṇavarṇā rātriḥ sadanāni sthānāni svakīyāntyārdhayāmalakṣaṇānyāraik | arecitavatī | kalpitavatītyarthaḥ | ū ityetatpadapūraṇam | api caite rātryuṣasau samānabandhū samānenaikena sūryātmakena bandhunā sakhyā yukte | yadvā | sūryeṇa saha [continues on the next page]

Sense (mine): "Śvetī is a name of Uṣas. Ruśatī = shining. White-coloured Uṣas, ruśadvatsā: she who has the bright Sun as her calf (vatsa): as a calf moves about near its mother, so, because the Sun constantly stays near Uṣas, she is so called. Or: as a calf drinks the mother's milk, so (the Sun) drinks the juice called avaśyāya (dew) of Uṣas, and is therefore called vatsa [the printed verb is doubtful]. Such Uṣas has come. After she has come, black Night has made ready (āraik) the places (sadanāni) — her own last half-watch (yāma) — i.e. has arranged them. Ū is a mere filler. And these two, Night and Uṣas, are samānabandhū, 'joined by one common kinsman or friend, who is the Sun'; or: with the Sun …" continues

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.2), continued from p. 9

सम्बद्धे । यथोषा उदेष्यता सूर्येण सम्बद्धा एवं रात्रिरप्यस्तंयता सूर्येण सम्बद्धा । अमृते मरणरहिते कालात्मकतया नित्यत्वात् । अनूची अनुपूर्वमञ्चतो गच्छन्त्यौ । प्रथमं रात्रिः पश्चादुषा इत्यनेन क्रमेण गच्छन्त्यौ । यद्वा सूर्यगत्यैवानुसारेण गच्छन्त्यौ । एवम्भूते वर्णं सर्वेषां प्राणिनां रूपमामिनाने जरयन्त्यौ । यद्वा स्वकीयं रूपं हिंसन्त्यौ । उषसा स्वैशं तमो निवर्तते । प्रकाशात्मकमुषसो रूपं रात्र्या । एवंविधे सत्यौ द्यावा द्योतमाने चरतः । प्रतिदिवसमावर्तेते । यद्वा । द्यावा नभःसान्तरिक्षमार्गेण चरतः प्रतिदिवसं गच्छतः । अत्र निरुक्तम् । रुशद्वत्सा सूर्यवत्सा रुशदिति वर्णनाम रोचतेर्ज्वलतिकर्मणः । सूर्यमस्या वत्समाहुः साहचर्याद्रसहरणाद्वा । रुशती श्वेत्यागात् । श्वेत्या श्वेततेः । आरैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः कृष्णवर्णा रात्रिः कृष्णं कृष्यतेर्निकृष्टो वर्णः । अमृते अमरणधर्माणौ । अनूची अनुगते इतरेतरमभिप्रेत्य । द्यावा वर्णं चरतः । आमिनाने अन्योन्यस्याध्यात्मं कुर्वाणे । नि. २-२० ॥ [the Nirukta passage read from this page as printed; doubtful words [?]]

sambaddhe | yathoṣā udeṣyatā sūryeṇa sambaddhā evaṃ rātrirapyastaṃyatā sūryeṇa sambaddhā | amṛte maraṇarahite kālātmakatayā nityatvāt | anūcī anupūrvamañcato gacchantyau | prathamaṃ rātriḥ paścāduṣā ityanena krameṇa gacchantyau | yadvā sūryagatyaivānusāreṇa gacchantyau | evambhūte varṇaṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ rūpamāmināne jarayantyau | yadvā svakīyaṃ rūpaṃ hiṃsantyau | uṣasā svaiśaṃ tamo nivartate | prakāśātmakamuṣaso rūpaṃ rātryā | evaṃvidhe satyau dyāvā dyotamāne carataḥ | pratidivasamāvartete | yadvā | dyāvā nabhaḥsāntarikṣamārgeṇa carataḥ pratidivasaṃ gacchataḥ | atra niruktam | ruśadvatsā sūryavatsā ruśaditi varṇanāma rocaterjvalatikarmaṇaḥ | sūryamasyā vatsamāhuḥ sāhacaryādrasaharaṇādvā | ruśatī śvetyāgāt | śvetyā śvetateḥ | āraigu kṛṣṇā sadanānyasyāḥ kṛṣṇavarṇā rātriḥ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣyaternikṛṣṭo varṇaḥ | amṛte amaraṇadharmāṇau | anūcī anugate itaretaramabhipretya | dyāvā varṇaṃ carataḥ | āmināne anyonyasyādhyātmaṃ kurvāṇe | ni. 2-20 ‖ [the Nirukta passage read from this page as printed; doubtful words [?]]

Sense (mine): "… sambaddhe (connected): as Uṣas, about to appear, is connected with the Sun, so Night too, as the Sun sets, is connected with him. Amṛte — free from death, being eternal by their nature as Time. Anūcī — going one after the other: first Night, afterwards Uṣas, going in this order; or going following the Sun's course. Being such, they āmināne — wear out (age) the varṇa, the form, of all living beings; or they destroy each its own form: by Uṣas the darkness of Night is turned back, and the luminous form of Uṣas by Night. Being thus, they roam (carataḥ) shining (dyāvā), revolving every day; or they go along the sky and atmosphere each day." Yāska is then cited (Ni. 2-20): "ruśadvatsā = having the Sun as calf; ruśat is a name for colour, from ruc 'to shine'…; they call the Sun her calf, from association or from drawing off the juice; śvetyā from śvit; kṛṣṇā — Night, black, dark colour; amṛte — two of non-dying nature; anūcī — following each other; āmināne — doing the work of one another…" sense given from the print; the last clauses are tersely worded and a little doubtful [?]

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): on śvetyā (a derivative of the root śvit, the suffix yat in the abstract sense with elision of the causative ṇi, then the affix ac by the arśa-ādi class); amṛte (a bahuvrīhi with nañ; accent on the first syllable by the rule on jara-mara-mitra-mṛtāḥ); anūcī (añc with kvin, with the ṅīp feminine; nasal elision; lengthening; the udātta of the ṅīp; elision of the case-ending by supāṃ sulug); āmināne (mī "to injure", class 9 kryādi, with the participle suffix śānac; shortening by mināteḥ…). ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"ruśatī — shining; śvetyā — with white colour, Uṣas; ruśadvatsā — having the shining Sun as calf; āgāt — has risen; kṛṣṇā — black-coloured Night; asyāḥ — to this Uṣas; sadanāni — (the latter half-watch of Night) as places of birth; āraik ū — has prepared; ete — these Night and Uṣas; samānabandhū — having a common (Sun as) kinsman (the Sun being related to both); amṛte — eternal; anūcī — each following the other (Uṣas after Night, and again in the same order); varṇam — the form (of objects); āmināne — making them old (as time passes); dyāvā — shining in the atmosphere; carataḥ — move every day."

original p. 11

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Uṣas, who is the mother of the Sun, has been born, shining, from the last watch of black-coloured Night. This Night and Uṣas are both closely related with the Sun (Night comes after the Sun's setting and Uṣas comes before the Sun's rising); being of the form of Time they are eternal; both come in one order (after Night, Uṣas); they destroy each other's form (Uṣas destroys the darkness and Night destroys the light); or, by their motion the forms of objects become aged (are made to grow old); and thus both of them move about in the atmosphere."

English Translation (as printed)

The white-shining dawn, the parent of the Sun has arrived ; dark night has sought her own abode ; both allied to the same (sun) ; immortal, succeeding to each other and mutually effacing each other's complexion, they traverse the heavens.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

श्वेत्या — Śvetyā. "Vibhāvarī, sūnarī" — among the sixteen names of Uṣas (Ni. 3-19 as printed [?]) it is stated; so the meaning is Uṣas. Śvetyā — white-coloured; Sāyaṇa explains the meaning as "of auspicious lustre". Yāska also says "śvetyāgāt śvetyā śvetater dhātoḥ śvetavarṇārthaḥ"; for the word śvetyā derived from the root śvit (śvetati) of the bhvādi class, he gives the sense "white-coloured".

रुशद्वत्सा — "ruśad dīptaḥ sūryo vatso yasyāḥ sā": she who has the shining Sun as her calf. That a calf plays near its mother is common in the world. Following this, the Sun is the calf of Uṣas, being near Uṣas. The relation of mother and son between Uṣas and the Sun is on account of Uṣas's lustre and of his moving near. Whereas Sāyaṇa explains that "the calf drinks the mother's milk", (so) the Sun also, having fully received Uṣas's lustre, becomes lustrous — so he says. The Nirukta-writer says:

रुशद्वत्सा सूर्यवत्सा । रुशदिति वर्णनाम । रोचतेर्ज्वलतिकर्मणः । सूर्यमस्या वत्समाहुः साहचर्याद्रसहरणाद्वा ॥ (नि. २-२०)

ruśadvatsā sūryavatsā | ruśaditi varṇanāma | rocaterjvalatikarmaṇaḥ | sūryamasyā vatsamāhuḥ sāhacaryādrasaharaṇādvā ‖ (ni. 2-20)

original p. 12

Ruśadvatsā — "the word means 'a calf who has lustre': the Sun. Ruśat is, as Sāyaṇa explains, a word derived from the root ruc, with the meaning 'lustre' (kānti). Likewise he establishes the sonship (putratva, vatsabhāva) of the Sun in relation to Uṣas. And in order to make firm the meaning stated by the Ṛk idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ, this second Ṛk ruśadvatsā has arisen. The last part of Night is called Uṣas — so they point out Uṣas-time. Skandasvāmin, Sāyaṇa and Yāska, as they establish, explain also in another way the sonship of the Sun in respect of Uṣas. They quote also a passage of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa —

वत्स इत्यादित्य उच्यते । स ह्युषसो वत्सस्थानीयः अपत्यत्वात् । श्रुतेर्दर्शनात् । एवं हि श्रुतौ श्रूयते — प्रजापतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायत् । दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्यन्ये । तामृश्यो भूत्वा रोहितं भूतामभ्यैत् (ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३३ [?]) इत्येवमाद्युपक्रम्य । तद्वा इदं प्रजापतेः रेतः सिक्तमधावत्तदपसरोऽभवत् (ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३३ [?]) इति च । तदग्निना वैश्वानरेण पर्योढधुः [?] तं मरुतोऽघ्नन् [?] । तदग्निर्वैश्वानरः प्रत्यायावयत् [?] । तस्य यद्रेतः प्रथममुदधीयत तदसावादित्योऽभवत् (ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३४ [?]) इत्येवं प्रजापतेः रेतसः उषसि जात आदित्य इति श्रूयते । अतस्तदुपपन्नमस्य अपत्यत्वम् ॥

vatsa ityāditya ucyate | sa hyuṣaso vatsasthānīyaḥ apatyatvāt | śruterdarśanāt | evaṃ hi śrutau śrūyate — prajāpatirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyat | divamityanya āhuruṣasamityanye | tāmṛśyo bhūtvā rohitaṃ bhūtāmabhyait (ai. brā. 3-33 [?]) ityevamādyupakramya | tadvā idaṃ prajāpateḥ retaḥ siktamadhāvattadapasaro 'bhavat (ai. brā. 3-33 [?]) iti ca | tadagninā vaiśvānareṇa paryoḍhadhuḥ [?] taṃ maruto 'ghnan [?] | tadagnirvaiśvānaraḥ pratyāyāvayat [?] | tasya yadretaḥ prathamamudadhīyata tadasāvādityo 'bhavat (ai. brā. 3-34 [?]) ityevaṃ prajāpateḥ retasaḥ uṣasi jāta āditya iti śrūyate | atastadupapannamasya apatyatvam ‖

(Note: The Sanskrit is copied letter by letter from the Kannada-script print; the words marked [?] are doubtful; the reference numerals are small and I give them only as read.)

Sense (Kannada, as explained): "In the 3rd [book?], khaṇḍas 33 and 34 [as printed, [?]] of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa it is said that Āditya is the son of Uṣas. Prajāpati, i.e. Brahmā, set his mind on enjoying his own daughter Div ('heaven') or Uṣas (some say the one, others the other); she took the form of a doe, he assumed the form of a stag. When Brahmā's semen fell, Vaiśvānara (Agni) held it; the Maruts too … and Vaiśvānara brought it back. The first portion of Brahmā's seed took the form of Āditya. Thus it is said that Āditya was born, by Prajāpati, in Uṣas, from his seed, and so the sonship of the Sun in relation to Uṣas is explained. And they say (the bhāṣya) 'yadvā prātaḥ prātaḥ uṣasaḥ sakāśād ādityo jāyate tadabhiprāyam asyā patyatvam' [sic — the printed patyatvam; the sense is apatyatvam, "sonship"]: or, every morning, from near Uṣas the Sun is born — this is the intention of the (word) 'sonship'; since every morning the Sun's rising is only from Uṣas, the Sun is the calf of Uṣas, and in this way too the sonship of the Sun in relation to Uṣas may be said."

Kṛṣṇā sadanāni asyāḥ āraik — "Night, joined with the darkness of black colour, making in her own last watch a dwelling for Uṣas, becomes the place of Uṣas's birth."

original p. 13

"This idea itself is stated clearly in the Ṛk idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ as 'rātry uṣase yonim āraik'. In the Nirukta too —

कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः अरिचित् । कृष्णवर्णा रात्रिः कृष्णा । कृष्णं कृष्यतेर्निकृष्टो वर्णः ॥

kṛṣṇā sadanānyasyāḥ aricit | kṛṣṇavarṇā rātriḥ kṛṣṇā | kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣyaternikṛṣṭo varṇaḥ ‖

— so this part is explained."

अमृते — Amṛte. "Mṛta is death; amṛta, those who have no death, i.e. have no destruction; Night and Uṣas are spoken of by the word amṛta."

अनूची — Anūcī: "anugacchantyau, 'going after each other': Night and Uṣas both move following each other's motion — in the order 'first Night, then Uṣas' or 'first Uṣas, then Night'; thus each follows the other and both keep moving; or, as they say, both follow the going of the Sun."

समानबन्धू — Samānabandhū. "Night and Uṣas both have the Sun alone as kinsman; or they are connected with the Sun's rising and setting: Uṣas is connected with the rising of the Sun, Night with the Sun's setting. Because of this, they have common kinship — so Sāyaṇa says. The Nirukta-writer explains the word samānabandhū as 'having one single kind of rule (bandhana)'. Skandasvāmin: 'samāna bandhū — ubhe rātryuṣasī': Night and Uṣas both have a common kinsman, or a common bond (bandhana), and so explains their common kinship:

समानो बन्धुर्ययोस्ते समानबन्धू । प्रजापतिर्हि रात्र्युषसोः समानबन्धुः जनयितृत्वात् । आदित्यो वा । स हि जनयितृत्वेन रात्रेर्बन्धुः । जन्यत्वेन उषसः । जनयितृत्वेन वा उभयोः । स ह्यस्तमयेन रात्रिं जनयति उदयेन चोषसम् ॥

samāno bandhuryayoste samānabandhū | prajāpatirhi rātryuṣasoḥ samānabandhuḥ janayitṛtvāt | ādityo vā | sa hi janayitṛtvena rātrerbandhuḥ | janyatvena uṣasaḥ | janayitṛtvena vā ubhayoḥ | sa hyastamayena rātriṃ janayati udayena coṣasam ‖

— so they explain: Night and Uṣas, the two, have one and the same kinsman; Prajāpati, being the producer of Night and Uṣas, is their kinsman. Or Āditya: as the producer of Night he is its kinsman, and as the one born (of Uṣas) he is Uṣas's [kinsman]; or by being the producer of both: for by setting he produces Night, and by rising, Uṣas."

original p. 14

"… Because of this, he (Āditya) is both a kinsman of Uṣas and, according to this explanation, the producer of Night and the one produced of Uṣas. The rising of Night is from the setting of Āditya; and [the rising] of Uṣas, in the sense that he himself rises at her rising, is the meaning."

द्यावा वर्णं चरत आमिनाने — Dyāvā varṇaṃ carata āmināne. "For this sentence Sāyaṇa, Skandasvāmin and the Nirukta-writer have each given a different explanation. Āmināne is derived from the root mīñ 'to injure', with the prefix ā, so the word has the meaning 'injuring'. Construing this word āmināne with the word varṇam, they give the sense: Night, with her black colour, and Uṣas, with her bright light, destroy each other's — 'the light of Uṣas' by Night's black colour and 'the colour of Night' by Uṣas's shining — and move about, the two of them, in the atmosphere. And [another explanation:] Night and Uṣas, varṇam āmināne, 'injuring the form (varṇa) of living beings', dyāvā carataḥ, 'move in the atmosphere' — in this interpretation they move along bringing about, also, the changes in the bodies' form of living beings — thirty [?] — so the sense becomes. These two kinds of meaning are stated in the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya. Skandasvāmin:

द्यौर्दीप्तेर्दीप्यतेर्वा दीप्त्यर्थस्येदं रूपम् । स्वेन स्वेन तेजसा दीप्ते । शुक्लं कृष्णं च आत्मीयं वर्णं चरतः गच्छतः प्राप्नुतः ॥

dyaurdīpterdīpyatervā dīptyarthasyedaṃ rūpam | svena svena tejasā dīpte | śuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca ātmīyaṃ varṇaṃ carataḥ gacchataḥ prāpnutaḥ ‖

— dyautī dīptau, dīpī dīptau: from the roots with the sense 'to shine' the form dyāvā is made. Night and Uṣas shine each with its own black and bright lustre: this is one kind of meaning.

द्यावेति दिवः पर्यायः तृतीयैकवचनान्तश्च दिवा सह महत्त्वादिना गुणेन स्पर्धमाने दिवा वा अनुग्रहमाणे स्वं स्वं वर्णं प्राप्नुतः ॥

dyāveti divaḥ paryāyaḥ tṛtīyaikavacanāntaśca divā saha mahattvādinā guṇena spardhamāne divā vā anugrahamāṇe svaṃ svaṃ varṇaṃ prāpnutaḥ ‖

The word dyāvā is in the instrumental singular; it is a synonym of the words meaning divaḥ, 'atmosphere'. Night and Uṣas are competing with the sky, seeing its greatness and other qualities; or, receiving favour from the luminous form of the sky, they get each their own colour: this is the second kind of meaning."

original p. 15

द्यौर्हि तमसा ज्योतिषा चात्मन्यवदानेन वा अनुगृह्णाति रात्र्युषसोः । [last words doubtful [?]]

dyaurhi tamasā jyotiṣā cātmanyavadānena vā anugṛhṇāti rātryuṣasoḥ | [last words doubtful [?]]

"The atmosphere has within itself both darkness and lights; since it favours Night and Uṣas, these two keep their own colours — this is the third kind of meaning. As for the meaning of the word āmināne, they too say as Sāyaṇa has said:

आमिनाने—आजोषदर्थे [?] मीञ् हिंसायां ईषत् हिंसन्त्यौ । रात्रिर्ह्युषसो रूपं ज्योतीरीषद्धिनस्ति । उषा अपि रात्रेस्तमः ॥

āmināne—ājoṣadarthe [?] mīñ hiṃsāyāṃ īṣat hiṃsantyau | rātrirhyuṣaso rūpaṃ jyotīrīṣaddhinasti | uṣā api rātrestamaḥ ‖

— Night and Uṣas destroy each other's own forms: i.e. Night destroys Uṣas's light a little, and Uṣas, Night's darkness; and he gives also another kind of meaning:

आमिनाने इत्याकारोऽध्यर्थे । मिनतिरपि सामर्थ्यात् करोत्यर्थः । आत्मीयं रूपं दिव उपरि कुर्वाणे ॥

āmināne ityākāro 'dhyarthe | minatirapi sāmarthyāt karotyarthaḥ | ātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ diva upari kurvāṇe ‖

— the letter ā in āmināne is in the sense of adhi ('over, above'); the root mī is in the sense of 'doing'. Hence (the Kannada: "Night and Uṣas shine beyond the atmosphere with each its own form") — they give yet another kind of meaning. The Nirukta-writer:

द्यावा वर्णं चरतः — द्यावौ ते इव द्योतनात् । अपि वा द्यावा चरतः तयोः सह चरत इति स्यात् । आमिनाने आमिनाने अन्योन्यस्याध्यात्मं कुर्वाणे ॥ (नि. २-२०)

dyāvā varṇaṃ carataḥ — dyāvau te iva dyotanāt | api vā dyāvā carataḥ tayoḥ saha carata iti syāt | āmināne āmināne anyonyasyādhyātmaṃ kurvāṇe ‖ (ni. 2-20)

— giving the meaning, and saying of āmināne that 'each shines with its own form, outdoing the other', to give the sense of adhi for the prefix ā of āmināne they cite a Ṛk (Ni. 3-2 [as printed, [?]]):

पुरु त्वा दाश्वाँ वोचेऽरिरग्ने तव स्विदा । तोदस्येव शरण आ महस्य ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१५०-१)

puru tvā dāśvā~ voce 'riragne tava svidā | todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-150-1)

— "here they have explained the words ā mahasya as adhi mahataḥ ('over the great')." Gloss editorial and tentative: the Ṛk is cited only for the prefix; the Kannada gives no translation of it.

original p. 16

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on the words ruśadvatsā (a bahuvrīhi, the first member keeps its natural accent, Pā. 6-2-1 [as read]), śvetyā (śvit "to be white"; the ṇic, then yat — aco yat — in the sense of the action, loss of ṇi, pugantalaghūpadhasya ca guṇa; the ac suffix of the possessive by arśa-ādibhyo 'c; ṭāp by ajādyatas ṭāp; accent), agāt (explained in the earlier Ṛk), sadanāni (sad with lyuṭ in the sense of the locus; anā for yu by yuvor anākau; accent by liti), samānabandhū (bahuvrīhi; first-member accent), amṛte (nañ-bahuvrīhi, ña-iñja-ra-mara-mitra-mṛtāḥ accent), anūcī (anu+añc with kvin; nasal elision by anidita hal-upadha…; feminine in ṅīp by the añcateś chopasaṃkhyānam statement; bha-designation and elision of a by aca…). Sūtra numbers are small; I give none.

original p. 17

Grammar page of Ṛk 2, concluded (noted briefly): anūcī (lengthening of the preceding vowel; the ṅīp ending with its accent; supāṃ sulug, elision of the dual ending); carataḥ (car "to move, eat", laṭ 3rd dual; nighāta accent after a word that ends in an accented syllable); āmināne (mīñ "to injure", kryādi class, śānac in the laṭ sense; shortening by mīnāter nigame; śnā by kryādibhyaḥ śnā; final accent as the ending is cit). ‖ 2 ‖ (printed numeral "२" [as in the Ṛk number]). Printer's ornament.

Rik 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.3)

समानो अध्वा स्वस्रोरनन्तस्तमन्यान्या चरतो देवशिष्टे । न मेथेते न तस्थतुः सुमेके नक्तोषासा समनसा विरूपे ॥ ३ ॥

samāno adhvā svasroranantastamanyānyā carato devaśiṣṭe | na methete na tasthatuḥ sumeke naktoṣāsā samanasā virūpe ‖ 3 ‖

original p. 18

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.3) Reading note after viewing the Pada: the Saṃhitā's nak-toṣāsā is the Pada's naktoṣasā (shortened); the Saṃhitā's anyānyā is the Pada's anyā-anyā, with the avagraha as printed.

समानः । अध्वा । स्वस्रोः । अनन्तः । तम् । अन्याऽअन्या । चरतः । देवशिष्टे इति देवऽशिष्टे । न । मेथेते इति । न । तस्थतुः । सुमेके इति सुऽमेके । नक्तोषसा । समनसा । विरूपे इति विऽरूपे ॥ ३ ॥

samānaḥ | adhvā | svasroḥ | anantaḥ | tam | anyā 'anyā | carataḥ | devaśiṣṭe iti deva 'śiṣṭe | na | methete iti | na | tasthatuḥ | sumeke iti su 'meke | naktoṣasā | samanasā | virūpe iti vi 'rūpe ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.3)

स्वस्रोर्भगिन्योः रात्र्युषसोरध्वा सञ्चरणसाधनभूतो मार्गः समान एक एव । येनैवाकाशमार्गेणोषा निर्गच्छति तेनैव रात्रिरपि । स च मार्गोऽनन्तोऽवसानरहितः । तं मार्गं देवशिष्टे देवेन द्योतमानेन सूर्येणानुशिष्टे शिक्षिते सत्यावन्यान्या एकैका चरतः । क्रमेण गच्छतः । अपि च सुमेके शोभनमेहने सर्वेषामुत्पादकत्वात् शोभनप्रजनने नक्तोषासा रात्रिरुषाश्च विरूपे तमःप्रकाशलक्षणाभ्यां विरुद्धरूपाभ्यां युक्ते अपि समनसा समानमनस्के ऐकमत्यं प्राप्ते सत्यौ न मेथेते । परस्परं न हिंस्तः । तथा न तस्थतुः । कचिदपि न तिष्ठतः । सर्वदा लोकानुग्रहार्थं गच्छत इत्यर्थः ॥

svasrorbhaginyoḥ rātryuṣasoradhvā sañcaraṇasādhanabhūto mārgaḥ samāna eka eva | yenaivākāśamārgeṇoṣā nirgacchati tenaiva rātrirapi | sa ca mārgo 'nanto 'vasānarahitaḥ | taṃ mārgaṃ devaśiṣṭe devena dyotamānena sūryeṇānuśiṣṭe śikṣite satyāvanyānyā ekaikā carataḥ | krameṇa gacchataḥ | api ca sumeke śobhanamehane sarveṣāmutpādakatvāt śobhanaprajanane naktoṣāsā rātriruṣāśca virūpe tamaḥprakāśalakṣaṇābhyāṃ viruddharūpābhyāṃ yukte api samanasā samānamanaske aikamatyaṃ prāpte satyau na methete | parasparaṃ na hiṃstaḥ | tathā na tasthatuḥ | kacidapi na tiṣṭhataḥ | sarvadā lokānugrahārthaṃ gacchata ityarthaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "The path (adhvā), the means of travel, of the two sisters Night and Uṣas is one and the same; by whatever sky-way Uṣas goes out, by that same Night too. That path is endless, without end. When that path has been taught (anuśiṣṭe, instructed) by the shining god, the Sun, the two (devaśiṣṭe) move one after the other, in order. Moreover, sumeke — having good (su) meha (generative power), being producers of all — Night and Uṣas, virūpe, being of opposite forms by the marks of darkness and light, yet being samanasā, of one mind (having come to agreement), na methete: do not injure each other; and na tasthatuḥ: do not stand still anywhere — they go always for the benefit of the world."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): anyānyā (doubling of the pronoun in the sense of reciprocal action, as a compound, with the second member made āmreḍita and unaccented; Pā. citation partly legible, "Ma. 8-1-12(?)" [?]); deva-śiṣṭe (śās "to instruct", kta with the iṭ prohibition, i for the penultimate by śāsa idaṅhaloḥ, Pā. 6-4-34; ṣatva; the first member keeps its accent in the tṛtīyā compound); methete (mith/meth "to understand, injure", bhvādi, anudāttet); sumeke (mih "to sprinkle", ghañ in the abstract sense, "those who have a good meha", the k by the Vedic usage; the second member accented on the first syllable); naktoṣāsā (the case-ending replaced by ā by supāṃ sulug; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā "of the penultimate seen in other words too").

original p. 19

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"svasroḥ — of the sisters Night and Uṣas; adhvā — the path of going about; samānaḥ — one and the same (and); anantaḥ — without end; tam — in that path; devaśiṣṭe — taught by the Sun; anyānyā — one after the other, in order; carataḥ — go about; sumeke — producers of all things; naktoṣāsā — Night and Uṣas; virūpe — though of forms opposed to each other; samanasā — of one mind; na methete — they do not obstruct each other (and); na tasthatuḥ — do not stand still in one place."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"For both Night and Uṣas the path of going about is one; and it is without end; both, taught by the Sun, go about in one and the same order; though their forms are different, the work intended for both is one. Therefore, being producers of all things, they do not thwart each other, nor stand in one place; they go on moving always."

English Translation (as printed)

The path of the sisters is unending; they travel it alternately, guided by the radiant (sun); combined in purpose, though of different forms, night and dawn, giving birth (to all things), obstruct not each other, neither do they stand still.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

स्वस्रोः — Svasroḥ. "bhaginyoḥ rātryuṣasoḥ" (Skandasvāmin):

रात्र्युषसौ ह्येकेन प्रजापतिना आदित्येन वा जन्येते इति उपपन्नमनयोर्भगिनीत्वम् ॥

rātryuṣasau hyekena prajāpatinā ādityena vā janyete iti upapannamanayorbhaginītvam ‖

"Night and Uṣas, as the two born from one — Brahmā (Prajāpati) or Āditya — are therefore bhaginī (sisters, born of the same). Or, since both move on one and the same path, they are called sisters."

देवशिष्टे — Devaśiṣṭe (Skandasvāmin):

शासिरत्र शुद्धोऽपि सामर्थ्यात् सोपसर्गार्थो द्रष्टव्यः । सर्वप्राणिनामुपकाराय देवैरनुशिष्टे । अनुज्ञाते इत्यर्थः ॥

śāsiratra śuddho 'pi sāmarthyāt sopasargārtho draṣṭavyaḥ | sarvaprāṇināmupakārāya devairanuśiṣṭe | anujñāte ityarthaḥ ‖

"The root śās, though here used without a prefix, must be understood, by its capacity, as having the meaning with a prefix (anu-śās). 'Directed (anuśiṣṭe) by the gods for the benefit of all living beings'; that is, 'permitted'." The Kannada: "Although the root śāsu is here used without any prefix, it should here be taken as having the sense expressed by the prefix. To do good to all beings they were granted permission by the gods."

original p. 20

"… and he explains that the two (Night and Uṣas) are intent on doing good to the world. Sāyaṇa [explains] devena dyotamānena sūryeṇa anuśiṣṭe śikṣite: Night and Uṣas, who are taught by the shining Sun, move in one and the same path in order: along the path where Night has moved, Uṣas moves; and again, along the path where Uṣas has moved, Night moves — so he explains the meaning."

विरूपे समनसा न मेथेते — Virūpe samanasā na methete. "Night has the form of darkness; Uṣas has the form of her own light. Therefore, since the two have no common colour, they are called virūpe. Yet both Night and Uṣas are one in intention and of one mind in the work of doing good to the world. Still, the two never meet in one place: they remain separate. One follows the other: after the day comes Night, after the night comes the Uṣas-time, going on following each other. Skandasvāmin, since the root methṛ is used here in the sense of 'to curse (ākrośana)', explains: they work always without grumbling; they do not scold (curse) one another."

सुमेके — Sumeke (Skandasvāmin):

सुमेके — मेकशब्दो मुखवचन इति केचिदाहुः । सुमुख्यौ । सृष्टेः प्रथमः संवत्सरः मेक इत्युच्यते इत्येके । तथाह । मेकसंवत्सरः ऋतवो मेकपुत्रा इति पौराणिकाः स्मरन्ति । शोभनो मेको ययोः सम्बन्धी सृष्टिकालजन्यतया के सुमेके । आद्यसंवत्सरसृष्टे इत्यर्थः ॥ [reading of tathāha and ke doubtful [?]]

sumeke — mekaśabdo mukhavacana iti kecidāhuḥ | sumukhyau | sṛṣṭeḥ prathamaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ meka ityucyate ityeke | tathāha | mekasaṃvatsaraḥ ṛtavo mekaputrā iti paurāṇikāḥ smaranti | śobhano meko yayoḥ sambandhī sṛṣṭikālajanyatayā ke sumeke | ādyasaṃvatsarasṛṣṭe ityarthaḥ ‖ [reading of tathāha and ke doubtful [?]]

"Of the sumeke that Skandasvāmin and Sāyaṇa say, śobhanamehane — all being producers, 'those who have an excellent generative power (indriya) as the means for the birth of all' — he gives yet another meaning. 'Because the word meka denotes "face" (mukha), they are those with beautiful faces' — so they say; and since the first year of creation is called meka and the Purāṇic writers remember 'meka-year; the seasons are meka's sons', those whose connection is with that fine meka, i.e. who, as born at the time of creation, belong to the first year: the Night and Uṣas created in the first year (saṃvatsara) of creation — so he explains, connecting with the Aṅgirases' [as the Kannada says: the sons of Meka are the seasons]."

अन्यान्या — Anyānyā — "ekaikā": "karmavyatihāre sarvanāmno dve bhavata iti vaktavyaṃ samāsavac ca bahulam — the word anya … (Sāyaṇa [explains]): in a pronoun-word, which expresses reciprocal action, doubled and joined as a compound; for the sense of anyonya, 'each other'." The sentence is cut at the foot of the page; it continues on p. 21.

original p. 21

"… the word anya is doubled: the idea is that Night and Uṣas, the two together, are one and the same, in one piece. Skandasvāmin:

अन्यान्या शब्दः परस्परपर्यायः तृतीयैकवचनान्तश्च । परस्परसम्बद्धे चरतः गच्छतः ॥

anyānyā śabdaḥ parasparaparyāyaḥ tṛtīyaikavacanāntaśca | parasparasambaddhe carataḥ gacchataḥ ‖

— the word anyānyā is a synonym of the word paraspara ('each other'), and ends in the instrumental singular. 'The two, joined to each other, go about.' Thus he explains that Night and Uṣas, joining in each other's work, go about."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on anantaḥ (a nañ-bahuvrīhi, accent on the last syllable of the later member by nañsubhyām, Pā. 6-2-172 [as read]), anyānyā (doubling of anya in reciprocal action by the Vārttika "karmavyatihāre sarvanāmno dve…", with the supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ elision of the sup in the compound-like doubling; āmreḍita designation of the second member; accent by anudāttaṃ ca), deva-śiṣṭe (śās of the adādi class, kta by niṣṭhā; the iṭ prohibition by yasya vibhāṣā; i for the penultimate by śāsa idaṅhaloḥ; ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca; the ṭ-substitute; the first member keeps its natural accent by tṛtīyā karmaṇi), methete (mith/meth "to understand, to injure", bhvādi; anudāttet — hence ātmanepada; laṭ, āthām → ete by ṭita ātmanepadānām ṭer e; ā → iy … lopo vyor vali; nighāta accent), tasthatuḥ (ṣṭhā, "to cease motion", liṭ 3rd dual; nighāta). Pā. numbers are partly legible; I give none.

Grammar page, concluded: sumeke (mih "to sprinkle", ghañ in the abstract sense; guṇa of the penultimate by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca; meha — the Vedic change of h to k; jñityādir nityam accent; the second member given the first-syllable accent by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi; dual), naktoṣasā ("naktaṃ ca uṣāś ca" — the case-ending replaced by ā by supāṃ sulug; the lengthening of the penultimate in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate), samanasā ("samānaṃ manaḥ yayoḥ te" — ā for the ending as before; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam — first member keeps its accent), virūpe ("viruddhaṃ rūpaṃ yayoḥ te"; first member keeps its accent; dual). ‖ 3 ‖

भास्वती नेत्री सूनृतानामचेति चित्रा वि दुरो न आवः । प्रार्प्या जगद्व्यु नो रायो अख्यदुषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ ४ ॥

bhāsvatī netrī sūnṛtānāmaceti citrā vi duro na āvaḥ | prārpyā jagadvyu no rāyo akhyaduṣā ajīgarbhuvanāni viśvā ‖ 4 ‖

original p. 23

भास्वती । नेत्री । सूनृतानाम् । अचेति । चित्रा । वि । दुरः । नः । आवरित्यावः । प्रऽअर्प्य । जगत् । वि । ऊं इति । नः । रायः । अख्यत् । उषाः । अजीः । भुवनानि । विश्वा ॥ ४ ॥

bhāsvatī | netrī | sūnṛtānām | aceti | citrā | vi | duraḥ | naḥ | āvarityāvaḥ [?] | pra 'arpya | jagat | vi | ūṃ iti | naḥ | rāyaḥ | akhyat | uṣāḥ | ajīḥ | bhuvanāni | viśvā ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.4)

भास्वती विशिष्टप्रकाशयुक्ता । सूनृतेति वाङ्नाम । सूनृतानां वाचां नेत्री प्रेरयित्री । उषसः प्रादुर्भावानन्तरं हि पशुपक्षिमृगादयः सर्वे शब्दं कुर्वन्ति । एवम्भूतोषा अचेति अस्माभिर्ज्ञायि । चित्रा चायनीयो ज्ञाता सा नोऽस्माकं दुरो द्वाराणि तमसा तिरोहितानि व्यावः । व्यवृणोत् । यथास्माभिर्दृश्यन्ते तथा तमो निवार्य प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः । अपि च जगत्सर्वं भुवनं प्रार्प्य प्रकाशं गमयित्वा नोऽस्माकं रायो धनानि व्यख्यत् । विशिष्टप्रकाशयुक्तान्यकरोत् । ऊ इत्येतत्पदपूरणम् । सैषोषा विश्वा भुवनानि सर्वाणि भुवनानि तमसा तिरोहितत्वेनाविद्यमानकल्पान्यजीगः उद्गिरति । स्वमुखान्निर्गमयति स्वकीयेन प्रकाशेन तमो निःसार्य पुनरुत्पन्नानीव करोतीत्यर्थः ॥

bhāsvatī viśiṣṭaprakāśayuktā | sūnṛteti vāṅnāma | sūnṛtānāṃ vācāṃ netrī prerayitrī | uṣasaḥ prādurbhāvānantaraṃ hi paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ sarve śabdaṃ kurvanti | evambhūtoṣā aceti asmābhirjñāyi | citrā cāyanīyo jñātā sā no 'smākaṃ duro dvārāṇi tamasā tirohitāni vyāvaḥ | vyavṛṇot | yathāsmābhirdṛśyante tathā tamo nivārya prakāśayatītyarthaḥ | api ca jagatsarvaṃ bhuvanaṃ prārpya prakāśaṃ gamayitvā no 'smākaṃ rāyo dhanāni vyakhyat | viśiṣṭaprakāśayuktānyakarot | ū ityetatpadapūraṇam | saiṣoṣā viśvā bhuvanāni sarvāṇi bhuvanāni tamasā tirohitatvenāvidyamānakalpānyajīgaḥ udgirati | svamukhānnirgamayati svakīyena prakāśena tamo niḥsārya punarutpannānīva karotītyarthaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "Bhāsvatī — endowed with exceptional light. Sūnṛtā is a name for speech; she is the leader (netrī, impeller) of the sūnṛtās, the speeches; for after the appearance of Uṣas all animals, birds, beasts and the rest make sounds. Such Uṣas acheti — has been known by us. Wonderful (citrā) and worth knowing, she has opened (vyāvaḥ, vyavṛṇot) our doors (duraḥ), covered over by darkness; that is, she shows by dispelling the darkness so that they may be seen by us. Moreover, having spread over the whole world, having sent it light, she has made our riches (rāyaḥ, wealth) shine out: she has made them endowed with distinct light. Ū is a filler. This Uṣas ajīgaḥ — 'brings forth' all the worlds (viśvā bhuvanāni), which, hidden by darkness, were as if non-existent: she draws them out of her own mouth, i.e. having driven out the darkness by her own light, she makes them as if born again."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): netrī (nī "to lead", suffix tṛc, feminine in ṅīp, accent on the ending); acheti (cit in the sense of knowing, aorist passive in ciṇ, with the Vedic irregularities); duraḥ ("dvāra-word replaced by dur in the Vedic accusative plural" — cited by Pā. 6-1-?? [?]); āvaḥ (vṛñ "to cover", aorist in the Vedic luṅ, the sic elided, guṇa; the hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ elision); prārpyā (ṛ "to go"; the augment puk by ṇau …); akhyat (khyā "to tell", the aṅ substitute for cli); ajīgaḥ (gṝ "to swallow"; luṅ with tip, bahulaṃ chandasi — śluṃ elision, doubling, reduplication, lengthening). The Pā. numerals are not clear enough to give.

original p. 24

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"bhāsvatī — the one endowed with light, Uṣas; sūnṛtānām — of speeches; netrī — the begetter; acheti — (by us) she is known; citrā — of various colours, she; naḥ — our; duraḥ — doors covered over with darkness; vi āvaḥ — she opened (an opening); jagat — the whole world; prārpyā — she, having filled with light; naḥ — our; rāyaḥ — wealth; vi akhyat u — made (them) full of light; uṣāḥ — Uṣas; viśvā bhuvanāni — all the world covered by darkness; ajīgaḥ — makes manifest."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Shining Uṣas, who (since beings begin to utter sound with the light of dawn) becomes known to us as the begetter of speech, makes us see doors hidden by darkness, lights up for us our wealth and the rest, and (the world which is covered by darkness and has become as if nonexistent) lights up the whole world."

English Translation (as printed)

Brilliant guide of the speakers of truth, the many-tinted dawn, is recognised by us ; she has opened our doors ; having illuminated the world, she has made our riches manifest. Ushas gives back all the regions (that had been swallowed up by night.)

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

सूनृतानां नेत्री — Sūnṛtānāṃ netrī — "vācāṃ utpādayitrī", the begetter of speech. The word sūnṛtā is stated among the sixteen names of Uṣas (Ni. 3-19 as printed [?]) and among the twenty-eight [?] names of food (Ni. 2-8 as printed [?]). Though it is read among the names of speech (vāṅnāma), it denotes the meaning "speech". The idea is that at Uṣas-time animals, birds and beasts begin to make sounds, so Uṣas produces the power of speech.

अचेति — Acheti — "cetyate jñāyate dṛśyata ity arthaḥ": (it is) perceived, known, seen. "Uṣas gives us the strength of intellect so that we know everything and makes us possessed of the heart of knowledge; she makes everything known (visible) to the eye."

original p. 25

नः दुरः वि आवः — Naḥ duraḥ vi āvaḥ (Skandasvāmin):

सर्वार्थानां दृशां वाग्द्वाराणि नः अस्मभ्यं विवृणोति प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः ।

sarvārthānāṃ dṛśāṃ vāgdvārāṇi naḥ asmabhyaṃ vivṛṇoti prakāśayatītyarthaḥ |

"She opens for us (asmabhyam) the doors of all things — of the eyes and of speech — i.e. she makes them manifest." The sense is: "At Uṣas-time she so makes it that the power of perceiving objects and the power of speech and of carrying on affairs become manifest, by removing the darkness."

प्रार्प्य रायः अख्यत् विश्वा अजीगः — Prārpya rāyaḥ akhyat viśvā ajīgaḥ (Skandasvāmin):

तेषु तेषु व्यापारेषु कृत्स्नं जगत् प्रवर्त्य । विविधं ख्यापितवती । जगर्तिरत्र सामर्थ्यात् गत्यर्थः । यो वां दूतो न धिष्ण्ये (ऋ. सं. २-६२-१ [?]) इति यथा ॥

teṣu teṣu vyāpāreṣu kṛtsnaṃ jagat pravartya | vividhaṃ khyāpitavatī | jagartiratra sāmarthyāt gatyarthaḥ | yo vāṃ dūto na dhiṣṇye (ṛ. saṃ. 2-62-1 [?]) iti yathā ‖

"Having set the whole world going in these and those activities, she made known the manifold. The root jāgṛ here, by capacity, has the sense of 'going' — as in 'yo vāṃ dūto na dhiṣṇye' (the Ṛk cited as in the print; its reference is doubtful [?])." Kannada: "Uṣas, as the setting going of all the world in the work it has to perform, makes the variety of the world manifest: ajīgaḥ (the root) jāgṛ here, by capacity, means 'going'. — Uṣas gives light to those worlds, all of which, covered by darkness, were as if without cause (asatkalpa, 'as if non-existent'), and brings them to life again as if re-born by her own light. She also gives light in our understanding so that we know the ways in which wealth is obtained. This is the purport of Skandasvāmin's explanation: that Uṣas, who does such service to the whole world, acts of herself everywhere, by herself."

Grammar page on bhāsvatī (bhās + matup, ma → va by mādupadhāyāś ca…; feminine ṅīp since the suffix is ugit), netrī (ṇīñ "to lead", initial ṇ → n; tṛc in the agent sense; guṇa; ṅīp; the yaṇ substitution in the udātta position; accent by udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt), acheti (cit "to know", aorist, 3rd singular ta; ciṇ by ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ; guṇa; elision of ta by ciṇo luk; augment). Grammar page continued: duraḥ (the word dvār, dur for the Vedic accusative plural with saṃprasāraṇa by rayer mṛtau bahulam…; accusative plural); āvaḥ (vṛñ "to cover", aorist luṅ, tip; elision of i by itaś ca; cli, sic elided by mantre ghasa-hvara…; guṇa; ur — raparaḥ; tip elided after the consonant-ending by hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ…; no augment by chandasy api…; the visarga); prārpyā (ṛ "to go", ṇic; the puk augment; the suffix lyap in the compound with pra — samāse 'nañpūrve ktvo lyap; elision of the ṇi; lengthening in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate); rāyaḥ (accent of the ending by ūḍidaṃpadādi…); akhyat (khyā "to tell", aorist, tip; cli → aṅ by asti-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ; elision of the root's ā by āto lopa iṭi ca; augment); ajīgaḥ (gṝ "to swallow", aorist 3rd singular with tip; as before elision of i; śluṃ in place of śnā by bahulaṃ chandasi; doubling and ut by ṛta ut; reduplication, a → i…; lengthening of the root vowel by Vedic usage).

जिह्मश्ये चरितवे मघोन्याभोगय इष्टये राय उ त्वम् । दभ्रं पश्यद्भ्य उर्विया विचक्ष उषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ ५ ॥

jihmaśye caritave maghonyābhogaya iṣṭaye rāya u tvam | dabhraṃ paśyadbhya urviyā vicakṣa uṣā ajīgarbhuvanāni viśvā ‖ 5 ‖

jihma 'śye | caritave | maghonī | ā 'bhogaye | iṣṭaye | rāye | ūṃ iti | tvam | dabhram | paśyat 'bhyaḥ | urviyā | vi 'cakṣe | uṣāḥ | ajīḥ | bhuvanāni | viśvā ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.5)

मघोनीत्युषसो नामधेयम् । मघोनी धनवत्युषा जिह्मश्ये जिह्मं वक्रं शयानाय पुरुषाय चरितवे चरितुं शयनादुत्थाय स्वापेक्षितं प्रति गन्तुं वृच्छन्ती भवति । त्वम् । अयमेकशब्दपर्यायः सर्वनामशब्दः [?] । यदाह । त्वे इति विग्रहार्थीयं सर्वनामानुदात्तम् [?] । नि. १-२ । इति । त्वमेकं प्रति आभोगये आभोगाय शब्दादिविषयार्थम् । तथापरं प्रति इष्टये यागार्थम् । तथान्यं प्रति राये धनार्थं च वृच्छन्तीति शेषः । उ शब्दः पादपूरणार्थः [?] । अपि च दभ्रमल्पं पश्यद्भ्योऽन्धकारावृतत्वेनेषद्दृष्टिभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यो विचक्षे विशिष्टप्रकाशाय वृच्छन्ती उर्विया उर्वी विस्तीर्णोषा सर्वाणि भूतजातानि तमसा तिरोहितानि प्रकाशदानेनोद्गीर्णानीव करोति ॥

maghonītyuṣaso nāmadheyam | maghonī dhanavatyuṣā jihmaśye jihmaṃ vakraṃ śayānāya puruṣāya caritave carituṃ śayanādutthāya svāpekṣitaṃ prati gantuṃ vṛcchantī bhavati | tvam | ayamekaśabdaparyāyaḥ sarvanāmaśabdaḥ [?] | yadāha | tve iti vigrahārthīyaṃ sarvanāmānudāttam [?] | ni. 1-2 | iti | tvamekaṃ prati ābhogaye ābhogāya śabdādiviṣayārtham | tathāparaṃ prati iṣṭaye yāgārtham | tathānyaṃ prati rāye dhanārthaṃ ca vṛcchantīti śeṣaḥ | u śabdaḥ pādapūraṇārthaḥ [?] | api ca dabhramalpaṃ paśyadbhyo 'ndhakārāvṛtatveneṣaddṛṣṭibhyo manuṣyebhyo vicakṣe viśiṣṭaprakāśāya vṛcchantī urviyā urvī vistīrṇoṣā sarvāṇi bhūtajātāni tamasā tirohitāni prakāśadānenodgīrṇānīva karoti ‖

Sense (mine): "Maghonī is a name of Uṣas: the wealthy Uṣas, to the man lying curled up (jihmaśye, 'crooked-lying'), to move about (caritave), rising from sleep to go toward what each requires, is appearing (vṛcchantī). Tvam — [the Nirukta: the pronoun, a synonym of 'one'] — to one person, for ābhogaya, 'enjoyment', i.e. for the objects of sound and so on; to another, for iṣṭaye, for sacrifice; to yet another, for rāye, wealth — she appears, is the ellipsis. U is a filler [?]. Moreover, to men who see a little (dabhram), seeing but slightly because covered by darkness — for their vicakṣe, 'clear seeing' — Uṣas, wide (urviyā, urvī, 'broad'), appears; she makes all living beings that were hidden by darkness appear as if they had been drawn out, by the giving of light."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): jihmaśye (jihmam śete — the compound jihma-śī, with the kvip, the accent of the later member by kṛdutta-pada-prakṛti-svaratva; yaṇ — the dative singular in Vedic ṅe → e with the svarita); ābhogaye (the Vedic dative with ya); urviyā (uru with the Vedic ī-feminine in kvip bāhulaka; Pā. 6-4-?? [?]); vicakṣe (cakṣiṅ "to speak", vi; ṅe → e in the infinitive sense by kṛtyārthe… [?]).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"maghonī — the generous (Uṣas); jihmaśye — (to) the man sleeping curled up; caritave — to rise and go about (helping); tvam — to one; ā bhogaye — for the sake of (sensual) enjoyment; iṣṭaye — for performing sacrifice [(tvam —) to another]; rāye — for wealth [(to) another]; dabhram — dimly (because of darkness); paśyadbhyaḥ — to those who see; vicakṣe — for seeing well; uṣāḥ — Uṣas; viśvā bhuvanāni — the whole world; ajīgaḥ — makes manifest."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Uṣas rouses the men who lie curled up asleep and sets each upon his task — one to sensual enjoyment, one to the acquisition of wealth, and another to sacrifice and the like. Objects seen only faintly she makes seen plainly; and the whole world, covered by darkness, she makes plain by her light."

original p. 29

English Translation (as printed)

The opulent (dawn) arouses to exertion the man bowed down in sleep,—one man to enjoyments, another to devotion, another to (the acquirement of) wealth ; she has enabled those who were almost sightless to see distinctly. The expansive Ushas has given back all the regions.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

मघोनी — Maghonī — "dhanavatī uṣāḥ": the word magha, among the twenty-eight [?] names of wealth beginning with dhana (Ni. 2-10 as printed [?]), is stated; so magha means wealth. "Because she has wealth, 'dhanavatī uṣāḥ'," Sāyaṇa says. In the mantra "nūnaṃ sā te prati varaṃ jaritre duhīyad indra dakṣiṇā maghonī" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-21 as read on the clearer printing of the same Ṛk on p. 38; the first reading "3-11-3?" on p. 29 was unclear) too, for the word maghonī Yāska explains (Ni. 1-7 as printed [?]): "magham iti dhananāmadheyaṃ maṃhater dānakarmaṇaḥ" ("magha is a name for wealth, from maṃh, giving"). The word magha is stated among the sixteen names of Uṣas (Ni. 3-19 as printed [?]).

जिह्मश्ये चरितवे — Jihmaśye caritave: "jihmaṃ śete iti jihmaśīḥ": the word jihma means "crooked". He who lies curled up by throwing his hands and feet is jihmaśī. Thus Uṣas creates enthusiasm, so that a desire arises that the man who is lying curled up, from laziness, should go about.

त्वम् — Tvam. "ayam eka-śabda-paryāyaḥ sarvanāma-śabdaḥ" and "yadāha — tve iti vigrahārthīyaṃ sarvanāmānudāttam" (Ni. 1-9 as printed [?]): "tva is a word that is a synonym of 'one'. It belongs to the group of pronouns (sarvanāman). It has the anudātta accent." "ardhanāmety eke" — some think that this word denotes "half portion"; "nipāta ity eke" — some say that the word tva is an indeclinable particle (nipāta). The Ṛk:

ऋचां त्वः पोषमास्ते पुपुष्वान् गायत्रं त्वो गायति शक्वरीषु । ब्रह्मा त्वो वदति जातविद्यां यज्ञस्य मात्रां वि मिमीत उ त्वः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-७१-११)

ṛcāṃ tvaḥ poṣamāste pupuṣvān gāyatraṃ tvo gāyati śakvarīṣu | brahmā tvo vadati jātavidyāṃ yajñasya mātrāṃ vi mimīta u tvaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-71-11)

— "Here the word tvaḥ is used in the sense of 'one'. Therefore Uṣas, who herself performs all kinds of work at once, gives enthusiasm to one who is lying curled up by habit to go about, to one so that he may enjoy [objects of sense], to another so that she may produce in him a desire for sacrifice, and another she sets at once to the sacrifice. The dhaniṣṭha (rich man) becomes active in gathering the wealth he needs. In this way Uṣas pervades all, fulfilling the intentions of the people — this is the sense."

original p. 30

दभ्रं पश्यद्भ्यः उर्विया विचक्षे — Dabhraṃ paśyadbhyaḥ urviyā vicakṣe. Yāska explains the meaning of the word dabhra as "small" and cites the Ṛk "upopa me parā mṛśa mā me dabhrāṇi manyathāḥ" as an example:

दभ्रं पश्यद्भ्यः उर्विया विचक्षे दभ्रमल्पम् । दभ्रमर्भकमित्यल्पस्य । दभ्नोतेः सुदम्भं भवति । उपोप मे परा मृश मा मे दभ्राणि मन्यथाः । सर्वाहमस्मि रोमशा गान्धारीणामिवाविका ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१२६-७ [as read]) (नि. ३-३० [?])

dabhraṃ paśyadbhyaḥ urviyā vicakṣe dabhramalpam | dabhramarbhakamityalpasya | dabhnoteḥ sudambhaṃ bhavati | upopa me parā mṛśa mā me dabhrāṇi manyathāḥ | sarvāhamasmi romaśā gāndhārīṇāmivāvikā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-126-7 [as read]) (ni. 3-30 [?])

"Therefore dabhra means 'small'. When, because of the darkness, the true nature of things is not understood properly, the objects appear as small in size. Thus the world, covered by darkness, which appears small in size, Uṣas makes great by her light and reveals its real condition."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on jihmaśye (śīṅ "to lie"; jihmaṃ śete → jihmaśī; the suffix kvip by kvip ca; the first-member accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; the dative singular ṅe, yaṇ by eranekācaḥ [as printed]; the svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ), caritave (car "to move", infinitive suffix tavai [for tumun] by tumarthe sesesen…; augment iḍ; jñityādir nityam accent on the first syllable; indeclinable by kṛnmejantaḥ), ābhogaye (ābhoga with the dative singular ṅe → ya by Vedic yaka-augment; or ā + bhuj "to protect, enjoy" with kvip by uṇādayo bahulam; the change of j to g; ābhogī; guṇa; ay-substitution; first-member accent in the compound). Sūtra numbers small; I give none beyond those marked "as printed".

original p. 31

Grammar page of Ṛk 5, concluded (noted briefly): iṣṭaye (iṣu "to wish", the suffix ktic by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām, Pā. 3-3-174 as read [?]; dative singular), rāye (ūḍidaṃpadādi… accent on the ending), paśyadbhyaḥ (dṛś "to see", śatṛ; paśya substitution by pāghrādhmā…, Pā. 7-3-78 as read [?]; śap is pit, the root accent remains), urviyā (urvī + su, with iyaṅ by the Vārttika iyāḍiyājīkārāṇām upasaṃkhyānam; elision of the feminine ending; accent on the last syllable since cit), vicakṣe (vi + cakṣiṅ "to speak clearly"; kvip by sampadādibhyaḥ kvip; accent of the first member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt), viśvā (śi of the neuter plural replaced by ā by śeś chandasi bahulam). ‖ 5 ‖

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.6)

क्षत्राय त्वं श्रवसे त्वं महीया इष्टये त्वमर्थमिव त्वमित्यै । विसदृशा जीविताभिप्रचक्ष उषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ ६ ॥

kṣatrāya tvaṃ śravase tvaṃ mahīyā iṣṭaye tvamarthamiva tvamityai | visadṛśā jīvitābhipracakṣa uṣā ajīgarbhuvanāni viśvā ‖ 6 ‖

original p. 32

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.6)

क्षत्राय । त्वम् । श्रवसे । त्वम् । महीयै । इष्टये । त्वम् । अर्थम्ऽइव । त्वम् । इत्यै । विऽसदृशा । जीविता । अभिऽप्रचक्षे । उषाः । अजीगः । भुवनानि । विश्वा ॥ ६ ॥

kṣatrāya | tvam | śravase | tvam | mahīyai | iṣṭaye | tvam | artham 'iva | tvam | ityai | vi 'sadṛśā | jīvitā | abhi 'pracakṣe | uṣāḥ | ajīgaḥ | bhuvanāni | viśvā ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.6)

क्षत्राय । धननामैतत् । धनार्थं त्वमेकं प्रत्युषा वृच्छन्तीति शेषः । तथा श्रवसेऽन्नार्थं त्वमेकं प्रति । महीयै महत्यै इष्टये अग्निष्टोमादिमहायज्ञार्थं त्वमेकं प्रति वृच्छन्ति । तथार्थमिवापेक्षितमर्थं प्रतीत्यै गमनार्थं त्वमेकं प्रति वृच्छन्ति । अपि च विसदृशा विलक्षणानि नानारूपाणि जीविता जीवितानि जीवनोपायभूतानि कृषिवाणिज्यादीन्यभिप्रचक्षे अभिमुख्येन प्रकाशयितुं वृच्छन्त्युषाः सर्वाणि भूतजातानि तमसा निगीर्णान्यजीगः प्रकाशनेनोद्गीर्णानीवाकरोत् ॥

kṣatrāya | dhananāmaitat | dhanārthaṃ tvamekaṃ pratyuṣā vṛcchantīti śeṣaḥ | tathā śravase 'nnārthaṃ tvamekaṃ prati | mahīyai mahatyai iṣṭaye agniṣṭomādimahāyajñārthaṃ tvamekaṃ prati vṛcchanti | tathārthamivāpekṣitamarthaṃ pratītyai gamanārthaṃ tvamekaṃ prati vṛcchanti | api ca visadṛśā vilakṣaṇāni nānārūpāṇi jīvitā jīvitāni jīvanopāyabhūtāni kṛṣivāṇijyādīnyabhipracakṣe abhimukhyena prakāśayituṃ vṛcchantyuṣāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtajātāni tamasā nigīrṇānyajīgaḥ prakāśanenodgīrṇānīvākarot ‖

Sense (mine): "Kṣatra — a name for wealth: Uṣas appears (vṛcchanti) for the sake of wealth to the one (man); so for śravas (food) to the one; for the mahīyai iṣṭaye — the great sacrifice, the Agniṣṭoma and the like — to the one; and for arthamiva, 'for the sake of the thing wanted', for ityai, to go, to the one. Moreover, to show forth (abhipracakṣe) in front the viṣadṛśā jīvitā, the various forms of livelihood — agriculture, trade and the rest — Uṣas appears; all beings hidden (swallowed) by darkness she brings out, as if vomited out (ajīgaḥ), by giving light."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): tvam (a pronoun-word, wholly unaccented by the Phiṭ-sūtra 4-10 as cited [?]); mahīyai (from mahī, the dative in īyai by the elongation chāndasa; or the yāṭ augment — Pā. 7-3-113 as read [?]); visadṛśā (dṛś with kvin by the Vārttika; samānasya chandasi — sa for samāna; the Vedic elision of śi; accent of the first member); abhipracakṣe (cakṣ in the sense of the infinitive with sen; elision of k by skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca).

original p. 33

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"tvam — one man; kṣatrāya — for wealth; tvam — another; śravase — for food; tvam — another; mahīyai — for great (such as the Agniṣṭoma); iṣṭaye — for sacrifices; tvam — another; arthamiva — [turning] towards the desired object; ityai — for going out; visadṛśā — of various kinds; jīvitā — the efforts; abhipracakṣe — for making them shine well (inciting); uṣāḥ — Uṣas; viśvā bhuvanāni — the whole world (covered by darkness); ajīgaḥ — again makes manifest."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Uṣas, inciting people to take up their various efforts for the sake of wealth, food, sacrifices and other desired objects, and their means, makes the whole world (which, covered with darkness, was nearly lost) manifest."

English Translation (as printed)

The dawn rouses one man to acquire wealth, another to earn food, another to achieve greatness, another to sacrifices, another to his own (persuits [sic]), another to activity, and lights all men to their various means of maintaining life. Ushas has given back all the regions.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

क्षत्राय — Kṣatrāya. "Because magham, reknaḥ … are stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 as read [?]), the word kṣatra denotes wealth: 'in order to obtain wealth' is the sense."

श्रवसे — Śravase. "The word śravas is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 as read [?]), so it denotes wealth. This word is used also in the meaning 'fame' or 'glory' (kīrti), and in the meaning 'food' (anna).

प्र वो महे मन्दमानायान्धसोऽर्चा विश्वानराय विश्वाभुवे । इन्द्रस्य यस्य सुमखं सहो महि श्रवो नृम्णं च रोदसी सपर्यतः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-५०-१ [as read])

pra vo mahe mandamānāyāndhaso 'rcā viśvānarāya viśvābhuve | indrasya yasya sumakhaṃ saho mahi śravo nṛmṇaṃ ca rodasī saparyataḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-50-1 [as read])

original p. 34

— in this Ṛk, "mahac chravaṇīyaṃ yaśaḥ" (Ni. 11-10 as read [?]): the word śravas denotes fame.

अमन्दान्स्तोमान्प्र भरे मनीषा सिन्धावधि क्षियतो भाव्यस्य । यो मे सहस्रममिमीत सवानतूर्तो राजा श्रव इच्छमानः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१२६-१ [as read])

amandānstomānpra bhare manīṣā sindhāvadhi kṣiyato bhāvyasya | yo me sahasramamimīta savānatūrto rājā śrava icchamānaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-126-1 [as read])

Here also "śravaḥ praśaṃsām icchamānaḥ" (Ni. 9-11 as read [?]): the word śravas denotes fame.

उत स्मैनं वस्त्रमथिं न तायुमनु क्रोशन्ति क्षितयो भरेषु । नीचायमानं जसुरिं न श्येनं श्रवश्चाच्छा पशुमच्च यूथम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-३८-५ [as read])

uta smainaṃ vastramathiṃ na tāyumanu krośanti kṣitayo bhareṣu | nīcāyamānaṃ jasuriṃ na śyenaṃ śravaścācchā paśumacca yūtham ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-38-5 [as read])

Here too: "śravaś cācchā paśumac ca yūtham — śravaś cāpi paśumac ca yūtham praśaṃsāṃ ca" (Ni. 4-31 as read [?]): the word śravas denotes fame.

आसस्राणासः शवसानमच्छेन्द्रं सुचक्रे रथ्यासो अश्वाः । अभि श्रव ऋजुम्यन्तो वहेयुर्नू चिन्नु वायोरमृतं वि दस्येत् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-३७-३ [as read; numerals small])

āsasrāṇāsaḥ śavasānamacchendraṃ sucakre rathyāso aśvāḥ | abhi śrava ṛjumyanto vaheyurnū cinnu vāyoramṛtaṃ vi dasyet ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 6-37-3 [as read; numerals small])

Here "śrava ity annanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ vāyoḥ śāstraṃ bhakṣako na vidasyed iti" (Ni. 10-6 as read [?]): the word śravas has the meaning "food". "From these examples there are many meanings for the word śravas; Sāyaṇa explained the meaning 'for the sake of food'."

विसदृशा — Visadṛśā — "vigatasādṛśyāni, vilakṣaṇāni nānārūpāṇi" (devoid of likeness, unlike, of many forms): "As soon as Uṣas-time comes, the one who earns wealth, the one who labours for food, the one who performs great sacrifices, the one who aspires to accomplish desires of many kinds, and the one who achieves the means of livelihood — in all of these, enthusiasm and knowledge arise. This is by Uṣas's power: she awakens all the worlds. When morning comes and it is light, people become engaged in the various works of each. All of this is the power of Uṣas — such is the intention."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page, begun: kṣatrāya (an underived stem, the name of wealth; accent on the final syllable by Phiṭ-sūtra 1 "phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ"), tvam (the stem yuṣmad, am for su; tva substituted [for the whole of tvam]; elision by śeṣe lopaḥ; wholly unaccented by Phiṭ 4-10 "tva sama sima…" as read [?]). Continues on the next page.

original p. 35

Grammar page of Ṛk 6, continued (noted briefly): śravase (śru "to hear"; the suffix asun; guṇa of u; av; dative singular); mahīyai (the form to be mahyai: mah "to honour"; the suffix iṅ(?) added to all roots — Uṇ. sūtra, number as read "4-???" [?]; giving the stem mahī; in the feminine, with ṅīṣ by kṛdikārād aktinaḥ [as printed]; the āṭ augment before the dative ending; vṛddhi; Vedic insertion of ī; the yaṇ substitution with the accent on the ending by udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt; or, with the ending after mahī changed by vyatyayo bahulam and yāḍ-āpaḥ, with the Vedic final-accent); artham (ṛ "to go", the suffix thak[?]; guṇa; raparatva; accent on the first syllable since the suffix is pit; accusative singular); ityai (iṇ "to go", adādi; ktin in the feminine and the abstract sense by striyāṃ ktin; final accent by vyatyaya; or ktic; as before the ending's accent by udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt); visadṛśā (dṛś in the tṛdādi group takes kañ by the Vārttika; with samāna in the first member by samānasya chandasy amūrdha…; the neuter plural śi replaced by ā by śeś chandasi bahulam; bahuvrīhi — first-member accent; "in the same way jīvitāni becomes jīvitā").

original p. 36

Grammar page, concluded: abhipracakṣe (abhi; cakṣiṅ "to speak clearly", a root with several senses, here used in the sense of "to shine"; the infinitive in se by tumarthe sesen…; elision of k by skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca; ṣatva by ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si; the ṣa from the suffix by the change of s; indeclinable by kṛn mejantaḥ). ‖ 6 ‖

एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि व्युच्छन्ती युवतिः शुक्रवासाः । विश्वस्येशाना पार्थिवस्य वस्व उषो अद्येह सुभगे व्युच्छ ॥ ७ ॥

eṣā | divaḥ | duhitā | prati | adarśi | vi 'ucchantī | yuvatiḥ | śukra 'vāsāḥ | viśvasya | īśānā | pārthivasya | vasvaḥ | uṣaḥ | adya | iha | su 'bhage | vi | uccha ‖ 7 ‖

original p. 37

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.7)

दिवो दुहिता व्योम्नो दुहितृस्थानीया । तस्य हि पूर्वार्धे उषा उत्पद्यते । सैषा व्युच्छन्ती तमो वर्जयन्ती प्रत्यदर्शि सर्वैः प्राणिभिर्दृष्टाभूत् । कीदृशी सा । युवतिर्योवयित्री फलानां पुरुषैः प्रापयित्री नित्ययौवनोपेता वा शुक्रवासाः श्वेतवसना निर्मलदीप्तिर्वा तथा विश्वस्य सर्वस्य पार्थिवस्य पृथिव्याः संबन्धिनो वस्वो धनस्येशानेश्वरी । हे सुभगे शोभनधने उषः तादृशी त्वमद्यास्मिन्काले इहास्मिन्देवयजनदेशे व्युच्छ । तमांसि विवासय । वर्जयेत्यर्थः ॥

divo duhitā vyomno duhitṛsthānīyā | tasya hi pūrvārdhe uṣā utpadyate | saiṣā vyucchantī tamo varjayantī pratyadarśi sarvaiḥ prāṇibhirdṛṣṭābhūt | kīdṛśī sā | yuvatiryovayitrī phalānāṃ puruṣaiḥ prāpayitrī nityayauvanopetā vā śukravāsāḥ śvetavasanā nirmaladīptirvā tathā viśvasya sarvasya pārthivasya pṛthivyāḥ saṃbandhino vasvo dhanasyeśāneśvarī | he subhage śobhanadhane uṣaḥ tādṛśī tvamadyāsminkāle ihāsmindevayajanadeśe vyuccha | tamāṃsi vivāsaya | varjayetyarthaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "Divo duhitā — like a daughter of the sky (vyoman); for in the eastern part of it Uṣas is born. This Uṣas, dispelling (vyucchantī) the darkness, pratyadarśi — has come into view of all beings. What is she like? Yuvatiḥ — she who unites (yāvayitrī) men with the fruits [of their works], or one with ever-fresh youth; śukravāsāḥ — white-robed, or of spotless splendour; and īśānā — the mistress — of all (viśvasya) earthly (pārthivasya) wealth (vasvaḥ). O subhage, possessed of fine wealth, Uṣas, such as thou art, to-day, here, in this place of sacrifice, vyuccha — dispel the darkness, drive it away, is the sense."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): divaḥ (the accent of the ending by the rule ūḍidam…); vyucchantī (uchi "to depart, dispel", tudādi; viv-āsa "driving away"); yuvatiḥ (the feminine of yūn by the Pāṇinian yūnas ti, number as read "4-1-77" [?]); śukravāsāḥ (vas "to cover"; "vaste sarvam ācchādayatīti" — the light is the vāsas; bahuvrīhi, first-member accent); īśānā (īś "to be master", adādi, the elision of śap; the root accent as the ending is anudāttet); pārthivasya (from pṛthivī, the suffix añ); vasvaḥ (gender change: genitive singular used for a feminine; the substitute of yaṇ for the elided jas ending in Vedic — "ṣaṣṭhyāḥ jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam").

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yuvatiḥ — one who gets men the results [of works]; or one ever-youthful; śukravāsāḥ — wearer of a white garment, or endowed with pure splendour; viśvasya — of all; pārthivasya — connected with the earth; vasvaḥ — of wealth; īśānā — the mistress; divo duhitā — the daughter of the atmosphere; eṣā — this Uṣas; vyucchantī — warding off the darkness; pratyadarśi — has come into the sight of beings; subhage — O possessor of auspicious wealth; uṣaḥ — O Uṣas, goddess! (now); adya — now; iha — in this sacrifice; vyuccha — drive away the darkness."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The goddess Uṣas, of spotless splendour, ever youthful, mistress of all wealth connected with the earth, like a daughter to the atmosphere, appears to everyone as a dispeller of darkness. O such Uṣas deity, here, in this sacrificial hall, now drive away the darkness."

original p. 38

English Translation (as printed)

The daughter of heaven, young, white-robed, the mistress of all earthly treasure, is beheld dissipating the darkness. Auspicious Ushas, shine upon us to-day in this (hall of sacrifice.)

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

दिवो दुहिता — Divo duhitā — "vyomno duhitṛsthānīyā": "the goddess Uṣas is constantly full of light and is the daughter of heaven (svarga). The meaning of the word duhitṛ: Yāska explains (Ni. 3-4 as read [?]) 'duhitā durhitā dūre hitā dogdhir vā': the woman who, being given in gift to a man, brings sorrow and also benefit to him; or, one who, though always living far from her father and mother, desires their welfare, therefore gets the name duhitā. As heaven is full of light, Uṣas, which is born from the eastern part of heaven, also illumines the other objects and gives beings a light in the form of knowledge, so she is called heaven's daughter — thus they explain."

शुक्रवासाः — Śukravāsāḥ:

वस्ते सर्वमाच्छादयतीति प्रकाशो वासः । श्वेतवसना निर्मलदीप्तिर्वा ॥

vaste sarvamācchādayatīti prakāśo vāsaḥ | śvetavasanā nirmaladīptirvā ‖

"The garment (vāsa) that covers everything is the light (prakāśa): hence, because everything is covered by it — the word vāsaḥ means 'a garment worn'. Because Uṣas has an exceedingly pure lustre, with no spot, she is said to be white-robed, or to have pure splendour — so it is described here."

युवतिः — Yuvatiḥ:

यावयित्री फलानां पुरुषैः प्रापयित्री । नित्ययौवनोपेता वा ॥

yāvayitrī phalānāṃ puruṣaiḥ prāpayitrī | nityayauvanopetā vā ‖

"One who makes men obtain the fruits (or purposes), or one who is always joined with youth: the meaning is 'one who is always young'."

सुभगे — Subhage — "śobhanadhanavatī": one who possesses excellent wealth. The word bhaga is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 as read [?]).

नूनं सा ते प्रति वरं जरित्रे दुहीयदिन्द्र दक्षिणा मघोनी । शिक्षा स्तोतृभ्यो माति धग्भगो नो बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥ (ऋ. सं. २-११-२१ [as read])

nūnaṃ sā te prati varaṃ jaritre duhīyadindra dakṣiṇā maghonī | śikṣā stotṛbhyo māti dhagbhago no bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 2-11-21 [as read])

original p. 39

"Here, in 'bhago naḥ' ('dhanaṃ no 'stu', 'may wealth be ours'), they give for the word bhaga the meaning 'wealth'. The word bhaga conveys the meanings Sūrya, dharma, wealth, woman, and avayava ('limb, part'). Here, accepting the sense 'wealth', they explain it."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on divaḥ (accent of the ending by ūḍidaṃpadādi…), adarśi (dṛś "to see", aorist luṅ 3rd singular ta; ciṇ in place of cli by ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ; guṇa of the penultimate; elision of ta by ciṇo luk; augment aṭ; tiṅ-nighāta accent), vyucchantī (uchī "to depart", tudādi; vivāsa "driving away"; śatṛ; the tuk augment by chaṃ ca [Pā. śe ca?]; ḍī — ugitaś ca — with num; the śa class-sign accent on the śa; compound with the prefix vi, first-member accent), yuvatiḥ (yūn + ti in the feminine by yūnas ti; the stem designation sv-ādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne; n-elision by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; final accent from the suffix), śukravāsāḥ (vas "to cover", ghañ; guṇa/vṛddhi of the penultimate by ata upadhāyāḥ; "śukraṃ vāsaḥ yasya saḥ" — bahuvrīhi, first-member accent), īśānā (īś "to be lord", adādi; śānac; elision of śap by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; feminine ṭāp by ajādyatas ṭāp; root-accent retained because anudāttet; accent by tāsyanudāttet…; nominative singular). Sūtra numbers small; I give none beyond.

original p. 40

Grammar page, concluded: pārthivasya (pṛthivyāḥ idam — the suffix añ by pṛthivyā ñāñau, Pā. 4-1-?? [?]; the vṛddhi taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ; jñityādir nityam — first-syllable accent; genitive singular); vasvaḥ (vasu — a word that in the Vedic usage is neuter, by vyatyayo bahulam made masculine; guṇa on the genitive ending ṅas is prevented by jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam, since it is optional; yaṇ substituted); subhage (śobhanaṃ bhagaṃ yasyāḥ sā; the vocative with nighāta by āmantritasya ca); vyuccha (uchī "to depart"; loṭ 2nd singular, the elision of hi by ato heḥ; nighāta after an accented word). ‖ 7 ‖
