॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.8)

परायतीनामन्वेति पाथ आयतीनां प्रथमा शश्वतीनाम् । व्युच्छन्ती जीवमुदीरयन्त्युषा मृतं कं चन बोधयन्ती ॥ ८ ॥

parāyatīnāmanveti pātha āyatīnāṃ prathamā śaśvatīnām | vyucchantī jīvamudīrayantyuṣā mṛtaṃ kaṃ cana bodhayantī ‖ 8 ‖

original p. 41

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.8) Reading note after viewing the Pada: the first Pada-word is printed with a lengthened-vowel mark, as parā-yatīnām with the avagraha, written परा३यतीनाम् in the print's manner; the Saṃhitā's ityuṣā is the Pada's uṣāḥ; the Saṃhitā's kaṃ cana stays as two words.

परा३यतीनाम् । अनु । एति । पाथः । आऽयतीनाम् । प्रथमा । शश्वतीनाम् । विऽउच्छन्ती । जीवम् । उत्ऽईरयन्ती । उषाः । मृतम् । कम् । चन । बोधयन्ती ॥ ८ ॥

parā3yatīnām | anu | eti | pāthaḥ | ā 'yatīnām | prathamā | śaśvatīnām | vi 'ucchantī | jīvam | ut 'īrayantī | uṣāḥ | mṛtam | kam | cana | bodhayantī ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.8)

परायतीनां परागच्छन्तीनामतीतानामुषसां सम्बन्धि पाथोऽन्तरिक्षैकदेशलक्षणं स्थानम् । पाथोऽन्तरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यातम् । नि. ६-७ [?] इति यास्कः । अद्यतन्युषा अन्वेति । अनुगच्छति । अतीता उषसो यथा व्युष्टा एवमेवैषापि व्युच्छतीत्यर्थः । तथायतीनामागच्छन्तीनां शश्वतीनां बह्वीनामुषसां प्रथमाद्या भवति । एषा यथा वर्तते एवमेवागामिन्योऽप्युषस इत्यर्थः । तादृशी व्युच्छन्ती तमो वर्जयन्ती जीवं प्राणिनां जीवात्मानमुदीरयन्त्युषा मृतं स्वापसमये प्रलीनेन्द्रियत्वान्मृतमिव सन्तं कं चन कमपि पुरुषं बोधयन्ती पुनरिन्द्रियप्रवेशेन चेतनं कुर्वती प्रवर्तते इति शेषः ॥

parāyatīnāṃ parāgacchantīnāmatītānāmuṣasāṃ sambandhi pātho 'ntarikṣaikadeśalakṣaṇaṃ sthānam | pātho 'ntarikṣaṃ pathā vyākhyātam | ni. 6-7 [?] iti yāskaḥ | adyatanyuṣā anveti | anugacchati | atītā uṣaso yathā vyuṣṭā evamevaiṣāpi vyucchatītyarthaḥ | tathāyatīnāmāgacchantīnāṃ śaśvatīnāṃ bahvīnāmuṣasāṃ prathamādyā bhavati | eṣā yathā vartate evamevāgāminyo 'pyuṣasa ityarthaḥ | tādṛśī vyucchantī tamo varjayantī jīvaṃ prāṇināṃ jīvātmānamudīrayantyuṣā mṛtaṃ svāpasamaye pralīnendriyatvānmṛtamiva santaṃ kaṃ cana kamapi puruṣaṃ bodhayantī punarindriyapraveśena cetanaṃ kurvatī pravartate iti śeṣaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "Parāyatīnām — of the Uṣases that have gone away, the past ones — their pātha, the place that is a portion of the atmosphere. Pātha = atmosphere, explained under pathā (Ni. 6-7 [?]), says Yāska. The present Uṣas follows (anveti) it: as the past Uṣases have shone, so this one shines too. Likewise she is prathamā, the first, of the āyatīnām, the coming, śaśvatīnām, many Uṣases: as she is, so also the Uṣases to come will be. Such Uṣas, dispelling darkness, jīvam udīrayantī, rousing the jīva, the living self of creatures, mṛtam, those who, at the time of sleep, with their senses dissolved, are as if dead — kaṃ cana, any man whatever — bodhayantī, waking, making conscious again by the entering of the senses, she proceeds."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): parāyatīnām (iṇ "to go", the participle śatṛ in the laṭ sense; yaṇ for iṇ; feminine ṅīp by ugitaś ca; the genitive plural nām accented on the first syllable by the Vedic rule jyāṃ chandasi bahulam).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"uṣāḥ — Uṣas; parāyatīnām — of the Uṣases of the past; pāthaḥ — the path; anveti — follows; āyatīnām — of those that come hereafter; śaśvatīnām — of the countless Uṣases; prathamā — becomes the first; vyucchantī — Uṣas who drives out darkness; mṛtam — (being sleepless) as if dead; kaṃ cana jīvam — any person (or creature); udīrayantī — rousing with warmth; bodhayantī — making (him) one with awakened senses."

original p. 42

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The present Uṣas follows the path of the many past Uṣases (that is, she too, like them, is a dispeller of darkness) and is the first of the countless Uṣases that are to come (those to come hereafter will also be, like her, dispellers of darkness); driving out the darkness, Uṣas rouses living beings with warmth (those who in the state of sleep are as if dead), and gives consciousness to each one."

English Translation (as printed)

Following the path of the mornings that have passed, and first of the endless mornings that are to come, Ushas, the disperser of darkness, arouses living beings, and awakens every one (that lay) as dead.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

परायतीनां पाथः — Parāyatīnāṃ pāthaḥ — "antarikṣaikadeśalakṣaṇaṃ sthānam": a place (sthāna), a portion of the atmosphere. "The word pātha has many meanings. Here it is used in the sense of 'path'. Pāthontarikṣaṃ pathā vyākhyātam (Ni. 6-7 as read [?]): Yāska, in giving the derivation of the word panthāḥ ('path'), says of the word pātha that it denotes the atmosphere, observes that this word's meaning is also being specially explained, and, to show that the word has several meanings, gives examples:

यत्रा चक्रुरमृता गातुमस्मै श्येनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः । प्रति वां सूर उदिते विधेम नमोभिर्मित्रावरुणोत हव्यैः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ७-६३-५ [as read])

yatrā cakruramṛtā gātumasmai śyeno na dīyannanveti pāthaḥ | prati vāṃ sūra udite vidhema namobhirmitrāvaruṇota havyaiḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 7-63-5 [as read])

— the word pātha in this Ṛk denotes the atmosphere.

उषासृज [?] त्मन्या समञ्जन्देवानां पाथ ऋतुथा हवींषि । वनस्पतिः शमिता देवो अग्निः स्वदन्तु हव्यं मधुना घृतेन ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-११०-१० [as read]) (The first word is printed letter by letter as above; the context suggests upa sṛja, but I give the print, not the guess.)

Here pātha means food. Uṣas comes before the Sun's rising, each day, always before sunrise. Therefore the Uṣases of the present, though later than the former Uṣases, as the former passed away, so they, too, pass away; since they pass away like those, these too are destroyed, following the destruction of those others along the atmospheric path.

original p. 43

प्रथमा आयतीनाम् — Prathamā āyatīnām — "āgacchantīnāṃ prathamā ādyā bhavati": "Of the Uṣases yet to come, the one who rises now is the first, in the sense of the 'first'; so Skandasvāmin:

परायतीनां परागच्छन्तीनां गवादिजातीनामनुगच्छति पन्थानः । आगच्छन्तीनां च प्रथमा बह्वीनां नित्यानां वा । योऽक्ष्णा [?] दूरवर्तिनो गवादिजातयो यश्च सन्निकृष्टाः सर्वव्यापित्वात्ताः सर्वा अनुगच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥ [read from the print; the words marked [?] are doubtful]

parāyatīnāṃ parāgacchantīnāṃ gavādijātīnāmanugacchati panthānaḥ | āgacchantīnāṃ ca prathamā bahvīnāṃ nityānāṃ vā | yo 'kṣṇā [?] dūravartino gavādijātayo yaśca sannikṛṣṭāḥ sarvavyāpitvāttāḥ sarvā anugacchatītyarthaḥ ‖ [read from the print; the words marked [?] are doubtful]

— 'She follows the paths of the going-away (past) ones, of the classes such as cows, etc.; and of the coming ones, she is first of the many, or of the eternal ones; as to those classes — cows etc. — that are far away and those that are near, because she pervades all, she follows all of them'." "As Uṣas pervades everywhere, she follows the courses of things that are eternal, whether far away or near at hand. The classes (jāti) of cows and the like, though eternal as classes, in the individual are subject to destruction; they follow the course of things that perish with the destruction of the individual; and she is first in the origin of the things that remain" — so they explain.

जीवमुदीरयन्ती मृतं बोधयन्ती — Jīvam udīrayantī mṛtaṃ bodhayantī:

जीवात्मानं प्राणिनां शयनादूर्ध्वं प्रेरयन्त्युषाः मृतमिव सन्तं पुरुषं पुनरिन्द्रियप्रवेशेन चेतनं कुर्वती प्रवर्तते ॥

jīvātmānaṃ prāṇināṃ śayanādūrdhvaṃ prerayantyuṣāḥ mṛtamiva santaṃ puruṣaṃ punarindriyapraveśena cetanaṃ kurvatī pravartate ‖

"Uṣas, who drives out the darkness, rouses with warmth the jīvātman of the beings lying in comfort; and any being who sleeps, completely unconscious as if dead, she wakes, makes him knowing, and sets him to his own works — this is the meaning."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on parāyatīnām (parā a prefix; iṇ "to go"; śatṛ in the laṭ sense by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau; śap elided by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; yaṇ in place of i by iṇo yaṇ, giving yat; the feminine in ṅīp by ugitaś ca, since śatṛ loses its luk [as printed]; nuṭ in the genitive plural by hrasvanadyāpo nuṭ; and the Vedic accent by jyāṃ chandasi bahulam [as read]), eti (iṇ "to go", adādi, laṭ 3rd singular; nighāta), udīrayantī (īr "to throw", curādi; ṇic in the svārtha by satyāpāśa…; śatṛ; guṇa; ayādeśa; ṅīp; the rephottarākāra), mṛtam (mṛṅ "to die"; kta by niṣṭhā; final accent), bodhayantī (budh "to know", ṇic in the causative by hetumati ca; śatṛ; feminine ṅīp; accent). Pā. numbers are small; none given. ‖ 8 ‖ running on to p. 44 The grammar of Ṛk 8 concludes at the top of this page with the guṇa and ayādeśa in bodhayantī, the feminine ṅīp, and the accent of the ṇic-ending; the end-mark ‖ 8 ‖ is printed after it.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.9)

उषो यदग्निं समिधे चकर्थ वि यदावश्चक्षसा सूर्यस्य । यन्मानुषान्यक्ष्यमाणा अजीगस्तद्देवेषु चकृषे भद्रमप्नः ॥ ९ ॥

uṣo yadagniṃ samidhe cakartha vi yadāvaścakṣasā sūryasya | yanmānuṣānyakṣyamāṇā ajīgastaddeveṣu cakṛṣe bhadramapnaḥ ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.9)

हे उषस्त्वमग्निं गार्हपत्यादिरूपं समिधे समिन्धनाय प्रज्वलनार्थं यच्चकर्थ कृतवती । उषःकाले ह्यग्नयो होमार्थमुपसमिध्यन्ते । अपि च तमसा तिरोहितं जगत्सूर्यस्य चक्षसा प्रकाशेन यद्वा व्यावः व्यवृणोः तमसा विश्लिष्टमकरोः । तथा मानुषान् मनुष्यान् [?] यक्ष्यमाणान् यागं करिष्यतस्त्वं यदजीगः पूर्वं तमसा ग्रस्तान्प्रकाशेनोद्गीर्णानिवाकरोः । हे उषो देवेषु मध्ये त्वमेव भद्रं भजनीयं तदेतत्त्रिविधमप्नः कर्म चकृषे कृतवती ॥

he uṣastvamagniṃ gārhapatyādirūpaṃ samidhe samindhanāya prajvalanārthaṃ yaccakartha kṛtavatī | uṣaḥkāle hyagnayo homārthamupasamidhyante | api ca tamasā tirohitaṃ jagatsūryasya cakṣasā prakāśena yadvā vyāvaḥ vyavṛṇoḥ tamasā viśliṣṭamakaroḥ | tathā mānuṣān manuṣyān [?] yakṣyamāṇān yāgaṃ kariṣyatastvaṃ yadajīgaḥ pūrvaṃ tamasā grastānprakāśenodgīrṇānivākaroḥ | he uṣo deveṣu madhye tvameva bhadraṃ bhajanīyaṃ tadetattrividhamapnaḥ karma cakṛṣe kṛtavatī ‖

Sense (mine): "O Uṣas, since thou hast caused Agni — the Gārhapatya and the others — to be kindled (samidhe, for kindling, for blazing); for at the time of Uṣas the fires are kindled for the oblation. Further, since thou hast vi āvaḥ — opened, uncovered — the world hidden by darkness by the cakṣas, the light, of the Sun; made it free from darkness. Also, since thou hast made those men who are about to sacrifice (yakṣyamāṇān) — who are going to perform the sacrifice — as though brought forth (ajīgaḥ) from the darkness that had swallowed them before, by thy light — O Uṣas, among the gods thou alone hast done this threefold good (bhadram, 'to be honoured') work (apnaḥ)."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): āvaḥ (vṛñ "to cover", aorist, the elision of cli by mantre ghasa…; elision of s after a consonant-ending by hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ; the augment āṭ by chandasy api dṛśyate); mānuṣān (manu with the suffix añ in the sense of "born", ṣuk augment [as printed], and puk).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he uṣaḥ — O Uṣas; tvam — you; agnim — the Gārhapatya and other fires; samidhe — for the sake of kindling (by the fuel etc.); yat — for what reason; cakartha — you have made; sūryasya cakṣasā — by the Sun's light; yat — for which reason; vi āvaḥ — (as) you have made manifest (the world covered by darkness); yakṣyamāṇān — those who will perform sacrifice; mānuṣān — men; yat ajīgaḥ — as you have made them fit for their duties; tat — therefore; deveṣu — among the gods (you); bhadram — auspicious; apnaḥ — (of the three kinds mentioned above) deeds; cakṛṣe — you have done."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Uṣas, among the gods you alone are she who has done these three auspicious deeds: the kindling of the Gārhapatya and other fires, the manifestation of the whole world covered by darkness, and the readiness for their duties of men who perform sacrifices."

original p. 46

English Translation (as printed)

Ushas, inasmuch as you have caused the sacred fire to be kindled, inasmuch as you have lighted the world with the light of the sun, inasmuch as you have wakened men to perform sacrifice, you have done good service to the gods.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अप्नः — Apnaḥ. "The word apnas is stated among the sixteen names of form (rūpa) (Ni. 3-?? [as read, "3-13", [?]]) and among the twenty-six [as read] names of action (Ni. 2-1 [as read]). Uṣas, as soon as she rises, kindles the Gārhapatya fire for the oblation; she makes the world, which is hidden by darkness, visible by the Sun's light; she makes the sacrificers and everyone else, delivered from the affliction of darkness, protected and alert in their duties. Because she performs these three kinds of work, she is held worthy of worship among the gods."

"The intention of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and of Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya is the same, but the word-order in the two books is different. Skandasvāmin:

उषसि ह्युदिताय अग्निहोत्रेण आहवनीयं समिन्धयन्ति नानुदितायामकस्मादुषा इव समिन्धवतीत्युच्यते [?] ।

uṣasi hyuditāya agnihotreṇa āhavanīyaṃ samindhayanti nānuditāyāmakasmāduṣā iva samindhavatītyucyate [?] |

— 'As soon as Uṣas has risen, those who perform agnihotra have the Āhavanīya fire kindled; before the rising of Uṣas they do not worship the Āhavanīya fire; therefore Uṣas makes the fire blaze up' — so says Skandasvāmin. And he explains: 'uṣaso hi prakāśaḥ sūryāt udeṣyataḥ prabhavati' — the light of Uṣas arises from the Sun who is about to rise."

उषःकाले होमार्थमुपसमिन्धतेऽग्नयः । सूर्यस्य प्रकाशेन तमसा विश्लिष्टमकरोः ॥

uṣaḥkāle homārthamupasamindhate 'gnayaḥ | sūryasya prakāśena tamasā viśliṣṭamakaroḥ ‖

"At Uṣas-time the fires are kindled for the oblation; by the Sun's light thou hast freed [the world] from darkness" — so Sāyaṇa too explains.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.10)

कियात्या यत्समया भवाति या व्यूषुर्याश्च नूनं व्युच्छान् । अनु पूर्वाः कृपते वावशाना प्रदीध्याना जोषमन्याभिरेति ॥ १० ॥

kiyātyā yatsamayā bhavāti yā vyūṣuryāśca nūnaṃ vyucchān | anu pūrvāḥ kṛpate vāvaśānā pradīdhyānā joṣamanyābhireti ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.10) Reading note after viewing the Pada: the second याः is printed in the second line as "योः" or a damaged "याः" [?]; I give याः, as the Saṃhitā's yāś ca requires. The Saṃhitā's kiyātyā is the Pada's kiyāti | ā; the Saṃhitā's vyūṣur is the Pada's vi-ūṣuḥ; the Saṃhitā's vyucchān is the Pada's vi-ucchān.

कियाति । आ । यत् । समया । भवाति । याः । विऽऊषुः । याः । च । नूनम् । विऽउच्छान् । अनु । पूर्वाः । कृपते । वावशाना । प्रऽदीध्याना । जोषम् । अन्याभिः । एति ॥ १० ॥

kiyāti | ā | yat | samayā | bhavāti | yāḥ | vi 'ūṣuḥ | yāḥ | ca | nūnam | vi 'ucchān | anu | pūrvāḥ | kṛpate | vāvaśānā | pra 'dīdhyānā | joṣam | anyābhiḥ | eti ‖ 10 ‖

original p. 49

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.10)

समयेत्यव्ययं समीपवचनम् । उषाः समया भवाति समीपस्था भवतीति यदेतत् कियाति कियति काले प्रवृत्तं परिसमाप्तं नेत्याकारः प्रश्नार्थः । इदमुक्तं भवति । उषा येन कालेन संयुक्ता स कालः कियान् तस्य कालस्य किं परिमाणमिति । अनेनोषसोऽनन्तत्वमुक्तम् । तदेव स्पष्टीकरोति । पुरा या उषसो व्यूषुः व्युष्टाः सञ्जाताः । नूनमवश्यमितः परं याश्चोषसो व्युच्छान् व्युच्छन्ति व्युष्टा भविष्यन्ति । तत्र पूर्वा व्युष्टा अतीता उषसो वावशाना कामयमानेदानीं वर्तमानोषा अनु कृपते अनुकल्पते समर्था भवति । अतीता उषसो यथा प्रकाशमकुर्वन् तद्वदेषापि प्रकाशं करोतीत्यर्थः । तथा प्रदीध्याना प्रकर्षेण दीप्यमानोषा अन्याभिरागामिभिरुषोभिर्जोषं सङ्गच्छते । आगामिन्योऽप्येतदीयं प्रकाशमनुकुर्वन्तीत्यर्थः ॥ [a few words in this passage are small and doubtful [?]]

samayetyavyayaṃ samīpavacanam | uṣāḥ samayā bhavāti samīpasthā bhavatīti yadetat kiyāti kiyati kāle pravṛttaṃ parisamāptaṃ netyākāraḥ praśnārthaḥ | idamuktaṃ bhavati | uṣā yena kālena saṃyuktā sa kālaḥ kiyān tasya kālasya kiṃ parimāṇamiti | anenoṣaso 'nantatvamuktam | tadeva spaṣṭīkaroti | purā yā uṣaso vyūṣuḥ vyuṣṭāḥ sañjātāḥ | nūnamavaśyamitaḥ paraṃ yāścoṣaso vyucchān vyucchanti vyuṣṭā bhaviṣyanti | tatra pūrvā vyuṣṭā atītā uṣaso vāvaśānā kāmayamānedānīṃ vartamānoṣā anu kṛpate anukalpate samarthā bhavati | atītā uṣaso yathā prakāśamakurvan tadvadeṣāpi prakāśaṃ karotītyarthaḥ | tathā pradīdhyānā prakarṣeṇa dīpyamānoṣā anyābhirāgāmibhiruṣobhirjoṣaṃ saṅgacchate | āgāminyo 'pyetadīyaṃ prakāśamanukurvantītyarthaḥ ‖ [a few words in this passage are small and doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Samayā is an indeclinable meaning 'near'. 'Uṣāḥ samayā bhavāti' — 'Uṣas is near': for how long (kiyāti), for how much time has this been going on, and when will it end? — the ā has the sense of a question. This is what is meant: for how much time is Uṣas joined — how long is that time, what is the measure of that time? By this is stated the endlessness of Uṣas. He makes that clear: the Uṣases who formerly vyūṣuḥ — had dawned, been born; and those who surely hereafter vyucchān — will dawn. Among them, wishing for the past dawned Uṣases, the Uṣas of the present anu kṛpate: is able to follow, is capable. As the past Uṣases made light, so this one too makes light: this is the sense. And pradīdhyānā, shining forth brilliantly, Uṣas joṣam — meets with the other, coming Uṣases: the coming ones too will imitate her light."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): kiyāti (the suffix ghá by kim-idaṃbhyāṃ vo ghaḥ, Pā. 5-2-40 as printed; by the capacity of this gha-rule vatup takes the gha form even after kim in the sense of measure; kim → kī by idaṅkimor īś kī, Pā. 6-3-90 as printed; the elision of a by yasya iti ca; the accent on the first syllable of the suffix; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā as Vedic); bhavāti (subjunctive, laṭ, with the augment aṭ in the leṭ); vyūṣuḥ (vas "to dwell", vi-prefixed in the sense of "to shine forth"; liṭ; kittva, with saṃprasāraṇa and doubling); vyucchān (uchī "to dispel"; the augment leṭ; elision of the final consonant-conjunction); kṛpate (kṛpū "to be able", the substitution of ṣ by vyatyaya); vāvaśānā (vaś "to wish", kānt; śānac in the liṭ sense by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ); pradīdhyānā (dīdhīṅ "to shine", laṭ śānac; the elision of śap by adādi…); the accent of the compound with the prefix by gatisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"uṣāḥ — Uṣas; samayā bhavāti — is near (this is the meaning); yat — that which (it is); kiyāti ā — for how long a time?; yāḥ — whichever Uṣases; vyūṣuḥ — have gone by; nūnam — certainly; yāḥ ca — whichever Uṣases; vyucchān — will arise; tatra — among them; pūrvāḥ — the earlier (gone by) ones; vāvaśānā — desiring (the present Uṣas); anu kṛpate — follows; pradīdhyānā — the Uṣas who shines in a special way; anyābhiḥ joṣam — together with others (who come later); eti — goes on."

original p. 50

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Since when has Uṣas been thus? The Uṣas of exceptional lustre, wanting to give light (this is her need), proceeds, following the order of the Uṣases that have passed away (working), together with the Uṣases who come after her."

English Translation (as printed)

For how long a period is it that the dawns have risen? for how long a period will they rise? still desirous to bring us light, Ushas pursues the functions of those that have gone before, and shinning [sic] brightly, proceeds with the others (that are to follow.)

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अनुकृपते — Anukṛpate — "anukalpate samarthā bhavati": "Since the Uṣases rise every day earlier than the rising of the Sun, among these there are three divisions in usage: past (atīta), that is, passed; present (vartamāna), that is, those reached in the time arrived at; future (āgāmi), those yet to come. Sāyaṇa says that in the light of the Uṣas who is now going on, she is able to follow, by her own light, the light of those past ones, and he describes the similarity of lustre between the past, the present (Uṣases) in respect of their light. Skandasvāmin, because the root kṛp is read in the forty-four [as read] arcati-actions (Ni. 3-14 as read [?]) beginning 'arcati, gāyati', explains anukṛpate as 'worships':

यच्च उषस्युदितायां स्तोतारः स्तुवन्ति तदुषा इव स्तौतीत्युच्यते ।

yacca uṣasyuditāyāṃ stotāraḥ stuvanti taduṣā iva stautītyucyate |

— 'when Uṣas has risen, the singers praise; since that is what praising belongs to Uṣas, it is said "Uṣas as it were praises".' The gods who come at once when Uṣas has risen, praise [her]; those who praise are those who belong to Uṣas; so Uṣas-time itself is praised: he explains this as an upacāra (figurative usage). In this way a difference of view is found in the two bhāṣyas in the matter of the sense."

Ā — Skandasvāmin: "ākāro 'tre [?] pādapūraṇaḥ | nūnam api pādapūraṇaḥ" — "the ā is used for filling out the line; and nūnam too is for filling out the line", as in Skandasvāmin's exposition. Sāyaṇa: "ākāraḥ praśnārthaḥ": 'uṣā yena kālena saṃyuktā sa kālaḥ kiyān kiṃ parimāṇam' — the letter ā conveys a question: "How much is the extent of the time with which Uṣas is joined?" From this he says that the measure of time which is united with the pervasion of Uṣas-time does not come within the range of knowledge; and then he describes the subtle aspects of the matter concerning the endlessness of Uṣas-time.

original p. 51

वावशाना — Vāvaśānā — "kāmayamānā": "Sāyaṇa also says 'desired' (apekṣitā). Skandasvāmin:

वावशाना — वश कान्तौ वाश्र शब्दने इत्येतयोरन्यतरस्येदं रूपं कामयमाना शब्दं कुर्वन्त्यर्थः । यच्च उषस्युदितायां कामयन्ते शब्दं वा कुर्वन्ति तदुषस्युपचर्यते ॥ [reading of the first words, vāśra śabdane, as printed [?]]

vāvaśānā — vaśa kāntau vāśra śabdane ityetayoranyatarasyedaṃ rūpaṃ kāmayamānā śabdaṃ kurvantyarthaḥ | yacca uṣasyuditāyāṃ kāmayante śabdaṃ vā kurvanti taduṣasyupacaryate ‖ [reading of the first words, vāśra śabdane, as printed [?]]

— The form vāvaśānā arises from the root vaś with the sense 'to wish' (kānti), or from the root vāś(ṛ) with the sense 'to make a sound'. Hence 'desired', or: the charming quality, desirable to all, of Uṣas-time, and the recitation of stotras and śastras and the like that take place at Uṣas-time, are in Uṣas-time itself: they reveal the nature of Uṣas — so Skandasvāmin explains."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly)

īyuḥ | te | ye | pūrva 'tarām | apaśyan | vi 'ucchantīm | uṣasam | martyāsaḥ | asmābhiḥ | ūṃ iti | nu | prati 'cakṣyā | abhūt | o iti | te | yanti | ye | aparīṣu | paśyān ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.11)

ये मर्त्यासो मरणधर्माणो मनुष्या व्युच्छन्तीं विवासयन्तीं पूर्वतरामतिशयेन पूर्वां विप्रकृष्टामुषसमपश्यन् दृष्टवन्तः । ते मनुष्या ईयुः । गताः । तथास्माभिरपि नु इदानीं प्रतिचक्ष्या प्रकर्षेण द्रष्टव्याभूत् । जाता । तथापरीषु भाविनीषु रात्रिषु ये मनुष्या एतामुषसं पश्यान् पश्यन्ति ते । ओ उ इति निपातद्वयसमुदायः । तत्र उ इत्येतदवधारणे । एव यन्ति । आगच्छन्त्येव । कालत्रयेऽप्येषा व्याप्य वर्तत इत्यर्थः ॥

ye martyāso maraṇadharmāṇo manuṣyā vyucchantīṃ vivāsayantīṃ pūrvatarāmatiśayena pūrvāṃ viprakṛṣṭāmuṣasamapaśyan dṛṣṭavantaḥ | te manuṣyā īyuḥ | gatāḥ | tathāsmābhirapi nu idānīṃ praticakṣyā prakarṣeṇa draṣṭavyābhūt | jātā | tathāparīṣu bhāvinīṣu rātriṣu ye manuṣyā etāmuṣasaṃ paśyān paśyanti te | o u iti nipātadvayasamudāyaḥ | tatra u ityetadavadhāraṇe | eva yanti | āgacchantyeva | kālatraye 'pyeṣā vyāpya vartata ityarthaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "The mortals (martyāsaḥ, men subject to death) who saw the pūrvatarām Uṣas — the very earlier, remote one — as she dawned, dispelling the darkness: those men īyuḥ, have gone. Likewise she has now become praticakṣyā, to be seen eminently, by us. And likewise in the coming nights those men who will see this Uṣas — they come, yanti. O u is a combination of two particles; of these u is in the sense of restriction ('indeed'): they surely come. The sense is that she pervades all three times."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): īyuḥ (iṇ "to go", liṭ 3rd plural jhi → us; the yaṇ substitute; doubling; the lengthening of the reduplication by dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti, Pā. 6-4-56 as read [?]); te (the pronoun, s → … Vedic substitution); martyāsaḥ (the asuk augment after the ā of jas — ājjaser asuk).

original p. 54

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"ye martyāsaḥ — which men; vyucchantīm — the rising; pūrvatarām — very ancient; uṣasam — Uṣas; apaśyan — saw; te — they; īyuḥ — are dead; (tathā — likewise); asmābhiḥ u — by us too (Uṣas); nu — now; praticakṣyā — as clearly to be seen; abhūt — has become (so); aparīṣu — in the coming nights; ye — whichever men; paśyān — will see (this Uṣas); te — they; āyanti u — are coming (they will be born hereafter)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The men who saw the Uṣases that rose in ancient times are no longer here. The Uṣas that now rises is visible to us. Men who will see the Uṣas that will rise later are yet to be born. (That is, Uṣas is seen to exist eternally, in the past, the future and the present.)"

English Translation (as printed)

Those mortals who beheld the pristine Ushas dawning have passed away ; to us she is now visible, and they approach who may behold her in aftertimes.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ये मर्त्यासः व्युच्छन्तीं पूर्वतरामुषसमपश्यन् ते ईयुः । अस्माभिः नु प्रतिचक्ष्या अभूत् — Ye martyāsaḥ vyucchantīṃ pūrvatarām uṣasam apaśyan te īyuḥ | asmābhiḥ nu pratīcakṣyā abhūt. "Men who by nature are subject to death saw in earlier times the Uṣases who revealed to the whole world the charm that they possess, and experienced joy. And she, showing her beauty, passed away like those. In the same way these (Uṣases) too will pass in the course of time. We, seeing at present this Uṣas-time, which has been obtained according to the present time, [her] (heart-ravishing) beauty, rejoice. Men who will rejoice seeing the Uṣases that will rise afterwards are yet to be born. Thus it is to be understood that Uṣas rises following the three times, and so pervades the three times. Though men are subject to death, they enjoy the delight of Uṣas in the three times of past, future and present; therefore the all-pervasion of Uṣas, according to the times, and in reference to the men concerned, appears to the men — thus Sāyaṇa explains the purport."

original p. 55

"Following the same view, Skandasvāmin explains:

अतीतैर्वर्तमानैरागामिभिश्च सर्वैर्मानुष्यैरुषा दृश्यते नास्मादिवत् कैश्चिदेव इति समस्तार्थः । [read as printed; words after dṛśyate doubtful [?]]

atītairvartamānairāgāmibhiśca sarvairmānuṣyairuṣā dṛśyate nāsmādivat kaiścideva iti samastārthaḥ | [read as printed; words after dṛśyate doubtful [?]]

— 'Uṣas is seen by all men, past, present and future; not, as with us [i.e. as with a man, a thing], by some only': this is the whole sense. Those who were before saw Uṣas-time and experienced delight; those who are now present see and rejoice; in the same way those who will be born afterwards will see and rejoice. Therefore the idea that 'we, because we are impermanent, only some see the Uṣas-time' is not what is intended here: he explains the meaning that Uṣas is within the sight of everyone."

मर्त्यासः — Martyāsaḥ — "mānuṣyāḥ", men. "Because the word martya is stated among the twenty-five [as read] names of man (nara) (Ni. 2-3 as read [?]), the word martya has the meaning 'man'."

Grammar page on: īyuḥ (iṇ "to go", adādi; liṭ 3rd plural; jhi → us by parasmaipadānām ṇalatusus…, Pā. 3-4-82 as read [?]; since an ajādi suffix follows, yaṇ for i by iṇo yaṇ, Pā. 6-4-81 as read [?]; in the doubling the sthānivadbhāva by dvirvacane 'ci; the reduplication lengthened by dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti; no nighāta since it begins the pāda; final accent from the suffix); pūrvatarām (atiśayena pūrvā pūrvatarā — the suffix taras in the comparative by dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau; accent on the pit); apaśyan (dṛśir "to see", aorist/imperfect laṅ, 3rd plural; yadvṛttānnityam, no nighāta; augment aṭ, being udātta, gives the first-syllable accent); martyāsaḥ (martya with jas, the augment asuk by ājjaser asuk, Pā. 7-1-50 as read [?]; s → ru → visarga); praticakṣyā (cakṣiṅ "to speak clearly", here in the sense of seeing; ṇyat by ṛhaloṇyat; ṭāp by ajādyataṣ ṭāp).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.12)

यावयद्द्वेषाः । यावयन्ति अस्मत्तः पृथक्कृतानि द्वेषांसि द्वेष्ट्राणि [?] राक्षसादीनि ययोषा सा तथोक्ता । न ह्युषसि जातायां राक्षसादयोऽवतिष्ठन्ते यतस्ते निशाचराः । ऋतपाः ऋतस्य सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य वा पालयित्री । ऋतेजा यज्ञार्थं प्रादुर्भूता । सत्यामुषस्यहनि यागा अनुष्ठीयन्ते अतो यज्ञार्थं जातेत्युच्यते । सुम्नावरी । सुम्नमिति सुखनाम । तद्वती । सूनृताः । वाङ्नामैतत् । पशुपक्ष्यादीनां वचांस्यीरयन्ती प्रेरयन्त्युत्पादयन्तीति । सुमङ्गलीः सौमङ्गल्योपेता । पत्या कदाचिदपि न वियुक्तेत्यर्थः । देववीतिं देवैः कामयमानं यज्ञं बिभ्रती धारयन्ती । हे उषः श्रेष्ठतमा अतिशयेन प्रशस्ता त्वमिहास्मिन्देवयजनदेशेऽद्यास्मिन्यागसमये व्युच्छ । विवासय ॥ [the word after dveṣāṃsi read as dveṣṭrāṇi [?]]

yāvayaddveṣāḥ | yāvayanti asmattaḥ pṛthakkṛtāni dveṣāṃsi dveṣṭrāṇi [?] rākṣasādīni yayoṣā sā tathoktā | na hyuṣasi jātāyāṃ rākṣasādayo 'vatiṣṭhante yataste niśācarāḥ | ṛtapāḥ ṛtasya satyasya yajñasya vā pālayitrī | ṛtejā yajñārthaṃ prādurbhūtā | satyāmuṣasyahani yāgā anuṣṭhīyante ato yajñārthaṃ jātetyucyate | sumnāvarī | sumnamiti sukhanāma | tadvatī | sūnṛtāḥ | vāṅnāmaitat | paśupakṣyādīnāṃ vacāṃsyīrayantī prerayantyutpādayantīti | sumaṅgalīḥ saumaṅgalyopetā | patyā kadācidapi na viyuktetyarthaḥ | devavītiṃ devaiḥ kāmayamānaṃ yajñaṃ bibhratī dhārayantī | he uṣaḥ śreṣṭhatamā atiśayena praśastā tvamihāsmindevayajanadeśe 'dyāsminyāgasamaye vyuccha | vivāsaya ‖ [the word after dveṣāṃsi read as dveṣṭrāṇi [?]]

Sense (mine): "Yāvayaddveṣāḥ — she by whom dveṣas ('hostile beings'), the rākṣasas and the rest, set apart from us, are driven off, yāvayanti: such is the meaning of the name. For when Uṣas is born the rākṣasas and the others do not remain, since they are night-wanderers. Ṛtapāḥ — the protectress of ṛta, truth, or of the sacrifice. Ṛtejā — born for the sake of the sacrifice: when Uṣas has come, in the day the sacrifices are performed; hence she is said to be born for sacrifice. Sumnāvarī — sumna is a name for happiness: she who has it. Sūnṛtāḥ — a name for speech: she stirs up, brings forth, the voices of animals and birds. Sumaṅgalīḥ — having auspiciousness; never separated from her husband, is the sense. Devavītim — the sacrifice that the gods desire, which she bibhratī, bears. O Uṣas, śreṣṭatamā, most praised, shine (vyuccha) here, in this place of the gods' sacrifice, to-day, at this time of sacrifice — drive away [the darkness]."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): yāvayaddveṣāḥ (yu with miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ, the ṇic causative; śatṛ; in the compound the accent of the first member by the bahuvrīhi rule, with the Vedic śatṛ shortening at the end of the first member); ṛtapāḥ (pā "to protect", viṭ; ṛte "the ṛta"); ṛtejāḥ (jan "to be born", viṭ — janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ, nasal dropped by vidyatoranunāsikasyātvam, locative in the compound by tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam, with aluk); sumnāvarī (sumna + vanip, in the Vedic by chandasīvanipāv…, the feminine ṅīp, n → r by the rephādeśa; lengthening seen in other words too); sumaṅgalīḥ (sumaṅgalā in the gaurādi class, feminine in ṅīṣ by Pā. 4-1-41 as read [?]; the Vedic option of the ṅīṣ with the nominative plural; elision of the su; the visarga); devavītim (vī in the sense of "to go, to bear, to desire, to eat"; "devair vīyate kāmyata iti devavītiḥ"; ktin in the passive; the first member with first-member accent, as it begins with dā…).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yāvayaddveṣāḥ — she who makes the rākṣasas fruitless, i.e. destroys them; ṛtapāḥ — she who guards truth and sacrifice; ṛtejāḥ — one born for sacrifices; sumnāvarī — she who is happy (who gives happiness) …

original p. 58

… sūnṛtāḥ — good words; īrayantī — (the animals and birds) producing [them] from themselves; sumaṅgalīḥ — endowed with auspiciousness; devavītim — the sacrifice that is desired by the gods; bibhratī — bearing; he uṣaḥ — O Uṣas, (goddess) (uṣo devate); śreṣṭatamā — (in the manner stated above) most excellent (you); iha — in this place of sacrifice; adya — now (at the sacrifice-time); vyuccha — shine."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Uṣas is the destroyer of rākṣasas (the night-wanderers, the rākṣasas, do not remain after the light); she is born for the sake of sacrifices (people perform sacrifice and the like when the light has come); she brings it about that good sounds arise; she is auspicious (never separated from a husband), happy; the bearer of sacrifices desired by the gods; being in this way most excellent, may Uṣas rise now in our sacrificial hall."

English Translation (as printed)

The beings hostile (to acts of devotion) now withdraw, for she is the protectress of sacred rites, who is manifested for their performance ; she is the giver of happiness, the awakener of pleasant voices, the enjoyer of felicity, and provider of food for the gods : most excellent Ushas, dawn to-day on this (sacrificial hall.)

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

यावयद्द्वेषाः — Yāvayaddveṣāḥ — "yāvayanti asmattaḥ pṛthakkṛtāni dveṣāṃsi dveṣṭṛāṇi rākṣasādīni yayoṣā sā": "Uṣas, who sets apart by her own light those rākṣasas and others who hate men and harm them — [beings] that are moving about at night by nature — they are made to go away. As soon as Uṣas-time comes, the rākṣasas and others go away: this is the meaning."

ऋतपाः — Ṛtapāḥ — "ṛtasya satyasya yajñasya vā pālayitrī": "she protects truth and the sacrifice: this is the meaning. The word ṛta is read among the names of water (udakanāma) (Ni. 1-12 as read [?]). The Nirukta-writer gives an example, saying that the word ṛta denotes truth and also denotes the meaning 'sacrifice' — Special Topics of Ṛk 12, continued from p. 58 — the Nirukta-writer's examples for the word ṛta:

original p. 59

न यातव [?] इन्द्र जूजुवुर्नो न वन्दना शविष्ठ वेद्याभिः । स शर्धदर्यो विषुणस्य जन्तोर्मा शिश्नदेवा अपि गुर्ऋतं नः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ७-२१-५ [as read])

na yātava [?] indra jūjuvurno na vandanā śaviṣṭha vedyābhiḥ | sa śardhadaryo viṣuṇasya jantormā śiśnadevā api gurṛtaṃ naḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 7-21-5 [as read])

"In this Ṛk the word ṛta conveys the meaning 'truth' or 'sacrifice'; he says 'satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā' (Ni. 4-18 as read [?])."

तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समञ्जन्त्स्वदया सुजिह्व । मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृन्धन्देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥ (नि. ८-२ and ऋ. सं. १०-११०-२ [as read])

tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samañjantsvadayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛndhandevatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖ (ni. 8-2 and ṛ. saṃ. 10-110-2 [as read])

and in this Ṛk too —

देवेभ्यो वनस्पते हवींषि हिरण्यपर्ण प्रतिवस्त्र अर्थम् [?] । प्रदक्षिणिद्रनयया [?] नियूय ऋतस्य वक्षि पथिभी रजिष्ठैः ॥ (नि. ८-२० [as read])

devebhyo vanaspate havīṃṣi hiraṇyaparṇa prativastra artham [?] | pradakṣiṇidranayayā [?] niyūya ṛtasya vakṣi pathibhī rajiṣṭhaiḥ ‖ (ni. 8-20 [as read])

— in this Ṛk too the word ṛta conveys 'sacrifice'.

ऋतेजाः — Ṛtejāḥ — "yajñārthaṃ prādurbhūtā": "those who perform sacrifice obtain Uṣas's rising only for the purpose of performing the sacrifice. Since, after Uṣas-time has arrived, the sacrifices are carried on in the day, it is said here that Uṣas rises for the purpose of sacrifice." Skandasvāmin:

ऋतशब्दोऽत्र आदित्यवचनः । पञ्चम्याश्च स्थाने सप्तमी । आदित्याज्जनित्री ।

ṛtaśabdo 'tra ādityavacanaḥ | pañcamyāśca sthāne saptamī | ādityājjanitrī |

"The word ṛta means 'Āditya'. Here the locative is used in place of the ablative (pañcamī); [the meaning is] 'one who is born of Āditya'." In the sense of the fifth case the seventh case is used: he explains that Uṣas is born from the Sun.

सुम्नावरी — Sumnāvarī — "sumnam iti sukhanāma | tadvatī": "sumnāvarī is stated among the sixteen names of Uṣas, 'vibhāvarī, sūnarī, bhāsvatī' (Ni. 3-19 as read [?]), so the sense is Uṣas. Since the word sumna is read among the twenty [as read] names of happiness, 'śaṃ…' (the first word of the list, as printed, is doubtful [?]) (Ni. 3-6 as read [?]), sumna means happiness. Skandasvāmin explains: 'prāṇināṃ sukhakarī' — Uṣas-time causes happiness to living beings."

original p. 60

सूनृता ईरयन्ती — Sūnṛtā īrayantī — "vāṅnāmaitat": it means speech. "The word sūnṛtā is stated among the names of Uṣas (Ni. 3-19 as read [?]) and also among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]). But the Bhāṣyakāra explains that the word sūnṛta conveys the meaning 'speech', and says:

सूनृता वाचः ईरयन्ती प्रेरयन्ती । उषा उदयोत्तरकालं हि प्राणिनां वचः प्रवर्तन्ते । अतः स्वैव ताः प्रेरयन्तीति व्यपदिश्यते ॥ [as read; the last word doubtful [?]]

sūnṛtā vācaḥ īrayantī prerayantī | uṣā udayottarakālaṃ hi prāṇināṃ vacaḥ pravartante | ataḥ svaiva tāḥ prerayantīti vyapadiśyate ‖ [as read; the last word doubtful [?]]

— 'since after the rising of Uṣas (so say they) animals and birds and beasts begin to make sounds, Uṣas is said to impel everyone to speak'."

सुमङ्गलीः — Sumaṅgalīḥ — "suṣṭhu maṅgalopetā | patyā kadācid api na viyuktā": "endowed with excellent auspiciousness. [The sense is that] Uṣas is always together with her husband, never separated." Yāska:

कनिक्रदज्जनुषं प्रब्रुवाण इयर्ति वाचमरितेव नावम् । सुमङ्गलश्च शकुने भवासि मा त्वा का चिदभिभा विश्व्या विदत् ॥ (ऋ. सं. २-४३-२ [as read])

kanikradajjanuṣaṃ prabruvāṇa iyarti vācamariteva nāvam | sumaṅgalaśca śakune bhavāsi mā tvā kā cidabhibhā viśvyā vidat ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 2-43-2 [as read])

— quoting this Ṛk as an example, in explaining the meaning of the word maṅgala (Ni. 6-9 as read [?]):

सुमङ्गलश्च शकुने भवासि । भवेत्कल्याणमङ्गलः । मङ्गलं गिरतेर्गृणात्यर्थे । गिरत्यर्थानिति वा । अङ्गमङ्गवत् [?] । मज्जयति पापकमिति नैरुक्ताः । मां गच्छन्तीति वा । मा च त्वा काचिदभिभूता सर्वतो विदत् ॥

sumaṅgalaśca śakune bhavāsi | bhavetkalyāṇamaṅgalaḥ | maṅgalaṃ giratergṛṇātyarthe | giratyarthāniti vā | aṅgamaṅgavat [?] | majjayati pāpakamiti nairuktāḥ | māṃ gacchantīti vā | mā ca tvā kācidabhibhūtā sarvato vidat ‖

"Having explained for the word sumaṅgala the meaning 'auspicious' (kalyāṇa), [he says] the word maṅgala 'swallows' (girati) anarthān, 'evils', i.e. destroys troubles. The Nirukta-writers say it 'plunges' (majjayati), i.e. destroys, sin. Or because it is for ever coming to me (māṃ gacchanti), or because no harm may ever overcome thee — so this word has the name maṅgala."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 12; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page, begun: yāvayaddveṣāḥ (yu "to mix, to separate", adādi; ṇic by hetumati ca; vṛddhi of u by āto 'ñjñiti[?]; āv substitution; then śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śap; the guṇa and ay for the ṇic; the vowel by ato guṇe — pararūpa; giving yāvayat; the Vedic chandasy ubhayathā, in which the śatṛ ending is also ārdhadhātuka …).

original p. 61

Grammar page of Ṛk 12, continued (noted briefly): yāvayaddveṣāḥ — the personal-ending being accented, the śap keeps its accent by sati śiṣṭasvaraḥ balīyaḥ; the first-member accent in the bahuvrīhi by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; the Vedic shortening yāvayat-dveṣāḥ at the end of the first member; ṛtapāḥ (pā "to protect", adādi; viṭ by ato maninkvanibvanipaś ca, the c serving to continue the viṭ; ending in ā; nominative singular); ṛtejāḥ (jan "to be born", viṭ by janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ; ā for the final n by vidyatoranunāsikasyātvam; the locative compound with aluk by tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam; the first-member accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt); sumnāvarī (sumnaṃ sukhaṃ asyā asti; vanip by the statement chandasīvanipaś ca; the stem sumnāvan; feminine ṅīp by vano re; n → r by rephādeśa; lengthening by anyeṣām api dṛśyate; the accent from the suffix, being pit); īrayantī (īr "to go, to move", curādi ṇic; śatṛ; feminine ṅīp by ugitaś ca; ṇic accent); sumaṅgalīḥ (sumaṅgalā in the gaurādi class as a name, hence ṅīṣ; the elision of the su is not prevented, by the statement "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante"; s → ru; visarga by kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ).

original p. 62

Grammar page, concluded: devavītim (vī "to go, to bring forth, to desire, to eat, to throw"; "devair vīyate kāmyate iti devavītiḥ" — the sacrifice; ktin in the passive by striyāṃ ktin, which is kit, so there is no guṇa; the first-member accent by the dāsībhārādi group). ‖ 12 ‖

Rik 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.13)

शश्वत्पुरोषा व्युवास देव्यथो अद्येदं व्यावो मघोनी । अथो व्युच्छादुत्तराँ अनु द्यूनजरामृता चरति स्वधाभिः ॥ १३ ॥

śaśvatpuroṣā vyuvāsa devyatho adyedaṃ vyāvo maghonī | atho vyucchāduttarā~ anu dyūnajarāmṛtā carati svadhābhiḥ ‖ 13 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.13) Reading note after viewing the Pada: the Saṃhitā's śaśvat-puroṣā is the Pada's śaśvat | purā | uṣāḥ; the Saṃhitā's vyāvo is the Pada's vi | āvaḥ; the Saṃhitā's vyucchād uttarāṃ is the Pada's vi | ucchāt | ut-tarān.

शश्वत् । पुरा । उषाः । वि । उवास । देवी । अथो इति । अद्य । इदम् । वि । आवः । मघोनी । अथो इति । वि । उच्छात् । उत्ऽतरान् । अनु । द्यून् । अजरा । अमृता । चरति । स्वधाभिः ॥ १३ ॥

śaśvat | purā | uṣāḥ | vi | uvāsa | devī | atho iti | adya | idam | vi | āvaḥ | maghonī | atho iti | vi | ucchāt | ut 'tarān | anu | dyūn | ajarā | amṛtā | carati | svadhābhiḥ ‖ 13 ‖

original p. 63

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.13)

देवी देवनशीलोषाः पुरा पूर्वस्मिन्काले शश्वन्नित्यं सन्ततं व्युवास व्युष्टवती । अथो अनन्तरमद्यास्मिन्काले मघोनी धनवत्युषाः तमसा तिरोहितमिदं सर्वं जगद् व्यावः [?] विवासितं प्रकाशेन तमसा वियुक्तमकरोत् । अथो अनन्तरमुत्तरानूर्ध्वतरानाविनो [?] द्यून् दिवसाननुलक्ष्यागामिन्यास्तु दिवसेषु व्युच्छात् व्युच्छति विवासयति । अतः कालत्रयव्यापिनी सोषा अजरा जरारहिता सर्वदैकरूपाऽमृता मरणरहिता च सती स्वधाभिरात्मीयैस्तेजोभिः सह चरति वर्तते ॥ [several words are small and doubtful [?]]

devī devanaśīloṣāḥ purā pūrvasminkāle śaśvannityaṃ santataṃ vyuvāsa vyuṣṭavatī | atho anantaramadyāsminkāle maghonī dhanavatyuṣāḥ tamasā tirohitamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagad vyāvaḥ [?] vivāsitaṃ prakāśena tamasā viyuktamakarot | atho anantaramuttarānūrdhvatarānāvino [?] dyūn divasānanulakṣyāgāminyāstu divaseṣu vyucchāt vyucchati vivāsayati | ataḥ kālatrayavyāpinī soṣā ajarā jarārahitā sarvadaikarūpā 'mṛtā maraṇarahitā ca satī svadhābhirātmīyaistejobhiḥ saha carati vartate ‖ [several words are small and doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Devī — Uṣas, of shining nature (devana); purā, in the past, śaśvat, constantly, vyuvāsa, shone forth. And now, adya, at this time, maghonī, the wealthy Uṣas, vyāvaḥ — has made all this world hidden by darkness free from darkness by light. And then, after this, in the coming days, the uttarān dyūn, she will vyucchāt, shine forth. Hence, that Uṣas, pervading the three times, ajarā, without old age, always of one form, amṛtā, without death, goes on, carati, together with her own splendours (svadhābhiḥ)."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): uvāsa (vas "to dwell"; in the liṭ the reduplication takes saṃprasāraṇa by liṭy abhyāsasyobhayeṣām); āvaḥ (from the same root vṛ in the aorist, the vikaraṇa elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; the s elided by hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ; the augment by chandasy api dṛśyate); ucchāt (leṭ with the augment aṭ); uttarān (the n becomes ru by dīrghād aṭi samānapāde; the nasalized ā by ato 'ṭi nityam); anu (a karmapravacanīya by anur lakṣaṇe, Pā. 1-4-84 as read [?]); ajarā, amṛtā (nañ-bahuvrīhi; the later member's first-syllable accent by ña-jara-mara-mitra-mṛtāḥ).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"devī uṣāḥ — goddess Uṣas; purā — in former times; śaśvat — continuously; vyuvāsa — rose; atho — after that; adya — now (at the present time); maghonī — Uṣas who has wealth; idam — this whole world (hidden by darkness); vyāvaḥ — made uncovered; atho — afterwards; uttarān — the coming; dyūn — days; anu vyucchāt — will make light; ajarā — therefore, without old age; amṛtā — immortal (Uṣas); svadhābhiḥ — with her own splendours; carati — goes about."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The goddess Uṣas rose every day in former times; the goddess, who is the support of wealth, is rising now in this world also; in the future, in the days to come, she will also give light; the ageless, deathless Uṣas goes about, endowed with splendour."

original p. 64

English Translation (as printed)

The divine Ushas dawned continually in former times ; the source of wealth, she still rises on this (world) ; so will she give light hereafter, through future days, for, exempt from decay or death, she goes on in her splendour.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

देवी उषाः — Devī uṣāḥ — "devanaśīlā": "she who has by nature luminosity; that is, the goddess Uṣas who shines — this is the meaning. The Nirukta-writer:

उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः । (नि. २-१८ [as read])

uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ | (ni. 2-18 [as read])

"From the root uchī with the meaning 'to drive away' he shows the sense that 'she (ucchati) drives away the darkness'. This explains the derivation of the word uṣas: the last part of the night is called Uṣas-time in usage," he says. "With regard to the matter that this Uṣas, having risen, passes away in order, he cites some Ṛks as examples —

अपोषा अनसः सरत्संपिष्टादह बिभ्युषी । नि यत्सीं शिश्नथद्वृषा ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-३०-१० [as read])

apoṣā anasaḥ saratsaṃpiṣṭādaha bibhyuṣī | ni yatsīṃ śiśnathadvṛṣā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-30-10 [as read])

in this Ṛk [the Nirukta explains] 'apāsarad uṣā anasaḥ saṃpiṣṭān meghāt bibhyuṣī' (Ni. 11-48 as read [?]): "Seeing the clouds driven by the wind, afraid of the wind, which will drive her too, Uṣas-time herself (hiding her own form) went away" — so it is described here.

एतदस्या अनः शये सुसंपिष्टं विपाश्या । ससार सीं परावतः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-३०-११ [as read])

etadasyā anaḥ śaye susaṃpiṣṭaṃ vipāśyā | sasāra sīṃ parāvataḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-30-11 [as read])

'etad asyā anaḥ āśete vimuktaṃ pāśi sasāroṣāḥ parāvataḥ preritavataḥ parāgatād vā' (Ni. 11-49 as read [?]): in this statement, which says, looking at the clouds changed into the form of water (the sense of udakabhāva), the chariot of Uṣas, being sheltered by the cloud, here is described as having loose joints [?] from the speed of the wind; from which it is to be understood that Uṣas is a deity of the middle region (madhyasthāna)."

original p. 65

उषाः — Uṣāḥ:

उषाः । उषा वस्तेः कान्तिकर्मणः उच्छतेरितरा माध्यमिका ॥ [Yāska; first words as read]

uṣāḥ | uṣā vasteḥ kāntikarmaṇaḥ ucchateritarā mādhyamikā ‖ [Yāska; first words as read]

"From the root vaś ('to desire, to shine') comes the form of the word uṣas in the sense 'lustrous'. Or from the root uchī 'to drive away' arises the form of the word uṣas. It means that Uṣas pours out the waters (udaka) that are in the clouds; or he gives the alternative meaning that she [Uṣas] makes the clouds stand in the middle (region). And from this it follows that Uṣas is a deity of the sky-region (dyusthāna) because of her lustrous form — and another [Uṣas] too. There is a doubt here. Yāska says (as the Kannada has it):

यद्योक्तं [?] — तद्वा इदं विकल्पेन द्युस्थानायोः [?] यो पुनरितरा माध्यमिका उषाः न तस्याः विकल्पः किं तर्हि उच्छतेरेव सा विवासनार्थस्य विवासयति उदकानि विवास्यते वा मेघो मध्यमेनेति [?] (नि. १२-८ [as read])

yadyoktaṃ [?] — tadvā idaṃ vikalpena dyusthānāyoḥ [?] yo punaritarā mādhyamikā uṣāḥ na tasyāḥ vikalpaḥ kiṃ tarhi ucchatereva sā vivāsanārthasya vivāsayati udakāni vivāsyate vā megho madhyameneti [?] (ni. 12-8 [as read])

[The Nirukta clause is read letter by letter from the print and is doubtful [?]; the Kannada gives its sense:] "From the root uchī, whose sense is 'to drive away', the Uṣas known through the word — she is in the middle region (atmosphere), pouring the waters that are in the clouds: she shines in the form of a deity, which is the alternative [that Yāska offers]."

उषस्तच्चित्रमा भरास्मभ्यं वाजिनीवति । येन तोकं च तनयं च धामहे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-९२-१३ [as read])

uṣastaccitramā bharāsmabhyaṃ vājinīvati | yena tokaṃ ca tanayaṃ ca dhāmahe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-92-13 [as read])

"In this Ṛk a prayer is made that wealth, cattle, sons, etc., that is common to both (kinds of Uṣas), be bestowed.

एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते । निष्कृण्वाना आयुधानीव धृष्णवः प्रति गावोऽरुषीर्यन्ति मातरः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-९२-१ [as read])

etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumañjate | niṣkṛṇvānā āyudhānīva dhṛṣṇavaḥ prati gāvo 'ruṣīryanti mātaraḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-92-1 [as read])

In this Ṛk it is said 'pūrve arddhe antarikṣalokasya': pūrvārdha means the atmospheric world; they explain that ketu here, for the word ketu, means 'knowledge', and for gāvaḥ 'rays': this Uṣas goddess, who shines by the Sun, performs two kinds of functions by two forms — thus he explains."

स्वधाभिः — Svadhābhiḥ — "ātmīyais tejobhiḥ": "by her own splendours. The word svadhā is read among the twenty-eight [as read] names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]) and among the hundred-and-one names of water (Ni. 1-12 as read [?]); but here both Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin explain the meaning as 'splendour'."

मघोनी उषाः — Maghonī uṣāḥ — "(dhanavatī)": "these words are not stated in the Nirukta among the words for Uṣas, but are used here in the meaning 'Uṣas'."

original p. 66

द्यून् — Dyūn — "divasān", days. The Nirukta-writer:

Sense (mine): "In the ātāsu, the wide regions, of the sky (divaḥ, nabhasaḥ): Uṣas vyadyaut — shines forth, by her añjibhiḥ, her manifest, illuminating splendours, in the widely spread quarters. This goddess (devī, of shining nature) apāvṛṇot — has removed the dark nirṇij, 'form' (nirṇik is a name for form) made by night: she has overpowered it with light. And Uṣas comes (ā yāti) with a well-yoked chariot, with red (aruṇebhiḥ) horses — or with her own red rays, as it were horses. What does she do? Prabodhayantī, she wakes up the sleeping beings."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): adyaut (dyut "to shine", aorist luṅ; the parasmaipada by the Pā. rule on dyutādibhyaḥ luṅi, 1-3-91 as read [?]; the cli elided by the Vedic usage; guṇa, or vṛddhi of the u …; or from dyai "to approach"… [as printed: yadvā dyai abhigamane, adādikaḥ…]).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"(uṣasu) divaḥ — of the atmosphere; ātāsu — in the quarters; añjibhiḥ — with illuminating splendour; vi adyaut — shines; devī — the luminous Uṣas; kṛṣṇāṃ nirṇijam — the black form (darkness); apa āvaḥ — has put away; aruṇebhiḥ — red-coloured; aśvaiḥ — with pervading rays (horses); suyujā — well yoked; rathena — by the chariot; prabodhayantī — rousing (the sleeping beings); ā yāti — comes."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Uṣas shines forth, by her rays, in the various regions of the atmosphere; the luminous one puts away the black form (darkness) which belongs to the night. She rouses the sleeping creatures, coming in a chariot yoked with red horses."

English Translation (as printed)

The divine Ushas lights up with her beams the quarters of the heavens ; she has thrown off her gloomy form, and awaking (those who sleep), comes in her car, drawn by purple steeds.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

आतासु — Ātāsu — "ātetāsu vistīrṇāsu dikṣu": "ātāḥ, āśāḥ, uparāḥ — among the eight names of the quarters (dik), since the word āśā is stated (Ni. 1-19 as read [?]), the meaning is 'quarters'."

original p. 69

निर्णिजम् — Nirṇijam — "rūpam": "nirṇik is read among the sixteen names of form (rūpa) (Ni. 3-13 as read [?]); so the meaning is 'form'."

अरुणेभिः अश्वैः — Aruṇebhiḥ aśvaiḥ — "aruṇaiḥ lohitavarṇaiḥ vyāpanaśīlaiḥ svakīyaiḥ kiraṇaiḥ turagair vā": "by her own rays, which are red-coloured and have a pervading nature, or by horses: this is the meaning. 'The red cows (gāvaḥ) of Uṣas' (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]): Yāska says that the red-coloured cows or rays are the vehicle of Uṣas. The idea is that the goddess Uṣas, pervading the atmosphere by her light, spreading in all the quarters, destroying the black form of the world that belongs to the night, comes shining in a chariot to which her red-coloured horses are yoked, or which is joined with red rays."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 14; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on añjibhiḥ (añjū "to anoint, to shine, to go"; the suffix i by the ṇādika [Uṇādi] rule; accent from the suffix; instrumental plural), divaḥ (accent of the ending by ūḍidaṃpadādi…), adyaut (dyut "to shine"; a root of the ātmanepada class, but by dyudbhyo luṅi, Pā. 1-3-91 as read [?], the parasmaipada in the aorist only; cli by cli luṅi; the cli elided by vyatyayo bahulam; elision of the i of tip by itaś ca; guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ is applicable, but in the Veda vṛddhi arises; or from dyai "to approach", adādi; luṅ 3rd singular tip; aṭ; elision of śap by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; vṛddhi by ukto vṛddhir luki hali; the augment aṭ: adyaut; nighāta), prabodhayantī (budh "to know", causative since it is the instigator's action; ṇic; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śap; guṇa and ayādeśa for the ṇic; the accent of the personal-ending by tāsyanudāttet…, so the ṇic accent remains; in the compound the first-member accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; feminine ṅīp by ugitaś ca).

original p. 70

Grammar page, concluded: aruṇebhiḥ (aruṇa + bhis, with aisbhāva optional by bahulaṃ chandasi, Pā. 7-1-10 as read [?], hence not applied here; et for the a before a plural jhal ending by bahuvacane jhaly et), yāti (yā "to go", laṭ 3rd singular; nighāta after an accented word), suyujā (yujir "to join"; because it belongs to the sampadādi group, kvip in the abstract; the stem suyuj; instrumental singular; the accent on the last syllable by nañsubhyām, Pā. 6-2-172 as read [?]). ‖ 14 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.15)

देवानां हविष्मावहन्तीत्येषोषसो याज्या । सूत्रितं च । आ द्यां तनोषि रश्मिभिरावहन्ती पोष्या वार्याणि । न ता अर्वा रेणुककाटो अश्नुते [?] । आश्व. ६-१४ [?] । इति ॥ पोष्या यावज्जीवं पोषणसमर्थानि वार्याणि वरणीयानि धनान्यावहन्ती सर्वं जनं प्रज्ञापयन्ती चेकिताना चित्रं विचित्रमाश्चर्यभूतं चायनीयं वा केतुं प्रज्ञापकं रश्मिं कृत्स्नजगत्प्रकाशनसमर्थं कृणुते स्वात्मनः प्रकाशं करोति । सैषेयुषीणां गमनवतीनां पूर्वमुत्पन्नानां शश्वतीनां बह्वीनामुषसामुपमा उप समीपे निर्मितोपमानभूता वा विभातीनां विशेषेण प्रकाशमानानामागामिनीनामुषसां प्रथमाद्या एवंभूतोषा व्यश्वैत् तेजसा प्रवृद्धासीत् ॥ [the sūtra quotation is small and partly doubtful [?]]

devānāṃ haviṣmāvahantītyeṣoṣaso yājyā | sūtritaṃ ca | ā dyāṃ tanoṣi raśmibhirāvahantī poṣyā vāryāṇi | na tā arvā reṇukakāṭo aśnute [?] | āśva. 6-14 [?] | iti ‖ poṣyā yāvajjīvaṃ poṣaṇasamarthāni vāryāṇi varaṇīyāni dhanānyāvahantī sarvaṃ janaṃ prajñāpayantī cekitānā citraṃ vicitramāścaryabhūtaṃ cāyanīyaṃ vā ketuṃ prajñāpakaṃ raśmiṃ kṛtsnajagatprakāśanasamarthaṃ kṛṇute svātmanaḥ prakāśaṃ karoti | saiṣeyuṣīṇāṃ gamanavatīnāṃ pūrvamutpannānāṃ śaśvatīnāṃ bahvīnāmuṣasāmupamā upa samīpe nirmitopamānabhūtā vā vibhātīnāṃ viśeṣeṇa prakāśamānānāmāgāminīnāmuṣasāṃ prathamādyā evaṃbhūtoṣā vyaśvait tejasā pravṛddhāsīt ‖ [the sūtra quotation is small and partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "'This āvahantī (Ṛk) is the yājyā of Uṣas, [offered] to the gods with the oblation'; and it is stated in the Sūtra — 'ā dyāṃ tanoṣi raśmibhiḥ āvahantī poṣyā vāryāṇi …' (Āśv. 6-14 as read [?]). Poṣyā — bringing for as long as life lasts desirable (vāryāṇi) riches that are able to nourish; making all people know (cekitānā); she makes (kṛṇute), for herself, a wonderful (citra) — or worthy-to-be-gathered — ketu, i.e. a ray that makes known, able to illumine the whole world. This Uṣas is the upamā of the many (śaśvatīnām) Uṣases that have gone, formerly born (īyuṣīṇām), or the pattern placed beside them; and prathamā, the first, of the Uṣases yet to come, shining specially (vibhātīnām); such Uṣas vyaśvait — has grown, by splendour, increased."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): poṣyā (puṣ "to nourish"; the suffix yat in the sense of the instrument or the object, with poṣaṇa; the accent on the first syllable by yato 'nāvaḥ; elision by śeś chandasi bahulam); vāryāṇi (vṛ "to choose", ṇyat by ṛhaloṇyat; the accent of ṇyat — ūḍavaravraṃsaṃsudaṃ hāṃ nyat… [as printed: iḍavaravṛtsaṃśaṃsu… [?]]); cekitānā (cit "to know", laṭ of the śānac, here in the Vedic liṭ; the elision of at by the chandasi… ; the accent of reduplication by abhyastānām ādiḥ); īyuṣīṇām (iṇ "to go"; kvasu; ṅīp by ugitaś ca; vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam; iṇo yaṇ…; the lengthening of the reduplication by dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti; ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca; ṅīp is pit hence unaccented); vibhātīnām (bhā "to shine", śatṛ; the ṅīp with ugitaś ca; ām with the accent jyāṃ chandasi bahulam); vyaśvait (śvit/śvi "to grow" [as printed: ṭuoś śvi gatiḥ vṛddhyoḥ], luṅ; elision of cli by bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk; guṇa; the vṛddhi by vyatyaya).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"poṣyā — nourishing; vāryāṇi — desirable riches; āvahantī — bringing; cekitānā — giving knowledge (to the ignorant); uṣāḥ — Uṣas (the goddess Uṣas); citram — wonderful; ketum — a ray that makes known; kṛṇute — makes; īyuṣīṇām — of the Uṣases that have gone before; śaśvatīnām — of the many; upamā — resembling; vibhātīnām — of the specially shining (Uṣases to come); prathamā — the first (to come); vyaśvait — has now risen, endowed with light."

original p. 72

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"(With her) she brings things that support life; (to those who are asleep, unconscious) she is the giver of knowledge; that Uṣas puts forth a wonderful light. Like the many past Uṣases, and first for those Uṣases to come that will shine — she is now shining."

English Translation (as printed)

Bringing with her life-sustaining blessings, and giving consciousness (to the unconscious), she imparts (to the world) her wonderful radiance. The similitude of the numerous dawns that have gone by, the first of the brilliant (dawns that are to come), Ushas has to-day appeared.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

केतुं कृणुते — Ketuṃ kṛṇute — "prajñāpakaṃ raśmim": "Sāyaṇa explains: 'a ray that makes the whole world knowing'. The Nirukta-writer, saying that the word ketu has the meanings 'knowledge', 'work' and 'ray', gives examples. 'ketaḥ, ketuḥ, cetaḥ' — among the eleven names of knowledge (prajñā) the word ketu is stated; hence the meaning 'knowledge':

नवोनवो भवति जायमानोऽह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रम् । भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन्प्र चन्द्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-८५-१९ [as read])

navonavo bhavati jāyamāno 'hnāṃ keturuṣasāmetyagram | bhāgaṃ devebhyo vi dadhātyāyanpra candramāstirate dīrghamāyuḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-85-19 [as read])

In 'ahnāṃ keturuṣasām etyagram' it is explained that 'ketu' is 'ahnaḥ kartā sūryaḥ' (the maker of the day, the Sun): so the word ketu signifies the meaning of 'doer of the action' (karma-kartṛ).

एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते । (ऋ. सं. १-९२-१ [as read])

etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumañjate | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-92-1 [as read])

In this Ṛk the word ketu is used in the sense of knowledge.

उदु त्यं जातवेदसं देवं वहन्ति केतवः । दृशे विश्वाय सूर्यम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५०-१ [as read])

udu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ | dṛśe viśvāya sūryam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-50-1 [as read])

original p. 73

"Here ketavaḥ is explained as 'raśmayaḥ', rays; the word ketu has the meaning 'ray'. Uṣas, rousing the whole world, or giving knowledge, reveals her own rays and illumines the world."

चित्रम् — Citram — "vicitram āścaryabhūtaṃ cāyanīyaṃ vā": "The word citra is that which causes wonder; or the meaning is 'worthy of honour':

उषस्तच्चित्रमा भरास्मभ्यं वाजिनीवति । येन तोकं च तनयं च धामहे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-९२-१३ [as read])

uṣastaccitramā bharāsmabhyaṃ vājinīvati | yena tokaṃ ca tanayaṃ ca dhāmahe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-92-13 [as read])

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अन्तरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११५-१)

citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-115-1)

— in these Ṛks the word citra is used in the sense 'worshipful (pūjya)'."

ईयुषीणामुपमा शश्वतीनाम् — Īyuṣīṇām upamā śaśvatīnām — "śaśvad iti bahunāma | gatvarīṇāṃ bahvīnāṃ madhye upamānabhūtā | atyantotkṛṣṭety arthaḥ" ("śaśvat is a name meaning 'many'; the 'gone', among the many, being the model; 'exceedingly excellent' is the meaning"). "The word śaśvat conveys the sense 'many'. For the many past Uṣases, this Uṣas of the present time is the upamāna (the standard of comparison); that is, the thing that gives the comparison is always of greater qualities. In the present case, as the Uṣas of the present time is compared with Uṣas, the superiority in light and the rest is in the Uṣas that is the standard of comparison, it is understood. Past Uṣas-times too shone just as the present does; the coming Uṣas-times will also be so: this is the main purport."

हे मनुष्या उदीर्ध्वम् । उत्तिष्ठत । यतोऽयं नः अस्माकं असुः शरीरस्य प्रेरयिता जीवो जीवात्मागात् । आगतवान् । केनोपस्प्रागात् [?] । अपक्रान्तम् । उषसः प्रकाशे सति सर्वजीवनव्यापारयोग्यः [?] । तस्य प्रेरणात्मा [?] रूपतेयासु [?] च जीवस्तद्देव ज्योतिर्वृत्ती [?] । आगच्छति । सूर्याय सूर्यस्य पन्थां मार्गमारैक् विविक्तं करोति । यातवे गमनाय । तस्मिन्देशे गन्म गच्छानो [?] यत्र यस्मिन्देश आयुः अन्ननामैतत् । अन्नं प्रतिरन्ते । प्रवर्धयन्तीत्यर्थः । उदारा दानेन प्रवर्धयन्ति ॥ [This passage is in small close type; I read it letter by letter and mark the words I could not settle [?]; the Kannada below gives the sense.]

he manuṣyā udīrdhvam | uttiṣṭhata | yato 'yaṃ naḥ asmākaṃ asuḥ śarīrasya prerayitā jīvo jīvātmāgāt | āgatavān | kenopasprāgāt [?] | apakrāntam | uṣasaḥ prakāśe sati sarvajīvanavyāpārayogyaḥ [?] | tasya preraṇātmā [?] rūpateyāsu [?] ca jīvastaddeva jyotirvṛttī [?] | āgacchati | sūryāya sūryasya panthāṃ mārgamāraik viviktaṃ karoti | yātave gamanāya | tasmindeśe ganma gacchāno [?] yatra yasmindeśa āyuḥ annanāmaitat | annaṃ pratirante | pravardhayantītyarthaḥ | udārā dānena pravardhayanti ‖ [This passage is in small close type; I read it letter by letter and mark the words I could not settle [?]; the Kannada below gives the sense.]

Sense (mine): "O men, udīrdhvam — rise up! For this life (jīva, the living self) — asuḥ naḥ, the impeller of our body — āgāt, has come. The darkness apa prāgāt, has gone out. When there is the light of Uṣas, [the creature is] fit for all activities of life. The light comes (eti). For the Sun (sūryāya) she has cleared (āraik) the path (panthām) to go (yātave); let us go (aganma) to that place where food (āyuḥ is a name for food) they cause to increase (pratirante — pravardhayanti) — the generous, by giving, make it increase."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): ūrdhvam (from īr "to go", adādi; anudāttet); āraik (ric "to empty", aorist; the vikaraṇa elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; guṇa by vyatyaya giving ai); panthām (accusative: the pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt rule by vyatyaya — the a); aganma (gam in the aorist luṅ; the vikaraṇa elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; mnoś ca, Pā. 8-2-64 as read [?], the m → n in the ma-ending).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"(he manuṣyāḥ — O men!) udīrdhvam — rise up (with warmth); naḥ — to us; asuḥ — the impeller; jīvaḥ — the jīvātman (of the nature of light); āgāt — has come; tamaḥ — darkness; apa prāgāt — has gone out; jyotiḥ — light; ā eti — comes; sūryāya — for the Sun; yātave — for going about; panthām — the path; āraik — is made clear; yatra — where; āyuḥ — food; pra tirante — they cause to grow (tatra — there); aganma — let us go."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O men, rise! The jīvātman who impels us has come (after the light the creatures all take up their works); the darkness has gone; there is light; the Sun's path has been made plain; let us go to the place where food is to be had."

English Translation (as printed)

Arise ; inspiring life revives ; darkness has departed ; light approaches. Ushas has opened the road for the sun to travel : let us repair to where they distribute food.

original p. 77

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

आयुः — Āyuḥ. "Andhaḥ, vājaḥ and so on — among the twenty-eight [as read] names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]) the word āyus is stated; so āyus means food."

"The meaning explained in this Ṛk is, as it were, a prayer addressed to the deity Uṣas, whether by the priests (ṛtvij) or by the sons and grandsons of the sacrificer. Uṣas-time has now arrived. The darkness has gone; Uṣas's light has increased. Uṣas has appeared in order that our vital breath, which stands in the place of the soul (jīvasthānīya) and was nearly dead (mṛtaprāya) in sleep, may be made ready to act. Our Uṣas — the one standing in the place of our vital breath — now having arisen, shows the way for the Sun, who is to move on. Since the Sun's rising is the end of Uṣas, the priests, Adhvaryu and the rest, [begin] to prepare, as food for the sacrifice, the oblations — Soma, Pavamāna and the like — thus Skandasvāmin explains."

"When the light of Uṣas has appeared, in all creatures the impulse arises to accomplish their own affairs. In this body, the light of the jīva, which exists in the form of the Supreme Self, shines forth. Uṣas has cleared the path for the Sun's going. Therefore, in whatever place men of excellent mind give food in abundance — to that place let us go: thus Sāyaṇa explains the meaning."

असुर्न आगात् — Asur na āgāt — "asur iti prāṇanāma" (a name for the breath); "asuḥ śarīrasya prerayitā" (the impeller of the body). "Skandasvāmin explains that the word asu conveys the meaning 'prāṇa' (life-breath). The Nirukta-writer, explaining the word asu as meaning both 'life-breath' and 'prajñā' (intelligence), gives examples suited to both meanings —

तेदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुराँ अभि देवा असाम । [first words doubtful [?]] ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-५३-४ [as read])

tedadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā~ abhi devā asāma | [first words doubtful [?]] ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-53-4 [as read])

And again —

असुराः असुरताः स्थानेष्वस्ताः स्थानेभ्य इति वा । अपि वासुरिति प्राणनामास्यः शरीरे भवति तेन तद्वन्तः । असोरसुरानसृजत तदसुराणामसुरत्वम् ॥ इति विज्ञायेते [?] (नि. ३-८ [as read])

"— here he explains that the word asu denotes life-breath.

वह्निः स्तोत्राणां वोढा रेभः । स्तोतृनामैतत् । स्तोतोषसो विभातीः प्रकाशमाना उषोदेवताः स्तवानः स्तुवन् वाचो वेदरूपायाः सम्बन्धीनि स्यूमना स्यूमानि सुस्तुतानि सन्ततान्यृक्छान्त्यादिय [?]न्युदियर्ति । उद्गमयति । उच्चारयति । अतो हे मघोनि मघवत्युषः अद्यास्मिन्समये गृणते स्तुवते तस्मै पुरुषाय तदुच्छ दृष्टिनिरोधकतया प्रसिद्धं स्वैशं तमो विवासय । वर्जय । अस्मे अस्मभ्यं च प्रजावत् प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिर्युक्तमायुरन्नं नि दिदीहि नितरां प्रकाशय । दीदेतिश्छान्दसो दीप्तिकर्मा । प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥ [this passage is in small close type; the words marked [?] are doubtful]

vahniḥ stotrāṇāṃ voḍhā rebhaḥ | stotṛnāmaitat | stotoṣaso vibhātīḥ prakāśamānā uṣodevatāḥ stavānaḥ stuvan vāco vedarūpāyāḥ sambandhīni syūmanā syūmāni sustutāni santatānyṛkchāntyādiya [?]nyudiyarti | udgamayati | uccārayati | ato he maghoni maghavatyuṣaḥ adyāsminsamaye gṛṇate stuvate tasmai puruṣāya taduccha dṛṣṭinirodhakatayā prasiddhaṃ svaiśaṃ tamo vivāsaya | varjaya | asme asmabhyaṃ ca prajāvat prajābhiḥ putrapautrādibhiryuktamāyurannaṃ ni didīhi nitarāṃ prakāśaya | dīdetiśchāndaso dīptikarmā | prayacchetyarthaḥ ‖ [this passage is in small close type; the words marked [?] are doubtful]

Sense (mine): "Vahniḥ — the bearer of the hymns, rebhaḥ (a name for a singer): the singer praising Uṣas, who shines forth (vibhātīḥ, the deity Uṣas), raises up the well-praised, continuous (sūmanā, 'stitched together') utterances, the chants of the Veda, and utters them. Therefore, O maghoni, wealthy Uṣas, adya, at this time, tad uccha — for him, the praiser (gṛṇate), drive away that darkness which is known as the obstructor of sight, remove it. And asme, to us, give prajāvat āyuḥ, food (āyus) together with progeny — sons, grandsons and the rest; ni didīhi, bestow constantly, make shine. The verb dīdeti in the Veda has the sense of shining (dīpti): 'give', is the sense."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): syūmanā (sivu "to sew", in the sense of continuation; the suffix manin in the passive, as the "seen" (dṛśi) in the rule covers all cases; accent by the augment etc.; the plural-neuter śi with the Vedic ā); iyarti (ṛ "to go", juhotyādi class, with śap → śluk; doubling; ṛ → iy; the reduplication of abhyasta gives the first-syllable accent); stavānaḥ (ṣṭuñ "to praise", śānac; the elision of śap by adādi; the śānac being ārdhadhātuka by chandasy ubhayathā, guṇa, avādeśa, the first-syllable accent from the suffix); vibhātīḥ (bhā "to shine", śatṛ, ṅīp by śatranumo nadyajādī; accent); gṛṇate (gṝ "to praise", kryādi; pā-… [the printed rule on prefix accent]); asme (the substitute asme for asmabhyam, by supāṃ sulug…, the dative: ṅe → e, śeḥ ādeśa).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha / Bhāvārtha the Kannada Pratipadārtha and Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 17 are on p. 81

original p. 81

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"vahniḥ — one who offers the stotras; rebhaḥ — the stotṛ; vibhātīḥ — shining by driving away darkness; uṣasaḥ — the Uṣas deities; stavānaḥ — praising; vācaḥ — words related to the Veda; syūmanā — joined (well-connected) ṛk-s (the stotras); udiyarti — utters (hence); maghoni — O Uṣas deity, who possess wealth; adya — now; gṛṇate — to the praiser; tad uccha — remove that darkness (which obstructs the sight); asme — to us also; prajāvat — endowed with sons, grandsons and offspring; āyuḥ — food; ni didīhi — make shine well (bestow)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The singer praises the shining Uṣases with Vedic hymns. O wealthy Uṣas deity, to such a singer take away the darkness. Give us food together with progeny."

English Translation (as printed)

The offerer of praise, the reciter of praise, celebrating the brilliant Ushas, repeats the well-connected words (of the Veda). Possessor of affluence, dawn to-day upon him who praise [sic] you ; bestow upon us food, whence progeny may be obtained.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

स्यूमना — Syūmanā — "sukhanāma": a name of happiness. "The word syūmana is stated among the twenty [as read] names of happiness (Ni. 3-14 as read [?]): the meaning is 'happiness'."

रेभः — Rebhaḥ — "stotṛnāmaitat": this is a name of a singer. "Among the many names of the praiser (stotṛ) — 'jaritā', 'kāruḥ' and the rest — the word rebhaḥ is stated (Ni. 3-18 as read [?]). The count of the names printed in the Kannada ('hundred-…') is not clear [?]."

"When Sāyaṇa explains the word syūmanā: 'syūmāni anusyūtāni saṅgatāni uktāni stotrāṇi' — stotras, when sung, in which the words of the hymn are connected with each other and give a good meaning. The singer recites stotras of such kind, he says. Skandasvāmin, since the word syūmanā denotes 'happiness', explains: 'sukhena akleśena stutilakṣaṇā vācaḥ udiyarti' — he recites, easily, without trouble, the Vedic sentences that have the nature of praise — [he gives the sense] 'he, of himself, performs the stotra-reciting with ease'. And (as the Kannada continues on the next page) …

original p. 82

… ātmanaḥ [read as printed, small [?]] parokṣarūpeṇa prathamapuruṣeṇa vyapadeśaḥ hotrākhyaṃ ṛtvik kutsanāmā vā ṛṣiḥ udgamayati uccārayati [read letter by letter from the small type; doubtful [?]]: 'the poet Kutsa, who acts as the hotṛ priest, referring to himself here indirectly, in the third person, as one who is engaged as hotṛ, utters this praise' — so he says. Further 'rebhaḥ — the stotṛ, vahniḥ — because of the capacity to carry (vahana), Agni too, being able to bear the oblations, praises the many kinds of lights of Uṣas, [and so] he explains the greatness of Uṣas."

अस्मे — Asme — "asmabhyaṃ ca": "In the Ṛk the prayer of the deity Uṣas is described: 'to the singers, to the sacrificers also, grant sons, grandsons and the rest, and food' — so both commentators explain the meaning. The Nirukta-writer explains that the word asme, though it has one form in all the cases, conveys the meaning of a particular case according to the context, and gives the following examples in the particular cases —

  1. अस्मे ते बन्धुः । वयमित्यर्थः ॥ अस्मे इत्येतत्पदं सर्वविभक्त्यन्तम् । तस्मादनेकार्थम् । एकमेव ह्येतच्छब्दरूपं सप्तस्वपि विभक्त्यर्थेषु वर्तते । प्रकरणादिवशात् तस्य नियमो भवति । तद्यथा — प्रथमायास्त्वात् — अस्मे ते बन्धुः । वयमित्यर्थः ॥ [as read; the second passage is in small type, doubtful [?]]

asme ityetatpadaṃ sarvavibhaktyantam | tasmādanekārtham | ekameva hyetacchabdarūpaṃ saptasvapi vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati | tadyathā — prathamāyāstvāt — asme te bandhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ ‖ [as read; the second passage is in small type, doubtful [?]]

— that is: the word asme is used, according to the context, in the sense of all seven cases. Which case's meaning is to be taken is to be said according to that context. For example, in the sentence 'asme te bandhuḥ' the word asme has the sense 'vayam' — 'we'. This is an example of the sense of the first case.

  1. अस्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । अस्मानित्यर्थः ॥ द्वितीयायास्त्वात् — [asme has the sense of the second case]; 'asmān', 'us'.

dvitīyāyāstvāt — [asme has the sense of the second case]; 'asmān* ', 'us '.*

"As an example of this meaning —

आ श्येनस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमामा उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११८-११ [as read])

ā śyenasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | have hi vāmaśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāmā uṣaso vyuṣṭau ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-118-11 [as read])

they cite this Ṛk. The word asme in this Ṛk has the meaning 'asmān' — 'us'."

original p. 83

  1. अस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । अस्माभिरित्यर्थः ॥ तृतीयायास्त्वात् —

tṛtīyāyāstvāt —

"Here asme means asmābhiḥ, 'by us' — the sense of the third case. In this matter —

भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेन्द्र क्रत्वा मरुत्वो यद्वशाम ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१६३-२ [as read; numerals small [?]])

bhūri cakartha yujyebhirasme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭhendra kratvā marutvo yadvaśāma ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-163-2 [as read; numerals small [?]])

— they cite this Ṛk as an example. Here asme means asmābhiḥ, 'by us'."

  1. अस्मे प्रयन्धि मघवन्नृजीषिन् । अस्मभ्यमित्यर्थः ॥ चतुर्थ्यास्त्वात् —

caturthyāstvāt —

"Here asme means asmabhyam, 'to us', the sense of the fourth case. Example —

अस्मे प्रयन्धि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निन्द्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः । अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराञ्छश्वत इन्द्र शिप्रिन् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-३६-१० [as read; [?]])

asme prayandhi maghavannṛjīṣinnindra rāyo viśvavārasya bhūreḥ | asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asme vīrāñchaśvata indra śiprin ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 3-36-10 [as read; [?]])

— the word asme in this Ṛk has the sense of the fourth case, 'asmabhyam', 'to us'."

  1. अस्मे आराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु । अस्मदित्यर्थः ॥ पञ्चम्यास्त्वात् —

pañcamyāstvāt —

"Here asme means asmat, 'from us' (from our region): the sense of the fifth case. Example —

तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम । स सुत्रामा स्ववाँ इन्द्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-४७-१२ [as read])

tasya vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyasyāpi bhadre saumanase syāma | sa sutrāmā svavā~ indro asme ārācciddveṣaḥ sanutaryuyotu ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-12 [as read])

— the word asme in this Ṛk has the sense of the fifth case, 'from us'."

  1. ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे । अस्माकमित्यर्थः ॥ षष्ठ्यास्त्वात् —

ṣaṣṭhyāstvāt —

"Here asme means asmākam, 'our', 'to us'. For the explanation of this meaning —

आ नो भर भगमिन्द्र द्युमन्तं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके । ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनाम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-३१-१८ [as read; [?]])

ā no bhara bhagamindra dyumantaṃ ni te deṣṇasya dhīmahi prareke | ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tamā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnām ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 3-31-18 [as read; [?]])

— the word asme in this Ṛk has, for asmākam, 'our', the sense of the sixth case."

original p. 84

  1. अस्मे धत्त वसवो वसूनि । अस्मास्वित्यर्थः ॥ सप्तम्यास्त्वात् —

saptamyāstvāt —

"Here asme means 'in us': the sense of the seventh case. Example —

अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-७९-४ [as read])

agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho | asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-79-4 [as read])

— the word asme in this Ṛk has the sense of the seventh case, 'asmāsu', 'in us'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 17; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on syūmanā (sivu "to sew", in the sense of continuation; the suffix manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante, Pā. 3-2-75 as read [?], stated to apply, by the word dṛśi, in all the specifications; the passive manin after the root; the ūṭh substitution for v by chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca, Pā. 6-4-19 as read [?]; the yaṇ; the form syūman; with the jas-neuter, śi → ā, elision by śeś chandasi bahulam; or ṭha, vuk in the abstract by ṇādika; "bound with bonds" is the sense; in the second view the first syllable is accented by vyatyaya), vācaḥ (genitive/accusative with the accent of the ending in jas/śas by sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ, Pā. 6-1-168), iyarti (ṛ "to go", juhotyādi, laṭ 3rd singular tip; śluḥ by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ, Pā. 2-4-75 as read [?]; the doubling of the root by ślau; i in the reduplication by arti-pipartyoś ca; guṇa of the root's ṛ by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; raparatva; abhyāsasyāsavarṇe, Pā. 6-4-78 as read [?], the iy substitute for the reduplication's i; tiṅ atiṅaḥ nighāta).

original p. 85

Grammar page of Ṛk 17, concluded (noted briefly): stavānaḥ (ṣṭuñ "to praise", adādi; śānac in the laṭ sense; śap elided by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; the śānac is made ārdhadhātuka by chandasy ubhayathā, Pā. 3-4-117 as read [?], so it is not jit… [as printed, compressed]; guṇa of the root's u; av; the śānac is cit, yet by vyatyaya the first syllable takes the accent; nominative singular); uccha (uchī "to dispel", loṭ 2nd singular; nighāta); gṛṇate (gṝ "to praise", kryādi; śatṛ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; prādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ in the root; kryādibhyaḥ śnā; sārvadhātukam apit makes the śatṛ ṅit, so śnābhyastayor ātaḥ, Pā. 6-4-112 as read [?], elides the ā; with the ṇatva of the n after ṛ; the stem gṛṇat; dative singular; the śatṛ without num is followed by the ajādi ending, hence by śatur anumo nadyajādī, Pā. 6-1-173 as read [?], the accent is on the ending); vibhātīḥ (bhā "to shine", śatṛ, ṅīp by ugitaś ca; as before the accent of the ṅīp ending by śatur anumo…; accusative plural); asme (the stem asmad; the dative singular ṅe following; supāṃ sulug, Pā. 7-1-39 as read [?], the śe substitution; śeṣe lopaḥ, Pā. 7-2-90 as read [?], elision of the part of asmad ending in m …). ‖ 17 ‖
