॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.18)

या गोमतीरुषसः सर्ववीरा व्युच्छन्ति दाशुषे मर्त्याय । वायोरिव सूनृतानामुदर्के ता अश्वदा अश्नवत्सोमसुत्वा ॥ १८ ॥

yā gomatīruṣasaḥ sarvavīrā vyucchanti dāśuṣe martyāya | vāyoriva sūnṛtānāmudarke tā aśvadā aśnavatsomasutvā ‖ 18 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 113.18)

याः । गोऽमतीः । उषसः । सर्वऽवीराः । विऽउच्छन्ति । दाशुषे । मर्त्याय । वायोःऽइव । सूनृतानाम् । उत्ऽअर्के । ताः । अश्वऽदाः । अश्नवत् । सोमऽसुत्वा ॥ १८ ॥

yāḥ | go 'matīḥ | uṣasaḥ | sarva 'vīrāḥ | vi 'ucchanti | dāśuṣe | martyāya | vāyoḥ 'iva | sūnṛtānām | ut 'arke | tāḥ | aśva 'dāḥ | aśnavat | soma 'sutvā ‖ 18 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.18)

दाशुषे हवींषि दत्तवते मर्त्याय मनुष्याय यजमानाय गोमतीः गोमद्भिः बहुभिर्गोभिर्युक्ताः सर्ववीराः सर्वैः शरणसमर्थैर्वीरैः शूरैर्युक्ताः या उषसो व्युच्छन्ति । तमो वर्जयन्ति । वायोरिव वायुवत्प्रेरितं [?] प्रवर्तमानानां सूनृतानां स्तुतिरूपाणां वाचामुदर्के समाप्तावश्वदा अश्वानां दात्र्यस्ता उषसः सोमसुत्वा सोमानामभिषोता यजमानोऽश्नवत् । व्याप्नोतु ॥ [a few words doubtful [?]]

dāśuṣe havīṃṣi dattavate martyāya manuṣyāya yajamānāya gomatīḥ gomadbhiḥ bahubhirgobhiryuktāḥ sarvavīrāḥ sarvaiḥ śaraṇasamarthairvīraiḥ śūrairyuktāḥ yā uṣaso vyucchanti | tamo varjayanti | vāyoriva vāyuvatpreritaṃ [?] pravartamānānāṃ sūnṛtānāṃ stutirūpāṇāṃ vācāmudarke samāptāvaśvadā aśvānāṃ dātryastā uṣasaḥ somasutvā somānāmabhiṣotā yajamāno 'śnavat | vyāpnotu ‖ [a few words doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "To the mortal (martyāya), man, the sacrificer (dāśuṣe) who has given oblations: the Uṣases that dawn (vyucchanti, drive out darkness), gomatīḥ — possessing many cows, sarvavīrāḥ — possessed of all the heroes, valiant men able to protect; vāyor iva — as of the wind, impelled, moving sūnṛtānām — of the speeches in the form of praise, at the udarke, at the completion [of the hymns]: those Uṣases that give horses (aśvadāḥ) — may the Soma-presser (somasutvā), the sacrificer, attain (aśnavat), obtain them."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): dāśuṣe (dāś "to give", kvasu suffix, with the nipāta accent; dative singular with vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam; ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca); aśnavat (aśū "to pervade", leṭ, by vyatyaya the parasmaipada; the augment aṭ in the leṭ; elision of the i of the ending by itaś ca); somasutvā (ṣuñ "to press", kvanip by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; ṭuk augment hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk).

original p. 87

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"dāśuṣe — to the sacrificer who offers oblations; martyāya — to the sacrificer who is a man; gomatīḥ — endowed with rays; sarvavīrāḥ — joined with strong men, able in every way; yāḥ uṣasaḥ — whichever Uṣases; vāyor iva — like the wind (moving swiftly); sūnṛtānām — of speeches of praise; udarke — at the end; aśvadāḥ — those who give horses; tāḥ — those Uṣases; somasutvā — the sacrificer who prepares the Soma juice; aśnavat — may he obtain, may he come near (to him)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"In the sacrifice the sacrificers and others praise the shining Uṣas deities with mantras that are quickly recited. After the end of their praise, may the Uṣas deity, who bestows wealth, such as horses, on the praiser, come near the sacrificer who has prepared the Soma and is awaiting [her]."

English Translation (as printed)

May he who has offered the libation obtain, upon the conclusion of his praises, (enunciated), like the wind, (with speed), (the favour of) those Ushasas who are givers of horses, and of cattle, and of progeny, and who shed light upon the mortal presenting to them (offerings).

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

दाशुषे — Dāśuṣe — "havīṃṣi dattavate": "to the sacrificer who offers oblations — this is the meaning. That dāśvān, sāhvān, and mīḍhvān [as printed: dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca] are irregularly formed (nipātita) [by the grammarians]. The Nirukta-writer explains the word dāśuṣe as 'dattavate' (to him who has given) and cites the Ṛk —

धाता ददातु दाशुषे प्राचीं जीवातुमक्षिताम् । वयं देवस्य धीमहि सुमतिं सत्यधर्मणः ॥ (अथ. सं. ७-१२-३ [as read; Atharvaveda, [?]])

dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe prācīṃ jīvātumakṣitām | vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ ‖ (atha. saṃ. 7-12-3 [as read; Atharvaveda, [?]])

as an example."

दाशुषे मर्त्याय — Dāśuṣe martyāya — "dāśvān iti yajamānanāma śākapūṇinā paritam [reading of the last word doubtful [?]]; tādarthye caturthī yajamānasya mānuṣasya cārthāya": Skandasvāmin says that the word dāśvān is the name of the sacrificer (yajamāna) — this is the view of Śākapūṇi; the fourth case is in the sense of 'for the sake of' [tādarthya]: 'for the sake of the sacrificer who is a man'.

original p. 88

गोमतीः — Gomatīḥ — "gomatyaḥ bahubhir gobhir yuktāḥ": "possessing many cows. As is said in the Nirukta, 'aruṇo gāva uṣasām' ('the red cows of the Uṣases'): because the Uṣases harness to their chariot cows of red colour, Skandasvāmin explains that the Uṣases are 'those who have cows'. The Nirukta-writer, explaining that the word go has many meanings — the earth (pṛthivī), the skin of a cow, [śleṣman (phlegm) [?]], the bow-string (maurvī, jyā), the rays of the Sun — gives different examples for each meaning."

सर्ववीराः — Sarvavīrāḥ — "sarvaiḥ śaraṇasamarthair vīraiḥ śūraiḥ yuktāḥ": "joined with all heroes, who can offer protection: the Uṣases are joined with strong, courageous men in every way, who go forward."

उदर्के — Udarke — "samāptau": "at the end. Sūnṛtānām udarke: at the end of the sentences of the form of stotras, so Sāyaṇa says: 'udarka ity ūrdhva ucyate yadvā yadvāyor [?] …' [the Sanskrit here is in small type and broken; I give its sense]: 'at the time of the dawn (prabhātavelāyām) of the (praise) words'. Skandasvāmin says: 'in the morning twilight, which has continuous production of stotras, like the rush of the wind' [as the Kannada has it]. The Uṣases having risen in time, the people in the sacrificial halls praise [her] with stotras hurriedly; therefore the morning that follows the passing of Uṣas also has the stotra-words produced — this is the idea."

अश्वदाः — Aśvadāḥ — "aśvānāṃ dātrīḥ": "the Uṣases give horses to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice — so says Sāyaṇa. Skandasvāmin: the Uṣases give horses, etc., to the singers of stotras and to those who sacrifice (yaṣṭṛ); or, in the giving of the dakṣiṇā, because the giving of horses is also prescribed, 'aśvadā' is an adjective of somasutvā — not of Uṣas: aśvasya dātā yajamānaḥ. Because the sacrificer who presses the Soma gives a horse when giving the dakṣiṇā, they are 'donors of horses'; the word aśvadā does not qualify Uṣas. He explains that it means the sacrificer who is the donor of horses."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.19)

हे उषस्त्वं देवानां माता जननी । उषसि सर्वे देवाः स्तुत्या प्रबोध्यन्ते अतः सा तज्जननवतीत्युच्यते । अत एवादितेर्देवानां मातुरनीकं प्रत्यनीकं प्रतिस्पर्धिनी त्वमित्यर्थः । यद्वा । दीव्यन्तीति देवा रश्मयः । तेषां निर्मात्री अदितेरखण्डनीयाया भूमेरनीकं मुखम् । यथेन्द्रियाश्रयत्वान्मुखं प्रकाशकं तथैवमुषा भूमेः प्रकाशयित्रीत्यर्थः । यज्ञस्य केतुः ज्ञापयित्री [?] बृहती महती सती वि भाहि । प्रकाशयस्व । अपि च प्रशस्तिकृत् सम्यक् स्तुतमिति प्रशंसनं कुर्वती नोऽस्मदीयाय ब्रह्मणे मन्त्ररूपाय स्तोत्राय व्युच्छ । विवासय । तदनन्तरं हे विश्ववारे सर्वैर्वरणीये उषो नोऽस्मान् जने जनपदे आजनय । अभिमुख्येन प्रादुर्भावय । आवस्थापयेत्यर्थः ॥ [a few words doubtful [?]]

he uṣastvaṃ devānāṃ mātā jananī | uṣasi sarve devāḥ stutyā prabodhyante ataḥ sā tajjananavatītyucyate | ata evāditerdevānāṃ māturanīkaṃ pratyanīkaṃ pratispardhinī tvamityarthaḥ | yadvā | dīvyantīti devā raśmayaḥ | teṣāṃ nirmātrī aditerakhaṇḍanīyāyā bhūmeranīkaṃ mukham | yathendriyāśrayatvānmukhaṃ prakāśakaṃ tathaivamuṣā bhūmeḥ prakāśayitrītyarthaḥ | yajñasya ketuḥ jñāpayitrī [?] bṛhatī mahatī satī vi bhāhi | prakāśayasva | api ca praśastikṛt samyak stutamiti praśaṃsanaṃ kurvatī no 'smadīyāya brahmaṇe mantrarūpāya stotrāya vyuccha | vivāsaya | tadanantaraṃ he viśvavāre sarvairvaraṇīye uṣo no 'smān jane janapade ājanaya | abhimukhyena prādurbhāvaya | āvasthāpayetyarthaḥ ‖ [a few words doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "O Uṣas, thou art the mother (mātā, producer) of the gods: at Uṣas-time all the gods are awakened by praise; therefore she is said to have produced them. For that very reason aditeḥ anīkam — thou art the counterpart of Aditi, the mother of the gods, her rival, is the sense. Or: devāḥ are the rays, 'those that shine'; thou art their maker; aditeḥ, of the indivisible earth, anīkam, 'face': as the face, because it is the seat of the senses, is what shows, so Uṣas is the shower of the earth. Yajñasya ketuḥ — the one who makes the sacrifice known, thou, being great (bṛhatī), vi bhāhi, shine forth. Moreover, praśastikṛt — thou who makest praise, brahmaṇe naḥ, for our hymn-prayer (stotra) in the form of a mantra, vyuccha, dispel the darkness. And afterwards, O viśvavāre, desired (varaṇīya) by all, Uṣas, naḥ jane ā janaya — bring us forth among the people, make us appear to the front, cause us to be established, is the sense." The bhāṣya continues on the next page with the grammatical tail of bṛhatī.

[?]").

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"(he uṣaḥ tvam — O Uṣas deity, you) devānām — of all the deities (of the rays); mātā — the mother (the place of origin); aditeḥ — of Aditi (of the indivisible earth); anīkam — the counterpart (she who is like the face); yajñasya — of the sacrifices; ketuḥ — the one who makes known (you who are such); bṛhatī — in a large form; vi bhāhi — shine well; praśastikṛt — as the praiser of stotras; naḥ — our; brahmaṇe — to hear the stotras; vyuccha — dawn (afterwards); viśvavāre — O Uṣas deity desired by all; naḥ — us; jane — among the people; ā janaya — make us foremost (face-bearers)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Uṣas, goddess, you are the mother of all the gods (of all the rays); a counterpart of Aditi (like a face to the earth); the revealer of the sacrifice; being such, shine in a great form. Approve our hymns and dawn for us. You who are desired by all, make us foremost among the people."

English Translation (as printed)

Mother of the gods, rival of Aditi, illuminator of the sacrifice, mighty Ushas, shine forth ; approving of our prayer, dawn upon us ; you are cherished by all ; make us eminent among the people.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

माता देवानाम् — Mātā devānām — "he uṣaḥ tvaṃ devānāṃ jananī": "Uṣas is the mother of the deities. As soon as Uṣas has risen, the priests who praise the deities awaken the deities in the sacrifices; therefore the motherhood of the gods is proper to Uṣas.

original p. 92

देवशब्देनात्र आदित्या उच्यन्ते । तेषां हि माता उषाः । प्रतिमासं च आदित्यभेदमङ्गीकृत्य बहुवचनम् ॥ (स्कं. भा.)

devaśabdenātra ādityā ucyante | teṣāṃ hi mātā uṣāḥ | pratimāsaṃ ca ādityabhedamaṅgīkṛtya bahuvacanam ‖ (skaṃ. bhā.)

— by the word deva the Ādityas are meant, and Uṣas is the mother of them (since Uṣas rises before the rising of the Ādityas), and, accepting for each month a different Āditya, the plural is used in devānām, Skandasvāmin explains."

अदितेरनीकम् — Aditer anīkam — "devānāṃ mātuḥ anīkaṃ pratyanīkaṃ pratispardhinī": "she is a rival to the divine mother Aditi, because she is the mother of the deities, or of the Ādityas. Since upamā, utprekṣā and other ornaments are made to explain a quality or an action property, in this Ṛk, which resembles the style of poetry to a great extent, the motherhood of the gods is attributed to Uṣas, and the anīka-hood of Aditi is also stated. Or, because the devas are luminous, the word deva means 'rays'. Thus, because she creates rays, Uṣas has the motherhood of the gods. In the same way the word aditi means 'the indivisible earth'. As a face to this earth, Uṣas exists. Because she illuminates the senses and the rest, the word anīka conveys the meaning 'face': thus the Bhāṣyakāra explains that Uṣas illumines the earth." Skandasvāmin:

अदितिशब्देनात्र अदीनत्वात् समग्रं ज्योतिरुच्यते । अनीकशब्दोऽपि ब्राह्मणानीकमितिवत् समूहवचनम् । अदीनस्य समग्रस्य प्रकाशाख्यस्य ज्योतिषः समूहः । अथवा अनीकशब्दः स्वाङ्गमुखवचनः इहाग्रत्वसामान्यात् उषसि प्रयुज्यते । अदीनस्य समग्रस्य अहर्लक्षणस्य ज्योतिषो मुखभूतेत्यर्थः ॥ (स्कं. भा.)

aditiśabdenātra adīnatvāt samagraṃ jyotirucyate | anīkaśabdo 'pi brāhmaṇānīkamitivat samūhavacanam | adīnasya samagrasya prakāśākhyasya jyotiṣaḥ samūhaḥ | athavā anīkaśabdaḥ svāṅgamukhavacanaḥ ihāgratvasāmānyāt uṣasi prayujyate | adīnasya samagrasya aharlakṣaṇasya jyotiṣo mukhabhūtetyarthaḥ ‖ (skaṃ. bhā.)

"The word aditi here, because of 'not being poor' (adīnatva), means 'the whole light'. The word anīka (like brāhmaṇānīka) denotes 'a mass'. Hence aditer anīkam — the whole mass (samūha) of light, which is called 'luminous mass'; or the word anīka means 'face' of the whole, undiminished, body: here, by the likeness of being at the front, it is used of Uṣas. Because the word uṣas denotes 'being of the form of light', it is said that she is the face of the light called ahas, 'day', which is shining — thus says Skandasvāmin."

यज्ञस्य केतुः — Yajñasya ketuḥ — "since the word ketu denotes knowledge, [Uṣas] gives rise to the knowledge by which one performs the sacrifice."

original p. 93

ब्रह्मणे — Brahmaṇe — "mantrarūpāya stotrāya": "(for the stotra which is in the form of a mantra). The word brahma is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of wealth (Ni. 2-?? as read "2-10" [?]), so it conveys the meaning 'wealth'. Here it is used, however, in the sense of the stotra recited by those who perform sacrifice."

yat | citram | apnaḥ | uṣasaḥ | vahanti | ījānāya | śaśamānāya | bhadram | tat | naḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | mamahantām [as printed; a misprint for māmahantām? [?]] | aditiḥ | sindhuḥ | pṛthivī | uta | dyauḥ ‖ 20 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 113.20)

चित्रं चायनीयमप्न आप्तव्यं यद्धनमुषसो वहन्ति आनयन्ति । ईजानाय हविर्भिरिष्टवते शशमानाय स्तुतिभिः संभजमानाय पुरुषाय भद्रं भजनीयं तद्धनवतीति शेषः । यदनेन सूक्तेनास्माभिः प्रार्थितं तस्मिन्मित्रादयः षट् देवता मामहन्ताम् । पूजितं कुर्वन्तु ॥ [continued on the next page with the grammatical tail]

citraṃ cāyanīyamapna āptavyaṃ yaddhanamuṣaso vahanti ānayanti | ījānāya havirbhiriṣṭavate śaśamānāya stutibhiḥ saṃbhajamānāya puruṣāya bhadraṃ bhajanīyaṃ taddhanavatīti śeṣaḥ | yadanena sūktenāsmābhiḥ prārthitaṃ tasminmitrādayaḥ ṣaṭ devatā māmahantām | pūjitaṃ kurvantu ‖ [continued on the next page with the grammatical tail]

Sense (mine): "The wonderful (citra), worthy-to-be-gained (apnaḥ) wealth that the Uṣases bring (vahanti) — good (bhadra), to be enjoyed, for the man ījānāya, who has sacrificed with oblations, and śaśamānāya, who praises with hymns: may [the Uṣases] have that wealth — is the completion. What has been prayed for by us in this Sūkta, in that may these six deities, Mitra and the rest, māmahantām — make it honoured, make it worthy (made to be of success)."

original p. 95

Grammatical tail of the bhāṣya on Ṛk 20 (characterized, not transcribed): apnaḥ (āp(ḷ) "to obtain" — the asun suffix by the Uṇādi rule with the wide reading of "bahulam"; the shortening of the root vowel and the augment nuṭ); ījānāya (yaj, liṭ in the Veda; kānac; vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti — saṃprasāraṇa; doubling; the lengthening of the reduplication); śaśamānāya (śaś "to leap" [printed: śaśa plutagatau]; tācchīlya suffix cānaś; śap elided in the liṭ sense; the accent by sarvadhātukāsvarābhāve…).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"citram — wonderful; apnaḥ — which should be obtained; yat — which wealth; uṣasaḥ — the Uṣas deities; vahanti — bring (that); ījānāya — to him who performs sacrifice with oblations; śaśamānāya — to him who praises; bhadram — becomes auspicious; naḥ — our; tat — (the prayer made by this Sūkta); mitraḥ — Mitra; varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa; aditiḥ — Aditi; sindhuḥ — the deity of the ocean; pṛthivī — the earth; uta — and; dyauḥ — the atmosphere (the deity of heaven and the rest); mamahantām — let (them) protect, let them approve."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"All the desired wealth that the Uṣases bring makes for auspiciousness for those who offer sacrifice and those who praise. Let Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth and the deities of the atmosphere protect this praise or prayer that has been made by this Sūkta."

English Translation (as printed)

Whatever valuable wealth the Ushasas convey, is beneficial to the sacrificer and to the praiser. May Mitra, Varuna, Aditi,—ocean, earth and heaven, be favourable to this our prayer.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अप्नः — Apnaḥ — "āptavyam": "worthy to be obtained, desired by all. The word apnas is stated among the twenty-six [as read] words denoting action (karma) (Ni. 2-1 [as read, [?]])."

चित्रम् — Citram — "cāyanīyaṃ pūjyam": "worthy of honour. The word citra is read (Ni. 3-?? and 3-? as read [?]) in the meaning 'cāyanīya', 'maṃhanīya' (worthy of honour, worthy to be given)."

शशमानाय — Śaśamānāya — "stutibhiḥ saṃbhajamānāya puruṣāya": "to the man who, praising with stotras, serves; that is, to the sacrificer. The Nirukta-writer —

original p. 96

— explaining the word śaśamāna ... [śaśamānaḥ śaṃsamānaḥ (Ni. 6-8 as read [?])] as 'śaṃsamāna', 'praising', says 'yo vāṃ yajñaiḥ śaśamāno ha dāśati ity api nigamo bhavati' ('there is also this Vedic passage'):

यो वां यज्ञैः शशमानो ह दाशति कविर्होता यजति मन्मसाधनः । उपाह तं गच्छथो वीथो अध्वरमच्छा गिरः सुमतिं गन्तमस्मयू ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१५१-७ [as read; numeral small, [?]])

yo vāṃ yajñaiḥ śaśamāno ha dāśati kavirhotā yajati manmasādhanaḥ | upāha taṃ gacchatho vītho adhvaramacchā giraḥ sumatiṃ gantamasmayū ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-151-7 [as read; numeral small, [?]])

— he has cited this Ṛk."

भद्रम् — Bhadram — "bhajanīyam": "worthy of being obtained. The goddess Uṣas gives wealth, which is the most worthy to be obtained, to those who perform sacrifice with oblations and to those who praise with stotras, with hymns of praise. The chief intention is that by the recitation of this Sūkta, which is in the form of a stotra of this goddess Uṣas, the deities Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the ocean, Earth, the Atmosphere [and so on] may accept our prayer and show us favour."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 20; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on apnaḥ (āp(ḷ) "to obtain", with the sense of action given by āpaḥ karmākhyāyāṃ hrasvo nuṭ ca vā, Uṇ. 4-?? as read [?]; since the word "bahulam" is wide in the Uṇādi, the suffix asun arises even when the sense of action is absent; the root vowel shortened; the augment nuṭ; the stem apnas; the first-syllable accent by jñityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197 as read [?]), vahanti (vah "to carry", laṭ 3rd plural; no nighāta here, because yat precedes — yadvṛttānnityam [as printed, "nipātair yad yadi…", Pā. 8-1-30 as read [?]]; the ending, being adupadeśa, unaccented, the root accent remains by tāsyanudāttet…), ījānāya (yaj, liṭ in the Vedic sense by chandasi liṭ… the kānac substitution by liṭaḥ kānajvā; the saṃprasāraṇa of the ya by vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti; doubling; the reduplication's ā-lengthening and elision of the consonant; citaḥ final accent; dative singular), śaśamānāya (śaś "to leap, to go"; cānaś by tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu cānaś; śap; the augment muk by āne muk, for the a of the stem…).

original p. 97

Grammar page of Ṛk 20, concluded (noted briefly): śaśamānāya — the cānaś is sārvadhātuka, so adupadeśa causes the sārvadhātuka unaccentedness; since it is cit, the final syllable is accented by citaḥ, Pā. 6-1-163 as read [?], and the accent is on the last syllable of the stem; dative singular as before. Bhadram (bhadi "to be auspicious, to be happy" [printed: bhadi kalyāṇe sukhe ca]; the Uṇādi suffix ra; the accent on the last syllable from the suffix). The other words were explained above. ‖ 20 ‖

Colophon: nūrahadimūraneya sūkta samāptavu — "The hundred-and-thirteenth Sūkta is ended."

End of Sūkta 113 (Ṛks 1–20, printed pp. 2–97; Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 16). The page continues with the opening of Sūkta 114 (the one hundred-and-fourteenth, "imā rudrāya"), which is not part of this unit.

Sūkta 114 — "imā rudrāya"

original p. 97,

श्रीः / सूक्तम् ११४ — Heading (Kannada): "nūrahadinālkaneya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-fourteenth Sūkta."

Anukramaṇī (Sanskrit, as printed):

इमा रुद्रायेत्येकादशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं कुत्सस्यार्षम् । दशम्येकादश्यौ त्रिष्टुभौ शिष्टा नव जगत्यः । रुद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । इमा एकादश रौद्रं द्विः त्रिष्टुबन्तमिति ॥ शूलगवादिषु रुद्रदेवत्येषु कर्मसु अनेन सूक्तेन दिगुपस्थेया । तथा च सूत्रितम् । कद्रुद्रायेमा रुद्रायो ते पितरिमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिर इति सर्वरुद्रयज्ञेषु दिशामुपस्थानम् । आ. गृ. ४-८-३० । इति ॥

imā rudrāyetyekādaśarcaṃ navamaṃ sūktaṃ kutsasyārṣam | daśamyekādaśyau triṣṭubhau śiṣṭā nava jagatyaḥ | rudro devatā | tathā cānukrāntam | imā ekādaśa raudraṃ dviḥ triṣṭubantamiti ‖ śūlagavādiṣu rudradevatyeṣu karmasu anena sūktena digupastheyā | tathā ca sūtritam | kadrudrāyemā rudrāyo te pitarimā rudrāya sthiradhanvane gira iti sarvarudrayajñeṣu diśāmupasthānam | ā. gṛ. 4-8-30 | iti ‖

Sense: "'imā rudrāya' — the ninth sūkta (of this anuvāka), of eleven Ṛks, the ṛṣi's work being Kutsa's. The tenth and eleventh are Triṣṭubh, the remaining nine Jagatī. The deity is Rudra; so the Anukramaṇī says 'imā ekādaśa raudraṃ dviḥ triṣṭubantam'. In rites addressed to Rudra such as the śūlagava, the quarters are to be worshipped with this sūkta; and so the Sūtra says: 'kad rudrāya', 'imā rudrāya', 'yo te pitar' (?), 'imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane gira iti — in all Rudra sacrifices the worship of the quarters' (Āśv. Gṛ. 4-8-30 as printed [?])."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "This sūkta, imā rudrāya, is the ninth sūkta in the sixteenth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. The ṛṣi is Kutsa, son of Aṅgiras; the deity is Rudra. The tenth and eleventh Ṛks are in Triṣṭubh metre; the others are Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā: 'imā ekādaśa raudraṃ dviḥ triṣṭubantam'. In the rites related to Rudra such as the śūlagava, the quarters are to be worshipped with this sūkta; it is explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra, 4-8-30 [as printed]."

original p. 98

सूक्त—११४ (Sūkta 114) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१६ ॥ सूक्त—११४ ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—५, ६ ॥ small numerals; read as printed Number of Ṛks: 11. Ṛṣi: Kutsa Āṅgirasa. Devatā: Rudra. Chandas: Ṛks 1–9 Jagatī; 10–11 Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.1)

इमा रुद्राय तवसे कपर्दिने क्षयद्वीराय प्र भरामहे मतीः । यथा शमसद्द्विपदे चतुष्पदे विश्वं पुष्टं ग्रामे अस्मिन्ननातुरम् ॥ १ ॥

imā rudrāya tavase kapardine kṣayadvīrāya pra bharāmahe matīḥ | yathā śamasaddvipade catuṣpade viśvaṃ puṣṭaṃ grāme asminnanāturam ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.1)

इमाः । रुद्राय । तवसे । कपर्दिने । क्षयत्ऽवीराय । प्र । भरामहे । मतीः । यथा । शम् । असत् । द्विऽपदे । चतुःऽपदे । विश्वम् । पुष्टम् । ग्रामे । अस्मिन् । अनातुरम् ॥ १ ॥

imāḥ | rudrāya | tavase | kapardine | kṣayat 'vīrāya | pra | bharāmahe | matīḥ | yathā | śam | asat | dvi 'pade | catuḥ 'pade | viśvam | puṣṭam | grāme | asmin | anāturam ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.1)

रुद्राय । रोदयति सर्वमन्तकाल इति रुद्रः । यद्वा । रुशं संसाराख्यं दुःखं द्रावयति विनाशयतीति रुद्रः । यद्वा । रुतः शब्दरूपा उपनिषदः ताभिर्द्रूयते गम्यते प्रतिपाद्यत इति रुद्रः । यद्वा । रुत् शब्दात्मिका वाणी तत्प्रतिपाद्यापि विद्या वा तामुपासकेभ्यो राति ददातीति रुद्रः । यद्वा । रुणद्भ्याव्योतीति रुदेन्धकारादि [?] । तद्द्रावयति विदारयतीति रुद्रः । यद्वा । कदाचिद्देवासुरसंग्रामे ग्न्यात्मको रुद्रो देवैर्निक्षिप्तं धनमपहृत्य निरगात् । असुराञ्जित्वा देवा एनमन्विष्य दृष्ट्वा धनमपाहरन् । तदानीमरुदत् । तस्माद्रुद्र इत्याख्यायते । तथा च तैत्तिरीयकम् । सोऽरोदीद्यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम् । तै. सं. १-५-१-१ । इति । तस्मै रुद्राय मतीर्मननीया इमा स्तुतीः प्र भरामहे । प्रकर्षेण निष्पादयामः । कीदृशाय । तवसे प्रवृद्धाय कपर्दिने जटिलाय क्षयद्वीराय क्षयन्तो विनश्यन्तो वीरा यस्मिन्नादृशाय । यद्वा । क्षयतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । क्षयन्तः प्राप्तैश्वर्या वीरा मरुद्गणाः पुत्रा यस्य तस्मै । यथा येन प्रकारेण शं शमनीयानां रोगाणामुपशमनं द्विपदेऽस्मदीयाय मनुष्याय चतुष्पदे गवाश्वप्रभृतये चासत् भवेत् तेन प्रकारेण स्तुतीः कुर्म इत्यर्थः । अत्रोऽस्मिन्नस्मदीये ग्रामे वर्तमानं विश्वं सर्वं प्राणिजातमनातुरम् आतुरो रुग्णः । तद्रहितं सत् पुष्टं प्रवृद्धं भवतु ॥ [the grammatical tail follows in the print; the Sanskrit above is read letter by letter from small type; the words marked [?] are doubtful]

rudrāya | rodayati sarvamantakāla iti rudraḥ | yadvā | ruśaṃ saṃsārākhyaṃ duḥkhaṃ drāvayati vināśayatīti rudraḥ | yadvā | rutaḥ śabdarūpā upaniṣadaḥ tābhirdrūyate gamyate pratipādyata iti rudraḥ | yadvā | rut śabdātmikā vāṇī tatpratipādyāpi vidyā vā tāmupāsakebhyo rāti dadātīti rudraḥ | yadvā | ruṇadbhyāvyotīti rudendhakārādi [?] | taddrāvayati vidārayatīti rudraḥ | yadvā | kadāciddevāsurasaṃgrāme gnyātmako rudro devairnikṣiptaṃ dhanamapahṛtya niragāt | asurāñjitvā devā enamanviṣya dṛṣṭvā dhanamapāharan | tadānīmarudat | tasmādrudra ityākhyāyate | tathā ca taittirīyakam | so 'rodīdyadarodīttadrudrasya rudratvam | tai. saṃ. 1-5-1-1 | iti | tasmai rudrāya matīrmananīyā imā stutīḥ pra bharāmahe | prakarṣeṇa niṣpādayāmaḥ | kīdṛśāya | tavase pravṛddhāya kapardine jaṭilāya kṣayadvīrāya kṣayanto vinaśyanto vīrā yasminnādṛśāya | yadvā | kṣayatiraiśvaryakarmā | kṣayantaḥ prāptaiśvaryā vīrā marudgaṇāḥ putrā yasya tasmai | yathā yena prakāreṇa śaṃ śamanīyānāṃ rogāṇāmupaśamanaṃ dvipade 'smadīyāya manuṣyāya catuṣpade gavāśvaprabhṛtaye cāsat bhavet tena prakāreṇa stutīḥ kurma ityarthaḥ | atro 'sminnasmadīye grāme vartamānaṃ viśvaṃ sarvaṃ prāṇijātamanāturam āturo rugṇaḥ | tadrahitaṃ sat puṣṭaṃ pravṛddhaṃ bhavatu ‖ [the grammatical tail follows in the print; the Sanskrit above is read letter by letter from small type; the words marked [?] are doubtful]

Sense (mine): "Rudrāya — Rudra is he who makes all weep (rodayati) at the end of time; or he who drives away (drāvayati) the sorrow called saṃsāra; or he who is approached (drūyate) by the ruta — the Upaniṣads of the nature of sound; or he who gives (rāti) to his worshippers the rut, speech, or the knowledge taught by it; or he who rends the darkness [?]. Or: once, in a battle of gods and asuras, Rudra, of the nature of fire, took away the wealth the gods had deposited and went off; the gods, having conquered the asuras, sought him, found him, and took the wealth back; he then wept (arudat); hence he is called Rudra: so also the Taittirīya (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-1-1 as printed [?]): 'He wept; that he wept is the Rudra-hood of Rudra'. To that Rudra we pra bharāmahe, we present, these matīḥ, thoughtful praises. To what sort of Rudra? Tavase — grown great; kapardine — with matted hair; kṣayadvīrāya — in whom heroes perish; or, kṣayati meaning lordship, he whose sons, the Marut hosts, are lords. So that (yathā) śam — cure of diseases — may be for our two-footed (men) and four-footed (cattle, horses…), in this way we make our praises. And may all the beings in this our village be anāturam, free from sickness, and puṣṭam, well nourished."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): tavase (tu "to grow", suffix asun by Uṇ., Uṇ. number as read "2-?? [?]"); kṣayadvīrāya (kṣi "to dwell, to rule"; śatṛ with the Vedic accent: a bahuvrīhi, first member keeps its accent); asat (as "to be", leṭ with the augment aṭ, the i elided); dvipade (dvau pādau yasya; pād → pad by saṃkhyāsupūrvasya [Pā. 5-4-140 as read, [?]]); catuṣpade (svarasya… bahuvrīhi first-member accent, sañjñā); ātura (tur "to hurry" with ā; the first-syllable accent).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) printed on pp. 99–100

"tavase — (to) him who is of great strength; kapardine — (to) him who bears matted locks on his head; kṣayadvīrāya — (to) him who destroys enemy heroes in battle, or [him who] is lordly, and who has heroes (the Marut deities) as sons; rudrāya — (to) Rudra (who, at the time of dissolution, makes all weep; or who destroys the sorrow of saṃsāra; or who is conveyed in words — known by the upaniṣads; or who gives to his worshippers the desired objects; or who removes the darkness of ignorance; or [the story:] when in a battle of gods and asuras this Rudra took away the wealth deposited, the gods, after conquering the asuras, sought him and took back the wealth; then Rudra wept in sorrow — therefore he is called Rudra) —

original p. 100

— imāḥ matīḥ — these stotras of ours, made with thought; pra bharāmahe — (with devotion) we offer; yathā — in what way (by thus offering the stotras); dvipade — for us men who have two feet; catuṣpade — for cattle, horses and other four-footed creatures; śam — happiness free from disease and other calamities; asat — shall come; asmin grāme — in this village (where we dwell); viśvam — all the creatures (humans and others); anāturam — free from disease; puṣṭam — and nourished: such a Rudra we offer these stotras to."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"To the deity called Rudra — of great strength, bearing matted hair on the head, destroyer of enemy heroes in battle, or [one] who has the lordly Marut deities as sons — we offer these stotras with devotion. By offering the stotras thus, may there be happiness, free from diseases and calamities, for men and for cattle and other beasts; and that all creatures, men and others, in this our village may be free from disease and be nourished, we offer these stotras with devotion to Rudra."

English Translation (as printed)

We offer these praises to the mighty Rudra, with the braided hair, the destroyer of heroes, in order that health may be enjoyed by bipeds, and quadrupeds, and that all beings in this village may be (well) nourished and exempt from disease.

original p. 101

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रुद्राय — Rudrāya. "Sāyaṇa has explained the word rudra in six ways. The word rudra is formed from the root ruḍ in the causative (ṇic). Yāska says 'rudro rauty-ucyamāno ruroyamāṇo dravati vā rodayater vā' [as printed: rudro rauti śabdaṃ karoti…] — rudra is he who makes a sound (rauti, from ru, stan 'thunders'), i.e. one who thunders like a cloud; or who runs (dravati) making a sound, in the middle of the sky; or from rodayati, 'makes to weep': he who makes the enemies weep, i.e. makes them rule [?] by his works — so he explains. Further, following the history related in the Kauṣītaki [Brāhmaṇa — as read, 'kauṣohanisathi', doubtful [?]] — that Prajāpati, seeing his own daughter, was struck by arrows and made distressed — or following the intention of a branch of the Maitrāyaṇīya school, 'yad arodīt tad rudrasya rudratvam': because he wept he is Rudra (Ni. 10-? as read [?]) he has explained the sense of the word. Sāyaṇa's explanation of the word rudra is other than this: that at the time of dissolution he makes all weep; or destroys the sorrow of saṃsāra; or, because he is pratipādya (to be taught) by the Upaniṣads of the nature of sound; or because he teaches self-knowledge to seekers of self-knowledge; or because he destroys the ignorance that veils knowledge as a cloud veils light: thus having shown the different meanings of the word rudra arising from the meaning of the root ruta…"

"And in the opinion of the Itihāsa-writers, according to the history specified, he explains the sense of the word rudra, from the root rudir 'to shed tears' (aśruvimocane), by the śruti-statement 'so 'rodīd yad arodīt tad rudrasya rudratvam' (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-1-1 as printed [?]). From this the greatness of Rudra and the cause of his hostility toward living beings become manifest."

मतीः — Matīḥ — "mananīyāḥ": worthy of thought. "Among the forty-four [as read] arcati-names 'arcati, gāyati' and so on, the word manyate is stated (Ni. 3-14 as read [?]); so the meaning is 'worthy of worship' or 'praise'."

तवसे — Tavase — "pravṛddhāya": "since the word tavas is read among the twenty-eight [as read] names of strength 'ojaḥ, pājaḥ' (Ni. 2-9 as read [?]), the meaning is 'strong'."

क्षयद्वीराय — Kṣayadvīrāya — "kṣayanto vinaśyanto vīrā yasmin tādṛśāya | yadvā …"

original p. 102

"… kṣayante prāptaiśvaryāḥ vīrāḥ marudgaṇāḥ yasya: Sāyaṇa explains this word as an epithet of Rudra, 'one who destroys heroes, or one who has as sons the Marut hosts, who possess lordship'. Skandasvāmin, explaining the word in the way Sāyaṇa did, says:

क्षयद्वीरायेति — क्षि निवासगत्योः इत्यस्य क्षियतेर्वा गतिकर्मणो रूपं शुद्धोऽपि चात्र सामर्थ्यात् अभिपूर्वार्थे द्रष्टव्यम् । वीराणामपि शत्रूणामभिगन्ता क्षयद्वीरः । आत्मीयानां वीराणामभिप्रेतेषु निवासयिता क्षयद्वीरः ॥

kṣayadvīrāyeti — kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ ityasya kṣiyatervā gatikarmaṇo rūpaṃ śuddho 'pi cātra sāmarthyāt abhipūrvārthe draṣṭavyam | vīrāṇāmapi śatrūṇāmabhigantā kṣayadvīraḥ | ātmīyānāṃ vīrāṇāmabhipreteṣu nivāsayitā kṣayadvīraḥ ‖

— the word kṣayat, contained in the word kṣayadvīra, has the sense of 'dwelling' and 'going' (from the root kṣi), and, though the prefix abhi is not there, conveys the meaning of the prefix abhi. He explains the meaning: 'kṣayadvīra — one who goes against heroic enemies and fights them; or one who causes his own heroes to dwell in the places they desire'."

शम् — Śam — "since the word śam is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of happiness 'śiṃbātā, śatarā' (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), the meaning is 'happiness'. Yāska, in explaining the word śaṃyoḥ (śaṃ ca yoś ca), says 'śaṃ śamanaṃ ca rogāṇām' — the cure of diseases and happiness; and he cites this Mantra to give the sense of happiness —

अग्निदेवमुमते त्वं मन्यासै शं च नस्कृधि । क्रत्वे दक्षाय नो हि नु प्रण आयूंषि तारिषः ॥ [first words doubtful [?]] (वा. सं. ३८-५ [as read; Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā]) "

agnidevamumate tvaṃ manyāsai śaṃ ca naskṛdhi | kratve dakṣāya no hi nu praṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣaḥ ‖ [first words doubtful [?]] (vā. saṃ. 38-5 [as read; Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā]) "

द्विपदे — Dvipade — "dvau pādāv asya": one who has two feet.

यथा शम् असत् — Yathā śam asat — "the word asat is formed from the root as 'to be'. Sāyaṇa explains this as 'bhavet' (may be), and Skandasvāmin as 'bhavati' (is). The purport is: we praise Rudra so that he may favour us, that all who live in our dwelling — men with two feet, and beasts with four feet, with others besides — may live in comfort, free from disease."

original p. 103

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly)

Grammar page on rudrāya (rudir "to shed tears"; the suffix rak by roder nir luk ca (Uṇ. 2-?? as read [?]); being kit, no guṇa of the penultimate; accent from the suffix; dative singular), tavase (tu "to grow", a root fixed by sūtra in the sense of growth; Uṇādi suffix asi/asun; the a accented by the suffix; dative), kṣayadvīrāya (kṣi "to dwell/to rule"; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; guṇa and ayādeśa; chandasy ubhayathā, Pā. 3-4-117 as read [?], making the śatṛ ārdhadhātuka; the accent of the sārvadhātuka being unaccented because of adupadeśa, the udātta of the root remains; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam — first-member accent; dative), bharāmahe (bhṛñ "to bear", laṭ 1st plural; nighāta), yathā (nipātasya ca — lengthening in the Saṃhitā, Pā. 6-3-136 as read [?]), asat (as "to be", leṭ 3rd singular; the augment aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau; elision of i by itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; nighāta prevented by nipātair yad yadi… because yathā precedes, Pā. 8-1-30 as read [?]), dvipade (dvau pādau asya — dvipāt; saṃkhyāsupūrvasya, Pā. 5-4-140 as read [?], the final elision of pāda; pād → pad by pāde pat, Pā. 6-4-130 as read [?]; the rule that the part-change does not apply separately (ekadeśavikṛtam ananyavat, Paribh. 33 [?]); dvitribhyāṃ pād-daN-mūrdhasu bahuvrīhau, Pā. 6-2-197 as read [?], the first syllable of the later member accented).

original p. 104

Grammar page, concluded: catuṣpade (catvāraḥ pādā asya; as before; the first-member accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam, Pā. 6-2-1 as read [?]; since catur ends in r, the first syllable is accented by kṛṣṇasaṃkhyāyoḥ [as printed "phiṣ saṃkhyāyoḥ, Phi. 2-?"]); puṣṭam (puṣ "to nourish", niṣṭhā — kta; ṭatva of the t after ṣ; final accent from the suffix; accusative singular); anāturam (na vidyate āturaḥ yasya; nañsubhyām — Pā. 6-2-172 as read [?], the later member's first-syllable accent); asmin (ūḍidaṃpadādi, Pā. 6-1-171 as read [?], the accent of the ending). ‖ 1 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.2)

मृळा नो रुद्रोत नो मयस्कृधि क्षयद्वीराय नमसा विधेम ते । यच्छं च योश्च मनुरायेजे पिता तदश्याम तव रुद्र प्रणीतिषु ॥ २ ॥

mṛḷā no rudrota no mayaskṛdhi kṣayadvīrāya namasā vidhema te | yacchaṃ ca yośca manurāyeje pitā tadaśyāma tava rudra praṇītiṣu ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.2)

मृळ । नः । रुद्र । उत । नः । मयः । कृधि । क्षयत्ऽवीराय । नमसा । विधेम । ते ॥ यत् । शम् । च । योः । च । मनुः । आऽयेजे । पिता । तत् । अश्याम । तव । रुद्र । प्रऽनीतिषु ॥ २ ॥

mṛḷa | naḥ | rudra | uta | naḥ | mayaḥ | kṛdhi | kṣayat 'vīrāya | namasā | vidhema | te ‖ yat | śam | ca | yoḥ | ca | manuḥ | ā 'yeje | pitā | tat | aśyāma | tava | rudra | pra 'nītiṣu ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 105

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.2)

रुद्रदेवत्ये पशौ वपापुरोडाशयोर्मृळा नो रुद्रेत्यादिके द्वे अनुवाक्ये । तथा च सूत्रितम् । मृळा नो रुद्रोत नो मयस्कृधीति द्वे आ ते पितर्मरुतां सुम्नमेतु । आश्व. ३-८ [?] । इति ॥ हे रुद्र नोऽस्मभ्यमस्मदर्थं मृळ । शं सुखयिता भव । उताप्यपि च तदनन्तरं नोऽस्माकं मयः सुखं कृधि । कुरु । वयं च क्षयद्वीराय प्रसृतसर्ववीरं प्राप्तैश्वर्यैर्मरुद्भिर्युक्तं वा ते त्वां नमसा हविर्लक्षणेनान्नेन नमस्कारेण वा विधेम । परिचरेम । विधतिः परिचरणकर्मा । अपि च पिता उत्पादको मनुः स्वकीयेभ्यः प्रजाभ्यः शं रोगाणां शमनं योश्च भयानां यावनं च यदेतद्द्वयमायेजे देवेभ्यः सकाशात्प्राप्य दत्तवान् । हे रुद्र तव प्रणीतिषु प्रकृष्टनयनेषु सत्सु तद्द्वयमश्यामः । व्याप्नुयाम ॥

rudradevatye paśau vapāpuroḍāśayormṛḷā no rudretyādike dve anuvākye | tathā ca sūtritam | mṛḷā no rudrota no mayaskṛdhīti dve ā te pitarmarutāṃ sumnametu | āśva. 3-8 [?] | iti ‖ he rudra no 'smabhyamasmadarthaṃ mṛḷa | śaṃ sukhayitā bhava | utāpyapi ca tadanantaraṃ no 'smākaṃ mayaḥ sukhaṃ kṛdhi | kuru | vayaṃ ca kṣayadvīrāya prasṛtasarvavīraṃ prāptaiśvaryairmarudbhiryuktaṃ vā te tvāṃ namasā havirlakṣaṇenānnena namaskāreṇa vā vidhema | paricarema | vidhatiḥ paricaraṇakarmā | api ca pitā utpādako manuḥ svakīyebhyaḥ prajābhyaḥ śaṃ rogāṇāṃ śamanaṃ yośca bhayānāṃ yāvanaṃ ca yadetaddvayamāyeje devebhyaḥ sakāśātprāpya dattavān | he rudra tava praṇītiṣu prakṛṣṭanayaneṣu satsu taddvayamaśyāmaḥ | vyāpnuyāma ‖

Sense (mine): "For the animal sacrifice addressed to Rudra, 'mṛḷā no rudra' and 'uta no' are the two anuvākyā verses for the omentum and the cake; and the Sūtra says 'mṛḷā no rudra uta no mayas kṛdhi — these two; and ā te pitar marutāṃ sumnam etu' (Āśv. 3-8 as read [?]). O Rudra, be gracious to us — mṛḷa, be a giver of śam, comfort; and then also make mayas, happiness, for us. And we vidhema, serve (the root vidh means 'to attend on') thee, kṣayadvīrāya — who hast heroes spread out everywhere, or who art joined by the Maruts who have lordship — with namasā, food in the form of oblation, or salutation. And that pair, śam (cure of diseases) and yoḥ (driving off of fears), which our progenitor Manu obtained from the gods and gave (āyeje) to his own people — O Rudra, may we reach that pair, under thy praṇīti, thy excellent guidance."

Grammatical tail: mṛḷa (mṛḍ "to be gracious", tudādi; dyāv → lengthening in the Saṃhitā); kṛdhi (kṛ with hi → dhi, u elided by śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi hedhiḥ); mayaḥ (the visarga); kṣayadvīrāya (the verb-governing dative); vidhema (vidh "to arrange/serve", tudādi); āyeje (yaj, liṭ, saṃprasāraṇa not applied before the e: vityabhyāsalopaḥ); aśyāma (aśū "to pervade", the parasmaipada by vyatyaya; vikaraṇa elided by bahulaṃ chandasi). Sūtra numbers small; not given.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he rudra — O Rudra; naḥ — to us; mṛḷa — make comfort; uta — and; naḥ — to us; mayaḥ kṛdhi — make happiness (we also); kṣayadvīrāya — (to) him who has destroyed heroes; te — to you (or, to thy self); namasā — with oblation or salutations (praising and so on); vidhema — let us serve; he rudra — O Rudra; pitā — the progenitor; manuḥ — Manu (for his own descendants); śam — the cure of disease and so on; yoḥ — freedom from fear; yat — which (of the two); ā yeje — obtained from the gods and gave; tat — those; tava — thy; praṇītiṣu — under the leading of thy [kindly] look; aśyāma — may we obtain (from thee)."

original p. 106

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Rudra, be gracious to us; make happiness for us; we also serve thee with oblations and salutations. May thou graciously favour us, who trust in thee alone, with the freedom from diseases and the freedom from fears which Manu, the primal ancestor of us all, obtained from the deities and gave to us."

English Translation (as printed)

Be gracious to us, Rudra ; grant us happiness, for we worship the destroyer of heroes with oblations ; and by your directions, Rudra, may we obtain that freedom from disease and exemption from dangers which our progenitor, Manu, bestowed upon us, (having obtained them from the gods.)

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

"Of the Ṛks in the vapā and purodāśa offerings related to Rudra, the first two, 'mṛḷā no rudra', are to be used as puroanuvākyā mantras, says the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, citing 'mṛḷā no rudro ta no mayas kṛdhīti dve ā te pitar marutāṃ sumnam etu' (Āś. 3-8 as read [?])."

मयः — Mayaḥ — "sukham": happiness. "The word mayas is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of happiness (Ni. 3-?? as read [?])."

क्षयद्वीराय — Kṣayadvīrāya — "kṣapitasarvavīraṃ prāptaiśvaryair marudbhir yuktaṃ vā": "the meaning of this word has been explained in the previous Ṛk. The Nirukta-writer explains it as 'one who has the strength to destroy heroes' (vīrān kṣapayati), and cites —

इमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिरः क्षिप्रेषवे देवाय स्वधाव्ने । अषाळ्हाय सहमानाय वेधसे तिग्मायुधाय भरता शृणोतु नः ॥ (नि. १०-२ and ऋ. सं. २-३३-६ [as read])

imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane giraḥ kṣipreṣave devāya svadhāvne | aṣāḷhāya sahamānāya vedhase tigmāyudhāya bharatā śṛṇotu naḥ ‖ (ni. 10-2 and ṛ. saṃ. 2-33-6 [as read])

as an example of this Ṛk" —

दृढधन्वने — स्थिरधन्वने । क्षिप्रेषवे — शीघ्रं बाणान् मुञ्चते । देवाय — दानादिगुणयुक्ताय । स्वधाव्ने — अन्नवते । अषाळ्हाय —

dṛḍhadhanvane — sthiradhanvane | kṣipreṣave — śīghraṃ bāṇān muñcate | devāya — dānādiguṇayuktāya | svadhāvne — annavate | aṣāḷhāya —

original p. 107

— इतरेण तिरस्कारं अप्राप्ताय । सहमानाय — शत्रूनभिभवित्रे । तिग्मायुधाय — तीक्ष्णायुधवते । रुद्राय — रुद्राय । इमा गिरः — इमाः स्तुतीः ।

— itareṇa tiraskāraṃ aprāptāya | sahamānāya — śatrūnabhibhavitre | tigmāyudhāya — tīkṣṇāyudhavate | rudrāya — rudrāya | imā giraḥ — imāḥ stutīḥ |

"'sthiradhanvane' — to him of firm bow; 'kṣipreṣave' — who quickly looses arrows; 'devāya' — endowed with the qualities of giving and the like; 'svadhāvne' — who has food; 'aṣāḷhāya' — who has never been overcome (insulted) by another; 'sahamānāya' — who always overcomes enemies; 'tigmāyudhāya' — who has sharp weapons; 'rudrāya' — to Rudra; 'imā giraḥ' — these praises': he explains the meaning 'we speak these stotras'. On the matter that the Maruts are the sons of Rudra —

प्र यो शुम्भन्ते जनयो न सप्तयो यामन्रुद्रस्य सूनवः सुदंससः । रोदसी हि मरुतश्चक्रिरे वृधे मदन्ति वीरा विदथेषु घृष्वयः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-८५-१ [as read])

pra yo śumbhante janayo na saptayo yāmanrudrasya sūnavaḥ sudaṃsasaḥ | rodasī hi marutaścakrire vṛdhe madanti vīrā vidatheṣu ghṛṣvayaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-85-1 [as read])

— as said in this Ṛk, the Maruts are the sons of Rudra, and their excellence also is described as exceeding."

मृळ — Mṛḷa — "tvaṃ sukhayitā bhava: 'do thou give happiness.' From the root mṛḍa 'to be gracious', in the sense 'make happy'; the address to Rudra by 'mṛḷa' and the request 'mayaskṛdhi' — 'give happiness' — is described here. From this the greatness of Rudra — that he subdues the wicked and protects those who take refuge in him — becomes plain."

मनुरा येजे पिता — Manur āyeje pitā — "pitā manuḥ — Manu, the father; śaṃ ca rogāṇāṃ śamanaṃ yoś ca bhayānāṃ yāvanaṃ ca: [the pair] the quieting of diseases, and the keeping-off of fears: Sāyaṇa explains that Manu worshipped thee, having obtained these from the deities, with sacrifices. Skandasvāmin, making the construction go in the same sense, explains that śam means the cessation of diseases come from the past, and that yoḥ means the keeping-off of those that may come later through distress (aniṣṭa); and that Manu worshipped Rudra with sacrifice and obtained both for his people."

मनुः — Manu: "Though the name Manu is read in many places in the Ṛgveda, a fuller account is nowhere found. Manu may be understood as the primal ancestor of the Mānava line and the guide in the order of performing sacrifices. [Here follows a legend:] When he was giving his estate to his sons, the youngest, Nābhānediṣṭha, was studying in the gurukula as a brahmacārin; so no share had been left for him; having finished his studies he came and, to ask for his share, asked his father (Manu); [Manu told him]: 'Go to the place where the Aṅgirases are performing a sacrifice; if you teach them certain mantras they will give you as much wealth as you want' —" continues on the next page

original p. 108

"… [the Aṅgirases] would give him wealth': so [Manu] said." The sentence is cut at the top of the page; the sense is as above. "This story is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda; since the sacrifice made by this Manu is famous, the matter of Manu's sacrifice is alluded to in various places in the Ṛgveda. The matter of this Manu is stated also outside the Ṛgveda: in the Atharvaveda; the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (references printed as a cluster of small numerals — 1-5-1-3 [?], 2-5-1-3 [?], 3-1-6-1 [?], 3-1-9-4 [?], 5-… [?] — I cannot read them reliably); the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā; the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa; the Jaiminīya Upaniṣad-Brāhmaṇa (3-?-? [?]); and other places."

"Manu has many names: since he is the son of Vivasvān (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-?-? as read [?]) — a deity, Vivasvat — he is Vaivasvata (Atharva 8-?-? [?]; Śatapatha Br. 13-4-3-3 as read [?]); since he belongs to the family of Savarṇā he is Sāvarṇi; since he belongs to the line of Saṃvaraṇa he is Sāṃvaraṇi (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-?-? as read [?])."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.3)

हे मीळ्हः सेक्तः कामाभिवर्षक नित्यतरुणो वा रुद्र क्षयद्वीरस्य क्षपितप्रतिपक्षस्य मरुद्भिर्युक्तस्य वा तव सुमतिं शोभनां कल्याणीमनुग्रहात्मिकां बुद्धिं ते त्वत्सम्बन्धिनो वयं देवयज्यया देवयागेन त्वद्देवत्येन यज्ञेनाश्याम प्राप्नुयाम । त्वं चास्माकं विशः प्रजा अभिलक्ष्याचर । आगच्छ । किं कुर्वन् । सुम्नायन्नित् । सुम्नमिति सुखनाम । तासां प्रजानां सुखमिच्छन्नेव सुखप्रद एव भवेत्यर्थः । तथोऽरिष्टवीराः । वीर्यार्जायन्त इति वीराः प्रजाः । अरिष्टा अहिंसिता वीरा येषां तथाभूताः सन्तो वयं ते तुभ्यं हविःरूपपुरोडाशादिकं जुहवाम । चोदिते आधारे प्रक्षिपाम । सुमतिम् । मतिर्मननम् । शोभनं मननं यस्यां बुद्धौ सा सुमतिः । [grammatical tail follows in the print: mīḷhvaḥ — mih "to sprinkle", kvasu by dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvān, nominal, the vocative; sumnāyan — kyac in the sense of desiring; etc.]

he mīḷhaḥ sektaḥ kāmābhivarṣaka nityataruṇo vā rudra kṣayadvīrasya kṣapitapratipakṣasya marudbhiryuktasya vā tava sumatiṃ śobhanāṃ kalyāṇīmanugrahātmikāṃ buddhiṃ te tvatsambandhino vayaṃ devayajyayā devayāgena tvaddevatyena yajñenāśyāma prāpnuyāma | tvaṃ cāsmākaṃ viśaḥ prajā abhilakṣyācara | āgaccha | kiṃ kurvan | sumnāyannit | sumnamiti sukhanāma | tāsāṃ prajānāṃ sukhamicchanneva sukhaprada eva bhavetyarthaḥ | tatho 'riṣṭavīrāḥ | vīryārjāyanta iti vīrāḥ prajāḥ | ariṣṭā ahiṃsitā vīrā yeṣāṃ tathābhūtāḥ santo vayaṃ te tubhyaṃ haviḥrūpapuroḍāśādikaṃ juhavāma | codite ādhāre prakṣipāma | sumatim | matirmananam | śobhanaṃ mananaṃ yasyāṃ buddhau sā sumatiḥ | [grammatical tail follows in the print: mīḷhvaḥ — mih "to sprinkle", kvasu by dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvān, nominal, the vocative; sumnāyan — kyac in the sense of desiring; etc.]

Sense (mine): "O mīḷhvaḥ — sprinkler, one who showers desires, or always-young Rudra — may we, belonging to thee, aśyāma, obtain by devayajyayā, by sacrifice to the gods, to thee as deity, the sumati, the excellent, auspicious, graciously-disposed mind (buddhi) of thee, kṣayadvīrasya, who hast destroyed adversaries or art joined with the Maruts. And do thou ā cara, come to our viśaḥ, subjects, descendants. Doing what? Sumnāyann it — sumna is a name for happiness; wishing happiness to those people, be only a giver of happiness. And we, ariṣṭavīrāḥ — having sons (heroes, vīrāḥ, offspring) unhurt — juhavāma te haviḥ, offer thee oblations such as cakes into the sacrificial fire. Sumatim — mati is thinking: sumati is that understanding in which there is good thinking."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun on p. 110, completed on p. 111

"mīḍhvaḥ — O one who grants the desired objects, or who is ever young; rudra — O Rudra; kṣayadvīrasya — of thee, who destroyest opposing heroes or art joined with the Marut deities; tava — thy; sumatim — graciously-disposed (favouring) understanding; te — (we) who belong to thee; devayajyayā — by the sacrifices made for the gods; aśyāma — may we obtain; (tvaṃ ca — and thou); asmākam — our; viśaḥ — people (descendants)…

original p. 111

… udveśi [as printed, [?]] (?); sumnāyan it — being a giver of happiness only; ā cara — come (afterwards, we); ariṣṭavīrāḥ — having children free from sorrow; te — to thee; haviḥ — caru, purodāśa and the like; juhavāma — we offer in the fire."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Rudra, who grantest what we desire, may thy favour be upon us the sacrificers; come, giving happiness to our children; we, endowed with sorrow-free children, offer thee caru and purodāśa and the rest."

English Translation (as printed)

Rudra, showerer (of benefits), may we obtain, through our worship of the gods, the favour of you, the destroyer of heroes : come to our posterity, purposing to promote their happiness, while we, having our sons in safety, offer you oblations.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

मीळ्हः — Mīḷhaḥ — "kāmābhivarṣaka nityataruṇo vā": "Sāyaṇa says: one who fulfils the wishes of those who take refuge in him, or one who is always enjoying youthful vigour. Skandasvāmin says the word mīḍhva arises from the root mih with the sense 'to sprinkle' — [mīḍhvān = one who sprinkles] — one who sprinkles with the water that is called rain; or mīḍhvān is a Vedic form of mīḍhaṃ = wealth, [giving] 'wealth'. Mīḷhuṣ is read among the twenty-eight [as read] names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 as read [?]). Sāyaṇa explains that the word mīḍhvas, since it conveys 'wealth', with the matup suffix, means 'Rudra who has wealth'."

सुमतिम् — Sumatim — "matir mananam | śobhanaṃ mananaṃ yasyāṃ buddhau sā sumatiḥ | śobhanāṃ kalyāṇīm anugrahātmikāṃ buddhim": "manana means firm resolve: an understanding that is a steadfast resolve that there be welfare for us all. The prayer to Rudra is that he should accept our salutations and our oblations. The word sumati —

वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम राजा हि कं भुवनानामभिश्रीः । (ऋ. सं. १-९८-१ [as read])

vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma rājā hi kaṃ bhuvanānāmabhiśrīḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-98-1 [as read])

original p. 112

(Ṛ. 1-98-1 as just cited; Ni. 2-?? as read [?]): "… in this Ṛk and in other Ṛks the word [sumati] is used in the sense of 'kalyāṇī matiḥ', auspicious understanding —

धाता ददातु दाशुषे प्राचीं जीवातुमक्षिताम् । वयं देवस्य सुमतिं सत्यधर्मणः ॥ (अथ. सं. ७-१२-३ [as read])

dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe prācīṃ jīvātumakṣitām | vayaṃ devasya sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ ‖ (atha. saṃ. 7-12-3 [as read])

अङ्गिरसो नः पितरो नवग्वा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोम्यासः । तेषां वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियानामपि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१४-६ [as read])"

aṅgiraso naḥ pitaro navagvā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somyāsaḥ | teṣāṃ vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyānāmapi bhadre saumanase syāma ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-14-6 [as read])"

सुम्नायन् [sic as heading: sumnāyan; the print's heading is Sumnāyan] — "sumna is read among the twenty-eight [as read] names of happiness (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]); so it conveys the meaning 'happiness'. The sense is: Rudra, accepting the oblations we offer, will favour with happiness those who honour him with salutations, and their children."

अरिष्टवीराः — Ariṣṭavīrāḥ — "ariṣṭā ahiṃsitā vīrā yeṣāṃ tathābhūtāḥ | vīryārjāyanta iti vīrāḥ prajāḥ": "Though, following the grammatical derivation, the word vīra has various meanings, here the sense is 'offspring (sons), born of virility'. The Nirukta-writer interprets it likewise —

शिक्षा स्तोतृभ्यो माति धग्भगो नो बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः । (ऋ. सं. २-११-२१ [as read])

śikṣā stotṛbhyo māti dhagbhago no bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 2-11-21 [as read])

— citing this Ṛk. Here Rudra is prayed to: may no harm come to our sons and the like. Skandasvāmin: 'ariṣṭavīrāḥ — ahiṃsitaputrapautrāḥ': 'we, with sons and grandsons unharmed, shall be so,' he says."

इत् / विशः — It / Viśaḥ — "prajāḥ": "Among the nipātas some convey a meaning; others are meaningless and exist for completing the sentence. Here the word it is for filling out the line. Sāyaṇa explains the word viśaḥ as 'descendants'; abhilakṣya ācara means 'look upon our children and favour them' — that is the prayer. Skandasvāmin says the same: 'viśaḥ — manuṣyān asmākaṃ sambandhinaḥ putrapautrādīn ṛtvijo vā prati ācara' — 'to our people, our related sons and grandsons, or to the priests [officiating], come' — that is, having looked at us men, our sons and grandsons, or the priests, may he favour them."

original p. 113

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.4)

त्वेषम् । वयम् । रुद्रम् । यज्ञऽसाधम् । वङ्कुम् । कविम् । अवसे । नि । ह्वयामहे । आरे । अस्मत् । दैव्यम् । हेळः । अस्यतु । सुऽमतिम् । इत् । वयम् । अस्य । आ । वृणीमहे ॥ ४ ॥

tveṣam | vayam | rudram | yajña 'sādham | vaṅkum | kavim | avase | ni | hvayāmahe | āre | asmat | daivyam | heḷaḥ | asyatu | su 'matim | it | vayam | asya | ā | vṛṇīmahe ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.4)

अवसे रक्षणाय रुद्रं महादेवं नि ह्वयामहे । नितरामाह्वयामः । कीदृशं त्वेषं दीप्तं यज्ञसाधं यज्ञस्य साधयितारम् । एष हि यज्ञं स्विष्टं करोति । तथा च तैत्तिरीयके । देवा वै यज्ञाद्रुद्रमन्तरायन्सित्यपाक्रम्यात्मानं [?] स्विष्टं वै न इदं भविष्यति यदिमं राधयिष्यामः इति तत्स्विष्टकृतः स्विष्टकृत्त्वम् । तै. सं. ३-६-१-३ [as read] । इति । वङ्कुं कुटिलगन्तारं कविं क्रान्तदर्शिनम् । स च रुद्रो दैव्यं देवस्य द्योतमानस्य सम्बन्धि हेळः क्रोधमस्मदारेऽस्मत्तो दूरदेशेऽस्यतु प्रेरयतु । अस्य महादेवस्य सुमतिमित् शोभनामनुग्रहरूपां बुद्धिमेव वयमा वृणीमहे । अभिमुख्येन सम्भजामहे ॥ [the grammatical tail follows in small type: yajñasādham — yajñaṃ sādhayati iti yajñasāḥ, sidhu "to accomplish", kvip; vaṅkum — vaki "crookedness", the Uṇādi u; hvayāmahe — hve "to call", laṭ 1st plural, saṃprasāraṇa, ṇiti…; daivyam — devād yañ [Pā. 4-1-85 as read [?]]; asyatu — asu "to throw", divādi; vṛṇīmahe — vṛñ "to choose", kryādi.]

avase rakṣaṇāya rudraṃ mahādevaṃ ni hvayāmahe | nitarāmāhvayāmaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tveṣaṃ dīptaṃ yajñasādhaṃ yajñasya sādhayitāram | eṣa hi yajñaṃ sviṣṭaṃ karoti | tathā ca taittirīyake | devā vai yajñādrudramantarāyansityapākramyātmānaṃ [?] sviṣṭaṃ vai na idaṃ bhaviṣyati yadimaṃ rādhayiṣyāmaḥ iti tatsviṣṭakṛtaḥ sviṣṭakṛttvam | tai. saṃ. 3-6-1-3 [as read] | iti | vaṅkuṃ kuṭilagantāraṃ kaviṃ krāntadarśinam | sa ca rudro daivyaṃ devasya dyotamānasya sambandhi heḷaḥ krodhamasmadāre 'smatto dūradeśe 'syatu prerayatu | asya mahādevasya sumatimit śobhanāmanugraharūpāṃ buddhimeva vayamā vṛṇīmahe | abhimukhyena sambhajāmahe ‖ [the grammatical tail follows in small type: yajñasādham — yajñaṃ sādhayati iti yajñasāḥ, sidhu "to accomplish", kvip; vaṅkum — vaki "crookedness", the Uṇādi u; hvayāmahe — hve "to call", laṭ 1st plural, saṃprasāraṇa, ṇiti…; daivyam — devād yañ [Pā. 4-1-85 as read [?]]; asyatu — asu "to throw", divādi; vṛṇīmahe — vṛñ "to choose", kryādi.]

Sense (mine): "For protection (avase) we invoke (ni hvayāmahe) Rudra, the great god, constantly. What is he like? Tveṣam — shining; yajñasādham — who accomplishes the sacrifice, for he makes the sacrifice well-offered (sviṣṭa): as the Taittirīya says: 'The gods kept Rudra away from the sacrifice [?]; "this (sacrifice) of ours will not be well-offered if we do not satisfy him": hence the sviṣṭakṛt-ness of the Sviṣṭakṛt' (Tai. Saṃ. 3-6-1-3 as read [?]). Vaṅkum — the crooked-going; kavim — far-seeing. May that Rudra asyatu, cast āre, far from us, the haḍaḥ (anger) of the god, the shining one, belonging to the divine. And we ā vṛṇīmahe, choose, turn toward, the sumati, the good, favour-natured mind of this great god."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"tveṣam — of shining form; yajñasādham — the accomplisher of sacrifice; vaṅkum — of crooked (curving) motion; kavim — who knows the past and the future (kavi); rudram — Rudra; avase — for (our) protection; ni hvayāmahe — we invoke (that Rudra); daivyam — that which belongs to the deities; helaḥ — anger; asmat — from us; āre — far away; asyatu — may (he) cast; asya — of this Rudra; sumatim it — the graciously-disposed intention; vayam — we; ā vṛṇīmahe — choose (we desire)."

original p. 115

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"We pray for protection to Rudra, who is of shining form, the accomplisher of sacrifices, of crooked going, and knower of past and future. Let Rudra cast far from us the anger of the deities. We choose only his favour."

English Translation (as printed)

We invoke for our preservation the illustrious Rudra, the accomplisher of sacrifices, the tortuous, the wise : may he remove far from us his celestial wrath for we earnestly solicit his favour.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

यज्ञसाधम् — Yajñasādham — "yajñaṃ sādhayati iti yajñasāṭ": "(that is) he who removes the obstacles to the sacrifice, by subduing the thorns of the sacrifice (yajñakaṇṭaka), who brings the sacrifice to completion. Sāyaṇa explains that Rudra makes the sacrifice proceed excellently, eṣa hi yajñaṃ sviṣṭaṃ karoti — this Rudra makes the sacrifice go on in the right way. Stating in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā the speciality of Rudra, he says —

देवा वै यज्ञाद्रुद्रमन्तरायन् [?] इत्याद्युपक्रम्य स्विष्टं वै न इदं भविष्यति यदिमं राधयिष्यामः इति तत्स्विष्टकृतः स्विष्टकृत्त्वम् ॥ (तै. सं. ३-६-१-३ [as read])

devā vai yajñādrudramantarāyan [?] ityādyupakramya sviṣṭaṃ vai na idaṃ bhaviṣyati yadimaṃ rādhayiṣyāmaḥ iti tatsviṣṭakṛtaḥ sviṣṭakṛttvam ‖ (tai. saṃ. 3-6-1-3 [as read])

original p. 116

"… because we serve Rudra, our sacrifices become suhutas, well-offered — thus the Taittirīya text speaks."

वङ्कुम् — Vaṅkum — "kuṭilagantāram": "he who moves in a crooked path, in order to bewilder the asuras or to subdue [them] — this is the meaning. Skandasvāmin: 'vaṅkuśabdo 'tra vaki kauṭilye ity asya vakragāmī' — since the word vaṅku is derived from the root vaki 'to be crooked', it denotes one with a crooked course, he explains, and gives the example —

यत्ते दिक्षु प्रराध्यं [?] वङ्कू वारस्य पर्णेन [?] (ऋ. सं. ८-१-११ [as read; the Ṛk is in small type and the quotation unclear [?]])"

yatte dikṣu prarādhyaṃ [?] vaṅkū vārasya parṇena [?] (ṛ. saṃ. 8-1-11 [as read; the Ṛk is in small type and the quotation unclear [?]])"

कविम् — Kavim — "krāntadarśinam" (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya): "one who shows the right way. Since the word kavi is stated among the twenty-four [as read] names of the wise (medhāvin) (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), Skandasvāmin explains it as 'the intelligent'."

हेळः — Heḷaḥ — "krodhaḥ": "anger. Because the word heḷa is stated among the twelve [as read] names of anger (krodha), beginning 'hṛṇi' (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]), Skandasvāmin explains the meaning krodha:

दैव्यं हेळः क्रोधनामैतत् । देवानां स्वभूतं क्रोधमस्यतु क्षिपतु । यथास्मभ्यं देवाः न क्रुध्येयुः तथा करोतु हेळः ।

daivyaṃ heḷaḥ krodhanāmaitat | devānāṃ svabhūtaṃ krodhamasyatu kṣipatu | yathāsmabhyaṃ devāḥ na krudhyeyuḥ tathā karotu heḷaḥ |

— the word heḷaḥ has the meaning 'anger'. [The meaning:] 'may Rudra so act that the deities may not be angry with us — that is, may he grant us favour.'"

सुमतिमित् — Sumatim it — "it is in the sense of eva" (indeed): "sumatim eva — śobhanām eva — the kindly-disposed mind, in the form of favour, of Rudra. He explains: 'we desire this of Rudra, that it may be in our regard'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly)

tveṣam (tviṣī "to shine", in the pacādi group; ac; guṇa of the penultimate; the final accent from the suffix), yajñasādham (yajñaṃ sādhayati iti yajñasāṭ; ṣidhu "to accomplish", ṇic by hetumati ca; siddhyater apāralaukike, Pā. 6-4-?? as read [?], ṇic-… ātva; or rādh/sādh "to accomplish"; kvip;

… after the ṇi-elision kvip; the first-member accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; accusative singular); vaṅkum (vaki "to be crooked"; the Uṇādi suffix u; the num augment by idito num dhātoḥ; anusvāra → homorganic nasal; accent from the suffix); avase (av "to protect", the suffix asun applicable after any root; nit, hence the first-syllable accent; dative singular); ni hvayāmahe (hvāñ "to compete, to call", with ni — nisamupavibhyo hvaḥ, Pā. 1-3-30 as read [?], ātmanepada; laṭ 1st plural mahiṅ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; śap; ay for e; nighāta); daivyam (devasya idam daivyam; devād yañ — yañ in the sense of "its", Pā. 4-1-85 as read [?]; elision of a by yasyeti ca; vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ; jñityādir nityam, first-syllable accent); heḷaḥ (heḍṛ "to disregard", Uṇādi asun; nit, first-syllable accent; accusative singular); asyatu (asu "to throw", divādi; loṭ 3rd singular tip, with tu by eruḥ, Pā. 3-4-86 as read [?]; śyan by divādibhyaḥ śyan; nighāta); vṛṇīmahe (vṛñ "to choose", kryādi; loṭ/laṭ 1st plural mahiṅ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; kryādibhyaḥ śnā; sārvadhātukam apit, ṅit; ī for ā by ī halyaghoḥ; ṇatva, since the n follows ṛ, with the vikaraṇa … no guṇa since ṅit; nighāta). ‖ 4 ‖

दिवो वराहमरुषं कपर्दिनं त्वेषं रूपं नमसा नि ह्वयामहे । हस्ते बिभ्रद्भेषजा वार्याणि शर्म वर्म छर्दिरस्मभ्यं यंसत् ॥ ५ ॥

divo varāhamaruṣaṃ kapardinaṃ tveṣaṃ rūpaṃ namasā ni hvayāmahe | haste bibhradbheṣajā vāryāṇi śarma varma chardirasmabhyaṃ yaṃsat ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.5)

दिवः । वराहम् । अरुषम् । कपर्दिनम् । त्वेषम् । रूपम् । नमसा । नि । ह्वयामहे । हस्ते । बिभ्रत् । भेषजा । वार्याणि । शर्म । वर्म । छर्दिः । अस्मभ्यम् । यंसत् ॥ ५ ॥

divaḥ | varāham | aruṣam | kapardinam | tveṣam | rūpam | namasā | ni | hvayāmahe | haste | bibhrat | bheṣajā | vāryāṇi | śarma | varma | chardiḥ | asmabhyam | yaṃsat ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.5)

वराहं वराहारमुत्कृष्टभोजनम् । यद्वा । वराहवद्दृढाङ्गम् । अरुषमारोचमानं कपर्दिनं जटाभिर्युक्तं त्वेषं तेजसा दीप्यमानं रूपं निरूपणीयं वेदान्तैरधिगम्यं एवंभूतं रुद्रं नमसा हविर्लक्षणेनान्नेन नमस्कारेण वा दिवो द्युलोकसकाशात् नि ह्वयामहे । नितरामाह्वयामः । स आहूतो रुद्रो हस्ते स्वकीये बाहौ वार्याणि सर्वैर्वरणीयानि भेषजा भैषज्यानि रोगशमनहेतुभूतानि बिभ्रत् धारयन् अस्मभ्यं स्तोतृभ्यः शर्म अरोग्यलक्षणं सुखं वर्म आयुधानां निवारकं कवचं छर्दिः गृहनामैतत् गृहं च यंसत् प्रयच्छतु ॥ [the grammatical tail follows: bibhrat — ḍubhṛñ "to bear, to nourish", juhotyādi, śatṛ, doubling, abhyastānām…; bhaiṣajā — bhiṣaj "treating", kaṇḍvādi…; vāryāṇi — vṛñ, ṇyat…; chardiḥ — ucchṛdir "to shine" or "to play" (dīptidevanayoḥ), the is suffix [Uṇ.]; yaṃsat — yamu "to stop", leṭ with the augment aṭ; sip, bahulaṃ leṭi — sic…]

varāhaṃ varāhāramutkṛṣṭabhojanam | yadvā | varāhavaddṛḍhāṅgam | aruṣamārocamānaṃ kapardinaṃ jaṭābhiryuktaṃ tveṣaṃ tejasā dīpyamānaṃ rūpaṃ nirūpaṇīyaṃ vedāntairadhigamyaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ rudraṃ namasā havirlakṣaṇenānnena namaskāreṇa vā divo dyulokasakāśāt ni hvayāmahe | nitarāmāhvayāmaḥ | sa āhūto rudro haste svakīye bāhau vāryāṇi sarvairvaraṇīyāni bheṣajā bhaiṣajyāni rogaśamanahetubhūtāni bibhrat dhārayan asmabhyaṃ stotṛbhyaḥ śarma arogyalakṣaṇaṃ sukhaṃ varma āyudhānāṃ nivārakaṃ kavacaṃ chardiḥ gṛhanāmaitat gṛhaṃ ca yaṃsat prayacchatu ‖ [the grammatical tail follows: bibhrat — ḍubhṛñ "to bear, to nourish", juhotyādi, śatṛ, doubling, abhyastānām…; bhaiṣajā — bhiṣaj "treating", kaṇḍvādi…; vāryāṇi — vṛñ, ṇyat…; chardiḥ — ucchṛdir "to shine" or "to play" (dīptidevanayoḥ), the is suffix [Uṇ.]; yaṃsat — yamu "to stop", leṭ with the augment aṭ; sip, bahulaṃ leṭi — sic…]

Sense (mine): "Varāham — he whose food is excellent (vara-āhāra), or, whose limbs are firm like those of a boar. Aruṣam — shining; kapardinam — bearing matted hair; tveṣam — blazing in splendour; rūpam — to be considered (nirūpaṇīya), to be understood by the Vedānta texts: such a Rudra we call down (ni hvayāmahe) with namasā — with food in the form of oblation or with salutation — from the heavenly world. Invoked, may that Rudra, holding in his own hand desirable (vāryāṇi) medicines (bheṣajā) that are the cause of curing diseases, grant us, the praisers, śarma — happiness in the form of health; varma — armour that wards off weapons; chardiḥ — a name of a house — and a house."

original p. 119

Grammatical tail of the bhāṣya, concluded — characterized, not transcribed: bheṣajā (bhiṣaj "to heal", the neuter plural śi → ā, by śeś chandasi bahulam with elision); chardiḥ (ucchṛdir "to shine, to play"; the suffix is by Uṇādi; "chṛdyate dīpyate suvarṇādibhir gṛhaṃ prakāśate iti chardiḥ gṛham"); yaṃsat (yamu "to restrain"; leṭ, with the augment aṭ; sip → elision of the i by itaś ca lopaḥ; the elision of the s … in the leṭ).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"varāham — one who has excellent food, or one of firm body; aruṣam — of shining form; kapardinam — wearer of matted locks; tveṣam — of great splendour; rūpam — (Rudra), who is to be known by the Vedas and so on; namasā — by salutations, or by food in the form of oblations, in order to give; divaḥ — from the world of heaven; ni hvayāmahe — we call (invoke) down (that Rudra, being invoked); haste — in his hand; vāryāṇi — desired by all; bheṣajā — medicinal herbs; bibhrat — holding; asmabhyam — to us (the singers of praises); śarma — happiness in the form of health; varma — protective armour and so on; chardiḥ — a house for dwelling in; yaṃsat — may he grant."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"We invoke from the world of heaven with salutations Rudra, of firm body, of excellent food, of shining form, wearing matted locks, of great splendour, who is to be known by the Vedānta. May Rudra, thus invoked by us, holding medicinal herbs in his hand, grant us the armour and weapons that guard health, and dwelling-houses."

English Translation (as printed)

We invoke from heaven, with reverence, him who has excellent food who is radiant, and has braided hair, who is brilliant, and is to be ascertained (by sacred study), holding in his hands excellent medicaments : may he grant us health, defensive armour, and a (secure) dwelling.

original p. 120

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

वराहम् — Varāham — "varāhāram utkṛṣṭabhojanam": "Sāyaṇa explains: he who takes excellent food, or takes food to excess; or 'varāhavad dṛḍhāṅgam' — whose body is as firm as that of a varāha (wild boar). Skandasvāmin:

वराहनामासुरः केतुसदृक्षः [?] वराहः इति मेघनाम । केतुसदृशम् एकदेशसादृश्येन वैष समस्तसादृश्यं च व्यपदेशः रुद्रस्य नीलत्वात् कण्ठो मेघसदृशः । मेघसदृशकण्ठमित्यर्थः ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

varāhanāmāsuraḥ ketusadṛkṣaḥ [?] varāhaḥ iti meghanāma | ketusadṛśam ekadeśasādṛśyena vaiṣa samastasādṛśyaṃ ca vyapadeśaḥ rudrasya nīlatvāt kaṇṭho meghasadṛśaḥ | meghasadṛśakaṇṭhamityarthaḥ ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

— Rudra, whose strength is like that of the asura named Varāha [or: the one who has a boar's form]; or, since varāha is a name of the cloud, because of resemblance in one respect [ekadeśa] the whole resemblance is spoken of: because of Rudra's blueness (nīlatva) his throat is like a cloud; the meaning is 'whose throat is like a cloud'. The word varāha, being read among the thirty-one [as read] names of the cloud (Ni. 1-10 as read [?]), has the meaning 'cloud'. Since the likeness (upamā) is said to be stated completely in respect of one part, the throat of Rudra is compared with the cloud: Rudra has a throat that is like the cloud in being dark blue; therefore he is called by the word varāha. Or:

वराहः सूकर उच्यते तदाकारं देवता हि तं तमाकारं महाभाग्ययोगात् भजते । अत उपपन्नो हि रुद्रस्य वराहाकारव्यपदेशः ।

varāhaḥ sūkara ucyate tadākāraṃ devatā hi taṃ tamākāraṃ mahābhāgyayogāt bhajate | ata upapanno hi rudrasya varāhākāravyapadeśaḥ |

— varāha denotes the boar: 'the deities, by their great fortune, assume whatever form they like' — so Rudra's being described as having the form of a boar is proper. The deities take on the forms they desire by the power of their own energy and the success of their austerity: hence Rudra too has the form of a boar. Thus [Skandasvāmin] explains the meaning in three ways."

"The Nirukta-writer:

वराहो मेघो भवति । वराहारः वरमाहारमाहार्षीदिति च ब्राह्मणम् ॥ (नि. ५-४ [as read])

varāho megho bhavati | varāhāraḥ varamāhāramāhārṣīditi ca brāhmaṇam ‖ (ni. 5-4 [as read])

— for the word varāha he gives the meaning 'cloud'; and: varam āharati iti varāhaḥ — he who takes the excellent [food]; or mūlaṃ vahati iti varāhaḥ — he who lifts up the roots (the bulbs) that are in the earth, hence 'boar'; or from bringing water, thus explained in two ways —

अस्येदु मातुः सवनेषु सद्यो महः पितुं पपिवाञ्चार्वन्ना । मुषायद्विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान्विध्यद्वराहं तिरो अद्रिमस्ता ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-६१-७ [as read])

asyedu mātuḥ savaneṣu sadyo mahaḥ pituṃ papivāñcārvannā | muṣāyadviṣṇuḥ pacataṃ sahīyānvidhyadvarāhaṃ tiro adrimastā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-61-7 [as read])

In this Ṛk the word varāha is used in the sense of 'cloud'.

original p. 121

विश्वेत्ता विष्णुराभरदुरुक्रमस्त्वेषितः शतं महिषान्क्षीरपाकमोदनं वराहमिन्द्र एमुषम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-७७-१० [as read])

viśvettā viṣṇurābharadurukramastveṣitaḥ śataṃ mahiṣānkṣīrapākamodanaṃ varāhamindra emuṣam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 8-77-10 [as read])

अयमुपमीतरो वराहः एतस्मादेव बृहति मूलानि वरं वरं मूलं बृहतीति वा ॥ (नि. ५-४)

ayamupamītaro varāhaḥ etasmādeva bṛhati mūlāni varaṃ varaṃ mūlaṃ bṛhatīti vā ‖ (ni. 5-4)

[Yāska] says that the explanation of the word varāha is still of another kind, and quotes this; the Nirukta-writer, explaining that the word varāha has also the meaning 'asura', cites the Brāhmaṇa sentence of the Maitrāyaṇīya school 'varam āhāram āhārṣīt' ('he took the excellent food'). And again —

आङ्गिरसोऽपि वराहा उच्यन्ते ।

āṅgiraso 'pi varāhā ucyante |

— 'the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis are also called varāha': explaining the meaning of the word varāha [in this sense, he cites] —

स ईं सत्येभिः सखिभिः शुचद्भिर्गोधायसं वि धनसैरदर्दः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्वृषभिर्वराहैर्घर्मस्वेदेभिर्द्रविणं व्यानट् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-६७-७ [as read])

sa īṃ satyebhiḥ sakhibhiḥ śucadbhirgodhāyasaṃ vi dhanasairadardaḥ | brahmaṇaspatirvṛṣabhirvarāhairgharmasvedebhirdraviṇaṃ vyānaṭ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-67-7 [as read])

In this Ṛk the Aṅgirases are denoted by the word varāha.

वि त्वत्कृन्न योजनमचेति स्सस्रह [?] यन्मरुतो गोतनो वः । पर्क [?] हिरण्यचक्रानयोदंष्ट्रान्विधावतो वराहून् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-८८-५ [as read]; the quotation is in small type and corrupt in the print [?])

vi tvatkṛnna yojanamaceti ssasraha [?] yanmaruto gotano vaḥ | parka [?] hiraṇyacakrānayodaṃṣṭrānvidhāvato varāhūn ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-88-5 [as read]; the quotation is in small type and corrupt in the print [?])

"And these middle-region deity-groups are also called varāha: they are called varāhavaḥ (the deities of the middle region, i.e. of the atmosphere)" — thus he explains this Ṛk. "Following the view of the Nirukta-writer so stated, Skandasvāmin explains the word varāha in three ways and Sāyaṇa in two. But in this Ṛk the word varāha being stated, there is the plural in 'mādhyamikāḥ devagaṇāḥ varāhavaḥ' for which, as he explains, 'te sapta sapta marutāṃ gaṇāḥ' ('those seven-seven groups of Maruts'), meaning the troops of Maruts. Just as in the case of the Maruts, who are the group of the [seven times] seven deities, the word varāhavaḥ is used of them, so the word varāha is applied to the deity of the middle region" — and, so explaining, he illustrates the very Ṛk 'divo varāham'."

original p. 122

अरुषम् — Aruṣam — "ārocamānam": "one who shines — so Sāyaṇa; Skandasvāmin: 'aruṣatir gatikarmā' — [the word aruṣa is derived from a root that means going]; because it means 'going', the word aruṣa is explained as 'one who goes against enemies, or goes to the sacrifice' (śatrūn yajñaṃ vā prati)."

रूपम् — Rūpam — "nirūpaṇīyaṃ vedāntair adhigamyam": "Rudra's own form is what is investigated by the Vedas and the Vedānta, and, being what is to be known by that very [study], the form of Rudra is that which is to be known by the Vedānta — thus Sāyaṇa. Skandasvāmin:

अत्र नेरीते मत्वर्थो रूपशब्दो द्रष्टव्यः । महाभाग्ययोगादनेकप्रकारैः रूपैः रूपवन्तम् ॥

atra nerīte matvartho rūpaśabdo draṣṭavyaḥ | mahābhāgyayogādanekaprakāraiḥ rūpaiḥ rūpavantam ‖

— here the word rūpa is to be understood in the sense of matup, 'having form'; thus he explains that Rudra shines with many kinds of forms by his unsurpassed austerity and merit."

नमसा — Namasā — "by salutations, or by offering food in the form of oblations: we invoke Rudra to come down here from heaven — as Sāyaṇa explains; and Skandasvāmin, explaining likewise, gives the special meaning 'praise' to the word namas."

वार्याणि भेषजा हस्ते बिभ्रत् — Vāryāṇi bheṣajā haste bibhrat — "Rudra holds in his hands always medicines that have the power to destroy diseases desired to be removed by all; so he brings happiness to all. Therefore the prayer is made that Rudra come to our sacrifice and give us happiness. That Rudra is the lord of medicines is said in —

सहस्रं ते स्वपिवात भेषजा मा नस्तोकेषु तनयेषु रीरिषः । ओषधीनां पतये नमः ॥ [as read; the reference is in small type] (ऋ. सं. २-३३-१३ [as read; [?]])

sahasraṃ te svapivāta bheṣajā mā nastokeṣu tanayeṣu rīriṣaḥ | oṣadhīnāṃ pataye namaḥ ‖ [as read; the reference is in small type] (ṛ. saṃ. 2-33-13 [as read; [?]])

and other mantras."

वर्म — Varma — "varmātra kavacam ucyate": "armour — that is, armour able to ward off the injury done by enemies: āyudhānāṃ nivārakam — that which protects against the weapons hurled by foes, so that no danger may come: the prayer is that Rudra, being pleased, favour us with such armour."

original p. 123

छर्दिः — Chardiḥ — "since the word is stated among the twenty-two [as read] names of house (gṛha), 'gayaḥ', 'kṣayaḥ' and so on (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), it means 'house'. The prayer to Rudra is that he grant us a house suitable for living in happily. By the epithets varāham, aruṣam, kapardinam, tveṣam, rūpam, Rudra, who is shown to be possessed of power, is invoked with salutations and the offering of oblations; and since a prayer is made in this Ṛk that he grant cure of disease, happiness, armour against all kinds of danger from enemies, and a dwelling, it is understood that Rudra grants these to those who take refuge in him."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly)

divaḥ (accent of the ending by ūḍidaṃpadādi…), kapardinam (kapardaḥ asya asti; the suffix ini by ata iniṭhanau, Pā. 5-2-115 as read [?]; accent on the i from the suffix), bibhrat (ḍubhṛñ "to bear, to nourish", juhotyādi; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; doubling by ślau; i in the reduplication by bhṛñām it, Pā. 7-4-76 as read [?]; sārvadhātukam apit makes the śatṛ ṅit, and since the jus-ādi (jhi) is not there, guṇa of the root's i is not applied; yaṇ; the num augment is prevented by nābhyastācchatuḥ, Pā. 7-1-78 as read [?]); bheṣajā (bhiṣaj "to heal", does not belong to the kaṇḍvādi group; yak by kaṇḍvādibhyo yak, Pā. 3-1-27 as read [?], in its own sense [svārthe]; or the ac suffix by pacādi, being an ākṛtigaṇa; elision of a by yasya iti ca; ato lopaḥ; and this is established by the statement sumaṅgalabheṣajāc ca, Pā. 4-1-30 as read [?]; śi → elision by śeś chandasi bahulam, Pā. 6-1-70 as read [?]); vāryāṇi (vṛñ "to choose"; ṇyat by ṛhaloṇyat; vṛddhi by aco 'ñṇiti; raparatva by uraṇ raparaḥ; tuk-augment is prevented in ṇyat…; the tit svarita is overruled by the iḍavaravṛdhi… [as printed] — the first syllable acute by Pā. 6-1-?? as read [?]).

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.6)

इदं पित्रे मरुतामुच्यते वचः स्वादोः स्वादीयो रुद्राय वर्धनम् । रास्वा च नो अमृत मर्तभोजनं त्मने तोकाय तनयाय मृळ ॥ ६ ॥

idaṃ pitre marutāmucyate vacaḥ svādoḥ svādīyo rudrāya vardhanam | rāsvā ca no amṛta martabhojanaṃ tmane tokāya tanayāya mṛḷa ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.6)

इदम् । पित्रे । मरुताम् । उच्यते । वचः । स्वादोः । स्वादीयः । रुद्राय । वर्धनम् । रास्व । च । नः । अमृत । मर्तऽभोजनम् । त्मने । तोकाय । तनयाय । मृळ ॥ ६ ॥

idam | pitre | marutām | ucyate | vacaḥ | svādoḥ | svādīyaḥ | rudrāya | vardhanam | rāsva | ca | naḥ | amṛta | marta 'bhojanam | tmane | tokāya | tanayāya | mṛḷa ‖ 6 ‖
