॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.6)

इदं स्तुतिलक्षणं वचो मरुतामेकोनपञ्चाशत्संख्याकानां देवविशेषाणां पित्रे जनकाय रुद्रायेश्वरायोच्यते । उच्चार्यते । कीदृशं स्वादोः स्वादीयो रसवतो मधुफलादेरपि स्वादुतरम् । अतिशयेन हर्षजनकमित्यर्थः । वर्धनं स्तुत्यस्य प्रवर्धकम् । स्तोत्रेण हि देवता हृष्टा सती प्रवर्धते । रुद्रस्य च मरुतां पितृत्वमेवमाम्नायते । पुरा कदाचिदिन्द्रोऽसुराञ्जित्वा तदानीं दितिरसुरमातेन्द्रहननसमर्थं पुत्रं कामयमाना तपसा भर्तुः सकाशाद्गर्भं लेभे । इमं वृत्तान्तमवगच्छन्निन्द्रो वज्रहस्तः सन् सूक्ष्मरूपो भूत्वा तस्या उदरं प्रविश्य तं गर्भं सप्तधा बिभेद । पुनरप्येकैकं सप्तखण्डमकरोत् । ते सर्वे गर्भैकदेशा योनेर्निर्गत्यारुदन् । एतस्मिन्नवसरे लीलार्थं गच्छन्तौ पार्वतीपरमेश्वराविमान्ददृशतुः । महेशं प्रति पार्वत्यैवमुवाच । इमे मांसखण्डा यथा प्रत्येकं पुत्राः सम्पद्यन्तामेवं त्वया कार्यं मयि चेत्प्रीतिरस्तीति । स च महेश्वरस्तान्समानरूपान् समानवयसः समानालङ्कारान्स्प्रष्ट्वा गौर्यै प्रददौ केवमे पुत्राः सन्तिति । अतः सर्वेषु मारुतेषु सूक्तेषु मरुतो रुद्रपुत्रा इति स्तूयन्ते । रौद्रेषु च मरुतां पिता रुद्र इति । अपि च हे अमृत मरणरहित रुद्र मर्तभोजनं मर्तानां मनुष्याणां भोगपर्याप्तमन्नं नोऽस्मभ्यं रास्व । प्रयच्छ । तथा त्मने आत्मने द्वितीयार्थे चतुर्थी मां तोकाय तोकं पुत्रं तनयाय तनयं तत्पुत्रं च मृळ सुखय । पित्रे उदात्तेन विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं रास्व रा दाने व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । त्मने मन्त्रेष्वाङ्यादेरात्मन इत्यत्राऽऽऽदेः [?] छन्दसि दृश्यते । का. ६-४-१४१-१ इति वचनादात्मन आकारलोपः ॥ [read from the print; a few words in the Purāṇic story are in small type, partly doubtful [?]]

idaṃ stutilakṣaṇaṃ vaco marutāmekonapañcāśatsaṃkhyākānāṃ devaviśeṣāṇāṃ pitre janakāya rudrāyeśvarāyocyate | uccāryate | kīdṛśaṃ svādoḥ svādīyo rasavato madhuphalāderapi svādutaram | atiśayena harṣajanakamityarthaḥ | vardhanaṃ stutyasya pravardhakam | stotreṇa hi devatā hṛṣṭā satī pravardhate | rudrasya ca marutāṃ pitṛtvamevamāmnāyate | purā kadācidindro 'surāñjitvā tadānīṃ ditirasuramātendrahananasamarthaṃ putraṃ kāmayamānā tapasā bhartuḥ sakāśādgarbhaṃ lebhe | imaṃ vṛttāntamavagacchannindro vajrahastaḥ san sūkṣmarūpo bhūtvā tasyā udaraṃ praviśya taṃ garbhaṃ saptadhā bibheda | punarapyekaikaṃ saptakhaṇḍamakarot | te sarve garbhaikadeśā yonernirgatyārudan | etasminnavasare līlārthaṃ gacchantau pārvatīparameśvarāvimāndadṛśatuḥ | maheśaṃ prati pārvatyaivamuvāca | ime māṃsakhaṇḍā yathā pratyekaṃ putrāḥ sampadyantāmevaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ mayi cetprītirastīti | sa ca maheśvarastānsamānarūpān samānavayasaḥ samānālaṅkārānspraṣṭvā gauryai pradadau kevame putrāḥ santiti | ataḥ sarveṣu māruteṣu sūkteṣu maruto rudraputrā iti stūyante | raudreṣu ca marutāṃ pitā rudra iti | api ca he amṛta maraṇarahita rudra martabhojanaṃ martānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ bhogaparyāptamannaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ rāsva | prayaccha | tathā tmane ātmane dvitīyārthe caturthī māṃ tokāya tokaṃ putraṃ tanayāya tanayaṃ tatputraṃ ca mṛḷa sukhaya | pitre udāttena vibhakterudāttatvaṃ rāsva rā dāne vyatyayenātmanepadam | tmane mantreṣvāṅyāderātmana ityatrā ' ' 'deḥ [?] chandasi dṛśyate | kā. 6-4-141-1 iti vacanādātmana ākāralopaḥ ‖ [read from the print; a few words in the Purāṇic story are in small type, partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "This speech (vacaḥ) in the form of praise is uttered for the pitṛ, the father, the begetter, of the Maruts — a special group of gods numbering forty-nine — namely Rudra, the lord. How is it? Svādoḥ svādīyaḥ — sweeter than even sweet things like honey-fruit: exceedingly delight-giving. Vardhanam — increasing the one praised: for a deity, delighted by a stotra, grows. And that Rudra is the father of the Maruts is thus handed down: once, long ago, Indra having conquered the asuras, Diti, mother of the asuras, desiring a son able to slay Indra, obtained from her husband by austerity a embryo. Indra, learning this, vajra in hand, made himself subtle, entered her womb, and split that embryo into seven; then again he made each into seven pieces. All these parts of the embryo came out of the womb and wept. At that moment Pārvatī and Parameśvara, going for sport, saw them. Pārvatī said to Maheśa: 'Let these pieces of flesh become sons, each one, thus; do this for me, if you love me.' And Maheśvara, touching them — made of the same form, same age, same ornaments — gave them to Gaurī (saying), 'These are [your] sons.' Hence in all the Mārut-sūktas the Maruts are praised as Rudra's sons; and in the Raudra [hymns] Rudra is the father of the Maruts. Moreover, O deathless Rudra, martabhojanam — food sufficient for the enjoyment of mortal men, rāsva, give to us; and for tmane, myself (the dative in the sense of the accusative), me, tokāya, my son, and tanayāya, his son — mṛḷa, give happiness."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): pitre (the ending accented, udātta); rāsva (rā "to give", ātmanepada by vyatyaya); tmane (ātman, with the loss of the initial ā in the Vedic usage, as stated in Kā. 6-4-141-1 as printed).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"svādoḥ — than sweet things such as honey, by having flavour; svādīyaḥ — more flavourful (pleasing, delight-giving); vardhanam — increasing; idam vacaḥ — this speech in the form of praise; marutām — to the Marut deities; pitre — the begetter; rudrāya — for Rudra; ucyate — is uttered; āmṛta — O deathless Rudra; martabhojanam — food that is to be enjoyed by men; naḥ — to us; rāsva — give; (tathā — and so); tmane — to me; tokāya — to (my) son; tanayāya — (to his) son (and to me); mṛḷa — be gracious."

original p. 126

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"We offer to Rudra, the father of the Maruts, these stotra-sentences, which are more pleasing than honey and the like. O deathless Rudra, give us food fit for human enjoyment. (And likewise) make for me, my children and grandchildren happiness."

English Translation (as printed)

This praise, the sweetest of the sweet, and cause of increase (to the reciter), is addressed to Rudra, the father of the Maruts : immortal Rudra grant us food sufficient for mortals, and bestow happiness on me, my son and my grandson.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

मरुतां पित्रे — Marutāṃ pitre — "There are forty-nine Marut deities; the meaning is: to Rudra, the begetter of the Marut deities. Indra, having conquered the asuras, [the story:] Diti, mother of the asuras, practised austerity in order to get a son who could overcome Indra, and by her husband's service became with child. Indra, learning this, under the pretext of serving the mother, entered the womb of Diti in a subtle form, with his thunderbolt, and cut that embryo first into seven parts, and then each of them into seven, thus forty-nine pieces. Pārvatī and Parameśvara, who move about the world for the good of men, saw these pieces that fell on the earth, having slipped out of the womb. Pārvatī, feeling pity for those lumps of flesh, begged her husband to give them life; at her request Parameśvara made those forty-nine lumps of flesh into sons of one form, ornament and age, and told Pārvatī 'These are your children.' From this tradition the Maruts are said in the Sūktas to be Rudra's sons, and Rudra is said to be the Maruts' father."

स्वादोः स्वादीयः — Svādoḥ svādīyaḥ — "rasavato madhuphalāder api svādutaram | atiśayena harṣajanakam ity arthaḥ": the phrase stutilakṣaṇaṃ vacaḥ (speech of the nature of praise) is a qualifier of the sentence stuti-rūpa vākya. "People who eat, or those who use foods (bhakṣya-bhojya), take pleasure in sweet things such as ghee and honey, which are healthful and pleasing and give joy to the mind;

original p. 127

so a speech addressed to a deity, or a speech uttered with devotion to win the deity, gives the deity pleasure with regard to its devotee and increases the joy of the mind. For this reason the Ṛk says vardhanam ('increasing'). This word, derived from the root vṛdhu vṛddhau, means that the speech of the form of praise increases the pleasure in the mind of the deity by making manifest the greatness of the deity or of the qualities of the object praised. From this the deity, hearing the stotra, becomes pleased with him who praises. 'stotreṇa hi devatā hṛṣṭā satī pravardhate' — Sāyaṇa explains the word vardhana thus; Skandasvāmin too says 'stutir hi devānāṃ vṛddhikarī' — praise increases the strength of the gods."

मर्तभोजनम् — Martabhojanam — "Mortals (marta) are men, who are subject to death. The prayer to Rudra is to favour them so that objects for their enjoyment (food) be obtained. Skandasvāmin: because bhojana is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 as read [?]), the phrase martabhojanam means 'wealth that is the means of enjoyment for men'."

त्मने — Tmane — "dvitīyārthe caturthī": "Here the fourth case is used in the sense of the second case; the meaning is 'me'. The word, meaning ātman ('self'), is used in many other Ṛks:

कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरायोः कथा जाते कवयः को वि वेद । विश्वं त्मना बिभृतो यद्ध नाम वि वर्तेते अहनी चक्रियेव ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१८५-१ [as read])

katarā pūrvā katarāparāyoḥ kathā jāte kavayaḥ ko vi veda | viśvaṃ tmanā bibhṛto yaddha nāma vi vartete ahanī cakriyeva ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-185-1 [as read])

— here tmanā = ātmanā.

तन्न स्तोरिसमद्भुतं पुरु वारं पुरु त्मना ॥ [as read; quotation partly doubtful [?]] (ऋ. सं. १-१४३-१० [as read])

tanna storisamadbhutaṃ puru vāraṃ puru tmanā ‖ [as read; quotation partly doubtful [?]] (ṛ. saṃ. 1-143-10 [as read])

— in this Ṛk puru tmanā means 'bahv ātmanā'.

राकामहं सुहवां सुष्टुती हुवे शृणोतु नः सुभगा बोधतु त्मना । (ऋ. सं. २-३२-४ [as read])

rākāmahaṃ suhavāṃ suṣṭutī huve śṛṇotu naḥ subhagā bodhatu tmanā | (ṛ. saṃ. 2-32-4 [as read])

— in this Ṛk too the word tmanā is explained in the Nirukta in the sense of ātmanā."

original p. 128

तनयाय — Tanayāya — "tokāya [and] tanayāya: tokam = son, tanayam = his son; toka means a son, tanaya a grandson (son's son). The words tuk, tokam, tanayam are stated among the fifteen [as read] names of offspring (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]); so the meaning is 'son'. Thus:

सहस्रं ते स्वपिवात भेषजा मा नस्तोकेषु तनयेषु रीरिषः । (ऋ. सं. २-३३-२ [as read])

sahasraṃ te svapivāta bheṣajā mā nastokeṣu tanayeṣu rīriṣaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 2-33-2 [as read])

येन तोकं च तनयं च धामहे । (ऋ. सं. १-९२-१३ [as read])

yena tokaṃ ca tanayaṃ ca dhāmahe | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-92-13 [as read])

— in these Ṛks the words toka and tanaya are explained as 'sons and grandsons'. Skandasvāmin, following this, explains likewise, and says that the prayer stated is that 'Rudra be gracious to all, to our sons and grandsons who serve Rudra'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.7)

हे रुद्र नोऽस्माकं मध्ये महान्तं वृद्धं मा वधीः । मा हिंसीः । उतापि च नोऽस्माकमर्भकं बालं मा हिंसीः । तथा नोऽस्माकं मध्य उक्षन्तं सेक्तारं मध्यवयस्कं युवानं मा वधीः । उतापि च नोऽस्मदीयमुक्षितं गर्भरूपेण स्त्रीषु निषिक्तमपत्यं मा वधीः । तथा नोऽस्माकं पितरं जनकं मा वधीः । उतापि च मातरं जननीं मा वधीः । तथा नोऽस्माकं प्रियः स्नेहविषयास्तन्वः शरीराणि तनूषु भवा वा प्रजा वा हे रुद्र मा रिरिषः । मा हिंसीः ॥ [grammatical tail: vadhīḥ — han with vadha-substitution, luṅ 2nd singular, sic, iṭ, the elision by ato lopasya sthānivadbhāvāt…; ririṣaḥ — riṣ "to injure", the ṇyanta luṅ, caṅ, doubling, ṇilopa, the reduplication shortening by bahulaṃ chandasi.]

he rudra no 'smākaṃ madhye mahāntaṃ vṛddhaṃ mā vadhīḥ | mā hiṃsīḥ | utāpi ca no 'smākamarbhakaṃ bālaṃ mā hiṃsīḥ | tathā no 'smākaṃ madhya ukṣantaṃ sektāraṃ madhyavayaskaṃ yuvānaṃ mā vadhīḥ | utāpi ca no 'smadīyamukṣitaṃ garbharūpeṇa strīṣu niṣiktamapatyaṃ mā vadhīḥ | tathā no 'smākaṃ pitaraṃ janakaṃ mā vadhīḥ | utāpi ca mātaraṃ jananīṃ mā vadhīḥ | tathā no 'smākaṃ priyaḥ snehaviṣayāstanvaḥ śarīrāṇi tanūṣu bhavā vā prajā vā he rudra mā ririṣaḥ | mā hiṃsīḥ ‖ [grammatical tail: vadhīḥ — han with vadha-substitution, luṅ 2nd singular, sic, iṭ, the elision by ato lopasya sthānivadbhāvāt…; ririṣaḥ — riṣ "to injure", the ṇyanta luṅ, caṅ, doubling, ṇilopa, the reduplication shortening by bahulaṃ chandasi.]

Sense (mine): "O Rudra, among us do not slay (mā vadhīḥ) the mahāntam, the aged; nor our arbhakam, the child; nor among us the ukṣantam, the sprinkler, the youth in middle age; nor our ukṣitam, the offspring cast into women in the form of an embryo; nor our father, the begetter; nor our mother, the bearer; and our dear tanvaḥ, bodies — or tanūṣu bhavāḥ, progeny born in the bodies — O Rudra, do not hurt (mā ririṣaḥ)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he rudra — O Rudra; naḥ — among us; mahāntam — the old (the elder); mā vadhīḥ — do not slay; uta — and; naḥ arbhakam — our child; mā (vadhīḥ) — do not slay; naḥ ukṣantam — our young men, the producers of children; mā (vadhīḥ); uta — and; naḥ — our; ukṣitam — the children in the womb; mā (vadhīḥ); naḥ pitaram — our father; mā (vadhīḥ); uta — and; mātaram mā (vadhīḥ) — do not slay our mother; naḥ priyāḥ — our dear; tanvaḥ — embodied progeny; mā ririṣaḥ — do not injure."

original p. 131

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Rudra, do not kill any one of us — the elders, the children, the youths who are begetters, the children in the womb, father, mother, and dear friends."

English Translation (as printed)

Injure not, Rudra, those amongst us who are old or young, who are capable of begetting, or who are begotten, nor a father, nor a mother, nor afflict our precious persons.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

तन्वः — Tanvaḥ — "śarīrāṇi tanūṣu bhavāḥ prajā vā": "though tanūḥ (the body) is a word that is singular, here the plural tanvaḥ is used; 'bodies, or progeny born from bodies'."

अर्भकम् — Arbhakam — "bālam": "since the word arbhaka is read among the twelve [as read] names of 'small' (hrasva) 'kṣullaka', 'hrasva' and so on (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), it means 'small'. Small here means a child not yet of age."

रुद्र — Rudra — "when explaining the meaning of this word they say 'rodayatīti rudraḥ' — Rudra is he who makes [the world] weep; and, following the quality of tamas mainly in all the world, [they say] Rudra is he who dissolves the world. Therefore in this Ṛk the prayer is made that Rudra may protect without harm us, who sacrifice to him and serve him with salutations; our children; our relatives who enjoy happiness in youth; the children in the womb in our lineage; our mothers and fathers; and our dear bodies."

उक्षन्तम् उक्षितम् — Ukṣantam, ukṣitam — "these words are formed from the root ukṣa secane, 'to sprinkle'. Ukṣantam: since it is in the present tense, 'one who sprinkles the seed (retas)', who is in youth (retasaḥ sektāram); and he explains that the word ukṣitam likewise has this meaning of derivation: 'the child in the womb now, who has to be born later'."

original p. 132

he rudra no 'smākaṃ tokādiviṣaye mā ririṣaḥ | mā hiṃsīḥ | tokaśabdaḥ putravācī | tanayastatputraḥ | āyurityantodāttro [?] manuṣyanāma | putrapautravyatirikto yo 'smadīyo manuṣyastasmin goṣu paśvādiṣu ca mā ririṣaḥ | hiṃsāṃ mā kṛthāḥ | tathā he rudra vīrān vikrāntān śauryopetānasmadīyān bhāmitaḥ kruddhaḥ san mā vadhīḥ | mā hiṃsīḥ | vayaṃ ca haviṣmanto havirbhiryuktāḥ santaḥ sadamit sarvadaiva tvāṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmahe ‖ āyau | iṇ gatau | chandasīṇaḥ ityanyatpratyayaḥ | bhāmitaḥ | bhāmu krodhe krodhikaraṇe ceti kartari ktaḥ | havāmahe | hveño 'liṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam ‖

Sense (mine): "O Rudra, in regard to our toka and the rest do not harm (mā ririṣaḥ). Toka denotes 'son'; tanaya, his son; āyu (accent on the last syllable) is a name of man: do not harm any men of ours other than sons and grandsons; nor goṣu, in cattle and other beasts. Likewise, O Rudra, do not kill, angered (bhāmitaḥ), our heroes, valiant men endowed with courage. And we, haviṣmantaḥ, equipped with oblations, ever (sadam it) call thee, havāmahe."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he rudra — O Rudra; naḥ toke — in the matter of our sons (offspring); mā ririṣaḥ — do not injure; tanaye mā — nor [injure] our grandsons; naḥ āyau mā — do not injure the people who are ours; naḥ goṣu — our cows; naḥ aśveṣu mā — nor our horses; naḥ vīrān — our heroes; bhāmitaḥ — angered; mā vadhīḥ — do not kill; (vayaṃ ca — we also); haviṣmantaḥ — possessing oblations and the like; sadam it — always; tvā — thee; havāmahe — we call (invoke) and worship."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Rudra, do not kill, in anger, our sons, grandsons, other people, cows, horses, or heroes. We always invoke and worship thee with oblations and the like."

English Translation (as printed)

Harm us not, Rudra, in our sons or grandsons, or other male descendants, nor in our cattle, nor in our horses ; inflamed with anger, kill not our valiant men, for we, presenting clarified butter, perpetually invoke you.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

आयौ — Āyau — "the word āyuḥ is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]); and āyus is also used in the sense of 'span of life'. But Sāyaṇa: 'āyur ity antodāttaḥ manuṣyanāma | putrapautravyatirikto yo 'smadīyaḥ manuṣyas tasmin' — āyu, with the accent on the last syllable, is a name for man: 'in a man of ours who is other than sons and grandsons'. Since the word āyu has the accent on the last syllable, here it conveys 'man', he explains: 'our relative, a man other than sons and grandsons'. Skandasvāmin says that since the word āyuś is stated among the names of man (Ni. 2-3 as read [?]) as āyavaḥ, the word conveys the meaning 'man', explaining paricārakāḥ — 'attendants, servants'. The word āyus is used in various contexts in different meanings —

original p. 135

मा नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिन्द्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतः परि ख्यन् । (ऋ. सं. १-१६२-१ [as read])

mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyurindra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-162-1 [as read])

— in this Ṛk, āyuḥ = satatagantā vāyuḥ — the wind, whose nature is to be always moving, is the sense in which it is used —

यमृत्विजो वृजने मानुषासः प्रयस्वन्त आयवो जीजनन्त । (ऋ. सं. १-६०-३ [as read])

yamṛtvijo vṛjane mānuṣāsaḥ prayasvanta āyavo jījananta | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-60-3 [as read])

एतानि वामश्विना वीर्याणि प्र पूर्व्याण्यायवोऽवोचन् । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-२३ [as read])

etāni vāmaśvinā vīryāṇi pra pūrvyāṇyāyavo 'vocan | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-23 [as read])

— in these Ṛks the Bhāṣyakāra explains āyavaḥ as 'manuṣyāḥ' (men);

नन्मा मायुः प्र सू तिर कृधी सहस्रसामृषिम् । [as read, [?]] (ऋ. सं. १-६०-११ [as read])

nanmā māyuḥ pra sū tira kṛdhī sahasrasāmṛṣim | [as read, [?]] (ṛ. saṃ. 1-60-11 [as read])

आहेळमानो वरुणेह बोध्युरुशंस मा न आयुः प्र मोषीः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-२४-११ [as read])

āheḷamāno varuṇeha bodhyuruśaṃsa mā na āyuḥ pra moṣīḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-24-11 [as read])

प्रायुस्तारिष्टं नी रपांसि मृक्षतं सेधतं द्वेषो भवतं सचाभुवा । (ऋ. सं. १-३४-११ [as read])

prāyustāriṣṭaṃ nī rapāṃsi mṛkṣataṃ sedhataṃ dveṣo bhavataṃ sacābhuvā | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-34-11 [as read])

— in these Ṛks and others the word āyus is explained as jīvita, 'life'.

ते नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिन्द्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतो जुषन्त । (ऋ. सं. ३-४६-३ [as read])

te no mitro varuṇo aryamāyurindra ṛbhukṣā maruto juṣanta | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-46-3 [as read])

— in this Ṛk the word āyus conveys the meaning 'food'.

"In this Ṛk, too, as in the previous Ṛk, the prayer is addressed to Rudra. Sāyaṇa explains that, accepting the locative (viṣayasaptamī) for all the seventh-case words here, the prayer is taught in this mantra that Rudra should not harm in matters concerning those men. Skandasvāmin, since the seventh case has the meaning of the second case, explains 'tokaṃ tanayaṃ mā vadhīḥ' — 'do not kill sons, grandsons and the like'."

भामितः — Bhāmitaḥ — "kruddhaḥ": angry. "Since the word bhāmate is read (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]) among the ten [as read] verb-names of the nature of anger (krodha), beginning reḍate, heḍate, the form bhāmitaḥ is derived from the root bhāmu ('to be angry'). The prayer is made here that Rudra, being angry, should not harm us or the members of our household we have to support,

original p. 136

sukhaṃ rāsva | dehi | api ca te tvadīyā sumatiḥ kalyāṇe buddhirmṛḷayattamā mṛḍayitṛtamā sukhayitṛtamā | ata eva bhadrā bhajanīyā hi | yasmādevaṃ tasmādvayaṃ te tvadīyamavo rakṣaṇaṃ vṛṇīmahe | sambhajāmahe ‖ [grammatical tail: akaram — kṛ in the luṅ, the Vedic luṅlaṅliṭ for the present, cli → aṅ by kṛmṛdṛruhibhyaś chandasi; guṇa; pitar — vocative, nighāta of pitar marutām; asme — supāṃ sulug, the śe substitution for the plural dative; mṛḷayattamā — mṛḍ "to be gracious", śatṛ in the ṇic; tamap with the Vedic accent.]

Sense (mine): "For the devasuvāṃ haviḥṣu [offerings] in the Rudra-pasu rite, 'upa te stomān' is the yājyā and anuvākyā; and in the Sūtra: 'upa te stomān paśupā ivākaram — two' (Āś. 4-11 as read [?]). O Rudra, I bring stomān, mantras in the form of praise, to thee (upākaram): I offer them. An illustration: paśupā iva — as a herdsman who protects cattle, having taken in the morning the cattle entrusted to him, returns them in the evening to their owners, so I return to thee, as a means of praising thee, the mantras in the form of praise [which came] from thee. O pitar marutām, father of the gods named Maruts, Rudra, asme, to us, give sumnam, happiness. And thy sumati, thy favourable understanding, is mṛḷayattamā, the most gracious, the happiness-making; therefore it is bhadrā, to be honoured. Since that is so, we vṛṇīmahe, we choose, ava, thy protection."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he rudra — O Rudra; stomān — the mantras in the form of praise; paśupā iva — like a herdsman (who has taken in the morning the cattle he has led off and brings them in the evening and gives them to the owner); te — to thee; upa ā akaram — I offer (those mantras obtained from thee); he marutāṃ pitaḥ — O father of the Maruts; asme — to us; sumnam — happiness; rāsva — give; te — thy; sumatiḥ — auspicious or favouring thought; mṛḷayattamā — extremely happiness-making; bhadrā hi — is worthy of being honoured; atha — therefore; vayam — we; te avaḥ — thy protection; vṛṇīmahe — pray for (seek)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Rudra, as a cowherd brings back at evening to the owner the cattle taken off in the morning, I offer to thee the mantras in the form of praise obtained from thee. O father of the Maruts, make happiness for us. Because thy favour is most happiness-giving and auspicious, we pray for thy protection."

English Translation (as printed)

I restore to you, the praises (derived from you), as a shepherd (returns his sheep to their owner) ; father of the Maruts, bestow happiness upon me ; your auspicious benignity is the cause of successive delight, therefore we especially solicit your protection.

original p. 139

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

सुम्नम् — Sumnam — "sukham": "since the word sumna is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of happiness (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), the meaning is 'happiness'."

पशुपा इव उप आ अकरम् — Paśupā iva upa ā akaram — "I offer, give, mantras in the form of praise. One who protects cattle, taking them in the morning under his charge to protect them, goes to the forest, grazes them, and in the evening duly hands over to each person his cows, back into his control. In the same way the mantras in the form of praise of Rudra, and the mantras in the form of praise of other deities, shine by the favour of those deities and are used in the praise of those deities. And in the same way the mantras that have Rudra for deity, ending in the praise of Rudra, are to be accepted both by those who sacrifice and by those who perform worship and the like; therefore, by the favour of Rudra, we praise Rudra with the mantras that have come into our minds — this is the sense. From this Rudra is the place for offering the stotras [to him]. Skandasvāmin explains likewise —

भवतस्सकाशाल्लब्धान् स्तोमान् भवत्सन्निधावेव सर्वानुच्चारयामीति [?] ।

bhavatassakāśāllabdhān stomān bhavatsannidhāveva sarvānuccārayāmīti [?] |

— 'the praises obtained from thee, I utter all of them only in thy presence' — so he says."

मरुतां पितः — Marutāṃ pitaḥ — "the fatherhood of Rudra to the Maruts has been explained in the 6th Ṛk."

सुमतिः मृळयत्तमा — Sumatiḥ mṛḷayattamā — "atiśayena sukhayitṛtamā": "the favourable intention of Rudra, who grants auspiciousness to others, is pleasant to all and worthy of honour. The word mṛḷayat, derived from the root mṛḍa 'to be gracious', is a word meaning 'happy'. Saying that this word has also the meaning 'honour', the Nirukta-writer cites examples —

क्षेत्रस्य पतिना वयं हितेनेव जयामसि । गामश्वं पोषयित्न्वा स नो मृळातीदृशे ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-५७-१ [as read])

kṣetrasya patinā vayaṃ hiteneva jayāmasi | gāmaśvaṃ poṣayitnvā sa no mṛḷātīdṛśe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-57-1 [as read])

— here: 'mṛḷātir dānakarmā vā pūjākarmā vā' (Ni. 10-?? as read [?]): the word mṛḷāti is used in the sense of giving or of honouring.

क्षेत्रस्य पतिं मधुमन्तमूर्मिं धेनुरिव पयो अस्मासु धुक्ष्व । मधुश्चुतं घृतमिव सुपूतमृतस्य नः पतयो मृळयन्तु ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-५७-३ [as read])

kṣetrasya patiṃ madhumantamūrmiṃ dhenuriva payo asmāsu dhukṣva | madhuścutaṃ ghṛtamiva supūtamṛtasya naḥ patayo mṛḷayantu ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-57-3 [as read])

original p. 140

मृळयतिर्दानकर्मा पूजाकर्मा वा । (नि. १०-१६ [as read])

mṛḷayatirdānakarmā pūjākarmā vā | (ni. 10-16 [as read])

— in the Nirukta the root mṛḍ is said to be of the sense of 'happiness' or of 'honouring'. The main idea is that Rudra's favourable intention may be gracious to us, and may come to be worthy of honour and productive of happiness."

paśupā iva (paśūn pāti iti paśupāḥ; pā "to protect"; the viṭ suffix by ato maninkvanibvanipaś ca, Pā. 3-2-74 as read [?]; the first-member-accent by kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva); akaram (ḍukṛñ "to do"; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ, Pā. 3-4-6 as read [?], luṅ in the present sense; 1st singular mip; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ, Pā. 3-4-101 as read [?], the am substitution; cli → aṅ by kṛmṛdṛruhibhyaś chandasi, Pā. 3-1-59 as read [?]; the aṅ ṅit-like — ṅidvad; aṅ-guṇa by yadi śloṣo guṇaḥ [as printed, [?]]; raparatva; the augment aṭ; nighāta); rāsva (rā "to give", ātmanepada by vyatyaya; thāsaḥ se → sva by savābhyāṃ vāmau, ṣatva; no nighāta since it stands at the beginning of the pāda, the vikaraṇa-less … the root accent remains); pitaḥ marutām (by paramam api chandasi [as printed — the statement that the āmantrita pitaḥ with the following marutām is treated as a whole] — the nighāta (anudātta) applies to both words by āmantritasya ca, Pā. 8-1-19 as read [?]); asme (the stem asmad; the plural dative bhyas following; supāṃ sulug, Pā. 7-1-39 as read [?], the śe substitution; śeṣe lopaḥ, the elision of the part ending in m [mapar-yantasya]; sāvekācaḥ… the ending accented); bhadrā (bhadi "to be auspicious, happy"; the Uṇādi ra; ṭāp in the feminine); mṛḷayattamā (mṛḍa "to be gracious"; ṇic by hetumati ca; after the ṇyanta the śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śap; guṇa of the ṇic; ay substitution; the chandasy ubhayathā, Pā. 3-4-117 as read [?], making the śatṛ ārdhadhātuka, …).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.10)

हे क्षयद्वीर क्षपितसर्वशत्रुजन रुद्र ते त्वदीयं गोघ्नं यद्गोहननं यद्वा गोहननसाधनमायुधम् । उताऽपि च पुरुषघ्नं पुरुषहननं तत्साधनमायुधं वा तदुभयमारे दूरेऽस्मत्तो विप्रकृष्टदेशे भवतु । अस्मे अस्मासु ते त्वदीयं सुम्नं सुखमस्तु । भवतु । अपि च नोऽस्माकं मृळ । सुखसिद्ध्यर्थं प्रसन्नो भव । हे देव द्योतमान रुद्र नोऽस्माकमधि ब्रूहि च । अधिवचनं पक्षपातेन वचनं ब्राह्मणायाधि ब्रूयात् । तै. सं. २-५-११-१ [as read] । इति यथा । अध अथ चानन्तरं च द्विबर्हा द्वयोः स्थानयोः पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च परिवृद्धः । यद्वा । द्वयोर्दक्षिणोत्तरमार्गयोर्ज्ञानकर्मणोर्वा परिवृद्धः स्वामी । स त्वं नोऽस्मभ्यं शर्म सुखं यच्छ । देहि ॥ [grammatical tail: gośnam — han "to injure", the ka suffix by the statement "ghaṅarthe kavidhānam" in the abstract or instrumental; dvibarhāḥ — bṛh/vṛh "to grow", the asun suffix; first-member accent.]

he kṣayadvīra kṣapitasarvaśatrujana rudra te tvadīyaṃ goghnaṃ yadgohananaṃ yadvā gohananasādhanamāyudham | utā 'pi ca puruṣaghnaṃ puruṣahananaṃ tatsādhanamāyudhaṃ vā tadubhayamāre dūre 'smatto viprakṛṣṭadeśe bhavatu | asme asmāsu te tvadīyaṃ sumnaṃ sukhamastu | bhavatu | api ca no 'smākaṃ mṛḷa | sukhasiddhyarthaṃ prasanno bhava | he deva dyotamāna rudra no 'smākamadhi brūhi ca | adhivacanaṃ pakṣapātena vacanaṃ brāhmaṇāyādhi brūyāt | tai. saṃ. 2-5-11-1 [as read] | iti yathā | adha atha cānantaraṃ ca dvibarhā dvayoḥ sthānayoḥ pṛthivyāmantarikṣe ca parivṛddhaḥ | yadvā | dvayordakṣiṇottaramārgayorjñānakarmaṇorvā parivṛddhaḥ svāmī | sa tvaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ śarma sukhaṃ yaccha | dehi ‖ [grammatical tail: gośnam — han "to injure", the ka suffix by the statement "ghaṅarthe kavidhānam" in the abstract or instrumental; dvibarhāḥ — bṛh/vṛh "to grow", the asun suffix; first-member accent.]

Sense (mine): "O kṣayadvīra, Rudra, destroyer of all enemy folk: thy gonhnam — the killing of cows, or the weapon that is the means of killing cows; and puruṣaghnam — the killing of men, or the weapon that kills men: let both be āre, far from us. Asme — in us — may thy sumna, happiness, be. And mṛḷa, be gracious to us, for the accomplishment of happiness. O shining god Rudra, adhi brūhi, speak on our behalf — adhivacana is speech with partiality [for a party], as 'let him speak on behalf of the Brāhmaṇa' (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-11-1 as read [?]). And then dvibarhāḥ — increased in two places, in earth and in the atmosphere; or, increased in the two paths, the southern and northern [the paths of knowledge and of ritual action], the lord. Such as thou art, śarma, happiness, give (yaccha) to us."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he kṣayadvīra — O Rudra, destroyer of enemies; te — thy; gonhnam — the weapon that is the means of killing cows; uta — and; puruṣaghnam — the weapon that kills men; āre — (from us) far away (be); asme — in us; te — thy; sumnam — happiness; astu — be (and); naḥ mṛḷa — be the cause of happiness to us; deva — O shining Rudra; naḥ adhi brūhi ca — speak on our side; atha ca — afterwards; dvibarhāḥ — thou who art lord of earth and atmosphere (or lord of the two paths of knowledge and of action); naḥ — to us; śarma — happiness; yaccha — give."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Rudra, destroyer of enemies, may thy weapons that kill cows and kill men be far from us. May we have happiness; make us happy; O shining one, speak on our side; thou who art lord of the earth and atmosphere, or of both the path of knowledge and the path of action, give us happiness."

English Translation (as printed)

Destroyer of heroes, may your cow-killing or man-slaying (weapon) be far away, and let the felicity granted by you be ours ; favour us ; speak,

original p. 143

brilliant hero, in our behalf, and grant us, you who are mighty over the two (realms of heaven and earth), prosperity.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

क्षयद्वीर — Kṣayadvīra — "kṣapitasarvaśatrujana": "he who destroys all enemies: Rudra. The meaning of the word kṣayadvīra has been explained in the Ṛks 1-114-1 [and] 1-114-2 [as printed, "1-114-2-?" read as 2 and 3 [?]].

In this Ṛk, since weapons that kill cows and kill men are to be kept far away, the prayer is made that Rudra's graciousness may be in us, and that Rudra may grant happiness. And in accordance with the śruti-statement 'brāhmaṇāyādhi brūyāt' (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-11-1 as read [?]) — 'one should speak, on behalf of, to the Brāhmaṇa, words full of trust' — the prayer is expressed that Rudra, too, show his trust in words in our regard."

द्विबर्हाः — Dvibarhāḥ — "pṛthivī and antarikṣa — one who is excellent in both these places. Or, Sāyaṇa explains: the lord who, protecting the paths — the path of knowledge and the path of action — known as the southern and northern paths, so that they are not obstructed by others, favours so that those entitled to them have entrance into the paths. Skandasvāmin:

द्विबर्हाः — बृंहिवृद्ध्यर्थः यस्मात् स्तोतुः द्वयोर्वर्धयिता बृंह धातुवृद्धौ । [?]

dvibarhāḥ — bṛṃhivṛddhyarthaḥ yasmāt stotuḥ dvayorvardhayitā bṛṃha dhātuvṛddhau | [?]

— the root bṛṃh conveys the meaning of increase. 'Therefore Rudra makes increase for those who sacrifice and for those who praise.' Or, 'since Rudra, in sacrifice and in battle, the two in which [the one] stands in the middle and the one in the upper [madhyamottamayoḥ], by the form of heroism (vīryarūpeṇa) is middle-ranked in the atmosphere, as the Āditya he receives the juice of the world in the atmosphere by his energy' [the Sanskrit of this passage is in small type and corrupt in the print [?]]. In sacrifice and in battle he favours those who rely on him by his own strength with increase: hence he is dvibarhāḥ. Since Rudra is a deity of the middle region (atmosphere), as the Āditya he collects the sap of the atmosphere by his surpassing power and has the capacity to grow in the atmosphere; therefore they explain dvibarhāḥ as 'having increase in two ways'. 'dvayoḥ sthānayor barhate pravardhate iti dvibarhāḥ' — the account of the meaning of this word is given in different ways in the two bhāṣyas."

original p. 144

गोघ्नम् — Gonhnam — "the Bhāṣyakāra explains the meaning as 'a weapon that is the means of killing cows'. Here the word go may be taken in the general sense of 'cattle'. As in the śruti-statement 'paśūnāṃ pataye' — Rudra being lord of animals protects them — in the Ṛk 8 of this very sūkta, 'mā no goṣu mā no aśveṣu ririṣaḥ', the prayer is: do not harm our cows, our horses. Therefore the prayer is made here that [Rudra] protect, without loss to us, our cows and other animals."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly)

gonhnam (han "to injure, to go"; the ka suffix by the statement "ghaṅarthe kavidhānam" in the abstract or instrumental sense; being kit, gamahanajana…, Pā. 6-4-98 as read [?], elision of the penultimate; hoho 'nte, Pā. 7-3-54 as read [?], the h → gh (kutva) because n follows; accent from the suffix; as it is a compound whose later member ends in kṛt preceded by a kāraka, the first-member-accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, Pā. 6-2-139 as read [?]; likewise puruṣaghnam); kṣayadvīra (kṣayantaḥ vīrāḥ yasmin saḥ; the vocative nighāta by āmantritasya ca, Pā. 8-1-19 as read [?]); astu (as "to be", loṭ 3rd singular; nighāta); mṛḷa (mṛḍa "to be gracious", loṭ 2nd singular; standing at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; the vikaraṇa accent remains; lengthening in the Saṃhitā by dyaicotastijaḥ, Pā. 6-3-?? as read [?]); brūhi (brūñ "to speak", loṭ 2nd singular; nighāta); yaccha (dāṇ "to give"; loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi; pāghrādhmā…, Pā. 7-3-78 as read [?], yaccha for dā; ato heḥ, elision of hi; nighāta); dvibarhāḥ (bṛha/bṛhi "to grow"; dvayoḥ sthānayoḥ barhate pravardhate iti dvibarhāḥ; the asun suffix by sarvadhātubhya asun; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca…

Ṛk 11 (Triṣṭubh)

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.11)

अवोचाम नमो अस्मा अवस्यवः शृणोतु नो हवं रुद्रो मरुत्वान् । तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ ११ ॥

avocāma namo asmā avasyavaḥ śṛṇotu no havaṃ rudro marutvān | tanno mitro varuṇo māmahantāmaditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 114.11)

अवोचाम । नमः । अस्मै । अवस्यवः । शृणोतु । नः । हवम् । रुद्रः । मरुत्वान् । तत् । नः । मित्रः । वरुणः । ममहन्ताम् । अदितिः । सिन्धुः । पृथिवी । उत । द्यौः ॥ ११ ॥

avocāma | namaḥ | asmai | avasyavaḥ | śṛṇotu | naḥ | havam | rudraḥ | marutvān | tat | naḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | mamahantām | aditiḥ | sindhuḥ | pṛthivī | uta | dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 146

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 114.11)

अवस्यवो रक्षणमिच्छन्तो वयमवोचाम । एतत्सूक्तरूपं स्तोत्रमवादिष्म । अस्मै रुद्राय नमो नमस्कारोऽस्तु । मरुत्वान् मरुद्भिः स्वकीयैः पुत्रैर्युक्तो रुद्रश्च नोऽस्माकं हवमाह्वानं शृणोतु । स्वीकरोतु । यदस्माभिरुक्तं नोऽस्मदीयं तत्सर्वं मित्रादयः षड्देवता मामहन्ताम् । पूजयन्तु । उतत्तद्वोऽस्यार्थे ॥ [grammatical tail: avocāma — brūñ "to speak", luṅ; vacir substitution; ceḥ sic… asyati-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ, aṅ for cli; vaca um, augment; avasyavaḥ — ava "to protect", bhāve asun, supa ātmanaḥ kyac, kyac chandasi, u by kyāc chandasi; havam — hveñ, saṃprasāraṇa, ap; marutvān — ṛkāya [as printed: ṛtvijaḥ], matup, tasau matvarthe, bha-designation.]

avasyavo rakṣaṇamicchanto vayamavocāma | etatsūktarūpaṃ stotramavādiṣma | asmai rudrāya namo namaskāro 'stu | marutvān marudbhiḥ svakīyaiḥ putrairyukto rudraśca no 'smākaṃ havamāhvānaṃ śṛṇotu | svīkarotu | yadasmābhiruktaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ tatsarvaṃ mitrādayaḥ ṣaḍdevatā māmahantām | pūjayantu | utattadvo 'syārthe ‖ [grammatical tail: avocāma — brūñ "to speak", luṅ; vacir substitution; ceḥ sic… asyati-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ, aṅ for cli; vaca um, augment; avasyavaḥ — ava "to protect", bhāve asun, supa ātmanaḥ kyac, kyac chandasi, u by kyāc chandasi; havam — hveñ, saṃprasāraṇa, ap; marutvān — ṛkāya [as printed: ṛtvijaḥ], matup, tasau matvarthe, bha-designation.]

Sense (mine): "We, avasyavaḥ, desiring protection, have spoken (avocāma): we have uttered this stotra in the form of the sūkta. To this Rudra be namaḥ, salutation. Marutvān — Rudra, accompanied by the Maruts, his own sons — may he hear (śṛṇotu) our hava, invocation: accept it. What has been said by us, our [prayer], may the six deities Mitra and the rest mamahantām — honour (grant)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"avasyavaḥ — we, desirous of protection; avocāma — have recited this sūkta; asmai — to this; rudrāya — Rudra; namaḥ — salutation (be); marutvān — he who is joined with the Maruts; rudraḥ — Rudra; naḥ havam — our invocation; śṛṇotu — may hear, accept; naḥ tat — this praise uttered by us; mitraḥ — Mitra; varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa; aditiḥ — Aditi, the mother of the gods; sindhuḥ — the deity of the ocean; pṛthivī — the deity of the earth; uta — and; dyauḥ — the deity of heaven and so on, together; mamahantām — may they protect."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"We who desire protection have praised in this manner. Salutation to Rudra. May Rudra, who is joined with the Maruts, accept this our prayer. And may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the deities of the ocean, the earth and heaven make this praise of ours worthy."

English Translation (as printed)

Desirous of protection, we have said, reverence be to him ; may Rudra, with the Maruts, hear our invocation ; and may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi-ocean, earth, and heaven be favourable to this our prayer.

original p. 147

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अवस्यवः — Avasyavaḥ — "avaḥ — anna (food), rakṣaṇa (protection), from av 'to protect' (vā). Since the word avas is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]), avas means food —

इवा त्वार्चन्नवसे वन्दमानः सोमस्येवांशुं प्रति जागराहम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१४६-३ [as read])

ivā tvārcannavase vandamānaḥ somasyevāṃśuṃ prati jāgarāham ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-146-3 [as read])

— the word avase, avanāya in this Ṛk is used in the sense of 'for protection'. We have recited these stotras for the sake of food and for the sake of our protection. The prayer is expressed that Rudra, who is joined with his sons the Marut deities, may hear our stotras and protect us."

मित्रो वरुणो ममहन्ताम् — Mitro varuṇo mamahantām — "may Varuṇa and Mitra and Aditi and Sindhu and Pṛthivī and the atmosphere — these six deities — hear our praise and make for us growth. Or, from the root mah with the pūjārtha sense 'to honour', the form mamahantām arises: the meaning is 'may this stotra be honoured by the deities, bringing delight to their minds'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar page, noted briefly)

avocāma (brūñ "to speak", luṅ 1st plural; brūvo vaciḥ, Pā. 2-4-53 as read [?], vaci for the root; cli as vikaraṇa; asyati-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ, Pā. 3-1-52 as read [?], the aṅ for cli; vaca um, Pā. 7-4-20 as read [?], the augment um; ito 'tyāt kar [as printed, [?]]; guṇa; the augment aṭ; ato dīrgho yañi, Pā. 7-3-101 as read [?], lengthening before ma for the stem ending in a; at the beginning of a pāda there is no nighāta; as the augment is udātta the word has the first-syllable accent); avasyavaḥ (av "to protect", in the abstract sense sarvadhātubhya asun, Pā. 3-4-?? as read [?]; avaḥ ātmana icchati iti avasyati, supa ātmanaḥ kyac, Pā. 3-1-8 as read [?]; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; after the kyac-ending kyāc chandasi, Pā. 3-2-170 as read [?], the u suffix; ato lopaḥ, Pā. 6-4-48 as read [?], the elision of the a of kyac; the word becomes avasyu; the accent from the suffix on the last syllable; nominative plural jas with guṇa by jasi ca, Pā. 7-3-109 as read [?], and avādeśa); śṛṇotu (śru "to hear", loṭ 3rd singular; śṛ for śru by śruvaḥ śṛ ca, Pā. 3-1-74 as read [?], śnu as vikaraṇa; guṇa; ṇatva; no nighāta at the beginning of a pāda; the vikaraṇa accent remains); havam (hveñ "to compete, to call", the suffix ap in the abstract sense by bhāve 'nupasargasya, Pā. 3-3-?? as read [?]; saṃprasāraṇa of the root, pūrvarūpa; guṇa and av; ap is pit hence unaccented, by supiti [as printed] the root accent remains; accusative singular); marutvān (marutaḥ asya santi; matup by tad asyāsty asmin, Pā. 5-2-94 as read [?]; jhayaḥ, Pā. 8-2-10 as read [?], va for the m of matup; te mantrārthe, the bha-designation by svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne, Pā. 1-4-?? Sūkta 115 — "citraṃ devānām"

original p. 149

Heading (Kannada): "nūrahadinaidaneya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-fifteenth Sūkta."

Anukramaṇī and Sāyaṇa's introduction (Sanskrit, as printed):

चित्रमिति षडृचं दशमं सूक्तं कुत्सस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं सूर्यदेवताकम् । तथा चानुक्रान्तं । चित्रं षट् सौर्यमिति ॥ अश्विनशस्त्रे सूर्योदयादूर्ध्वं सौर्याणि सूक्तानि शंसनीयानि । तत्रेदं सूक्तं शंसनीयम् । सूत्रितं च । चित्रं देवानां नमो मित्रस्य । आ. ६-५ । इति ॥ अदितेस्त्रिस्र ऋचः सौर्यस्य पशोर्वपापुरोडाशहविषां क्रमेणानुवाक्याः । ततो द्वे वपापुरोडाशयोर्याज्ये । तथा च सूत्रितम् । चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकमिति पञ्च शं नो भव चक्षसा शं नो अह्नेति [?] । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥ अतिमूर्तिनाम्न्येकाहे शुनासीर्ये पर्वणि च सूर्यस्य हविषश्चित्रं देवानामित्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च तरणिर्विश्वदर्शतश्चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकमिति याज्यानुवाक्याः । आ. ८-८ [?] । इति ॥

citramiti ṣaḍṛcaṃ daśamaṃ sūktaṃ kutsasyārṣaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ sūryadevatākam | tathā cānukrāntaṃ | citraṃ ṣaṭ sauryamiti ‖ aśvinaśastre sūryodayādūrdhvaṃ sauryāṇi sūktāni śaṃsanīyāni | tatredaṃ sūktaṃ śaṃsanīyam | sūtritaṃ ca | citraṃ devānāṃ namo mitrasya | ā. 6-5 | iti ‖ aditestrisra ṛcaḥ sauryasya paśorvapāpuroḍāśahaviṣāṃ krameṇānuvākyāḥ | tato dve vapāpuroḍāśayoryājye | tathā ca sūtritam | citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkamiti pañca śaṃ no bhava cakṣasā śaṃ no ahneti [?] | ā. 3-8 | iti ‖ atimūrtināmnyekāhe śunāsīrye parvaṇi ca sūryasya haviṣaścitraṃ devānāmityeṣā yājyā | sūtritaṃ ca taraṇirviśvadarśataścitraṃ devānāmudagādanīkamiti yājyānuvākyāḥ | ā. 8-8 [?] | iti ‖

Sense: "citram — the sixth-Ṛk, tenth sūkta (of this anuvāka), of Kutsa; Triṣṭubh; deity Sūrya; so the Anukramaṇī: 'citraṃ ṣaṭ sauryam'. In the Aśvina-śastra, after sunrise, the Solar hymns are to be recited; among them this sūkta is to be recited; and so the Sūtra: 'citraṃ devānāṃ namo mitrasya' (Āś. 6-5 as read [?]). The three Ṛks addressed to Aditi [as read: aditestisra ṛcaḥ, the print's wording is doubtful [?]] are the anuvākyās in turn for the omentum, the cake and the oblations of the Solar animal sacrifice; then two are the yājyās of the omentum and the cake; and so the Sūtra says 'citraṃ devānām udagād anīkam — five; śaṃ no bhava cakṣasā śaṃ no ahnā' (Āś. 3-8 as read [?]). In the one-day rite called Atimūrti, in the Śunāsīrya parvan, 'citraṃ devānām' is the yājyā for the oblation to Sūrya; and the Sūtra says 'taraṇir viśvadarśataḥ' and 'citraṃ devānām udagād anīkam' as yājyā and anuvākyā (Āś. 8-8 as read [?])."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "This sūkta citraṃ devānām is the tenth sūkta in the sixteenth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa; the deity is Sūrya; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said 'citraṃ ṣaṭ sauryam'. In the recitation of the Aśvina-śastra mantras, when the sūktas related to Sūrya are recited after sunrise, this sūkta is applied, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra sūtra 'citraṃ devānāṃ namo mitrasya' (Āś. 6-5 as read [?]). The first three Ṛks of this sūkta, in the offering of the omentum, the cake and the oblations in the animal sacrifice connected with Sūrya, are to be used as puroanuvākyā mantras, and the next two Ṛks as yājyā mantras, as stated in the sūtra 'citraṃ devānām udagād anīkam iti pañca śaṃ no bhava cakṣasā śaṃ no ahnā' (Āś. 3-8 as read [?]). And in the ekāhe called Atimūrti, when the śunāsīra [rite] is performed, one Ṛk 'citraṃ devānām' is to be used as a yājyā mantra for Sūrya; the sūtra 'taraṇir viśvadarśataś citraṃ devānām udagād anīkam iti yājyānuvākyāḥ' (Āś. 8-8 as read [?]) shows this."

original p. 150

सूक्त—११५ (Sūkta 115) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१६ ॥ सूक्त—११५ ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—६ small numeral; as printed ॥ Number of Ṛks: 6. Ṛṣi: Kutsa Āṅgirasa. Devatā: Sūrya. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 115.1)

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अन्तरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥ १ ॥

citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 115.1)

चित्रम् । देवानाम् । उत् । अगात् । अनीकम् । चक्षुः । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । अग्नेः । आ । अप्राः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । अन्तरिक्षम् । सूर्यः । आत्मा । जगतः । तस्थुषः । च ॥ १ ॥

citram | devānām | ut | agāt | anīkam | cakṣuḥ | mitrasya | varuṇasya | agneḥ | ā | aprāḥ | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | antarikṣam | sūryaḥ | ātmā | jagataḥ | tasthuṣaḥ | ca ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 115.1)

देवानां दीव्यन्तीति देवा रश्मयः । तेषां देवजनानामेव वानीकं तेजःसमूहरूपं चित्रमाश्चर्यकरं सूर्यस्य मण्डलमुदगात् । उदयाचलं प्राप्तमासीत् । कीदृशम् । मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेश्च । उपलक्षणमेतत् । तदुपलक्षितानां जगतां चक्षुः प्रकाशकम् । चक्षुरिन्द्रियस्थानीयं वा । उदेयं प्राप्य च द्यावापृथिवी दिवं पृथिवीमन्तरिक्षं चाप्राः । स्वकीयेन तेजसा आ समन्तादपूरयत् । उद्गृहीतमण्डलान्तर्वर्ती सूर्योऽन्तर्यामितया सर्वस्य प्रेरकः परमात्मा जगतो जङ्गमस्य तस्थुषः स्थावरस्य चात्मा स्वरूपभूतः । स हि सर्वस्य स्थावरजङ्गमात्मकस्य कार्यवर्गस्य कारणं । कारणाच्च कार्यं नातिरिच्यते । तथा च पारमर्षं सूत्रं । तदनन्यत्वमारम्भणशब्दादिभ्यः । वेदां. २-१-१४ [as read] । इति ॥ यद्वा । स्थावरजङ्गमात्मकस्य सर्वस्य प्राणिजातस्य जीवात्मा । उदिते हि सूर्ये मृतप्रायं सर्वं जगत्प्रबुद्धं चेष्टायुक्तं सदुपलभ्यते । तथा च श्रूयते । योऽसौ तपन्नुदेति स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेतीति । तै. आ. १-१४-१ [as read] । इति ॥ [grammatical tail follows: aprāḥ — prā "to fill", luṅ, cli…; jagataḥ — gam with kvip… tasthuṣaḥ — ṣṭhā with kvasu, saṃprasāraṇa…]

devānāṃ dīvyantīti devā raśmayaḥ | teṣāṃ devajanānāmeva vānīkaṃ tejaḥsamūharūpaṃ citramāścaryakaraṃ sūryasya maṇḍalamudagāt | udayācalaṃ prāptamāsīt | kīdṛśam | mitrasya varuṇasyāgneśca | upalakṣaṇametat | tadupalakṣitānāṃ jagatāṃ cakṣuḥ prakāśakam | cakṣurindriyasthānīyaṃ vā | udeyaṃ prāpya ca dyāvāpṛthivī divaṃ pṛthivīmantarikṣaṃ cāprāḥ | svakīyena tejasā ā samantādapūrayat | udgṛhītamaṇḍalāntarvartī sūryo 'ntaryāmitayā sarvasya prerakaḥ paramātmā jagato jaṅgamasya tasthuṣaḥ sthāvarasya cātmā svarūpabhūtaḥ | sa hi sarvasya sthāvarajaṅgamātmakasya kāryavargasya kāraṇaṃ | kāraṇācca kāryaṃ nātiricyate | tathā ca pāramarṣaṃ sūtraṃ | tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ | vedāṃ. 2-1-14 [as read] | iti ‖ yadvā | sthāvarajaṅgamātmakasya sarvasya prāṇijātasya jīvātmā | udite hi sūrye mṛtaprāyaṃ sarvaṃ jagatprabuddhaṃ ceṣṭāyuktaṃ sadupalabhyate | tathā ca śrūyate | yo 'sau tapannudeti sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyodetīti | tai. ā. 1-14-1 [as read] | iti ‖ [grammatical tail follows: aprāḥ — prā "to fill", luṅ, cli…; jagataḥ — gam with kvip… tasthuṣaḥ — ṣṭhā with kvasu, saṃprasāraṇa…]

Sense (mine): "Devānām — the devāḥ are the rays ('those that shine, dīvyanti'); of those very bright beings, the anīka — a mass of splendour, a wonder-working orb of the Sun — udagāt, has risen, has reached the eastern mountain. How is it? It is the cakṣuḥ, eye, shower, of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni — and this is an indication of the worlds characterised by them: or it stands in the place of the organ of sight. And having risen, it āprāḥ filled dyāvāpṛthivī, heaven, earth and the atmosphere, with its own splendour. The Sun, abiding within the risen orb, as inner controller, the impeller of all, the Supreme Self, is the ātmā, the very nature, of jagataḥ, the moving, and tasthuṣaḥ, the unmoving. For he is the cause of the whole class of effects, moving and unmoving; and the effect is not other than the cause; as the sūtra of Pārāśarya (Vyāsa) says, 'tad ananyatvam ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ' (Vedānta-sūtra 2-1-14 as read [?]). Or: he is the jīvātman of the entire class of beings, moving and unmoving; for when the Sun rises, the whole world, nearly dead, is found awake and active; as the śruti says: 'yo 'sau tapann udeti sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇān ādāyodeti' (Tai. Ā. 1-14-1 as read [?])."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"devānām — of the shining rays; anīkam — the mass; citram — the wonder-causing; mitrasya varuṇasya agneḥ — of Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni (the universe together with these); cakṣuḥ — the eye-like (disc of the Sun); udagāt — having risen; dyāvāpṛthivī — heaven and earth; antarikṣaṃ ca — and the atmosphere; ā aprāḥ — has filled everywhere; sūryaḥ — the Sun abiding in the orb; jagataḥ — of the moving (and); tasthuṣaḥ ca — of the unmoving world; ātmā — the essential self (the impeller)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The orb of the Sun, which is a mass of shining rays, wonder-causing, the eye-like [shower] of the whole universe beginning with Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni, has risen and filled the heavens, the earth and the atmosphere. That Sun abiding in the orb is the essential self of this moving and unmoving world, as its inner controller and impeller."

original p. 152

English Translation (as printed)

The wonderful host of rays has risen ; the eye of Mitra, Varuna, and Agni ; the sun, the soul of all that moves or is immoveable, has filled (with his glory) the heaven, the earth and the firmament.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

देवानाम् — Devānām — "among the many meanings, taking the sense 'splendour' from the root div, 'those that shine, cause light (dīvyanti)' — here the word deva means rays. In accordance with the view that holds only the quality as the meaning (dharmamātra), when one considers 'ray' as having parts, those devas are, taking them as possessors of parts, the shining deities — this is conveyed."

अनीकम् — Anīkam — "samūhaḥ": "the word anīka has many meanings, as in the Ṛk

माता देवानामदितेरनीकं यज्ञस्य केतुर्बृहती वि भाहि । (ऋ. सं. १-११३-१९ [as read])

mātā devānāmaditeranīkaṃ yajñasya keturbṛhatī vi bhāhi | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-113-19 [as read])

where anīka means 'rival' [pratispardhi] and 'face' [mukha]. In this Ṛk, which follows the style of poetry and is a description of the Sun at the time of rising, instead of saying that the Sun's rays rise, the mass of rays shining exceedingly is said to rise; and this mass is described as inexpressible [anirvacanīya]. This is to be understood as the ornament rūpaka (metaphor), because the description of the Sun's rising and the Sun's form are, according to the meaning that the Sun is a mass of rays, a figure."

चित्रम् — Citram — "vicitram āścaryakaram": "Sāyaṇa so explains the word citra. By this, the description of the Sun's rising is also a statement of his nature, and since the Sun's form is a mass of rays, it is a rūpaka too."

चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः — Cakṣur mitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ — "the three names Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni are indicated; seeing the general meaning of these terms, it is said here by way of indication (upalakṣaṇa) that the organ of sight, which creates the knowledge that should be known, is the Sun. By this [it is said that] the Sun is the eye of the world together with Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni and the rest

original p. 153

— the meaning being: the Sun appears as the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni, or of the world, by the sentence that is mentioned in the first words as 'a mass'."

आ अप्राः — Ā aprāḥ — "the form of the word aprāḥ, from the root prā 'to fill', takes the prefix ā and is used here. By this the deities and the virtuous and the mass of ascetics, for this world, for the eye, being the ātman of the world of moving and unmoving beings, the Sun fills with his splendour earth, atmosphere and heaven everywhere. That is, the Sun, having risen, illumines the whole world with his lustre."

सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च — Sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthuṣaś ca — "though the Sun, who is a mass of lustre, abides in the middle of the orb, he, having pervaded all, is the inner controller (antaryāmin) of all and impels them to do their works in the proper time. Therefore he is the cause of the origin of the whole class of effects, moving (cara) and unmoving (sthira): the self-nature that is cause becomes the effect according to time and place. The sage Vyāsa, who composed the Vedānta-sūtras, expresses this idea in the sūtra 'tadananyatvam ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ': the meaning of the sūtra is that the cause is not different from the effect — the effect is non-different from the cause. Following this sūtra it is one meaning that the Sun is the Supreme Self. Or: as soon as the Sun has risen, the world, which is like dead, without the knowledge or power to do any work, is lit by the power of knowledge and, like life, shows its liveliness: the śruti 'yo 'sau tapann udeti sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇān ādāyodeti' (Tai. Ā. 1-?-? as read [?]) explains this meaning clearly. The Sun, by making all beings conscious by his rising, is the ātman, the jīva: this shows the greatness of the Sun.

"Apart from this, according to the modern scientific view too, the Sun is the cause of all movements of all things in the world; from the Sun we obtain all kinds of power (energy). For the movements in the life of beings, the motion of the winds that move in the atmosphere, the formation of clouds, the fall of rain, the growth of plants that arise on the earth in all directions, the flow of rivers — for all such works the Sun, or the Sun's rays, are the cause. If there were no light of the Sun …" continues on the next page

original p. 154

"… in this world, if the dense darkness covers it, not even a blade of grass would move. Therefore the sentence sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthuṣaś ca may fittingly be said to express the idea 'The sun is the source of all energies so far as this world (earth) is concerned'" (this last clause is printed in English, as quoted).

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 115.2)

सूर्यो देवीमुषसं रोचमानां मर्यो न योषामभ्येति पश्चात् । यत्रा नरो देवयन्तो युगानि वितन्वते प्रति भद्राय भद्रम् ॥ २ ॥

sūryo devīmuṣasaṃ rocamānāṃ maryo na yoṣāmabhyeti paścāt | yatrā naro devayanto yugāni vitanvate prati bhadrāya bhadram ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 115.2)

सूर्यः । देवीम् । उषसम् । रोचमानाम् । मर्यः । न । योषाम् । अभि । एति । पश्चात् । यत्र । नरः । देवऽयन्तः । युगानि । विऽतन्वते । प्रति । भद्राय । भद्रम् ॥ २ ॥

sūryaḥ | devīm | uṣasam | rocamānām | maryaḥ | na | yoṣām | abhi | eti | paścāt | yatra | naraḥ | deva 'yantaḥ | yugāni | vi 'tanvate | prati | bhadrāya | bhadram ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 115.2)

सूर्यो देवीं दानादिगुणयुक्तां रोचमानां दीप्यमानामुषसमुषोऽभिमानिनीं देवतां पश्चादभ्येति । उषसः प्रादुर्भावानन्तरं तामभिलक्ष्य गच्छति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मर्यो न योषाम् । यथा कश्चिन्मनुष्यः शोभनमयवां [?] गच्छन्तीं युवतिं स्त्रियं सततमनुगच्छति तद्वत् । यत्र यस्यामुषसि जातायां देवयन्तो देवं द्योतमानं सूर्यं यष्टुमिच्छन्तो नरो यज्ञस्य नेतारो यजमाना युगानि । युगशब्दः कालवाची । तेन च तत्र कर्तव्यानि कर्माणि लक्ष्यन्ते । यथा दर्शपूर्णमासाविति । अग्निहोत्रादीनि कर्माणि वितन्वते । विस्तारयन्ति । यद्वा । देवयन्तो देवयोगार्थं धनमात्मन इच्छन्तो यजमानपुरुषा युगानि हलादिना [?] [? हलाद्यवयवभूतानि] कर्षणाय वितन्वते । प्रसारयन्ति । तामुषसमनुगच्छतीत्यर्थः । एवंविधं भद्रं कल्याणं सूर्यं प्रति भद्राय कल्याणरूपाय कर्मफलाय स्तुमः इति शेषः । यद्वा । देवयन्तो देवकामा यजमाना युगानि युग्मानि भूत्वा पत्नीभिः सहिताः सन्तो भद्रं कल्याणमग्निहोत्रादिकं कर्म भद्राय तत्फलार्थं प्रति प्रतीकं यस्यामुषसि प्रवृत्त्यायां वितन्वते । विस्तारयन्ति ॥ [the grammatical tail follows: maryaḥ — mṛñ "to die", the suffix yat; niṣṭarkyadevahūya… as an irregular formation; yugāni; yuj; vitanvate — tanu "to extend", laṭ.] [reading marked [?] where the small type was doubtful]

sūryo devīṃ dānādiguṇayuktāṃ rocamānāṃ dīpyamānāmuṣasamuṣo 'bhimāninīṃ devatāṃ paścādabhyeti | uṣasaḥ prādurbhāvānantaraṃ tāmabhilakṣya gacchati | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | maryo na yoṣām | yathā kaścinmanuṣyaḥ śobhanamayavāṃ [?] gacchantīṃ yuvatiṃ striyaṃ satatamanugacchati tadvat | yatra yasyāmuṣasi jātāyāṃ devayanto devaṃ dyotamānaṃ sūryaṃ yaṣṭumicchanto naro yajñasya netāro yajamānā yugāni | yugaśabdaḥ kālavācī | tena ca tatra kartavyāni karmāṇi lakṣyante | yathā darśapūrṇamāsāviti | agnihotrādīni karmāṇi vitanvate | vistārayanti | yadvā | devayanto devayogārthaṃ dhanamātmana icchanto yajamānapuruṣā yugāni halādinā [?] [? halādyavayavabhūtāni] karṣaṇāya vitanvate | prasārayanti | tāmuṣasamanugacchatītyarthaḥ | evaṃvidhaṃ bhadraṃ kalyāṇaṃ sūryaṃ prati bhadrāya kalyāṇarūpāya karmaphalāya stumaḥ iti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | devayanto devakāmā yajamānā yugāni yugmāni bhūtvā patnībhiḥ sahitāḥ santo bhadraṃ kalyāṇamagnihotrādikaṃ karma bhadrāya tatphalārthaṃ prati pratīkaṃ yasyāmuṣasi pravṛttyāyāṃ vitanvate | vistārayanti ‖ [the grammatical tail follows: maryaḥ — mṛñ "to die", the suffix yat; niṣṭarkyadevahūya… as an irregular formation; yugāni; yuj; vitanvate — tanu "to extend", laṭ.] [reading marked [?] where the small type was doubtful]

Sense (mine): "The Sun abhyeti, follows after, the goddess Uṣas, endowed with qualities such as generosity, shining (rocamānā), after her appearing. An illustration: maryo na yoṣām — as a man constantly follows a good-looking young woman who is going. When Uṣas has arisen, nāraḥ, men, leaders of the sacrifice, sacrificers, devayantaḥ — wishing to worship the shining Sun — yugāni vitanvate: yuga is a word for time, and by it the works to be done then are indicated, such as the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa; they perform the Agnihotra and other works: they spread out. Or: devayantaḥ — wishing wealth for themselves for the sake of association with the gods, the sacrificer-men spread out the yokes — the parts of the plough — for ploughing (karṣaṇāya) (this alternative is in small type, partly doubtful [?]); they follow that Uṣas. Such an auspicious (bhadram) Sun we praise for the auspicious fruit of works in the form of welfare. Or: devayantaḥ — wishing for the gods, the sacrificers, being in pairs (yugāni, couples), together with their wives, perform bhadram, the auspicious work, Agnihotra and the like, for the sake of its fruit, in each [morning] when Uṣas has arisen."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yatra — when (Uṣas has risen); devayantaḥ — wishing to worship the Sun, or desiring wealth for sacrifices to the deities, or eager to worship the deities; naraḥ — sacrificers; yugāni — the Darśa-pūrṇamāsa and other sacrifices that must be done in due order of time; vitanvate — they spread forth at that Uṣas-time; maryaḥ — as a man (any man); yoṣām — a fair young woman; na — as (he follows) from behind; sūryaḥ — the Sun; rocamānām — the shining; uṣasam devīm — Uṣas the deity; paścāt abhyeti — follows (after Uṣas's rising the Sun rises); bhadram prati — to such an auspicious one (the Sun); bhadrāya — for welfare (we pray)."

original p. 157

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"At the rising of Uṣas, the performers of sacrifices, wishing to worship the Sun and others by sacrifices, perform the Darśa-pūrṇamāsa and other sacrifices that must be done in due order of time. As a man follows a beautiful woman, the Sun follows the shining Uṣas. We worship such an auspicious Sun for welfare."

English Translation (as printed)

The sun follows the divine and brilliant Ushas, as a man (follows a young and elegant) woman ; at which season, pious men perform (the ceremonies established for) ages, worshipping the auspicious (sun), for the sake of good (reward)

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

मर्यो न योषाम् — Maryo na yoṣām — "since the word marya is read among the twenty-five [as read] names of man (manuṣya), 'naraḥ' and so on (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]), the word marya means man (Ni. 3-2 and Ni. 4-? as read [?]: 'marya iti manuṣyanāma'). As a man, seeing a beautiful woman, follows her, the Sun follows Uṣas. The manner of a man who is a lover is described here as the cause of the Sun's rising, which comes after the rising of Uṣas. The qualifiers devīm rocamānām show the excellent natural qualities of Uṣas."

देवयन्तः — Devayantaḥ — "the word deva here, according to the context, denotes the Sun: those who desire sacrifice to the Sun — this is the sense. Or the meaning may also be given: those who desire to worship other deities; or, the Bhāṣyakāra explains, those who desire wealth for the sake of worshipping the deities."

नरः — Naraḥ — "yajñasya netāro yajamānāḥ": the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice. "Since the word nara is stated among the twenty-five [as read] names of man (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]), the meaning is 'men'."

युगानि वितन्वते — Yugāni vitanvate — "the word yuga denotes time; from this [the sense is]: the sacrificers perform, in accordance with the times (kāla), the works to be done — Darśa-pūrṇamāsa and the like, and Agnihotra and so on. The word devayantaḥ has one explanation of this kind."

original p. 158

"… for the sake of association with the gods, wishing for wealth for themselves — those who perform sacrifice, aiming at the deities, are sacrificers who desire wealth (dhanāpekṣiṇaḥ): this is the meaning; and for the word yugāni [he gives] 'the parts that form the plough (halādyavayavabhūtāni), for karṣaṇāya, for tillage': [the sense] 'having prepared the implements useful for farming — the plough and the rest — at Uṣas-time, they do the Agnihotra and other works, and afterwards perform works that serve as the means of getting wealth necessary for worldly affairs': this is another kind of meaning. For the word devayantaḥ the meaning: sacrificers who serve the deities and desire their favour (devakāmāḥ). These sacrificers —

युगशब्दः कालविशेषे रथाद्युपकरणे च । (का. ६-१-१३० [as read; Kāśikā])

yugaśabdaḥ kālaviśeṣe rathādyupakaraṇe ca | (kā. 6-1-130 [as read; Kāśikā])

— since the word yuga conveys a particular time and also the equipment of a chariot and the like, yugāni bhūtvā patnībhiḥ sahitāḥ santaḥ — 'being in pairs, together with their wives, performing auspicious works such as Agnihotra, on the rising of Uṣas, in order to obtain the fruit of it': he explains yet another meaning."

भद्रं भद्राय वितन्वते — Bhadraṃ bhadrāya vitanvate — "both words bhadra have the meaning 'auspicious'; one bhadra is the qualifier of the Sun. 'Because they offer sacrifice to the Sun who produces auspiciousness, they praise [him] at Uṣas-time, in order to please the Sun and obtain auspicious fruit' — is the sense."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly)

rocamānām (ruc "to shine", śānac in the laṭ sense; śap; guṇa of the penultimate; āne muk, Pā. 7-2-82 as read [?], the augment muk; the root accent remains as the sārvadhātuka is unaccented); maryaḥ (mṛñ "to die"; yat is irregularly formed by chandasi niṣṭarkyadevahūya…, Pā. 3-1-123 as read [?]; first-syllable accent by yato 'nāvaḥ, Pā. 6-1-213 as read [?]); eti (iṇ "to go", adādi laṭ 3rd singular; nighāta); paścāt (paścāt, by paścāt, Pā. 5-3-33 as read [?], the paś substitution for apara; astāti, the ati suffix is irregularly formed); yatra (nipātasya ca, Pā. 6-3-136 as read [?], lengthening in the Saṃhitā).

original p. 159

Grammar page of Ṛk 2, concluded (noted briefly): naraḥ (nī "to lead"; ap by ṛdor ap, Pā. 3-3-57 as read [?]; guṇa of the root; the root accent remains since ap is pit); devayantaḥ (devān ātmana icchati devayati; kyac by supa ātmanaḥ kyac, Pā. 3-1-8 as read [?]; na chandasy aputrasya, Pā. 7-4-35 as read [?], the lengthening of the a is prevented; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; the stem devayat; nominative plural); yugāni (yujir "to join"; the suffix ghañ in the passive; yugaśabdaḥ kālaviśeṣe rathādyupakaraṇe ca, as read in the Uṇādi list [Kā.], hence no guṇa of the penultimate because of the suffix; for that reason the final accent; cajoḥ kughiṇṇyatoḥ, Pā. 7-3-52 as read [?], the g for j); vitanvate (tanu "to extend", laṭ 3rd plural; ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ, Pā. 7-1-5 as read [?], ā for jh; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; tanādikṛñbhya uḥ, Pā. 3-1-79 as read [?], u as the vikaraṇa; no guṇa as the suffix is ṅit-like by sārvadhātukam apit; yaṇ; since yatra precedes there is no nighāta by nipātair yad yadi…, Pā. 8-1-30 as read [?]; the compound with the prefix vi, through saha supā, Pā. 2-1-4 as read [?], by splitting of rule, is a compound with the verb; and the end of the compound is accented by samāsasya, Pā. 6-1-223 as read [?]). ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 115.3)

भद्राः कल्याणाः । अश्वा एतग्वा इत्येतदुभयमश्वनाम । तत्रैकं क्रियापरं योजनीयम् । अश्वाः सूर्यस्य रथं वहन्तो व्यापनशीला वा हरितः हर्तारश्मयस्तद्वन्तो वा चित्राः विचित्रावयवा अनुमाद्यासः अनुक्रमेण सर्वैः स्तुत्या माद्यनीयाः । एवम्भूताः सूर्यस्यैतग्वा अश्वाः । यद्वा । एतं गन्तव्यं मार्गं गन्तारोऽश्वाः । एतं शबलवर्णं वा प्राप्नुवन्तोऽश्वाः । नमस्यन्तोऽस्माभिर्नमस्यमानाः सन्तो दिवोऽन्तरिक्षस्य पृष्ठमुपरिप्रदेशं पूर्वभागलक्षणमास्थुः । अतिष्ठन्ति । प्राप्तवन्तः । यद्वा । हरितो रसहरणशीला रश्मयो भद्रादिलक्षणविशिष्टा दिवः पृष्ठं नभःस्थलमातिष्ठन्ति । अस्थाय च द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ सद्यस्तदानीमेवैकेनाह्ना परि यन्ति । परितो गच्छन्ति । व्याप्नुवन्तीत्यर्थः ॥ [grammatical tail: aśvāḥ — aśū "to pervade", with kvin, aśipruṣītyādinā; etagvāḥ — iṇ "to go", asi-hasi- …, the suffix tan, gamer ṇauḍādiko bhāve… ṭa [as printed]; bahuvrīhi with first-member accent; anumādyāsaḥ — madi "to praise", yat, yatonāva; namasyantaḥ — namovarivaś …, kyac in the sense of honour; asthuḥ — ṣṭhā, luṅ, gātisthā… elision of sic, jhi → jus.] [a few words doubtful in small type [?]]

bhadrāḥ kalyāṇāḥ | aśvā etagvā ityetadubhayamaśvanāma | tatraikaṃ kriyāparaṃ yojanīyam | aśvāḥ sūryasya rathaṃ vahanto vyāpanaśīlā vā haritaḥ hartāraśmayastadvanto vā citrāḥ vicitrāvayavā anumādyāsaḥ anukrameṇa sarvaiḥ stutyā mādyanīyāḥ | evambhūtāḥ sūryasyaitagvā aśvāḥ | yadvā | etaṃ gantavyaṃ mārgaṃ gantāro 'śvāḥ | etaṃ śabalavarṇaṃ vā prāpnuvanto 'śvāḥ | namasyanto 'smābhirnamasyamānāḥ santo divo 'ntarikṣasya pṛṣṭhamuparipradeśaṃ pūrvabhāgalakṣaṇamāsthuḥ | atiṣṭhanti | prāptavantaḥ | yadvā | harito rasaharaṇaśīlā raśmayo bhadrādilakṣaṇaviśiṣṭā divaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ nabhaḥsthalamātiṣṭhanti | asthāya ca dyāvāpṛthivī dyāvāpṛthivyau sadyastadānīmevaikenāhnā pari yanti | parito gacchanti | vyāpnuvantītyarthaḥ ‖ [grammatical tail: aśvāḥ — aśū "to pervade", with kvin, aśipruṣītyādinā; etagvāḥ — iṇ "to go", asi-hasi- …, the suffix tan, gamer ṇauḍādiko bhāve… ṭa [as printed]; bahuvrīhi with first-member accent; anumādyāsaḥ — madi "to praise", yat, yatonāva; namasyantaḥ — namovarivaś …, kyac in the sense of honour; asthuḥ — ṣṭhā, luṅ, gātisthā… elision of sic, jhi → jus.] [a few words doubtful in small type [?]]

Sense (mine): "Bhadrāḥ — auspicious. Aśvāḥ and etagvāḥ are both names for horses; of these one is to be taken as a verb-qualifier. The horses of the Sun carry his chariot, pervading, haritaḥ (green-tawny, or taking away [hartāraḥ] the rays or possessing them), citrāḥ — of varied limbs, anumādyāsaḥ — to be gladdened in due order by the praise of all. Such are the etagvā aśvāḥ of the Sun. Or: etagvāḥ — horses that go along the road to be travelled; or horses that attain the variegated colour. Namasyantaḥ — being saluted by us — they have mounted (āsthuḥ) the pṛṣṭha, the upper region, of divaḥ, of the atmosphere, namely the eastern part. Or: the rays that take away the sap, with the characters of auspiciousness and so on, mount the back of the sky (the region of space). And having mounted, they go round (pari yanti) dyāvāpṛthivī, heaven and earth, sadyaḥ — at that very time, in a single day."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"bhadrāḥ — auspicious; haritaḥ — of green-tawny colour; citrāḥ — having wonderful limbs; anumādyāsaḥ — praiseworthy in succession; aśvāḥ — the swift ones; sūryasya — of the Sun; etagvāḥ — the horses; namasyantaḥ — worshipped by us; divaḥ pṛṣṭham — the upper part of the atmosphere; ā asthuḥ — they move mounting up; dyāvāpṛthivī — earth and sky; sadyaḥ — in the same day; pari yanti — go round."

original p. 161

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The Sun's horses are auspicious; of wonderful limbs; they have the power of swift movement; they are praised by us. Such green-tawny horses of the Sun, worshipped by us, move mounting in the upper part of the sky. These horses go round earth and sky in a single day."

English Translation (as printed)

The auspicious, swift horses of the sun, well-limbed, road-traversing, who merit to be pleased with praise, reverenced by us, have ascended to the summit of the sky, and quickly circumambulate earth and heaven.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अश्वाः — Aśvāḥ — "turagāḥ — from the root aśū 'to pervade' (vyāptau); or 'those whose nature is to pervade' — those who move swiftly, or whose nature is to pervade."

एतग्वाः — Etagvāḥ — "etaṃ gantavyaṃ mārgaṃ gantāro 'śvāḥ | etāṃ śabalavarṇaṃ vā prāptavanto 'śvāḥ": "horses that go along the road they have to travel; hence 'horses', since they go along the road that lies ahead; or because the word eta conveys various (śabala — mottled) colours (turmeric-yellow, red, white), 'horses endowed with many colours'. Skandasvāmin —

एतग्व इत्यश्वनामान्यत्रेह तु अश्वेन पौनरुक्त्यप्रसङ्गात् क्रियाशब्दः । अतीतेप्सहसः [?] मार्गस्य गन्तारः ॥

etagva ityaśvanāmānyatreha tu aśvena paunaruktyaprasaṅgāt kriyāśabdaḥ | atītepsahasaḥ [?] mārgasya gantāraḥ ‖

— the word etagva elsewhere is a name of horse; but here, since it would be a repetition with aśva, it is a verb-word [i.e. an adjective of action]: 'those that go on the roads they travelled before' (the meaning given in the Kannada: 'those who move on the paths that were traversed on the days that have gone')."

अनुमाद्यासः — Anumādyāsaḥ — "madatir arcatikarmā anuṣṭutyāḥ": "the root mad is read among the forty-four [as read] words beginning arcati (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), 'worthy of praise'. (praises)"

original p. 162

दिवः पृष्ठम् आ अस्थुः — Divaḥ pṛṣṭham ā asthuḥ — "antarikṣasya pūrvabhāgalakṣaṇam upari pradeśaṃ prāptavantaḥ": "they reach the upper region of the atmosphere, namely the eastern part. Or: the rays that draw up the sap (rasaharaṇaśīlāḥ), distinguished by auspiciousness and the rest, mount the sky." "Namasyantaḥ — being worthy of salutation, pervasive, praiseworthy, of many colours, moving along the roads of going fixed for each — the horses of the Sun; or the Sun's rays, which draw water, the Sun's rays and horses spread in the upper part of the atmosphere over earth, atmosphere and everything at the very rising of the Sun. Since the epithets stated in this Ṛk apply equally to the Sun's rays and horses, the sense is that the Sun, in a chariot yoked with such horses, shines with his rays and moves, as the regulator of time."
