॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 115.4)

सूर्यस्य सर्वप्रेरकस्यादित्यस्य तद्देवत्वमीश्वरत्वम् । स्वातन्त्र्यमिति यावत् । महित्वं महत्त्वं माहात्म्यं च तदेतत् । तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्छब्दाध्याहारः । यत्कर्तोः कर्मणामेतत् । प्रारब्धपरिसमाप्तस्य कृष्यादिलक्षणस्य कर्मणो मध्या मध्येऽपरिसमाप्त एव तस्मिन्कर्मणि विततं विस्तीर्णं स्वकीयं रश्मिजालमस्तं गच्छन् सूर्यः सं जभार । अस्माल्लोकाच्छास्त्रात्मन्युपसंहरति । कर्मकराश्च प्रवृत्तमपरिसमाप्तमेव विसृज्यास्तमयं यन्तं सूर्यं दृष्ट्वा । ईदृशं स्वातन्त्र्यं महिमा च सूर्यव्यतिरिक्तस्य कस्यापि न सूर्य एवेदृशं स्वातन्त्र्यं महिमानं चावगाहते । अपि च । इदित्यवधारणे । यदेदयुक्तास्मिन्नेव काले हरितो रसहरणशीलान्स्वरश्मीन् हरिद्वर्णानश्वान्वा सधस्थात्सहस्थानादस्माल्लोकादादायायुक्त । अन्यत्र संयुक्तान्करोति । यद्वा । युजिः केवलोऽपि विपूर्वो द्रष्टव्यः । यद्वैवासौ स्वरश्मीन्विश्वान्सधस्थात् । सह तिष्ठन्त्यस्मिन्निति सधस्थो रथः । तस्मादयुक्त । अमुञ्चत् । आत् अनन्तरमेव रात्री निशा वास आच्छादयित्र तमः सिमस्मै । सिमशब्दः सर्वशब्दपर्यायः । सप्तम्यर्थे चतुर्थी । सर्वस्मिन् लोके तनुते । विस्तारयतीति । यद्वा । वासो वासरमहः । तत्सर्वस्मादस्माल्लोकादपनीय रात्री तमस्तनुते । अत्र निरुक्तम् । तत्सूर्यस्य देवत्वं तन्महित्वं मध्ये यत्कर्मणां क्रियमाणानां वितत[?] संह्रियते । यदा सायुक्त [?] हरणानादित्यर्श्मीन् हरितोऽश्वान्वा । अथ रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै वेसर महरवयुवती सर्वस्मात् ॥ नि. ४-११ [as read] । इति ॥ [the grammatical tail follows in the print: mahitvam — mah "to honour", ini, tasya bhāvas tvatalau; madhyā — supāṃ sulug… ḍāc, kartoḥ — kṛ with tun, guṇa, jñityādi first-syllable accent; vitatam — tanu, niṣṭhā, udāttasya…; jabhāra — bhṛ, liṭ, hṛgrahorbhaḥ — the bha for ha; ayukta — yuj, luṅ, jhalo jhali, sic elision; sadhasthāt — sadha with sthā, ka…; rātrī — rātreś cājasau, jas…] [read from the print; the Nirukta passage is in small type and partly doubtful [?]]

sūryasya sarvaprerakasyādityasya taddevatvamīśvaratvam | svātantryamiti yāvat | mahitvaṃ mahattvaṃ māhātmyaṃ ca tadetat | tacchabdaśruteryacchabdādhyāhāraḥ | yatkartoḥ karmaṇāmetat | prārabdhaparisamāptasya kṛṣyādilakṣaṇasya karmaṇo madhyā madhye 'parisamāpta eva tasminkarmaṇi vitataṃ vistīrṇaṃ svakīyaṃ raśmijālamastaṃ gacchan sūryaḥ saṃ jabhāra | asmāllokācchāstrātmanyupasaṃharati | karmakarāśca pravṛttamaparisamāptameva visṛjyāstamayaṃ yantaṃ sūryaṃ dṛṣṭvā | īdṛśaṃ svātantryaṃ mahimā ca sūryavyatiriktasya kasyāpi na sūrya evedṛśaṃ svātantryaṃ mahimānaṃ cāvagāhate | api ca | idityavadhāraṇe | yadedayuktāsminneva kāle harito rasaharaṇaśīlānsvaraśmīn haridvarṇānaśvānvā sadhasthātsahasthānādasmāllokādādāyāyukta | anyatra saṃyuktānkaroti | yadvā | yujiḥ kevalo 'pi vipūrvo draṣṭavyaḥ | yadvaivāsau svaraśmīnviśvānsadhasthāt | saha tiṣṭhantyasminniti sadhastho rathaḥ | tasmādayukta | amuñcat | āt anantarameva rātrī niśā vāsa ācchādayitra tamaḥ simasmai | simaśabdaḥ sarvaśabdaparyāyaḥ | saptamyarthe caturthī | sarvasmin loke tanute | vistārayatīti | yadvā | vāso vāsaramahaḥ | tatsarvasmādasmāllokādapanīya rātrī tamastanute | atra niruktam | tatsūryasya devatvaṃ tanmahitvaṃ madhye yatkarmaṇāṃ kriyamāṇānāṃ vitata[?] saṃhriyate | yadā sāyukta [?] haraṇānādityarśmīn harito 'śvānvā | atha rātrī vāsastanute simasmai vesara maharavayuvatī sarvasmāt ‖ ni. 4-11 [as read] | iti ‖ [the grammatical tail follows in the print: mahitvam — mah "to honour", ini, tasya bhāvas tvatalau; madhyā — supāṃ sulug… ḍāc, kartoḥ — kṛ with tun, guṇa, jñityādi first-syllable accent; vitatam — tanu, niṣṭhā, udāttasya…; jabhāra — bhṛ, liṭ, hṛgrahorbhaḥ — the bha for ha; ayukta — yuj, luṅ, jhalo jhali, sic elision; sadhasthāt — sadha with sthā, ka…; rātrī — rātreś cājasau, jas…] [read from the print; the Nirukta passage is in small type and partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Of the Sun — the Āditya who impels all — that devatva, lordship (that is, independence); and that mahitva, greatness, majesty — this is it [with yat supplied from the tat]: kartoḥ, of works — in the middle (madhyā) of work begun and not finished, such as ploughing, the Sun, going to his setting, saṃ jabhāra — draws together his extended net of rays, drawing it from this world into himself; and the workmen, seeing the Sun going to his setting, leave off the work begun, unfinished. Such independence and greatness belongs to no one but the Sun: the Sun alone attains such independence and majesty. Moreover, it is for emphasis: yad edayukta — at that very time, when he takes, from this world, from sadhasthāt, from the common place, his sap-drawing haritaḥ — rays, or green-tawny horses — and unyokes (ayukta) them: elsewhere he yokes them. Or the root yuj is to be understood with the prefix vi (as viyuj); or the sadhastha is the chariot ('in which they stand together'), from which he unyoked, released them. Āt, immediately after, rātrī, the night, vāsaḥ — a covering, darkness — tanute, spreads, simasmai — sima is a synonym of sarva, 'all'; the fourth case in the sense of the seventh: in the whole world. Or vāsaḥ = vāsaram, day; removing it from all this world, night spreads the darkness. The Nirukta here: [quotation of the Ṛk with explanation] (Ni. 4-11 as read [?])."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) printed on p. 165

original p. 165

(Grammatical tail of the bhāṣya, concluded — characterized, not transcribed: jabhāra — hṛgrahor bhaḥ; ayukta — yuj with luṅ, jhalo jhali elision of sic; sadhasthāt — sadha + sthā with the suffix ka; the dhatva by sadha māda-sthayoś chandasi; rātrī — rātreś cājasau, jas → ī.)

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yat — (by) which; kartoḥ — works such as ploughing; madhyā — in the middle; vitatam — extended (his own rays); saṃ jabhāra — draws into himself; tat — that; sūryasya — of the Sun; devatvam — lordship (independence); tat — that; mahitvam — greatness; yadā — when; haritaḥ — green-tawny (his horses or rays); sadhasthāt — (from the common place of both) from this earth; ayukta — he yokes; āt it — immediately; rātrī — night; vāsaḥ — the covering darkness; simasmai — in all places; tanute — spreads."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"When the Sun draws his rays into himself — [that is,] the works such as ploughing, though not finished, remain [unfinished] — that is the Sun's lordship and his greatness; and when he has drawn his rays from this earth, afterwards night spreads the darkness."

English Translation (as printed)

Such is the divinity, such is the majesty of the sun, that when he has set, he has withdrawn (into himself) the diffused (light which had been shed) upon the unfinished task ; when he has unyoked his coursers from his car, then night extends the veiling darkness over all.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

मध्या कर्तोः — Madhyā kartoḥ — "madhye aparisamāpta eva tasmin karmaṇi": "in the middle of the work not yet finished. Kartoḥ — karmanāmaitat — this is a name of work: prārabdhaparisamāptasya kṛṣyādilakṣaṇasya karmaṇaḥ. The word kartoḥ is the word apnas; since apas is read among the fifteen [as read] names of work (Ni. 2-1 as read [?]), the meaning is 'work'. When the Sun draws in his rays, the Sun, going to his setting, stops [people] in the very middle of the works they are doing —

original p. 166

— without regard to whether they are complete or not. Following this, those who do agricultural work and others who perform works for livelihood stop their works in the middle, each his own. That at the Sun's setting all stop their works is a custom of the world; this is described here in another way. From the time of the Sun's rising, the Sun's rays spread in all directions, filling earth and atmosphere, and are drawn back at the time of setting in a moment: it stops everything at the same time. [By this] his independence is shown as the greatness equal to that of the Lord who is all-independent and impels everything. In just that way, the Sun at his setting stops the men performing their works, each in his own work. The greatness of the Sun, ordering everything in sequence by his rising and setting alone, is exceedingly wonderful. Such greatness is not in any other deity. The sentence tat sūryasya devatvaṃ tan mahitvam makes this clear."

हरितः सधस्थादयुक्त — Haritaḥ sadhasthād ayukta — "the Sun, withdrawing from this world his rays that draw up water, or the horses of his chariot, makes them spread elsewhere; because of that the Sun's chariot moves elsewhere. Then night draws away the black cloth that covers everything. This means that day, which makes light, runs away. Yāska:

तत्सूर्यस्य देवत्वं तन्महित्वं मध्ये यत्कर्मणां क्रियमाणानां विततं संह्रियते । यदायुक्त हरणानादित्यर्श्मीन् हरितोऽश्वान्वा । अथ रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै वेसर महरवयुवती सर्वस्माद्वा रात्रीव वासस्तनुते इति ॥ (नि. ४-११ [as read])

tatsūryasya devatvaṃ tanmahitvaṃ madhye yatkarmaṇāṃ kriyamāṇānāṃ vitataṃ saṃhriyate | yadāyukta haraṇānādityarśmīn harito 'śvānvā | atha rātrī vāsastanute simasmai vesara maharavayuvatī sarvasmādvā rātrīva vāsastanute iti ‖ (ni. 4-11 [as read])

— the Sun withdraws his rays that draw water, or his horses, before they spread across the earth; at that moment he stops, and, following this, people in the world stop their works in the middle and he sets: such is the Sun's independence and greatness, which exists in the Sun alone. It does not exist in any other deity. Night, spreading the darkness over all places, removes the daylight — thus they explain."

सधस्थात् — Sadhasthāt — "saha tiṣṭhanty asmin iti sadhasthaḥ ratha: [that in which they stand together, a chariot]. In connection with this the word sadhasthāt is explained as 'from the chariot in which the horses are'."

original p. 167

सिमस्मै — Simasmai — "simaśabdaḥ sarvaparyāyaḥ saptamyarthe caturthī": "the word sima is a synonym of sarva. Because the fourth case is used in the sense of the seventh, the meaning is 'in all'."

वासः — Vāsaḥ — "ācchādayitṛtamaḥ | vāso vāsaram ahaḥ (Sā. bhā.)": "Sāyaṇa explains two meanings: the darkness that covers all, and day as a synonym of vāsara. Skandasvāmin:

आत् तद्वैव च रात्री वासः वासश्चभ्रोत्रे क्रियाशब्दः । वस आच्छादन इत्यस्य । वस्त्र वचनो वा । सामर्थ्यात् कृष्णं वासः आह नान्यत् । तत्सारूप्यात् तमसि प्रयुज्यते । कृत्स्नस्य जगतः आच्छादयित्वात् कृष्णवासःस्वरूपं वा तमः ॥ [small type, doubtful [?]]

āt tadvaiva ca rātrī vāsaḥ vāsaścabhrotre kriyāśabdaḥ | vasa ācchādana ityasya | vastra vacano vā | sāmarthyāt kṛṣṇaṃ vāsaḥ āha nānyat | tatsārūpyāt tamasi prayujyate | kṛtsnasya jagataḥ ācchādayitvāt kṛṣṇavāsaḥsvarūpaṃ vā tamaḥ ‖ [small type, doubtful [?]]

— āt (= immediately); the word vāsas is derived from the root vas 'to cover' (ācchādana), hence 'cloth'. Of all cloth, only black cloth is meant here; cloth of other colours does not cover like black cloth. By the act or quality of covering, tamas is called 'black garment' (kṛṣṇavāsaḥ), because [it makes] the whole world unseen: 'the darkness like a black cloth'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly)

mahitvam (mah "to honour"; the Uṇādi suffix in (iṇ), giving mahi; tasya bhāvas tvatalau, Pā. 5-1-119 as read [?], tva in the abstract sense; likewise in devatvam; final accent from the suffix); madhyā (madhya + the locative singular, with supāṃ sulug, Pā. 7-1-39 as read [?], ḍā substituted; being ḍit, the ṭi is elided: madhyā); kartoḥ (ḍukṛñ "to do"; Uṇādi tun; being ṅit-like, guṇa of the root by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; raparatva by uraṇ raparaḥ; jñityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197 as read [?], first-syllable accent; genitive/ablative singular).

original p. 168

Grammar page of Ṛk 4, concluded (noted briefly): vitatam (tanu "to extend", with vi; niṣṭhā, kta in the passive by niṣṭhā, Pā. 3-2-102 as read [?]; since udito vā, Pā. 7-2-56 as read [?], gives an optional iṭ before ktvā, the iṭ augment here is prohibited by yasya vibhāṣā, Pā. 7-2-15 as read [?]; the final nasal of the root elided by anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām…, Pā. 6-4-37 as read [?]; the prefix keeps its accent by gatir anantaraḥ, Pā. 6-2-49 as read [?]); jabhāra (hṛñ "to take", liṭ 3rd singular; ṇal for tip by parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…; doubling of the root; ur at, the reduplication's ṛ → a; halādiśeṣa; kuhoś cuḥ, Pā. 7-4-62 as read [?]; vṛddhi of the penultimate by ata upadhāyāḥ, Pā. 7-2-116 as read [?]; hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi, Pā. 8-2-32 as read [?], bha for the h; nighāta); ayukta (yujir "to join", luṅ 3rd singular ta; cleḥ sic, sic as the substitute; jhalo jhali, Pā. 8-2-26 as read [?], its elision; coḥ kuḥ, Pā. 8-2-30 as read [?], k for the j of the root; khari ca, Pā. 8-4-55 as read [?], ta [for da]; the augment aṭ; since yadā precedes, no nighāta by nipātair yad yadi…, Pā. 8-1-30 as read [?]; the augment being udātta the word has first-syllable accent); sadhasthāt (ṣṭhā "to cease from motion"; by the statement "ghañarthe kavidhānam" the suffix ka in the locative sense; ā to lopa iṭi ca [as printed], elision of the ā; sadha for saha by sadhamādasthayoś chandasi, Pā. 6-3-96 as read [?]; since it belongs to the dāsībhārādi group the kṛt-second-member accent is overruled and the first member keeps its accent); rātrī (rātreś cājasau, Pā. 4-1-31 as read [?], ṅīp in the Veda); tanute (tanu "to extend", laṭ 3rd singular; nighāta). ‖ 4 ‖

तन्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याभिचक्षे सूर्यो रूपं कृणुते द्योरुपस्थे । अनन्तमन्यद्रुशदस्य पाजः कृष्णमन्यद्धरितः सं भरन्ति ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 115.5)

तत्तदानीमुदयसमये मित्रस्य वरुणस्यैतदुभयोपलक्षितस्य सर्वस्य जगतोऽभिचक्षे अभिमुख्येन प्रकाशनाय द्योर्नभस उपस्थ उपस्थाने मध्ये सूर्यः सर्वस्य प्रेरकः सविता रूपं सर्वस्य निरूपकं प्रकाशकं तेजः कृणुते । करोति । अपि चास्य सूर्यस्य हरितो रसहरणशीला रश्मयो हरिद्वर्णा अश्वा वान्यतमवसानरहितं कृत्स्नस्य जगतो व्यापकं रुशद्दीप्यमानं श्वेतवर्णं पाजः । बलनामैतत् । बलयुक्तमतिबलस्याभि नैशस्य [?] कमसो निवारणे समर्थमन्यत्तमसो विलक्षणं तेजः सं भरन्ति । अहनि स्वकीययोगमनेन निष्पादयन्ति । तथा कृष्णं कृष्णवर्णमन्यत्तमः स्वकीयोपगमनेन रात्रौ । अस्य रश्मयोऽस्यैवं कुर्वन्ति किमु वक्तव्यं तस्य माहात्म्यमिति सूर्यस्य स्तुतिः ॥ [grammatical tail: abhicakṣe — cakṣiṅ "to speak", kvip with sampadādi; kṛṇute — kṛvi, u; dyoḥ — div, dyubhyaḥ…; upasthe — sthā with ka by ghañarthe kavidhānam; pājaḥ — pā "to protect", asun with juṭ-augment, as in the Uṇādi sūtra (Uṇ. 4-?? as read [?]), the jhuṭ augment of asun; anantam — nañ-compound, the accent of the later member's first syllable; haritaḥ — nominative plural, accent…] [partly in small type; marked [?] where doubtful]

tattadānīmudayasamaye mitrasya varuṇasyaitadubhayopalakṣitasya sarvasya jagato 'bhicakṣe abhimukhyena prakāśanāya dyornabhasa upastha upasthāne madhye sūryaḥ sarvasya prerakaḥ savitā rūpaṃ sarvasya nirūpakaṃ prakāśakaṃ tejaḥ kṛṇute | karoti | api cāsya sūryasya harito rasaharaṇaśīlā raśmayo haridvarṇā aśvā vānyatamavasānarahitaṃ kṛtsnasya jagato vyāpakaṃ ruśaddīpyamānaṃ śvetavarṇaṃ pājaḥ | balanāmaitat | balayuktamatibalasyābhi naiśasya [?] kamaso nivāraṇe samarthamanyattamaso vilakṣaṇaṃ tejaḥ saṃ bharanti | ahani svakīyayogamanena niṣpādayanti | tathā kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇamanyattamaḥ svakīyopagamanena rātrau | asya raśmayo 'syaivaṃ kurvanti kimu vaktavyaṃ tasya māhātmyamiti sūryasya stutiḥ ‖ [grammatical tail: abhicakṣe — cakṣiṅ "to speak", kvip with sampadādi; kṛṇute — kṛvi, u; dyoḥ — div, dyubhyaḥ…; upasthe — sthā with ka by ghañarthe kavidhānam; pājaḥ — pā "to protect", asun with juṭ-augment, as in the Uṇādi sūtra (Uṇ. 4-?? as read [?]), the jhuṭ augment of asun; anantam — nañ-compound, the accent of the later member 's first syllable; haritaḥ — nominative plural, accent…] [partly in small type; marked [?] where doubtful]

Sense (mine): "At that time, at the rising, for abhicakṣe, the manifest showing, of all the world (characterised by Mitra and Varuṇa), the Sun, the impeller of all, Savitṛ, rūpam kṛṇute, makes a form — a light that shows all — dyor upasthe, in the lap, the middle, of the sky. And this Sun's haritaḥ — sap-drawing rays or green-tawny horses — saṃ bharanti, bring about, in the daytime, by their own coming, one thing: anantam, endless, pervading the whole world, ruśat, shining white pājaḥ — strength (pāja is a name of strength): a mighty light, able to remove the darkness, different from darkness; and, in the night, by their going away, kṛṣṇam anyat, another thing, black: the darkness. If his rays do thus, what is to be said of his greatness? — this is the praise of the Sun."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) on p. 170 Grammar tail of the bhāṣya concluded: pājaḥ — the asun with the augment juṭ, as the Uṇādi sūtra [Uṇ. 4-?? as read, [?]] says "pā rakṣaṇe… pājaso balam"; upasthe — ghañarthe kavidhānam, ka suffix; marud-vṛdhādi, first-member accent dyoḥ as jasi-saso… Pā. 6-1-110 [?], pūrvarūpa.

original p. 170

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"tat — then (at sunrise); mitrasya varuṇasya — Mitra and Varuṇa, [the universe] beginning with these; abhicakṣe — to make [it] shine; dyoḥ upasthe — in the middle of the sky; sūryaḥ — the Sun, the impeller of all; rūpam — the shining light; kṛṇute — makes (and also); asya — of this Sun's; haritaḥ — sap-drawing rays (or the Sun's horses); anantam — [this world] endless; ruśat — shining; pājaḥ — strong; anyat — the light different from darkness; saṃ bharanti — fill (by day); kṛṣṇam — black-coloured; anyat — darkness; saṃ bharanti — [they] make rays in the night when they go away."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"At the time of rising, the Sun makes in the middle of the sky a light that illumines this world together with Mitra and Varuṇa. His rays make by day the light able to drive away darkness, and by their going away make the darkness at night."

English Translation (as printed)

The sun is the sight of Mitra and Varuna, displays his form (of brightness) in the middle of the heavens, and his rays extend, on one hand, his infinite and brilliant power, or, on the other (by their departure), bring on the blackness of night.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

सूर्यः — Sūryaḥ — "sarvasya prerakaḥ savitā": "by his rising he makes the whole world capable of knowledge and action and urges it to its works: he is the deity denoted by the word savitṛ. Or: sarati iti sūryaḥ — he who moves in the atmosphere, so he is called sūrya."

original p. 171

रूपं कृणुते — Rūpaṃ kṛṇute — "sarvasya nirūpakaṃ prakāśakaṃ tejaḥ karoti": "at the very time of rising he displays his own light, which shows everything, accompanied by the deities Mitra and Varuṇa, in the middle of the atmosphere, for the sake of lighting the world."

मित्रः — Mitraḥ — "primīteḥ trāyate": "he who protects from death, or he who runs (dravati), 'who rushes to the water, pouring from the atmosphere, ... (sammanvānaḥ)'; Yāska:

मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा । अमित्रः [?] मेदयतेर्वा स्निह्यतेर्वा । स्नेहयति सर्वं हि वृष्ट्यादिना ।

mitraḥ pramītestrāyate saṃminvāno dravatīti vā | amitraḥ [?] medayatervā snihyatervā | snehayati sarvaṃ hi vṛṣṭyādinā |

— mitra from primīteḥ trāyate: 'who protects from death'; or from saṃmimāno dravati — mi 'to cast' [the water]; or from medayati or snihyati — he makes all moist with rain and so on. In this way the Nirukta-writer explains the derivation of the word mitra, citing

मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्याम् । मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभिचष्टे मित्राय हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-५९-१ [as read])

mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyām | mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābhicaṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ ghṛtavajjuhota ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 3-59-1 [as read])

— Mitra supports the whole universe; he makes men follow works such as ploughing; and he praises Mitra's greatness: he helps men by making rain and so on (Ni. 10-22 as read [?])."

वरुणः — Varuṇaḥ — "meghajālena vyāyeṣ vṛṇoti": "varuṇa is explained as 'one who covers the atmosphere with a mass of clouds'; citing

नीचीनबारं वरुणः कबन्धं प्र ससर्ज रोदसी अन्तरिक्षम् । तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूमिम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ५-८५-३ [as read])

nīcīnabāraṃ varuṇaḥ kabandhaṃ pra sasarja rodasī antarikṣam | tena viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā yavaṃ na vṛṣṭirvyunatti bhūmim ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 5-85-3 [as read])

— 'having made the cloud with its mouth turned downward, Varuṇa moistens, by great rain, heaven, earth and atmosphere, as rain wets the earth like barley': thus he explains the greatness of Varuṇa, who causes rain for the greatness of the earth and atmosphere (Ni. 10-4 as read [?])."

पाजः — Pājaḥ — "balayuktam": "since the word pāja is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of strength, 'ojaḥ', 'śavaḥ' (Ni. 2-9 as read [?]), pājaḥ means 'strength'."

रुशत् — Ruśat — "ruśad iti varṇanāma | rocater jvalatikarmaṇaḥ": "the word ruśat, derived from the root ruc with the meaning 'lustre', means 'shining', or 'of white colour'."

original p. 172

हरितः — Haritaḥ — "the word harita is stated among the twenty-one [as read] names of rivers (nadīnāma) (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]) and in the ādityaraśmi-names, 'harita ādityasya' (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]); Sāyaṇa explains this word as 'the sap-drawing rays, or the green-tawny horses' — the rays or the Sun's horses, whose nature is to dry up water."

अनन्तं पाजः सं भरन्ति — Anantaṃ pājaḥ saṃ bharanti — "since ruśat is an adjective of pājaḥ (the word meaning strength), the Sun's rays, spread over the whole world, produce by their auspicious lustre a most abundant light, and drive away the darkness of night and spread light everywhere."

कृष्णमन्यत् — Kṛṣṇam anyat — "kṛṣṇavarṇam anyat tamaḥ svakīyopagamanena rātrau": "in the daytime, the Sun's rays shine, giving their brightness so that the darkness of night is entirely destroyed. The Sun, shining by his rays in the daytime with a form of splendour, at the time of night, because he has set, withdraws his rays so that another form — black — different from the shining form of day, may come about. His rays are in this way the cause of the ordering of day and night; therefore the greatness of the Sun who has such rays is exceedingly wonderful. The Nirukta-writer, on the topic that the Sun's rays draw up the sap, cites —

कृष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत्पतन्ति । (यजु. सं. [Vāj.?] ३-४१-४२ [?])

kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divamutpatanti | (yaju. saṃ. [Vāj.?] 3-41-42 [?])

— 'the green-tawny ones, the beautiful-winged, clothing themselves with the waters, fly up to heaven' — explaining: this Lord the Āditya, when for the favour of the world he takes the water into himself, as an embryo, enters the northern course (uttarāyaṇa); then his rays, honoured, harayaḥ, sap-drawing ones, draw up the water (Ni. 2-?? as read [?])."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly)

abhicakṣe (cakṣiṅ "to speak", with abhi; kvip in the abstract sense by sampadādibhyaḥ kvip, Vārt. 3-3-108 as read [?], giving abhicakṣ; the compound with the prefix keeps the later member's accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, Pā. 6-2-139 as read [?]; dative singular);

original p. 173

kṛṇute (kṛvi "to injure, to do"; idito num dhātoḥ, Pā. 7-1-58 as read [?], the num augment; dhinvikṛṇvor a ca, Pā. 3-1-80 as read [?], u as the vikaraṇa, with a substituted for the final; ato lopaḥ, Pā. 6-4-48 as read [?]; by sthānivadbhāva there is no guṇa of the penultimate; nighāta); upasthe (ṣṭhā "to cease from motion"; by ghañarthe kavidhānam the suffix ka in the locative sense; ā to lopa iṭi ca, Pā. 6-4-64 as read [?], the elision of ā; gatir anantaraḥ, Pā. 6-2-49 as read [?], the prefix keeps its accent; since it belongs to the marudvṛdhādi group the first member takes the final accent); dyoḥ (the word dyo; genitive singular ṅas; jasi ca … pūrvarūpa, Pā. 6-1-110 as read [?]; s → ru → visarga); ruśat (ruśa "to shine"; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śap by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ, Pā. 3-1-77 as read [?], śa; as adupadeśa the sārvadhātuka is unaccented; the root accent remains); pājaḥ (pāti rakṣati iti pājaḥ = strength; pā "to protect"; asun by pāter bale juṭ ca, Uṇ. 4-?? as read [?]; the augment juṭ; pājas; pājaḥ asyāsti, in the sense of the possessor, vin by asmāyāmedhā…, Pā. 5-2-121 as read [?], which in the Veda is elided; first-syllable accent by jñityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197 as read [?]); bharanti (bhṛñ "to bear", bhvādi laṭ 3rd plural; nighāta). ‖ 5 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 115.6)

अद्या देवा उदिता सूर्यस्य निरंहसः पिपृता निरवद्यात् । तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ ६ ॥

adyā devā uditā sūryasya niraṃhasaḥ pipṛtā niravadyāt | tanno mitro varuṇo māmahantāmaditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 115.6)

अद्य । देवाः । उत्ऽइता । सूर्यस्य । निः । अंहसः । पिपृत । निः । अवद्यात् । तत् । नः । मित्रः । वरुणः । ममहन्ताम् । अदितिः । सिन्धुः । पृथिवी । उत । द्यौः ॥ ६ ॥

adya | devāḥ | ut 'itā | sūryasya | niḥ | aṃhasaḥ | pipṛta | niḥ | avadyāt | tat | naḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | mamahantām | aditiḥ | sindhuḥ | pṛthivī | uta | dyauḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 115.6)

हे देवा द्योतमानाः सूर्यरश्मयः । अद्यास्मिन्काले सूर्यस्यादित्यस्योदिता उदयेन सत्येतत्स्तुतेः प्रसरन्तो यूयमस्मानंहसः पापान्निष्पिपृत । निष्पारयत । पालयतेत्यर्थः । यदिदमस्माभिरुक्तं नोऽस्मदीयं तन्मित्रादयः षड्देवता मामहन्ताम् । पूजयन्तु । अनुमन्यन्तां रक्षन्त्विति यावत् । मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायकोऽहरभिमानी देवः । वरुणोऽनिष्टानां निवारयिता रात्र्यभिमानी । अदितिरखण्डनीयोदीना वा देवमाता । सिन्धुः स्यन्दनशीलोदकाभिमानिनी देवता । पृथिवी भूलोकस्याधिष्ठात्री । द्यौर्द्युलोकस्य । उतशब्दः समुच्चये ॥ [grammatical tail: adya — nipātasya ca, lengthening in the Saṃhitā; uditā — ut + iṇ, ktin in the abstract, supāṃ sulug, ḍādeśa, ṭi-elision; accent; pipṛta — pṝ "to protect, to fill", loṭ 2nd plural, juhotyādi, śluḥ, doubling, arti-pipartyoś ca, i for the reduplication; tabādeśa by taptanaptanathanāś ca; sārvadhātukam apit, ṅit, guṇa prevented…] [read from the print; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

he devā dyotamānāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ | adyāsminkāle sūryasyādityasyoditā udayena satyetatstuteḥ prasaranto yūyamasmānaṃhasaḥ pāpānniṣpipṛta | niṣpārayata | pālayatetyarthaḥ | yadidamasmābhiruktaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ tanmitrādayaḥ ṣaḍdevatā māmahantām | pūjayantu | anumanyantāṃ rakṣantviti yāvat | mitraḥ pramītestrāyako 'harabhimānī devaḥ | varuṇo 'niṣṭānāṃ nivārayitā rātryabhimānī | aditirakhaṇḍanīyodīnā vā devamātā | sindhuḥ syandanaśīlodakābhimāninī devatā | pṛthivī bhūlokasyādhiṣṭhātrī | dyaurdyulokasya | utaśabdaḥ samuccaye ‖ [grammatical tail: adya — nipātasya ca, lengthening in the Saṃhitā; uditā — ut + iṇ, ktin in the abstract, supāṃ sulug, ḍādeśa, ṭi-elision; accent; pipṛta — pṝ "to protect, to fill", loṭ 2nd plural, juhotyādi, śluḥ, doubling, arti-pipartyoś ca, i for the reduplication; tabādeśa by taptanaptanathanāś ca; sārvadhātukam apit, ṅit, guṇa prevented…] [read from the print; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "O shining devāḥ, rays of Sūrya: to-day, at this time, with the Sun's uditā, rising, spreading forth by the praise made of this, deliver (niṣ pipṛta) us from aṃhas, sin; protect. What we have said, may the six deities, Mitra and the rest, mamahantām, honour: may they approve, protect. Mitra — the deity of the day who protects from death; Varuṇa — who wards off evils, the deity of night; Aditi — the indivisible (or undiminished) mother of the gods; Sindhu — the deity of the flowing waters; Pṛthivī — the presiding deity of the earth; Dyau — of heaven; uta in the sense of 'and'."

original p. 175

(Grammatical tail, concluded: pipṛta — loṭ with loṭo laṅvat, ta → ta by tasthasthamipāṃ…; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ; the doubling in śluḥ; ur at, halādiśeṣa; arti-pipartyoś ca; sārvadhātukam apit, the tabādeśa by taptanaptanathanāś ca; dīrghaḥ in the Saṃhitā by tuṣughṛtyādinā.)

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he devāḥ — O shining rays; adya — now; sūryasya uditā — at the rising of the Sun; aṃhasaḥ — from sin; niḥ pipṛta — protect, separating; naḥ — our; tat — this stotra; mitraḥ — Mitra; varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa; aditiḥ — Aditi; sindhuḥ — the deity of the ocean; pṛthivī — the earth; uta — and; dyauḥ — the deity of heaven and the rest; mamahantām — honour and protect."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O shining rays of the Sun, as soon as the Sun has risen, protect us, delivering us from sins. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Pṛthivī, Sindhu and the deities of the atmosphere make this praise of ours worthy."

English Translation (as printed)

This day, gods, with the rising of the sun, deliver us from heinous sins ; and may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi,—ocean, earth, and heaven, be favourable to this our prayer.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

देवाः — Devāḥ — "dyotamānāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ": "the word deva, derived from the root div, means 'lustrous', or 'shining'. The rays of the Sun, shining, spread over everything exceedingly after the Sun's rising. The hope is expressed here that the rays of the Sun, spreading their light in this way, may destroy all our sins —

mitra — primīteḥ trāyaḥ: Mitra, the presiding deity of the day, who protects from death; Varuṇa, the presiding deity of the night, who wards off evils; Aditi, the mother of the gods; Sindhu, the presiding deity of the ocean;

original p. 176

the earth, and the atmosphere too — praising the Sun in this way, may they protect us, destroying our sins: this wish is expressed here."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly)

Sūkta 116 — "nāsatyābhyām"

original p. 177

Heading (Kannada): "nūrahadināraneya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-sixteenth Sūkta."

Anukramaṇī and Sāyaṇa's introduction (Sanskrit, as printed):

सप्तदशेऽनुवाके पञ्च सूक्तानि । तत्र नासत्याभ्यामिति पञ्चविंशत्यृचं प्रथमं सूक्तम् । उशिक्संज्ञायामङ्गिरजस्य महिष्या दास्यां दीर्घतमसोत्पादितः कक्षीवानस्य सूक्तस्य ऋषिः । त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । अश्विनौ देवता । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । नासत्याभ्यां पञ्चाधिका कक्षीवान्दैर्घतमस उशिक्सूत आश्विनं वा इति । तुह्यादिपरिभाषयेदमादीनि पञ्च सूक्तान्याश्विदेवत्यानि ॥ प्रातरेनुवाकस्याश्विने क्रतौ त्रैष्टुभे छन्दसीदमादीनि त्रीणि सूक्तानि । अथाश्विन इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । ग्रावाणेव नासत्याभ्यामिति त्रीणि । आ. ४-१४ [?] । इति ॥ आश्विनशस्त्रे चैतानि शस्यानि प्रातरनुवाकन्यायेन । आ. ६-५ । इत्येतदिष्टत्वात् ॥

saptadaśe 'nuvāke pañca sūktāni | tatra nāsatyābhyāmiti pañcaviṃśatyṛcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktam | uśiksaṃjñāyāmaṅgirajasya mahiṣyā dāsyāṃ dīrghatamasotpāditaḥ kakṣīvānasya sūktasya ṛṣiḥ | triṣṭup chandaḥ | aśvinau devatā | tathā cānukrāntam | nāsatyābhyāṃ pañcādhikā kakṣīvāndairghatamasa uśiksūta āśvinaṃ vā iti | tuhyādiparibhāṣayedamādīni pañca sūktānyāśvidevatyāni ‖ prātarenuvākasyāśvine kratau traiṣṭubhe chandasīdamādīni trīṇi sūktāni | athāśvina iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | grāvāṇeva nāsatyābhyāmiti trīṇi | ā. 4-14 [?] | iti ‖ āśvinaśastre caitāni śasyāni prātaranuvākanyāyena | ā. 6-5 | ityetadiṣṭatvāt ‖

Sense: "In the seventeenth anuvāka there are five sūktas. The first of these, nāsatyābhyām, has twenty-five Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kakṣīvān, whom Dīrghatamas begot on Uśij, a maidservant of the queen of Aṅgiraja (the king of the Aṅgas) [as the Sanskrit reads: uśik-saṃjñāyām aṅgirajasya mahiṣyā dāsyāṃ dīrghatamasotpāditaḥ kakṣīvān]. The metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity the two Aśvins. So the Anukramaṇī says: 'nāsatyābhyāṃ pañcādhikā kakṣīvān dairghatamasa uśiksūta āśvinaṃ vā' (twenty-five Ṛks, by Kakṣīvān, son of Dīrghatamas and of Uśij; or addressed to the Aśvins). By the rule beginning 'tuhyādi' the five sūktas beginning with this are addressed to the Aśvins. In the Aśvina rite of the Prātaranuvāka, in the Triṣṭubh metre, the three sūktas beginning with idam: in the section 'athāśvina' the Sūtra says 'grāveva nāsatyābhyām iti trīṇi' (Āś. 4-14 as read [?]). And these are to be recited in the Aśvina-śastra, on the model of the Prātaranuvāka (Āś. 6-5 as read [?]), as it is prescribed."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "With the sūkta nāsatyābhyām the seventeenth anuvāka begins. In this anuvāka (Sūktas 116–120) there are five sūktas. Of these the sūkta nāsatyābhyām is the first. It has twenty-five Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kakṣīvān, born of Dīrghatamas on Uśij, the maidservant of the queen of King Aṅgiraja [as the Kannada reads]. The deities are the two Aśvins; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā, 'nāsatyābhyāṃ pañcādhikā kakṣīvān dairghatamasa uśiksūta āśvinaṃ vā'. By the occurrence of the word tu hi etc. in the sūtra, the five sūktas hereafter are to be known as having the Aśvins as deity. At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, these three sūktas are applied for the Triṣṭubh mantras relating to the Aśvins, as the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains in the section 'athāśvina' by the sūtra 'grāveva nāsatyābhyām iti trīṇi' (Āś. 4-?? as read [?]); and it is directed in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra itself that, when reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras for the Aśvina-śastra, these sūktas are to be recited (Āś. 6-5 as read [?])."

original p. 178

नासत्याभ्यां बर्हिरिव प्र वृञ्जे स्तोमा इयर्म्यभ्रियेव वातः । यावर्भगाय विमदाय जायां सेनाजुवा न्यूहतू रथेन ॥ १ ॥

nāsatyābhyāṃ barhiriva pra vṛñje stomā iyarmyabhriyeva vātaḥ | yāvarbhagāya vimadāya jāyāṃ senājuvā nyūhatū rathena ‖ 1 ‖

नासत्याभ्याम् । बर्हिःऽइव । प्र । वृञ्जे । स्तोमान् । इयर्मि । अभ्रियाऽइव । वातः । यौ । अर्भगाय । विऽमदाय । जायाम् । सेनाऽजुवा । निऽऊहतुः । रथेन ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.1)

बर्हिरिव यथा कश्चिद्यजमानो योगार्थं बर्हिः प्र वृञ्जे प्रकर्षेणा-न्यूनानतिरिक्तं योगाय पर्याप्तं दर्भं वृङ्क्ते छिनत्ति । संपादयेति यावत् । एवमहं नासत्याभ्यामश्विभ्यां स्तोमान् स्तुतीरीयर्मि । संपादयामि । एतदेव दिदीर्क्रियते । अभ्रियेव यथाभ्रियाण्यभ्रेषु मेघेष्ववस्थितानुदकानि वातो वायुर्वर्षणार्थं बहुशः प्रेरयति एवमहमश्विभ्यां स्तोत्रार्णीयर्मि । बहुशः प्रेरयामि । कीदृशावश्विनौ । अर्भगाय बालाय स्वयंवरलब्धभार्याय विमदायैतत्संज्ञाय राजर्षये मध्येमार्गं स्वयंवरार्थमागच्छन्तामलभ्मानन्यैर्नृपैः सह योद्धुमुद्यतकन्यानेवेऽपि तस्मै सेनाजुवा शत्रुसेनायाः प्रेरकेण शत्रुभिर्दुष्प्रधर्षेण रथेन यावश्विनौ जायां भार्यां पर्यनुक्रान्तां न्यूहतुः । शत्रून्निहत्य तदीयं गृहं प्रापयामासतुः । ताभ्यामित्यर्थः ॥ [grammatical tail follows in the print: nāsatyābhyām — sat "good", satsu bhavau satyau, na satyau asatyau, na asatyau nāsatyau; nañ with the nañ … sat… avyaya pūrvapada prakṛtisvaratva; vṛñje — vṛji "to leave", adādi, idit the num; iyarmi — ṛ "to go", juhotyādi, śluḥ, doubling, arti-pipartyoś ca; abhriyā iva; arbhagāya — arbha + ga, arbhaka…; sainājuvā — ju "to be quick", saunra root, kvip, dīrgha…; nyūhatuḥ — vah "to carry", liṭ, vacisvapi…, saṃprasāraṇa…] [this passage is in small type; read letter by letter; words marked [?] are doubtful]

barhiriva yathā kaścidyajamāno yogārthaṃ barhiḥ pra vṛñje prakarṣeṇā-nyūnānatiriktaṃ yogāya paryāptaṃ darbhaṃ vṛṅkte chinatti | saṃpādayeti yāvat | evamahaṃ nāsatyābhyāmaśvibhyāṃ stomān stutīrīyarmi | saṃpādayāmi | etadeva didīrkriyate | abhriyeva yathābhriyāṇyabhreṣu megheṣvavasthitānudakāni vāto vāyurvarṣaṇārthaṃ bahuśaḥ prerayati evamahamaśvibhyāṃ stotrārṇīyarmi | bahuśaḥ prerayāmi | kīdṛśāvaśvinau | arbhagāya bālāya svayaṃvaralabdhabhāryāya vimadāyaitatsaṃjñāya rājarṣaye madhyemārgaṃ svayaṃvarārthamāgacchantāmalabhmānanyairnṛpaiḥ saha yoddhumudyatakanyāneve 'pi tasmai senājuvā śatrusenāyāḥ prerakeṇa śatrubhirduṣpradharṣeṇa rathena yāvaśvinau jāyāṃ bhāryāṃ paryanukrāntāṃ nyūhatuḥ | śatrūnnihatya tadīyaṃ gṛhaṃ prāpayāmāsatuḥ | tābhyāmityarthaḥ ‖ [grammatical tail follows in the print: nāsatyābhyām — sat "good", satsu bhavau satyau, na satyau asatyau, na asatyau nāsatyau; nañ with the nañ … sat… avyaya pūrvapada prakṛtisvaratva; vṛñje — vṛji "to leave", adādi, idit the num; iyarmi — ṛ "to go", juhotyādi, śluḥ, doubling, arti-pipartyoś ca; abhriyā iva; arbhagāya — arbha + ga, arbhaka…; sainājuvā — ju "to be quick", saunra root, kvip, dīrgha…; nyūhatuḥ — vah "to carry", liṭ, vacisvapi…, saṃprasāraṇa…] [this passage is in small type; read letter by letter; words marked [?] are doubtful]

Sense (mine): "As a certain sacrificer pra vṛñje, cuts, barhiḥ, sacred grass, for the sacrifice — cuts just enough, neither less nor more — thus I, for the two Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, iyarmi, produce, stomān, praises. This is the very thing that is meant. Abhriyeva vātaḥ — as the wind drives many times, for rain, the waters that stand in the clouds, so I drive the stotras many times to the Aśvins. What are the Aśvins like? For arbhagāya, the young, vimadāya, the royal sage of that name, who, going to a svayaṃvara [self-choice], on the way, was ready to fight other kings, they nyūhatuḥ, carried off — with senājuvā, the chariot that drives against the hostile army, impossible to resist by enemies — his jāyām, bride, parya-anukrāntām, whom they had won; having slain the enemies, they brought her to his house: that is, 'for those two'."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun on p. 179, completed on p. 180

"arbhagāya — to the youthful; vimadāya — to (the king) Vimada by name; senājuvā — which drives the enemy's army; rathena — by the chariot; yau — which Aśvin deities; jāyām — the wife; nyūhatuḥ — brought to his house, after killing (the enemies) — (such); nāsatyābhyām — to the Nāsatyas (the Aśvin deities); barhiḥ —

original p. 180

— (a sacrificer, for the sacrifice) the sacred grass, [cutting] — pra vṛñje iva — as one cuts and prepares (and); vātaḥ — the wind; abhriyā iva — as (it brings together) the waters in the clouds (to cause rain); stomān — these stotra-sentences; iyarmi — I compose."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"For the Nāsatyas — the Aśvin deities — who put the bride of the youthful Vimada in their chariot, having destroyed the enemies, and presented her [to him], I compose these stotra-sentences, as a sacrificer cuts and prepares the sacred grass for the sacrifice, and as the wind gathers the clouds together [for rain]."

English Translation (as printed)

In like manner as a worshipper strews the sacred grass for the Nasatyas, so do I urge on their laudations, as the wind drives on the clouds : they, who gave a bride to the youthful Vimada, and bore her away in their car, outstripping the rival host.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

"Kakṣīvān, the ṛṣi of this sūkta, is the son born to the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas of Uśij. This woman Uśij, they say in the Purāṇas and elsewhere, was the maidservant of the queen of the king of Kaliṅga [as the Kannada reads]; the king of Kaliṅga, desiring sons, sent his wife to the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas for the sake of [begetting] a son; the queen, not wishing this, secretly sent in her own place her maidservant Uśij to the ṛṣi; and by the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas this son Kakṣīvān was born of her. The ṛṣi Kakṣīvān, though born of a Kṣatriya [sic: of a maidservant] woman, became famous as a Brāhmaṇa because of his connection with brāhmaṇas. This ṛṣi is greatly famed among those who perform sacrifices, as —

एवं वै पर आटनारः कक्षीवाँ औशिजो वीतहव्यः श्रायसस्त्रसदस्युः पौरुकुत्सः । सजानामा [?] अतिष्ठत ॥ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]] (तै. सं. ५-६-५-३ [as read])

evaṃ vai para āṭanāraḥ kakṣīvā~ auśijo vītahavyaḥ śrāyasastrasadasyuḥ paurukutsaḥ | sajānāmā [?] atiṣṭhata ‖ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]] (tai. saṃ. 5-6-5-3 [as read])

— is said in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda. Therefore this ṛṣi is very famous in the performance of sacrifices, in the composition of mantras. This ṛṣi is

विमदाय — Vimadāya — "Vimada is a royal sage, who is the ṛṣi of altogether twenty-?? Ṛks in the 10th maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda, Sūktas 20–2? [as read: "10-20-?" to "10-2?-?"] [?]. In these sūktas, Ṛ. नासत्याभ्याम् — Nāsatyābhyām — "Sāyaṇa explains: aśvibhyām, 'by the Aśvins', i.e. for the Aśvin deities.

अश्विनोरेको नासत्यनामा दस्रनामा अपरः साहचर्यात्तयोरन्यकरनाम्नापि उभयोरभिधानम् । न वा असत्यौ सत्यावेव नासत्यौ नासत्ययोरर्थायेये ॥ [as read; small type [?]]

aśvinoreko nāsatyanāmā dasranāmā aparaḥ sāhacaryāttayoranyakaranāmnāpi ubhayorabhidhānam | na vā asatyau satyāveva nāsatyau nāsatyayorarthāyeye ‖ [as read; small type [?]]

— of the two Aśvin deities, one has the name Nāsatya and the other Dasra. They always move about together, each beside the other, and dwell together. Therefore, as soon as the name of one is spoken, the number 'two', i.e. both Aśvin deities, becomes easily known. 'Asatya' means 'not true'; the nañ-negation in nāsatya signals the two negations — 'not untrue': i.e. 'true'. Skandasvāmin explains that praise is here directed for the sake of these Aśvin deities.

"In the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, 'satsu bhavau satyau | na satyau asatyau | na asatyau nāsatyau': they who are among the good (sat) are called satya; those other than these are asatya; those who are the opposite of these asatyas are nāsatya — so the meaning of the word nāsatya is explained. Yāska —

सत्यावेव नासत्यावित्यौर्णवाभः सत्यस्य प्रणेतारावित्याग्रायणः नासिकाप्रभवणौ बभूवतुरिति वा ॥ (नि. ६-१३ [as read])

satyāveva nāsatyāvityaurṇavābhaḥ satyasya praṇetārāvityāgrāyaṇaḥ nāsikāprabhavaṇau babhūvaturiti vā ‖ (ni. 6-13 [as read])

original p. 182

— Aurṇavābha [says]: they are always the ones who speak truth, who are not untrue; the Aśvin deities are called nāsatya. Āgrāyaṇa says: because they make sacrifices go on and make water available, they have the fame of Nāsatya. Some others say that, when the Sun, in the form of a horse, was united with the deity Saṃjñā [ātmā], the two were born from her nostril (nāsikā), so they are Nāsatya."

बर्हिः इव प्र वृञ्जे — Barhiḥ iva pra vṛñje — "yogārthaṃ barhiḥ paryāptaṃ darbhaṃ vṛṅkte chinatti": "just as a sacrificer cuts, for the sake of the sacrifice, enough darbha grass — neither less nor more — so I, for the Aśvin deities, compose the praises. The word barhis is read among the sixteen names of the atmosphere (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]) and among the hundred-and-one [as read] names of water (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]). The meaning is: as one cuts the darbha so that it is enough for the sacrifice, I use my words for the praise of the Aśvin deities. Yāska —

बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् परिच्छेदनात् ।

barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt paricchedanāt |

— explains that the darbha is cut and used in the sacrifice, so that it is famed by the name barhis, and cites

प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वस्तोरस्या वृज्यते अग्रे अह्नाम् । व्यु प्रथते वितरं वरीयो देवेभ्यो अदितये स्योनम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-११०-४ [as read])

prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vastorasyā vṛjyate agre ahnām | vyu prathate vitaraṃ varīyo devebhyo aditaye syonam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-110-4 [as read])

प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वसनायास्याः प्रवृज्यते अग्रे अह्नां बर्हिः पूर्वाह्णे तद्विप्रथते वितरं विकीर्णतरमिति वा विस्तीर्णतरमिति वा वरीयो वरतरमुरुतरं वा देवेभ्यः शादितये च स्योनम् । स्योनमिति सुखनाम स्यतेरवस्यन्तीत्येत् सेवितव्यं भवतीति वा ॥ (नि. ८-८ [as read])

prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vasanāyāsyāḥ pravṛjyate agre ahnāṃ barhiḥ pūrvāhṇe tadviprathate vitaraṃ vikīrṇataramiti vā vistīrṇataramiti vā varīyo varataramurutaraṃ vā devebhyaḥ śāditaye ca syonam | syonamiti sukhanāma syateravasyantītyet sevitavyaṃ bhavatīti vā ‖ (ni. 8-8 [as read])

— citing the Ṛk prācīnaṃ barhiḥ, he explains that at the time of the sacrifice the darbhas are cut, evenly, and spread in three layers [on the altar] near the sacrificial hall, to make a seat for the gods and for Aditi to sit upon. 'The four sides of the darbha spread in this way are famed as barhis,' he explains. 'Here, as the ṛṣi, the seer of the mantra, offers mantras (barhir iva pra vṛñje), the simile appears: as the sacrificer, for the sacrifice, cuts and uses darbhas, so that there is no deficiency or excess, so I say this stotra, which expresses the greatness of the Aśvin deities, exactly right — with no deficiency or excess.'"

original p. 183

अभ्रियेव वातः — Abhriyeva vātaḥ — "meghe(ṣu) avasthitāni udakāni vāyur iva": "as the wind drives the waters that are in the clouds so that they rain, I shall say the stotras many times for the Aśvin deities and drive them, as the sacrificers recite them in the sacrifice."

अर्भगाय — Arbhagāya — "vimadāya bālāya svayaṃvaralabdhabhāryāya vimadasaṃjñāya rājarṣaye": "the royal sage named Vimada, going to a svayaṃvara, was chosen in the svayaṃvara by a princess. As he was bringing her home after marrying her, in the middle of the road other kings, because this princess had been won by this Vimada, rose against him to fight. Then Vimada praised the Aśvin deities by the mantras —

अग्निमीळे भुजां यविष्ठम् ॥ [as read; the first words of Ṛ. 10-20-1 as printed] (ऋ. सं. १०-२०-१ [as read])

agnimīḷe bhujāṃ yaviṣṭham ‖ [as read; the first words of Ṛ. 10-20-1 as printed] (ṛ. saṃ. 10-20-1 [as read])

— By this, the story is understood: the Aśvin deities, pleased, fought the enemies in battle for him, who was unable to conquer them, and brought him with his wife. This story is hinted at in the Ṛk

याभिः पत्नीर्विमदाय न्यूहथुरा घ वा याभिररुणीरशिक्षतम् । याभिः सुदास ऊहथुः सुदेव्यं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१९ [as read])"

yābhiḥ patnīrvimadāya nyūhathurā gha vā yābhiraruṇīraśikṣatam | yābhiḥ sudāsa ūhathuḥ sudevyaṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-19 [as read])"

अर्भगः — Arbhagaḥ — "arbham alpaṃ gāyati śabdayatīty arbhagaḥ": "the word arbhaka is stated among the twelve [as read] names of 'small' (hrasva) (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), so it means 'small'; he who sounds a little (the small child) is called arbhaga, the name of a child."

सेनाजुवा — Senājuvā — "śatrusenāyāḥ prerakeṇa śatrubhir duṣprāseṇa": "by the chariot that drives the enemy's army, i.e. which is not to be approached by enemies — so Sāyaṇa; and Skandasvāmin: 'senājuvā senayā saha gantrā svasenāparivṛtena' — by the chariot which goes together with the army, i.e. which moves surrounded by their own army."

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.2)

वीळुपत्मभिराशुहेमभिर्वा देवानां वा जूतिभिः शाशदाना । तद्रासभो नासत्या सहस्रमाजा यमस्य प्रधने जिगाय ॥ २ ॥

vīḷupatmabhirāśuhemabhirvā devānāṃ vā jūtibhiḥ śāśadānā | tadrāsabho nāsatyā sahasramājā yamasya pradhane jigāya ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.2)

वीळुपत्मऽभिः । आशुहेमऽभिः । वा । देवानाम् । वा । जूतिऽभिः । शाशदाना । तत् । रासभः । नासत्या । सहस्रम् । आजा । यमस्य । प्रऽधने । जिगाय ॥ २ ॥

vīḷupatma 'bhiḥ | āśuhema 'bhiḥ | vā | devānām | vā | jūti 'bhiḥ | śāśadānā | tat | rāsabhaḥ | nāsatyā | sahasram | ājā | yamasya | pra 'dhane | jigāya ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 186

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.2)

वीळुपत्मभिः । वीळिति बलनाम । बलवदुत्पतनैः आशुहेमभिः शीघ्रगमनैः । वाकबः [?] समुच्चये । हे नासत्यावश्विनौ एवंभूतैरश्वैश्च देवानामिन्द्रादीनां जूतिभिः प्रेरणैश्च शाशदाना शाश्यमानयोरर्थाय प्रेर्यमाणयोर्युवयोर्वाहनभूतो यो रासभः प्रजापतिना दत्तः स यमस्य वैवस्वतस्य प्रीतिकरे प्रधने प्रकृष्टधनोपेते आजा आजौ सङ्ग्रामे तत्शत्रूणां सहस्रं जिगाय । जितवान् । वैवस्वतो हि बहूनां मरणहेतुना सङ्ग्रामेण तुष्टो भवति । यद्वा । जैतव्यत्वेन प्रजापतिना निहितमृक्षहस्रं शीघ्रगमनयुक्तो रासभो जिगाय । जयेनालभत । अन्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वमेवाजिं प्राप्य युवानां जयं प्रापयामास । तथा चास्मिन्नर्थे प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञे दुहितरं प्रायच्छत् । ऐ. ब्रा. १-८ [as read] । इत्यादिकं ब्राह्मणमनुसन्धेयम् ॥ [grammatical tail: vīḷupatmabhiḥ — vīḷu strength, patman from pat, vīḷuvat patmān…; āśuhemabhiḥ — āśu + hi "to go", hemanin…; jūtibhiḥ — jūti, ūtiyūtijūti… ktin, the udātta accent; śāśadānā — śasu "to command", śāna with tācchīlya… ṣatva…; ājā — ājau, ḍādeśa by supāṃ sulug; jigāya — ji "to conquer", liṭ, ṇal, sanliṭoḥ… kutva, gakāra.] [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

vīḷupatmabhiḥ | vīḷiti balanāma | balavadutpatanaiḥ āśuhemabhiḥ śīghragamanaiḥ | vākabaḥ [?] samuccaye | he nāsatyāvaśvinau evaṃbhūtairaśvaiśca devānāmindrādīnāṃ jūtibhiḥ preraṇaiśca śāśadānā śāśyamānayorarthāya preryamāṇayoryuvayorvāhanabhūto yo rāsabhaḥ prajāpatinā dattaḥ sa yamasya vaivasvatasya prītikare pradhane prakṛṣṭadhanopete ājā ājau saṅgrāme tatśatrūṇāṃ sahasraṃ jigāya | jitavān | vaivasvato hi bahūnāṃ maraṇahetunā saṅgrāmeṇa tuṣṭo bhavati | yadvā | jaitavyatvena prajāpatinā nihitamṛkṣahasraṃ śīghragamanayukto rāsabho jigāya | jayenālabhata | anyebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvamevājiṃ prāpya yuvānāṃ jayaṃ prāpayāmāsa | tathā cāsminnarthe prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchat | ai. brā. 1-8 [as read] | ityādikaṃ brāhmaṇamanusandheyam ‖ [grammatical tail: vīḷupatmabhiḥ — vīḷu strength, patman from pat, vīḷuvat patmān…; āśuhemabhiḥ — āśu + hi "to go", hemanin…; jūtibhiḥ — jūti, ūtiyūtijūti… ktin, the udātta accent; śāśadānā — śasu "to command", śāna with tācchīlya… ṣatva…; ājā — ājau, ḍādeśa by supāṃ sulug; jigāya — ji "to conquer", liṭ, ṇal, sanliṭoḥ… kutva, gakāra.] [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Vīḷupatmabhiḥ — vīḷu is a name for strength: by strong leaps; āśuhemabhiḥ — by swift goings; vā — and (in the sense 'together'). O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, with such horses, and with devānām, the impulses of the gods Indra and the rest, śāśadānā — for you two who are impelled for the purpose of the command(s), that rāsabha (ass) who was given by Prajāpati, which is your vehicle, yamasya, of Yama Vaivasvata, in his delightful pradhane, rich-booty battle, ājā — in the war — conquered (jigāya) a thousand of the enemies. For Vaivasvata is pleased with a war that causes the death of many. Or: the ass, which is swift, won the thousand [thousand-cattle?] placed by Prajāpati as to be won; he obtained them by victory; having reached the contest before the other gods, he made the victory attained by you two — as in the Brāhmaṇa: 'prajāpatir vai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchat' (Ai. Br. 1-8 as read [?])."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"vīḷupatmabhiḥ — of the strongest (strong-flying); vā — and; āśuhemabhiḥ — swift-going (horses); nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; devānām — by the gods Indra and the rest; jūtibhiḥ — by encouragement; śāśadānā — greatly impelled; rāsabhaḥ — the ass (your vehicle); yamasya — of Yama (the pleasing); pradhane — specially wealthy; ājā — in the battle; tat — those (enemies); sahasram — a thousand; jigāya — conquered."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, joined with the strongest and swiftest horses, and impelled by the encouragement of the gods, thy ass (thy vehicle) conquered many thousand enemies in the pleasing battle of Yama."

original p. 187

English Translation (as printed)

Nasatyas, borne by strong and rapid (steeds) and (urged) by the encouragements of the gods, the ass of you, thus instigated, overcame a thousand (enemies) in conflict, in the war grateful to Yama.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

वीळुपत्मभिः — Vīḷupatmabhiḥ — "vīḷu balavat patantīti vīḷupatmānaḥ": "vīḷu is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of strength (Ni. 2-9 as read [?]), so it means strength: those who fly (patanti) with strength, i.e. 'those that leap'. Sāyaṇa explains: vīḷu means strength, 'vīḷv iti balanāma balavad utpatanaiḥ'."

आशुहेमभिः — Āśuhemabhiḥ — "āśu śīghraṃ hinvanti gacchantīti āśuhemānaḥ": "those who go with speed."

शाशदाना — Śāśadānā — "śāśyamānayor arthāyaṃ preryamāṇayor yuvayor vāhanabhūto": "'thy vehicle (the ass), who is urged exceedingly, O Aśvin deities'. Śāsana means 'commanding'. For the word śāśadāna, formed from the root śasu, which has the sense of 'to slay' (yajarthādi, taken in the sense hiṃsā or intensive [atiśaya]), Sāyaṇa gives the meaning in accordance with the maxim 'dhātūnām anekārthatvam' — roots have many meanings. In the Nirukta (Ni. 6-1? as read [?]) there is an explanation of the word śāśadānaḥ as śāśādyamānaḥ ['much commanded']; and

अभि सिन्धो अजिगादस्य शत्रून् विशेन [?] वृषभेण पुरो भेत् । संवज्रेणासृजद्वृत्रमिन्द्रः प्र स्वां मतिमतिरच्छाशदानः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५३-१० [as read; the first words printed doubtfully [?]])

abhi sindho ajigādasya śatrūn viśena [?] vṛṣabheṇa puro bhet | saṃvajreṇāsṛjadvṛtramindraḥ pra svāṃ matimatiracchāśadānaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-53-10 [as read; the first words printed doubtfully [?]])

— this Ṛk is given as an example, and it is said that the word is used in the sense of 'cleaving' (bhedana)."

रासभः प्रधने आजौ तत् सहस्रं जिगाय — Rāsabhaḥ pradhane ājau tat sahasraṃ jigāya — "the ass, which Brahmā (Caturmukha) gave to the Aśvin deities as their vehicle, impelled by Indra and other deities and by swift-moving horses above, brings Yama pleasure by making abundant wealth available; in the battle, winning a thousand Ṛks bet by Brahmā (as a wager), he procured the victory for the Aśvin deities — thus Sāyaṇa explains the meaning. The word āji is stated among the twenty-four [as read] names of battle, 'pūrṇaḥ', 'vivāk' (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]); the explanation of the words āji and pradhana is in the Nirukta of Yāska (Ni. 7-?? as read [?]). Example:

original p. 188

न्यक्रन्दयन्नुपयन्त एनममेहयन् वृषभं मध्य आजेः । तेन सूभर्वं शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः प्रधने जिगाय ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१०२-९ [as read])

nyakrandayannupayanta enamamehayan vṛṣabhaṃ madhya ājeḥ | tena sūbharvaṃ śatavatsahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pradhane jigāya ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-102-9 [as read])

न्यक्रन्दयन्नुपयन्त एनमित्याख्याते । अमेहयन् वृषभं मध्य आजेः राजयनस्याजवनस्येति वा तेन तं सुभर्वं राजानं भर्वति हिनस्ति कर्मणा । तद्वा सुभर्वं सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः प्रधने जिगाय । प्रधन इति सङ्ग्रामनाम प्रकीर्णान्यस्मिन् धनानि भवन्ति ॥ (नि. ९-२४ [as read])

nyakrandayannupayanta enamityākhyāte | amehayan vṛṣabhaṃ madhya ājeḥ rājayanasyājavanasyeti vā tena taṃ subharvaṃ rājānaṃ bharvati hinasti karmaṇā | tadvā subharvaṃ sahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pradhane jigāya | pradhana iti saṅgrāmanāma prakīrṇānyasmin dhanāni bhavanti ‖ (ni. 9-24 [as read])

— in this example, the words pradhana and āji are used in the sense of battle (saṅgrāma, yuddha).

हरी इन्द्रस्य । रोहितौ अग्नेः । हरित आदित्यस्य । रासभावश्विनोः । अजा पूष्णः । पृषतो मरुताम् । अरुणो गाव उषसः । श्यावाः सवितुः । विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः । नियुतो वायोरिति दशादिष्टोपयोजनानि ॥ (नि. १-२५ [as read])

harī indrasya | rohitau agneḥ | harita ādityasya | rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ | ajā pūṣṇaḥ | pṛṣato marutām | aruṇo gāva uṣasaḥ | śyāvāḥ savituḥ | viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ | niyuto vāyoriti daśādiṣṭopayojanāni ‖ (ni. 1-25 [as read])

— thus, in the sentence which gives the vehicles of those deities, it is said that the two asses are the vehicles of the Aśvin deities. Sāyaṇa, in explaining the meaning of sahasraṃ jigāya — 'he conquered a thousand' — cites the sentence prajāpatir vai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchat (Ai. Br. 4-?? as read [?]). Skandasvāmin here says 'prajāpatir vai somāya rājñe' (Ai. Br. 4-2-1 [as read; [?]]) and so on, explaining that the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence that tells the story that Prajāpati gave his daughter to King Soma is to be cited here. And he cites all this as an example —

प्रजापतिः सवितुः दुहितरं सूर्यां सोमाय राज्ञे प्रायच्छत् । येत्वन्ये देवाः कां वरयितुमागच्छन् । तेभ्यो विवाहादेनं केरमुक्षसहस्रमदात् ॥ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

prajāpatiḥ savituḥ duhitaraṃ sūryāṃ somāya rājñe prāyacchat | yetvanye devāḥ kāṃ varayitumāgacchan | tebhyo vivāhādenaṃ keramukṣasahasramadāt ‖ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

यदेतदाश्विनं नाम तस्मिन् देवा विवादमकुर्वन् । ममेदमस्तु ममेदमस्त्विति । तेब्रुवन् । अजिं धावाम । यो नो जेष्यति तस्येदं भविष्यतीति । तेग्नेर्गृहपतेरुपर्योदित्यं काष्ठां कृत्वाभिधावन् । काष्ठा आजयन्ते उच्यते । अश्वतरीरथेनाग्निराजिमधावत् । गोभिर्रथेनोषाः । हरिभ्यामिन्द्रः । गर्दभरथेनाश्विनौ । तेश्चाश्विनावजयताम् । इति ॥ (ऐ. ब्रा. ४-२-४ [as read])

yadetadāśvinaṃ nāma tasmin devā vivādamakurvan | mamedamastu mamedamastviti | tebruvan | ajiṃ dhāvāma | yo no jeṣyati tasyedaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | tegnergṛhapateruparyodityaṃ kāṣṭhāṃ kṛtvābhidhāvan | kāṣṭhā ājayante ucyate | aśvatarīrathenāgnirājimadhāvat | gobhirrathenoṣāḥ | haribhyāmindraḥ | gardabharathenāśvinau | teścāśvināvajayatām | iti ‖ (ai. brā. 4-2-4 [as read])

"Brahmā gave his daughter, named Sūryā, daughter of the deity Savitṛ, in marriage to King Soma. Then the other deities came to ask for her. He gave them, after the marriage, a thousand Ṛks. These Ṛks became known by the name 'Aśvin'. The deities who had come over those Ṛks quarrelled: 'I want it, I want it'. Afterwards they decided among themselves that whoever should win in the contest should get these Ṛks. Then, from Agni, the householder, upward to the Āditya [Sun] as the goal, they made a race and began to run. Then Agni came to the contest in a chariot yoked with mules [aśvatarī]; Uṣas came in a chariot yoked with red cows; Indra came with a chariot yoked with the two bay horses (hari); the Aśvin deities came in a chariot yoked with asses. In the race the Aśvin deities won; a thousand Ṛks fell to them. From this these Ṛks became known as 'Aśvina': thus the Itihāsa is explained." And, "for the word ājā the meaning of aśvādeḥ dhāvanabhūmi — the place where horses and others run — is called āji": explaining this, [he gives for] yamasya: 'the word yama [ṃasya?] is said of the Āditya, because he destroys the darkness of night; hence here the word yama must be taken to mean āditya':

तस्य सम्बन्धिन्याः । इति पुनरादित्यस्याजिसम्बन्ध उच्यते । आदित्यस्तस्या अन्तेऽसीत् । तथाहि ब्राह्मणम् । तेऽग्नेर्गृहपतेरुपर्यादित्यं काष्ठामकुर्वत । (ऐ. ब्रा. ४-२-४)

tasya sambandhinyāḥ | iti punarādityasyājisambandha ucyate | ādityastasyā ante 'sīt | tathāhi brāhmaṇam | te 'gnergṛhapateruparyādityaṃ kāṣṭhāmakurvata | (ai. brā. 4-2-4)

— the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence is cited as an example to state the connection between the war (āji) and the Āditya (Sun). Pradhane — "the word explained as 'in battle, in the fight'; and agnyādibhiḥ saha saṃspardhāyām — in the battle where Agni and other deities contend with one another."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.3)

अत्रेयमाख्यायिका । तुग्रो नामाश्विनोः प्रियः कश्चिद्राजर्षिः । स द्वीपान्तरविर्भिः शत्रुभिरत्यन्तमुपद्रुतः सन् तेषां जयाय स्वपुत्रं भुज्युं सेनया सह नावा प्राहेषीत् । सा च सौर्मर्धये [?] समुद्रमतिदूरं गतानावयवशेन भिन्नासीत् । तदानीं स भुज्युः शीघ्रमश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तौ च स्तुतौ सेनया सहितं भुज्युं मद्भिरीयासु नौप्रारोह्य पितुस्तुग्रस्य समीपं त्रिभिरहोरात्रैः प्रापयामासतुरिति । अयमर्थ इदमादिकेन तृचेन प्रतिपाद्यते । हशब्दः प्रसिद्धौ । तुग्रः खलु पूर्वं शत्रुभिः पीडितः सन् तेजोजयार्थमुदमेघे । उदकैर्मिहृते सिच्यते इत्युदकमेघः समुद्रः । तस्मिन् भुज्युमेतत्संज्ञं प्रियं पुत्रमवाहाः । नावा गन्तुं पर्यत्याक्षीत् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । ममृवान् म्रियमाणः सन्ननलोभे कश्चिन्मनुष्यो रयिं न यथा धनं परित्यजति तद्वत् । हे अश्विनौ तं च भुज्युं मध्येसमुद्रं निमग्नं नौभिः पित्रसमीपमूहथुः । युवां प्रापितवन्तौ । कीदृशीभिः । आत्मन्वतीभिरात्मीयाभिः । युवयोः स्वभूताभिरित्यर्थः । यद्वा । धृतिरात्मा । धारणवतीभिरित्यर्थः । अन्तरिक्षप्रुद्भिरतिस्वच्छत्वादन्तरिक्षे जलस्योपरिष्ठादेव गन्तृभिः । अपोदकाभिः सुश्लिष्टत्वादपगतोदकाभिः । अस्पृष्टोदकाभिरित्यर्थः ॥ [the grammatical tail follows in small type: udameghe — mih "to sprinkle", ghañ, nyaṅkvādīnāṃ ca (Pā. 7-3-53) kutva; udakasya udaḥ saṃjñāyām (Pā. 6-3-57); mamṛvān — mṛṅ "to die", kvasu; kradiniyamāt… vasvekājāḍdhasām, niyamād abhāvaḥ — no iṭ; ahāḥ — ohāk "to leave", luṅ, tip, cleḥ sic, āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvād aṭ na kriyate, bahulaṃ chandasi, iṭ not applied, halṅyābbhyaḥ — elision of tip, ru-visarga; or mantre ghasa… cleḥ luk; nāvā…; ātmanvatībhiḥ — ātmanaḥ matup, mādupadhāyāḥ — va; ano nuṭ, nuṭ augment; nalopaḥ; hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matub…, matup accent udāttatva; antarikṣaprudbhiḥ — pru [as printed pruj] "to go", kvip…] [small type; read with doubt — words marked [?]]

atreyamākhyāyikā | tugro nāmāśvinoḥ priyaḥ kaścidrājarṣiḥ | sa dvīpāntaravirbhiḥ śatrubhiratyantamupadrutaḥ san teṣāṃ jayāya svaputraṃ bhujyuṃ senayā saha nāvā prāheṣīt | sā ca saurmardhaye [?] samudramatidūraṃ gatānāvayavaśena bhinnāsīt | tadānīṃ sa bhujyuḥ śīghramaśvinau tuṣṭāva | tau ca stutau senayā sahitaṃ bhujyuṃ madbhirīyāsu nauprārohya pitustugrasya samīpaṃ tribhirahorātraiḥ prāpayāmāsaturiti | ayamartha idamādikena tṛcena pratipādyate | haśabdaḥ prasiddhau | tugraḥ khalu pūrvaṃ śatrubhiḥ pīḍitaḥ san tejojayārthamudameghe | udakairmihṛte sicyate ityudakameghaḥ samudraḥ | tasmin bhujyumetatsaṃjñaṃ priyaṃ putramavāhāḥ | nāvā gantuṃ paryatyākṣīt | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | mamṛvān mriyamāṇaḥ sannanalobhe kaścinmanuṣyo rayiṃ na yathā dhanaṃ parityajati tadvat | he aśvinau taṃ ca bhujyuṃ madhyesamudraṃ nimagnaṃ naubhiḥ pitrasamīpamūhathuḥ | yuvāṃ prāpitavantau | kīdṛśībhiḥ | ātmanvatībhirātmīyābhiḥ | yuvayoḥ svabhūtābhirityarthaḥ | yadvā | dhṛtirātmā | dhāraṇavatībhirityarthaḥ | antarikṣaprudbhiratisvacchatvādantarikṣe jalasyopariṣṭhādeva gantṛbhiḥ | apodakābhiḥ suśliṣṭatvādapagatodakābhiḥ | aspṛṣṭodakābhirityarthaḥ ‖ [the grammatical tail follows in small type: udameghe — mih "to sprinkle", ghañ, nyaṅkvādīnāṃ ca (Pā. 7-3-53) kutva; udakasya udaḥ saṃjñāyām (Pā. 6-3-57); mamṛvān — mṛṅ "to die", kvasu; kradiniyamāt… vasvekājāḍdhasām, niyamād abhāvaḥ — no iṭ; ahāḥ — ohāk "to leave", luṅ, tip, cleḥ sic, āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvād aṭ na kriyate, bahulaṃ chandasi, iṭ not applied, halṅyābbhyaḥ — elision of tip, ru-visarga; or mantre ghasa… cleḥ luk; nāvā…; ātmanvatībhiḥ — ātmanaḥ matup, mādupadhāyāḥ — va; ano nuṭ, nuṭ augment; nalopaḥ; hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matub…, matup accent udāttatva; antarikṣaprudbhiḥ — pru [as printed pruj] "to go", kvip…] [small type; read with doubt — words marked [?]]

Sense (mine): "Here is the story. Tugra was a royal sage dear to the Aśvins. Being greatly harassed by enemies of the neighbouring islands, he sent his son Bhujyu, with an army, in a ship, to conquer them. And that ship, through damage of its parts [?], went far into the ocean and was broken. Then Bhujyu quickly praised the Aśvins. And they, praised, put Bhujyu with his army on ships of their own and brought him to his father Tugra in three days and nights. This sense is declared by the three Ṛks beginning with this one. Ha is a particle of 'well known'. Tugra, once harassed by enemies, for the sake of conquest, udameghe, in the udameghā — 'which is sprinkled by waters (udakair mihyate secyate)', the ocean — avāhāḥ — sent that Bhujyu, his dear son, going by ship; and then abandoned him — as an illustration: a man mamṛvān, dying, (not clinging out of greed?) leaves his wealth, so he left [him]. O Aśvins, you ūhathuḥ, carried that Bhujyu, sunk in the middle of the sea, to his father's neighbourhood, by nāubhiḥ, ships. What kind of ships? Ātmanvatībhiḥ — your own, belonging to you; or: ātman is firmness — those having firmness; antarikṣaprudbhiḥ — travelling over the water's surface as if in the atmosphere, because they are very clear; apodakābhiḥ — the water having been drawn off, because of close fitting — not touched by water."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"tugraḥ — Tugra (the royal sage, for the sake of conquest over enemies); udameghe — in the ocean; bhujyum — his son Bhujyu by name; mamṛvān — one who is dying; kaścit — (a man) greedy; rayim na — (as one abandons his wealth, in his extreme distress); avāhāḥ ha — sent away (to the sea)…

original p. 193

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 3, concluded: "… naṣṭam [?] (lost, sent away to the sea); (aśvinau — O Aśvin deities); tam — that Bhujyu (sunk in the midst of the ocean); ātmanvatībhiḥ — your own; antarikṣaprudbhiḥ — moving in the atmosphere (that is, over the surface of the water); apodakābhiḥ — which, being tight, let no water enter; nāubhiḥ — by ships; ūhathuḥ — you carried him to his father's house."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"When Tugra sent his son Bhujyu to the sea (to conquer the enemies who were oppressing him), like a greedy man at the point of death who with great difficulty gives up his wealth [?], you carried him, who was sinking in mid-ocean, in your own ships — which always float and let no water enter — and set him down at his father's house."

English Translation (as printed)

Tugra, verily, Aswins, sent (his son) Bhujyu to sea, as a dying man parts with his riches ; but you brought him back in vessels of your own, floating over the ocean, and keeping out the waters.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

"In this Ṛk is recounted the history: the royal sage who is famed by the name Tugra and is dear to the Aśvin deities, unable to bear the trouble the enemies in the other islands caused him, sent his son Bhujyu with an army to the other islands in order to subdue them; Bhujyu, travelling with the army on the sea in a ship (boat), found his ship broken in the middle. Then Bhujyu, son of Tugra, quickly praised the Aśvin deities. They, hearing his praise, were pleased, took Bhujyu with the army onto their ships and, travelling three days and nights without rest (continuously), brought him to the house of his father King Tugra."

तुग्रः — Tugraḥ — "Tugra was a king. That he was the father of Bhujyu is stated in the Ṛgveda in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-3, 1-117-14, 6-62-6 [as read; [?]]; in the Ṛks in which Bhujyu is spoken of as the son of Tugra the name of Tugra occurs, and also, as Taugrya, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-?-? ; 1-?-? [as read], 8-?-? [numerals partly illegible [?]].

original p. 194

The name Tugra is also in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-? ; 1-117-? ; 1-?-? ; 1-?-? ; 6-?-? ; 10-?-? [numerals too small to read reliably [?]]. In the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-8 [as read], 6-?-? and 10-49-4 [as read] the Tugra spoken of must be a different person, since there he is said to be Indra's enemy."

भुज्युम् — Bhujyum — "that Bhujyu was a son of Tugra, and that the Aśvin deities protected him when he was sinking in the middle of the ocean (through destruction of his ship), is said in the Ṛgveda in many places —

याभिरन्तकं जसमानमारे भुज्युं याभिरव्यथिभिर्जिजिन्वथुः । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-६ [as read])

yābhirantakaṃ jasamānamāre bhujyuṃ yābhiravyathibhirjijinvathuḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-6 [as read])

— in this Ṛk the bhujyu [explained by the Bhāṣyakāra as] 'sarvasya pālakam etatsaṃjñaṃ samudramadhye nimagnaṃ tugrasya putraṃ rājarṣim': the royal sage Bhujyu, son of the king Tugra, who was sinking in the ocean, was protected by the Aśvin deities.

याभिः शंताती भवथो ददाशुषे भुज्युं याभिरवथो याभिरधिगुम् । ओम्यावतीं सुभरामृतस्तुभं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-२० [as read])

yābhiḥ śaṃtātī bhavatho dadāśuṣe bhujyuṃ yābhiravatho yābhiradhigum | omyāvatīṃ subharāmṛtastubhaṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-20 [as read])

In this Ṛk too: 'you protected Bhujyu, the son of Tugra'.

युवं तुग्राय पूर्व्येभिरेवैः पुनर्मन्या अभवतं युवाना । युवं भुज्युमर्णसो निः समुद्राद्विभिरूहथुरृज्रेभिरश्वैः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-४ [as read])

yuvaṃ tugrāya pūrvyebhirevaiḥ punarmanyā abhavataṃ yuvānā | yuvaṃ bhujyumarṇaso niḥ samudrādvibhirūhathurṛjrebhiraśvaiḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-4 [as read])

Here also: 'O Aśvins, you carried Bhujyu, son of Tugra, who was sunk in the middle of the sea — (the one who is sunk out of the water-mass, the ocean, [= arṇasaḥ]) — with swift horses [ṛjrebhir aśvaiḥ], having brought him out from the unfathomable ocean, as it were from drowning; you took him to his father's house." the above is the Kannada exposition of the Ṛk; the sentence that follows in the print is its explanatory gloss.

याभिरन्तकं जसमानमारे भुज्युं याभिरव्यथिभिर्जिजिन्वथुः । याभिः कर्कन्धुं वय्यं च जिन्वथस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विनागतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-६ [as read])

yābhirantakaṃ jasamānamāre bhujyuṃ yābhiravyathibhirjijinvathuḥ | yābhiḥ karkandhuṃ vayyaṃ ca jinvathastābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvināgatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-6 [as read])

याभिः शंताती भवथो ददाशुषे भुज्युं याभिरवथो याभिरधिगुम् । ओम्यावतीं सुभरामृतस्तुभं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-२० [as read])

yābhiḥ śaṃtātī bhavatho dadāśuṣe bhujyuṃ yābhiravatho yābhiradhigum | omyāvatīṃ subharāmṛtastubhaṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-20 [as read])

he cited these Ṛks as examples.

original p. 196

तुग्रः — Tugraḥ — "tugra iti soyam ityabhisambandhāt pitṛkaḥ śabdeneda putrasyābhidhānam": "in this mantra the word tugra is used as a synonym of Bhujyu, son of Tugra. As in the usage 'soyam' [= this very one] in the pratyabhijñā (recognition), Skandasvāmin explains that by the word tugra, which denotes the father, the son Bhujyu is here referred to; the sense is 'the son of Tugra'. This is an adjective of the word Bhujyu, since Bhujyu is Tugra's son."

उदमेघे — Udameghe — "udakair mihyate secyate iti udamegha — samudraḥ": "the ocean, because it is sprinkled with water (rain)."

रयिं न — Rayiṃ na — "the word rayi is read among the hundred-and-one names of water (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]) and among the twenty-eight [as read] names of wealth. And —

नू च पुरा च सदनं रयीणां जातस्य च जायमानस्य च क्षाम् । सतश्च गोपां भवतश्च भूरेर्देवा अग्निं धारयन् द्रविणोदाम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-७३-२ [as read])

nū ca purā ca sadanaṃ rayīṇāṃ jātasya ca jāyamānasya ca kṣām | sataśca gopāṃ bhavataśca bhūrerdevā agniṃ dhārayan draviṇodām ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-73-2 [as read])

— the Nirukta-writer cites this Ṛk as an example and explains, 'rayir iti dhananāma rāter dānakarmaṇaḥ' (Ni. 4-?? as read [?]): the word rayi means wealth, formed from the root rā 'to give'."

ममृवान् — Mamṛvān — "the meaning is: Tugra, like a man who, though he has the strongest attachment to wealth, abandons the wealth at the point of death when death approaches, sent his son Bhujyu with great distress on the sea voyage."

आत्मन्वतीभिः — Ātmanvatībhiḥ — "ātmīyābhiḥ: yadvā dhṛtirātmā dhāraṇāvatībhir ity arthaḥ": "the Aśvin deities protected Bhujyu from distress with ships which were their own; or, because the word ātman has the meaning dhṛti (firmness), or dhairya, they made him — Bhujyu, who was in distress — firm in mind, and protected him by seating him in the ships."

अन्तरिक्षप्रुद्भिः — Antarikṣaprudbhiḥ — "since the Aśvin deities' ships are very clear, and very swift, they used to move only on the upper side of the water."

original p. 197

अपोदकाभिः — Apodakābhiḥ — "suślīṣṭatvād apagatodakābhiḥ asprṣṭodakābhir ity arthaḥ": "because the ships are built with no crack or opening, so well made, water does not enter at all; this is the meaning. In these three qualifying words the nature of the Aśvins' ship [being what it is, uttamatva] is manifested [in contrast to other ships]. And the next Ṛk is also a description of the Aśvins' ships."

तिस्रः क्षपस्त्रिरहातिव्रजद्भिर्नासत्या भुज्युमूहथुः पतंगैः । समुद्रस्य धन्वन्नार्द्रस्य पारे त्रिभी रथैः शतपद्भिः षळश्वैः ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.4)

हे नासत्या सेनया सहोदके निमग्नं भुज्युं तिस्रः क्षपस्त्रिसंख्याका रात्रीस्त्रिरहा त्रिनारमावृत्तान्यहानि चातिव्रजद्भिरतिक्रम्य गच्छद्भिरेतावन्तं कालमतिव्याप्य वर्तमानैः पतंगैः पतद्भिः सञ्चारिभिस्त्रिभिस्त्रिसंख्यैः रथैरारोहथुः [?] ऊहथुः । युवामूढवन्ताविति चेत् उच्यते । समुद्रस्याम्बुराशेर्मध्ये धन्वन् धन्वनि जलवर्जिते प्रदेशे । आर्द्रस्योदकेनार्द्रीभूतस्य समुद्रस्य पारे तीरदेशे च । कथंभूतैरथैः । शतपद्भिः शतसंख्यैश्चक्रलक्षणैः पादैरुपेतैः । षळश्वैः षड्भिरश्वैर्युक्तैः ॥ [grammatical tail follows: tisraḥ — tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ, tisṛ substitution; kṣapaḥ; tiraḥ…; ahā — ahan, ṭi; patangaiḥ — paṭḷ "to go", paterangac, Uṇ. 1-?? as read [?]; dhanvan — dhanvi "to go", with kanin [kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanidraviṇāt…]; supāṃ sulug, ṅi → luk; śatapadbhiḥ — śataṃ pādā yeṣām, saṃkhyāsupūrvasya, pād → pad; ṣaḍaśvaiḥ — ṣaṭ + aśva, ayasmayādīni …] [read from the print; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

he nāsatyā senayā sahodake nimagnaṃ bhujyuṃ tisraḥ kṣapastrisaṃkhyākā rātrīstrirahā trināramāvṛttānyahāni cātivrajadbhiratikramya gacchadbhiretāvantaṃ kālamativyāpya vartamānaiḥ pataṃgaiḥ patadbhiḥ sañcāribhistribhistrisaṃkhyaiḥ rathairārohathuḥ [?] ūhathuḥ | yuvāmūḍhavantāviti cet ucyate | samudrasyāmburāśermadhye dhanvan dhanvani jalavarjite pradeśe | ārdrasyodakenārdrībhūtasya samudrasya pāre tīradeśe ca | kathaṃbhūtairathaiḥ | śatapadbhiḥ śatasaṃkhyaiścakralakṣaṇaiḥ pādairupetaiḥ | ṣaḷaśvaiḥ ṣaḍbhiraśvairyuktaiḥ ‖ [grammatical tail follows: tisraḥ — tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ, tisṛ substitution; kṣapaḥ; tiraḥ…; ahā — ahan, ṭi; patangaiḥ — paṭḷ "to go", paterangac, Uṇ. 1-?? as read [?]; dhanvan — dhanvi "to go", with kanin [kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanidraviṇāt…]; supāṃ sulug, ṅi → luk; śatapadbhiḥ — śataṃ pādā yeṣām, saṃkhyāsupūrvasya, pād → pad; ṣaḍaśvaiḥ — ṣaṭ + aśva, ayasmayādīni …] [read from the print; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "O Nāsatyas, Bhujyu, sunk with his army in the water — for three kṣapaḥ (nights), trir ahā (three days — days recurring thrice) — you carried (ūhathuḥ) by three pataṅgaiḥ, 'flying', i.e. swift-moving, three in number, chariots, atiprajadbhiḥ — going far beyond, continuing over so much time. If it be asked 'where did you carry him?' it is said: samudrasya dhanvan — in the waterless region in the middle of the ocean — and ārdrasya pāre — on the shore of the ocean made wet by water. What chariots? Śatapadbhiḥ — having a hundred 'feet', i.e. hundred wheels; ṣaḍaśvaiḥ — drawn by six horses."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he nāsatyā — O Aśvin deities; bhujyum — Bhujyu (who was sunk in the sea with his army); tisraḥ kṣapaḥ — three nights (and); triraha — three days; ativrajadbhiḥ — passing over (going on beyond); pataṅgaiḥ — swift-moving; śatapadbhiḥ —

original p. 200

— with a hundred wheels (feet); ṣaḷaśvaiḥ — six horses yoked; tribhiḥ rathaiḥ — by three chariots; samudrasya — of the ocean; dhanvan — in the waterless region; ārdrasya — of the wet; samudrasya — of the ocean; pāre — in the region of the shore; ūhathuḥ — you carried him away."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, three days and three nights, in a continuous swift course, in three chariots of a hundred wheels, with six horses yoked (to each), you carried Bhujyu (sunk with his army) both through waterless regions near the ocean and through the regions of the shore of the sea."

English Translation (as printed)

Three nights and three days, Nasatyas, have you conveyed Bhujyu in three rapid, revolving cars, having a hundred wheels, and drawn by six horses, along the dry shore of the sea.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

तिस्रः क्षपः — Tisraḥ kṣapaḥ — "trisaṃkhyākā rātrīḥ": "since the word kṣapaḥ is stated among the twenty-two [as read] names of night (rātri) — śyāvī, śarvarī and so on (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]) — kṣapaḥ means night."

पतङ्गैः — Pataṅgaiḥ — "patadbhiḥ": "since the word pataṅga is read among the sixteen names of horses, 'atya', 'haya' and so on (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]), though the word pataṅga denotes the meaning 'horse', Sāyaṇa explains it as patadbhiḥ — 'moving'."

धन्वन् — Dhanvan — "jalavarjite pradeśe": "in a region without water. Since the word dhanva is stated among the sixteen names of the atmosphere, 'ambara', 'viyat' and so on (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]), dhanvan means 'atmosphere'. In the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and in Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya, it is explained as 'nirudakapradeśa' (a waterless region). Yāska:

धन्वान्तरिक्षं धन्वन्त्यस्मादापः ॥ [as read: dhanvāntarikṣaṃ dhanvanty asmād āpaḥ]

dhanvāntarikṣaṃ dhanvantyasmādāpaḥ ‖ [as read: dhanvāntarikṣaṃ dhanvanty asmād āpaḥ]

— 'the waters flow out from it; therefore the atmosphere is called by the name dhanva' — he explains the meaning, and cites

यः पर्स्याः पारावतस्तिरो धन्वातिरोचते । स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-९३-?३ [as read; [?]])

yaḥ parsyāḥ pārāvatastiro dhanvātirocate | sa naḥ parṣadati dviṣaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-93-?3 [as read; [?]])

as an example."

original p. 201

समुद्रस्य — Samudrasya — "ambu-rāśeḥ": "the Nirukta-writer explains the word as 'a mass of waters' —

तत्र समुद्र इत्येतत्पार्थिवेन समुद्रेण सन्दिह्यते । समुद्रः कस्मात् समुद्द्रवन्त्यस्मादापः समभिद्रवन्त्येनमापः संमोदन्तेऽस्मिन्भूतानि समुदको भवति समुनत्तीति वा ॥ (नि. २-१० [as read])

tatra samudra ityetatpārthivena samudreṇa sandihyate | samudraḥ kasmāt samuddravantyasmādāpaḥ samabhidravantyenamāpaḥ saṃmodante 'sminbhūtāni samudako bhavati samunattīti vā ‖ (ni. 2-10 [as read])

— thus he examines the meaning of the word samudra. Among the sixteen names of the atmosphere the word pṛthivī and the word samudra are stated. Of these, since the sense 'mass of water' is established for the word samudra, there arises a doubt whether samudra means the atmosphere, the earth, or the sea. By four derivations — 'waters flow out of it', 'waters flow into it', 'beings rejoice in it', 'full of water' [samudako bhavati] or 'it wets (samunatti)' — he settles the sense of the word samudra as a collection of water. The word samudra is also used in other places in the sense of 'cloud'.

अश्मन्वाधाराणि निमन्तरिक्षमतोर्णे बद्धं सविता समुद्रम् । (ऋ. सं. १०-१८५-१ [as read; the first words doubtful [?]])

aśmanvādhārāṇi nimantarikṣamatorṇe baddhaṃ savitā samudram | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-185-1 [as read; the first words doubtful [?]])

तस्याः समुद्रा अधि वि क्षरन्ति तेन जीवन्ति प्रदिशश्चतस्रः । (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-४२ [as read])

tasyāḥ samudrā adhi vi kṣaranti tena jīvanti pradiśaścatasraḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-42 [as read])

samuditā samudro meghaḥ samudrā adhi vikṣaranti varṣanti meghāḥ — the clouds rained: here the word samudra is used in the senses of atmosphere and cloud. Likewise —

महः समुद्रं वरुणस्तिरो दधे धीरा इच्छेकुर्धरुणेष्वारभम् । (ऋ. सं. ७-८७-६ [as read])

mahaḥ samudraṃ varuṇastiro dadhe dhīrā icchekurdharuṇeṣvārabham | (ṛ. saṃ. 7-87-6 [as read])

— in this the word samudra denotes the Āditya. For the word samudra the meanings Āditya, cloud, mass of water are acceptable both by convention and by derivation: in each place the meaning must be stated according to the context. Here, by the maxim yogād rūḍher balīyasī ('convention is stronger than derivation'), samudra means a mass of water."

"The Aśvin deities helped the royal prince Bhujyu — who, with his army, was sinking in the water in the middle of the ocean — to reach, for three days (completely) and nights as well, in ceaseless motion, in their swift ships which have no connection with water, the land of the dry waste that is samudra …

original p. 202

… it is also said here that these [chariots] had many wheels and six horses yoked. As the Aśvin deities came with Bhujyu, it is described here that these three persons came safely to the shore in three chariots."

शतपद्भिः — Śatapadbhiḥ — "śatasaṃkhyākaiś cakralakṣaṇaiḥ pādair upetaiḥ": "(with a hundred 'feet', which are wheels) — Sāyaṇa explains that the Aśvin deities' chariots had hundreds of wheels. Śata here, by capacity, is used in the plural sense 'many' — śatāśrātra bahunāma sāmarthyāc chātra bahutve vartate; pāda is the wheel; pādaśabdo 'pi cakrapādavacanaḥ — tricakrapādair ity arthaḥ: the word śata here conveys by capacity the meaning 'many'; the word pāda is explained as 'wheel'. Therefore Skandasvāmin explains the word śatapadbhiḥ as 'having three wheels': the chariot has three wheels. He cites the Ṛk which makes this meaning clear —

क्व १ त्री चक्रा त्रिवृतो रथस्य क्व १ त्रयो वन्धुरो ये सनीळाः । कदा योगो वाजिनो रासभस्य येन यज्ञं नासत्योपयाथः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३४-९ [as read])

kva 1 trī cakrā trivṛto rathasya kva 1 trayo vandhuro ye sanīḷāḥ | kadā yogo vājino rāsabhasya yena yajñaṃ nāsatyopayāthaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-34-9 [as read])

— here it is described that the Aśvin deities' chariot has three wheels."

भुज्युम् — Bhujyum — "the explanation of this word is in the special topics on the third Ṛk of this sūkta."
