॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.5)

हे अश्विनौ अनारम्भण आलम्बनरहिते समुद्रे तत्कर्माऽवीरयेथाम् । विक्रान्तं कृतवन्तौ युवाम् । अनारम्भणस्येव स्पष्टीकरोति । अनास्थाने । आस्थीयतेऽस्मिन्नित्यास्थानो भूप्रदेशः । तद्रहिते स्थातुमशक्ये जल इत्यर्थः । अग्रभणे । ग्रहणे । हस्तेन ग्राह्यं शाखादिकमपि यत्र नास्ति तस्मिन्नित्यर्थः । किं पुनस्तत्कर्म । भुज्युं समुद्रे मग्नं शतारित्रां बहुरित्रां । यैः काष्ठैः पार्श्वतो बद्धैर्जलालोडने सति नौः शीघ्रं गच्छति तान्यरित्राणि । ईदृशीं नावमातस्थिवांसमास्थितवन्तमारूढवन्तं कृतास्तं गृहानयैतत् । पितुस्तुग्रस्य गृहं प्रति यदोहथुः । तत्प्रापणमन्यैर्दुःशकं युवां समुद्रमध्ये कृतवन्ताविस्यर्थः ॥ अनारम्भणे । आरभ्यते इत्यारम्भणम् । कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति कर्मणि ल्युट् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । अवीरयेथाम् । शूर वीर विक्रान्तौ चुरादिरात्मनेपदी । अनास्थानाग्रभणयोः पूर्ववल्लक्ष्यस्वरः । अयं तु विशेषः । हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वम् । अस्तम् । अस्यतेऽस्मिन् सर्वमित्यस्तं गृहम् । असिहसीत्यादिना तन्प्रत्ययः । शतारित्राम् । रु गतौ । अर्तिलूधूसू…। (पा. ३-२-१८४) इति करण इत्रप्रत्ययः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ [grammatical tail partly small type; doubtful words [?]]

he aśvinau anārambhaṇa ālambanarahite samudre tatkarmā 'vīrayethām | vikrāntaṃ kṛtavantau yuvām | anārambhaṇasyeva spaṣṭīkaroti | anāsthāne | āsthīyate 'sminnityāsthāno bhūpradeśaḥ | tadrahite sthātumaśakye jala ityarthaḥ | agrabhaṇe | grahaṇe | hastena grāhyaṃ śākhādikamapi yatra nāsti tasminnityarthaḥ | kiṃ punastatkarma | bhujyuṃ samudre magnaṃ śatāritrāṃ bahuritrāṃ | yaiḥ kāṣṭhaiḥ pārśvato baddhairjalāloḍane sati nauḥ śīghraṃ gacchati tānyaritrāṇi | īdṛśīṃ nāvamātasthivāṃsamāsthitavantamārūḍhavantaṃ kṛtāstaṃ gṛhānayaitat | pitustugrasya gṛhaṃ prati yadohathuḥ | tatprāpaṇamanyairduḥśakaṃ yuvāṃ samudramadhye kṛtavantāvisyarthaḥ ‖ anārambhaṇe | ārabhyate ityārambhaṇam | kṛtyalyuṭo bahulamiti karmaṇi lyuṭ | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | avīrayethām | śūra vīra vikrāntau curādirātmanepadī | anāsthānāgrabhaṇayoḥ pūrvavallakṣyasvaraḥ | ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ | hṛgrahorbha iti bhatvam | astam | asyate 'smin sarvamityastaṃ gṛham | asihasītyādinā tanpratyayaḥ | śatāritrām | ru gatau | artilūdhūsū…| (pā. 3-2-184) iti karaṇa itrapratyayaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖ [grammatical tail partly small type; doubtful words [?]]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, in the sea, anārambhaṇe, which has nothing to hold on to, you did that deed (avīrayethām): you did a valiant act. He makes the 'no-support' plain: anāsthāne — āsthāna is a place of the earth where one stands: where there is none, i.e. in water where one cannot stand. Agrabhaṇe — in a place where there is not even a branch or the like that may be grasped by the hand. And what is that deed? [That] you carried Bhujyu, sunk in the sea, śatāritrām — [in a ship] with many oars (aritra; the pieces of wood fixed at the sides by which, when they stir the water, the ship goes quickly are called aritras); such a ship, he having mounted it, asta, to the house — to the house of his father Tugra, you carried; this feat, difficult for others, you two did in the middle of the sea."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinau — O Aśvin deities; śatāritrām — furnished with a hundred oars; nāvam — in the ship; ātasthivāṃsam — seated; bhujyum — Bhujyu; astam — to (his father's) house; ūhathuḥ yat — that you carried; tat — that great feat; anārambhaṇe — [in a place] without support; anāsthāne — without a place to stand; agrabhaṇe — where there is nothing to grasp; samudre — in the ocean; avīrayethām — you accomplished."

original p. 205

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"You accomplished the great feat of carrying Bhujyu in a ship with a hundred oars to his father's house. You did this feat in the sea, where there is no support, no place to stand, no object to lay hold of."

English Translation (as printed)

This exploit you achieved, As'wins, in the ocean where there is nothing to give support, nothing to rest upon, nothing to cling to, that you brought Bhujyu, sailing in a hundred-oared ship, to his father's house.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अनास्थाने — Anāsthāne — "āsthīyate 'smin ity āsthāno bhūpradeśaḥ | tadrahite sthātum aśakye jale": "since the land is favourable to creatures for standing comfortably, it has the name āsthāna. The ocean, which is the opposite of it, is called anāsthāna. The idea is that one cannot stand on a ship [sic: in the water]. Likewise the ocean provides no support to those who come to it. In the sea, means of protection such as creepers (by which one may be saved from sinking) — that is, strong trees, ropes etc., fit to hold on to so as not to sink in the water — are not there to be held (grahaṇa) or to be seized; hence it is called agrahaṇa. So the act the Aśvin deities performed when protecting Bhujyu, who was sinking in the unsupported, ungraspable ocean, is a deed of extreme valour, which only very brave persons perform."

original p. 206

शतारित्राम् — Śatāritrām — "bahvaritrām — [a ship] with many oars: the pieces of wood fixed to the sides of a ship by which it is made to move forward in the water are called aritra. They say it is 'a paddle' [huṭṭu]. The meaning is that the ship of the Aśvin deities, to go very swiftly in the water, had a hundred paddles — the instruments for rowing [it]."

अस्तम् — Astam — "gṛhanāmaitat | gayaḥ kṣayaḥ": "since the word asta is read among the two [as read: iṣṭa… the 'twenty-two'] names of house, 'gaya', 'kṣaya' and so on (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), asta means house. The Aśvin deities brought Bhujyu and set him down at the house of his father King Tugra: this is the meaning. The purport is that the act of rescuing a man sinking in mid-ocean, which no one else can perform, is praise-worthy, and the Aśvin deities performed it."

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.6)

यम् । अश्विना । ददथुः । श्वेतम् । अश्वम् । अघाश्वाय । शश्वत् । इत् । स्वस्ति । तत् । वाम् । दात्रम् । महि । कीर्तेन्यम् । भूत् । पैद्वः । वाजी । सदम् । इत् । हव्यः । अर्यः ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.6)

अत्रेदमाख्यायते । पेदुर्नाम कश्चित्स चाश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तस्मै प्रीतौ कंचिच्छ्वेतवर्णमश्वं दत्तवन्तौ । स चाश्वस्तस्य पौत्रेऽद्य [?] जयं चकारेति । एतदत्र प्रतिपाद्यते । हे अश्विनौ युवामघाश्वायाहन्तव्याश्वाय पेदुनाम्ने राजर्षये यं श्वेतवर्णमश्वं ददथुः । दत्तवन्तौ । सोऽश्वस्तस्मै स्वस्ति जयलक्षणं मङ्गलं शश्वदित् नित्यमेव चकार । वां युवयोस्तद्दात्रं दानं महि महदतिगम्भीरम् । अत एव कीर्तेन्यं सर्वैः कीर्तनीयं प्रशस्यं भूत् । अभूत् । तस्मात्पैद्वः पेदोः सम्बन्धी पतनशीलः शीघ्रगामी वार्यः शत्रूणां प्रेरयिता युद्धेषु प्रेरयितव्यो वा वाजी वेजनवानश्वः सदमित् सदैव हव्योऽस्माभिराह्वातव्यः ॥ [grammatical tail: dātram — dā "to give", dātrañ (tran), dāpā… Uṇ.? ; mahi — mah "to honour", in, sarvadhātubhya in, itīn; kīrtenyam — kīrt "to praise", tenyāyāḥ… kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ (Pā. 3-4-14 as read [?]) — kenyat; bhūt — bhū, luṅ, bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi, no augment; paidvaḥ — pedoḥ sambandhī, tasyedam, añ, chandaso varṇalopaḥ; havyaḥ — hvayati, ceyo yadiha yat; saṃprasāraṇa; aryaḥ — ṛ "to go", āśūṃ yādayaś ca, Uṇ.; ṇyat…] [small type; read letter by letter; words marked [?] doubtful]

atredamākhyāyate | pedurnāma kaścitsa cāśvinau tuṣṭāva | tasmai prītau kaṃcicchvetavarṇamaśvaṃ dattavantau | sa cāśvastasya pautre 'dya [?] jayaṃ cakāreti | etadatra pratipādyate | he aśvinau yuvāmaghāśvāyāhantavyāśvāya pedunāmne rājarṣaye yaṃ śvetavarṇamaśvaṃ dadathuḥ | dattavantau | so 'śvastasmai svasti jayalakṣaṇaṃ maṅgalaṃ śaśvadit nityameva cakāra | vāṃ yuvayostaddātraṃ dānaṃ mahi mahadatigambhīram | ata eva kīrtenyaṃ sarvaiḥ kīrtanīyaṃ praśasyaṃ bhūt | abhūt | tasmātpaidvaḥ pedoḥ sambandhī patanaśīlaḥ śīghragāmī vāryaḥ śatrūṇāṃ prerayitā yuddheṣu prerayitavyo vā vājī vejanavānaśvaḥ sadamit sadaiva havyo 'smābhirāhvātavyaḥ ‖ [grammatical tail: dātram — dā "to give", dātrañ (tran), dāpā… Uṇ.? ; mahi — mah "to honour", in, sarvadhātubhya in, itīn; kīrtenyam — kīrt "to praise", tenyāyāḥ… kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ (Pā. 3-4-14 as read [?]) — kenyat; bhūt — bhū, luṅ, bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi, no augment; paidvaḥ — pedoḥ sambandhī, tasyedam, añ, chandaso varṇalopaḥ; havyaḥ — hvayati, ceyo yadiha yat; saṃprasāraṇa; aryaḥ — ṛ "to go", āśūṃ yādayaś ca, Uṇ.; ṇyat…] [small type; read letter by letter; words marked [?] doubtful]

Sense (mine): "Here this is told. A certain man named Pedu praised the Aśvins; they, pleased, gave him a white horse. That horse made victory for his [son's/grandson's — doubtful [?]] ... This is here set forth. O Aśvins, the white horse which you two gave to the royal sage named Pedu, aghāśvāya — 'whose horses are not to be killed' — that horse made for him, always (śaśvad it), svasti, welfare in the form of victory. That gift (dātram) of you two is mahi, great, very profound; therefore kīrtenyam, to be praised by all, it has become. Therefore, paidvaḥ — the horse of Pedu, falling [swooping], swift-going, aryaḥ — the impeller of enemies, or to be impelled in battles, vājī — the horse that has speed — is sadam it, always, havyaḥ, to be invoked by us."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) on p. 209

original p. 209

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; aghāśvāya — to him whose horses are indestructible, to the royal sage named Pedu; yam — which; śvetam aśvam — white horse; dadathuḥ — you gave; saḥ aśvaḥ — that horse; svasti — good (in the form of victory); śaśvat it — always (made); vām — your; tat dātram — that gift; mahi — great (is, therefore); kīrtenyam — praised by all; bhūt — it has become; paidvaḥ — belonging to Pedu (named Pedu); āryaḥ — the destroyer of enemies; vājī — that horse; sadamit — always; havyaḥ — is to be invoked by us."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, the white horse that you gave to the king named Pedu, whose horses are indestructible, always made for him welfare. Your gift is great and worthy of being praised. That horse of Pedu is a destroyer of enemies. We should invoke it always."

English Translation (as printed)

As'wins, the white horse you gave to Pedu, whose horses were indestructible, was ever to him success ; that, your precious gift, is always to be celebrated ; the horse of Pedu, the scatterer (of enemies) is always to be invoked.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अघाश्वाय — Aghāśvāya — "ahantavyāśvāya pedunāmne rājarṣaye": "taking it to mean 'to the royal sage named Pedu, whose horses cannot be struck down by anyone in battles', for the word paidvaḥ [Sāyaṇa] explains: 'pedoḥ sambandhī patanaśīlaḥ śīghragāmī vā' — 'belonging to Pedu, swift-moving by nature'. Skandasvāmin:

अघाश्वो नाम राजा युयुत्सुरात्मनोऽश्वं अश्विनौ यदोचे सतेतं चाविनाशं । तस्मै अश्विनौ बलवन्तमात्यन्तवेगिनं जयकरं सर्वत्राप्रतिहतगमनमश्वं सतेतं चाविनाशं ददथुरिति । तदेतदिहोच्यते ॥ [small type, partly doubtful [?]]

aghāśvo nāma rājā yuyutsurātmano 'śvaṃ aśvinau yadoce satetaṃ cāvināśaṃ | tasmai aśvinau balavantamātyantaveginaṃ jayakaraṃ sarvatrāpratihatagamanamaśvaṃ satetaṃ cāvināśaṃ dadathuriti | tadetadihocyate ‖ [small type, partly doubtful [?]]

— 'a king named Aghāśva, desiring to fight, asked the Aśvins for a horse for himself; to him the Aśvins gave a horse, strong, very swift, victory-giving, whose course was unobstructed everywhere, ever-lasting and imperishable' — this is what is said here. The king named Aghāśva, who wished to fight, being strong though ... [the Kannada continues: 'conducting himself with speed, going everywhere without hindrance, procuring victory']

original p. 210

"… [the king Aghāśva, being] always without suffering defeat, prayed to the Aśvin deities: 'give me a horse'. They, in accordance with his prayer, gave him a white horse of his liking. — thus the story is told. For the word aghāśva the name of the king, and for the word paidva — since it is read among the names of horse (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]) — 'paidvaḥ aśvanāmaitat: paidvaḥ means the horse [Pedu's]' — so he explains it. Sāyaṇa: 'pedur nāma kaścit sa cāśvinau tuṣṭāva tasmai prītau kiñcit śvetavarṇam aśvaṃ dattavantau' — a man named Pedu praised the Aśvin deities; they, pleased with his praise, gave him a white horse: since the two [commentators] explain thus, there is a difference in the explanation of the words pedu and aghāśva."

आर्यः — Āryaḥ — "śatrūṇāṃ prerayitā yuddheṣu prerayitavyo vā": "he who urges enemies in wars, or who is to be urged on in battles: giving courage, i.e. producing enthusiasm for fighting — thus Sāyaṇa explains. Skandasvāmin, since the word ārya is stated among the names of īśvara (lord) (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]):

प्र केतुना बृहता यात्यग्निरा रोदसी वृषभो रोरवीति । दिवश्चिदन्ताँ उपमाँ उदानळपामुपस्थे महिषो ववर्ध ॥ [as read in the print? — the print here gives:] प्र कैत्वे अद्य शिशिविष्ट नामार्यः शंसामि वयुनानि विद्वान् । (ऋ. सं. २-१००-? [?])

pra ketunā bṛhatā yātyagnirā rodasī vṛṣabho roravīti | divaścidantā~ upamā~ udānaḷapāmupasthe mahiṣo vavardha ‖ [as read in the print? — the print here gives:] pra kaitve adya śiśiviṣṭa nāmāryaḥ śaṃsāmi vayunāni vidvān | (ṛ. saṃ. 2-100-? [?])

— the word āryaḥ is explained as īśvara, 'lord': he explains that, by reason of this horse's going being unobstructed everywhere, being the lord over horses that move without obstruction at speed."

सदमित् — Sadamit — "sadam + it, sadaiva: 'always'. The word sadam is an indeclinable (nipāta); it is also an indeclinable. Nipāta — a word which, although it has one form like an avyaya, is used in many meanings. The Nirukta-writer —

अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थे अमिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छन्ति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमिमृदिति ॥ (नि. १-४ [as read])

atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe amitākṣareṣu grantheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchanti padapūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamimṛditi ‖ (ni. 1-4 [as read])

— the words kam, īm, it, u serve in large prose works for completing a sentence; in small verse works they are padding of the line. Though they are used for filling out a sentence or a line, they are 'meaningless' (anarthaka) since they do not convey the sense that is expressed in the work. For he says they have no definite sense. For an example of the particle kam

muñcāmi tvā haviṣā jīvanāya kamajñātayakṣmāduta rājayakṣmāt | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-161-1 [as read])

विमेनं सृजता सुखे मन्दिमिन्द्राय मन्दिने । (ऋ. सं. १-८-? [as read; [?]])

vimenaṃ sṛjatā sukhe mandimindrāya mandine | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-8-? [as read; [?]])

and, for the particle it,

तमिद्वर्धन्तु नो गिरो वत्सं संशिश्वरीरिव । (ऋ. सं. ८-१०-१४ [as read; [?]])

tamidvardhantu no giro vatsaṃ saṃśiśvarīriva | (ṛ. saṃ. 8-10-14 [as read; [?]])

and, for the particle u,

अयमु ते समतसि कपोत इव गर्भधिम् । (ऋ. सं. १-३०-४ [as read])

ayamu te samatasi kapota iva garbhadhim | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-30-4 [as read])

he gives these Ṛks."

वाजी — Vājī — "vegavān": "since the word vāji is read among the twenty-six [as read] names for horse (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]) the meaning is 'horse'; because it moves with speed it is famed as vājī. The Aśvin deities, to fulfil the wish of the king who did austerities or praised them, gave him a horse; the greatness and the praiseworthiness of this gift of a horse is expressed by the words dātraṃ mahi kīrtenyam."

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.7)

युवं नरा स्तुवते पज्रियाय कक्षीवते अरदतं पुरंधिम् । कारोतराच्छफादश्वस्य वृष्णः शतं कुम्भाँ असिञ्चतं सुरायाः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.7)

युवम् । नरा । स्तुवते । पज्रियाय । कक्षीवते । अरदतम् । पुरम्ऽधिम् । कारोतरात् । शफात् । अश्वस्य । वृष्णः । शतम् । कुम्भान् । असिञ्चतम् । सुरायाः ॥ ७ ॥

yuvam | narā | stuvate | pajriyāya | kakṣīvate | aradatam | puram 'dhim | kārotarāt | śaphāt | aśvasya | vṛṣṇaḥ | śatam | kumbhān | asiñcatam | surāyāḥ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.7)

अत्रेयमाख्यायिका । कक्षीवानृषिः पुरा कंसाशिरोहितज्ञानः सन् ज्ञानार्थमश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तस्मा अश्विनौ प्रभूतां धियं बुद्धिं दत्तवन्तौ । इति तदाह । हे नरा नेतारावश्विना युवं युवां पज्रियाय । पज्रा इत्यङ्गिरसामाख्या । पज्रा वाङ्गिरस इत्यामनात् । तेषां कुले जाताय कक्षीवते । कक्ष्या रज्जू रश्मयस्तद्वते । तत्कक्षसंज्ञाय स्तुवते युवयोः स्तुतिं कुर्वते मह्यं पुरंधिं प्रभूतां धियं बुद्धिमरदतम् । व्यलिखितम् । यथा सर्वार्थगोचरा भवति तथा कृतवन्ताविस्यर्थः । अपि च कारोतरात् । कारोतरो नाम वैदलक्षम् [?] र्वेष्टितो भाजनविशेषो यस्मिन्सुरायाः स्रावणं क्रियते । लुप्तोपमम् । कारोतरादिव सुरायाः संपादिकास्तां स्रावयन्ति एवमेव युवां वृष्णः सेचनसमर्थस्य युष्मदीयस्याश्वस्य शफात् खुरात् सुरायाः शतं कुम्भानसंख्यातान्सुराघटानसिञ्चतम् । आपूरयतम् । यद्वा । सिञ्चतिः पूरणार्थः । कारोतरस्थानीयाद्युष्मदीयाश्वस्य खुराद्यो सुरा प्रवहति तयासंख्यातान् घटानसिञ्चतम् । आपूरयतम् । ये जनाः सौत्रामण्यादिकर्मणि युष्मद्गाग्यां [?] सुरां योचन्ते तेषामित्यर्थः ॥ [grammatical tail follows: stuvate — ṣṭuñ "to praise", śatṛ; adādi śap luk, śatur anumaḥ…; pajriyāya — pajra + chaikaḥ ghac [as printed]; kakṣīvate — asandīvad… matup, kṣīvat, nipātāt, kakṣyā saṃprasāraṇa, vatvam ca; aradatam — rad "to scratch" [vilekhane]; purandhim — purandhir bahudhīr iti yāskaḥ, Ni. 6-13 as read [?], pṛṣodarādi — purandhi formation; or puraṃ pūrayitavyaṃ sarvaviṣayajātam asyāṃ dhīyate; kārotarāt…; asiñcatam — ṣiciṅ "to sprinkle"…] [small type; marked [?] where doubtful]

atreyamākhyāyikā | kakṣīvānṛṣiḥ purā kaṃsāśirohitajñānaḥ san jñānārthamaśvinau tuṣṭāva | tasmā aśvinau prabhūtāṃ dhiyaṃ buddhiṃ dattavantau | iti tadāha | he narā netārāvaśvinā yuvaṃ yuvāṃ pajriyāya | pajrā ityaṅgirasāmākhyā | pajrā vāṅgirasa ityāmanāt | teṣāṃ kule jātāya kakṣīvate | kakṣyā rajjū raśmayastadvate | tatkakṣasaṃjñāya stuvate yuvayoḥ stutiṃ kurvate mahyaṃ puraṃdhiṃ prabhūtāṃ dhiyaṃ buddhimaradatam | vyalikhitam | yathā sarvārthagocarā bhavati tathā kṛtavantāvisyarthaḥ | api ca kārotarāt | kārotaro nāma vaidalakṣam [?] rveṣṭito bhājanaviśeṣo yasminsurāyāḥ srāvaṇaṃ kriyate | luptopamam | kārotarādiva surāyāḥ saṃpādikāstāṃ srāvayanti evameva yuvāṃ vṛṣṇaḥ secanasamarthasya yuṣmadīyasyāśvasya śaphāt khurāt surāyāḥ śataṃ kumbhānasaṃkhyātānsurāghaṭānasiñcatam | āpūrayatam | yadvā | siñcatiḥ pūraṇārthaḥ | kārotarasthānīyādyuṣmadīyāśvasya khurādyo surā pravahati tayāsaṃkhyātān ghaṭānasiñcatam | āpūrayatam | ye janāḥ sautrāmaṇyādikarmaṇi yuṣmadgāgyāṃ [?] surāṃ yocante teṣāmityarthaḥ ‖ [grammatical tail follows: stuvate — ṣṭuñ "to praise", śatṛ; adādi śap luk, śatur anumaḥ…; pajriyāya — pajra + chaikaḥ ghac [as printed]; kakṣīvate — asandīvad… matup, kṣīvat, nipātāt, kakṣyā saṃprasāraṇa, vatvam ca; aradatam — rad "to scratch" [vilekhane]; purandhim — purandhir bahudhīr iti yāskaḥ, Ni. 6-13 as read [?], pṛṣodarādi — purandhi formation; or puraṃ pūrayitavyaṃ sarvaviṣayajātam asyāṃ dhīyate; kārotarāt…; asiñcatam — ṣiciṅ "to sprinkle"…] [small type; marked [?] where doubtful]

Sense (mine): "Here this story. The ṛṣi Kakṣīvān, long ago, ... [the text is doubtful here: kaṃsāśirohitajñānaḥ [?]] praised the Aśvins for knowledge; to him the Aśvins gave abundant dhī, understanding. This is said. O leaders, Aśvins, you, to the praiser pajriyāya — pajrāḥ is a name for the Aṅgirases ('pajrā vāṅgirasaḥ') — born in their family, kakṣīvate, to Kakṣīvān (kakṣyā = rope, rays: he who has them: that is, his name), purandhim — abundant understanding, aradatam, you 'scratched out' [i.e. opened]: you so made [his understanding] that it is capable of grasping all objects. And further: kārotarāt — a kārotara is a particular vessel [covered with a strainer(?)] in which the filtering of spirit (surā) is done. As the makers of spirit let it flow down from the kārotara, thus you two asiñcatam, filled, a hundred kumbhān, jars, of surā, from the śapha, hoof, of your ... vṛṣṇaḥ, vigorous, horse. Or: the root sic has the sense of 'to fill': with the surā that streams from the hoof of your horse, standing in the place of the kārotara, you filled uncounted jars, [for] the people who, in the Sautrāmaṇī and other rites, beg spirit of you."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"narā — O leaders, Aśvin deities; yuvam — you two; pajriyāya — born in the family of the Aṅgirases; stuvate — to the one who praises you (who has hidden knowledge); kakṣīvate — to Kakṣīvān by name (to me); purandhim — abundant understanding; aradatam — you gave; kārotarāt — as spirit is made to flow in a vessel called kārotara; vṛṣṇaḥ — capable of sprinkling; aśvasya — of your horse; śaphāt — from the hoof; surāyāḥ — of spirit; śatam kumbhān — a hundred (many) jars (for those who offer the Sautrāmaṇī and the like); asiñcatam — you filled."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, who lead men on the right path, to me, Kakṣīvān, born in the family of the Aṅgirases, who praise you (and whose knowledge was hidden), you gave the unfolding of understanding. From the hoof of your horse, which can sprinkle, as spirit is poured out in the vessel called kārotara, you filled a hundred jars with spirit (for those who offer the Sautrāmaṇī and the like)."

original p. 214

English Translation (as printed)

You gave leaders (of sacrifice), to Kakshivat, of the race of Pajra various knowledge ; you filled from the hoof of your vigorous steed, as if from a cask, a hundred jars of wine.

original p. 215

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

नरा — Narā — "netārau aśvinau": "the Aśvin deities who urge the understanding along the right path — so Sāyaṇa; Skandasvāmin explains narā as 'manuṣyākārau manuṣyāṇām ākāra iva ākāro yayoḥ' — those who have the form of men."

पज्रियाय कक्षीवते — Pajriyāya kakṣīvate — "pajrā ity aṅgirasām ākhyā | pajrā vāṅgirasa ity āmnānāt | teṣāṃ kule jātāya": "pajrā is a name of the Aṅgirases, as the śruti says 'pajrā vā aṅgirasaḥ'; the one born in their family — so Sāyaṇa explains. Skandasvāmin: though pājaḥ is read among the names of strength in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-9 as read [?]), the word pājas here is a name of food; therefore pajra is 'he whose is [the food] in the form of the oblation (havis)': 'for stuvate, yajate: one who prepares food in the form of oblation to offer to the deities, and praises' — [so pajriya is] the one who praises or sacrifices'; he explains in one manner; and —

अथवा प्रजा अङ्गिरस उच्यन्ते । तेषामपत्यभूतः पज्रियः । पौराणिका हि कक्षीवन्तमाङ्गिरसं स्मरन्ति । एवं ह्याहुः — उशिजो वृवदुक्थश्च ऋषिर्दीर्घतमास्तथा । कक्षीवाँस्त्र्यस्त्रिंशत्स्मृता ह्यङ्गिरसां वराः ॥ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]] इति । एवमाङ्गिरसां अपत्यं त्रयस्त्रिंशत्तमः कक्षीवान् । तस्मै कक्षीवते । मह्यमेवेत्यर्थः ॥

athavā prajā aṅgirasa ucyante | teṣāmapatyabhūtaḥ pajriyaḥ | paurāṇikā hi kakṣīvantamāṅgirasaṃ smaranti | evaṃ hyāhuḥ — uśijo vṛvadukthaśca ṛṣirdīrghatamāstathā | kakṣīvā~stryastriṃśatsmṛtā hyaṅgirasāṃ varāḥ ‖ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]] iti | evamāṅgirasāṃ apatyaṃ trayastriṃśattamaḥ kakṣīvān | tasmai kakṣīvate | mahyamevetyarthaḥ ‖

— 'Or: the Aṅgirases are called prajāḥ; the one who is their offspring is pajriya. The Purāṇa-writers remember Kakṣīvān as an Aṅgirasa; thus they say: "Uśija, Vṛvadukthā [sic in the print: vṛvaduktha], the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas, and Kakṣīvān — these are remembered as the thirty-three chiefs of the Aṅgirases." So Kakṣīvān is the thirty-third in the line of the Aṅgirasa descendants. To that Kakṣīvān: that is, to me, is the meaning.' The Kannada: 'those born in the family of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis are famed as pajrās. Those born in their family are called pajriyas. The Purāṇa-writers say that the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān, the seer of the mantras of this sūkta, was born in the line of these Aṅgirasa ṛṣis. Among those who are well-known in the Aṅgirasa line — Uśija, Vṛvaduktha, Dīrghatamas, Kakṣīvān, — thirty-three persons — this Kakṣīvān is the thirty-third. This Kakṣīvān had a great deal of ignorance. To be rid of his ignorance and to obtain the highest knowledge he praised the Aśvin deities. They, pleased with his praise, bestowed on him extraordinary knowledge: so the Itihāsa is explained. Sāyaṇa also tells this story."

कक्षीवते — Kakṣīvate — "kakṣyā nāma rajjū raśmiḥ | tadvate tatkakṣasaṃjñāya": "kakṣyā is the name of the rope that binds the horse; he who has it is kakṣīvān: the meaning of the word kakṣīvān.

original p. 216

कारोतरात् शफात् वृष्णः — Kārotarāt śaphāt vṛṣṇaḥ — "kārotaro nāma vaidalacarmaveṣṭito bhājanaviśeṣaḥ yasmin surāyāḥ srāvaṇaṃ kriyate": "a vessel made of well-prepared leather is called a kārotara, because spirit is poured into it. By putting spirit into it it is [the mark] of being pleasing [?]. Taking the word vṛṣṇaḥ in the sense of 'sprinkling' and of 'filling', he explains the meaning: the Aśvin deities caused a hundred jars of spirit, uncounted, to enter, to be filled, merely by the hoof of their horse. Since there is great need of spirit in sacrifices such as the Sautrāmaṇī, the Aśvin deities made spirit easy to obtain for those [sacrificers] — this is his explanation."

"Skandasvāmin tells a story on this matter:

आश्विनौ इतिहासमाचक्षते । अश्विनौ यदृच्छया पर्येटन्तौ पिबन्नुक्रं बालसमूहं ददर्श । स तौ सुरां ययाचे । तस्मै अश्विनौ देवता महाभाग्यात् अश्वशफादुद्धृत्य घटशतं सुरायै ददतुरिति । तदिहोच्यते कारोतराच्चादित्यादिना । कारोतर इति कूपनाम । तस्मादृश्यान्त इह अश्वशफे प्रयुज्यते । अश्वस्य शफादुद्धृत्य मत्तबालकेभ्यः सुरायाः घटशतं दत्तवन्त इत्यर्थः ॥ [small type, partly doubtful [?]]

āśvinau itihāsamācakṣate | aśvinau yadṛcchayā paryeṭantau pibannukraṃ bālasamūhaṃ dadarśa | sa tau surāṃ yayāce | tasmai aśvinau devatā mahābhāgyāt aśvaśaphāduddhṛtya ghaṭaśataṃ surāyai dadaturiti | tadihocyate kārotarāccādityādinā | kārotara iti kūpanāma | tasmādṛśyānta iha aśvaśaphe prayujyate | aśvasya śaphāduddhṛtya mattabālakebhyaḥ surāyāḥ ghaṭaśataṃ dattavanta ityarthaḥ ‖ [small type, partly doubtful [?]]

— 'The Aśvins, wandering at will, saw a group of children drinking spirit. They asked the Aśvins for spirit. The deities Aśvins, by their great power, drew from a horse's hoof a hundred jars of spirit and gave them: this is what is said here: kārotarāt — kārotara is a name of a well; so, in the sense of an example, it is used here for the horse's hoof': they drew from the horse's hoof and gave a hundred jars of spirit to the intoxicated children.' The Kannada: the Aśvin deities, wandering at their own will, saw a group of boys who had been drinking intoxicating drink. The boys asked them 'give us drink'. Then the Aśvin deities, in accordance with the power belonging to their divinity, by their horse's hoof, caused many jars of spirit to be filled — as if by the form of ... [reading doubtful [?]] — and gave the drink to those children: thus the Itihāsa is told. And this very matter —

तद्वां नरा शंस्यं पज्रियेण कक्षीवता नासत्या परिज्मन् । शफादश्वस्य वाजिनो जनाय शतं कुम्भाँ असिञ्चतं मधूनाम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-७ [as read])

tadvāṃ narā śaṃsyaṃ pajriyeṇa kakṣīvatā nāsatyā parijman | śaphādaśvasya vājino janāya śataṃ kumbhā~ asiñcataṃ madhūnām ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-7 [as read])

— he cites the Ṛk, saying that this is also stated in the Ṛk." Note: the print here gives a verse of the same shape as the Ṛk under comment; the reading of its first two pādas — 'tad vāṃ narā śaṃsyaṃ pajriyeṇa kakṣīvatā nāsatyā parijman' — is as printed but is not the standard text of this very Ṛk [Ṛ. 1-116-7]; I give the print and do not correct it from memory.

पुरंधिम् — Purandhim — "prabhūtāṃ dhiyam: abundant understanding; 'excess of understanding' means to know all subjects well. In this matter Skandasvāmin, under the phrase aradatam purandhim [says] —

original p. 217

पुरंधिं बह्वर्थविषयां प्रज्ञाम् । अथवा रदतिः विलेखनार्थ इव । कक्षीवतो बह्वर्थविषयां प्रज्ञां विलिखितवन्तौ जडां सतीं तीक्ष्णीकृतवन्तौ । अतीतानागतवर्तमानसमर्थां सर्वार्थग्रहणसमर्थां च कक्षीवतः प्रज्ञां कृतवन्तौ स्थ इत्यर्थः । तदेतत्क्लेशानुयुक्तम् — याभिः परिज्मा तनयस्य मज्मना द्विमाता तूर्षु तरणिर्विभूषति । याभिस्त्रिमन्तुरभवद्विचक्षणस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-४ [as read])

puraṃdhiṃ bahvarthaviṣayāṃ prajñām | athavā radatiḥ vilekhanārtha iva | kakṣīvato bahvarthaviṣayāṃ prajñāṃ vilikhitavantau jaḍāṃ satīṃ tīkṣṇīkṛtavantau | atītānāgatavartamānasamarthāṃ sarvārthagrahaṇasamarthāṃ ca kakṣīvataḥ prajñāṃ kṛtavantau stha ityarthaḥ | tadetatkleśānuyuktam — yābhiḥ parijmā tanayasya majmanā dvimātā tūrṣu taraṇirvibhūṣati | yābhistrimanturabhavadvicakṣaṇastābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-4 [as read])

— 'the root rad has the meaning of "to scratch" elsewhere, but here, because it is used in the sense of "to give", they gave the understanding that moves in many subjects; or, since the meaning of "scratching" is the same for the root rad, the Aśvin deities "scratched" (cleared away) Kakṣīvān's dull intellect, which has many objects, and thereby sharpened it — and he explains the sense: they made the intelligence quick in all the three times, past, present and future'; he cites the Ṛk 1-112-4 [as read] as quoted. In this matter Yāska says 'purandhir bahudhīḥ' (Ni. 6-13 [as read]) — purandhi is 'one who has many understandings'. Or: puraṃ pūrayitavyaṃ sarvaviṣayajātam asyāṃ dhīyate avasthāpyate iti purandhir buddhiḥ — 'what is to be filled up, the whole range of objects, is placed (dhīyate) in it: hence purandhi, understanding'. Yāska, explaining that the word purandhi conveys 'one who has much understanding', cites

अध्वर उक्थे यज्ञे श्रुष्टीभगं नासत्या पुरंधिम् । [as read; doubtful [?]] (ऋ. सं. २-४३-४? [as read])

adhvara ukthe yajñe śruṣṭībhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhim | [as read; doubtful [?]] (ṛ. saṃ. 2-43-4? [as read])

and says (Ni. 6-13) 'purandhiḥ bahudhīḥ'. From this Sāyaṇa explains: understanding that stands firm in all kinds of subjects; or, that which comprises all subjects. Besides this, Yāska has explained the word purandhi in another place —

original p. 218

पुरन्धिर्बहुधीस्तत्कः । पुरन्धिर्भगः पुरस्तात्तस्यान्नादेश इत्येकम् । इन्द्र इत्यपरं स बहुकर्मतमः पुरां च दारयितृतमः । वरुण इत्यपरं तं प्रज्ञया स्तौति ॥ (नि. ६-१३ [as read])

purandhirbahudhīstatkaḥ | purandhirbhagaḥ purastāttasyānnādeśa ityekam | indra ityaparaṃ sa bahukarmatamaḥ purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ | varuṇa ityaparaṃ taṃ prajñayā stauti ‖ (ni. 6-13 [as read])

— so he explains the word purandhi. "Here purandhi means 'one who has great understanding'. Since all deities have much understanding, who is the deity denoted by the word purandhi? Some say purandhi is Bhaga. Why? In the Ṛk

ता अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टीभगं नासत्या पुरंधिम् । (ऋ. सं. २-४३-४ [as read; [?]])

tā adhvara uśato yakṣyagne śruṣṭībhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhim | (ṛ. saṃ. 2-43-4 [as read; [?]])

— the purandhi standing in that place is an adjective of Bhaga, so some say that purandhi denotes the deity Bhaga. Some say the word purandhi denotes Indra: since dhīḥ is read among the names of karman (Ni. 2-1 as read [?]), purandhi means 'one who does many deeds' — more than other deities, he (Indra) is bahukarmatamaḥ; one who does such brave deeds, [so] the word purandhi denotes Indra. Or 'purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ' — since Indra destroyed the cities of asuras such as Śambara, some argue that purandhi is Indra. And some say purandhi is Varuṇa; for the word dhī signifies prajñā (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]); because men praise Varuṇa with their intellect (prajñayā) or his intellect pervades, therefore purandhi is Varuṇa — and to establish this matter, they cite

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.8)

अत्रेदमाख्यानम् । अत्रिमृषिमसुराः शतद्वारे पीडायन्त्रगृहे प्रवेश्य तुषाग्निनाबाधिषत । तदानीं तेन ऋषिना स्तुतावश्विनावग्निमुदकेनोपशमय्य तस्मात्पीडागृहादविकलेन्द्रियवर्गं सन्तं निरगमयतामिति । तदेतत्रेत्यादिना प्रतिपाद्यते । हे अश्विना युवां हिमेन हिमवच्छीतेनोदकेन घ्रंसं दीप्यमानमत्रेर्बाधनार्थमसुरैः प्रक्षिप्तं तुषाग्निमवारयेथाम् । युवां निवारितवन्तौ । शीतीकृतवन्तावित्यर्थः । अपि चास्मा असुरपीडया कार्श्यं प्राप्तायात्रये पितुमतीं । पितुरित्यन्ननाम । अन्नयुक्तामूर्जं बलप्रदं रसात्मकं क्षीरादिकमधत्तम् । पुष्ट्यर्थं प्रायच्छतम् । ऋबीसेऽपगतप्रकाशे पीडायन्त्रगृहेऽवनीतमवाङ्मुखतयासुरैः प्रापितमत्रिं सर्वगणम् । गणः समूहः । सर्वेषामिन्द्रियाणां पुत्रादीनां वा गणेनोपेतं स्वस्ति अविनाशो यथा भवति तथोन्निन्यथुः । तस्माद्गृहादुद्गमय्य युवां स्वगृहं प्रापितवन्तौ । यद्वा । हिमेन शीतेन वृष्ट्युदकेनाग्निवत्तीक्ष्णं घ्रंसं अहर्नामैतत् । सामर्थ्यात्रिदाघकालीनमहरवारयेथाम् । तस्माद्धर्मात्तीक्ष्णं निवारितवन्तौ । अपि चास्मा अग्नये पितुमतीं चरुपुरोडाशादिलक्षणान्नोपेतामूर्जं बलकरं रसात्मकमुपस्तरणाभिघारात्मकं घृतमधत्तम् । वृष्ट्युत्पादनेनाग्नेर्योगार्थं हवींषि निष्पादितवन्तावित्यर्थः । ऋबीसेऽपगततेजस्के पृथिवीद्रव्येऽवनीतोषधीनामुत्पादनायावस्थानीतम् । पार्थिवाग्निना परिपक्वा उदकेन क्लिन्ना ह्योषधिवनस्पतयो विरोहन्ति । अत्रिं हविषामत्तारमोषधिवनस्पत्यादीनां वा एवंविधमग्निं सर्वगणं व्रीहियवाद्योषधिगणोपेतं हे अश्विनौ युवां स्वस्ति अविनाशो यथा भवति तथोन्निन्यथुः । व्रीह्याद्योषधिवनस्पतिरूपेण भूमेरुपरिप्रापितवन्तौ । कारणात्मना पार्थिवाग्नौ वर्तमानं सर्वमोषधिवनस्पत्यादिकमश्विनौ प्रवर्षणेन व्यक्तीकृतवन्ताविस्यर्थः । अयं पक्षो यास्केन हिमेनोदकेनेत्यादिनोक्तः । नि. ६-३६ ॥ [grammatical tail: pitumatīm — pitu "food", matup with the udātta; ṛbīse — ṛbīsam apagatabhāsam … apacitabhāsam apahṛtabhāsam (Ni. 6-?? as read [?]); pṛṣodarādi; atrim — ad "to eat", adeḥ striṇ ca… tri; avanītam — gatir anantaraḥ, the prefix accent; svasti — as "to be", bhāve ktin, chandasy ubhayathā, sārvadhātukatvād asaḥ… bhūbhāvābhāvaḥ]

atredamākhyānam | atrimṛṣimasurāḥ śatadvāre pīḍāyantragṛhe praveśya tuṣāgninābādhiṣata | tadānīṃ tena ṛṣinā stutāvaśvināvagnimudakenopaśamayya tasmātpīḍāgṛhādavikalendriyavargaṃ santaṃ niragamayatāmiti | tadetatretyādinā pratipādyate | he aśvinā yuvāṃ himena himavacchītenodakena ghraṃsaṃ dīpyamānamatrerbādhanārthamasuraiḥ prakṣiptaṃ tuṣāgnimavārayethām | yuvāṃ nivāritavantau | śītīkṛtavantāvityarthaḥ | api cāsmā asurapīḍayā kārśyaṃ prāptāyātraye pitumatīṃ | piturityannanāma | annayuktāmūrjaṃ balapradaṃ rasātmakaṃ kṣīrādikamadhattam | puṣṭyarthaṃ prāyacchatam | ṛbīse 'pagataprakāśe pīḍāyantragṛhe 'vanītamavāṅmukhatayāsuraiḥ prāpitamatriṃ sarvagaṇam | gaṇaḥ samūhaḥ | sarveṣāmindriyāṇāṃ putrādīnāṃ vā gaṇenopetaṃ svasti avināśo yathā bhavati tathonninyathuḥ | tasmādgṛhādudgamayya yuvāṃ svagṛhaṃ prāpitavantau | yadvā | himena śītena vṛṣṭyudakenāgnivattīkṣṇaṃ ghraṃsaṃ aharnāmaitat | sāmarthyātridāghakālīnamaharavārayethām | tasmāddharmāttīkṣṇaṃ nivāritavantau | api cāsmā agnaye pitumatīṃ carupuroḍāśādilakṣaṇānnopetāmūrjaṃ balakaraṃ rasātmakamupastaraṇābhighārātmakaṃ ghṛtamadhattam | vṛṣṭyutpādanenāgneryogārthaṃ havīṃṣi niṣpāditavantāvityarthaḥ | ṛbīse 'pagatatejaske pṛthivīdravye 'vanītoṣadhīnāmutpādanāyāvasthānītam | pārthivāgninā paripakvā udakena klinnā hyoṣadhivanaspatayo virohanti | atriṃ haviṣāmattāramoṣadhivanaspatyādīnāṃ vā evaṃvidhamagniṃ sarvagaṇaṃ vrīhiyavādyoṣadhigaṇopetaṃ he aśvinau yuvāṃ svasti avināśo yathā bhavati tathonninyathuḥ | vrīhyādyoṣadhivanaspatirūpeṇa bhūmerupariprāpitavantau | kāraṇātmanā pārthivāgnau vartamānaṃ sarvamoṣadhivanaspatyādikamaśvinau pravarṣaṇena vyaktīkṛtavantāvisyarthaḥ | ayaṃ pakṣo yāskena himenodakenetyādinoktaḥ | ni. 6-36 ‖ [grammatical tail: pitumatīm — pitu "food", matup with the udātta; ṛbīse — ṛbīsam apagatabhāsam … apacitabhāsam apahṛtabhāsam (Ni. 6-?? as read [?]); pṛṣodarādi; atrim — ad "to eat", adeḥ striṇ ca… tri; avanītam — gatir anantaraḥ, the prefix accent; svasti — as "to be", bhāve ktin, chandasy ubhayathā, sārvadhātukatvād asaḥ… bhūbhāvābhāvaḥ]

Sense (mine): "Here this story. The Asuras, having put the ṛṣi Atri into a hundred-doored torture-chamber, hurt him with a fire of husks. Then, Atri having praised the Aśvins, they put out the fire with water and brought him out of that torture-house with all his sense-organs intact: this is what is set forth beginning hima. O Aśvins, with himena, with water cold like snow, you stopped the ghraṃsa, the blazing husk-fire thrown by the Asuras to torment Atri. You stopped it: cooled it. And for this man, emaciated by the Asuras' torment, for Atri, you adhattam, gave, pitumatīm — pitu is a name for food: [an ūrj, strength-giving, sap-natured substance, such as] milk, provided with food — to nourish him. Ṛbīse — in the lightless torture-chamber; avanītam — put in it by the Asuras head downward; Atri sarvagaṇam — gaṇa is a collection; endowed with the whole group of all his organs, or of his sons and so on — you unninyathuḥ, drew out, so that there would be welfare, imperishableness. Having taken him out of that house you brought him to his own house. Or: himena — with the water of rain, cold; ghraṃsa is a name for 'day': you kept off the day, sharp as fire, of the hot season — you stopped it, a sharp thing from the heat. And for this Agni (fire), you gave pitumatīm — [the ghee] with food, provided with oblations such as caru and purodāśa; ūrjam — strength-making, sap-natured ghee, in the form of the upastaraṇa and abhighāraṇa [layers of ghee in the sacrifice]; by causing rain you produced oblations for the union with Agni. In the ṛbīsa — the earth-substance from which the splendour is gone — you avanītam, placed, to produce herbs. Herbs and trees, ripened by the earthly fire and moistened by water, grow. O Aśvins, such an Agni — the eater (atri) of oblations, or of herbs, trees and the rest — sarvagaṇam, together with the whole group of herbs such as rice and barley, you brought up, so that there might be imperishableness; as rice and the other herbs and trees, you brought them to the surface of the earth: that is, all that was present in the earthly fire in the form of cause — herbs, trees and the rest — you made manifest by the downpour. This view is stated by Yāska in 'himenodakena' (Ni. 6-36 as read [?])."

original p. 222

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; ghraṃsam — blazing; agnim — fire (sent by the Asuras to harm Atri); himena — with cold water like snow; avārayethām — you put out (and also); asmai — to this (Atri, emaciated by the Asuras' torment); pitumatīm — endowed with food; ūrjam — strength-giving (milk and the like); adhattam — you gave (for nourishment); ṛbīse — in the torture-pit which was covered with darkness (by the Asuras); avanītam — thrown head down; atrim — Atri; sarvagaṇam — with all his senses [intact]; svasti — without any harm; unninyathuḥ — you raised up (and brought home)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"You put out with water cold as snow the blazing fire (sent by the Asuras to harm Atri), and gave to Atri, emaciated by the Asuras' torment, strength-giving milk and the like for nourishment; and you raised up the Atri who had been thrown head downward into the torture-pit of darkness, with all his limbs intact, and brought him home."

English Translation (as printed)

You quenched with cold (water) the blazing flames (that encompassed Atri) and supplied him with food-supported strength ; you extricated him, As'wins, from the dark (cavern) into which he had been thrown headlong, and restored him to every kind of welfare.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

हिमेन — Himena — "himavat śītena udakena": "with water that is cold like snow. Himena vṛṣṭyudakena: with rain-water. Ghraṃsam — dīpyamānam agnim: the burning fire, [which was] sharp and fierce; the word ghraṃsa is stated among the twelve names of day (ahar) (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]), and since the word is also read in the names of 'day', Sāyaṇa explains here that the meaning is 'day in the hot season'. The Asuras seized the ṛṣi named Atri and, to torment him, shut him in a house with many doors, a machine of torture, head downward, and cast him into a fire of husks (the fire of a kiln). By this the ṛṣi Atri, unable to bear the heat of the fire (his body burning), praised the Aśvin deities; they brought cold water like snow and saved the ṛṣi Atri: the Itihāsa is stated in this Ṛk by these words.

original p. 223

And in general: in the hot season, from the heat of the Sun, the days are made to burn with heat, [and when] the rain falls on the world these Aśvin deities make all comfortable — two kinds of meaning appear here. In Sāyaṇa's exposition both kinds of meaning, the ṛṣi Atri and Agni the fire, are explained."

हिमेन — Himena — "himaṃ punar hanter vā hinoter vā": "the word hima is derived from the root han, 'to kill', or from hinoti, 'to increase':

हिमं पुनर्हन्तेर्वा हिनोतेर्वा । अजरमजरणधर्माणमनर्ममप्रतृतमन्यस्मिन् यत्रेमानि सर्वाणि भूतान्यभिसंतिष्ठन्ते ॥ (नि. ४-१२ [as read; [?]])

himaṃ punarhantervā hinotervā | ajaramajaraṇadharmāṇamanarmamapratṛtamanyasmin yatremāni sarvāṇi bhūtānyabhisaṃtiṣṭhante ‖ (ni. 4-12 [as read; [?]])

— the word hima, from the root han 'to kill'; because in the cold season the herbs and trees are destroyed, so that in that season the leaves of the trees fall off and they become nearly dead, the word hima signifies 'killing', 'destroying'. And the other derivation, 'from hinoti', from the root hi 'to increase', Yāska's explanation says: in this cold season barley and other grains sprout and grow, so for the word hima the meaning 'satisfaction' may be given. Here the sense 'cold water' is to be taken. In the same way the word ghraṃsa too is read among the names of day (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]).

यो अस्मै घ्रंस उत वा य ऊधनि सोमं सुनोति भवति द्युमाँ अहः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ५-३४-५ [as read; [?]])

yo asmai ghraṃsa uta vā ya ūdhani somaṃ sunoti bhavati dyumā~ ahaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 5-34-5 [as read; [?]])

— in this Ṛk, the Nirukta-writer, as an example, says (Ni. 6-?? as read [?]) 'ghraṃsa ity ahar nāma | grasyate 'smin rasaḥ': the word ghraṃsa is a name of ahar, the day; since the waters (juices) are sucked up by it [in this season], the day gets the name ghraṃsa: the meaning is explained; and

यद्देवयन्तमवथः शचीभिः परि घ्रंसमोमना वां वयो गात् ॥ (ऋ. सं. २-३९-४? [as read; [?]])

yaddevayantamavathaḥ śacībhiḥ pari ghraṃsamomanā vāṃ vayo gāt ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 2-39-4? [as read; [?]])

— in this Ṛk too (Ni. 6-?? as read [?]) the word ghraṃsa is used as denoting day. And the Nirukta-writer, in explaining the meaning of the word ṛbīsa, cites this very Ṛk (Ni. 6-36 as read [?]): 'himenodakena grīṣmāṃśe agniṃ ghraṃsam ahar avārayethām' [= "in the hot season you checked the fire, the day, with water"]; bīsa [the explanation] — at the end of the hot season, you saved [us] from the difficulty of the day which, causing heat, draws out the water [— so he explains]."

original p. 224

Skandasvāmin —

हिममित्युदकनाम । वृष्टिलक्षणेनोदकेन । यत्रासुरैः प्रक्षिप्तं तमुग्निं घ्रंसं । घृ क्षरणदीप्त्योरित्यस्यायं क्रियाशब्दो न त्वहर्नाम ॥

himamityudakanāma | vṛṣṭilakṣaṇenodakena | yatrāsuraiḥ prakṣiptaṃ tamugniṃ ghraṃsaṃ | ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyorityasyāyaṃ kriyāśabdo na tvaharnāma ‖

— "Hima is a word for water: with water in the form of rain. The fire, ghraṃsa, cast by the Asuras in that place: the word ghraṃsa is a verb-word [i.e. derived from the root ghṛ, which means 'to flow' and 'to shine'] and is not a name of 'day'." For the word hima he gives the meaning 'water' — that is, rain-water. "The ṛṣi Atri, thrown by the Asuras into the fire, was made to suffer by the fire; the word ghraṃsa, derived from the root ghṛ with the senses of 'dripping' (kṣaraṇa) and 'shining' (dīpti, brilliance), is a word expressing an action; it is not the name of day: this is the meaning."

"The word pitu is stated among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]). 'pituḥ — annanāma'; 'pāteḥ vā pibater vā pyāyater vā' (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]): the word pitu denotes food. Since Yāska explains that this word is derived either from the root pā 'to protect', or from the root pā with the sense 'to drink', or from the root pyāyī 'to increase', 'to grow' — it is explained that, by [the sentence] 'the Aśvins gave to Atri, afflicted by the fire, food and strength-giving milk etc. that make for growth', they gave food in the form of caru and purodāśa for Agni and ghee and milk, liquid and oily substances, for the sacrifice to Agni, so that [it] may increase, by causing rain — thus pitumatīm ūrjam asmā adhattam is explained."

ऋबीसे — Ṛbīse — "apagatatejaske apagataprakāśe pīḍāyantragṛhe": "in the house of torture-machines, 'in the dark, without light, which has no connection with brilliance' — so Sāyaṇa. The Nirukta-writer: 'ṛbīsam bīsam ṛbīsam apagatabhāsam apahṛtabhāsam apahitabhāsam gatabhāsam vā' (Ni. 6-36 as read [?]) — the word ṛbīsa is used in the sense of 'devoid of lustre (black), or full of darkness'. It denotes the earth, he says. Citing this very Ṛk, 'himenāgnim':

हिमेनोदकेन ग्रीष्मान्ते अग्निं घ्रंसमहरवारयेथामन्वतीं चास्मा ऊर्जमधत्तमग्नये योऽयमृबीसे पृथिव्यामग्निरंतरौषधिवनस्पतिषु । तमुन्निन्यथुः सर्वगणं सर्वनामानं गणो गणाद्गुणश्च । यद्वृप्ताः ओषधय उद्यन्ति प्राणिनश्च पृथिव्यां तदश्विनो रूपं तेनैशा स्तौति ॥ (नि. ६-३६ [as read; the Sanskrit is small type, partly doubtful [?]])

himenodakena grīṣmānte agniṃ ghraṃsamaharavārayethāmanvatīṃ cāsmā ūrjamadhattamagnaye yo 'yamṛbīse pṛthivyāmagniraṃtarauṣadhivanaspatiṣu | tamunninyathuḥ sarvagaṇaṃ sarvanāmānaṃ gaṇo gaṇādguṇaśca | yadvṛptāḥ oṣadhaya udyanti prāṇinaśca pṛthivyāṃ tadaśvino rūpaṃ tenaiśā stauti ‖ (ni. 6-36 [as read; the Sanskrit is small type, partly doubtful [?]])

— the Aśvin deities, at the end of the summer season, created rain so that the heat from fire should not be a hindrance to the days, and thereby made conditions favourable for the sacrifices in which oblations pleasing to Agni may be got. Plants and trees, which ripen [by fire] from the branch, and which are in the inner part of the earth, in these, as well as in water, they make the fire (denoted by all words) manifest;

original p. 225

[and] because they brought up the seeds in the earth, they made the herbs and creatures to be produced. 'The Aśvin deities, who have such greatness, are praised here as being in the forms that bring such effects' — thus the explanation of the sense."

सर्वगणम् — Sarvagaṇam — "in the sense of Atri the word sarvagaṇa means one furnished with all organs and with sons and grandsons. In the sense of Agni: the fire, ripening, through the earthly fire, the seeds sown in the earth, makes the herbs and trees grow; as Agni devours them in the form of oblations, it is joined with the group of herbs such as rice."

स्वस्ति — Svasti — "avināśo yathā bhavati tathā": "Sāyaṇa explains it as an adverbial qualifier of the action: 'so that there is no destruction — so that in an excellent way, equal, without any calamity'. The word svasti is said (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]) 'svastīty avināśināma asti rabhisūjyate su asti'; 'the meaning is "not liable to destruction". In this word the two words su + asti are combined, and asti is in the sense of "worship"' — so the Nirukta-writer explains. This word is used in this same meaning in many places —

स नः पितेव सूनवेऽग्ने सूपायनो भव । सचस्वा नः स्वस्तये ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१-९ [as read])

sa naḥ piteva sūnave 'gne sūpāyano bhava | sacasvā naḥ svastaye ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-1-9 [as read])

— here svastaye means 'for our welfare'. And pathyā svastiḥ panthā āntarikṣaṃ tannivāsāt (Ni. 11-?? as read [?]), stating the word svasti —

स्वस्तिरिद्धि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्णस्वत्यभि या वाममेति । सा नो अमा सो अरणे नि पातु स्वावेशा भवतु देवगोपा ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-६३-१६ [as read])

svastiriddhi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇasvatyabhi yā vāmameti | sā no amā so araṇe ni pātu svāveśā bhavatu devagopā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-63-16 [as read])

he cites this Ṛk, and

स्वस्तिरेव हि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्णस्वती … धनवत्यभ्येति यो वसूनि वनवीयानि सा … देवीगोप्री देवान् गोपायिष्यति देवा एनां गोपायन्तीति वा ॥ (नि. ११-४१ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]])

svastireva hi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇasvatī … dhanavatyabhyeti yo vasūni vanavīyāni sā … devīgoprī devān gopāyiṣyati devā enāṃ gopāyantīti vā ‖ (ni. 11-41 [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]])

original p. 226

— explaining the greatness of svasti: 'svasti is that which is in the atmosphere; more praiseworthy than all deities; possessing wealth; bestowing water. May she give protection to those who dwell in the forest and in the house, both outside and inside the house; may this shining goddess protect the deities, and the deities protect her; or may she protect us who offer oblations; or may the rays in the heavenly region protect her' — so he explains.

"Skandasvāmin —

स्वस्ति अन्तर्णीतमत्वर्थोऽत्र स्वस्तिशब्दः । स्वस्तिमतं अविनष्टं जीवन्तमित्यर्थः ॥

svasti antarṇītamatvartho 'tra svastiśabdaḥ | svastimataṃ avinaṣṭaṃ jīvantamityarthaḥ ‖

— since the word svasti is used here in the sense of 'impelling' (preraṇa), the sense is that, as though [he were] a living thing, the Aśvin deities protected the ṛṣi Atri; thus Kutsa too speaks:

याभिः कुत्सं श्रुतर्यं नर्यमावतं [?] … [as printed:] याभिः शुचन्तिं धनसां सुषंसदं तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावन्तमत्रये । याभिः पृश्निगुं पुरुकुत्समावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१६ [as read])

yābhiḥ kutsaṃ śrutaryaṃ naryamāvataṃ [?] … [as printed:] yābhiḥ śucantiṃ dhanasāṃ suṣaṃsadaṃ taptaṃ gharmamomyāvantamatraye | yābhiḥ pṛśniguṃ purukutsamāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-16 [as read])

— he cites this Ṛk."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly)

agnim (agi "to go"; aṅgeḥ nalopaś ca, Uṇ. 4-?? as read [?], the suffix ni; since it is it, the num augment, then its elision; the accent from the suffix on the last syllable); avārayethām (vṛñ "to cover, to ward off"; prayojakavyāpāre — hetumati ca, Pā. 3-1-26 as read [?], ṇic; aco ñṇiti, Pā. 7-2-115 as read [?], vṛddhi of the root's ṛ because of the ṇic; after the ṇyanta, laṅ 2nd dual āthām; śap; guṇa of the ṇic; ay; āto ṅitaḥ, Pā. 7-2-81 as read [?], iya for the ā of āthām; the augment aṭ; nighāta); pitumatīm (pituḥ asyāsti iti pitumatī — pitu means food; tad asyāsty asmin, Pā. 5-2-94 as read [?], matup; in the feminine ugitaś ca, Pā. 4-1-6 as read [?], ṅīp; hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup, Pā. 6-1-176 as read [?], matup takes udātta).

Grammar page of Ṛk 8, concluded (noted briefly): adhattam (ḍudhāñ "to hold, to nourish"; laṅ 2nd dual; nighāta after an accented word); ṛbīse (Yāska explains this word: 'ṛbīsam abīsam apagatabhāsam apacitabhāsam apahṛtabhāsam gatabhāsaṃ vā' (Ni. 6-36 as read [?]) — the sense being "without brilliance"; the desired form and accent are accomplished by pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam, Pā. 6-3-109 as read [?]); atrim (ad "to eat"; the suffix tri by the Uṇādi sūtra ader ṇic ca… [as printed: ādeśrinicaḥ, Uṇ. 4-?? as read [?]] with the word ca); avanītam (ṇīñ "to carry"; kta by niṣṭhā, Pā. 3-2-102 as read [?]; gatir anantaraḥ, Pā. 6-2-49 as read [?], the prefix ava keeps its accent); unninyathuḥ (ṇīñ "to carry", liṭ 2nd dual; nighāta); sarvagaṇam (sarve gaṇā yasya saḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam, Pā. 6-2-1 as read [?]; the first member keeps its accent); svasti (as "to be", adādi; striyāṃ ktin, Pā. 3-3-94 as read [?], ktin in the abstract sense; chandasy ubhayathā, Pā. 3-4-117 as read [?], so it is sārvadhātuka, hence bhū substitution does not arise by aster bhūḥ, Pā. 2-4-52 as read [?]; nañsubhyām, Pā. 6-2-172 as read [?], final accent). ‖ 8 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.9)

परावतं नासत्यानुदेथामुच्चाबुध्नं चक्रथुर्जिह्मबारम् । क्षरन्नापो न पायनाय राये सहस्राय तृष्यते गोतमस्य ॥ ९ ॥

parāvataṃ nāsatyānudethāmuccābudhnaṃ cakrathurjihmabāram | kṣarannāpo na pāyanāya rāye sahasrāya tṛṣyate gotamasya ‖ 9 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.9)

परा । अवतम् । नासत्या । अनुदेथाम् । उच्चाऽबुध्नम् । चक्रथुः । जिह्मऽबारम् । क्षरन् । आपः । न । पायनाय । राये । सहस्राय । तृष्यते । गोतमस्य ॥ ९ ॥

parā | avatam | nāsatyā | anudethām | uccā 'budhnam | cakrathuḥ | jihma 'bāram | kṣaran | āpaḥ | na | pāyanāya | rāye | sahasrāya | tṛṣyate | gotamasya ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.9)

अत्रेदमाख्यानम् । कदाचिन्मरुभूमौ वर्तमानस्य स्तोतुर्गोतमस्य ऋषेः समीपं देशान्तरे वर्तमानं कूपमुत्थाप्याश्विनौ प्रापयेताम् । प्रापय्य च तं कूपं स्नानपानादिसौकर्ययोपरिमूलमधोबिलमवास्थापयेतामिति । तदेतदाह । हे नासत्या सत्यस्वभावौ सत्यस्य नेतारौ नासिकाप्रभवौ वाश्विनौ युवामवतं कूपं नामैतत् । अनस्त्रातं कूपं परानुदेथाम् । गोतमस्य ऋषेः समीपे प्रेरितवन्तौ । तदनन्तरं तं कूपमुच्चाबुध्नम् । उच्चैरुपरिष्टाद्बुध्नो मूलं यस्य स तथोक्तः । जिह्मबारम् । जिह्ममधस्ताद्वर्तमानतया वक्रं बारं द्वारं यस्य स तथोक्तः । एवंगुणविशिष्टं चक्रथुः । युवामकृषाथाम् । तस्मात्तृप्यते पिपासतो गोतमस्य पायनाय पानार्थमापो न आपस्त्व [?] । अयं नकारश्चार्थे । क्षरन् । प्रवाहरूपेण निरगमन् । कीदृशस्य । रायै । हविंषि दत्तवतः । सहस्राय सहनशीलाय । यद्वा । सहस्रसंख्याकाय । रायै धनाय । एतत्सङ्ख्यधनलाभार्थं चाक्षरन् ॥ अनुदेथाम् । णुद प्रेरणे । तौदादिकः । जिह्मबारम् । द्वारशब्दस्य पृषोदरादित्वाद्वारादेशः । क्षरन् । क्षर सञ्चलने । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङो लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः । पायनाय । हेतुमति णिच् । शाच्छासाह्वेति युक् । भावे ल्युट् । राये । रा दाने । राति ददातीति रैः । रातेर्दैः । उ. २-६६ । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । तृष्यते । ञित्रृषा पिपासायाम् । क्यन् । लटः शतृ । कृषो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी वक्तव्या । पा. २-३-६२-१ । इति चतुर्थी ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

atredamākhyānam | kadācinmarubhūmau vartamānasya stoturgotamasya ṛṣeḥ samīpaṃ deśāntare vartamānaṃ kūpamutthāpyāśvinau prāpayetām | prāpayya ca taṃ kūpaṃ snānapānādisaukaryayoparimūlamadhobilamavāsthāpayetāmiti | tadetadāha | he nāsatyā satyasvabhāvau satyasya netārau nāsikāprabhavau vāśvinau yuvāmavataṃ kūpaṃ nāmaitat | anastrātaṃ kūpaṃ parānudethām | gotamasya ṛṣeḥ samīpe preritavantau | tadanantaraṃ taṃ kūpamuccābudhnam | uccairupariṣṭādbudhno mūlaṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ | jihmabāram | jihmamadhastādvartamānatayā vakraṃ bāraṃ dvāraṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ cakrathuḥ | yuvāmakṛṣāthām | tasmāttṛpyate pipāsato gotamasya pāyanāya pānārthamāpo na āpastva [?] | ayaṃ nakāraścārthe | kṣaran | pravāharūpeṇa niragaman | kīdṛśasya | rāyai | haviṃṣi dattavataḥ | sahasrāya sahanaśīlāya | yadvā | sahasrasaṃkhyākāya | rāyai dhanāya | etatsaṅkhyadhanalābhārthaṃ cākṣaran ‖ anudethām | ṇuda preraṇe | taudādikaḥ | jihmabāram | dvāraśabdasya pṛṣodarāditvādvārādeśaḥ | kṣaran | kṣara sañcalane | bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge 'pītyaḍabhāvaḥ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | tiṅo lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ | pāyanāya | hetumati ṇic | śācchāsāhveti yuk | bhāve lyuṭ | rāye | rā dāne | rāti dadātīti raiḥ | rāterdaiḥ | u. 2-66 | ūḍidamiti vibhakterudāttatvam | tṛṣyate | ñitrṛṣā pipāsāyām | kyan | laṭaḥ śatṛ | kṛṣo nittvādādyudāttatvam | ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī vaktavyā | pā. 2-3-62-1 | iti caturthī ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Here this story. Once, the praising ṛṣi Gotama was in a desert; the Aśvins, having lifted up a well that was in another country, brought it near him; and having brought it, they set it with its root above and its opening (bila) below, for ease of bathing, drinking and so on. This is said: O Nāsatyas — of true nature, leaders of the truth, or born from the nose — you avatam, the well (avata is a word for 'well'), [that was] unbathed (unused), parā anudethām — you drove (it) near the ṛṣi Gotama. After that you made the well uccābudhnam — its budhna, root (bottom), standing upward high; jihmabāram — whose bāra (door), because it lies below, is crooked (jihma): endowed with such qualities you made it. Therefore the waters (āpaḥ), for the pāyanāya, drinking, of the thirsty (tṛṣyate) Gotama, kṣaran, streamed out in the form of a flow. [For] what sort of man? Rāye — who has given oblations; sahasrāya — patient; or: [the man] for [receiving] a thousand [in number]; rāye — wealth: and they flowed for the obtaining of wealth of such number."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he nāsatyā — O Aśvin deities, of true nature (born from the nose); avatam — the well (that was to come); parā — [you drove it] to the neighbourhood (of Gotama); anudethām — you impelled (that well, after the father [?]); uccābudhnam — with the root (bottom) turned upward; jihmabāram — with the mouth turned downward [= curved]; cakrathuḥ — you made; rāye — to one who gave oblations; sahasrāya — patient; tṛṣyate — thirsty; gotamasya — for Gotama; pāyanāya — for drinking; āpaḥ na — water also; kṣaran — you made to flow."

original p. 229

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Nāsatyas, you brought the well near Gotama, you made its bottom upward and its mouth downward, and you made the water flow so that Gotama, who offers oblations, who is patient, who is thirsty, could drink."

English Translation (as printed)

Nasatyas, you raised up the well, and made the base, which had been turned upwards, the curved mouth so that the water issued for the beverage of the thirsty Gotama, the offerer.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

नासत्या — Nāsatyā — "satyasvabhāvau": "those who always speak the truth, and lead along the true path, or the Aśvin deities who were born from the nostril when the Āditya was in the form of a horse — thus the sense. The Nirukta-writer: 'satyāv eva nāsatyāv ity aurṇavābhaḥ | satyasya praṇetārāv ity āgrāyaṇaḥ | nāsikāprabhavau babhūvatur iti vā' (Ni. 6-13 as read [?]) — Sāyaṇa explains the word nāsatya in the very manner that [the Nirukta] states."

अवतम् — Avatam — "since the word avata is stated among the fourteen [as read] names of well (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), it means well."

उच्चाबुध्नम् — Uccābudhnam — "uccair upariṣṭād budhno mūlaṃ yasya saḥ: one whose root (bottom) is above, high — 'whose base part is on the upper side' (that is, as if turned head downward, the bottom of the well is turned upward)."

original p. 230

जिह्मबारम् — Jihmabāram — "jihmam adhastād vartamānatayā vakraṃ bāraṃ dvāraṃ yasya saḥ": "the word jihma is not used here in the sense 'crooked' or 'bent'; the meaning is 'with the mouth turned downward' (i.e. 'the mouth of the well lies beneath'). A ṛṣi named Gautama (sic; = Gotama), greatly afflicted by thirst, searched for water to drink in a desert, and, not finding it, prayed to the Aśvin deities for water. They brought him a well filled with water and made the bottom of the well [be] upward, and the upper part of the well, where the water is, downward, so that the ṛṣi could drink the water with a vessel: thus the Itihāsa tells that his thirst was removed. This is here set out. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-?-? [numerals partly illegible [?]] it is said that the Marut deities brought the well to Gautama's neighbourhood and quenched his thirst."

आपो न — Āpo na — "āpaś ca — the na here is in the sense of 'and' (ca), the ca being in the sense of 'together'. Sāyaṇa explains that the Aśvin deities made the water easy to come by for Gotama to drink and for him to get a thousand (in number) of wealth for the performance of sacrifices and so on. Skandasvāmin: in the expression na rāye sahasrāya [sic] ... the word na is in the sense of simile (upamārthīya): 'as though a thousand (in number) of wealth', the word na denotes a figurative sense (upacāra) here, but according to the force of words it is used here only in the sense of comparison: 'as if with a thousand pieces of wealth, as the Aśvins favoured him to perform sacrifices, so, to remove his thirst, they brought a well (made it with the bottom upward) and made water for him to drink by a vessel from the well'."

Sense (mine): "… yuvānam santam kanīnām, [who was] made a young man, you made pati, husband (supporter), of the kanīnām, maidens. [As to the kaṇīnām explanation, the Sanskrit tail is compressed.]" The first sentence of this bhāṣya, begun on p. 232, was: "Here this story. The ṛṣi named Cyavana, whose limbs were aged, full of wrinkles and grey hair, deserted by his sons and others, praised the Aśvins; being praised, they removed the old age of that ṛṣi and made him young again. This is what is said: O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, from the aged Cyavana — the ṛṣi called Cyavana — the vavri, the dark covering of the body, [that is] the old age, you pra amuñcatam, released completely. An illustration: as one wearing a mail-coat covering the whole body, then discards it; and O Dasras — the two beautiful ones named Dasra — you prātiratam, increased, the āyuḥ, life, of the ṛṣi deserted by sons and others; and immediately you made him, now young,... husband of maidens."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; jujuruṣaḥ — of the aged; cyavānāt — from the ṛṣi named Cyavana; vavrim — the old age that covers the whole body — [the thing that was] a black covering; drāpim iva — as a coat of mail is taken off; pra amuñcatam — you released; uta — and; he dasrā — O Dasras (of beautiful form); jahitasya — [of the ṛṣi] deserted by sons and others; āyuḥ — life; prātiratam — you increased; āt it — immediately (after the attainment of youth); kanīnām — of young girls; patim — as husband; akṛṇutam — you made."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Nāsatyas, Dasras, you took off the old age that covered the body of the aged ṛṣi Cyavana, as one removes a coat of mail; you increased the life of him deserted by sons and others, and after he had regained youth you made him a husband of young girls."

English Translation (as printed)

Nasatyas, you stripped off from the aged Chyavana his entire skin, as if it had been a coat of mail ; you reversed, Dasras, life of the sage who was without kindred, and constituted him the husband of many maidens.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

द्रापिमिव वव्रिं प्रामुञ्चतम् — Drāpim iva vavriṃ prāmuñcatam — "drāpir iti kavacasyākhyā | yathā kaścit kavacaṃ kṛtsna-śarīra-vyāpakaṃ dhṛtvā paścāt śarīrāt pṛthak karoti tadvat": "drāpi is the name of a coat of mail. Like one who, wearing a coat of mail that covers the whole body, afterwards removes it from the body, the ṛṣi Cyavana took off old age from his body. The ṛṣi named Cyavana was an old man

original p. 234

— his body was full of white hair and wrinkles and the like; so his sons and others abandoned him. Then the ṛṣi Cyavana praised the Aśvin deities with stotras, pleased them, and, having got rid of old age through them, attained youth: this is the Itihāsa told in this Ṛk. Skandasvāmin has told this Itihāsa differently. This story is found in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.

अत्र शतपथे (श. ब्रा. ४-१-५) अधीतमितिहासमाचक्षते । शर्यातो नाम राजा सङ्क्रीडद्भिः कृतापराधाय कुपिताय जीर्णाय च्यवनाय प्रत्याप्त्यर्थं सुकन्यां नाम कन्यां दुहितरं ददौ । तां तत्रासीनां दृष्ट्वाऽश्विनौ पुनः पुनरूचतुः । किं किं जीर्णेनाकृतरूपं कामयसे । आवाम् सम्भजेति । सा तौ प्रत्युवाच । यस्मै मां पिता आदात्, नाहं तं जीवन्तं हास्यामीति । तद्वैज्जर्णित्वा सुकन्यामुवाच । यदि त्वामेतौ पुनरेवं ब्रूयातां तयोस्त्वमेनं प्रतिब्रूयाः । असर्वा वसुसम्पद्धा सन्तौ पतिं मे निन्दथ इति । तौ यदि त्वां प्रति ब्रूयातां केनासर्वौ वसुसमृद्धौ चेति तत एनौ प्रतिब्रूयाः । पतिं मे पुनर्युवानं कुरुतं । अथ वां वक्ष्यामीति । सा तथोक्ता चैतामश्विनौ प्रत्यूचतुः । एतं ह्रदमवतरतु । अशो यत् कामयते तेन वयसा युक्त उत्तरिष्यतीति । स ऋषिस्तं ह्रदमवतीर्योत्तत्तारेति … तदेतदितिहासेनोच्यते जुजुरुषो नासत्येत्यादिना । (श. ब्रा. ४-१-५ [as read; the first words and the numerals are in small type, partly doubtful [?]])

atra śatapathe (śa. brā. 4-1-5) adhītamitihāsamācakṣate | śaryāto nāma rājā saṅkrīḍadbhiḥ kṛtāparādhāya kupitāya jīrṇāya cyavanāya pratyāptyarthaṃ sukanyāṃ nāma kanyāṃ duhitaraṃ dadau | tāṃ tatrāsīnāṃ dṛṣṭvā 'śvinau punaḥ punarūcatuḥ | kiṃ kiṃ jīrṇenākṛtarūpaṃ kāmayase | āvām sambhajeti | sā tau pratyuvāca | yasmai māṃ pitā ādāt, nāhaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ hāsyāmīti | tadvaijjarṇitvā sukanyāmuvāca | yadi tvāmetau punarevaṃ brūyātāṃ tayostvamenaṃ pratibrūyāḥ | asarvā vasusampaddhā santau patiṃ me nindatha iti | tau yadi tvāṃ prati brūyātāṃ kenāsarvau vasusamṛddhau ceti tata enau pratibrūyāḥ | patiṃ me punaryuvānaṃ kurutaṃ | atha vāṃ vakṣyāmīti | sā tathoktā caitāmaśvinau pratyūcatuḥ | etaṃ hradamavataratu | aśo yat kāmayate tena vayasā yukta uttariṣyatīti | sa ṛṣistaṃ hradamavatīryottattāreti … tadetaditihāsenocyate jujuruṣo nāsatyetyādinā | (śa. brā. 4-1-5 [as read; the first words and the numerals are in small type, partly doubtful [?]])

— "a king named Śaryāti, because the sons [of his] when playing had committed an offence against the angry, aged Cyavana, to propitiate Cyavana gave him his own daughter, a maiden named Sukanyā. The Aśvin deities, seeing her seated there, asked her again and again: 'What do you want of this old man, who is [past] all form? Take us [as husbands].' She answered: 'To whom my father gave me, I shall not abandon him while he lives.' Cyavana heard it, and told Sukanyā: 'If these two say that to you again, answer them: "You, being without wealth [and] not whole, find fault with my husband."' [And] if they ask you 'how are we not whole, and how wealth-complete?', then answer them: 'Make my husband young again; then I shall tell you.' As she was thus told, she told the Aśvins so. They said: 'Let him enter this pool; he will come out with the age he desires.' The ṛṣi entered the pool and came out [young]. This is stated in the Itihāsa by 'jujuruṣo nāsatyā' and so on.

"The king named Śaryāti, because his sons were wandering about, [taking them to have given offence], gave his daughter Sukanyā to the old ṛṣi Cyavana, angered, in marriage. While that Sukanyā was in the hermitage of the ṛṣi Cyavana, the Aśvin deities came there and, saying 'Abandon this old husband and marry us', spoke to her many times; she replied: 'My father gave me to this ṛṣi. I shall not abandon him as long as he lives.' The ṛṣi Cyavana heard it and, when they asked her again, instructed her: 'When you are asked in this manner, what is the reason you reproach my husband, when you are rich in wealth? — ask them in return how they are. Then they will answer you how they are rich in wealth. Then say: "Give my husband youth; afterwards I shall answer you."' Sukanyā spoke with the Aśvin deities as the ṛṣi Cyavana had taught. They told her: 'If your husband bathes in this pool, your wish will be fulfilled. Your husband will become youthful.' Hearing what the Aśvin deities said, he bathed in that pool and came up a youth."

original p. 235

वव्रिम् — Vavrim — "the word vavri is stated among the sixteen names of form (rūpa), 'nirṇik', 'varṇa' and so on (Ni. 3-13 as read [?]). Vavriḥ rūpanāma (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]): vṛṇoti iti sa saṃ — it covers its own form: that is the sense (of 'something that conceals')."

दस्रा — Dasrā — "etatsaṃjñau darśanīyau vāśvinau": "the persons famed by the name dasra — the Aśvin deities, whose form is beautiful —

युवं वृकेणाश्विना वपन्तेषं दुहन्ता मनुषाय दस्रा । अभि दस्युं बकुरेणा धमन्तोरु ज्योतिश्चक्रथुरार्याय ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११७-२१ [as read])

yuvaṃ vṛkeṇāśvinā vapanteṣaṃ duhantā manuṣāya dasrā | abhi dasyuṃ bakureṇā dhamantoru jyotiścakrathurāryāya ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-117-21 [as read])

in this Ṛk the word dasrā is used in the sense of the Aśvin deities. Dasrā = 'śatrūṇāṃ dāsayitārau daṃsayitārau vā karmāṇāṃ kṛṣyādīnāṃ kārayitārau vā varṣādyanugraheṇa — the destroyers of enemies, the doers of work, ... [the Sanskrit here is small type, partly doubtful [?]]'."

original p. 236

"… destroyers of enemies, or those who cause them to be destroyed, or those who perform works such as agriculture, favouring them with rain: so the meaning."

आयुः — Āyuḥ — "jīvanam": "the Aśvin deities favoured the ṛṣi Cyavana with the state of living in health (together with breath). Since the word āyus is stated among the twenty-eight [as read] names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]), the meaning may also be 'food'."

आत् + इत् — Āt + it — "anantaram eva": "the particles āt and it are used here in the sense of 'immediately afterwards'.

यदेदयुक्त हरितः सधस्थादाद्रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११५-४)

yadedayukta haritaḥ sadhasthādādrātrī vāsastanute simasmai ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-115-4)

— in this Ṛk (1-115-4) āt is used in the sense of atha ('then'). The ṛṣi Cyavana, when he entered the pool, [as an old man] arose from it afterwards a youth: this is the meaning."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.11)

अत्रेदमाख्यानम् । वन्दनो नाम कश्चिदृषिः । स चासुरैः कूपे निखाते उत्तरीतुमशक्नुवन्नश्विनावस्तौत् । तमश्विनौ कूपादुन्निन्यतुरिति । तदाह । नरारोगृस्य [?] नेतारौ हे नासत्यावश्विनौ वां युवयोः सम्बन्धि अभिष्टिमदभ्येषणयुक्तमभिमुख्येन प्राप्तव्यं तथा वरूथं वरणीयं कामयितव्यं तत्कर्म शंस्यम् । अस्माभिः प्रशंसनीयं । राध्यम् । आराधनीयं च । किं पुनस्तत्कर्म । विद्वांसा जानन्तौ युवां निधिमिव निक्षिप्तं धनमिवापगूळ्हम् अरण्ये निर्जने देशे कूपमध्येऽसुरैर्निगूढं वन्दनाय वन्दनमृषिं दर्शतात् । दर्शनीयाद्दर्श्यात् [?] पिपासुभिर्दृप्स्वात्मकूपादुदूपथुः । उदहार्ष्टम् । एवं यदेतत्कर्मकूपाद्धरणं तदित्यर्थः ॥ शंस्यम् । शन्सु स्तुतौ । अस्माण्यन्तादचोयदिति यत् । यकोनावितयादिउदात्तत्वम् । अभिष्टिमत् । अभिपूर्वादिषगतावित्यस्माद्भावे क्तिन् । मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः इत्यादिना क्तिन उदात्तत्वम् ।… कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेणैव स एव शिष्यते । शकन्ध्वादित्वात्पररूपत्वम् । तादौ चेति तु गतिस्वरस्य सर्वविधीनां छन्दसि विकल्पितत्वादप्रवृत्तिः । ततो मतुप् । अन्तोदात्तादुत्तरस्य तस्य ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यामित्यादात्तत्वम् । वरूथम् । वृञ्ज्याभ्यामूथन् । उ. २-६ । विद्वांसा । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । अपगूळ्हम् । गुहू संवरणे । कर्मणि निष्ठा । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । ढत्वधत्वष्टुत्वढलोपदीर्घाः । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । दर्शतात् । भृमृदृशीत्यादिनातच् । ऊपथुः । डुवप् बीजसन्तानेसन्ताने । लिट्यथुसि यजादित्वात्सम्प्रसारणम् । द्विर्वचनादि । वन्दनाय । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः सम्प्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थी ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

atredamākhyānam | vandano nāma kaścidṛṣiḥ | sa cāsuraiḥ kūpe nikhāte uttarītumaśaknuvannaśvināvastaut | tamaśvinau kūpādunninyaturiti | tadāha | narārogṛsya [?] netārau he nāsatyāvaśvinau vāṃ yuvayoḥ sambandhi abhiṣṭimadabhyeṣaṇayuktamabhimukhyena prāptavyaṃ tathā varūthaṃ varaṇīyaṃ kāmayitavyaṃ tatkarma śaṃsyam | asmābhiḥ praśaṃsanīyaṃ | rādhyam | ārādhanīyaṃ ca | kiṃ punastatkarma | vidvāṃsā jānantau yuvāṃ nidhimiva nikṣiptaṃ dhanamivāpagūḷham araṇye nirjane deśe kūpamadhye 'surairnigūḍhaṃ vandanāya vandanamṛṣiṃ darśatāt | darśanīyāddarśyāt [?] pipāsubhirdṛpsvātmakūpādudūpathuḥ | udahārṣṭam | evaṃ yadetatkarmakūpāddharaṇaṃ tadityarthaḥ ‖ śaṃsyam | śansu stutau | asmāṇyantādacoyaditi yat | yakonāvitayādiudāttatvam | abhiṣṭimat | abhipūrvādiṣagatāvityasmādbhāve ktin | mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ ityādinā ktina udāttatvam |… kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇaiva sa eva śiṣyate | śakandhvāditvātpararūpatvam | tādau ceti tu gatisvarasya sarvavidhīnāṃ chandasi vikalpitatvādapravṛttiḥ | tato matup | antodāttāduttarasya tasya hrasvanuḍbhyāmityādāttatvam | varūtham | vṛñjyābhyāmūthan | u. 2-6 | vidvāṃsā | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterākāraḥ | apagūḷham | guhū saṃvaraṇe | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | ḍhatvadhatvaṣṭutvaḍhalopadīrghāḥ | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | darśatāt | bhṛmṛdṛśītyādinātac | ūpathuḥ | ḍuvap bījasantānesantāne | liṭyathusi yajāditvātsamprasāraṇam | dvirvacanādi | vandanāya | kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyamiti karmaṇaḥ sampradānatvāccaturthī ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Here this story. A certain ṛṣi named Vandana, when the Asuras had dug a well [and put him in it] and he could not get out, praised the Aśvins; the Aśvins drew him up out of the well. This is said: O leaders (narā), Nāsatyas, Aśvins, that deed of yours — abhiṣṭimat (accompanied by help), to be attained by effort, and varūtham, to be chosen, desirable — is śaṃsyam, praiseworthy by us, and rādhyam, to be propitiated. What was that deed? Knowing, vidvāṃsā, you ūpathuḥ — drew up — nidhim iva apagūḍham, like a treasure hidden, [the ṛṣi] hidden by the Asuras in a lonely place in the forest, in the middle of a well, vandanāya — Vandana the ṛṣi — darśatāt — from the visible, from the self-made well by the thirsty, [from] the well: that is, the very act of raising him from the well. …"

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) on p. 239

original p. 239

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"narā — O leader Aśvin deities; vidvāṃsā — knowing (the circumstance); nidhim iva — like treasure (hidden); apagūḷham — (hidden in the well); vandanāya — the ṛṣi named Vandana; darśatāt — from the well which was visible (to travellers); ut ūpathuḥ — you raised up (and); yat — which exploit; tat vām — that of yours; abhiṣṭimat — to be attained by us; varūtham — worth desiring; śaṃsyam — worthy of praise; rādhyam ca — and to be adored."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O leader Aśvin deities, you, knowing, drew up and saved Vandana, hidden like a treasure in a well in the lonely place the Asuras chose, from the well visible to all; we have learned it. As this matter gives us joy, we praise it with respect."

English Translation (as printed)

Nasatyas, leaders, glorious was that exploit of yours, one to be celebrated, to be adored, to be desired by us, when, becoming aware (of the circumstance), you extricated Vandana, (hidden), like a concealed treasure, from the (well) that was visible (to travellers)

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

निधिमिवापगूळ्हम् — Nidhim ivāpagūḷham — "nidhim iva nikṣiptaṃ dhanam iva araṇye nirjane deśe kūpamadhye 'suraiḥ nigūḍham": "the Asuras threw a ṛṣi named Vandana into a well in a lonely place in the middle of a forest. From there he praised the Aśvin deities. They, who protect those who praise them, knowing the ṛṣi's condition, drew him out of the well and protected him, as one joyfully takes out hidden wealth: this Itihāsa is told here. The protection of the ṛṣi that the Aśvin deities performed is accompanied by abhiṣṭi (help), and is fit to be seen by all who look; fit to be praised by all and fit to be worshipped by all: all this is shown by the words tat karma, abhiṣṭimat, varūtham, śaṃsyam, rādhyam.

original p. 240

याभी रेभं निवृतं सितमद्भ्य उद्वन्दनमैरयतं स्वर्दृशे । याभिः कण्वं प्रसिषासन्तमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-५ [as read])

yābhī rebhaṃ nivṛtaṃ sitamadbhya udvandanamairayataṃ svardṛśe | yābhiḥ kaṇvaṃ prasiṣāsantamāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-5 [as read])

In this Ṛk it is said that the Aśvin deities protected Rebha, who had fallen in a well, together with Vandana and Kaṇva. Skandasvāmin cites this Ṛk —

रेभमृषिं सन्ध्याकाले स्नात्वा ह्रदादुत्तीर्णं अग्निहोत्रं होतुं स्वाश्रममागच्छन्तं असुरा ददृशुः । ते देवानामयं यष्टा स्तोता चेति ज्ञात्वा सङ्क्रुद्धाः तं ताडयित्वा बद्ध्वा च कस्मिंश्चिद्ध्रदे प्रक्षिप्य दशरात्रं धारयाञ्चक्रुः ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

rebhamṛṣiṃ sandhyākāle snātvā hradāduttīrṇaṃ agnihotraṃ hotuṃ svāśramamāgacchantaṃ asurā dadṛśuḥ | te devānāmayaṃ yaṣṭā stotā ceti jñātvā saṅkruddhāḥ taṃ tāḍayitvā baddhvā ca kasmiṃściddhrade prakṣipya daśarātraṃ dhārayāñcakruḥ ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

— 'the Asuras saw the ṛṣi Rebha, who at twilight, having bathed, came up from a pool and was going to his hermitage to make the Agnihotra offering. Knowing that he was a sacrificer and praiser of the gods, they, enraged, beat him, bound him, and, throwing him into a pool, kept him there ten nights.' In Kannada: the ṛṣi named Rebha, at twilight, having bathed, coming out of the river, was going to his hermitage to perform Agnihotra; the Asuras saw him, and, knowing that he worships and praises the gods, in anger they attacked him, tied him with rope and threw him into that river, [and] kept him bound for ten nights. Afterwards the Aśvin deities, pleased with his praise, protected that ṛṣi: so it is described. In some Ṛks it is described that the Asuras pushed Rebha and Vandana into the well, and that they came to be protected by the Aśvin deities when they praised them. In some places the matter of Vandana alone is stated:

शुभे रुक्मं न दर्शतं निखातमुदूपथुरश्विना वन्दनाय । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-५ [as read; the number is that printed here after the Ṛk, though the same number is printed for the previous Ṛk — as printed [?]])

yuvaṃ vandanamṛśyādudūpathuryuvaṃ sadyo viśpalāmetave kṛthaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-39-8 [as read])

yuvaṃ śayoravasaṃ pipyathurgaviḥ pra dīrgheṇa vandanastāryāyuṣā | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-? [as read])

— 'the praise is that you made the aged body of Vandana like the body of a youth, so that he might live for long'."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.12)

अत्रेयमाख्यायिका । इन्द्रो दध्यीचे प्रवर्ग्यविद्यां मधुविद्यां चोपदिश्य यदीमामन्यस्मै वक्ष्यसि शिरस्ते छेत्स्यामीत्युवाच । तदोरश्विनावश्वस्य शिरश्छित्त्वा दध्यीचः शिरः प्रच्छिद्यान्यत्र निधाय तत्राश्वशिरः प्रत्यधत्ताम् । केन च दध्यङ् ऋचः सामानि यजूंषि च प्रवर्ग्यविषयाणि मधुविद्याप्रतिपादकं ब्राह्मणं चाश्विनावध्यापयामास । तदिन्द्रो ज्ञात्वा वज्रेण तच्छिरोऽच्छिनत् । अथाश्विनौ तस्य स्वकीयं मानुषं शिरः प्रत्यधत्ताम् । इति शाट्यायनवाजसनेययोः प्रपञ्चेनोक्तम् । तदेतत्प्रतिपाद्यते । हे नरा नेतारावश्विनौ वां युवयोः सम्बन्ध्युग्रमुद्गूर्णमन्यैर्दुष्करं दंसः कर्मनामैतत् । युवाभ्यां पुरा कृतं तत्कर्म सनये धनलाभार्थमाविष्कृणोमि । प्रकटीकरोमि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । तन्यतुर्न । यथा मेघस्थः शब्दो वृष्टिं मेघान्निर्वर्तमानमुदकं प्रवर्षणेन सर्वत्र प्रकटयति तद्वत् । किं तत्कर्म । आथर्वणः अथर्वणः पुत्रो दध्यङ् ऋषिरश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा युष्मास्मार्थेन प्रतिहितेन शिरसा वां युवाभ्यामिमां मधुविद्यां यद्यदा खलु प्रोवाच प्रोक्तवान् । तदानीमश्वस्य शिरः सन्धानलक्षणं पुनर्मानुषस्य शिरः प्रतिसन्धानलक्षणं च यद्वदवदीयं कर्म तदाविष्कृणोमीत्यर्थः ॥ सनये । षणु दाने । खनिकषिकष्यञ्जिशिवसिद्धिनिस्तनिवनिसनिग्रन्थिभ्यश्चेतीप्रत्ययः । तन्यतुः । तनु विस्तारे । युतन्यञ्जेत्यादिना यतुच् । यद्वा । स्तन शब्दे । बाहुलकाद्यतुच् । छान्दसः सलोपः । वृष्टिम् । वृष्यते सिच्यतेऽनेनेति वृष्टिः । मन्त्रे … [the print continues on p. 244; this part in small type, partly doubtful [?]]

atreyamākhyāyikā | indro dadhyīce pravargyavidyāṃ madhuvidyāṃ copadiśya yadīmāmanyasmai vakṣyasi śiraste chetsyāmītyuvāca | tadoraśvināvaśvasya śiraśchittvā dadhyīcaḥ śiraḥ pracchidyānyatra nidhāya tatrāśvaśiraḥ pratyadhattām | kena ca dadhyaṅ ṛcaḥ sāmāni yajūṃṣi ca pravargyaviṣayāṇi madhuvidyāpratipādakaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāśvināvadhyāpayāmāsa | tadindro jñātvā vajreṇa tacchiro 'cchinat | athāśvinau tasya svakīyaṃ mānuṣaṃ śiraḥ pratyadhattām | iti śāṭyāyanavājasaneyayoḥ prapañcenoktam | tadetatpratipādyate | he narā netārāvaśvinau vāṃ yuvayoḥ sambandhyugramudgūrṇamanyairduṣkaraṃ daṃsaḥ karmanāmaitat | yuvābhyāṃ purā kṛtaṃ tatkarma sanaye dhanalābhārthamāviṣkṛṇomi | prakaṭīkaromi | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | tanyaturna | yathā meghasthaḥ śabdo vṛṣṭiṃ meghānnirvartamānamudakaṃ pravarṣaṇena sarvatra prakaṭayati tadvat | kiṃ tatkarma | ātharvaṇaḥ atharvaṇaḥ putro dadhyaṅ ṛṣiraśvasya śīrṣṇā yuṣmāsmārthena pratihitena śirasā vāṃ yuvābhyāmimāṃ madhuvidyāṃ yadyadā khalu provāca proktavān | tadānīmaśvasya śiraḥ sandhānalakṣaṇaṃ punarmānuṣasya śiraḥ pratisandhānalakṣaṇaṃ ca yadvadavadīyaṃ karma tadāviṣkṛṇomītyarthaḥ ‖ sanaye | ṣaṇu dāne | khanikaṣikaṣyañjiśivasiddhinistanivanisanigranthibhyaścetīpratyayaḥ | tanyatuḥ | tanu vistāre | yutanyañjetyādinā yatuc | yadvā | stana śabde | bāhulakādyatuc | chāndasaḥ salopaḥ | vṛṣṭim | vṛṣyate sicyate 'neneti vṛṣṭiḥ | mantre … [the print continues on p. 244; this part in small type, partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Here this story. Indra, having taught Dadhyañc the Pravargya-vidyā and the Madhu-vidyā, said: 'If you speak this to another, I shall cut off your head.' Then the Aśvins cut off the head of a horse and, having cut off Dadhyañc's head and placed it elsewhere, set the horse's head on him. And with that Dadhyañc taught the Aśvins the Ṛks, Sāmans and Yajus relating to the Pravargya, and the Brāhmaṇa that expounds the Madhu-vidyā. Indra, learning of it, cut off that head with his thunderbolt. Then the Aśvins set on him his own human head again: thus it is told at length in the Śāṭyāyana and Vājasaneya [texts]. This is set forth: O leaders, Aśvins, I make manifest aviḥ kṛṇomi, for the gaining of wealth, that fierce (ugram) act of yours, hard for others to do — daṃsaḥ is a name for 'work' — formerly done by you, as thunder (tanyatuḥ) in the cloud makes rain (the water that streams from the clouds) manifest everywhere by its downpour. What was that act? When the son of Atharvan, the ṛṣi Dadhyañc, aśvasya śīrṣṇā — with the horse's head placed by you on him — told you this Madhu-vidyā: then the act of setting on the horse's head and again setting the man's head — such an act of yours I make manifest." Grammatical tail of the bhāṣya on Ṛk 12, concluded — characterized, not transcribed: vṛṣṭim (mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ, ktin with udātta); ātharvaṇaḥ (atharvan + aṇ, tasyāpatyam; the ṭi elision by Pā. 6-4-?? as read [?]); śīrṣṇā (śīrṣan in the Veda, śīrṣan chandasi, Pā. 6-1-60 as read [?], the śiras → śīrṣan; the ṣ …; the instrumental ending accented by the anta-udātta of the stem.
