॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"narā — O Aśvin deities; ātharvaṇaḥ — the son of Atharvan; dadhyaṅ — the ṛṣi named Dadhyañc; aśvasya — of the horse; śīrṣṇā — with the head (obtained by your power); vām — to you two; īm — the Madhu-vidyā; yat ha — when; uvāca — taught; yat — which; vām — of you; tat — that; ugram — (to others) unachievable; daṃsaḥ — daring deed; tanyatuḥ — thunder; vṛṣṭiṃ na — as (it makes) rain (manifest); sanaye — for the sake of obtaining wealth; āviḥ kṛṇomi — I make manifest."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, the ṛṣi Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, [having] a horse's head (obtained by your power), taught you the Madhu-vidyā. I make manifest that deed of yours, impossible for others, as thunder makes rain manifest, for the sake of obtaining wealth."

English Translation (as printed)

I proclaim, leaders (of sacrifice), for the sake of acquiring wealth, that inimitable deed which you performed, as the thunder (announces) rain, when, provided by you with the head of a horse, Dadhyanch, the son of Atharvan, taught you the mystic science.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

दंसः — Daṃsaḥ — "since the word daṃsaḥ is stated among the twenty-six [as read] names of work (karman) 'apaḥ', 'apnaḥ' (Ni. 2-1 as read [?]), daṃsaḥ denotes work. The seer of the mantra — [the ṛṣi] declares with this mantra that the Aśvin deities perform a work that is difficult for others [to do]. The sound produced by the cloud makes manifest the rain, the water of the cloud, as it falls: so this stotra makes manifest the power of the Aśvin deities; and by the recital and study of it wealth is obtained according to one's wish: it is described so. By this the unique power of the Aśvin deities is described in the first half of this mantra."

original p. 245

दध्यङ् ह यन्मध्वाथर्वणः — Dadhyaṅ ha yan madhv ātharvaṇaḥ — "atharvaṇaḥ putraḥ | vitataṃ nāmaṃ ṛṣiḥ" [as printed, the Sanskrit is small type: 'ātharvaṇaḥ — atharvaṇa is the name of a ṛṣi, [the Kannada:] the ṛṣi named Ātharvaṇa [= Dadhyañc], son of the ṛṣi named Atharvan'. The Nirukta-writer: 'dadhyaṅ pratyaktho dhyānam iti vā pratyaktam asmin dhyānam iti vā' (Ni. 12-?? as read [?]): dadhyañc, atharvā, manuḥ — these three words, though not synonyms, since they convey another meaning ('being connected with the qualities of the Āditya'), denote three persons who are ṛṣis who move together with the Āditya, living in the atmosphere (dyusthāna). When it is said that they are not other than the Āditya, two kinds of explanation are given: that they are inhabitants of the atmosphere and that they are connected with the qualities of the Āditya. For this reason he explains in two ways: 'dhyānam asmin pratyaktam, pratyakto dhyānam' — 'in him meditation is directly seen', or 'one directly seen in meditation'.

"Skandasvāmin and Sāyaṇa both tell a story here. This Itihāsa is well known in the Vājasaneya Brāhmaṇa.

आथर्वणाय — दधीचे मध्वाख्यं परं ब्रह्म इन्द्र उवाच । प्रोच्यं च यदि वक्ष्यसि शिरस्ते पतिष्यतीति । तमश्विनौ मध्वर्थिनावागत्य ऊचतुः । प्रब्रूहि नौ परं ब्रह्मेति । स तौ प्रत्युवाच । शिरःपातभयान्न ब्रवीमीति । तौ तं प्रत्यूचतुः । अन्यत्ते आवां शिर आदधाहे । तेन प्रब्रूहि । स तथेति प्रपेदे । तस्याश्विनौ शिरश्छित्त्वाश्वशिर आदधाते । तेनासौ तानध्यापयांचकारेति । तदेतदिहोच्यते दध्यङ् ह यदित्यादिना ॥

ātharvaṇāya — dadhīce madhvākhyaṃ paraṃ brahma indra uvāca | procyaṃ ca yadi vakṣyasi śiraste patiṣyatīti | tamaśvinau madhvarthināvāgatya ūcatuḥ | prabrūhi nau paraṃ brahmeti | sa tau pratyuvāca | śiraḥpātabhayānna bravīmīti | tau taṃ pratyūcatuḥ | anyatte āvāṃ śira ādadhāhe | tena prabrūhi | sa tatheti prapede | tasyāśvinau śiraśchittvāśvaśira ādadhāte | tenāsau tānadhyāpayāṃcakāreti | tadetadihocyate dadhyaṅ ha yadityādinā ‖ [Skandasvāmin; small type; partly doubtful [?]]

— 'To Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan, Indra taught the supreme Brahman named Madhu, saying "If you tell it to another, your head will fall". The Aśvins, desiring the honey-knowledge, came and said: "Teach us the supreme Brahman." He answered: "I do not teach it from fear of my head falling." They said: "We shall set another head on you; teach with that." He agreed. The Aśvins cut off his head and put on a horse's head; with that he taught them. This is what is said here by dadhyaṅ ha yat and so on.' In Kannada: Indra taught the ṛṣi Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, the teaching of the Supreme Brahman, which is known by the name Madhu (Madhu-vidyā), saying 'if you teach this to anyone else, your head will fall'. The Aśvin deities, eager to obtain the Madhu-vidyā, came to the ṛṣi Dadhyañc and asked him 'teach us the Supreme Brahman taught in the Madhu-vidyā'. He told them that he would not teach for fear that his head would fall. Then the Aśvin deities said: 'we shall set another head on you; teach [us]': hearing it, he agreed. Then the Aśvin deities cut off his head and set on a horse's head. He taught them the Madhu-vidyā: this is the Itihāsa told in Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya."

तदिन्द्रो ज्ञात्वा वज्रेण तच्छिरोऽच्छिनत् । अथाश्विनौ तस्य स्वकीयं मानुषं शिरः प्रत्यधत्ताम् ॥

tadindro jñātvā vajreṇa tacchiro 'cchinat | athāśvinau tasya svakīyaṃ mānuṣaṃ śiraḥ pratyadhattām ‖

"Indra, learning of it, cut off [the horse's] head with his thunderbolt. Afterwards the Aśvin deities set on him again his own human head."

original p. 246

"Indra, learning of this, cut off the head of the ṛṣi Dadhyañc with his thunderbolt. Afterwards the Aśvin deities set Dadhyañc's own earlier human head on his body and protected him: this part of the Itihāsa is stated in the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya."

अश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा वां ईं यदुवाच — Aśvasya śīrṣṇā vāṃ īṃ yad uvāca — "yuṣmat-sāmarthyena pratihitena śirasā yuvābhyām imām madhuvidyāṃ yadā ca uktavān: the power of yours that brought and placed the horse's head, the fact that the ṛṣi Dadhyañc taught the Madhu-vidyā, and that you, receiving the teaching, protected him by the exchange of heads: this is described in this Ṛk, 'I make it manifest'.

"The ṛṣi named Dadhyañc or Dadhīca is famous in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. The Bhāṣyakāra tells here a legend: when the ṛṣi Dadhyañc, son of Atharvan, was living, the Asuras, by the sight of him, fled in fear. After he died and went to heaven, the Asuras spread fearlessly over the whole earth. Then Indra sought that ṛṣi for the purpose of fighting these Asuras. [He was told] 'the ṛṣi has gone to heaven'. Then Indra asked those near him whether any part of the ṛṣi's limbs remained; they said: 'Once the ṛṣi Dadhīca taught the Madhu-vidyā to the Aśvin deities; only the head of the horse which was [then] set on him remains; where it is, we do not know.' Then, when Indra said 'find it', they searched and brought it: it had fallen in a lake called Śaryaṇāvat near Kurukṣetra. Indra, with the marrow of the bones of that head, conquered the Asuras: that is, he made futile the nine-hundred-and-ninety [as read — ombhattu sala tombhattu, 'nine times ninety']… eight hundred and ten [?] māyā-snares of the Asuras. In explaining this number the Bhāṣyakāra says: for conquering the deities of the three worlds the Asuras first had three kinds of māyā: each of them being threefold as present, past, future, [so] altogether nine kinds. And those nine māyās, joined with the three powers beginning with enthusiasm (utsāha), are 9 × 3 = 27. These, joined with the three guṇas beginning with sattva, are 27 × 3 = 81. These eighty-one māyās, being used in the ten quarters, are altogether 81 × 10 = 810; or nine times ninety, 9 × 90 = 810. Thus Indra rendered fruitless the net of māyā of such [number] of the Asura named Vṛtra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-13 as read [?]) — so he explains.

"Skandasvāmin tells another Itihāsa: in the past there were Asuras named Kālakañja. They became powerful and killed the deities, giving them great trouble. Then the deities [went to Brahmā …]" continues on p. 247

original p. 247

"… [Skandasvāmin's other Itihāsa, continued:] [the deities], to destroy these Asuras, begged Brahmā to tell them a means: 'O deities, there is a ṛṣi named Dadhyañc; go to him; he will know the proper means for the destruction of the Asuras.' As Brahmā had said, the deities went to the ṛṣi Dadhīca and gave him the message that Brahmā had sent them. That ṛṣi, by yoga-vision, understood the matter for which they had come, and, in the yoga-samādhi, gave up his own life-breaths. Then Indra, with the marrow of that ṛṣi's bones, destroyed the Asuras. This very matter is described in this Ṛk, Skandasvāmin says (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-13 [as read; [?]])."

"There is a tradition that the head of Dadhīca was the horse's head, and that it was given to him by the Aśvin deities. After the death of the ṛṣi Dadhīca, Indra sought the head, which had remained as a horse's head. It is described in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-13 that it was found fallen in a lake called Śaryaṇāvat, at the foot of a mountain."

"As to how the horse's head came to Dadhīca, Skandasvāmin tells an earlier Itihāsa: Indra taught Dadhīca, the son of Atharvan, the form of the Supreme Brahman known as Madhu, and said 'you must not tell this to anyone; if you tell, your head will fall'. After some time the Aśvin deities came to the ṛṣi Dadhīca; and when they begged him to tell the form of Brahman that Indra had taught, Dadhīca said: 'Indra will say my head will fall; I shall not teach it for fear of that.' The Aśvins then said: 'do not worry about that; we shall give you another head if your head falls.' Dadhīca agreed. Hence, when Dadhīca's head fell, the Aśvin deities cut off a horse's head, brought it and joined it to Dadhīca's body. Hence it is said that Dadhīca's head was like a horse's head: this matter the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān has described in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-12 [as read] and 1-117-22 [as read] [the numerals are small [?]].

"The name of this ṛṣi is found in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in the Ṛks 1-84-13 ; 1-?-? ; 1-?-? ; 1-117-22 ; 1-119-9 [as read, partly illegible [?]] and others; and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3-?-?-? ; 5-?-?-? [?]; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 1?-?; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 14-1-1-? ; 14-?-?-? [?], 4-?-?-? ; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2-5-? ; 4-?-? [as read] and other places. This cluster of reference numerals is too small and blurred to read with confidence; I give them only as these partial readings."

original p. 248

The Western scholar Welson [sic — printed in English "Welson"; elsewhere "Wilson"] writes on this matter thus (English, as printed):

We have here rather obscure allusions to a legend which was probably afterwards modified by the Purana's in which the name also occurs as Dadhicha. In the Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Vol. I. it is merely related, that the gods, being oppressed by the kalakeya Asuras, solicited from the sage Dadhicha his bones, which he gave them, and from which Twashtri fabricated the thunderbolt with which Indra slew Vritra and routed the Asuras. The legend of the text differs from this ; Indra—having taught the sciences called Pravargya vidya and Madhu-vidya to Dadhyanch, threatened that he would cut off his head if ever he taught them to any one else ; the Aswins prevailed upon him, nevertheless, to teach them the prohibited knowledge, and, to evade Indra's threat, took off the head of the sage, replacing it by that of a horse ; Indra, apprized of Dadhyanch's breach of faith, struck off his equine head with the thunderbolt ; on which the Aswins restored to him his own. The Pravargya vidya is said to imply certain verses of the Rik, Yajur, and Sama Vedas, and the Madhu-vidya the Brahmana.

आथर्वणः — Ātharvaṇaḥ — "that the ṛṣi named Atharvan is the father of the ṛṣi Dadhīca is stated in this Ṛk. Mantras that contain many secret and māyā-knowledges are in the Atharvaveda, and it is well known that this Veda has acquired this name because this ṛṣi Atharvan was skilled in these sciences, and was the seer of many sūktas of that Veda.

"The ṛṣi named Atharvan is the original ancestor of a famous group of twenty-one [as read] ṛṣis. In the places where the plural of this word is used, it means the ṛṣi's descendants. In some places, for example —

and other Ṛks, there is praise of the gift: a king named Aśvatha gave to the Atharvan family chariots, cows, and so on.

Sense (mine): "Vadhrimatī was the daughter of a certain royal sage, whose husband was impotent. She called on the Aśvins for the sake of obtaining a son. Hearing her call, the Aśvins came and gave her a son called Hiraṇyahasta. This is what is said: O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, purubhujā, protectors of many, or having abundant hands, in mahe yāman, the great, worshipful yāman — yāma is a hymn ('that which goes') — in that [hymn], who grant the desired fruit: purandhiḥ — the much-minded, vadhrimatī — vadhri is an eunuch incapable of begetting a son; the king's daughter of that name who has such [a husband] — ājohavīt, called, again and again with praise, for obtaining a son. And you heard the call of Vadhrimatī. Illustration: śāsur iva — as a pupil listens attentively to the words of his teacher, so you. And having heard, O Aśvins, you gave her a son named Hiraṇyahasta, 'golden-handed', or having a beautiful hand."

"purubhujā — protectors of many people, or those of great hands; nāsatyā — O Aśvin deities; mahe — worshipful; yāman — hymns (made [by one]); karā — who grant the desired fruit; vām — you two; purandhiḥ — the wise (the princess named Vadhrimatī); ājohavīt —

original p. 252

— called again and again (in praise); vadhrimatyāḥ — of Vadhrimatī, who had an impotent man as husband; āhvānam — the call; śāsuḥ iva — like a pupil who listens attentively to the words of his teacher; śrutam — you heard; anantaram — afterwards; aśvinau — O Aśvin deities; hiraṇyahastam — a son named Hiraṇyahasta; adattam — you gave."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, protectors of many people, to Vadhrimatī, a wise woman, who had an impotent husband and who again and again called on you, eager to please you with praise in the proper manner, you listened as a pupil listens attentively to his teacher's words, and gave (favoured her with) a son named Hiraṇyahasta."

English Translation (as printed)

The intelligent (Vadhrimati) idvoked [sic] you NASATYAS, who are the accomplishers (of desires) and the protectors of many, with a sacred hymn ; herr [sic] prayer was heard, like (the instruction of) a teacher, and you, Aswins, gave to the wife of an impotent husband, Hiranyahasta, her son,

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

पुरुभुजा — Purubhujā — "bahūnāṃ pālakau prabhūtahastau vā": "protectors of many people; or, doing extraordinary giving, having broad hands (ati-dānaśīlau hastau) — so Sāyaṇa says. 'Receivers of many oblations (bahūnāṃ haviṣām abhyavahartārau) or protectors of those who are distressed (ārtānāṃ pālayitārau)', explains Skandasvāmin: Aśvins who accept many oblations or protect the afflicted."

यामन् — Yāman — "yāmani yāti gacchatīti yāmaḥ stotram": "the hymn recited by those who praise. Because the stotṛ and the deity are connected by knowledge, this stuti has the name yāma. Skandasvāmin: 'yāmann iti yoddhāro yasmin sa yāmaḥ saṅgrāmaḥ ihābhipretaḥ' — 'in which warriors go: yāma means battle; here this is meant'; the arena where heroes who fight are gathered for a fight is called a saṅgrāma — so he explains."

वध्रिमती — Vadhrimatī — "vadhriḥ putrotpādanāsaktaḥ ṣaṇḍakaḥ | tadvatī rājaputrī": "vadhri is an impotent man, incapable of producing a son; the princess who has such a husband is vadhrimatī" — Sāyaṇa so explains the name of one whose husband is such an impotent man.

original p. 253

"… vadhrimatī — 'she who has an impotent man as husband': so Sāyaṇa explains. Skandasvāmin —

वध्रिमती नाम योधी शत्रुभिः सङ्ग्रामे छिन्नहस्ता । अश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तस्याः अश्विनौ हिरण्यहस्तं ददतुः इति ॥

vadhrimatī nāma yodhī śatrubhiḥ saṅgrāme chinnahastā | aśvinau tuṣṭāva | tasyāḥ aśvinau hiraṇyahastaṃ dadatuḥ iti ‖

— vadhrimatī is the name of a woman warrior (yodhī) in battle, whose hand was cut off by enemies; she praised the Aśvins; to her the Aśvins gave a golden hand [hiraṇyahastam]." "Skandasvāmin explains the meaning of the word vadhrimatī as 'the woman who fights (the princess named Vadhrimatī) in a battle, who has lost a hand [cut off] in the war with the enemies'. Though Skandasvāmin and Sāyaṇa, in giving the meaning of this Ṛk, have different intentions in different places, in the matter that they favoured her with a son named Hiraṇyahasta the intention of both is of one kind. Sāyaṇa, explaining that since the word vadhri means 'impotent', she who has him as husband is vadhrimatī, relates the Itihāsa that a princess who had an impotent husband praised the Aśvin deities greatly and pleased them; they, pleased with her praise, appeared to her in person and gave her the boon that a son named Hiraṇyahasta should be born as she wished. Skandasvāmin, however, says that the woman warrior named Vadhrimatī, her hand cut off by enemies in battle, praised the Aśvin deities; they made her hand as it was before, according to her wish; and, saying that the hand too was golden:

हिरण्यहस्तः — Hiraṇyahastaḥ — "hiraṇmayau hastau yasmin sa hiraṇyahastaḥ | bāhuḥ": "the word hiraṇya means 'gold'. Hence he explains that he is 'one who has golden arms'. Sāyaṇa explains the word hiraṇyahasta as 'one with beautiful (hitaramaṇīya, pleasant) hands, [giving] comfort', or as 'one who has the name Hiraṇyahasta', as a qualifier of the son."

शासुरिव — Śāsur iva — "the Aśvin deities, hearing the praises of those who praise them, as a pupil listens attentively to the teacher's teaching, fulfil their wishes: this is the meaning of the word śāsur iva."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.14)

वर्तिका चटकसदृशस्य पक्षिणः स्त्री । तामरण्ये वर्तमानेन शुना ग्रस्तां पुरा किलाश्विनावमोचयताम् । तदेतदाह । हे नरा नेतारौ नासत्यावश्विनौ युवं युवामभीके भीगते [?] वृकवर्तिकयोः सङ्ग्रामे वृकस्य विकर्तकस्य शुन आस्नः आस्यादत्तिकां चटकसदृशीमुमुक्तम् । अमोचयतम् । यास्कस्त्वाह । पुनः पुनर्वर्तते प्रतिदिवसमावर्तत इति वर्तिकोषाः । तां वृकेणावरकेण सर्वजगत्प्रकाशनाच्छादयित्रा सूर्येण ग्रस्तां तदीयमुखादश्विनावमुञ्चतामिति । उतोऽपि च पुरुभुजा महाबाहू प्रभूतहस्तौ वा युवं ह युवां खलु कृपमाणं स्तुवन्तं कविं विक्रान्तं मन्त्रवृषिं विचक्षे विशेषेण द्रष्टुं [समर्थमकृणुतं ।] आकुरुतम् ॥ आस्नः । पद्दन्नित्यादिनास्यशब्दस्यासन्नादेशः । आल्लोपोनः । इत्यकारलोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणोदिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अमुमुक्तम् । मुचेर्लङ्तर्थे लिङ्बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः । कृपः स्तुतिरिति … ताः तुदादिषु द्रष्टव्यः । विचक्षे । तुमर्थे सेसेनसेति सेप्रत्ययः । स्कोः संयोगाद्योरिति सलोपः ॥ [small type; read letter by letter; doubtful words [?]]

vartikā caṭakasadṛśasya pakṣiṇaḥ strī | tāmaraṇye vartamānena śunā grastāṃ purā kilāśvināvamocayatām | tadetadāha | he narā netārau nāsatyāvaśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāmabhīke bhīgate [?] vṛkavartikayoḥ saṅgrāme vṛkasya vikartakasya śuna āsnaḥ āsyādattikāṃ caṭakasadṛśīmumuktam | amocayatam | yāskastvāha | punaḥ punarvartate pratidivasamāvartata iti vartikoṣāḥ | tāṃ vṛkeṇāvarakeṇa sarvajagatprakāśanācchādayitrā sūryeṇa grastāṃ tadīyamukhādaśvināvamuñcatāmiti | uto 'pi ca purubhujā mahābāhū prabhūtahastau vā yuvaṃ ha yuvāṃ khalu kṛpamāṇaṃ stuvantaṃ kaviṃ vikrāntaṃ mantravṛṣiṃ vicakṣe viśeṣeṇa draṣṭuṃ [samarthamakṛṇutaṃ |] ākurutam ‖ āsnaḥ | paddannityādināsyaśabdasyāsannādeśaḥ | ālloponaḥ | ityakāralopaḥ | udāttanivṛttisvareṇoditi vibhakterudāttatvam | amumuktam | mucerlaṅtarthe liṅbahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya śluḥ | kṛpaḥ stutiriti … tāḥ tudādiṣu draṣṭavyaḥ | vicakṣe | tumarthe sesenaseti sepratyayaḥ | skoḥ saṃyogādyoriti salopaḥ ‖ [small type; read letter by letter; doubtful words [?]]

Sense (mine): "Vartikā is the female of a bird like the sparrow (caṭaka). Once, it is said, the Aśvins released her when she was seized by a dog [wolf] that was in the forest. This is what is said: O leaders, Nāsatyas, Aśvins, abhīke — in the battle between the vṛka (wolf) and the vartikā — you released the quail-like vartikā from the mouth (āsnaḥ) of the vṛka, the tearer, the dog. [Yāska says: vartikā 'she who returns again and again', that is, Uṣas; the vṛka, the coverer — the Sun, who covers by illuminating the whole world — had seized her; the Aśvins released her from his mouth.] And further, O purubhujā (great-armed, or having many hands), yuvaṃ ha, you indeed made kavim, the courageous ṛṣi, who was kṛpamāṇam, praising, vicakṣe, able to see well."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"narā — leaders; he nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; yuvam — you two; abhīke — in battle; vṛkasya — of the dog (wolf); āsnaḥ — from the mouth; vartikām — the bird called vartikā (the quail); amumuktam — you released; uto — and; purubhujā — O mighty-armed; yuvam ha — you; kṛpamāṇam — one who praises; kavim — the (blind) ṛṣi named Kavi; vicakṣe — to see well; akṛṇutam — you made (capable)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O leader Nāsatyas, you two released the bird called vartikā from the mouth of the wolf, in the battle between the wolf and the vartikā. And you, of mighty arms, favoured the (blind) ṛṣi named Kavi, who praises [you], with the power to see well."

English Translation (as printed)

Nasatyas, leaders, you liberated the quail from the mouth of the dog that had seized her, and you, who are benefactors of many, have granted to the sage who praises you, to behold (true wisdom).

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अभीके — Abhīke — "vṛkavartikayoḥ saṅgrāme ābhigate": "the word abhīka is stated among the twenty-four [as read] names of saṅgrāma (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]) and among the sixteen [as read] names of words denoting the quarters (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]). Here saṅgrāma means 'battle': in a forest, a dog (wolf) and a quail; when the dog caught the quail, the Aśvin deities saved the quail that was caught in the dog's mouth: this Itihāsa is conveyed by the words. Another meaning is also manifest here: that Uṣas was released from the Sun. In this meaning Yāska explains the word vartikā as 'Uṣas', since she comes every day and repeats again and again; the Sun, who illumines the whole world with his own light and releases it, is the one to be denoted by the word vṛka because he covers this Uṣas also (the one who lets go): Uṣas is seized by the vṛka with this light. Therefore, to convey the meaning — 'the Aśvin deities released Uṣas, who was seized by the Sun' — he says the sentence 'punaḥ punar vartate pratidivasam āvartate iti vartikā uṣāḥ' (Ni. 5-?? as read [?]).

original p. 257

वृकस्य — Vṛkasya — "vikartakasya: atiśayena hiṃsāṃ karoti iti": "the word vṛka is stated among the eighteen [as read] names of vajra (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]) and among the fourteen [as read] names of thieves (stena) (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]). And —

वृकः वृक्षश्चन्द्रमा भवति विवृतज्योतिष्को वा विकृतज्योतिष्को वा विक्रान्तज्योतिष्को वा ॥ (नि. ५-२० [as read])

vṛkaḥ vṛkṣaścandramā bhavati vivṛtajyotiṣko vā vikṛtajyotiṣko vā vikrāntajyotiṣko vā ‖ (ni. 5-20 [as read])

— because it is of shining light, or because by its excess of cool (śītakara) light it disfigures the others, or because it has more light than the planets, stars and the like, the moon is denoted by the word vṛka: thus Yāska explains the meaning of the word vṛka —

अरुणो मा सकृद्वृकः पथा यन्तं ददर्श हि । उज्जिहीते निचाय्या तष्टेव पृष्ट्यामयी वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१०५-१८ [as read])

aruṇo mā sakṛdvṛkaḥ pathā yantaṃ dadarśa hi | ujjihīte nicāyyā taṣṭeva pṛṣṭyāmayī vittaṃ me asya rodasī ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-105-18 [as read])

as an example, and —

अरुण आरोचनो मासकृन्मासानां चार्धमासानां च कर्ता भवति चन्द्रमा वृकः पथा यन्तं ददर्श नक्षत्रगणमभिजिहीते निचाय्य येन येन योक्ष्यमाणो भवति चन्द्रमास्तष्टेव पृष्ट्यामयी जानीतं मे वाक्यस्य द्यावापृथिव्याविति ॥ (नि. ५-२१ [as read])

aruṇa ārocano māsakṛnmāsānāṃ cārdhamāsānāṃ ca kartā bhavati candramā vṛkaḥ pathā yantaṃ dadarśa nakṣatragaṇamabhijihīte nicāyya yena yena yokṣyamāṇo bhavati candramāstaṣṭeva pṛṣṭyāmayī jānītaṃ me vākyasya dyāvāpṛthivyāviti ‖ (ni. 5-21 [as read])

— in this Ṛk the word vṛka is explained as meaning the moon.

आदित्योऽपि वृक उच्यते । यदावृङ्क्ते [?] (नि. ५-२१)

ājohavīdaśvinā vartikā vāmāsno yatsīmumuñcataṃ vṛkasya | vi jayuṣā yayathuḥ sādvade rjātaṃ viṣvāco ahataṃ viṣeṇa ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-8 [as read])

vṛkaścidasya vāraṇa urāmathirā vayuneṣu bhūṣati | semaṃ naḥ stomaṃ jujuṣāṇa ā gahīndra pra citrayā dhiyā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 8-66-8 [as read])

śataṃ meṣānvṛkye cakṣadānamṛjrāśvaṃ taṃ pitā 'ndhaṃ cakāra | tasmā akṣī nāsatyā vicakṣa ādhattaṃ dasrā bhiṣajāvanarvan ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-16 [as read])

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 14; grammar page, noted briefly)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.15)

अगस्त्यपुरोहितः खेलो नाम राजा । तस्य सम्बन्धिनी विश्पला नाम स्त्री सङ्ग्रामे शत्रुभिश्छिन्नपादासीत् । पुरोहितेनागस्त्येन स्तुतावश्विनौ रात्रावागत्याद्योमयं पादं समधत्तां । तदेतदाह । आजा आजौ सङ्ग्रामे ऽगस्त्यपुरोहितस्य खेलस्य सम्बन्ध्याः विश्पलाख्यायाश्चरित्रं चरणं वेरिव वेः पक्षिणः पर्णं पतत्रमिवाच्छेदि हि । पुरा भिन्नमभूत्खलु । हे अश्विनौ युवामगस्त्येन स्तुतौ सन्तौ परितक्म्यायां रात्रौ । परितक्म्यां रात्रिः परित एनां तकेतीति यास्कः । नि. ११-२१ । एनामुभयतः सूर्यो गच्छतीति तस्यार्थः । रात्रावागत्य सद्यस्तदानीमेव हिते शत्रुषु निहिते धने जेतव्ये विषयभूते सति सर्तवे सर्तुं गन्तुं विश्पलाया आयसीमयोमयीं जङ्घां जङ्घोपलक्षितं पादं प्रत्यधत्तं । सन्धानमेकीकरणं कृतवन्ताविस्यर्थः ॥ चरित्रम् । अर्तिलूधूसूखनसहचर इत्रः इति करणे इत्रः । आजा । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्डादेशः । आयसीम् । अयोऽशब्दाद्विकारार्थे प्राणिरजतादिभ्योऽञ् । पा. ४-३-१५४ । टिड्ढाणञित्यादिना ङीप् ॥

agastyapurohitaḥ khelo nāma rājā | tasya sambandhinī viśpalā nāma strī saṅgrāme śatrubhiśchinnapādāsīt | purohitenāgastyena stutāvaśvinau rātrāvāgatyādyomayaṃ pādaṃ samadhattāṃ | tadetadāha | ājā ājau saṅgrāme 'gastyapurohitasya khelasya sambandhyāḥ viśpalākhyāyāścaritraṃ caraṇaṃ veriva veḥ pakṣiṇaḥ parṇaṃ patatramivācchedi hi | purā bhinnamabhūtkhalu | he aśvinau yuvāmagastyena stutau santau paritakmyāyāṃ rātrau | paritakmyāṃ rātriḥ parita enāṃ taketīti yāskaḥ | ni. 11-21 | enāmubhayataḥ sūryo gacchatīti tasyārthaḥ | rātrāvāgatya sadyastadānīmeva hite śatruṣu nihite dhane jetavye viṣayabhūte sati sartave sartuṃ gantuṃ viśpalāyā āyasīmayomayīṃ jaṅghāṃ jaṅghopalakṣitaṃ pādaṃ pratyadhattaṃ | sandhānamekīkaraṇaṃ kṛtavantāvisyarthaḥ ‖ caritram | artilūdhūsūkhanasahacara itraḥ iti karaṇe itraḥ | ājā | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterḍādeśaḥ | āyasīm | ayo 'śabdādvikārārthe prāṇirajatādibhyo 'ñ | pā. 4-3-154 | ṭiḍḍhāṇañityādinā ṅīp ‖

Sense (mine): "Khela was a king whose priest was Agastya. His [relation] Viśpalā, a woman, had had her foot cut off by enemies in battle. Agastya, the priest, praised the Aśvins, who came at night and fitted an iron foot. This is what is said: ājā — in the battle, [in] the battle of Khela whose priest was Agastya, the caritra, the foot, of Viśpalā was cut off like a bird's wing (vaḥ iva parṇam), the patatra; formerly it had been broken. O Aśvins, you, praised by Agastya, in paritakmyāyām, in the night (paritakmyā = 'night': Yāska: 'it goes around this'; Ni. 11-?? as read [?]; the sense: 'the Sun goes on both sides of it'), came, and at once, when wealth was placed [in the enemies], at the time of the contest, for going — for sartave — you fitted to Viśpalā an āyasī, iron, jaṅghā (that is, a foot indicated by the shank): you united it, made it one."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"(he aśvinau — O Aśvin deities); ājā — in battle; khelasya — of the king named Khela (belonging to him); viśpalāyāḥ [as printed viśpalā, the woman]; caritram — the foot; veḥ — of a bird; parṇam iva — like a wing; acchedi hi — was cut; paritakmyāyām — at night (you two, when praised by Agastya, the priest of Khela, came); sadyaḥ — at once; hite — placed [by the enemies]; dhane — for the sake of wealth; sartave — to go (to run for the purpose); viśpalāyai — for Viśpalā; āyasīm — made of iron; jaṅghām — foot; pratyadhattam — you joined (gave)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, in battle, to Viśpalā, [the wife] of Khela, whose foot was cut off like a bird's wing — you two, praised by his priest, the sage Agastya, came at night and, so that she might run to win the wealth placed by the enemies, joined an iron foot."

original p. 262

English Translation (as printed)

The foot of (Vispala, the wife of) Khela, was cut off, like the wing of a bird, in an engagement by night ; immediately you gave her an iron leg, that she might walk, the hidden treasure (of the enemy being the object of the conflict).

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

परितक्म्यायाम् — Paritakmyāyām — "paritakmyā rātriḥ": "'night'. Yāska: 'parita enāṃ takti' (Ni. 11-?? as read [?]), 'enāṃ sūryo ubhayataḥ gacchatīti tasyārthaḥ': 'the Sun goes to both sides of her'. The word paritakmyā is [used] for night, because the Sun, being [in the position] at both the beginning of the night and at its end, [goes about it]. Skandasvāmin explains paritakmyāyām as 'senāyāṃ vartamānāyām': 'when there was an army'. King Khela had made the ṛṣi Agastya his house-priest. He had a wife named Viśpalā. While the battle was being fought against the enemies, the woman Viśpalā's foot was cut off and lost. Then, to get a foot for Viśpalā, the ṛṣi Agastya praised the Aśvin deities; and the Aśvin deities came at night and, in place of the cut-off feet [sic: foot], joined iron feet so that she could walk with her feet [again]: this Itihāsa is told here. This matter is described in the Ṛks —

याभिर्विश्पलां धनसामथर्व्यं सहस्रमीळ्ह आजावजिन्वतम् । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१० [as read])

yābhirviśpalāṃ dhanasāmatharvyaṃ sahasramīḷha ājāvajinvatam | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-10 [as read])

अगस्त्यो ब्रह्मणा वावृधानः सं विश्पलां नासत्या परिणीतम् [?] । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-११ [as read])

agastyo brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānaḥ saṃ viśpalāṃ nāsatyā pariṇītam [?] | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-11 [as read])

अमुञ्चतं वर्तिकामंहसो निः प्रति जङ्घां विश्पलाया अधत्तम् । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-८ [as read])

amuñcataṃ vartikāmaṃhaso niḥ prati jaṅghāṃ viśpalāyā adhattam | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-8 [as read])

युवं वन्दनमृश्यादुदूपथुर्युवं सद्यो विश्पलामेतवे कृथः । (ऋ. सं. १०-३९-८ [as read])"

yuvaṃ vandanamṛśyādudūpathuryuvaṃ sadyo viśpalāmetave kṛthaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-39-8 [as read])"

चरित्रम् — Caritram — "caraṇam: Sāyaṇa explains caritra as 'foot' (pāda), 'that by which one goes'; the foot is the instrument for going; Skandasvāmin explains that jaṅghā — the shank — is here intended: it is the means of motion, the means of walking."

original p. 263

धने हिते — Dhane hite — "in the expression dhane hite the locative is a locative of cause (nimitta saptamī): the word nimitta is used for the purpose (prayojana). In this meaning it is accepted as being the cause; therefore hitam dhanam prāptum yaḥ anīkaḥ prakrāntaḥ saṅgrāmaḥ tasya gamanasya vyāghātārtham: 'for wealth that was favourable, the war that was begun — in order to avoid the obstruction to the going' — it is explained that the iron foot was joined so that she might go without hindrance in the war undertaken for gaining the wealth. Sāyaṇa explains: 'śatruṣu nihite dhane jetavye viṣayabhūte sati' — in the war made in order to conquer and make one's own the wealth that is in the enemies' possession."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.16)

वृषागिरः पुत्र ऋज्राश्वो नाम राजर्षिः । तस्य समीपे ऽश्विनोर्वाहनभूतो रासभो वृकी भूत्वावतस्थे । स च तस्या आहारार्थमेकोत्तरशतसंख्याकान्मेषान् [?] स्वभूतानेषां शकलीकृत्य प्रददौ । ऋज्राश्वः शतमेकं च मेषानिति मन्त्रान्तरे दर्शनात् । एवं पौरामाहिते प्रवृत्तं पिता शापेन नेत्रहीनमकरोत् । तेन स्तूयमानावश्विनावस्मद्वाहननिमित्तमस्यान्धं जातमिति जानन्तौ तस्मा अक्षिणी प्रायच्छतामिति । तदेतदाह । अत्र तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्छब्दाध्याहारः । यं ऋज्राश्वः शतं शतसंख्याकान्मेषान्वृक्यै आत्मना पोषितायै वृकस्त्रियै शकलीकृत्य प्रादात् । तं चक्षदानं क्षदतेरत्तिकर्मणः शकलीकरणार्थं शकलीकृत्य दत्तवन्तमृज्राश्वं पिता शापेनान्धं दृष्टिहीनं चकार । कृतवान् । हे नासत्या सत्यस्वभावौ सत्यस्य नेतारौ वा भिषजौ देवानां वैद्यभूतौ । अश्विनौ वै देवानां भिषजौ । ऐ. ब्रा. १-१८ । इति श्रुतेः । दस्रा दर्शनीयौ वेतत्संज्ञौ वा हे अश्विनावनर्वन्ननर्वणे दृष्टव्यं प्रति पित्रृशापाद्गमनरहिते अक्षी चक्षुषी विचक्षे विविधं द्रष्टुं समर्थे तस्मै ऋज्राश्वायाधत्तं । व्यधत्तम् । अकुरुतम् । वृक्यै । वृकोरण्यश्वा । तस्य स्त्री वृकी । जातेरस्त्रीविषयाद् । पा. ४-१-६३ । इति ङीष् । जसादिषु छन्दसि वावचनमिति चतुर्ध्येकवचनस्याडभावे यञादेश उदात्तस्वरितेरोर्यणो इति परस्यानुदात्तस्य स्वरितत्वम् । चक्षदानम् । क्षदेर्लिटः कानच् । चित्स्वरः । अक्षी । ई चिद्विवचने । पा. ६-१-२२ । इति परत्वाद्दक्षशब्दस्यैकारान्तादेशः । स चोदात्तः । तस्मिन् कृते सकृद्गतौ विप्रतिषेधे । परि. ४० । इति परिभाषया पुनर्नुम्न भवति । विचक्षे । चक्षेः संपदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । अनर्वन् । ऋ गतौ । अस्मादन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते इति दृशिग्रहणस्य विध्यङ्करोपसंग्रहार्थत्वाद्वनेवनिप् । अर्व गमनं विषयं प्रत्येनयोर्नास्तीति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्स्वभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । सुपां सुलुगिति द्विवचनस्य लुक् । छान्दसो नलोपाभावः ॥ [small type; read letter by letter; marked [?] where doubtful]

vṛṣāgiraḥ putra ṛjrāśvo nāma rājarṣiḥ | tasya samīpe 'śvinorvāhanabhūto rāsabho vṛkī bhūtvāvatasthe | sa ca tasyā āhārārthamekottaraśatasaṃkhyākānmeṣān [?] svabhūtāneṣāṃ śakalīkṛtya pradadau | ṛjrāśvaḥ śatamekaṃ ca meṣāniti mantrāntare darśanāt | evaṃ paurāmāhite pravṛttaṃ pitā śāpena netrahīnamakarot | tena stūyamānāvaśvināvasmadvāhananimittamasyāndhaṃ jātamiti jānantau tasmā akṣiṇī prāyacchatāmiti | tadetadāha | atra tacchabdaśruteryacchabdādhyāhāraḥ | yaṃ ṛjrāśvaḥ śataṃ śatasaṃkhyākānmeṣānvṛkyai ātmanā poṣitāyai vṛkastriyai śakalīkṛtya prādāt | taṃ cakṣadānaṃ kṣadaterattikarmaṇaḥ śakalīkaraṇārthaṃ śakalīkṛtya dattavantamṛjrāśvaṃ pitā śāpenāndhaṃ dṛṣṭihīnaṃ cakāra | kṛtavān | he nāsatyā satyasvabhāvau satyasya netārau vā bhiṣajau devānāṃ vaidyabhūtau | aśvinau vai devānāṃ bhiṣajau | ai. brā. 1-18 | iti śruteḥ | dasrā darśanīyau vetatsaṃjñau vā he aśvināvanarvannanarvaṇe dṛṣṭavyaṃ prati pitrṛśāpādgamanarahite akṣī cakṣuṣī vicakṣe vividhaṃ draṣṭuṃ samarthe tasmai ṛjrāśvāyādhattaṃ | vyadhattam | akurutam | vṛkyai | vṛkoraṇyaśvā | tasya strī vṛkī | jāterastrīviṣayād | pā. 4-1-63 | iti ṅīṣ | jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanamiti caturdhyekavacanasyāḍabhāve yañādeśa udāttasvariteroryaṇo iti parasyānudāttasya svaritatvam | cakṣadānam | kṣaderliṭaḥ kānac | citsvaraḥ | akṣī | ī cidvivacane | pā. 6-1-22 | iti paratvāddakṣaśabdasyaikārāntādeśaḥ | sa codāttaḥ | tasmin kṛte sakṛdgatau vipratiṣedhe | pari. 40 | iti paribhāṣayā punarnumna bhavati | vicakṣe | cakṣeḥ saṃpadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | anarvan | ṛ gatau | asmādanyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante iti dṛśigrahaṇasya vidhyaṅkaropasaṃgrahārthatvādvanevanip | arva gamanaṃ viṣayaṃ pratyenayornāstīti bahuvrīhau nañsvabhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | supāṃ sulugiti dvivacanasya luk | chāndaso nalopābhāvaḥ ‖ [small type; read letter by letter; marked [?] where doubtful]

Sense (mine): "Ṛjrāśva was a royal sage, son of Vṛṣāgiri. Near him the Aśvins' vehicle, the ass, stood in the form of a she-wolf. And he, for her food, cut up and gave 101 of his own sheep — as another mantra shows: 'ṛjrāśvaḥ śatam ekaṃ ca meṣān'. His father, [displeased by this deed], made him blind by a curse. The Aśvins, being praised by him, knowing that 'he became blind because of our vehicle', gave him eyes. This is what is said. Here, because the word tat is heard, a yat is to be supplied: that Ṛjrāśva who gave a hundred sheep, cut up in pieces, to the she-wolf vṛkyai that he had himself fed — him, cakṣadānam — kṣad is a verb of eating — who, to cut them up, cut into pieces and gave: his father by a curse made blind, devoid of sight. O Nāsatyas, of true nature, leaders of truth, physicians, healers of the gods — ‘the Aśvins are indeed physicians of the gods’ (Ai. Br. 1-18 as read [?]) — O Dasras, beautiful ones (or so named), anarvan — for the sake of him who could not move for seeing, because of the father's curse — akṣī, the two eyes, vicakṣe, able to see in various ways, ā adhattam, you placed for that Ṛjrāśva."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"(yaḥ — which Ṛjrāśva); śatam — a hundred; meṣān — sheep; vṛkyai — to the she-wolf (he gave); tam — that; cakṣadānam — one who cut and gave; ṛjrāśvam — Ṛjrāśva; pitā — his father; andham — blind (by curse, deprived of sight); cakāra — made; nāsatyā — of true nature; bhiṣajau — physicians (of the gods); dasrā — O beautiful Aśvin deities (you two) — for Ṛjrāśva; anarvan — (because of blindness) devoid of power to move toward objects (that had to be seen)

original p. 266

— (who had been); akṣī — both eyes; tasmai — to that Ṛjrāśva; vicakṣe — (so as to be) seeing; ādhattam — you made."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The ass, the vehicle of the Aśvin deities, was near Ṛjrāśva in the form of a she-wolf. For her food, that Ṛjrāśva cut up a hundred sheep and gave them to that she-wolf. His father, angered by this, cursed Ṛjrāśva and made him blind. You, of true nature, physicians of the deities, beautiful ones, made the eyes of Ṛjrāśva — who, being blind, was unable to go towards things — capable of sight."

English Translation (as printed)

When his father caused Rijrashwa, as he was giving to a she-wolf a hundred sheep cut up in pieces, to become blind, you, Dasras, physicians (of the gods), gave him eyes (that had been) unable to find their way, with which he might see.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

शतं मेषान् वृक्ये — Śataṃ meṣān vṛkye — "ātmanā poṣitāyai vṛkastriyai śakalīkṛtya prādāt": "a royal sage named Ṛjrāśva, son of the king named Vṛṣāgiri; the vehicle of the Aśvin deities, an ass, was near him in the form of a she-wolf. To feed it, Ṛjrāśva cut up a hundred sheep and used them. These sheep belonged to the subjects; but as the prince did this without their consent, since it was unfavourable to the people, the father of Ṛjrāśva, in his displeasure, cursed him, to become blind. By the father's curse Ṛjrāśva's eyes went. Then he praised the Aśvin deities. They, knowing that he had become blind because of their vehicle, made his eyes come as before and gave him the power of sight: such is the Itihāsa told in this Ṛk. The same Itihāsa [is told] in —

शतं मेषान्वृक्ये मामहानं तमः प्रणीतमृषिणा पित्रा । अक्षी ऋज्राश्वे अश्विनावधत्तं ज्योतिरन्धाय चक्रथुर्विचक्षे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१६ [as read; the words and the number as printed here, with its first pāda reading mamahānam… [?]])

śataṃ meṣānvṛkye māmahānaṃ tamaḥ praṇītamṛṣiṇā pitrā | akṣī ṛjrāśve aśvināvadhattaṃ jyotirandhāya cakrathurvicakṣe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-16 [as read; the words and the number as printed here, with its first pāda reading mamahānam… [?]])

original p. 267

शुनमन्धाय भरमह्वयत्सा वृकीरश्विना वृषणा नरेति । जारः कनीन इव चक्षदान ऋज्राश्वः शतमेकं च मेषान् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१८ [as read])

śunamandhāya bharamahvayatsā vṛkīraśvinā vṛṣaṇā nareti | jāraḥ kanīna iva cakṣadāna ṛjrāśvaḥ śatamekaṃ ca meṣān ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-18 [as read])

— it is related in these Ṛks. Here the "śataṃ meṣān" — a hundred sheep — is stated; and in the mantra beginning śunam andhāya it is stated 'śatam ekaṃ ca meṣān' [a hundred and one sheep]. Skandasvāmin too tells this Itihāsa in his bhāṣya in the same way. The name of this Ṛjrāśva is found in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-17 [as read], where Indra is said to have favoured him; and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-16 [as read] this Ṛjrāśva is said to be one of those who are Ambarīṣa, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna, Surādhas and Ṛjrāśva, sons of the king named Vṛṣāgir. His name is not mentioned again in the Ṛgveda."

चक्षदानम् — Cakṣadānam — "kṣadatir attikarmā": "kṣad is a verb of eating; here, in the sense of cutting into pieces (śakalīkaraṇa): 'having cut into pieces and given'. The root kṣad has the meaning bhakṣaṇa 'eating'; here it is used in the sense 'make into small pieces'; the meaning is 'cutting into little pieces or bits and giving'."

नासत्या — Nāsatyā — "of true nature, or leaders of truth, or those who take [a man] along the true path: the meaning of this word has been explained in the first Ṛk of this very sūkta."

भिषजा — Bhiṣajā — "devānāṃ vaidyau": "aśvinau vai devānāṃ bhiṣajau (Ai. Br. 1-18 as read [?]; Tai. Saṃ. 2-?-?-? [?]) — thus the śruti: the physicians of the gods are the Aśvin deities, as stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā."

दस्रा — Dasrā — "darśanīyau vaitatsaṃjñau vā": "the name dasra is well known for the Aśvin deities; or the meaning 'having a beautiful form' may also be given for dasra."

अनर्वन् — Anarvan — "anarvaṇe draṣṭavyaṃ prati pitṛśāpād gamanarahite": "in respect of what should be seen, because of the father's curse, there is no movement of sight. Skandasvāmin for this word —

अर्तेर्गत्यर्थस्येदं रूपम् । अर्वन्तं प्रत्याश्रितता या न गतः सोऽनर्वा । अनर्वणि अनन्याश्रिते स्वायत्ते । पित्रा शापेनासेतुमन्धकम् इत्यर्थः ॥

artergatyarthasyedaṃ rūpam | arvantaṃ pratyāśritatā yā na gataḥ so 'narvā | anarvaṇi ananyāśrite svāyatte | pitrā śāpenāsetumandhakam ityarthaḥ ‖

original p. 268

"… formed from the root ṛ (ṛ gatau, of the sense 'to go'), the word arvan conveys the meaning 'one who has movement/independence (svatantra)'. The one who has no independence, other than that of others, is anarvan. 'One who is without any other support and who is not under his own control is also called by the word anarvan.' He explains that the Aśvin deities, when Ṛjrāśva, in such a state, was unable to escape the curse of his father, gave him [new] eyes and protected him. Citing the Ṛk

याभिः शचीभिर्वृषणा परावृजं प्रान्धं श्रोणं चक्षस एतवे कृथः । याभिर्वर्तिकां ग्रसितामुमुक्षतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-८ [as read])

yābhiḥ śacībhirvṛṣaṇā parāvṛjaṃ prāndhaṃ śroṇaṃ cakṣasa etave kṛthaḥ | yābhirvartikāṃ grasitāmumukṣataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-8 [as read])

— he explains that this meaning is stated here. Yāska:

अनर्वा प्रत्यृतोऽन्यस्मिन् । अनर्वमप्रत्यृतमन्यस्मिन् ॥ (नि. ६-३३ [as read])

anarvā pratyṛto 'nyasmin | anarvamapratyṛtamanyasmin ‖ (ni. 6-33 [as read])

— 'anarvā: one who is dependent on no other' — explaining the meaning as one who is in his own independence, resting on another, he cites

अनर्वाणं वृषभं मन्द्रजिह्वं बृहस्पतिं वर्धया नव्यमर्कैः । गाथान्यः सुरुचो यस्य देवा आशृण्वन्ति नवमानस्य मर्ताः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१९०-१ [as read])

anarvāṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ mandrajihvaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ vardhayā navyamarkaiḥ | gāthānyaḥ suruco yasya devā āśṛṇvanti navamānasya martāḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-190-1 [as read])

In this Ṛk the word anarvan is used in the sense of 'one who is not under another's control'. Sāyaṇa: 'arva gamanaṃ viṣayaṃ prati enayor nāsti iti bahuvrīhau anarvaṇī' — arva means 'going'; since the eyes have not the power of looking — which is going [towards the object] — they are anarvaṇī: 'the two that have no power of seeing, or have no sight, or are blind eyes'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 16; grammar page, noted briefly)

vṛkye (vṛka is a dog of the forest; its feminine is vṛkī; since it denotes a class (jāti), in the feminine jāter astrīviṣayād ayopadhāt, Pā. 4-1-63 as read [?], ṅīṣ; yasyeti ca, Pā. 6-4-148 as read [?], elision of the a; the dative singular following, by jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam, a statement, āṇ nadyāḥ, Pā. 7-3-112 as read [?], the āṭ augment does not arise, so yaṇ substitution by the rule; in the place of the udātta a yaṇ; its following [syllable] being anudātta, by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ anudāttasya, Pā. 8-2-4 as read [?], it takes svarita).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.17) Bhāṣya of Ṛk 17, continued from p. 270:

सविता स्वदुहितरं सूर्याभ्यां सोमाय राज्ञे प्रदातुमैच्छत् । तां सूर्यां सर्वे देवा वरयामासुः । तेऽन्योन्यमूचुः । आदित्यमवधिं कृत्वाजिं धावाम । योऽस्माकं मध्य उज्जेष्यति तस्येयं भविष्यतीति । तत्राश्विनावुदजयताम् । सा च सूर्या जितवतोस्तयो रथमारुरोह । अत्र प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञे दुहितरं प्रायच्छत् । ऐ. ब्रा. ४-२ । इत्यादिकं ब्राह्मणमनुसन्धेयम् । इदं चाख्यानं सूर्याविवाहस्य स्तावकेन सत्येनोत्तभिता भूमिरिति सूक्तेन विस्पष्टमुपलभ्यते । हे अश्विना वां युवयोर्‍रथं कार्ष्मेव । कार्ष्मशब्दः काष्ठवाचि । यथा काष्ठमाजिधावनस्यावधितया निर्दिष्टं लक्ष्यमाशुगामिनी कश्चित्सर्वेभ्यः [?]

savitā svaduhitaraṃ sūryābhyāṃ somāya rājñe pradātumaicchat | tāṃ sūryāṃ sarve devā varayāmāsuḥ | te 'nyonyamūcuḥ | ādityamavadhiṃ kṛtvājiṃ dhāvāma | yo 'smākaṃ madhya ujjeṣyati tasyeyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | tatrāśvināvudajayatām | sā ca sūryā jitavatostayo rathamāruroha | atra prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchat | ai. brā. 4-2 | ityādikaṃ brāhmaṇamanusandheyam | idaṃ cākhyānaṃ sūryāvivāhasya stāvakena satyenottabhitā bhūmiriti sūktena vispaṣṭamupalabhyate | he aśvinā vāṃ yuvayorrathaṃ kārṣmeva | kārṣmaśabdaḥ kāṣṭhavāci | yathā kāṣṭhamājidhāvanasyāvadhitayā nirdiṣṭaṃ lakṣyamāśugāminī kaścitsarvebhyaḥ [?]

original p. 271

… धावद्भ्यः पूर्वं प्राप्नोति । एवमेव सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वमर्वता शीघ्रगामिनाश्वेन करणभूतेन युवाभ्यां जयन्ती जेयमानाशी सूर्यस्य सवितुर्दुहिता सूर्यारुढवती । विश्वे सर्व इतरे देवा एतदारोहणस्थानं हृद्भिर्हृदयैरन्वमन्यन्त । अन्वजानन् । तदानीं हे नासत्यावश्विनौ श्रिया ऋक्सहस्रलाभरूपया सम्पदा कान्त्या वा युवां सं सचेथे । सङ्गच्छेथे ॥ जयन्ती । जि जये धातुः । वृत्त्यर्थे । पदन्नित्यादिना हृदयशब्दस्य हृद्भावः । सचेथे । षच समवाये । सश्चतेः । स्वरितेत्त्वादात्मनेपदम् ॥ [grammar tail in small type, partly doubtful [?]]

… dhāvadbhyaḥ pūrvaṃ prāpnoti | evameva sarvebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvamarvatā śīghragāmināśvena karaṇabhūtena yuvābhyāṃ jayantī jeyamānāśī sūryasya saviturduhitā sūryāruḍhavatī | viśve sarva itare devā etadārohaṇasthānaṃ hṛdbhirhṛdayairanvamanyanta | anvajānan | tadānīṃ he nāsatyāvaśvinau śriyā ṛksahasralābharūpayā sampadā kāntyā vā yuvāṃ saṃ sacethe | saṅgacchethe ‖ jayantī | ji jaye dhātuḥ | vṛttyarthe | padannityādinā hṛdayaśabdasya hṛdbhāvaḥ | sacethe | ṣaca samavāye | saścateḥ | svaritettvādātmanepadam ‖ [grammar tail in small type, partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "… [as a runner] reaches [the goal] before all the runners, so, before all the gods, with the swift-going horse as the instrument, jayantī, winning by you two, the daughter of the Sun, of Savitṛ, ātiṣṭhat, mounted the chariot. Viśve — all the other gods anvamanyanta hṛdbhiḥ, assented with their hearts, to this mounting. Then, O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, śriyā — by splendour, in the form of obtaining a thousand Ṛks, or by beauty — you saṃ sacethe, were united."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"(he aśvinau — O Aśvin deities); kāṣṭheva — as (one reaches) a place fixed as the limit; arvatā — by your swift-going horse; jayantī — the one who was won; sūryasya — of the Sun; duhitā — daughter; vām — your; ratham — chariot; ā atiṣṭhat — mounted; viśve — all the others; devāḥ — gods; hṛdbhiḥ — with the heart; anvamanyanta — approved; (tadānīm — then); śriyā — with splendour (with beauty, with fame); sam sacethe u — you two were united."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Nāsatyas, the daughter of the Sun, won by your swift horse, as one wins by reaching the place fixed as the goal in a race, mounted your chariot. The other gods too, all of them, approved. (Therefore) you became possessed of fame."

English Translation (as printed)

The daughter of the sun ascended your car, (like a runner) to a goal : when you won (the race) with your swift horse, all the gods looked on with (anxious heart), and you, Nasatyas, were associated with glory.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

काष्र्मेव — Kārṣmeva — "kārṣmaśabdaḥ kāṣṭhavācī": "as one who runs reaches, before all the other runners, a goal fixed as the end-point of the race, a limit; so before all the gods [the Aśvins]. The word kārṣma means 'a post (kaṭṭige)'. When there is a contest, in order to know who is superior and who is inferior among those taking part, or who is more excellent, a particular tree standing on a fixed spot is chosen. Those who run quickly and touch (reach) that tree are considered to have won. Such a fixed place is here called by the word kārṣma. This is current in games. In English they say (Goal), the place fixed for conveying victory or defeat. To know the one who excels among the competitors, with many persons present a single goal is fixed; and the one who reaches that first is held to be the best of all. In this way, to know who is the best among themselves, the deities appointed Sūryā as the goal; the Aśvin deities won it; from this it was decided that their excellence — or superiority — over the other deities is established: this is described here. Savitṛ, wishing to give his daughter named Sūryā in marriage to King Soma, when this was settled the deities came to choose her. Then they all assembled and agreed among themselves: 'We shall fight [run]; the Sūryā-devī will be the prize of the winner in the contest'. In the contest that then took place among the other deities and the Aśvin deities, the Aśvins prevailed. The goddess Sūryā mounted the chariot of the Aśvin deities, declared the best of all the other deities. This Itihāsa is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as 'prajāpatir vai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchat' (Ai. Br. 4-2 as read [?]) and is narrated here. Moreover this upākhyāna is told in detail in the 'Satyenottabhitā bhūmiḥ' sūkta, the 85th sūkta of the tenth maṇḍala. Besides this, Skandasvāmin [explains]: 'kriyate teditī kārṣmaṃ śubhāśubhalakṣaṇaṃ karma tadyathā karṣāmā…' [reading doubtful [?]] — 'the action that is done, of the nature of good or bad, [the sense is:] Sūryā, in the manner that a farmer comes and sows, herself came and mounted the chariot of the Aśvin deities' — and he explains kārṣma as 'that which is made'." The page begins with the end of the special topic: the first lines — "… [the word] kārṣma is in that sense of 'a post'" — and carries on as above.

original p. 272

अर्वता — Arvatā — "śīghram avadhiṃ prāpnuvatā yuṣmadīyena aśvena karaṇabhūtena": "your horse which is the means for reaching, very swiftly, everything that is to be reached. The word arvan is stated among the twenty-six [as read] words for horse (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]); hence 'horse'. In the Nirukta 'arvā — gamanaśīlatvād' ['ṛṇotyarvā'?] is explained as 'one who has the nature of going' (Ni. 2-?? as read [?])."

श्रिया — Śriyā — "ṛksahasralābharūpayā sampadā kāntyā vā": "in the Sūryā-vivāha (Sūryā's marriage) they gave a thousand Ṛks as a fitting gift; therefore [śriyā means] endowed with the wealth in the form of obtaining a thousand mantras; or, because of the marriage of Sūryā, the maiden, the Aśvin deities are possessed of beauty — thus the meaning."

original p. 273

vām (yuṣmad and asmad in the genitive, ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vāṃnāvau, Pā. 8-1-20 as read [?]; the vām substitute, the unaccented one, in the special case); sūryasya (suvati karmaṇi lokaṃ preyati iti sūryaḥ; sū "to impel"; rājasūyasūryamṛṣodyarucyakupyakṛṣṭapacyāvyathyāḥ, Pā. 3-1-114 as read [?], kyap is irregularly formed with the elision; ruṭ ... nipātita; since the suffix is pit, the root accent remains); atiṣṭhat (ṣṭhā "to cease from motion"; laṅ 3rd singular; pāghrādhmā…, Pā. 7-3-78 as read [?], tiṣṭha substituted; the augment aṭ; nighāta after an accented word); arvatā (ṛ "to go"; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante, Pā. 3-2-75 as read [?], vanip; arvaṇas tṛṇasāvanañaḥ [arvaṇas tasāv anañaḥ], Pā. 6-4-127 as read [?], tṛ is a final substitute; the instrumental singular); jayantī (ji "to conquer"; anudāttet… vṛttyayo bahulam, Pā. 3-1-?? as read [?], śatṛ in the laṭ sense; in the feminine, ugitaś ca, Pā. 4-1-6 as read [?], ṅīp; ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ, Pā. 7-1-70 as read [?], num; since adupadeśa, the sārvadhātuka is unaccented, hence tāsyanudāttet…, Pā. 6-1-186 as read [?], the root accent remains); amanyanta (manu "to know", divādi; laṅ 3rd plural; nighāta); hṛdbhiḥ (the word hṛdaya; when the instrumental plural follows, padannomāsa…, Pā. 6-1-63 as read [?], hṛd substitute; ūḍidaṃpadādi…, Pā. 6-1-171 as read [?], the ending's accent); śriyā (when the instrumental singular follows, aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvoriyaṅuvaṅau, Pā. 6-4-77 as read [?], iy; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ, Pā. 6-1-168 as read [?], the ending's accent).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.18)

हे अश्विनौ हयन्ता स्तुतिभिराहूयमानौ युवां भरद्वाजाय सम्भ्रियमाणहविर्लक्षणान्नाय यजमानाय दिवोदासायैतत्संज्ञाय राजर्षयेऽभीष्टं फलं दातुं वर्तिस्तदीयं गृहं यद्यदायातं । आगच्छतं तदानीं रेवद्धनयुक्तमन्नं वां युवयोः सचनः सेवनो रथ उवाह । तस्मै दिवोदासाय प्रापयामास । अपि च तस्मिन्रथे वृषभो ऽनड्वान् शिंशुमारो ग्राहश्च परस्परविरुद्धावपि स्वसामर्थ्यप्रकटनाय युक्तौ वाहनतया संयुक्तावास्ताम् ॥ दिवोदासाय । दिवश्च दासे षष्ठ्या आलुग्वक्तव्यः । का. ६-३-२१-२ । इत्यलुक् । दिवोदासादीनां छन्दस्यपसंख्यानमिति पूर्वपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । भरद्वाजाय । भृञ् भरणे । अस्माद्यत्यनिशत्र [?] प्रत्ययः कर्मणि । शतुश्छन्दस्युभयथेत्यर्धधातुकत्वेन लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वाभावात्प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वं । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । हयन्ता । हय गतौ । कर्मणि लटो व्यत्ययेन शपि । बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणं । शपि गुणे छान्दसो ऽयादेशः । रेवत् । रयिशब्दान्मतुप् । रयेर्मतौ बहुलमिति सम्प्रसारणं । छन्दसीरः इति मतुपो वत्वम् । रयिशब्दाच्च । का. ६-१-१२३-१ । इति मतुप उदात्तत्वम् । सचनः । षच सेवने । अनुदात्तेत्त्वाच्च हलादेरिति युच् । युक्ता । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः ॥

he aśvinau hayantā stutibhirāhūyamānau yuvāṃ bharadvājāya sambhriyamāṇahavirlakṣaṇānnāya yajamānāya divodāsāyaitatsaṃjñāya rājarṣaye 'bhīṣṭaṃ phalaṃ dātuṃ vartistadīyaṃ gṛhaṃ yadyadāyātaṃ | āgacchataṃ tadānīṃ revaddhanayuktamannaṃ vāṃ yuvayoḥ sacanaḥ sevano ratha uvāha | tasmai divodāsāya prāpayāmāsa | api ca tasminrathe vṛṣabho 'naḍvān śiṃśumāro grāhaśca parasparaviruddhāvapi svasāmarthyaprakaṭanāya yuktau vāhanatayā saṃyuktāvāstām ‖ divodāsāya | divaśca dāse ṣaṣṭhyā ālugvaktavyaḥ | kā. 6-3-21-2 | ityaluk | divodāsādīnāṃ chandasyapasaṃkhyānamiti pūrvapadādyudāttatvam | bharadvājāya | bhṛñ bharaṇe | asmādyatyaniśatra [?] pratyayaḥ karmaṇi | śatuśchandasyubhayathetyardhadhātukatvena lasārvadhātukānudāttatvābhāvātpratyayādyudāttatvaṃ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | hayantā | haya gatau | karmaṇi laṭo vyatyayena śapi | bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇaṃ | śapi guṇe chāndaso 'yādeśaḥ | revat | rayiśabdānmatup | rayermatau bahulamiti samprasāraṇaṃ | chandasīraḥ iti matupo vatvam | rayiśabdācca | kā. 6-1-123-1 | iti matupa udāttatvam | sacanaḥ | ṣaca sevane | anudāttettvācca halāderiti yuc | yuktā | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterākāraḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, hayantā — being invited with praise — you, to bharadvāja, 'the one who maintains food (vāja)' — the sacrificer who prepares oblations in the form of food, Divodāsa, the royal sage of this name — when you went to the vartiḥ, the house, to give the desired fruit, then your sacanaḥ (serviceable) chariot uvāha — carried (and brought to that Divodāsa) revat, wealth-possessing food. Further, in that chariot a vṛṣabha (bull) and a śiṃśumāra (porpoise [or crocodile/grāha]), though mutually opposed, were yoked, to make manifest their own power, as vehicles."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; hayantā — you two who were called with praise; bharadvājāya — [to him] who gave oblations; divodāsāya — to the royal sage named Divodāsa (to give him the desired fruit); vartiḥ — [his] house; yat — when; āyātam — you went; revat — wealth-possessing (food); vām — of you; sacanaḥ — helpful; rathaḥ — chariot; uvāha — carried; vṛṣabhaḥ ca — the bull; śiṃśumāraḥ ca — and the porpoise; yuktā — were yoked together (by your power)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, you, who were called with praise, when you went to the house of the royal sage named Divodāsa, who had prepared oblations, to give the desired fruit, carried wealth-possessing food in your helpful chariot. (Then) a bull and a porpoise were yoked together to your chariot by your power."

original p. 276

English Translation (as printed)

When, Ashwins, being invited, you went to his dwelling, (to give due rewards) to Divodasa, offering oblations, then, your helping chariot conveyed (food and) treasure, and the bull and the porpoise were yoked together.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

भरद्वाजाय दिवोदासाय — Bharadvājāya divodāsāya — "sambhriyamāṇahavirlakṣaṇānnāya yajamānāya etatsaṃjñāya rājarṣaye": "the royal sage named Divodāsa, to perform a sacrifice, collected the substances suitable for the sacrifice so that they might be useful in the rites, and invited the Aśvin deities. The Aśvin deities came to this king's house to fulfil his wish. When they came with their chariot yoked to a bull and a porpoise — an aquatic creature — these two creatures, naturally opposed to one another, worked with a single intention without quarrelling. Sāyaṇa explains that by this the greatness of the Aśvin deities is made manifest."

वर्तिः — Vartiḥ — "Sāyaṇa explains the word vartis as 'house'; Skandasvāmin as 'vartanyā mārgeṇa', 'by the road'. And accordingly —

दिवोदासाय इति पदस्य दिवोदासार्थं शम्बरवधे दिवोदासस्य साहाय्यं कर्तुं शम्बर इत्यसुरं निग्रहे [?] । तदेतत्कुत्सेनाप्युक्तम् —

divodāsāya iti padasya divodāsārthaṃ śambaravadhe divodāsasya sāhāyyaṃ kartuṃ śambara ityasuraṃ nigrahe [?] | tadetatkutsenāpyuktam —

— for the word divodāsāya, for the sake of Divodāsa, in the killing of Śambara, to help Divodāsa, by subduing the Asura named Śambara: so he explains the meaning; and this is also said by Kutsa — saying that the ṛṣi Kutsa too tells this matter, he cites

याभिर्नुमामितिथिग्वं केशोजुवं दिवोदासं शम्बरहत्य आवतम् । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१४ [as read; the first words printed doubtfully [?]])

yābhirnumāmitithigvaṃ keśojuvaṃ divodāsaṃ śambarahatya āvatam | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-14 [as read; the first words printed doubtfully [?]])

— this Ṛk. Likewise for bharadvājāya — to a man who praises [you] desiring wealth, the Aśvins having taken wealth, substance, for the sake of giving wealth to the king who prays to them — thus he explains."

दिवोदासाय — Divodāsāya — "Divodāsa or Divodāsa Atithigva was a king, famed in the times of the Vedas, who was a very well-known king. He was the son of Vadhryaśva [as read], and again [the father of] Sudāsa …" continues on p. 277

original p. 277

"… son of Vadhryaśva [as read]. This Sudāsa was a famous royal sage of the Tṛtsu line in the Bharata clan. Therefore, with Divodāsa, 'Sudāsa [who is called] the Bharata' (Ṛ. Saṃ. numerals not readable [?]) is said, in several Ṛks such as these, to have been opposed to the enemy kings, together with Turvaśa and the Yadus. His chief enemy was the Asura Śambara, or Dāsa: this Śambara is said to be the chief of the people living in the hills (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-?-? ; 2-?-? ; 4-?-? ; 6-?-? [numerals not readable [?]]). That Divodāsa overcame him many times is described in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-14 [as read], 1-116-18, 1-130-?, 2-19-6 [as read], 4-26-3 [as read] and others, up to about ten [as the print counts] a run of small reference numerals, not read reliably [?]. Because he specially worshipped Agni, the name of Agni is derived from his name in the Ṛks 6-?-? [?] and others. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-?-? ; 1-?-? ; 6-?-? [?] and other places this name is found in the genealogy of the ṛṣi Bharadvāja, or of that ṛṣi's descendants. In the Ṛk 6-47-22 [as read] and in some Ṛks after it, there is a description of this Divodāsa's fighting with Paṇis, Pārāvatas and Bṛsaya on the bank of the Sarasvatī. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-10 [as read] the plural word divodāsebhiḥ is used, which indicates Divodāsa's descendants or his subjects. The name of Divodāsa is not found in the third, fifth, ninth and tenth maṇḍalas."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.19)

हे नासत्यावश्विनौ सुक्षत्रं शोभनबलं रयिं धनं स्वपत्यं शोभनैः पुत्रादिभिरुपेतं सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्योपेतमायुः । अन्ननामैतत् । एवंगुणविशिष्टमन्नं च वहन्ता धारयन्तौ युवां समनसा समानमनस्कौ सन्तौ जह्नावीं जह्नोर्महर्षेः सम्बन्धिनीं प्रजामायातं । अभिमुख्येनागच्छतं । कीदृशीं । वाजैर्बलैरन्नैर्वोपेतां । अह्नः । अत्राहःशब्देन तत्काले सवनं लक्ष्यते । तस्य प्रातःसवनादिरूपेण त्रिधा विभक्तं भागमंशं दधतीं बिभ्रतीम् । अनुसवनं हविर्भिर्यजमानामित्यर्थः ॥ सुक्षत्रं । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । सुवीर्यं । वीरवीर्यौ चेति बहुव्रीहावुत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । जह्नावीम् । जह्नुशब्दात्तस्येदमित्यर्थे ऽण् । टिड्ढाणञिति ङीप् । जाह्नवीशब्दस्य दीर्घयोर्विनिमयः । पृषोदरादित्वात् । उक्तं च । वर्णागमो वर्णविपर्ययश्च । का. ६-३-१०९ । इति अत एव मध्योदात्तत्वम् ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

he nāsatyāvaśvinau sukṣatraṃ śobhanabalaṃ rayiṃ dhanaṃ svapatyaṃ śobhanaiḥ putrādibhirupetaṃ suvīryaṃ śobhanavīryopetamāyuḥ | annanāmaitat | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭamannaṃ ca vahantā dhārayantau yuvāṃ samanasā samānamanaskau santau jahnāvīṃ jahnormaharṣeḥ sambandhinīṃ prajāmāyātaṃ | abhimukhyenāgacchataṃ | kīdṛśīṃ | vājairbalairannairvopetāṃ | ahnaḥ | atrāhaḥśabdena tatkāle savanaṃ lakṣyate | tasya prātaḥsavanādirūpeṇa tridhā vibhaktaṃ bhāgamaṃśaṃ dadhatīṃ bibhratīm | anusavanaṃ havirbhiryajamānāmityarthaḥ ‖ sukṣatraṃ | bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | suvīryaṃ | vīravīryau ceti bahuvrīhāvuttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | jahnāvīm | jahnuśabdāttasyedamityarthe 'ṇ | ṭiḍḍhāṇañiti ṅīp | jāhnavīśabdasya dīrghayorvinimayaḥ | pṛṣodarāditvāt | uktaṃ ca | varṇāgamo varṇaviparyayaśca | kā. 6-3-109 | iti ata eva madhyodāttatvam ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, sukṣatram — having good strength — rayim, wealth, svapatyam — endowed with good sons and the rest — suvīryam — endowed with good vigour — āyuḥ (a name of food): carrying (vahantā) food endowed with such qualities, you two, samanasā — of one mind — jahnāvīm, [the subjects] belonging to the great ṛṣi Jahnu — ā yātam, come to the front. What are they like? Vājaiḥ — endowed with strengths or foods. Ahnaḥ — here the word ahar indicates, by implication, the savana (soma-pressing) of that time; the portion divided threefold as the morning savana and so on; dadhatīm, bearing: [the sacrificers] who with oblations at each savana."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; sukṣatram — endowed with good strength; svapatyam — having good sons; suvīryam — endowed with good vigour; āyuḥ — food; rayim — wealth; vahantā — bringing; samanasā — of one mind; vājaiḥ — with food; ahnaḥ — in the day; tri bhāgam — in the three parts (of the savanas — morning, midday and evening); dadhatīm — bearing; jahnāvīm — the family of the ṛṣi Jahnu (the sacrificers); upa āyātam — come to."

original p. 280

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 19, concluded: "… tri bhāgam — the three kinds of sacrificial acts called the morning-savana, midday-savana and third savana; dadhatīm — which bear (perform); jahnāvīm — turning toward Jahnu the great ṛṣi's progeny; ā yātam — come."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, you both, of one mind, bringing strength, wealth, good offspring and food that gives vigour — you came to the descendants of the great ṛṣi Jahnu, who were performing three sacrificial acts, the Soma-sacrifice [with the three savanas, the morning savana etc.], provided with oblations and the like."

English Translation (as printed)

Nasatyas, bearing strength and wealth with posterity and vigour-sustaining food, you came, with one intention, to the family of Jahnu, (provided) with (sacrificial) viands, and possessing a third portion of the daily offerings).

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

जाह्नवीम् — Jāhnavīm — "jahnoḥ maharṣeḥ sambandhinīṃ prajām": "looking at the progeny (prajā) of the great ṛṣi Jahnu, and having compassion on them, the Aśvin deities with goodwill toward them accept the portions of the oblation that they offer separately at the three savanas — morning, midday and evening — and favour them with long life, strength, health, wealth and excellent progeny: so Sāyaṇa explains. This word jāhnavī is found in the Ṛgveda in this Ṛk too —

पुराणमोकः सख्यं शिवं वां युवोर्नरा द्रविणं जह्नाव्याम् । (ऋ. सं. ३-५८-६ [as read])

purāṇamokaḥ sakhyaṃ śivaṃ vāṃ yuvornarā draviṇaṃ jahnāvyām | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-58-6 [as read])

— and in this Ṛk the word is used so as to suggest also the meaning 'the wife of the great ṛṣi Jahnu'. Though in the Vedas Jahnu is spoken of as a single ṛṣi, in the Purāṇas, beginning with the Viṣṇu [Purāṇa], he is said to be a king in the lunar dynasty.

original p. 281

"Skandasvāmin —

जह्नोर्भार्या धनादिकामा सोमेनायजत् । तस्यै अश्विनावागत्य धनादीन् ददतुः । तदेतदिहोच्यते रयिमित्यादिना । जह्नुऋषेः पत्नी धनादीन् इच्छन्ती सोमयागं कृतवती । तदा अश्विनौ तस्मिन् यज्ञे आगत्य भागं स्वीकृत्य तां धनादिभिः सम्पादितवन्तौ [?]

jahnorbhāryā dhanādikāmā somenāyajat | tasyai aśvināvāgatya dhanādīn dadatuḥ | tadetadihocyate rayimityādinā | jahnuṛṣeḥ patnī dhanādīn icchantī somayāgaṃ kṛtavatī | tadā aśvinau tasmin yajñe āgatya bhāgaṃ svīkṛtya tāṃ dhanādibhiḥ sampāditavantau [?]

— the wife of Jahnu, desiring wealth and the like, performed a Soma-sacrifice; the Aśvins came and gave her wealth and the like: this is told here by rayim and so on. The wife of the ṛṣi Jahnu, wishing for wealth and so on, performed a Soma-sacrifice. Then the Aśvin deities came to that sacrifice, accepted the portions of the oblation, and, as she wished, favoured her with everything: [so] explaining it in one way, Skandasvāmin explains the word jāhnavī as 'the wife of Jahnu' and tells it; and again, 'jahnor apatyaṃ jāhnavī tasya prajā tāṃ balākāśva-kuśika-gādhi-viśvāmitra-prabhṛtikām' — 'the progeny of Jahnu is jāhnavī, [meaning] those beginning with Balākāśva, Kuśika, Gādhi, Viśvāmitra': he explains in another way that in the explanation 'Jahnu's offspring are jāhnavī', the Aśvin deities favoured the sons of Jahnu — Balākāśva, Kuśika, Gādhi and Viśvāmitra — thus giving another account of the meaning.

सुक्षत्रम् — Sukṣatram — "the word kṣatra is stated among the hundred-and-one [as read] names of water (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]). But Skandasvāmin explains 'kṣatram iti balanāma' — the word sukṣatra means 'having good strength' — 'together with the strength that is able to destroy bad demons such as Rākṣasas, which the Asuras and others drive off with their strength'."

रयिम् — Rayim — "dhanam: the word rayi is stated among the hundred-and-one names of water (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]) and also among the twenty-eight [as read] names of wealth (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]). And the Nirukta-writer explains: 'rayir iti dhananāma rāter dānakarmaṇaḥ' (Ni. 4-?? as read [?]): the word rayi, formed from the root rā 'to give', means wealth."

अह्नः त्रिः भागम् — Ahnaḥ triḥ bhāgam — "atra ahaḥśabdena tatkālānuṣṭheyaḥ somayāgo lakṣyate | tasya prātaḥsavanādirūpeṇa tridhā vibhaktaṃ bhāgam anusavanaṃ havirbhir yajamānām": "the word ahar here indicates the Soma sacrifice to be done at that time; the three-fold divided portion [the offering of oblations by the sacrificers at each savana] in the form of the morning savana and the rest. In the Nirukta 'ahaḥ kasmāt | adaḥ sa[?]…' [the Sanskrit is in small type]: because the work done at the time when the Sun shines is done in the day, the word ahar is explained; here the word ahar means the Soma sacrifice done in the day. In this Soma sacrifice, homa and other rites related to sacrifice, such as the extraction of soma-juice, are performed at the three times — morning savana, midday savana and third savana — and the main idea is that the Aśvin deities came to the sacrifices performed by the descendants of Jahnu and accepted the oblation-portions."

original p. 282

pari 'viṣṭam | jāhuṣam | viśvataḥ | sīm | su 'gebhiḥ | naktam | ūhathuḥ | rajaḥ 'bhiḥ | vi 'bhindunā | nāsatyā | rathena | vi | parvatān | ajarayū iti | ayātam ‖ 20 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.20)

जाहुषो नाम कश्चिद्राजा । विश्वतः सर्वतः परिविष्टं शत्रुभिः परिवृतं तं राजानं हे नासत्यावश्विनावजरयू जराऽरहितौ नित्यतरुणौ युवां विभिन्दुना विशेषेण सर्वस्य भेदकेनाश्वीयेन रथेन नक्तं रात्रौ सुगेभिः सुष्ठु गन्तुं शक्यै रजोभी रञ्जकैर्मार्गैरूहथुः । तस्माच्छत्रुसमूहान्निरगमयतम् । सीमिति पूरणार्थः । निर्गतेन तेन सह पर्वतान् शत्रुभिरारोढुमशक्यान् शिलोच्चयान् वियातं । विशेषेणागच्छतं । परिविष्टम् । विश प्रवेशने । कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सुगेभिः । सुदुरोरधिकरण इति गमेर्डः । विभिन्दुना । भिदिर् विदारणे । औणादिक उप्रत्ययो नुमागमश्च । अजरयू । न जरा अजरा । तामात्मन इच्छतः क्यच् । न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येति दीर्घस्योर्निषेधः । क्याच्छन्दसीत्युप्रत्ययः ॥

jāhuṣo nāma kaścidrājā | viśvataḥ sarvataḥ pariviṣṭaṃ śatrubhiḥ parivṛtaṃ taṃ rājānaṃ he nāsatyāvaśvināvajarayū jarā 'rahitau nityataruṇau yuvāṃ vibhindunā viśeṣeṇa sarvasya bhedakenāśvīyena rathena naktaṃ rātrau sugebhiḥ suṣṭhu gantuṃ śakyai rajobhī rañjakairmārgairūhathuḥ | tasmācchatrusamūhānniragamayatam | sīmiti pūraṇārthaḥ | nirgatena tena saha parvatān śatrubhirāroḍhumaśakyān śiloccayān viyātaṃ | viśeṣeṇāgacchataṃ | pariviṣṭam | viśa praveśane | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | sugebhiḥ | suduroradhikaraṇa iti gamerḍaḥ | vibhindunā | bhidir vidāraṇe | auṇādika upratyayo numāgamaśca | ajarayū | na jarā ajarā | tāmātmana icchataḥ kyac | na chandasyaputrasyeti dīrghasyorniṣedhaḥ | kyācchandasītyupratyayaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "Jāhuṣa was a certain king. Him, viśvataḥ — on all sides — pariviṣṭam, surrounded by enemies, O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, ajarayū, free from old age, ever-young — you, with vibhindunā, the splitter of all, the horse-drawn chariot, naktam, by night, by sugebhiḥ, easily traversable, rajobhiḥ, pleasing, roads, carried away (ūhathuḥ). So you brought him out from that mass of enemies. Sīm is a filler. With him thus brought out, you went [over] parvatān, the rocky heights that enemies cannot climb, you went widely."

Grammatical tail (characterized, not transcribed): pariviṣṭam (viś "to enter", kta in the passive; the prefix keeps its accent by gatir anantaraḥ); sugebhiḥ (su-du-ro-'dhikaraṇe: the ḍa suffix after gam); vibhindunā (bhidir "to split", the Uṇādi suffix u and the augment num); ajarayū (na jarā ajarā; tām ātmana icchataḥ — kyac; na chandasy aputrasya, no lengthening; kyāc chandasi, the suffix u).

original p. 284

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"ajarayū — free from old age, ever-young; he nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; viśvataḥ — on all sides; pariviṣṭam — surrounded by enemies; jāhuṣam — the king named Jāhuṣa; vibhindunā — that breaks everything; rathena — by (your) chariot; naktam — at night; sugebhiḥ — easily traversable; rajobhiḥ — by routes; ūhathuḥ — you took him, freeing him from the enemies; parvatān — to mountains (inaccessible to the enemies); vi āyātam — you brought him."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O ever-young Aśvin deities, the king named Jāhuṣa, surrounded by enemies on all sides, you carried by night, in your chariot that breaks all [obstacles], by (your power) easily passable routes, and went with him to the mountains (inaccessible to the enemies)."

English Translation (as printed)

Undecaying Nasatyas, you bore away by night, in your foe-overwhelming car, Jahusha, surrounded on every side by (enemies), through practicable roads, and went to (inaccessible) mountains.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

जाहुषम् — Jāhuṣam — "jāhuṣo nāma kaścid rājā": "Sāyaṇa explains that Jāhuṣa is a king named Jāhuṣa. Skandasvāmin —

जाहुषो नाम ऋषिः वृद्धः वृद्धया भार्ययो वृद्धैश्च पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः परिवृतो देवानीजे । तं दृष्ट्वासुराः तुङ्गैः पर्वतैः परिक्षिप्ते मरुदेशे प्राक्षिपन् । स तेको प्रवृद्धत्वात् स्वयं निर्गन्तुमशक्नुवन्महाकारुणिकावश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तमश्विनावागत्य निशैवैव रात्र्यामश्वीयेन रथेन तान् पर्वतानतिक्रामयां चक्रतुः इति ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

jāhuṣo nāma ṛṣiḥ vṛddhaḥ vṛddhayā bhāryayo vṛddhaiśca putrapautrādibhiḥ parivṛto devānīje | taṃ dṛṣṭvāsurāḥ tuṅgaiḥ parvataiḥ parikṣipte marudeśe prākṣipan | sa teko pravṛddhatvāt svayaṃ nirgantumaśaknuvanmahākāruṇikāvaśvinau tuṣṭāva | tamaśvināvāgatya niśaivaiva rātryāmaśvīyena rathena tān parvatānatikrāmayāṃ cakratuḥ iti ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

— 'Jāhuṣa, a ṛṣi, old, surrounded by his old wife and by old sons, grandsons and others, sacrificed to the gods. Seeing him, the Asuras threw him into a desert region surrounded by high mountains. He, being old, unable to come out by himself, praised the Aśvins, the greatly compassionate. The Aśvins came and, by night, in a chariot drawn by horses, carried him over those mountains.' In Kannada: a ṛṣi named Jāhuṣa, an old man, performed a sacrifice to the gods together with his old wife and with sons and grandsons, each of whom was old. The Rākṣasas, seeing this, took the ṛṣi to a desert surrounded by high mountains and placed him there. He, being very old, unable to leave that place, praised the Aśvin deities, supremely compassionate

original p. 285

— (with a hymn). Hearing his praise, the Aśvin deities came in a single night in their chariot and took Jāhuṣa across those mountains and saved him: thus the Itihāsa is told."

अजरयू — Ajarayū — "jararahitau nityataruṇau": "'na jarā ajarā tām ātmana icchataḥ': jarā is old age; they who have none — the Aśvin deities — are always young, endowed with youth: this is the meaning. In the word jarayū there is the suffix yu; it has come in the sense of matup [possession].

Yāska:

इदंयुरिदं कामयमानो ऽथापि तद्द्वयर्थे भाष्यते वसुंयुरिन्द्रो वसुमानित्यर्थः । अश्वयुर्गव्यू रथयुर्वसूयुरित्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (नि. ६-३१ [as read])

idaṃyuridaṃ kāmayamāno 'thāpi taddvayarthe bhāṣyate vasuṃyurindro vasumānityarthaḥ | aśvayurgavyū rathayurvasūyurityapi nigamo bhavati ‖ (ni. 6-31 [as read])

— Skandasvāmin, explaining Yāska's explanation, says that the word ajarayū has the sense of matup like the words idaṃyu, aśvayu, gavyu, rathayu [in 'possessing this', 'possessing horses', and so on]; and he cites the Ṛk —

इन्द्रो अश्रायि सुध्यो निरेके पज्रेषु स्तोमो दुर्यो न यूपः । अश्वयुर्गव्यू रथयुर्वसूयुरिन्द्र इद्रायः क्षयति प्रयन्ता ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५३-१४ [as read])

indro aśrāyi sudhyo nireke pajreṣu stomo duryo na yūpaḥ | aśvayurgavyū rathayurvasūyurindra idrāyaḥ kṣayati prayantā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-53-14 [as read])

and explains the word pariviṣṭam: by 'surrounded on all sides' (viśvataḥ), since pari only conveys the meaning of the root, and since [taking pari as with the sense of surrounding] the word viśvataḥ too would be repetition, he says that the meaning 'pervaded by old age' should be taken (vyāpta-jarayā), combining the prefix with the root's meaning: so 'by old age pervaded'."

रजोभिः — Rajobhiḥ — "rajaśabdo 'tra tejovacanaḥ tejasvibhiḥ śīghragāmibhir ity arthaḥ": "the word rajas here denotes lustre: [the meaning] by those that are brilliant and go swiftly. Since it is an adjective of sugebhiḥ, the word suga here is used for horse: therefore it is described that the Aśvin deities saved Jāhuṣa with a chariot to which swift, lustrous, strong horses were yoked."

pariviṣṭam (viś "to enter"; kta in the passive by niṣṭhā, Pā. 3-2-102 as read [?]; vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśām, Pā. 8-2-36 as read [?], ṣa for the ś of the root; as a consequence …
