॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.21)

एकस्या वस्तोरावतं रणाय वशमश्विना सनये सहस्रा । निरहतं दुच्छुना इन्द्रवन्ता पृथुश्रवसो वृषणावराती ॥ २१ ॥

ekasyā vastorāvataṃ raṇāya vaśamaśvinā sanaye sahasrā | nirahataṃ ducchunā indravantā pṛthuśravaso vṛṣaṇāvarātī ‖ 21 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.21)

एकस्याः । वस्तोः । आवतम् । रणाय । वशम् । अश्विना । सनये । सहस्रा । निः । अहतम् । दुच्छुनाः । इन्द्रवन्ता । पृथुश्रवसः । वृषणौ । अरातीः ॥ २१ ॥

ekasyāḥ | vastoḥ | āvatam | raṇāya | vaśam | aśvinā | sanaye | sahasrā | niḥ | ahatam | ducchunāḥ | indravantā | pṛthuśravasaḥ | vṛṣaṇau | arātīḥ ‖ 21 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.21)

हे अश्विना वशमेतत्संज्ञमृषिमेकस्या वस्तोरेकस्मिन्नहनि रणाय रमणीयाय सहस्रा सहस्रसंख्याकाय सनये धनलाभायावतम् । अरक्षतम् । स ऋषिः प्रकृष्टं यथा सहस्रसंख्यं धनमभते तथा रक्षितवन्ताविस्यर्थः । अपि च हे वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारावश्विनौ इन्द्रवन्ता इन्द्रेण संयुक्तौ युवां दुच्छुना दुःखस्य कर्तॄन् पृथुश्रवसो विस्तीर्णयशसोऽरातीः शत्रूनिरहतम् । निःशेषेणावधिष्टम् । यद्वा । कानीनस्य पृथुश्रवःसंज्ञस्य राज्ञः शत्रूनिति योज्यम् । सहस्रा । सुपां सुलुगिति चतुर्थ्या डादेशः । अहतम् । लङि थस्तम् । अनुदात्तो … [continued on p. 288; the grammar tail reads paṭ(e)śyādīnāṃ…, duścunāḥ — śunam iti sukhanāma, duṣṭaṃ śunaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ duśśunāḥ, parādiś chandasi bahulam, utkaratarapadādyudāttatvam (the first-syllable accent of the later member)] [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

he aśvinā vaśametatsaṃjñamṛṣimekasyā vastorekasminnahani raṇāya ramaṇīyāya sahasrā sahasrasaṃkhyākāya sanaye dhanalābhāyāvatam | arakṣatam | sa ṛṣiḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ yathā sahasrasaṃkhyaṃ dhanamabhate tathā rakṣitavantāvisyarthaḥ | api ca he vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣitārāvaśvinau indravantā indreṇa saṃyuktau yuvāṃ ducchunā duḥkhasya kartṝn pṛthuśravaso vistīrṇayaśaso 'rātīḥ śatrūnirahatam | niḥśeṣeṇāvadhiṣṭam | yadvā | kānīnasya pṛthuśravaḥsaṃjñasya rājñaḥ śatrūniti yojyam | sahasrā | supāṃ sulugiti caturthyā ḍādeśaḥ | ahatam | laṅi thastam | anudātto … [continued on p. 288; the grammar tail reads paṭ(e)śyādīnāṃ…, duścunāḥ — śunam iti sukhanāma, duṣṭaṃ śunaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ duśśunāḥ, parādiś chandasi bahulam, utkaratarapadādyudāttatvam (the first-syllable accent of the later member)] [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, vaśam — the ṛṣi named Vaśa — you protected on a single day (ekasyā vastoḥ), for raṇāya — delightful — a sahasrā, thousand-numbered, sanaye, gain of wealth: you protected him so that the ṛṣi might obtain, in an excellent manner, a thousand pieces of wealth. Moreover, O vṛṣaṇā, showerers of desires, indravantā, joined with Indra, you slew duśśunāḥ — doers of ill — the enemies of pṛthuśravas, of wide fame, utterly. Or, the 'enemies of the king named Pṛthuśravas, son of Kanīna' is how it should be joined."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinau — O Aśvin deities; vaśam — the ṛṣi named Vaśa; ekasyāḥ vastoḥ — in a single day; raṇasya — [for the sake of] the delightful; sahasrā — thousand-numbered; sanaye — for gain of wealth; āvatam — you protected; api ca — and further; vṛṣaṇau — O you who give desired objects (Aśvin deities); indravantā — joined with Indra; duśśunāḥ — doers of ill; pṛthuśravasaḥ — [the enemies] of Pṛthuśravas; arātīḥ — enemies; niḥ ahatam — you wholly slew."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, you protected the ṛṣi named Vaśa so that thousand-fold wealth might be obtained each day. And, O givers of desired objects, joined with Indra, you wholly destroyed the evil-doing enemies of Pṛthuśravas."

English Translation (as printed)

You preserved Vasha, Ashwins, (that he might obtain) in a single day a thousand acceptable gifts ; showerers (of benefits), associated with Indra, you destroyed the malignant enemies of Prithushravas

original p. 288

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रणाय — Raṇāya — "since the word raṇa is stated among the twenty-four [as read] names of battle, 'raṇaḥ', 'vivāk' (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]), it means battle: 'for the sake of battle', says Skandasvāmin. Sāyaṇa explains raṇāya as 'ramaṇīyāya', 'delightful', 'beneficial to the mind'. Sāyaṇa has explained the sense of this Ṛk in one way, and Skandasvāmin in another. Yet the intention that 'the Aśvin deities favour' is the same; in both explanations the greatness of the power of the Aśvin deities is described."

दुच्छुनाः — Duśśunāḥ — "duḥkhasya kartṝn: since the word śuna is stated among the thirty [as read] names of happiness (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), it conveys the meaning of happiness. Sāyaṇa: 'duṣṭaṃ śunaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ duśśunāḥ': 'those for whom happiness is spoiled': hence duśśunāḥ … by parādiś chandasi bahulam, Pā. 6-2-199 as read [?], the first-syllable accent of the later member."

original p. 289

"… [Sāyaṇa explains duśśunāḥ as] 'those who cause happiness to be spoiled', or 'those who cause obstruction in respect of happiness': this is the meaning; and in the first half of this Ṛk he describes the greatness of the Aśvin deities who favoured and protected the ṛṣi named Vaśa so that wealth of a thousand might be got every day. In the second half: 'pṛthuśravasaḥ arātīḥ niraḥatam' — 'kānīnasya pṛthuśravaḥsaṃjñasya rājñaḥ śatrūn niḥśeṣeṇāvadhiṣṭam': 'you wholly slew the enemies of the king named Pṛthuśravas, son of Kanyā [Kānīna]': to the king named Pṛthuśravas, the son of a maiden, who was giving a gift, while he was subduing his enemies, the Aśvin deities, joined with Indra, came and protected the king: thus he explains the connection of the greatness of the Aśvin deities in two separate sentences. Skandasvāmin: 'āvatam' — avatir gatyarthaḥ gatavantau (the root av conveys the sense of going; 'you went'); 'ekasyā vastoḥ sahasrā sanaye raṇāya āvatam': 'ekasmin ahni sahasrasaṃkhyākānāṃ dhanānāṃ lābhāya saṅgrāmārthaṃ gatavantau': 'for the gaining of a thousand pieces of wealth in one day you went for battle'. [The meaning:] 'to the king named Vaśa, to fight with enemies who destroyed one thousand [pieces] of wealth every day, the Aśvin deities went to battle, subdued the enemies of that king, and protected the king' — thus he explains. Saying 'this was told by Kutsa too', he cites

याभिर्विश्पलां धनसामथर्व्यं सहस्रमीळ्ह आजावजिन्वतम् । याभिर्वशमश्व्यं प्रेणिमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१० [as read])

yābhirviśpalāṃ dhanasāmatharvyaṃ sahasramīḷha ājāvajinvatam | yābhirvaśamaśvyaṃ preṇimāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-10 [as read])

this Ṛk, and

पृथुश्रवो नाम राजा सन्तैर्बहुभिर्दुर्भिक्षैः पीड्यमानो ऽश्विनावियोज [?] तुष्टाव च । तस्याश्विनौ तु महत्या वृष्ट्या तान्यपनिनतुरिति तदेतदिहोच्यते निरहतमित्यादि । दुच्छुना दुर्भिक्षा उच्यन्ते ॥

pṛthuśravo nāma rājā santairbahubhirdurbhikṣaiḥ pīḍyamāno 'śvināviyoja [?] tuṣṭāva ca | tasyāśvinau tu mahatyā vṛṣṭyā tānyapaninaturiti tadetadihocyate nirahatamityādi | ducchunā durbhikṣā ucyante ‖ [Skandasvāmin; small type; partly doubtful [?]]

— 'a king named Pṛthuśravas, tormented by many famines occurring uninterruptedly, pleased the Aśvin deities with oblations and praised them. They, by a great rain, removed these [famines]: this is what is said here by nirahatam and so on; duśśunāḥ means famines.' In Kannada: a king named Pṛthuśravas, pressed down by the ever-continuing and extreme famines, satisfied the Aśvin deities with oblations and praised them. They, satisfied, joined Indra, and by sending abundant rain destroyed that famine: this matter is made manifest here by the word nirahatam; explaining thus, for the word duśśunā he gives the meaning 'bad food (famine)', and for the word arāti he explains 'those who do not give': the word arāti — whoever it be, [one who] is unable to give anything, gives hindrance — thus conveying the meaning, he sets out in detail the power of famine, and makes it an adjective of duśśunā."

Sense (mine): "For the thirsty praiser named Śara, son of Ṛcatka, [the ārcatka], for his pātave, drinking, from the lower well (avatāt), O Aśvins, you made vāḥ, water, [rise] above, upward: you made it come to the fore. Likewise, O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, by your śacībhiḥ — your works, your services — for jasurāye, the wearied śayave cit, the ṛṣi named Śayu, you filled with milk the starya [stari — barren] cow that had ceased to bear, [the cow that gives milk for the Agnihotra]."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) on p. 293

original p. 293

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"ārcatkasya — of the son of Ṛcatka; śarasya cit — of Śara by name; pātave — for drinking; nīcāt — from the deep; avatāt — from the well; vāḥ — the water; uccā — upward; ā cakrathuḥ — you made (to come); (tathā — likewise); nāsatyā — O Aśvin deities; śacībhiḥ — [by your] works; jasuraye — [for] the wearied; śayave cit — Śayu, the ṛṣi; staryam — the barren; gām — the cow; pipyathuḥ — you filled [with milk]."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"For the sake of drinking for Śara, the son of Ṛcatka (who was thirsty), you made the water from the deep well rise up. And, O Nāsatyas, you made the barren cow of Śayu, the weary ṛṣi (for the sake of his sacrificial rites), yield milk by your works. (You made it give milk.)"

English Translation (as printed)

You raised the water from the bottom to the top of the well, for the drinking of Shara, the son of Richatka, and by your powers, Nasatyas, you filled, for the sake of the weary Shayu, the barren cow (with milk).

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

"In this Ṛk it is said that the Aśvin deities helped the ṛṣi named Śara, the son of the ṛṣi named Ṛcatka, who was thirsty, and Śayu, the ṛṣi who was weary from his toil in performing the sacrifices. Skandasvāmin has told this matter in his bhāṣya —

शरो नाम ऋषिः स मरुदेशे गच्छन् पिपासितस्तं सुदूरकोऽयं कूपं ददर्श स तं ततः पातुमक्षन्नर्व अश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तस्मात्तेषां सुलभ्यं चक्रतुरिति । तदेतदिहोच्यते शरस्य चिदित्यादिना ॥

śaro nāma ṛṣiḥ sa marudeśe gacchan pipāsitastaṃ sudūrako 'yaṃ kūpaṃ dadarśa sa taṃ tataḥ pātumakṣannarva aśvinau tuṣṭāva | tasmātteṣāṃ sulabhyaṃ cakraturiti | tadetadihocyate śarasya cidityādinā ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

— 'a ṛṣi named Śara, going in a desert, thirsty, saw a well at a great distance; unable to drink from it [for its depth?], he praised the Aśvins; they made the water easy to get for him: this is what is said here: śarasya cit and so on.' In Kannada: the ṛṣi named Śara, while going in the desert, searching for water because of thirst, saw water in a deep well, and because it was difficult to reach it, he praised the Aśvin deities in order that the water might be easily obtained. They, pleased with his praise,

original p. 294

caused the water of that well to rise up for him, and the opening of the well to be level, and so protected the ṛṣi: this Itihāsa is told in the Ṛk śarasya cit."

अवतात् — Avatāt — "since the word avata is stated among the fourteen [as read] names of well, kūpa, kātaḥ … (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), it means well."

वाः — Vāḥ — "udakam: since the word vār is stated among the hundred-and-one [as read] names of water (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]), it means water. The word vāḥ

कदा वसो स्तोत्रं हर्यत आव श्मशा रुधद्वाः । दीर्घं सुतं वाताप्याय ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१४४-१ [as read])

kadā vaso stotraṃ haryata āva śmaśā rudhadvāḥ | dīrghaṃ sutaṃ vātāpyāya ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-144-1 [as read])

is used in this Ṛk in the sense of water."

जसुरये — Jasuraye — "śrāntāya: when explaining the meaning of the word jasuri (Ni. 4-?? as read [?]) the Nirukta-writer cites

उत स्मैनं वस्त्रमथिं न तायुमनु क्रोशन्ति क्षितयो भरेषु । नीचायमानं जसुरिं न श्येनं श्रवश्चाच्छा पशुमच्च यूथम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-३८-५ [as read])

uta smainaṃ vastramathiṃ na tāyumanu krośanti kṣitayo bhareṣu | nīcāyamānaṃ jasuriṃ na śyenaṃ śravaścācchā paśumacca yūtham ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-38-5 [as read])

and explains jasuriṃ as 'jastaṃ baddhaṃ kaṭṭalpaṭṭa' [= bound, held fast], 'one who is wearied'."

स्तर्यम् — Staryam — "nivṛttaprasavāṃ | strīyate ācchādyate prasavasāmarthyābhāvena iti starīḥ": "a cow that, because of lack of capacity to bear young, is covered over: starī is the name of a cow with no power to conceive and bring forth (to give birth)."

गाम् पिप्यथुः — Gām pipyathuḥ — "payaso dogdhrīm payasā āpūritavantau": "you made the cow yield milk. The meaning is that they made her a milch cow."

शचीभिः जसुरये शयवे — Śacībhiḥ jasuraye śayave — "Sāyaṇa explains that Śayu, the ṛṣi, being wearied by serving the Aśvin deities. Skandasvāmin says 'śayave cit rājñe' [= 'to Śayu, a king'], 'śacībhiḥ svābhiḥ atiśayavatībhiḥ prajñābhir karmabhir vā jasuraye śatrūṇāṃ tāḍayitre tāḍitāya vā': 'by your own excellent intelligences or by works, [for him who] smites the enemies or is smitten by enemies': he explains that Śayu was a king, with an excellent or superior mind [buddhi], devoted to work, destroying enemies or being harassed by enemies. अवस्यते । स्तुवते । कृष्णियाय । ऋजुऽयते । नासत्या । शचीभिः । पशुम् । न । नष्टम्ऽइव । दर्शनाय । विष्णाप्वम् । ददथुः । विश्वकाय ॥ २३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.23)

अवस्यते अवनं रक्षणमात्मन इच्छते स्तुवते स्तुतिं कुर्वते कृष्णियाय । कृष्णो नाम कश्चित्तस्य पुत्राय ऋजूयते आर्जवमिच्छते विश्वकायेत्येतत्संज्ञाय ऋषये हे नासत्या युवां शचीभिरात्मीयैः कर्मभिर्विष्णाप्वं नाम विनष्टं पुत्रं दर्शनाय दर्शनार्थं ददथुः । दत्तवन्तौ । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पशुं न नष्टमिव । इव उपमार्थीयः पूरकः । यथा कश्चिन्नष्टं पशुं स्वामिनो दृष्टिपथं प्रापयति तद्वत् ॥ अवस्यते । अवस्शब्दात्सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । कृष्णियाय । कृष्णशब्दादपत्यार्थे छान्दसो घः ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

avasyate avanaṃ rakṣaṇamātmana icchate stuvate stutiṃ kurvate kṛṣṇiyāya | kṛṣṇo nāma kaścittasya putrāya ṛjūyate ārjavamicchate viśvakāyetyetatsaṃjñāya ṛṣaye he nāsatyā yuvāṃ śacībhirātmīyaiḥ karmabhirviṣṇāpvaṃ nāma vinaṣṭaṃ putraṃ darśanāya darśanārthaṃ dadathuḥ | dattavantau | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | paśuṃ na naṣṭamiva | iva upamārthīyaḥ pūrakaḥ | yathā kaścinnaṣṭaṃ paśuṃ svāmino dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāpayati tadvat ‖ avasyate | avasśabdātsupa ātmanaḥ kyac | kṛṣṇiyāya | kṛṣṇaśabdādapatyārthe chāndaso ghaḥ ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "To Viśvaka, son of Kṛṣṇa — who avasyate (desires protection for himself), stuvate (praises), ṛjūyate (is wishing rectitude) — O Nāsatyas, you, by your own works, gave Viṣṇāpva, the lost son, for sight, darśanāya, for him to see; as one who brings a lost animal into the sight of its owner."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; avasyate — desiring protection; stuvate — one who praises (you); kṛṣṇiyāya — the son of Kṛṣṇa; ṛjūyate — wishing for the straight path; viśvakāya — to Viśvaka; viṣṇāpvam — Viṣṇāpva by name (the lost son); naṣṭam iva — lost, as if he had gone astray; paśum na — as one brings back a lost animal; darśanāya — for sight; śacībhiḥ — by [your] works; dadathuḥ — you gave."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Nāsatyas, to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, who praised you, desiring your protection and the straight path, you, by your works, made visible again his lost son Viṣṇāpva, as one makes a lost animal visible [to its owner]."

English Translation (as printed)

Nasatyas, by your acts you restored to Vishwaka, the son of Krishna, soliciting your protection, adoring you, and a lover of rectitude, his son Vishnapu, (welcome) to his sight as an animal that had been lost.

original p. 298

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

पशुं न नष्टमिव — Paśuṃ na naṣṭam iva — "iva upamārthīyaḥ pūrakaḥ": "Sāyaṇa says that, since the words na and iva are in the sense of comparison, here the word iva is a padapūraka (filler). Skandasvāmin: 'paunaruktyāt astyupamārthasya samprati kārthaṃ prayogaḥ' (Ni. 1-?? as read [?]) — in the sense of 'yathā paśuṃ naṣṭaṃ kaścid idānīm asmai didṛkṣave dadyāt evam': 'as someone would now give a lost animal to him who wishes to see it, so [you gave]'. Here, since two words of comparison — na and iva — are present, there would be repetition; so for the word na the meaning of upamā is [said to be] samprati ('now'), and here, he explains, na is a padapūraka.

Viśvako nāma rājarṣeḥ putraḥ pramādād upananaṣṭe snehād vipatty-āśaṅkayā kasya pālanaṃ punar naṣṭaṃ darśanam icchan aśvinau tuṣṭāva … [the Sanskrit is in small type; read letter by letter and doubtful [?]]: 'Viśvaka, the son of a royal sage, when his own son was lost, through carelessness [?], afraid of calamity because of affection, praised the Aśvins, wishing to see again the lost [son]: to him the lovely Aśvins gave [back] the son: this is what is said here: avasyave and so on.' In Kannada: Viśvaka, the son of a royal sage, his son having gone out of his father's sight through carelessness, [Viśvaka] anxious through love, suspecting danger — wishing to see his son, praised the Aśvin deities; the Aśvin deities called that son and showed him to Viśvaka. Just as another person searches for an animal that had been lost, and calling it, shows it, so the Aśvin deities called the son of Viśvaka and brought and showed him: this is described here."

कृष्णियाय — Kṛṣṇiyāya — "kṛṣṇo nāma kaścit | tasya putraḥ kṛṣṇiyaḥ": "Kṛṣṇa is the name of a person; his son is kṛṣṇiya: the suffix comes in the sense of 'offspring' and gives the form kṛṣṇiya."

विश्वकाय — Viśvakāya — "etatsaṃjñāya — to the one named Viśvaka."

ऋजूयते — Ṛjūyate — "ṛjum ātmana icchate: for the sake of one who desires the straight (honest) conduct of a good man, without deceit and without crookedness; for the man who desires the practice of upright conduct — this is the meaning."

विष्णाप्वम् — Viṣṇāpvam — "Viṣṇāpva is the son of Viśvaka. This matter is told in this sūkta and in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-7 [as read]; 8-?-?; 10-65-12 [as read]."

daśa | rātrīḥ | aśivena | nava | dyūn | ava 'naddham | śnathitam | ap 'su | antariti | vi 'prutam | rebham | udani | pra 'vṛktam | ut | ninyathuḥ | somam 'iva | sruveṇa ‖ 24 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.24)

पुरा खलु रेभमृषिं पार्श्वैर्बद्ध्वासुराः कूपे कस्यचिद्दिवसस्य सायंकाले प्राक्षिपुः । स चाश्विनौ स्तुवन् दश रात्रीर्नवाहानि च कूपमध्ये तथैवावस्थितो ऽभूत् । दशमेऽहनि प्रातरश्विनौ तं कूपादुदतारयतामिति । तदाह । अप्सु कूपान्तर्वर्तिनीष्वप्स्वन्तर्मध्ये असुरैः पाशैर्दुःखहेतुना वाग्भिर्बद्धं श्नथितं शत्रुभिर्हिंसितं दश रात्रीर्दशसंख्याका निशा नव द्यून् नवसंख्याकान्यहानि च अशिवेन अकल्याणेन [?] …

purā khalu rebhamṛṣiṃ pārśvairbaddhvāsurāḥ kūpe kasyaciddivasasya sāyaṃkāle prākṣipuḥ | sa cāśvinau stuvan daśa rātrīrnavāhāni ca kūpamadhye tathaivāvasthito 'bhūt | daśame 'hani prātaraśvinau taṃ kūpādudatārayatāmiti | tadāha | apsu kūpāntarvartinīṣvapsvantarmadhye asuraiḥ pāśairduḥkhahetunā vāgbhirbaddhaṃ śnathitaṃ śatrubhirhiṃsitaṃ daśa rātrīrdaśasaṃkhyākā niśā nava dyūn navasaṃkhyākānyahāni ca aśivena akalyāṇena [?] …

Sense (mine): "Once, the Asuras, having bound the ṛṣi Rebha with ropes at the sides, threw him into a well at the evening of some day. And he, praising the Aśvins, remained so ten nights and nine days in the well. On the tenth day, in the morning, the Aśvins lifted him out of the well. This is said: in the waters (apsu) within the well, bound with ropes by the Asuras, a cause of pain, śnathitam — injured by enemies — for daśa rātrīḥ, ten nights, nava dyūn, nine days, aśivena, with misery …" the bhāṣya continues on p. 301

original p. 301

Bhāṣya of Ṛk 24, concluded from p. 300: "… aśivena — by misery; anavaddham — bound; [Rebha, who was bound in the well by the Asuras]. Having thus been bound in the waters inside the well, prvṛktam — scorched, viprutam — immersed (pluta) — Rebham, the ṛṣi named Rebha, udani, in the water, unninyathuḥ — you raised up sromam iva sruveṇa: as the Adhvaryu, at the time of Agnihotra, with a ladle (sruva), draws up from a vessel the soma-juice [to offer into the fire] …" [the Sanskrit of the following portion: yathāgnihotrahomārthamabhiṣutaṃ somarasaṃ kūpasadṛśe 'gnihotrasthālīmadhye vartamānaṃ sruveṇādhvaryur unnayati ūrdhvaṃ nayati tadvat]; and then the grammar tail, in small type: anavaddham — ṇah "to bind", niṣṭhā, kta; ṇaho dhaḥ; jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ; śnathitam — śnatha hiṃsārthaḥ, niṣṭhā; vipṛtam — pruj… gatau; anavaddham [again]; udani — padannomāsa… [the substitute udan for udaka].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"apsu antaḥ — inside the water (that was in the well); aśivena — by pain-causing (rope thrown by the Asuras); anavaddham — bound; śnathitam — injured; daśa rātrīḥ — ten nights; nava dyūn — nine days; udani — in the water; viprutam — immersed; pravṛktam — scorched; rebham — Rebha by name; sruveṇa — with a ladle (the Adhvaryu); somam iva — as soma-juice (when performing the Agnihotra, from the vessel [is drawn] upward); unninyathuḥ — you raised him up."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"You raised up from the well, as the Adhvaryu raises with a ladle the soma-juice out of a vessel at the time of Agnihotra, Rebha — who, thrown by the Asuras into the water in the well, bound with a pain-causing rope, injured, immersed for ten nights and nine days in the water, was scorched [with distress]."

English Translation (as printed)

Ashwins, you raised up, like Soma in a ladle, Rebha, who for ten nights and nine days had lain (in a well), bound with tight bonds, wounded, immersed, and suffering distress from the water.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अशिवेन — Aśivena — "duḥkhahetunā dāmnā": "'bound by a rope that is the cause of causing suffering': this is how Sāyaṇa explains the meaning of this Ṛk. The meaning stated in Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya is different, yet the general sense is the same. But Sāyaṇa tells this Itihāsa in full here. The meaning that Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya gives of this Itihāsa is understood from the explanations of the words of āyuḥ.

original p. 302

पुरा खलु रेभमृषिं पार्श्वैर्बद्ध्वासुराः कूपे कस्यचिद्दिवसस्य सायंकाले प्राक्षिपुः । स चाश्विनौ स्तुवन् दशरात्रीर्नवाहानि च कूपमध्ये क्लेशेनावतस्थे । दशमेऽहनि प्रातरश्विनौ तं कूपात् उदतारयतामिति । तदाह ॥

purā khalu rebhamṛṣiṃ pārśvairbaddhvāsurāḥ kūpe kasyaciddivasasya sāyaṃkāle prākṣipuḥ | sa cāśvinau stuvan daśarātrīrnavāhāni ca kūpamadhye kleśenāvatasthe | daśame 'hani prātaraśvinau taṃ kūpāt udatārayatāmiti | tadāha ‖

— 'The Asuras, having bound the ṛṣi named Rebha at the sides, threw him into a well at evening of a certain day. He remained in the middle of the well in distress for ten nights and nine days, praising the Aśvins. On the tenth day in the morning the Aśvins brought him out of the well. This is said.' In Kannada: a ṛṣi named Rebha was bound by the Asuras with ropes and thrown into a well at evening of a day. He lay in the water inside the well with his hands and feet bound for nine days, or ten nights, praising the Aśvin deities. Then on the tenth day, in the morning, the Aśvin deities came, lifted him out of the well and protected him. This Itihāsa is told here.

"Skandasvāmin:

अशिवेन । शिवं सुखम् । केशो ऽन्यादृशिवं दुःखं । तत्र ये रक्षः अशिवा उच्यन्ते । समूहाभिप्रायं च एकवचनं दुःखकरेण असुरसमूहेन ॥

aśivena | śivaṃ sukham | keśo 'nyādṛśivaṃ duḥkhaṃ | tatra ye rakṣaḥ aśivā ucyante | samūhābhiprāyaṃ ca ekavacanaṃ duḥkhakareṇa asurasamūhena ‖

— 'śiva is happiness; the opposite of it is aśiva, pain. Those who cause it, the Rākṣasas, are called aśivāḥ. The singular is used with the idea of a group: duḥkhakareṇa asurasamūhena, by a company of Asuras who cause pain.' Śiva means 'happiness'; what is distinct from happiness, the opposite of happiness, is pain. The Asuras, the cause of pain, are denoted by the word aśiva. The singular is used here with the meaning of a collection: the sense is 'by many Asuras, a group of causers of pain'."

श्नथितम् — Śnathitam — "śatrubhir hiṃsitam": "hurt by enemies — so Sāyaṇa; Skandasvāmin explains: 'struck' (tāḍitam), 'beaten' (kuḍiyalpaṭṭavan)."

प्रवृक्तम् — Pravṛktam — "prayajanena santaptaṃ ghṛmam iva vyathayā saṃtapyamānam" [as read; small type]: "scorched, like a hot vessel (gharma) by distress. Because he had been immersed in the water for ten nights, he was in distress like a person scorched by the heat of fire: so Sāyaṇa explains — [the root] vṛjī vārjane; Skandasvāmin explains it as nimagnam (immersed), since the root vṛj conveys the sense of 'to submerge' (majjana); the one who is immersed."

विप्रुतम् — Viprutam — "vyākṣiptasarvāṅgam: whose limbs are all scattered about (as the limbs were not able to be used properly, because of being tightly bound). Skandasvāmin: 'āpāṃ madhye karmabhiḥ vigataṃ rahitaṃ niṣkleśyam': 'in the middle of the waters one deprived of the power to do work, who is lying helpless': he explains that the Aśvin deities lifted Rebha, in this state, out of the well."

सोममिव स्रुवेण — Somam iva sruveṇa — "yathā kaścit sruveṇa somam unnayati tadvat: as one draws up soma with a ladle; by the word sruva — because of the similarity of the camasa and other soma-vessels — [the sense is:] as the soma-juice is raised up. Or

original p. 303

the Kātyāyana-ites [?], those who study the Yajurveda — kaṭhaśākhins — desiring brahmavarcasa, do homa of the soma-juice into the Agnihotra fire. The simile [is explained]: 'as soma-juice is raised up with the ladle' — here the comparison is stated, with the intention that they offer the soma-juice. By this simile the camasa and other vessels are indicated. When performing this homa, the camasa, sruva, iḍā and other sacrificial vessels are necessary; therefore, as the soma-juice in the camasa vessel is raised with the ladle for the time of homa, so Rebha was lifted from the well: this example is shown.

अश्वं न गूळ्हमश्विना दुरेवैर्ऋषिं नरा वृषणा रेभमप्सु । सं तं रिणीथो विप्रुतं दंसोभिर्न वां जूर्यन्ति पूर्व्या कृतानि ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-५ [as read; as printed here; the first pāda reads aśvaṃ na gūḷham aśvinā durevaiḥ… [?]])

aśvaṃ na gūḷhamaśvinā durevairṛṣiṃ narā vṛṣaṇā rebhamapsu | saṃ taṃ riṇītho viprutaṃ daṃsobhirna vāṃ jūryanti pūrvyā kṛtāni ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-5 [as read; as printed here; the first pāda reads aśvaṃ na gūḷham aśvinā durevaiḥ… [?]])

याभी रेभं निवृतं सितमद्भ्य उद्वन्दनमैरयतं स्वर्दृशे । याभिः कण्वं प्र सिषासन्तमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-५ [as read; the number printed as 1-112-5 also above [?]])

yābhī rebhaṃ nivṛtaṃ sitamadbhya udvandanamairayataṃ svardṛśe | yābhiḥ kaṇvaṃ pra siṣāsantamāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-5 [as read; the number printed as 1-112-5 also above [?]])

— in these Ṛks too the protection of the ṛṣi Rebha by the Aśvin deities is described."

रेभम् — Rebham — "that the Aśvin deities protected Rebha is stated in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-5 ; 1-116-24 ; 1-117-4 ; 1-117-5 ; 1-118-6 ; 10-39-9 [as read; the numerals partly legible [?]]."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 24; grammar page, noted briefly)

aśivena (na śivam aśivam; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…, Pā. 6-2-2 as read [?], the first member, an avyaya, keeps its accent); daśa, nava (these end in n and denote numbers; nr-saṃkhyāyoḥ [triṃśat…] Phiṭ-sūtra as read [?], first-syllable accent); anavaddham (ṇah "to bind"; niṣṭhā, kta, Pā. 3-2-102 as read [?]; no ṇaḥ, Pā. 6-1-65 as read [?], ṇatva…; naho dhaḥ, Pā. 8-2-34 as read [?], dh for the root's h; with a jhaṣ after, t arises; jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ, Pā. 8-2-40 as read [?], dh for the t of the suffix; jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi, Pā. 8-4-53 as read [?] …

original p. 304

Grammar page of Ṛk 24, concluded (noted briefly): anavaddham (… jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi gives d; ḍhatva…; ṣṭutva…; the elision of the preceding ḍh and the lengthening, as above; gatir anantaraḥ, Pā. 6-2-49 as read [?], the prefix ava keeps its accent; accusative singular); śnathitam (śnatha "to injure"; kta in the passive; ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ, Pā. 7-2-35 as read [?], the augment iṭ; final accent from the suffix); apsu (ūḍidaṃpadādi…, Pā. 6-1-171 as read [?], the ending takes udātta; locative plural); viprutam (pruj "to go"; kta as before; gatir anantaraḥ, the prefix vi keeps its accent; since it belongs to the kapilakādi group, l-form [pluta] arises optionally); udani (when the locative singular follows the word udaka, pad-dan-no-mās…, Pā. 6-1-63 as read [?], udan is substituted; vibhāṣā ṅiśyoḥ, Pā. 6-4-136 as read [?], the elision of the a of an is optional, so it does not arise here); ninyathuḥ (ṇīñ "to carry"; liṭ 2nd dual; nighāta after an accented word). ‖ 24 ‖

Ṛk 25 (the last Ṛk of Sūkta 116)

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.25)

प्र वां दंसांस्यश्विनाववोचमस्य पतिः स्यां सुगवः सुवीरः । उत पश्यन्नश्नुवन्दीर्घमायुरस्तमिवेज्जरिमाणं जगम्याम् ॥ २५ ॥

pra vāṃ daṃsāṃsyaśvināvavocamasya patiḥ syāṃ sugavaḥ suvīraḥ | uta paśyannaśnuvandīrghamāyurastamivejjarimāṇaṃ jagamyām ‖ 25 ‖

original p. 305

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 116.25)

प्र । वाम् । दंसांसि । अश्विनौ । अवोचम् । अस्य । पतिः । स्याम् । सुऽगवः । सुऽवीरः । उत । पश्यन् । अश्नुवन् । दीर्घम् । आयुः । अस्तम्ऽइव । इत् । जरिमाणम् । जगम्याम् ॥ २५ ॥

pra | vām | daṃsāṃsi | aśvinau | avocam | asya | patiḥ | syām | su 'gavaḥ | su 'vīraḥ | uta | paśyan | aśnuvan | dīrgham | āyuḥ | astam 'iva | it | jarimāṇam | jagamyām ‖ 25 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 116.25)

एवमनेन सूक्तेनाश्विनोर्महिमानं प्रशस्याधुना मन्त्रद्रष्टा स्वाभीष्टं प्रार्थयते । हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोर्दंसांसि पुरा कृतानि कर्माणि प्रावोचम् । इत्थं मुक्तवानस्मि । सोऽहं सुगवः शोभनगोयुक्तः सुवीरः शोभनवीरैः पुत्रैर्युक्तश्चास्य राष्ट्रस्य परिधिपतिः स्याम् । भवेयम् । उताऽपि च पश्यन्सर्वैरिन्द्रियैः स्वस्वविषयसमर्थैर्दीर्घं वर्षशतरूपेणायुष्टमायुर्जीवितं चाश्नुवन्प्राप्नुवन्नहमस्तमिव यथा गृहं स्वामी निष्कण्टकं प्रविशति एवं जरिमाणं जरां कण्टकरहितेन प्राप्नुयाम् । वृद्धः सन्किरकालं निवसेयमित्यर्थः ॥ स्याम् । अस्तेः प्रार्थनायां लिङ् । यासुट् । क्सोरल्लोप इत्यकारलोपः । अश्नुवन् । अशू व्याप्तौ । व्यत्ययेन शपि । जरिमाणम् । जृष् वयोहानौ । अस्माद्वौणादिक इमनिच् । जगम्याम् । गमेः प्रार्थनायां लिङ् । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

evamanena sūktenāśvinormahimānaṃ praśasyādhunā mantradraṣṭā svābhīṣṭaṃ prārthayate | he aśvinau vāṃ yuvayordaṃsāṃsi purā kṛtāni karmāṇi prāvocam | itthaṃ muktavānasmi | so 'haṃ sugavaḥ śobhanagoyuktaḥ suvīraḥ śobhanavīraiḥ putrairyuktaścāsya rāṣṭrasya paridhipatiḥ syām | bhaveyam | utā 'pi ca paśyansarvairindriyaiḥ svasvaviṣayasamarthairdīrghaṃ varṣaśatarūpeṇāyuṣṭamāyurjīvitaṃ cāśnuvanprāpnuvannahamastamiva yathā gṛhaṃ svāmī niṣkaṇṭakaṃ praviśati evaṃ jarimāṇaṃ jarāṃ kaṇṭakarahitena prāpnuyām | vṛddhaḥ sankirakālaṃ nivaseyamityarthaḥ ‖ syām | asteḥ prārthanāyāṃ liṅ | yāsuṭ | ksorallopa ityakāralopaḥ | aśnuvan | aśū vyāptau | vyatyayena śapi | jarimāṇam | jṛṣ vayohānau | asmādvauṇādika imanic | jagamyām | gameḥ prārthanāyāṃ liṅ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya śluḥ ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "Having thus, by this sūkta, praised the greatness of the Aśvins, the seer of the mantras now prays for his own desire. O Aśvins, vām, your daṃsāṃsi, works done in former times, pra avocam, I have declared. May I, sugavaḥ, endowed with good cattle, suvīraḥ, endowed with good sons, be the pati, lord, of the boundary [paridhi] of this realm. And paśyan — seeing with all the senses, each capable in its own object — aśnuvan, obtaining dīrgham āyuḥ, a long life of a hundred years: may I jagamyām, attain jarimāṇam, old age, astam iva, as a master [enters his house] into a house without thorns, freed from troubles; that is, 'may I live for a long time, when old'."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinau — O Aśvin deities; vām — your; daṃsāṃsi — [mighty] acts; pra avocam — I have declared (such as I am); sugavaḥ — having good cattle; suvīraḥ — having valiant sons; asya — of this realm; patiḥ syām — may I be lord; uta — and; paśyan — seeing (with eyes, having keenness of the senses); dīrgham āyuḥ — a long life; aśnuvan — obtaining (living for a long time); astam iva — as (the master of a house) enters his house; jarimāṇam — old age; jagamyām — may I enter."

original p. 306

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, I have described your great deeds. Grant that I, having valour and good cattle, may be the lord of this realm, and that, keen of senses, living long, I may afterwards (as a householder enters his house) enter old age."

English Translation (as printed)

Thus, Ashwins, have I declared your exploits ; may I become the master (of this place), having abundant cattle and a numerous progeny, and retaining my sight, and enjoying a long life : may I enter into old age, as (a master enters) his house.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

दंसांसि — Daṃsāṃsi — "purā kṛtāni karmāṇi: since the word daṃsaḥ is stated among the twenty-six [as read] names of work, 'apaḥ', 'apnaḥ' (Ni. 2-1 as read [?]), the word daṃsa means work. In this Ṛk, the number of acts is described in which the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān, who saw this sūkta and performed the pācana etc., having prayed to the Aśvin deities, who are the subject of this sūkta, [has asked for] what he must obtain; many works of the Aśvin deities that were done as favours to those who were in difficulties have been narrated. By this, the greatness of these deities being made clear, the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān prayed to the Aśvin deities that he might be lord of this realm with excellent cattle, sons and so on; that he might have a sharp sense-organs [indriyapāṭava] suitable for long life; that he might live long, free from disease, in a healthy body, and afterwards attain old age."

अस्तमिव — Astam iva — "yathā gṛhaṃ svāmī niṣkaṇṭakaṃ praviśati evaṃ jarāṃ kaṇṭakarahitena prāpnuyām vṛddhaḥ san ciraṃ kālaṃ niveseyam ity arthaḥ": "as the master of a house enters his house without any thorn (obstacle), so may I enter old age without obstacle, and, being old, long dwell [in life]: this is the meaning. The word asta is stated among the twenty-two [as read] names of house, 'gayaḥ', 'kṣayaḥ' and so on (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), so asta means house. As the master of a house enters his house without any fear or any trouble, so [the wish is expressed here] that, by the grace of the Aśvin deities, I may live long without any danger from disease etc., and afterwards pass in comfort the old age that remains."

original p. 307

सुगवः सुवीरः — Sugavaḥ suvīraḥ — "śobhanavīraiḥ putraiḥ pautrair upetaḥ": "'possessed of fine [valiant] sons, grandsons and so on': thus Sāyaṇa explains: suvīra = 'brave'. Skandasvāmin explains it as 'one with valiant sons and grandsons', or 'one with sons and grandsons engaged in good works'."

पश्यन् — Paśyan — "akṣibhyāṃ paśyan svasvaviṣayadarśanasamarthaiḥ sarvair indriyaiḥ": "although it is said only that he is 'seeing with the eyes', by the mode of upalakṣaṇa it is said that, so that the eye-organ may be sound for seeing with the eyes, all the other organs too, in their own functions, should be favoured so that health may be one and the same [in all]: this is the meaning."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 25; grammar page, noted briefly)

avocam (brūñ "to speak", vāci; luṅ 1st singular mip; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ, Pā. 3-4-101 as read [?], am substituted; brūvo vaciḥ, Pā. 2-4-53 as read [?], vaci for the root; asyativakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ, Pā. 3-1-52 as read [?], aṅ for cli; vaca um, Pā. 7-4-20 as read [?], the augment um; guṇa; the augment aṭ; nighāta); syām (as "to be"; vidhiniminantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭasamprapraśnaprārthaneṣu liṅ, Pā. 3-3-161 as read [?], liṅ in the sense of prayer; in the 1st singular, mip → am by liṅaḥ…; yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca, Pā. 3-4-103 as read [?], yāsuṭ; being ṅit-like, śnasor allopaḥ, Pā. 6-4-111 as read [?], elision of the a of the root; nighāta); suvīraḥ (vīravīryau ca, Pā. 6-2-120 as read [?], the later member's first-syllable accent); paśyan (dṛśir "to see"; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śap; pāghrādhmā…, Pā. 7-3-78 as read [?], paśya substituted; adupadeśa so the sārvadhātuka is unaccented, hence tāsyanudāttet…, Pā. 6-1-186 as read [?], the root accent remains); aśnuvan (aśū "to pervade"; though ātmanepada, vyatyayo bahulam, Pā. 3-1-85 as read [?], parasmaipada; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ, Pā. 3-1-73 as read [?], śnu as vikaraṇa; aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ…, Pā. 6-4-77 as read [?], uvaṅ; from the suffix accent the u before n takes udātta); jarimāṇam (jṝṣ "to grow old"; the Uṇādi suffix imanic; guṇa of the ṛ with raparatva; the word jariman; jñitisūtra citaḥ, Pā. 6-1-163 as read [?], final accent; accusative singular, sarvanāmasthāne cāsaṃbuddhau, Pā. 6-4-8 as read [?], lengthening of the penultimate); jagamyām (gam "to go"; liṅ in the sense of prayer; 1st singular am substituted; yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca, yāsuṭ; bahulaṃ chandasi, Pā. 2-4-73 as read [?], śluḥ for the vikaraṇa; ślau, Pā. 6-1-10 as read [?], doubling; kuhoś cuḥ, Pā. 7-4-62 as read [?], j for the reduplication's g by palatalization; nighāta). ‖ 25 ‖ The grammar of Ṛk 25 concludes at the top of this page with the accent of aśnuvan — śnu as vikaraṇa; uvaṅ for the u; the udātta on the u — and jarimāṇam, jagamyām as above.

original p. 308

Colophon: nūrahadināreṇe sūktavu samāptavu — "The hundred-and-sixteenth Sūkta is ended."

End of Sūkta 116 (Ṛks 1–25; printed pp. 177–308; Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 17).

Sūkta 117 — "madhvaḥ somasya"

original p. 308

Heading (Kannada): "nūrahadinēḷaneya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-seventeenth Sūkta."

Anukramaṇī (Sanskrit, as printed):

मध्वः इति पञ्चविंशत्यृचं द्वितीयं सूक्तम् । औशिजस्य कक्षीवत आर्षं त्रैष्टुभमाश्विनं । मध्वः इत्यनुक्रान्तम् । प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोः पूर्वसूक्तेन सहोक्तो विनियोगः ॥

madhvaḥ iti pañcaviṃśatyṛcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktam | auśijasya kakṣīvata ārṣaṃ traiṣṭubhamāśvinaṃ | madhvaḥ ityanukrāntam | prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayoḥ pūrvasūktena sahokto viniyogaḥ ‖

Sense: "madhvaḥ — the second sūkta (of this anuvāka), of twenty-five Ṛks; the ṛṣi's work being of Kakṣīvān, son of Uśij; Triṣṭubh; addressed to the Aśvins. The Anukramaṇī says 'madhvaḥ'. Its application in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Aśvina-śastra has been stated together with the preceding sūkta."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "This sūkta, madhvaḥ somasya, is the second sūkta in the seventeenth anuvāka. It has twenty-five Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kakṣīvān, son of Uśij. The deities are the Aśvin deities. The metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said beginning with 'madhvaḥ'. In the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka mantras, this sūkta, together with the preceding sūkta, is applied for the mantras related to the Aśvina-śastra."

original p. 309

सूक्त—११७ (Sūkta 117) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१७ ॥ सूक्त—११७ ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—small numerals; read "13, 14, 15, 16, 17" — as printed [?] ॥ Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 25. Ṛṣi: Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. Devatā: the Aśvins. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.1)

मध्वः सोमस्याश्विना मदाय प्रत्नो होता विवासते वाम् । बर्हिष्मती रातिर्विश्रिता गीरिषा यातं नासत्योप वाजैः ॥ १ ॥

madhvaḥ somasyāśvinā madāya pratno hotā vivāsate vām | barhiṣmatī rātirviśritā gīriṣā yātaṃ nāsatyopa vājaiḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.1)

मध्वः । सोमस्य । अश्विना । मदाय । प्रत्नः । होता । आ । विवासते । वाम् । बर्हिष्मती । रातिः । विऽश्रिता । गीः । इषा । यातम् । नासत्या । उप । वाजैः ॥ १ ॥

madhvaḥ | somasya | aśvinā | madāya | pratnaḥ | hotā | ā | vivāsate | vām | barhiṣmatī | rātiḥ | vi 'śritā | gīḥ | iṣā | yātam | nāsatyā | upa | vājaiḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.1) begun at the foot of p. 309; continues on p. 310 Bhāṣya of Ṛk 1, continued from p. 309:

हे अश्विना मध्वो मधुना माधुर्योपेतेन सोमस्य सोमेन मदाय युवयोर्मदार्थं प्रत्नः प्रशस्यो होता होमनिष्पादको यजमानो वां

he aśvinā madhvo madhunā mādhuryopetena somasya somena madāya yuvayormadārthaṃ pratnaḥ praśasyo hotā homaniṣpādako yajamāno vāṃ

युवामा विवासते । विवासतिः परिचरणकर्मा । आज् मर्यो दायां [?] । यथाशास्त्रं परिचरति । अपि च रातिर्दात्व्यं हविर्बर्हिष्मती । अस्मिन्नेन बर्हिषा युक्तं । युष्मदर्थं बर्हिष्मदादिकमित्यर्थः । तथा गीः स्तुतिलक्षणावाक् च विश्रिता । ऋत्विग्भिः समवेता । तैः स्तुतिरपि क्रियते इत्यर्थः । अतो हे नासत्यावश्विनौ इषास्मभ्यं दातव्येनान्नेन वाजैर्बलैश्च सह युवामुप यातं । अस्मत्समीपमा प्राप्नुतम् ॥ मध्वः । सुपां सुलुगिति सुशो भवन्तीति तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी । जसादिषु छन्दसि वावचनमिति घेर्ङिति गुणाभावे यणादेशः । मदाय । मदी हर्षे । मदोनुपसर्गे इत्यप् । रातिः । रा दाने । कर्मणि क्तिन् । मन्त्रे वृषेषेत्यादिना तस्योदात्तत्वम् । विश्रिता । श्रिञ् सेवायाम् । कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ [small type, partly doubtful [?]]

yuvāmā vivāsate | vivāsatiḥ paricaraṇakarmā | āj maryo dāyāṃ [?] | yathāśāstraṃ paricarati | api ca rātirdātvyaṃ havirbarhiṣmatī | asminnena barhiṣā yuktaṃ | yuṣmadarthaṃ barhiṣmadādikamityarthaḥ | tathā gīḥ stutilakṣaṇāvāk ca viśritā | ṛtvigbhiḥ samavetā | taiḥ stutirapi kriyate ityarthaḥ | ato he nāsatyāvaśvinau iṣāsmabhyaṃ dātavyenānnena vājairbalaiśca saha yuvāmupa yātaṃ | asmatsamīpamā prāpnutam ‖ madhvaḥ | supāṃ sulugiti suśo bhavantīti tṛtīyārthe ṣaṣṭhī | jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanamiti gherṅiti guṇābhāve yaṇādeśaḥ | madāya | madī harṣe | madonupasarge ityap | rātiḥ | rā dāne | karmaṇi ktin | mantre vṛṣeṣetyādinā tasyodāttatvam | viśritā | śriñ sevāyām | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam ‖ [small type, partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "The hotṛ serves you two (vivāsate; vivāsati = a verb of serving) as laid down in the śāstra. And the rāti, the oblation to be given, is barhiṣmatī, provided with the sacred grass: furnished with barhis for you; likewise the gīḥ, the speech in the form of praise, is viśritā, assembled with the priests: they too perform the praise. Therefore, O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, come, with iṣā, the food to be given to us, and vājaiḥ, with strengths, to us; reach our neighbourhood."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; madhvaḥ — sweet; somasya — with soma-juice; madāya — to please you; pratnaḥ — the ancient; hotā — the sacrificer who offers the oblations; vām — you two; ā vivāsate — serves (as laid down in the śāstra); rātiḥ — the oblation to be given to you; barhiṣmatī — provided with darbha (placed on the darbha); gīḥ — praising speech; viśritā — is ready among the priests; (ataḥ — therefore); he nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; iṣā — with food to be given to us; vājaiḥ — with strength; upa yātam — come (to us, both of you)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Aśvin deities, for your gratification, the ancient sacrificer, the doer of the homa, serves you with sweet soma-juice; the oblation to be given to you is ready on the darbha; the priests too are ready to praise; therefore, O Nāsatyas, (to us) come with strength and with oblations."

English Translation (as printed)

Ashwins, for your gratification by the pleasant Soma juice, your ancient worshipper adores you : the offering is placed upon the sacred grass, the hymn is ready (for repetition); come, Nasatyas, with food and with vigour.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

प्रत्नः होता — Pratnaḥ hotā — "ciraṃtanaḥ yajamānaḥ homaniṣpādakaḥ": "since the word pratna is stated among the six names of 'ancient' (purāṇa), 'pratnaḥ', 'pravayāḥ' and so on (Ni. 3-?? as read [?]), and —

सवित्रवन्तः परि वाचमासते पितैषां प्रत्नो अभि रक्षति व्रतम् । महः समुद्रं वरुणस्तिरो दधे धीरा इच्छेकुर्धरुणेष्वारभम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ७-८७-६ [as read])

savitravantaḥ pari vācamāsate pitaiṣāṃ pratno abhi rakṣati vratam | mahaḥ samudraṃ varuṇastiro dadhe dhīrā icchekurdharuṇeṣvārabham ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 7-87-6 [as read])

in this Ṛk Yāska explains pratna as 'ancient', so Sāyaṇa explains it as ciraṃtana — 'one who has come down from time long past', the sacrificer who offers oblations to the deities. In this Ṛk the sacrificer, as the hotṛ, serves the Aśvin deities with oblations mixed with sweet soma-juice. Because 'hotṛtva' is said here generally, the meaning is that the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān, the seer of the mantra, also, performing the sacrifice or praising, gives them delight."

बर्हिष्मती — Barhiṣmatī — "aśvinārthena barhiṣā yuktaṃ yuṣmadarthaṃ barhiṣy āsāditam": "on the sacrificial altar the darbhas called barhis are spread, and the oblation consecrated with mantras is prepared for the Aśvin deities."

गीः — Gīḥ — "stutilakṣaṇā vāk ca": "the speech in the form of praise: since [it] is spoken in the sacrifice for the Aśvin deities, hearing the praises of the sacrificers who perform sacrifice, addressed to the deities denoted by the word nāsatya, and the oblations they offer, the Aśvins are prayed in this Ṛk to come to our sacrifice in order to give us strength and food."

वाजैः — Vājaiḥ — "balaiś ca — annaṃ, payaḥ among the twenty-eight [as read] names of food (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]) are stated; so the word vāja means food. Sāyaṇa here explains the meaning as strength:

हिरण्यस्तूपः सवितर्यथा त्वाङ्गिरसो जुह्वे वाजे अस्मिन् । एवा त्वार्चन्नवसे वन्दमानः सोमस्येवांशुं प्रति जागराहम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१४९-५ [as read])

hiraṇyastūpaḥ savitaryathā tvāṅgiraso juhve vāje asmin | evā tvārcannavase vandamānaḥ somasyevāṃśuṃ prati jāgarāham ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-149-5 [as read])

original p. 312

पावका नः सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३-१० [as read])

pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī vājebhirvājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-3-10 [as read])

— in these Ṛks Yāska explains vāje as anne; so the word vāja has many meanings. And in 'ṛbhur vibhvā vāja iti sudhanvana āṅgirasasya trayaḥ putrā babhūvuḥ' (Ni. 11-?? as read [?]) according to Yāska's explanation, the three sons of the Aṅgirasa Sudhanvan were named Ṛbhu, Vibhvan and Vāja: so the word vāja is also the name of a person. Therefore the word vāja has many meanings."

madhvaḥ (the word madhu; the sixth case is used in the sense of the third, by the statement supāṃ suluk…; jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam, Pā. 7-3-109 as read [?], as the ghi-guṇa does not arise, yaṇ); aśvinā (in the vocative dual, supāṃ sulug, Pā. 7-1-39 as read [?], ā for the ending; āmantritasya ca, Pā. 8-1-19 as read [?], nighāta); madāya (madī "to rejoice"; mado 'nupasarge, Pā. 3-3-67 as read [?], the suffix ap; being pit, it is unaccented, so the root accent remains; dative singular); pratnāya… [pratne: pratnapūrvaviśveṣvimātāl, Pā. 5-4-?? as read [?]; the suffix tna in the sense of 'ancient', prāk; accent on the last syllable from the suffix]; hotā (hu "to offer, to eat"; tṛn in the agent sense; guṇa of the root; niṣṭhā… [nit] the first-syllable accent); vivāsate (vāsa "to serve"; laṭ 3rd singular; nighāta); rātiḥ (rā "to give"; striyāṃ ktin, Pā. 3-3-94 as read [?], ktin in the passive; mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ, Pā. 3-3-96 as read [?], udātta).

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.2)

यो वामश्विना मनसो जवीयान्रथः स्वश्वो विश आजिगाति । येन गच्छथः सुकृतो दुरोणं तेन नरा वर्तिरस्मभ्यं यातम् ॥ २ ॥

yo vāmaśvinā manaso javīyānrathaḥ svaśvo viśa ājigāti | yena gacchathaḥ sukṛto duroṇaṃ tena narā vartirasmabhyaṃ yātam ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.2)

हे अश्विना वां युवयोः स्वभूतो मनसो जवीयान्मनसो ऽप्यतिशयेन वेगवान् स्वश्वः शोभनाश्वैर्युक्तो य रथो विशः प्रजा आजिगाति । अभिमुख्येन गच्छति । येन रथेन सुकृतः शोभनं यागं कुर्वतो यजमानस्य दुरोणं देवयजनलक्षणं गृहं गच्छथः । हे नरा नेतारावश्विनौ तेन रथेनास्मभ्यमस्माकं वर्तिर्वर्तनाधिकरणं गृहं यातम् । आगच्छतम् ॥ जवीयान् । जवोऽस्यास्तीति जववान् तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । तत आतिशायनिक ईयसुन् । विन्मतोर्लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः । जिगाति । गा स्तुतौ । जौहोत्यादिकः । गतिकर्मसु पाठादत्र गत्यर्थः । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यभ्यासस्येत्त्वम् ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

he aśvinā vāṃ yuvayoḥ svabhūto manaso javīyānmanaso 'pyatiśayena vegavān svaśvaḥ śobhanāśvairyukto ya ratho viśaḥ prajā ājigāti | abhimukhyena gacchati | yena rathena sukṛtaḥ śobhanaṃ yāgaṃ kurvato yajamānasya duroṇaṃ devayajanalakṣaṇaṃ gṛhaṃ gacchathaḥ | he narā netārāvaśvinau tena rathenāsmabhyamasmākaṃ vartirvartanādhikaraṇaṃ gṛhaṃ yātam | āgacchatam ‖ javīyān | javo 'syāstīti javavān tadasyāstīti matup | tata ātiśāyanika īyasun | vinmatorluk | ṭeriti ṭilopaḥ | jigāti | gā stutau | jauhotyādikaḥ | gatikarmasu pāṭhādatra gatyarthaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasītyabhyāsasyettvam ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, that chariot of yours, which is manasaḥ javīyān, swifter than the mind, svaśvaḥ, drawn by good horses, viśaḥ ājigāti — goes in the front to the people. By which chariot you go to the duroṇam, the house, in the form of the place of sacrifice, of the sacrificer who performs a good sacrifice: O leaders, Aśvins, by that chariot come to our vartiḥ, our house — the place of dwelling."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he aśvinau — O Aśvin deities; vām — your (belonging to you); manasaḥ — than the mind; javīyān — extremely swift; svaśvaḥ — with good horses; yaḥ rathaḥ — which chariot; viśaḥ — to the people; ājigāti — goes toward; yena — by which chariot; sukṛtaḥ — [of him] who does auspicious sacrifices (the sacrificer); duroṇam — to the house of worship; gacchathaḥ — you go; tena — by that (chariot); he narā — O leader Aśvin deities; asmabhyam — to our; vartiḥ — house (dwelling-place); yātam — come."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O leader Aśvin deities, in the chariot, swifter than thought, yoked with good horses, in which you go toward the people, and in which you go to the house of worship of those who perform auspicious sacrifices — come, both of you, in that same chariot to our dwelling-place."

English Translation (as printed)

With that car, Ashwins, which, rapid as thought, drawn by good horses, appears before men, and with which you repair to the dwelling of the virtuous, come, leaders of (sacrifices), to our abode.

original p. 315

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अश्विना — Aśvinā — "Yāska considers who the Aśvin deities are. The sequence stated in the Nirukta on this matter runs thus —

अथातो द्युस्थाना देवताः । तासामश्विनौ प्रथमागामिनौ भवतः । अश्विनौ यद्व्यश्नुवाते सर्वं रसेनान्यो ज्योतिषान्यः । अश्वैरश्विनावित्यौर्णवाभः । तत्कावश्विनौ द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके । अहोरात्रावित्येके । सूर्याचन्द्रमसावित्येके । राजानौ पुण्यकृतावित्यैतिहासिकाः ॥ (नि. १२-१ [as read])

athāto dyusthānā devatāḥ | tāsāmaśvinau prathamāgāminau bhavataḥ | aśvinau yadvyaśnuvāte sarvaṃ rasenānyo jyotiṣānyaḥ | aśvairaśvināvityaurṇavābhaḥ | tatkāvaśvinau dyāvāpṛthivyāvityeke | ahorātrāvityeke | sūryācandramasāvityeke | rājānau puṇyakṛtāvityaitihāsikāḥ ‖ (ni. 12-1 [as read])

"From here onward the deities of the atmosphere-region (dyusthāna) are described; and, as the first of them, the question 'who are the Aśvins' is the first matter, and he begins the discussion: one who pervades everything with water (rasa), and one who pervades everything with light: two such exist, says one view; the teacher named Aurṇavābha says that the two Aśvin deities are two, [conveyed] by 'horses' (aśva). Others, in the inquiry 'who are the Aśvins', say that the two are those who pervade the earth with food and the atmosphere with light, [that is] heaven and earth, known as such to all [bhūyaṃ tarikṣa — as printed, doubtful [?]]. Others say that instead of saying that they are two who pervade the day with light and the night with dew, the Aśvins are time itself, in the form of day and night, which is the support of that pervasion. Still others — that they are the Sun and the Moon, since the Sun pervades with radiance and the Moon with water; being [those who] regulate time. The Itihāsa-writers (aitihāsikāḥ) — that is, those who know the course of events in former times, or who know what happened — say that the two Aśvin deities are two kings who had amassed merit. This view agrees with the view accepted by the teacher named Aurṇavābha.

तयोः कालः ऊर्ध्वमर्धरात्रात्प्रकाशीभावस्यानुविष्टम्भम् । अनुक्तनो भागो हि मध्यमः ज्योतिर्भाग आदित्यः ॥ (नि. १२-१ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]])

tayoḥ kālaḥ ūrdhvamardharātrātprakāśībhāvasyānuviṣṭambham | anuktano bhāgo hi madhyamaḥ jyotirbhāga ādityaḥ ‖ (ni. 12-1 [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]])

"Their time [of appearance] is before sunrise: the Aśvin deities' praises come before sunrise, and the Sun's praises follow after sunrise; the part of light that is a little less than the Sun's, [with a little] darkness, is before the Sun's rising and is called madhyama, 'the middle'. The portion of light that is entirely free of darkness and has luminosity is called āditya: so, as the middle portion, and as the highest, the time that exists in the intermediate and highest state is held to be the Aśvin deities: this is the view of the Nirukta-writer.

original p. 316

वसातिषु स्म चरथो सिता पेत्वाविव । कदेदमश्विना युवमभि देवाँ आगच्छतम् ॥ (नि. १२-१ [as read; the quotation is a Ṛk-pāda of doubtful reading in the print [?]])

vasātiṣu sma caratho sitā petvāviva | kadedamaśvinā yuvamabhi devā~ āgacchatam ‖ (ni. 12-1 [as read; the quotation is a Ṛk-pāda of doubtful reading in the print [?]])

इति सा निगदव्याख्याता । वसातिषु स्म चरथो वसातयो रातयो वसन्ते स्याः इतरेतरा तयोः वक्त्रीर्वा वहश्रीर्वा सिता पेत्वाविव । आसेत्वा वृत्रहणं सुरातयोः ॥ (नि. १२-१ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]])

iti sā nigadavyākhyātā | vasātiṣu sma caratho vasātayo rātayo vasante syāḥ itaretarā tayoḥ vaktrīrvā vahaśrīrvā sitā petvāviva | āsetvā vṛtrahaṇaṃ surātayoḥ ‖ (ni. 12-1 [as read; small type, doubtful [?]])

"'At the time when the light of the eye, which performs the function of seeing by the power of the deities, is little [as at night, and at the junctures of day and night] — like clouds that move about — I have recognized you with great effort at dawn.' Since it is said in this mantra 'you two come at the time when the other deities come for the sacrifice', for both of them the time of the sacrifice comes after midnight has passed. For the two, in two vessels (two potsherds, kapāla) the oblations are prepared. Both are of one intention and accomplish the work. From the mantra that is the basis of what Aurṇavābha says and what the Nirukta-writer says, both have constructed different meanings.

"In this mantra the word vasātiṣu — vasāti — is a name of a country. The two (princes) who were kings of it were called Vāsātya. They had many horses; therefore, 'those who possess horses', the name aśvin arose for them. They earned much merit and became helpers of the deities in sacrifices. These two, with the same form, appearance, and practice, wandering, joined the company of the deities: thus the teacher Aurṇavābha explains the meaning. Refuting this view, the Nirukta-writer —

तयोः समानकालयोः समानकर्मणोः संस्तुत्प्रत्ययोः असंस्तवे नैपोर्धर्त्रोर्भवति । वासात्म्यो ऽन्य उच्यते उषः पुत्रस्त्वान्य इति ॥ (नि. १२-१ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]])

tayoḥ samānakālayoḥ samānakarmaṇoḥ saṃstutpratyayoḥ asaṃstave naipordhartrorbhavati | vāsātmyo 'nya ucyate uṣaḥ putrastvānya iti ‖ (ni. 12-1 [as read; small type, doubtful [?]])

"For these two, the time is one, the work is of one kind, and the praise is eminently [equal], so the first half of the Ṛk vasātiṣu [as read] is able to describe the form and works of these two. From this: vāsātmya ('belonging to the vāsa-lineage'), one of the two, is said to be the son of the night, which is the middle [state]; and the other is the upaḥ-son, the son of Uṣas — thus he explains.

original p. 317

"By the meaning of the Ṛk that conveys praise, [showing] that the two are different, [the Nirukta] describes the one, the son of Night, who is vāsātmya, of the middle position, and the other as the son of Uṣas. The middle and highest rank of these Aśvin deities is also made clear in —

इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा३ नामभिः स्वैः । जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१८१-४ [as read])

iheha jātā samavāvaśītāmarepasā tanvā3 nāmabhiḥ svaiḥ | jiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumakhasya sūrirdivo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-181-4 [as read])

"In this Ṛk, with the explanation 'here and here' — in the dyusthāna and the madhyasthāna — [it is said] 'the one, jiṣṇuḥ, of the Sun? [as printed: 'Divaḥ anyaḥ, subhagaḥ putraḥ ūhe'] and 'the other conquering, jiṣṇur vām anyaḥ', one is carried by the wind as a son of the atmosphere (dyusthāna); and the other is the Āditya, victorious by nature: this shows their superior and middle states.

प्रातर्यावाणा वि बोधयन्तावश्विनावेह गच्छताम् । अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-२२-१ [as read])

prātaryāvāṇā vi bodhayantāvaśvināveha gacchatām | asya somasya pītaye ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-22-1 [as read])

"By this Ṛk it is explained that they are fond of praise [and that] both, working with a single intention, are companions.

प्रातर्यजध्वमश्विना हिनोत न सायमस्ति देवया अजुष्टम् । उतान्यो अस्मद्यजते वि चावः पूर्वःपूर्वो यजमानो वनीयान् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-५२-५ [as read; the number printed "३-२२-३" is doubtful [?]])

prātaryajadhvamaśvinā hinota na sāyamasti devayā ajuṣṭam | utānyo asmadyajate vi cāvaḥ pūrvaḥpūrvo yajamāno vanīyān ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 3-52-5 [as read; the number printed "3-22-3" is doubtful [?]])

"In this Ṛk it is stated that praise should be made to the Aśvin deities in the morning itself and oblations should be offered; and it is explained that the homa should not be performed for them in the evening. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka too — vāsātyau kṛṣṇau jagato nidhānau dyāvābhūmī cirathas saṃsakhāyau [as read; doubtful [?]] — beginning thus, the description of their form and colour [begins].

"The chariot of the Aśvin deities is to be understood as yoked with excellent horses, and as capable of going with exceeding speed, quicker than the speed of thought. The prayer is expressed in this Ṛk that the Aśvins, in such a chariot, come to the houses of us who are sacrificers and subjects."

वर्तिः — Vartiḥ — "vartanādhikaraṇaṃ gṛham: 'the house, a place of dwelling': so Sāyaṇa explains the word vartis." Yāska's examples for vartiḥ, Ni. 6-30 as read [?]:

original p. 318

तिरश्चिद्र्यो अर्यो परि वर्तिर्यातमदाभ्या माध्वी ममु श्रुतं हवम् । (ऋ. सं. ५-७५-? [as read; small type, doubtful [?]])

tiraścidryo aryo pari vartiryātamadābhyā mādhvī mamu śrutaṃ havam | (ṛ. saṃ. 5-75-? [as read; small type, doubtful [?]])

अभीदु शक्रः परशुर्यथा वनं पात्रेव भिन्दन्त्सत एति रक्षसः । (ऋ. सं. ६-१०१-?? [as read; doubtful [?]])

abhīdu śakraḥ paraśuryathā vanaṃ pātreva bhindantsata eti rakṣasaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 6-101-?? [as read; doubtful [?]])

"…so Yāska gives these as examples (Ni. 6-30 as read [?]). The word vartiḥ, combined with the prefix, he explains in the commentary: 'turning back, having made a turning-round, come with your chariot'; here vartiḥ is used as an adverbial qualifier of the action. Skandasvāmin explains vartiḥ as 'vartanyā mārgeṇa', 'by the road, by the path'."

दुरोणम् — Duroṇam — "devayajanalakṣaṇaṃ gṛham": "the house in the form of a sacrificial place for the gods, the house in which sacrifice is performed for the deities: the sacrificial hall. The word duroṇa is stated among the twenty-two [as read] names of house (Ni. 3-?? as read [?])."

विशः — Viśaḥ — "prajāḥ: 'subjects'. The word is stated among the names of man (Ni. 2-?? as read [?])."

aśvinā (supāṃ sulug, Pā. 7-1-39 as read [?], ā for the vocative dual ending; nighāta by āmantritasya ca); javīyān (javaḥ asyāsti iti javān; tad asyāsty asmin, Pā. 5-2-94 as read [?], matup; to it, in the comparative sense, dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau, Pā. 5-3-57 as read [?], īyasun; since this is later, vinmator luk, Pā. 5-3-65 as read [?], luk for matup; ṭer, Pā. 6-4-155 as read [?], elision of the ṭi [a]; jñityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197 as read [?], first-syllable accent; in the nominative with su following, ataḥ… upadhādīrgha; num, as ugit); jigāti (gā "to praise", juhotyādi — read in the group of verbs of going, so here used in the sense of going; laṭ 3rd singular tip; śluḥ as vikaraṇa; ślau, Pā. 6-1-10 as read [?], doubling; kuhoś cuḥ, Pā. 7-4-62 as read [?], j for the reduplication; bahulaṃ chandasi, Pā. 7-4-78 as read [?], i for the reduplication; because yaḥ is connected, no nighāta since yadvṛttān nityam, Pā. 8-1-66 as read [?]; abhyastānām ādiḥ, Pā. 6-1-189 as read [?], first-syllable accent).

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.3)

ऋषिं नरावंहसः पाञ्चजन्यमृबीसादत्रिं मुञ्चथो गणेन । मिनन्ता दस्योरशिवस्य माया अनुपूर्वं वृषणा चोदयन्ता ॥ ३ ॥

ṛṣiṃ narāvaṃhasaḥ pāñcajanyamṛbīsādatriṃ muñcatho gaṇena | minantā dasyoraśivasya māyā anupūrvaṃ vṛṣaṇā codayantā ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.3)

ऋषिम् । नरौ । अंहसः । पाञ्चऽजन्यम् । ऋबीसात् । अत्रिम् । मुञ्चथः । गणेन । मिनन्ता । दस्योः । अशिवस्य । मायाः । अनुऽपूर्वम् । वृषणा । चोदयन्ता ॥ ३ ॥

ṛṣim | narau | aṃhasaḥ | pāñca 'janyam | ṛbīsāt | atrim | muñcathaḥ | gaṇena | minantā | dasyoḥ | aśivasya | māyāḥ | anu 'pūrvam | vṛṣaṇā | codayantā ‖ 3 ‖

original p. 320

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.3)

हिमेनाग्निम् । ऋ. सं. १-११६-८ । इत्यनयोक्तो विवार्थः पुनः प्रकारान्तरेणानया प्रतिपाद्यते । अतस्तत्रोक्तं सर्वमत्रापि द्रष्टव्यम् । अक्षरार्थस्तु । हे नरौ नेतारौ वृषणौ कामानां वर्षितारावश्विनौ पाञ्चजन्यम् । निषादपञ्चमाश्चत्वारो वर्णाः पञ्च जनाः । तेषु भवं स्वभार्यानुना गृहीतमेतमृषिमत्रिं सूर्यं मोचयेत्यन्त्रि [?] सर्वेषां हिताचरणात्रात्र भव इत्युच्यते । तादृशमृषिमंहसः पापरूपाद्ऋबीसाच्छतद्वारे यन्त्रगृहे [?] त्रेः पीडार्थमसुरैः प्रक्षिप्तात्तुषाग्नेः सकाशाद्गणेनेन्द्रियवर्गेण पुत्रपौत्रादिगणेन वा सह मुञ्चथः । अमोचयतम् । किं कुर्वन्तौ । मिनन्ता शत्रून्हिंसन्तौ दस्योरुपक्षपयितुरशिवस्य दुःखकारिणोऽसुरस्य सम्बन्धिनीस्तस्मिन्न्नेत्रे प्रयुक्ता मायाश्चानुपूर्वमानुपूर्व्येण चोदयन्तौ प्रेरयन्तौ निवारयन्तौ ॥ पाञ्चजन्यम् । बहिर्देवपञ्चजनेभ्यश्चेति वक्तव्यम् । का. ४-३-६४-१ । इति भवार्थे ञ्यः । मिनन्ता । मीञ् हिंसायाम् । क्र्यादिकः । लटः शतृ । मीनातेर्निगम इति ह्रस्वत्वम् ॥ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

himenāgnim | ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-8 | ityanayokto vivārthaḥ punaḥ prakārāntareṇānayā pratipādyate | atastatroktaṃ sarvamatrāpi draṣṭavyam | akṣarārthastu | he narau netārau vṛṣaṇau kāmānāṃ varṣitārāvaśvinau pāñcajanyam | niṣādapañcamāścatvāro varṇāḥ pañca janāḥ | teṣu bhavaṃ svabhāryānunā gṛhītametamṛṣimatriṃ sūryaṃ mocayetyantri [?] sarveṣāṃ hitācaraṇātrātra bhava ityucyate | tādṛśamṛṣimaṃhasaḥ pāparūpādṛbīsācchatadvāre yantragṛhe [?] treḥ pīḍārthamasuraiḥ prakṣiptāttuṣāgneḥ sakāśādgaṇenendriyavargeṇa putrapautrādigaṇena vā saha muñcathaḥ | amocayatam | kiṃ kurvantau | minantā śatrūnhiṃsantau dasyorupakṣapayituraśivasya duḥkhakāriṇo 'surasya sambandhinīstasminnnetre prayuktā māyāścānupūrvamānupūrvyeṇa codayantau prerayantau nivārayantau ‖ pāñcajanyam | bahirdevapañcajanebhyaśceti vaktavyam | kā. 4-3-64-1 | iti bhavārthe ñyaḥ | minantā | mīñ hiṃsāyām | kryādikaḥ | laṭaḥ śatṛ | mīnāternigama iti hrasvatvam ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]

Sense (mine): "The matter stated by himenāgnim (Ṛ. 1-116-8) is here set forth in another way; therefore whatever was said there is to be understood here too. The literal sense: O leaders, O vṛṣaṇā, showerers of desires, Aśvins — pāñcajanyam: the four castes with the Niṣādas as the fifth are the pañca janāḥ; he who is among them [Atri], seized by his own [fire] — the ṛṣi Atri, who works the good of all, is therefore said to be 'born among them [all]' — such a ṛṣi you released from aṃhasaḥ, from the sin-like ṛbīsa [the dark pit], from the fire of husks thrown by the Asuras to torment Atri, in the hundred-doored torture-house, gaṇena — together with the group of his senses, or with the group of sons and grandsons. Doing what? Minantā — destroying enemies; dasyoḥ aśivasya māyāḥ — the devices applied to him by the Asura, the harmful one, the pain-giver; anupūrvam — in due order, driving off, [you] restraining them."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"he narau — O leader Aśvin deities; vṛṣaṇā — [you] who grant desired objects; pāñcajanyam — one connected with the five classes of men; atrim ṛṣim — the ṛṣi Atri; aṃhasaḥ — from the sin-like; ṛbīsāt — from the machine-house (from the fire thrown into the machine-house); gaṇena — together with his group of senses (sons and grandsons); minantā — destroying enemies; dasyoḥ — of the destroyer; aśivasya — of the pain-causing [Asura]; māyāḥ — the devices (employed against Atri); anupūrvam — completely; codayantā — [you] restraining; muñcathaḥ — you released."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O leader Aśvin deities, granters of desires: you released the ṛṣi Atri, connected with the five classes of men, from the sinful machine-house (from the fire thrown by the Asuras), with his senses unimpaired (together with his sons and grandsons); and you wholly destroyed the devices of those Asuras, who are destroyers and causers of pain."

English Translation (as printed)

  1. You liberated, leaders (of rites), the sage Atri, who was venerated by the five classes of men, from the wicked prison, together with his troop (of children), destroying his enemies and baffling, showerers (of benefits), the devices of the malignant Dasyus.
original p. 321

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

"In explaining the meaning of this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa says that the idea expressed in this Ṛk is described in the mantra

हिमेनाग्निं घ्रंसमवारयेथां पितुमतीमूर्जमस्मा अधत्तम् । ऋबीसे अत्रिमश्विनावनीतमुन्निन्यथुः सर्वगणं स्वस्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-८ [as read])

himenāgniṃ ghraṃsamavārayethāṃ pitumatīmūrjamasmā adhattam | ṛbīse atrimaśvināvanītamunninyathuḥ sarvagaṇaṃ svasti ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-8 [as read])

and that the same meaning is here stated again in another way."

पाञ्चजन्यम् — Pāñcajanyam — "niṣādapañcamāś catvāro varṇāḥ pañca janāḥ teṣu bhavam": "the four castes (brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, śūdra), with the Niṣāda (hunter) as the fifth, are denoted by the word pañcajana. Sāyaṇa explains the meaning as 'beneficial to them'. Skandasvāmin —

पाञ्चजन्यम् — पाञ्चजन्यः । पञ्चभ्यो जनेभ्यः गन्धर्वा पितरो देवाः असुरा रक्षांसीत्येतेभ्यो निषादपञ्चमेभ्यो वा चतुर्भ्यो वर्णेभ्यः हितं । पञ्चानां हि जनानां स्थितिकरी वृष्टिः । तस्या हेतुभूतो यज्ञः । तस्य कर्ता अत्रिः इत्येवमस्य हितत्वम् ॥

pāñcajanyam — pāñcajanyaḥ | pañcabhyo janebhyaḥ gandharvā pitaro devāḥ asurā rakṣāṃsītyetebhyo niṣādapañcamebhyo vā caturbhyo varṇebhyaḥ hitaṃ | pañcānāṃ hi janānāṃ sthitikarī vṛṣṭiḥ | tasyā hetubhūto yajñaḥ | tasya kartā atriḥ ityevamasya hitatvam ‖ [first words 'bāhyo daivyaḥ pāñcajanyaḥ (Vā. 4-3-?? [?])' as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

— 'beneficial to the five janas — Gandharvas, Pitṛs, Devas, Asuras, Rākṣasas; or to the four castes with the Niṣāda as fifth; for rain sustains the five peoples; its cause is sacrifice; Atri is its doer: so he is beneficial.' In Kannada: the suffix ṭya comes in the sense of 'beneficial to' after the word pañcajana, giving pāñcajanya; the pañcajanas — Gandharvas, Pitṛs, Devas, Asuras, Rākṣasas — [or Sāyaṇa's explanation]: both making the five-fold sense plain, he explains the word pāñcajanya specially for Atri as 'one who produces rain, beneficial to all'. Though Sāyaṇa too explains the adjective, he explains teṣu bhavam as in another way: 'svarbhānunā gṛhītam amuṃ sūryaṃ moco yo 'triḥ pañcajanebhya utpannaḥ — Atri, who released that Sun seized by Svarbhānu [Rāhu], born among the five peoples' — the ṛṣi Atri, who released the Sun when Rāhu had seized him. Skandasvāmin's explanation, that [by tya] 'beneficial' is meant because Atri is beneficial to all as the producer of rain, is well suited.

"The Nirukta-writer, since the word pañcajana is listed among the names of man, gives the derivation of pañcajana —

original p. 322

पञ्च जना इत्येतस्य निगमा भवन्ति ॥ (नि. ३-८ [as read])

pañca janā ityetasya nigamā bhavanti ‖ (ni. 3-8 [as read])

"[and] the Vedic sentence that explains the meaning of the word pañcajana among the words for man is thus —

कदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुराँ अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जादा उत यज्ञियासः पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-५३-४ [as read])

kadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā~ abhi devā asāma | ūrjādā uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-53-4 [as read])

he cites this Ṛk, and

पञ्च जनाः गन्धर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पञ्चम इत्यौपमन्यवः ॥ (नि. ३-८ [as read])

pañca janāḥ gandharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ pañcama ityaupamanyavaḥ ‖ (ni. 3-8 [as read])

— explaining the view that the 'five' are Gandharvas, Pitṛs, Devas, Asuras, Rākṣasas, and the view of Aupamanyava that the four castes together with the Niṣāda are the five peoples. Again —

निषादः कस्मान्निषदनो भवति निषण्णमस्मिन् पापकमिति नैरुक्ताः । यत्पाञ्चजन्यया विशा पञ्चजनीनया विशा पञ्चैवेक्ता संख्या स्त्रीनपुंसकेष्वविशिष्टा ॥

niṣādaḥ kasmānniṣadano bhavati niṣaṇṇamasmin pāpakamiti nairuktāḥ | yatpāñcajanyayā viśā pañcajanīnayā viśā pañcaivektā saṃkhyā strīnapuṃsakeṣvaviśiṣṭā ‖ [Nirukta-passage as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

— he explains the meaning of the word niṣāda: since sin is found in them in excess, he is called niṣāda; and from the number five contained in the word pāñcajanya in another Ṛk, 'yat pāñcajanyayā viśā', he explains that the distinctions of feminine, masculine and neuter do not occur in the people denoted by viś.

"Skandasvāmin, explaining the word dasyoḥ —

वि जानीह्यार्यान्ये च दस्यवो बर्हिष्मते रन्धया शासदव्रतान् । शाकी भव यजमानस्य चोदिता विश्वेत्ता ते सधमादेषु चाकन ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५१-८ [as read])

vi jānīhyāryānye ca dasyavo barhiṣmate randhayā śāsadavratān | śākī bhava yajamānasya coditā viśvettā te sadhamādeṣu cākana ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-51-8 [as read])

cites this Ṛk. In it he gives the meaning: those who perform sacrifices or observe vows are the ārya; those other than them are dasyus, enemies of the deities and not given to sacrifice. Sāyaṇa explains dasyu as 'upakṣapayituḥ aśivasya duḥkhakāriṇo 'surasya' — a harmful one who causes pain, increases suffering, takes life."

original p. 323

अनुपूर्वं चोदयन्ता — Anupūrvaṃ codayantā — "ānupūrvyeṇa preraya nto nivārayantau": "in the matter of the ṛṣi Atri, he explains two meanings: [they, the Aśvin deities,] averted the harmful deceits practised by the Asuras. Skandasvāmin: 'he vṛṣaṇā varṣitārau tāsu tāsv abhipretaphalāsu atriṃ codayantā upadeśādinā preraya ntau': 'O showerers, urging Atri to those desired fruits by instruction and so on' — the Aśvin deities, fulfilling the wishes of sacrificers, instructed the ṛṣi Atri so that he might obtain the desired fruits, and fulfilled his wishes: thus he explains the sense. That the Aśvin deities protected the ṛṣi Atri is described also by the ṛṣi Kutsa —

याभिः शुचन्तिं धनसां सुषंसदं तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावन्तमत्रये । याभिः पृश्निगुं पुरुकुत्समावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१६ [as read])

yābhiḥ śucantiṃ dhanasāṃ suṣaṃsadaṃ taptaṃ gharmamomyāvantamatraye | yābhiḥ pṛśniguṃ purukutsamāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-16 [as read])

— this Ṛk is cited."

Sense (mine): "O leaders, vṛṣaṇā, showerers of desires, Aśvins: you, having drawn up from the well the ṛṣi Rebha — hidden in the waters in a well, buried, by wicked [enemies] — viprutam, whose limbs were scattered, saṃ riṇīthaḥ, you restored, united, by your healing deeds, like a sick horse: you made him complete with all limbs. Your ancient deeds do not grow old; for they do not become aged."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"narā — leaders; vṛṣaṇā — givers of desired objects; aśvinā — O Aśvin deities; durevaiḥ — by wicked [Asuras]; apsu — in the water of the well; gūḷham — hidden; rebham ṛṣim — the ṛṣi Rebha (drawn up from the well); viprutam — whose limbs were scattered; tam — him; aśvam na — as one cures a sick horse; daṃsobhiḥ — by your healing actions; saṃ riṇīthaḥ — you made whole (made [him] complete with all limbs); vām — your; pūrvyā — ancient; kṛtāni — deeds; na jūryanti — do not grow old (are not forgotten)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O leaders, granters of desired objects, Aśvin deities, you drew up the ṛṣi Rebha hidden by wicked Asuras in the water of the well, and healed his scattered limbs, as one heals a sick horse. Your ancient (courageous) deeds do not grow old; they are not forgotten."

English Translation (as printed)

Leaders (of sacrifice), showerers (of benefits), you restored Rebha cast by unassailable (enemies) into the water, and wounded, like a (sick) horse, by your (healing) skill: your ancient exploits do not fade (from recollection).

original p. 326

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अश्वं न दंसोभिः सं रिणीथः — Aśvaṃ na daṃsobhiḥ saṃ riṇīthaḥ — "vyādhitam aśvam iva aśvinyair bhaiṣajyarūpaiḥ karmabhiḥ samadhattaṃ sarvair avayavair upetam akurutam ity arthaḥ": "as one makes a sick horse sound — healing, by acts in the form of medicine, with all its limbs complete — [you did so to Rebha]. The word daṃsa is stated among the twenty-six [as read] names of work (Ni. 2-?? as read [?]). The Asuras bound the ṛṣi named Rebha with ropes and threw him into a well; seeing that his limbs were in danger of destruction [apāya], the Aśvin deities raised him from the well, and, as one raises up a horse that has fallen into [a pit] and treats it with herbs and the like, they made medicine for the ṛṣi Rebha, treated him, and protected him so that he was in health: thus it is described."

वां पूर्व्या कृतानि न जूर्यन्ति — Vāṃ pūrvyā kṛtāni na jūryanti — "yuvayoḥ sambandhīni cirantanāni karmāṇi na jīrṇāni bhavanti": "the earlier acts of kindness done by the Aśvin deities in former times are never forgotten; the power of the Aśvin deities, and their nature of protecting with compassion those who are in difficulty, are described here. Skandasvāmin: 'na vāṃ yuvayoḥ jūryanti jīryante vinaśyantīty arthaḥ pūrvyā pūrvam iti purāṇanāma' — the word pūrva is a name for 'ancient'. Explaining the meaning as Sāyaṇa does, 'kṛtāni karmāṇi', he says that the acts done by the Aśvins in protecting those who were in distress are never destroyed but remain as examples; and the Itihāsa of Rebha, told in this Ṛk, is also told in

दश रात्रीरशिवेना नव द्यूनवनद्धं श्नथितमप्स्वन्तः । विप्रुतं रेभमुदनि प्रवृक्तमुन्निन्यथुः सोममिव स्रुवेण ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-२४ [as read])

daśa rātrīraśivenā nava dyūnavanaddhaṃ śnathitamapsvantaḥ | viprutaṃ rebhamudani pravṛktamunninyathuḥ somamiva sruveṇa ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-24 [as read])

— this Ṛk is cited."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"nirṛteḥ — of the earth; upasthe — on the lap; suṣupvāṃsam na — like one who lies asleep; tamasi — in darkness; kṣiyantam — remaining; sūryaṃ na — like the Sun, brilliant; śubhe — for adornment (that is made); rukmaṃ na — like a shining golden ornament; darśatam — beautiful; nikhātam — buried (by the Asuras in a well); vandanāya — Vandana the ṛṣi; he dasrā aśvinā — O beautiful Aśvin deities; udūpathuḥ — you drew up."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O beautiful Aśvin deities, you lifted up the ṛṣi Vandana — who was thrown by the Asuras into the well, like a man asleep in the lap of the goddess Earth, like the Sun covered in darkness (his brilliance hidden), like a golden ornament made for adornment and beautiful to behold."

English Translation (as printed)

You extricated, Dasras, the sage Vandana, cast into a well, like a handsome and splendid ornament designed for embellishment, and (lying), Ashwins, like one sleeping on the lap of the earth, or like the sun disappearing in darkness.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

"In this Ṛk the greatness of the Aśvin deities is described: they drew up out of the well the ṛṣi Vandana, who had been thrown by the Asuras into the water of the well, and saved him. Three similes are given concerning the ṛṣi Vandana, who, lying in the water of the well, was without strength and without lustre. Nirṛteḥ upasthe suṣupvāṃsaṃ na — like a man lying weak on the earth; tamasi kṣiyantaṃ sūryaṃ na — like the Sun, without lustre in darkness; śubhe rukmaṃ na — as a gold ornament made with great lustre appears beautiful: [such was] the ṛṣi Vandana. This is how Sāyaṇa describes the condition of the ṛṣi. Skandasvāmin gives more explanation on this matter.

"— asking when the Sun is in the darkness [as printed: tamasi nyuṣitair vā sūryaḥ]: the comparison 'like the Sun' is made here; and, considering at what time the Sun is covered by darkness, [the answer is]: 'when Vṛtra the Asura covered the Sun with clouds and made a great darkness, the Sun became lustreless; and when Indra subdued that Vṛtra, he made the Sun as he was before (that is, clearly visible to all)': he explains. vandanamṛṣiṃ yathā bhūmau suptaṃ kañcitkaściddhastena gṛhītvotthāpayet yathā ca vṛtrakṛtena tamasāvastabdhaṃ sūryaṃ divyārohaṇārthamindra uddhṛtavān yathā cātmanaḥ śobhanārthaṃ rukmaṃ nikhātaṃ santaṃ kaściduddharedevaṃ yuvāṃ vandanaṃ kūpe nipatitaṃ tata uddhṛtavantau iti samāsārthaḥ ‖ [small type; partly doubtful [?]]
