॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.6)

हे नरा नेतारौ नासत्यावश्विनौ परिज्मन् परिगमनेऽभीप्सस्य प्रापणे निमित्तभूते सति पज्रियेण पज्राणामङ्गिरसां कुले जातेन कक्षीवता मया वां युवयोः संबन्धि तत्कर्म शंस्यम् । प्रकर्षेण शंसनीयम् । तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्छब्दाध्याहारः । यज्ञनायोपेक्षमाणाय पुरुषाय वाजिनो वेगवतस्तदीयस्याश्वस्य शफान्निर्गतैर्मधूनां मधुभिः शतसंख्याकान्कुम्भानसिञ्चतम् । अपूरयतम् । सिञ्चतिरत्र पूरणार्थः । यदेतन्मधुना पूरणं तच्छंस्यमित्यर्थः ॥

he narā netārau nāsatyāvaśvinau parijman parigamane 'bhīpsasya prāpaṇe nimittabhūte sati pajriyeṇa pajrāṇāmaṅgirasāṃ kule jātena kakṣīvatā mayā vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhi tatkarma śaṃsyam | prakarṣeṇa śaṃsanīyam | tacchabdaśruteryacchabdādhyāhāraḥ | yajñanāyopekṣamāṇāya puruṣāya vājino vegavatastadīyasyāśvasya śaphānnirgatairmadhūnāṃ madhubhiḥ śatasaṃkhyākānkumbhānasiñcatam | apūrayatam | siñcatiratra pūraṇārthaḥ | yadetanmadhunā pūraṇaṃ tacchaṃsyamityarthaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "O leaders (narā), Nāsatyas, Aśvins — when parijman, the reaching of the desired object, is the occasion, pajriyeṇa — by me, Kakṣīvat, born in the family of the Pajras, the Aṅgirases — that deed of yours (vām) is śaṃsya, to be praised exceedingly. (From the word tat in the text, the word yat is to be supplied.) For the man who is waiting (upekṣamāṇāya, as printed; for the sacrifice [?]), you filled (asiñcatam, 'made full'; the root sic here has the sense of filling) a hundred jars with the honey (madhūnām) flowing from the hoof of his fleet (vājinaḥ) horse. That filling with honey is what is to be praised." (Printed yajñanāyopekṣamāṇāya — kept as printed [sic?].)

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.6) (Kannada, rendered)

narā — O leaders (of sacrifices); nāsatyā — Nāsatyas; janāya — for the (expectant) people; vājinaḥ aśvasya — of your fleet horse; śaphāt — from the hoof (flowing out); madhūnām — with sweet liquor; śataṃ kumbhān — a hundred jars; asiñcatam — you filled; (iti yat — what is said); vām — of you both; tat — that deed [?]; parijman — for the sake of obtaining the desired thing; pajriyeṇa — born in the race of Pajra (of the Aṅgirases); kakṣīvatā — by Kakṣīvat (by me); śaṃsyam — is to be praised.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.6) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Nāsatyas, leaders of sacrifices! I, called Kakṣīvat, born in the family of Pajra (the Aṅgirases), shall praise, for the attainment of what is desired, that great deed of yours: that for the people who longed for it you filled a hundred jars with the honey that flowed from the hoof of your swift horse."

English Translation (as printed)

"That (exploit) of yours, leader (of sacrifice), is to be celebrated, Nasatyas, by Kakshivat, of the race of Pajra, when you filled for the (expectant) man a hundred vases of sweet (liquors) from the hoof of your fleet horse."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 6)

Parijman — parigamane abhīpsasya prāpane nimittabhūte sati: "When the matter that is wanted (the sought-after object) has come to hand" — so Sāyaṇa; and (the Special Topic quotes) "sarvato gacchanti devā yatra, sa parijmā" … (the page ends here; continues p. 334).

original p. 334

continuing "… yajñaḥ." Since the place to which all the gods must go is the place where the sacrifice is conducted, Skandasvāmin too gives the word parijman here the meaning "sacrifice (yajña)."

Pajriyeṇa — pajrāṇām aṅgirasāṃ kule jātena: "Pajra is the name of the descendants of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis; 'born in their line' is the sense. Skandasvāmin: 'pājaḥ annaṃ haviḥ-lakṣaṇaṃ tadvetā [as printed; ?] athavā pajrāḥ aṅgirasaḥ tadapatyabhūtena mayā kakṣīvatā' — the word pājas means food in the form of oblation; 'one who has that', i.e. one who has prepared the oblation for the sacrifice; or the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis are the Pajras, and the one born in their line is Kakṣīvat — the ṛṣi, seer of this sūkta — thus he explains it in another way."

In this Ṛk the ṛṣi Kakṣīvat, seer of this sūkta, describing the glory of the Aśvins, sets forth their generosity. That is: when in the sacrifice the yajamāna wished for madya (spirituous drink), the Aśvins, by their grace, produced from the hoof of the horse great numbers of jars of that very drink — thus the generosity of the Aśvins is set out by Skandasvāmin. (Printed "Sautrā[?]ṇi" for the sacrifice named in the opening of this paragraph: reading doubtful [?].)

Kakṣīvatā — mayā: "Who is the ṛṣi of this mantra? 'By me' (mayā)," is Sāyaṇa's meaning. Nirukta says:

सोमानां स्वरणं कृणुहि ब्रह्मणस्पते । कक्षीवन्तं य औशिजः । (ऋ. सं. १-१८-१ [as printed])

somānāṃ svaraṇaṃ kṛṇuhi brahmaṇaspate | kakṣīvantaṃ ya auśijaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-18-1 [as printed])

सोमानां सोतारं प्रकाशनवन्तं कुरु ब्रह्मणस्पते कक्षीवन्तमिव य औशिजः । कक्षीवान् कक्ष्यावान् औशिजः उशिजः पुत्रः उशिग्वष्टेः कान्तिकर्मणः अपि त्वयं मनुष्यकक्ष एवाभिप्रेतः स्यात् तं सोमानां सोतारं मां प्रकाशनवन्तं कुरु ब्रह्मणस्पते ॥ [? several words small] (नि. ६-११ [as read])

somānāṃ sotāraṃ prakāśanavantaṃ kuru brahmaṇaspate kakṣīvantamiva ya auśijaḥ | kakṣīvān kakṣyāvān auśijaḥ uśijaḥ putraḥ uśigvaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇaḥ api tvayaṃ manuṣyakakṣa evābhipretaḥ syāt taṃ somānāṃ sotāraṃ māṃ prakāśanavantaṃ kuru brahmaṇaspate ‖ [? several words small] (ni. 6-11 [as read])

Sense (editorial and tentative): "'Make me, the presser of the soma-juices, a shining one (prakāśanavantam), O Brahmaṇaspati, like Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij.' Kakṣīvat (kakṣyāvān) is the Auśija, the son of Uśij, from the root vaś 'to desire' (kāntikarman); [the Nirukta adds that a man of the same 'enclosure' (kakṣa) may be intended]; 'make me, that presser of soma, a shining one, O Brahmaṇaspati.'"

Kannada: "From the root vaś kāntau ('to wish', kāntir icchā) the word uśik is formed. In this Ṛk, Kakṣīvat, born of the woman called Uśik, prays that Brahmaṇaspati (Soma, the king of the Brāhmaṇas) make him [one who presses the soma-juice]. From this it is understood that Kakṣīvat, as the son of the woman named Uśik, joined the company of men (the kakṣya) [?], performed sacrifices, and pleased the gods." Reading of the Kannada tail uncertain [?].

युवम् । नरा । स्तुवते । कृष्णियाय । विष्णाप्वम् । ददथुः । विश्वकाय । घोषायै । चित् । पितृसदे । दुरोणे । पतिम् । जूर्यन्त्यै । अश्विनौ । अदत्तम् ॥ ७ ॥

yuvam | narā | stuvate | kṛṣṇiyāya | viṣṇāpvam | dadathuḥ | viśvakāya | ghoṣāyai | cit | pitṛsade | duroṇe | patim | jūryantyai | aśvinau | adattam ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.7)

हे नरा नेतारावश्विनौ युवं युवां स्तुवते स्तोत्रं कुर्वते कृष्णियाय कृष्णाख्यस्य पुत्राय विश्वकाय विष्णाप्वं ददथुः । विष्णाप्वं नाम विनष्टं पुत्रं दत्तवन्तौ । घोषा नाम ब्रह्मवादिनी कक्षीवतो दुहिता । सा कुष्ठिनी सती कस्मैचिद्वरायादत्ता पितृगृहे विषण्णा जीर्णासीत् । साश्विनोरनुग्रहान्नष्टकुष्ठा सती पतिं लेभे । तदेतदाह । हे अश्विनौ पित्रा संबद्धे दुरोणे स्वकीयजनगृहे कुष्ठरोगेण भर्तारमप्राप्य पितृषदे पितृसमीपे विषण्णायै जूर्यन्त्यै जरां प्राप्नुवत्यै घोषायै चित् एतत्संज्ञायै ब्रह्मवादिन्यै अपि रोगोपशमनेन पतिं भर्तारमदत्तम् । युवां दत्तवन्तौ ॥

he narā netārāvaśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ stuvate stotraṃ kurvate kṛṣṇiyāya kṛṣṇākhyasya putrāya viśvakāya viṣṇāpvaṃ dadathuḥ | viṣṇāpvaṃ nāma vinaṣṭaṃ putraṃ dattavantau | ghoṣā nāma brahmavādinī kakṣīvato duhitā | sā kuṣṭhinī satī kasmaicidvarāyādattā pitṛgṛhe viṣaṇṇā jīrṇāsīt | sāśvinoranugrahānnaṣṭakuṣṭhā satī patiṃ lebhe | tadetadāha | he aśvinau pitrā saṃbaddhe duroṇe svakīyajanagṛhe kuṣṭharogeṇa bhartāramaprāpya pitṛṣade pitṛsamīpe viṣaṇṇāyai jūryantyai jarāṃ prāpnuvatyai ghoṣāyai cit etatsaṃjñāyai brahmavādinyai api rogopaśamanena patiṃ bhartāramadattam | yuvāṃ dattavantau ‖

Sense (mine): "O leaders, Aśvins! You (yuvam, you two) gave viṣṇāpvam to Viśvaka, son of Kṛṣṇa (kṛṣṇiya), who was praising you. Viṣṇāpva is a name: you gave back a lost son. Ghoṣā was a brahmavādinī, daughter of Kakṣīvat. Being a leper, she was not given in marriage to anyone, and remained sad and aged in her father's house. By the Aśvins' favour her leprosy having gone, she obtained a husband. That is what is said here: in the duroṇa, the house of her own people, connected with the father — not having obtained a husband because of leprosy, pitṛṣade, near her father, dejected (viṣaṇṇāyai), growing old (jūryantyai), to Ghoṣā, the brahmavādinī of that name — you gave a husband by curing the disease." (The bhāṣya adds grammar: pitṛṣade, from ṣadḷ viśaraṇādiṣu with kvip; jūryantyai, from jṛṣ vayohānau, laṭ, śatṛ, śyan of the Divādi class, bahulaṃ chandasi giving ut, hali ca lengthening, the accent of śyan — characterized, not transcribed.)

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.7) (Kannada, rendered)

Narā — O leaders; aśvinau — O Aśvins; yuvam — you two; stuvate — to him who praised (you); kṛṣṇiyāya — to the son of Kṛṣṇa; viśvakāya — to Viśvaka; viṣṇāpvam — Viṣṇāpva (his lost son) [you] dadathuḥ — gave; duroṇe — in the house of (her) people; pitṛṣade — (because of leprosy, unmarried) staying near her father; jūryantyai — to her who was growing old (attaining old age); ghoṣāyai — to Ghoṣā (making her disease cease); patim cit — a husband also; adattam — you graciously gave.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.7) (Kannada, rendered)

"O leaders, Aśvins! You gave to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, who praised you, the son called Viṣṇāpva (his lost son); and to Ghoṣā, who, unmarried, was staying near her father in the house of the family, and was attaining old age, you graciously gave a husband."

original p. 337

English Translation (as printed)

"You restored, leaders (of sacrifices), Vishnapu (his lost son) to Vishwaka, the son of Krishna, when he praised you; you bestowed, Ashwins, a husband upon Ghosha grwing [sic] old and tarrying in her father's dwelling."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 7)

The Aśvins gave back to Viśvaka — who praised them — his son named Viṣṇāpva, who had been lost (gone somewhere), and so showed him favour: this is described here.

Ghoṣāyai cit patim adattam — etat-saṃjñāyai brahmavādinyai api rogopaśamanena bhartāraṃ yuvāṃ dattavantau: "Ghoṣā is the name; to her, a woman brahmavādinī, the Aśvins gave a husband" — such is the meaning. Ghoṣā was a daughter of the ṛṣi Kakṣīvat. Because leprosy had come upon her, her husband abandoned her, so she lived in her own father's house, praised the Aśvins, and by their grace obtained her husband again and was freed of leprosy — thus the account (itihāsa) is told here.

Skandasvāmin explains this in another way, and quotes a Ṛk that expounds it. And he explains the account of the ṛṣi Viśvaka and his son named Viṣṇāpva, who was lost and then restored, and quotes a Ṛk that tells it:

अवस्यते स्तुवते कृष्णियाय ऋजूयते नासत्या शचीभिः । पशुं न नष्टमिव दर्शनाय विष्णाप्वं ददथुर्विश्वकाय ॥ [as read; third pāda doubtful [?]] (ऋ. सं. १-११६-२३)

avasyate stuvate kṛṣṇiyāya ṛjūyate nāsatyā śacībhiḥ | paśuṃ na naṣṭamiva darśanāya viṣṇāpvaṃ dadathurviśvakāya ‖ [as read; third pāda doubtful [?]] (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-23)

original p. 338

continuing the Special Topics of Ṛk 7 … "in this Ṛk the Aśvins are praised for the matter of the gift of a son (putradāna)."

घोषा नाम कक्षीवतो दुहिता सा दुर्भगत्वात् परित्यक्ता पितुरेव गृहे जरां जगाम । सा जीर्णा अश्विनौ शोभनं भगं ययाचे । तस्यै अश्विनौ स्वयमेव भगतां जग्मतुः इति । तदेतत् घोषैव वक्ष्यति ॥ [as read; the Skandasvāmin quotation in small type [?]]

ghoṣā nāma kakṣīvato duhitā sā durbhagatvāt parityaktā pitureva gṛhe jarāṃ jagāma | sā jīrṇā aśvinau śobhanaṃ bhagaṃ yayāce | tasyai aśvinau svayameva bhagatāṃ jagmatuḥ iti | tadetat ghoṣaiva vakṣyati ‖ [as read; the Skandasvāmin quotation in small type [?]]

On this matter:

आमाजुरश्चिद्भवथो युवं भगो नांशो दविता राशमस्य चित् । अन्धस्य चिन्नासत्या कृशस्य चिद्युवामिदाहुर्भिषजा रुतस्य चित् ॥ [as read; several words doubtful [?]] (ऋ. सं. १०-३९-३ [as read])

āmājuraścidbhavatho yuvaṃ bhago nāṃśo davitā rāśamasya cit | andhasya cinnāsatyā kṛśasya cidyuvāmidāhurbhiṣajā rutasya cit ‖ [as read; several words doubtful [?]] (ṛ. saṃ. 10-39-3 [as read])

— quoting this Ṛk, the history (itihāsa) is told here: Ghoṣā, the daughter of the ṛṣi Kakṣīvat, because of her ill-fortune was abandoned by her husband, grew old in her own father's house, lost her youth, and when she was growing old she prayed to the Aśvins for good fortune (saubhāgya); the Aśvins themselves took on the form of good fortune and fulfilled her desire.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly)

Yuvam — the word yuṣmad; second case dual form; since the rule prathamāyāś ca dvivacane bhāṣāyām is stated for the common language only, the ā-substitution does not occur here. Stuvate — root ṣṭuñ stutau; laṭ's sense, suffix śatṛ, luk of śap; ajiknudhātubhruvām iyuvaṅau (Pā. 6-4-77), substitution uv; dative singular form; śatur anumaḥ (Pā. 6-1-173), the final acute; udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya (Pā. 8-2-4), the unaccented syllable becomes svarita. Kṛṣṇiyāya (kṛṣṇasya ayaṃ kṛṣṇiyaḥ, suffix ghac in the sense of "belonging to"; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ, Pā. 7-1-2, iy substituted; ciṭaḥ, acute on the final). Viṣṇāpvam — yaṇ substituted in the place of an udātta (vi-snāpva?), followed by an anudātta, so udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ (as printed [?]) gives svarita for the anudātta. Dadathuḥ — root dudāñ dāne; liṭ, second person dual; tiṅanta accent nighāta.

original p. 339

Pitṛṣade — root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; when the word pitṛ is the upapada, kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76), suffix kvip; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 [number partly cut off]), the accent of the kṛdanta hindpart is the nature-accent of the base; dative singular form. Jūryantyai — root jṛṣ vayohānau; suffix śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; divādibhyaḥ śyan (Pā. 3-1-69), śyan as the vikaraṇa; bahulaṃ chandasi, the root gets ut followed by r; hali ca (Pā. 8-2-77), lengthening of the penultimate with final r; since the affix lasārvadhātuka follows (ā upadeśāt), tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-86 as printed [?]) makes it unaccented; because śyan has an indicatory ś, ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the initial acute; when the feminine is intended, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6), ṅīp; since ugit, num; dative singular form. Adattam — root dudāñ dāne; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta, accent nighāta. ‖ 7 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.8)

युवं श्यावाय रुशतीमदत्तं महः क्षोणस्याश्विना कण्वाय । प्रवाच्यं तद्वृषणा कृतं वां यन्नार्षदाय श्रवो अध्यधत्तम् ॥ ८ ॥

yuvaṃ śyāvāya ruśatīmadattaṃ mahaḥ kṣoṇasyāśvinā kaṇvāya | pravācyaṃ tadvṛṣaṇā kṛtaṃ vāṃ yannārṣadāya śravo adhyadhattam ‖ 8 ‖

original p. 340

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.8)

युवम् । श्यावाय । रुशतीम् । अदत्तम् । महः । क्षोणस्य । अश्विना । कण्वाय । प्रऽवाच्यम् । तत् । वृषणा । कृतम् । वाम् । यत् । नार्षदाय । श्रवः । अधिऽअधत्तम् ॥ ८ ॥

yuvam | śyāvāya | ruśatīm | adattam | mahaḥ | kṣoṇasya | aśvinā | kaṇvāya | pra 'vācyam | tat | vṛṣaṇā | kṛtam | vām | yat | nārṣadāya | śravaḥ | adhi 'adhattam ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.8) small, dense type; read with several doubts

हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां श्यावाय कुष्ठरोगेण श्यामवर्णायर्षये रुशतीं दीप्ततुचं [?] स्त्रियमदत्तम् । प्रायच्छतम् । अपि च क्षोणस्य क्षोणाय [?] पृष्ठि[?]ना गन्तुमशक्तः सन्नेकस्मिन्नेव स्थाने निवसति तस्मै कण्वायर्षये महस्तेजोरूपं चक्षुरिन्द्रियमदत्तमिति शेषः । तथा हे वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारौ वां युवयोस्तत्कृतं कर्म प्रवाच्यम् । प्रकर्षेण वाचनीयं शंसनीयम् । नार्षदाय नृषदपुत्राय बधिरायर्षये श्रवः श्रवणेन्द्रियं यदध्यधत्तम् । दत्तवन्तौ स्थ इति यत् तदित्यर्थः । अपर आह । ब्राह्मणस्य परीक्षार्थमसुराः कण्वमृषिं गूढे तमसि निदधुः । …

he aśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ śyāvāya kuṣṭharogeṇa śyāmavarṇāyarṣaye ruśatīṃ dīptatucaṃ [?] striyamadattam | prāyacchatam | api ca kṣoṇasya kṣoṇāya [?] pṛṣṭhi[?]nā gantumaśaktaḥ sannekasminneva sthāne nivasati tasmai kaṇvāyarṣaye mahastejorūpaṃ cakṣurindriyamadattamiti śeṣaḥ | tathā he vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣitārau vāṃ yuvayostatkṛtaṃ karma pravācyam | prakarṣeṇa vācanīyaṃ śaṃsanīyam | nārṣadāya nṛṣadaputrāya badhirāyarṣaye śravaḥ śravaṇendriyaṃ yadadhyadhattam | dattavantau stha iti yat tadityarthaḥ | apara āha | brāhmaṇasya parīkṣārthamasurāḥ kaṇvamṛṣiṃ gūḍhe tamasi nidadhuḥ | …

Sense (mine; the first part): "O Aśvins, you gave to Śyāva — a ṛṣi dark-hued from leprosy — a ruśatī, a shining(-skinned) woman [?]; and to Kaṇva, who being [blind (?)] could not move and dwelt in one place, you gave mahaḥ, light-like sight — the verb is understood. And, O showerers (vṛṣaṇā) of desires, that deed of yours is to be proclaimed (pravācya), to be spoken of with exaltation, praised: that you gave hearing (śravaḥ) to the deaf ṛṣi, the son of Nṛṣad (nārṣada)." — "Another says": the asuras, to test the brahmin, placed the ṛṣi Kaṇva in dense darkness; being there … (the Aśvins, coming, tell him that while … playing a vīṇā they will come; hearing that sound he is to call out the dawn) [the narrative runs through several lines of small type, read only in part [?]]. Then the second explanation: "kṣoṇasya — kṣoṇaḥ is a sound-making kind of vīṇā; mahaḥ mahataḥ kṣoṇasya śravaḥ śabdam adhyadhattam — you added to the sound, in order to know the dawn." Mahaḥ (from maha pūjāyām, an unādi suffix asi; or, on the other view, from the word mahat with the Vedic dropping in the genitive); kṣoṇasya (from kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ, lyuṭ in the agent sense by bahulam; kṣoṇa-ness by pṛṣodarādi); Yāska is quoted (Ni. 5-?), and on the alternative view the word is from tukṣu śabde with an unādi suffix; nārṣadāya (grammar; tail not transcribed). [This last portion of the printed bhāṣya is in very small type; characterized, not transcribed.]

original p. 341

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.8) (Kannada, rendered)

He aśvinā — O Aśvins; yuvam — you two; śyāvāya — to the ṛṣi named Śyāva (who was dark from leprosy); ruśatīm — a woman (wife) of shining beauty; adattam — gave; kṣoṇasya — (being blind and therefore unable to move) of the one who was unable to walk [as read [?]]; kaṇvāya — to the ṛṣi named Kaṇva; mahaḥ — sight in the form of light (dṛṣṭi) — you gave; tathā — likewise; vṛṣaṇā — O Aśvins who rain desired things; nārṣadāya — to the ṛṣi, the son of Nṛṣada (who was deaf); śravaḥ — the sense of hearing; adhyadhattam yat — you graciously gave (that which is called) whatever it be; [Alternatively: vṛṣaṇā — O Aśvins, showerers of desire; nārṣadāya kaṇvāya — to Kaṇva, son of Nṛṣada; mahaḥ — of great; kṣoṇasya — of the vīṇā; śravaḥ — sound; adhyadhattam yat — you increased (for the sake of knowing the time of dawn) whatever it be;] vām — of you both; tat kṛtam — that deed; pravācyam — is praiseworthy.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.8) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, you who fulfil desired things! You two gave to the ṛṣi called Śyāva a wife of shining form; to Kaṇva, who being blind was unable to move, you gave sight; and likewise you graciously gave the sense of hearing to the son of Nṛṣada: this deed of yours is praiseworthy."

English Translation (as printed)

"You gave, Aswins, a lovely bride to Syava; you gave sight to Kanwa, unable to see his way; showerers (of benefits), the deed is to be glorified by which you gave hearing to the son of Nrishada."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 8)

Yuvaṃ śyāvāya ruśatīm adattam — kuṣṭharogeṇa śyāmavarṇāya ṛṣaye dīptatvaciṃ [?] striyaṃ prāyacchatam: "The Aśvins graciously granted to a certain ṛṣi, black-coloured from leprosy, a radiant skin and the destruction of the leprosy" — thus Sāyaṇa's exposition describes it.

Skandasvāmin, on this matter:

युवं युवां श्यावाय कुष्ठिन्यात् [?] श्याववर्णाय अग्नेः पुत्रस्य घोरस्य ज्येष्ठपुत्राय रुशतीं दीप्तां त्वचं अदत्तं दत्तवन्तौ स्थः । कं हि युवानौ …

yuvaṃ yuvāṃ śyāvāya kuṣṭhinyāt [?] śyāvavarṇāya agneḥ putrasya ghorasya jyeṣṭhaputrāya ruśatīṃ dīptāṃ tvacaṃ adattaṃ dattavantau sthaḥ | kaṃ hi yuvānau …

original p. 342

Special Topics of Ṛk 8, continued; the Skandasvāmin quotation resumes "… vikṛtya bhitvā ca jaṅghayor madhye śirasi ca punaś ca saṃdhāya hiraṇyatvacaṃ punar ujjīvayām āñcakruḥ | tadetat purastād api vakṣyati ‖" [as read]

"— so it is said," and he quotes:

हिरण्यहस्तमश्विना रराणा पुत्रं नरा वध्रिमत्या अदत्तम् । त्रिधा ह श्यावमश्विना विकस्तमुज्जीवस ऐरयतं सुदानू ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११७-२४)

hiraṇyahastamaśvinā rarāṇā putraṃ narā vadhrimatyā adattam | tridhā ha śyāvamaśvinā vikastamujjīvasa airayataṃ sudānū ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-117-24)

Kannada: "The eldest son of the son of Agni, called Ghora, was dark-skinned from leprosy and had a disfigured form; the Aśvins, seeing him, cut his body at the shank and head, took out what causes the arising of the disease, and then joined it again as it was before, and made his skin shining — this account is told, and a Ṛk expounding it is quoted."

Mahaḥ kṣoṇasya — kṣoṇāya yaḥ dṛṣṭirāhityena gantum aśaktaḥ san ekasminn eva sthāne nivasati tasmai kaṇvāya ṛṣaye tejaḥ-… cakṣurindriyam adattam: "To Kaṇva, the ṛṣi who, being without sight, was unable to go and stayed in one place only, you gave the light-like sense of sight" — so Sāyaṇa explains, seeing that the ṛṣi Kaṇva was unable to see and stayed in one spot. (This repeated clause shows that the doubtful words in the bhāṣya on p. 340 are dṛṣṭirāhityena, "through lack of sight".)

Skandasvāmin also explains it in the same way and quotes:

युवं कण्वायापिरिप्ताय चक्षुः प्रत्यधत्तं सुष्टुतिं जुजुषाणा ॥ [as read] (ऋ. सं. १-११८-७ [as read])

yuvaṃ kaṇvāyāpiriptāya cakṣuḥ pratyadhattaṃ suṣṭutiṃ jujuṣāṇā ‖ [as read] (ṛ. saṃ. 1-118-7 [as read])

— "in explaining aśvinā kaṇvāya he takes the words mahaḥ kṣoṇasya into this sentence and makes it one sentence." And:

यन्नार्षदाय नृषदः पुत्राय कण्वाय क्षोणस्य क्षोणः शब्दकारी वीणाविशेषः । महः महतः क्षोणस्य श्रवः शब्दमध्यधत्तम् उषसो विज्ञानार्थमधिकमकुरुतम् ।

yannārṣadāya nṛṣadaḥ putrāya kaṇvāya kṣoṇasya kṣoṇaḥ śabdakārī vīṇāviśeṣaḥ | mahaḥ mahataḥ kṣoṇasya śravaḥ śabdamadhyadhattam uṣaso vijñānārthamadhikamakurutam |

Kannada: "When Kaṇva, the son of Nṛṣada, had no hearing, they made the sound of a vīṇā so that he might know that the dawn had come." Here kṣoṇa is taken as a kind of sound-making vīṇā.

अपर आह — ब्राह्मणस्य परीक्षार्थमसुराः कण्वमृषिं गूढे तमसि निदधुः । अत्रैव स्थितः सन् वृष्ट्यामुषसं [?] विजानीहि यदि त्वं ब्राह्मणोऽसि । तमश्विनावागत्योचतुः । वृष्ट्यायां [?] हर्म्यस्योपरि वीणां वादयन्तावावामागमिष्यावः । तं शब्दं श्रुत्वा वृष्ट्यामुषसं [?] ब्रूहि । तदेतत् प्रतिपाद्यते ॥ [as read; small type]

apara āha — brāhmaṇasya parīkṣārthamasurāḥ kaṇvamṛṣiṃ gūḍhe tamasi nidadhuḥ | atraiva sthitaḥ san vṛṣṭyāmuṣasaṃ [?] vijānīhi yadi tvaṃ brāhmaṇo 'si | tamaśvināvāgatyocatuḥ | vṛṣṭyāyāṃ [?] harmyasyopari vīṇāṃ vādayantāvāvāmāgamiṣyāvaḥ | taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā vṛṣṭyāmuṣasaṃ [?] brūhi | tadetat pratipādyate ‖ [as read; small type]

original p. 343

Kannada, continuing: "…[the Aśvins] caused the son of Nṛṣada, who was not hearing with his ears, to hear" — (Skandasvāmin) thus giving, in his own explanation, a construction different from that of Sāyaṇa, in one sentence (anvaya); the opinion of another (apara āha) is also stated by Sāyaṇa: "The asuras, to test the brahminhood of the Brāhmaṇa, took Kaṇva, the son of Nṛṣada, to a very dark place, put him there and said: 'You, staying here, find out when the dawn comes and goes; [if you are a Brāhmaṇa you will know],' and shut him in by force. He could not hear. Then the Aśvins came to him: 'We shall come on the roof of the house where the asuras have shut you and play the vīṇā; hearing its sound, know whether the dawn has come or gone' — and they made him able to hear." Thus Skandasvāmin states his own view.

Yāska — kṣoṇasya kṣayaṇasya (Ni. 6-6 [as read]): having weighed the meaning of the word kṣoṇa as "dwelling place", he says: "mahaḥ kṣoṇasyāśvinā kaṇvāya" is also a nigama (Vedic passage).

By the sentence pravācyaṃ tad vṛṣaṇā kṛtaṃ vām it is described that all the works of the Aśvins, who protect their dependants by fulfilling their wishes, are exceedingly praiseworthy.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly)

Ruśatīm (root ruś dīptau [as read]; laṭ's sense, suffix śatṛ; since lasārvadhātuka follows after ā upadeśāt, the root accent remains; in the feminine ugitaś ca, ṅīp; accusative singular form). Mahaḥ (root maha pūjāyām; the auṇādika suffix asi; accent of the final by the suffix; on the other view the word mahat, genitive singular, with Vedic loss of at; bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam, acute on the case-ending; or the root maha with kvip ca, Pā. 3-2-76, suffix kvip, giving mah; genitive singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādir viḥ, Pā. 6-1-168, acute on the case-ending). Kṣoṇasya (root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ; kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam, Pā. 3-2-113, lyuṭ in the agent sense; yuvor anākau, Pā. 7-1-1, ana substituted; pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam, the form kṣoṇa). On this matter … the page ends here; continues p. 344

original p. 344

Grammar page of Ṛk 8, concluded (noted briefly): On this matter Yāska speaks: kṣoṇasya kṣayaṇasya (Ni. 6-6 [as read]); when this second meaning is accepted, [the word comes] from tukṣu śabde; the auṇādika suffix na; on account of that, guṇa for the root's i-vowel [?]; ṇatva of the n; by the suffix's accent, the final acute.

Pravācyam — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; hetumati ca, Pā. 3-1-26, ṇic; after the ṇijanta acoyat, Pā. 3-1-92 (as the numeral list reads it; p. 335 reads 99 [?]), suffix yat; ṇic being the cause, ata upadhāyāḥ, Pā. 7-2-116, vṛddhi of the root's penultimate; ṇer aniṭi, Pā. 6-4-51, elision of ṇic; yatonāvaḥ, Pā. 6-1-213 (the numeral list reads 153 here and "6-1-2-3" on p. 335 [?]), …; as a gati-compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, Pā. 6-2-139, the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its own accent.

Nārṣadāya — nṛṣadaḥ apatyaṃ pumān; yaskādibhyo gotre [printed ṛṣyandhakavṛṣṇikurubhyaś ca, Pā. 4-1-114 as read], suffix aṇ; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ, Pā. 7-2-127 (as the numeral list reads it [?]), vṛddhi of the first vowel; ṛto 'raparaḥ [as read: uraṇ raparaḥ], it becomes r-final; by the suffix's accent the final acute; dative singular form.

Adhattam — root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; laṅ, second person dual; since there is a yuṣmad-connection [as read], nipātair yad yadi…, Pā. 8-1-30 [as read], prohibition of nighāta; the augment aṭ being udātta, the initial acute; tiṅ cododāttavati, Pā. 8-1-61 (as the numeral list reads it [?]), the gati (adhi) gets nighāta accent. ‖ 8 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.9)

पुरू वर्पांस्यश्विना दधाना नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वम् । सहस्रसां वाजिनमप्रतीतमहिहनं श्रवस्यं तरुत्रम् ॥ ९ ॥

purū varpāṃsyaśvinā dadhānā ni pedava ūhathurāśumaśvam | sahasrasāṃ vājinamapratītamahihanaṃ śravasyaṃ tarutram ‖ 9 ‖

original p. 345

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.9)

पुरु । वर्पांसि । अश्विना । दधाना । नि । पेदवे । ऊहथुः । आशुम् । अश्वम् । सहस्रऽसाम् । वाजिनम् । अप्रतिऽइतम् । अहिऽहनम् । श्रवस्यम् । तरुत्रम् ॥ ९ ॥

puru | varpāṃsi | aśvinā | dadhānā | ni | pedave | ūhathuḥ | āśum | aśvam | sahasra 'sām | vājinam | aprati 'itam | ahi 'hanam | śravasyam | tarutram ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.9) small type; read with some doubt

हे अश्विना पुरु पुरूणि बहूनि वर्पांसि । रूपनामैतत् । अस्मिन्ये [?] कर्मभिः कृतानि रूपाणि दधाना धारयन्तौ युवामाशुं शीघ्रगामिनमश्वं पेदवे पेदुनाम्ने स्तुवते राज्ञे न्यूहथुः । नितरां प्रापितवन्तौ । दत्तवन्तावित्यर्थः । कीदृशमश्वम् । सहस्रसां सहस्रसंख्याकस्य धनस्य सनितारं दातारम् । वाजिनं बलवन्तम् । अपि च अप्रतीतं शत्रुभिरप्रतिगतम् । अहिहनम् अहीनामागत्य हन्तॄणां शत्रूणां शत्रुहन्तारम् । श्रवस्यं श्रवः श्रवणीयं स्तोत्रं तत्र भवं स्तुतिविषयमित्यर्थः । तरुत्रं तरितारम् ॥

he aśvinā puru purūṇi bahūni varpāṃsi | rūpanāmaitat | asminye [?] karmabhiḥ kṛtāni rūpāṇi dadhānā dhārayantau yuvāmāśuṃ śīghragāminamaśvaṃ pedave pedunāmne stuvate rājñe nyūhathuḥ | nitarāṃ prāpitavantau | dattavantāvityarthaḥ | kīdṛśamaśvam | sahasrasāṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākasya dhanasya sanitāraṃ dātāram | vājinaṃ balavantam | api ca apratītaṃ śatrubhirapratigatam | ahihanam ahīnāmāgatya hantṝṇāṃ śatrūṇāṃ śatruhantāram | śravasyaṃ śravaḥ śravaṇīyaṃ stotraṃ tatra bhavaṃ stutiviṣayamityarthaḥ | tarutraṃ taritāram ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, puru — many (purūṇi) varpāṃsi (varpas is a name for form): taking on forms made by [your] deeds, you two, pedave — for the king named Pedu who praised [you] — ny ūhathuḥ brought near, gave, a swift (āśum) horse. What kind of horse? One that gives (sanitāram) wealth of a thousand sorts (sahasrasām); strong (vājinam); and unapproached by enemies (apratītam); the slayer (ahihanam) of enemies who come to kill (like serpents, ahi); śravasyam — worthy of fame (śravas), subject of the hymn; tarutram — one who carries across." The bhāṣya goes on with grammar of varpāṃsi, dadhānā, sahasrasām, śravasyam, tarutram (from tṝ plavanatarayoḥ, with uṇādi suffix) etc. — characterized, not transcribed (small type).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.9) (Kannada, rendered; page continues)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; puru varpāṃsi — many forms; dadhānā — taking on [them]; āśum — swift-going; sahasrasām — one that gives (wealth) of a thousand [count]; vājinam — strong; apratītam — not to be faced (by enemies); ahihanam — destroyer of enemies; śravasyam — worthy to be praised (by hearing); tarutram — (carrying across [?]) … continues on p. 346

original p. 346

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 9, continued tarutram — (one who carries across; the one that bears [one] over dangers [?]); aśvam — the horse; pedave — to Pedu (your worshipper); ni ūhathuḥ — you obtained for [him] (you graciously gave).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.9) (Kannada, rendered)

"O all you Aśvins who take on many forms! You graciously gave to Pedu one excellent horse — swift-going, giver of (wealth) of a thousand [count], strong, not to be withstood by enemies, worthy of praise, one that carries (across dangers)."

English Translation (as printed)

"Aswins, who assume many forms, you gave to Pedu a swift horse, the bringer of a thousand (treasures), powerful, irresistible, the destroyer of foes, the object of praise, the bearer (over dangers)"

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 9)

Pedave ūhathur āśum aśvam — pedunāmne stuvate śīghragāminam aśvaṃ nitarāṃ prāpitavantau dattavantāv ity arthaḥ: "The king famed as Pedu praised the Aśvins with much devotion; pleased with his praise, they gave him one very excellent and very swift horse" — this history is told here.

Varpāṃsi — aśvibhiḥ [as read [?]] karmabhiḥ kṛtāni rūpāṇi: "The word varpas is listed among the sixteen [?] names of form (Ni. 3-13 [as read]); hence the meaning is 'form'. The Aśvins took on various forms, in order to protect their dependants and others and to fulfil their wishes; therefore their greatness is inexpressible (anirvacanīya)" — such is the sense.

Sahasrasām — sahasrasaṃkhyākasya dhanasya sanitāraṃ dātāram: "The horse which the Aśvins gave to King Pedu gives wealth of a thousand-fold [count]" — such is the sense.

Apratītam — śatrubhir apratigatam: "By this word the power of the horse is described — that it cannot be withstood by enemies." And ahihanam — ahīnām āgatya hantṝṇāṃ śatrūṇāṃ śatrūṇāṃ vā hantāram: "Even though enemies fall upon it to kill it, this horse kills them; thus it describes the wonderful power of the horse."

original p. 347

Śravasyam — śravaḥ śravaṇīyaṃ stotram | tatra bhavam: "śravas is an object of hearing, a hymn; what exists there." The word śravas occurs among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-9 [as read; ?]); in the sense of "praise" in śrava icchamānaḥ (Ni. 9-11 [as read]); and as a name for food in śrava ity annanāma (Ni. 10-3). Hence it has many meanings.

Skandasvāmin: "pedur nāma rājā tasmai parayā bhaktyā parituṣṭāv aśvinau mahāvīryaṃ śvetam aśvaṃ dadatuḥ iti tat-prastāve [?] …" [as read; small type]: "King Pedu, the Aśvins, pleased by his supreme devotion, gave a most mighty white horse" — he states the sense, and quotes:

युवं श्वेतं पेदवे इन्द्रजूतमहिहनमश्विनादत्तमश्वम् । जोहूत्रमर्यो अभिभूतिमुग्रं सहस्रसां वृषणं वीड्वङ्गम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११८-९)

yuvaṃ śvetaṃ pedave indrajūtamahihanamaśvinādattamaśvam | johūtramaryo abhibhūtimugraṃ sahasrasāṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ vīḍvaṅgam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-118-9)

and "this [teacher] quotes another Ṛk of the same meaning also":

युवं श्वेतं पेदवेऽश्विनाश्वं नवभिर्वाजैर्नवती च वाजिनम् । चर्कृत्यं ददथुर्द्रावयत्क्षपं [? ] भगं न नृभ्यो हव्यं मयोभुवम् ॥ [as read; doubtful words [?]] (ऋ. सं. १०-३९-१०)

yuvaṃ śvetaṃ pedave 'śvināśvaṃ navabhirvājairnavatī ca vājinam | carkṛtyaṃ dadathurdrāvayatkṣapaṃ [? ] bhagaṃ na nṛbhyo havyaṃ mayobhuvam ‖ [as read; doubtful words [?]] (ṛ. saṃ. 10-39-10)

And for the word ahihanam, he explains [from the strength-pride of the horse, which kills enemies even when they are not …, or kills the asura named Ahi] — "ahi is the name of a rākṣasa; one who has also killed him" [the Kannada exposition is partly in small type, read with doubt [?]]; and for śravaḥ he gives the meaning "famous" (kīrtimantam), and quotes:

इन्द्रो अश्रायि सुध्यो निरेके पज्रेषु स्तोमो दुर्यो न यूपः । अश्वयुर्गव्यू रथयुर्वसूयुरिन्द्र इद्रायः क्षयति प्रयन्ता ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५१-१४)

indro aśrāyi sudhyo nireke pajreṣu stomo duryo na yūpaḥ | aśvayurgavyū rathayurvasūyurindra idrāyaḥ kṣayati prayantā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-51-14)

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar page, noted briefly)

Puru — śer chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-60 (as the numeral list reads it here; p. 352 reads 70 [?])), elision of śi. Varpāṃsi — root vṛñ varaṇe; vṛñśīṅbhyāṃ rūpe sāṅgayoḥ [as read; Uṇ. sū. 4-640 as printed [?]], the suffix asun, together with it the augment puk for the root; guṇa of the root's i-vowel [?] by the suffix's being the cause; becomes r-final; the word varpas; … the page ends mid-sentence; continues p. 348

original p. 348

Grammar page of Ṛk 9, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers only where legible): varpāṃsi — since the suffix is nit, the initial acute; accusative plural form. Dadhānā — root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; in the sense of laṭ, suffix śānac; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ, ślu as the vikaraṇa; doubling of the root; shortening and jaś substitution in the reduplicative syllable; abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189 [as read]), initial acute. Ūhathuḥ — root vaha prāpaṇe; liṭ, second person dual, athus; vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti, saṃprasāraṇa; doubling etc.; nighāta accent after an ajanta word. Sahasrasām — root ṣaṇu dāne; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. 6-1-64), s for ṣ; janasanakhanāṃ sañjhalopo … [Pā. 3-2-67 as read [?]], suffix viṭ; vidyoranunāsikasyātvam [as read], ā for the root-vowel; with viṭ following, sarvalopa; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Apratītam — root iṇ gatau; niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 (the list reads 103 on p. 348 and 102 on p. 363 for the same sūtra [?])), suffix kta; na pratītaḥ, apratītaḥ; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 [as read]), the former part (an indeclinable) keeps its natural accent. Śravasyam — root śru śravaṇe; suffix asun; the form śravas; śravasi bhavam, śravasyam; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110), suffix yat; since the suffix is tit, tit svaritam (Pā. 6-1-185 [as read]), svarita accent. Tarutram — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; aśitrādibhya itrotrau [as read] (Uṇ. sū. 4-?), suffix itra [?]; for the sake of that, guṇa of the root's vowel; becomes r-final; vṛtyayo bahulam [as read [?]], initial acute. Or: in the grasitaskabhita… (Pā. 7-2-34 [as read]) rule it is made irregular; since tarutṛ ends in tṛ, the case ending am — by the maxim saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ and ṛto ṅi sarvanāmasthānayoḥ the guṇa … [partly small type]; since the suffix is nit, jñityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197 as read), the initial acute. ‖ 9 ‖

original p. 349

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.10)

एतानि वां श्रवस्या सुदानू ब्रह्माङ्गूषं सदनं रोदस्योः । यद्वां पज्रासो अश्विना हवन्ते यातमिषा च विदुषे च वाजम् ॥ १० ॥

etāni vāṃ śravasyā sudānū brahmāṅgūṣaṃ sadanaṃ rodasyoḥ | yadvāṃ pajrāso aśvinā havante yātamiṣā ca viduṣe ca vājam ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.10)

एतानि । वाम् । श्रवस्या । सुदानू इति सुऽदानू । ब्रह्म । आङ्गूषम् । सदनम् । रोदस्योः । यत् । वाम् । पज्रासः । अश्विना । हवन्ते । यातम् । इषा । च । विदुषे । च । वाजम् ॥ १० ॥

etāni | vām | śravasyā | sudānū iti su 'dānū | brahma | āṅgūṣam | sadanam | rodasyoḥ | yat | vām | pajrāsaḥ | aśvinā | havante | yātam | iṣā | ca | viduṣe | ca | vājam ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.10) begun; continues p. 350

हे सुदानू शोभनदानावश्विना वां युवयोः संबन्धीन्येतानि समन्तरोक्तानि वीर्याणि श्रवस्या श्रवणीयानि सर्वैर्ज्ञातव्यानि भवन्ति । तदर्थं रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्यात्मना वर्तमानयोर्युवयोः । उक्तं च यास्केन । कक्ष्यावश्विना द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके । (नि. १२-१ [as read]) इति । तथा च तैत्तिरीयकम् । इमे अश्विना संवत्सरोऽग्निर्वैश्वानर इति । तयोर्युवयोः सदनं स्तोत्रसमीपे निवेशनं प्रसादनहेतुभूतं वाङ्गूषमाघोषणीयं ब्रह्म मन्त्ररूपं स्तोत्रं निष्पन्नमिति शेषः । यद्वदा पज्रासोऽङ्गिरसां गोत्रोत्पन्ना यजमाना हे अश्विनौ वां युवां हवन्ते स्तुतिभिरात्मरक्षणार्थमाह्वयन्ति तदानीमिषा …

he sudānū śobhanadānāvaśvinā vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhīnyetāni samantaroktāni vīryāṇi śravasyā śravaṇīyāni sarvairjñātavyāni bhavanti | tadarthaṃ rodasyordyāvāpṛthivyātmanā vartamānayoryuvayoḥ | uktaṃ ca yāskena | kakṣyāvaśvinā dyāvāpṛthivyāvityeke | (ni. 12-1 [as read]) iti | tathā ca kaittirīyakam [sic ?] | ime aśvinā saṃvatsaro 'gnirvaiśvānara iti | tayoryuvayoḥ sadanaṃ stotrasamīpe niveśanaṃ prasādanahetubhūtaṃ vāṅgūṣamāghoṣaṇīyaṃ brahma mantrarūpaṃ stotraṃ niṣpannamiti śeṣaḥ | yadvadā pajrāso 'ṅgirasāṃ gotrotpannā yajamānā he aśvinau vāṃ yuvāṃ havante stutibhirātmarakṣaṇārthamāhvayanti tadānīmiṣā …

Sense (mine): "O Sudānū — good givers, Aśvins! These (etāni) valorous deeds of yours (vām), just now spoken, are śravasyā — worthy of being heard, to be known by all. For that purpose [there is] of you two, who exist as heaven and earth (rodasyoḥ) — and Yāska has said: 'Some say that the Aśvins are heaven and earth' (Ni. 12-1) — and so too the Taittirīya (taittirīyakam, as the OCR list reads it): 'These two Aśvins are the year, Agni Vaiśvānara' — for these two, your seat (sadanam): the abode near the hymn, the cause of pleasing, āṅgūṣam — to be proclaimed aloud — the brahma, the hymn in the form of mantra, has been produced (the verb is understood). And when the Pajras, sacrificers born in the family of the Aṅgirases, call you, Aśvins, with praises for their own protection, then — [by] food (iṣā) …" breaks off; continues p. 350

original p. 350

Bhāṣya of Ṛk 10, continued "… iṣā yātam āgacchatam ca | viduṣe yuṣmadviṣayaṃ stotraṃ jānate mahyaṃ ca vājam annaṃ balaṃ vā prayacchatam iti śeṣaḥ ‖" ("Come with food; and give strength or food to me, who know the hymn concerning you" — the verb is understood). Then the bhāṣya's grammar tail: yātam — the prohibition of nighāta by the rule on ca and vā used in connection [?]; viduṣe — root vida jñāne; vider śatur vasuḥ, vasu; vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam; śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca, ṣatva — characterized, not transcribed.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.10) (Kannada, rendered)

Sudānū — O Aśvins who give desired things; vām — your; etāni — these (spoken of) deeds; śravasyā — worthy of praise (worth hearing); rodasyoḥ — (of the two who exist in earth and sky); sadanam — (the means of) accomplishing propitiation; āṅgūṣam — to be proclaimed aloud; brahma — the hymn in the form of mantra (has been prepared); yat — when; aśvinā — O Aśvins; pajrāsaḥ — sacrificers born in the family of Pajra (of the Aṅgirases); vām — you both; havante — call (for their own protection, with praises); iṣā — along with food; yātam — come; ca — and; viduṣe ca — also to me who know (your related praise); vājam — strength, (food) — give.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.10) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins who give generously! These deeds of yours, told up to now, are praiseworthy; the mantra which is to be proclaimed aloud, the means of propitiating you who dwell in earth and sky, (is a delight for you); when sacrificers born in the family of the Pajras (the Aṅgirases) call you with praises, come with food; and give strength or food to me, who know your praises."

English Translation (as printed)

"Liberal givers, these your exploits are to be celebrated, and the resounding prayer propitiates you will [sic] abiding in heaven and earth; when the descendants of Pajra invite you, Aswins, come with food, and grant strength to the sage (who worships you),"

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 10)

Sudānū — śobhanadānau aśvinau: "The Aśvins are always of a nature that does good [to others]. The Nirukta author too explains sudānavaḥ as kalyāṇadānāḥ (Ni. 6-24 [as read]) — 'those who give auspicious things'."

original p. 351

Śravasyā — śravaṇīyāni sarvair jñātavyāni bhavanti: "The meaning is: the works worthy of the Aśvins' praise, and the hymns also, are such as to be heard and known by all."

Rodasyoḥ — dyāvāpṛthivyātmanā vartamānayoḥ: "The word rodasī is read among the four names of heaven-and-earth (Ni. 3-22); hence the meaning is 'the two, heaven and earth'. The Nirukta author, weighing the meaning of the word aśvinau, begins with tat ka āśvinau (Ni. 12-1) and, saying 'dyāvāpṛthivyāv ity eke', explains that the Aśvins are [in the form of] heaven and earth (earth and mid-air); and in saying 'ahorātrāv ity eke', 'sūryācandramasāv ity eke' (Ni. 12-1) he describes the nature of the Aśvins: [they are in the form of] earth and mid-air, of day and night, of the sun and moon — thus he sets up their all-pervasiveness. And the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, ime aśvinā saṃvatsaro 'gnir vaiśvānaraḥ (Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-4-1), says that the Aśvins also have the form of Agni Vaiśvānara."

Pajrāsaḥ — aṅgirasāṃ gotrotpannāḥ: "Both Skandasvāmin and Sāyaṇa give the word pajra the meaning 'the descendants of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis'":

तद्वां नरा शंस्यं पज्रियेण कक्षीवता नासत्या परिज्मन् । शफादश्वस्य वाजिनो जनाय शतं कुम्भाँ असिञ्चतं मधूनाम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११७-६)

tadvāṃ narā śaṃsyaṃ pajriyeṇa kakṣīvatā nāsatyā parijman | śaphādaśvasya vājino janāya śataṃ kumbhā~ asiñcataṃ madhūnām ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-117-6)

— "In this Ṛk, for pajriyeṇa, the explanation aṅgirasāṃ kule jātena is given; so here pajrāsaḥ means the line of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis, that is: sacrificers born in the line of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis who perform sacrifices."

Sadanam — stotrasamīpe niveśanaṃ prasādanahetubhūtaṃ vā: "The word sadana occurs among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 2-24); on account of its use it is used elsewhere with the meaning 'water'."

कृष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत्पतन्ति । त आववृत्रन्त्सदनादृतस्यादिद्घृतेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-४७ [as read])

kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divamutpatanti | ta āvavṛtrantsadanādṛtasyādidghṛtena pṛthivī vyudyate ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-47 [as read])

"Here the word sadana is used in the sense of 'place of residence'. In the same way in this Ṛk Sāyaṇa gives the word sadana the meaning 'the dwelling in the vicinity of those who praise'."

original p. 352

Āṅgūṣam — āghoṣaṇīyam: "Praise (stuti) that proclaims quality or fame; this is called by the word śastra in the sacrifice. The Nirukta author, explaining the word āṅgūṣa as 'a hymn recited loudly and clearly' — āṅgūṣaḥ stomaḥ āghoṣaḥ (Ni. 5-12) — quotes:

एनाङ्गूषेण वयमिन्द्रवन्तोऽभि ष्याम वृजने सर्ववीराः । तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१०६-१? [as read; last digits doubtful [?]])

enāṅgūṣeṇa vayamindravanto 'bhi ṣyāma vṛjane sarvavīrāḥ | tanno mitro varuṇo māmahantāmaditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-106-1? [as read; last digits doubtful [?]])

Brahma — mantrarūpaṃ stotram: "The word brahma is read among the twenty-eight names of wealth (Ni. 3-9 as the numeral list reads it); so it is used in the sense of 'wealth', but here it is said in the sense of 'hymn'."

"In this Ṛk it is said that the Aśvins are of a nature to show favour and to bring auspiciousness (kalyāṇa) towards those of the Aṅgirasa family who praise them, and towards sacrificers; that because of the all-pervading nature that they have as the forms earth, mid-air, day and night, the moon and the sun, and because of their greatness, their power is spread everywhere, so that everyone ought to know their power, fame and the like and praise them; and also that the Aśvins should favour with food, strength and wealth those who know of the Aśvins and praise them, or who sacrifice to them and delight them with oblations."

Vājam — balam annaṃ vā: "The word vāja is stated both among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9 — both read thus in the numeral list, the second with its prefix lost), so it has many meanings; here it is used in the sense of strength or food."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Śravasyā — śravasi bhavāni śravasyāni; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110), suffix yat; tit svaritam (Pā. 6-1-185), the svarita accent; in the neuter śi substituted, giving the form; śer chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70), elision of śi. Sadanam — root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; in the sense of location, suffix lyuṭ; yuvoranākau, ana substituted; liti (Pā. 6-1-193), acute on the syllable before the suffix.

original p. 353

Pajrāsaḥ — pajra + jas; āj jaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50), asuk as the augment for jas; the final s becomes ru, visarga. Havante — root hvel spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, third person plural, jha replaced by anta; śap vikaraṇa; bahulaṃ chandasi, saṃprasāraṇa of the root; saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ, guṇa; av substituted; ato guṇe, pararūpa; because the preceding yat is there, nipātair yad yadi… (Pā. 8-1-30) prohibits nighāta; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by the upadeśa after the verbal ending, tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186), the root's accent remains. Yātam — root yā prāpaṇe, adādi; loṭ second person dual; by cavāyoge prathamā the nighāta is prohibited; by the suffix's accent, the final acute. Iṣā — instrumental singular form; sāvekācas tṛtīyādir viḥ (Pā. 6-1-168), acute on the case ending. Viduṣe — root vida jñāne; in the sense of laṭ, suffix śatṛ; vider śatur vasuḥ (Pā. 7-1-36), vasu substituted; the word vidvas; dative singular, with a following case ending, vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam (Pā. 6-4-131), saṃprasāraṇa of the v; saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa; śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (Pā. 8-3-60), ṣatva of the s; by the suffix's accent the vowel u is acute. ‖ 10 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.11)

सूनोर्मानेनाश्विना गृणाना वाजं विप्राय भुरणा रदन्ता । अगस्त्ये ब्रह्मणा वावृधाना सं विश्पलां नासत्यारिणीतम् ॥ ११ ॥

sūnormānenāśvinā gṛṇānā vājaṃ viprāya bhuraṇā radantā | agastye brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānā saṃ viśpalāṃ nāsatyāriṇītam ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 354

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.11)

सूनोः । मानेन । अश्विना । गृणाना । वाजम् । विप्राय । भुरणा । रदन्ता । अगस्त्ये । ब्रह्मणा । वावृधाना । सम् । विश्पलाम् । नासत्या । अरिणीतम् ॥ ११ ॥

sūnoḥ | mānena | aśvinā | gṛṇānā | vājam | viprāya | bhuraṇā | radantā | agastye | brahmaṇā | vāvṛdhānā | sam | viśpalām | nāsatyā | ariṇītam ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.11)

भुरणा भर्तारौ पोषकौ नासत्या सत्यस्वभावौ हे अश्विनौ सूनोः कुम्भात्प्रसूतस्यागस्त्यस्य खेलपुरोहितस्य [?] संबन्धिना मानेन स्तुत्यस्य परिच्छेदकेन स्तोत्रेण गृणाना स्तूयमानौ विप्राय मेधाविने भरद्वाजायर्षये वाजमन्नं रदन्ता विलिखन्तौ निष्पादयन्तौ युवां विश्पलां संग्रामे छिन्नजङ्घां खेलस्य संबन्धिनीं स्त्रियं समरिणीतम् । पुनरायस्या जङ्घया समयोजयतम् । तृतीयेन पादेन प्रथमपादोक्तोऽर्थो विप्रियते [?] । अगस्त्य ऋषौ ब्रह्मणा मन्त्ररूपेण स्तोत्रेण वावृधाना प्रवर्धिताविति ॥

bhuraṇā bhartārau poṣakau nāsatyā satyasvabhāvau he aśvinau sūnoḥ kumbhātprasūtasyāgastyasya khelapurohitasya [?] saṃbandhinā mānena stutyasya paricchedakena stotreṇa gṛṇānā stūyamānau viprāya medhāvine bharadvājāyarṣaye vājamannaṃ radantā vilikhantau niṣpādayantau yuvāṃ viśpalāṃ saṃgrāme chinnajaṅghāṃ khelasya saṃbandhinīṃ striyaṃ samariṇītam | punarāyasyā jaṅghayā samayojayatam | tṛtīyena pādena prathamapādokto 'rtho vipriyate [?] | agastya ṛṣau brahmaṇā mantrarūpeṇa stotreṇa vāvṛdhānā pravardhitāviti ‖

Sense (mine): "Bhuraṇā — nourishers, supporters; nāsatyā — of true nature; O Aśvins — being praised (gṛṇānā) by the māna, the measuring [hymn], praise-defining, belonging to Agastya, sūnoḥ — born of a jar (kumbha), the chaplain of Khela [as read [?]]; giving (radantā, i.e. 'producing', 'accomplishing') food (vāja) to the sage (viprāya), the wise ṛṣi Bharadvāja — you two samariṇītam: restored Viśpalā, the wife of Khela, whose shank was cut off in battle; you joined her again with an iron [āyasyā] shank. The sense stated in the first pāda is [re]explained by the third pāda. Vāvṛdhānā — made to grow by the ṛṣi Agastya with a hymn in the form of mantra." The bhāṣya then adds grammar of gṛṇānā (root gṝ śabde, with the Vedic vyatyaya, kartari suffix), bhuraṇā (root bhura dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ), kaṇḍvādi, ac, supāṃ sulug, vāvṛdhānā, tujādi etc. — characterized, not transcribed.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.11) (Kannada, rendered)

Bhuraṇā — nourishers; aśvinā — O Aśvins; sūnoḥ — from the jar (of Agastya, who was born, and the chaplain named Khela); mānena — by praise; gṛṇānā — being praised; viprāya — to the wise man (the ṛṣi Bharadvāja); vājam — food; radantā — you who gave; agastye — of Agastya; brahmaṇā — by the hymn in the form of mantra; vavṛdhānā — made to grow; viśpalām — Viśpalā, the wife of Khela, who had lost a leg in battle; sam ariṇītam — you made her whole with an iron leg.

original p. 355

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.11) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Nāsatyas, nourishers of men! Pleased by the praise of Agastya, born of a jar, you graciously gave food (the giver of strength) to the wise ṛṣi Bharadvāja; and, strengthened by Agastya's praise in the form of mantra, you gave Viśpalā, [wife of] Khela, who had lost a leg, an iron leg."

English Translation (as printed)

"Aswins, glorified by the praises of the son (of the jar), and giving food, nourishers (of men), to the sage (Bharadwaja), exalted by Agastya with prayer, you restored Nasatyas, Vispala."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 11)

Sūnoḥ — kumbhāt prasūtasya agastyasya khelapurohitasya: "A king called Khela had made the ṛṣi Agastya his chaplain. When he went to the battle and fought the enemy's host, his wife Viśpalā broke her leg [Kannada: "lost the foot"]. The ṛṣi Agastya prayed to the Aśvins; as the ṛṣi prayed, the Aśvins came and, giving appropriate treatment to the shank region of that woman's leg, protected her — this account is told by this Ṛk. Because the ṛṣi Agastya was born from a jar (kumbha), the word sūnu is used here, and so this matter is stated."

Skandasvāmin:

सूनुरित्यपत्यनाम । मीयते अनेनेति मानः कुम्भः । षष्ठीतृतीययोश्च व्यत्ययेन योजयितव्ये [?] । सूनुनास्यापत्यभूतेन कुम्भस्य अगस्त्यो हि उर्वशीदर्शनात् मित्रावरुणयोः स्कन्नात्रेतसः कुम्भे जातः । एवं चाख्यानविद आहुः — [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

sūnurityapatyanāma | mīyate aneneti mānaḥ kumbhaḥ | ṣaṣṭhītṛtīyayośca vyatyayena yojayitavye [?] | sūnunāsyāpatyabhūtena kumbhasya agastyo hi urvaśīdarśanāt mitrāvaruṇayoḥ skannātretasaḥ kumbhe jātaḥ | evaṃ cākhyānavida āhuḥ — [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

बहुधा पतितं रेतः कलशेऽथ जले स्थले । स्थले वसिष्ठस्तु मुनिः संभूतो ऋषिसत्तमः । कुम्भे त्वगस्त्यः स्कन्धभूतो [?] जले मत्स्यो महाद्युतिः ॥ इति । वसिष्ठोऽपि तत्पुत्रो वा वक्ष्यति ॥ [as read [?]]

bahudhā patitaṃ retaḥ kalaśe 'tha jale sthale | sthale vasiṣṭhastu muniḥ saṃbhūto ṛṣisattamaḥ | kumbhe tvagastyaḥ skandhabhūto [?] jale matsyo mahādyutiḥ ‖ iti | vasiṣṭho 'pi tatputro vā vakṣyati ‖ [as read [?]]

("Semen fallen in many ways — in the jar, in water and on land: on land arose the sage Vasiṣṭha, best of ṛṣis; in the jar, Agastya; in the water, the great-splendoured fish [?]" — thus the knowers of the legend say; "Vasiṣṭha too, or his son, will say it" — as read.)

सत्रे ह जातावि षिता नमोभिः कुम्भे रेतः सिषिचतुः समानम् । ततो ह मान उदियाय मध्यात्ततो जातमृषिमाहुर्वसिष्ठम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ७-३३-१३ [as read])

satre ha jātāvi ṣitā namobhiḥ kumbhe retaḥ siṣicatuḥ samānam | tato ha māna udiyāya madhyāttato jātamṛṣimāhurvasiṣṭham ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 7-33-13 [as read])

original p. 356

Special Topics of Ṛk 11, continued "… the word sūnu is read among the names of offspring (Ni. 3-2 [numeral list]); hence the meaning is 'son'. The word māna conveys the meaning 'jar (kumbha)'. If the case-ending in sūnoḥ mānena is taken in reverse (vyatyāsa), the meaning is mānasya sūnunā — 'by the son of the jar'. Since it is said here that the ṛṣi Agastya praised the Aśvins, the order of Agastya's origin is briefly told here: from the sight of the apsaras Urvaśī, the semen of Mitra and Varuṇa fell on the earth and in the water; from what fell on the earth, Agastya, and from what fell in the water, the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha, were born. This matter is told by the mantra quoted above beginning satre ha jātau." Having described it so, "evaṃ kumbhasyāpatyabhūto agastyaḥ khelasya ca purohitaḥ" — "thus Agastya, the son of the jar, is the chaplain of Khela": Skandasvāmin gives the meaning here just as Sāyaṇa says that Agastya, the son of the jar, was chaplain of King Khela.

"Sāyaṇa: mānena stutyasya paricchedakena stotreṇa gṛṇānā stūyamānau — [the Aśvins], praised by the hymn which marks the extent (iyattā) of the thing that is the object of praise; he gives the word māna the meaning 'praise', and explains that the Aśvins, pleased by the praise of the ṛṣi Bharadvāja, gave him food and wealth."

Brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānau ātmārthaṃ vardhamānau — "greatly delighted by praise in the form of mantra", so [Sāyaṇa] explains; and Skandasvāmin quotes:

चरित्रं हि वेरिवाच्छेदि पर्णमाजा खेलस्य परितक्म्यायाम् । सद्यो जङ्घामायसीं विश्पलायै धने हिते सर्तवे प्रत्यधत्तम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१५ [as read; not in the numeral list])

caritraṃ hi verivācchedi parṇamājā khelasya paritakmyāyām | sadyo jaṅghāmāyasīṃ viśpalāyai dhane hite sartave pratyadhattam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-15 [as read; not in the numeral list])

"Here it is said that for the woman Viśpalā they joined a leg made of iron."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Mānena — root māṅ māne, in the sense of the abstract noun, suffix lyuṭ; yuvoranākau, ana substituted; liti [as read], the acute on the syllable before the suffix. Gṛṇānā — root gṝ śabde, kryādi; kartari vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85), the agent-suffix in the sense of laṭ (śānac); kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. 3-1-81), śnā as vikaraṇa; snādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ (Pā. 7-3-80 [as read in the numeral list; the first word printed plādīnām? [?]]), shortening of the root; ṇatva of the n after the ṛ-sound; dual of gṛṇāna when au follows, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā substituted.

original p. 357

Grammar of Ṛk 11, continued sulug — by that, ā substituted for it; ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-193 [numeral list]), final acute. Bhuraṇā — root bhura dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; because it belongs to the pacādi group (nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ, Pā. 3-1-134), suffix ac; kaṇḍvādibhyo yak (Pā. 3-1-27), yak in the root's own sense; with aṭ following, yasya halaḥ (Pā. 6-4-49) elides the y, and ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48) the remaining a; supāṃ sulug, ā for the case ending; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19), nighāta accent; with regard to the word viprāya [the nighāta does not arise], since radantā is related to it and bhuraṇā is not related to it, there is no capacity for it, so parāṅgavadbhāva does not arise, and the whole group gets no nighāta. Radantā — root rada vilekhane; in the sense of laṭ, suffix śatṛ, śap vikaraṇa; the word radat; dual, with au following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 [numeral list]), ā substituted; num (as an ugit) — [and since] the lasārvadhātuka follows upadeśa, it is anudātta, so the root accent remains. Vavṛdhānā — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; when liṭ has come, liṭaḥ kānaj vā (Pā. 3-2-106), suffix kānac; guṇa of the root on that account; ur at (Pā. 7-4-66), a for the reduplicative syllable; becoming r-final, ādihalśeṣa; since the suffix is kit, guṇa of the root's light penultimate does not occur; in the Saṃhitā the reduplicative syllable is lengthened by the Vedic usage; tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya, [for the lengthening], and in the Pada-text too the long [vowel] is to be heard. Ariṇītam — root rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ, kryādi; laṅ, second person dual; tas-thas-…, tam substituted; kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. 3-1-81), śnā as vikaraṇa; snādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ (Pā. 7-3-80), shortening of the root; the suffix being ṅit, because there is aṅga in the hal-initial, ī halyaghoḥ (Pā. 6-4-113), ī for the vikaraṇa's ā; āṭ kuppvāṅ [as read [?]] — by this rule, ṇatva of the n; because of its standing after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 358

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.12)

कुह यान्ता सुष्टुतिं काव्यस्य दिवो नपाता वृषणा शयुत्रा । हिरण्यस्येव कलशं निखातमुदूपथुर्दशमे अश्विनाहन् ॥ १२ ॥

kuha yāntā suṣṭutiṃ kāvyasya divo napātā vṛṣaṇā śayutrā | hiraṇyasyeva kalaśaṃ nikhātamudūpathurdaśame aśvināhan ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.12)

कुह । यान्ता । सुऽस्तुतिम् । काव्यस्य । दिवः । नपाता । वृषणा । शयुऽत्रा । हिरण्यस्यऽइव । कलशम् । निऽखातम् । उत् । ऊपथुः । दशमे । अश्विना । अहन् ॥ १२ ॥

kuha | yāntā | su 'stutim | kāvyasya | divaḥ | napātā | vṛṣaṇā | śayu 'trā | hiraṇyasya 'iva | kalaśam | ni 'khātam | ut | ūpathuḥ | daśame | aśvinā | ahan ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.12) small type; read with several doubts

पुरा खलु उशनसः स्तुतिं गच्छन्तावश्विनौ मार्गमध्ये कूपे पतितं रेभं दृष्ट्वा तं कूपादुदतारयताम् । तदानीमश्विभ्यां गन्तव्यं काव्यस्य निवासस्थानमजानन् ऋषिरश्विनौ पृच्छति । हे दिवो नपाता द्योतमानस्य सूर्यस्य पुत्रौ वृषणा कामानां वर्षकावश्विना कुह कुत्र शयुत्रा शयने निवासस्थाने वर्तमानस्य काव्यस्य भार्गवस्य सुष्टुतिं शोभनां स्तुतिं श्रोतुं यान्ता गच्छन्तौ । यद्वा । शयुत्रेत्येतदश्विनोर्विशेषणम् । शयुनामकस्य त्रायकौ [?] युवाम् । हिरण्यस्येव कलशं यथा हिरण्यपूरितं कलशं भूम्यां निक्षिप्तं सर्वैर्दुर्ज्ञातं कश्चिदभिज्ञ उद्धरति एवमसुरैः कूपे निखातं दश रात्रीर्नव वाहानि च तत्रैव निवसन्तं रेभमवगत्य दशमेऽहन् अहनि उदूपथुः । कूपादुन्नीतवन्तौ । किं तन्निवासस्थानमिति प्रश्नः । रेभस्यानुक्तत्वादपि [?] दश रात्रीरिवेन [?] । (ऋ. सं. १-११६-२४) इति मन्त्रान्तरसामर्थ्यात्प्रतीतिः ॥

purā khalu [?] stutiṃ gacchantāvaśvinau mārgamadhye kūpe patitaṃ rebhaṃ [?] taṃ kūpādudatārayatām | tadānīmaśvibhyāṃ gantavyaṃ kāvyasya nivāsasthānamuta [?] aśvinau pṛcchati | he divo napātā dyotamānasya sūryasya putrau vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣakāvaśvinā kuha kutra śayutrā śayane nivāsasthāne vartamānasya kāvyasya bhārgavasya suṣṭutiṃ śobhanāṃ stutiṃ śrotuṃ yāntā gacchantau | yadvā | śayutretyetadaśvinorviśeṣaṇam | śayunāmakasya trāyakau [?] yuvām | hiraṇyasyeva kalaśaṃ yathā hiraṇyapūritaṃ kalaśaṃ bhūmyāṃ nikṣiptaṃ sarvairdurjñātaṃ kaścidabhijña uddharati evamasuraiḥ kūpe nikhātaṃ daśa rātrīrnava vāhāni ca tatraiva nivasantaṃ rebhamavagatya daśame 'han ahani udūpathuḥ | kūpādunnītavantau | kiṃ tannivāsasthānamiti praśnaḥ | rebhasyānuktatvādapi [?] daśa rātrīrivena [?] | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-24) iti mantrāntarasāmarthyātpratītiḥ ‖

Sense (mine; first sentences now read clearly from their repetition on p. 361): "Once, the Aśvins, going to hear the praise of Uśanas, saw Rebha fallen into a well in the middle of the road, and drew him up out of the well. Then the ṛṣi, not knowing the dwelling-place of Kāvya to which the Aśvins were to go, asks the Aśvins: O sons (napātā) of heaven — of the shining Sun — O showerers of desires, Aśvins, kuha — where are you going, to hear the fine praise (suṣṭutim) of Kāvya, the Bhārgava, who is staying in his (śayutrā) resting-place? Or: śayutrā is an epithet of the Aśvins — you two, who protect one named Śayu. Like a golden jar (hiraṇyasyeva kalaśam) — as a vessel filled with gold, buried in the earth, unknown to all, is lifted out by someone who knows it — so you drew Rebha, whom the asuras had buried in a well, who stayed there ten nights and nine days, out of the well on the tenth day (daśame 'han). — That is the question: what was that dwelling-place? From the other mantra, 'ten nights' (Ṛ. 1-116-24), it is understood." The page's small type continues with the grammar of the doubtful words (kuha, yāntā, suṣṭutim, śayutrā, kalaśam, nikhātam, daśame 'han) — characterized, not transcribed.

original p. 359

Bhāṣya of Ṛk 12, continued, small type "… Or: going towards the praise of Kāvya, where (kuha), in what place, did you two draw Rebha out? — such is the question. Kuha — [here follows the grammar: kuha formed by the rule ha ca chandasi [?] with the suffix in the sense of the seventh case; the parāṅgavadbhāva …; divo napātā, napāt by nābhāṇapād…; śayutrā by the suffix trā from śī; aśvinā; ahan]" — the printed bhāṣya ends with the formal analysis na jisambuddhyoḥ [?] etc. (characterized, not transcribed; small type).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.12) (Kannada, rendered)

Divaḥ — of the shining Sun; napātā — sons; vṛṣaṇā — showerers of desires; śayutrā — protectors of one named Śayu; aśvinā — O Aśvins; kuha — (O) where; śayutrā — in a place of resting (dwelling place); kāvyasya — of Bhārgava; suṣṭutim — fine praise (to hear); yāntā — are you going? And hiraṇyasya iva kalaśam — like a golden jar (that was hidden so that none could know); nikhātam — (by the asuras) buried (Rebha, who stayed there ten nights and nine days); daśame ahan — on the tenth day; ut ūpathuḥ — you lifted up.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.12) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, sons of the Sun, showerers of desires, protectors of one named Śayu! In what dwelling-place was the Bhārgava — to hear whose fine hymn of praise are you two going? And [how did you] lift up, on the tenth day, like a golden jar hidden so that none might know it, Rebha, who stayed ten nights and nine days buried by the asuras?"

English Translation (as printed)

"Whither were you going, son of heaven, showerers (of benefits), when on your way to the dwelling of Kavya, (to receive his) adoration, you raised up (Rebha), Aswins, on the tenth day, like a burried [sic] vessel full of gold?"

original p. 360

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 12)

In this Ṛk it is said that the Aśvins lifted out of the well and saved the ṛṣi Rebha, who had been lying in the well for nine days and ten nights:

दश रात्रीरशिवेना नव द्यून् अवनद्धं श्नथितमप्स्वन्तः । विप्रुतं रेभमुदनि प्रवृक्तमुन्निन्यथुः सोममिव स्रुवेण ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-२४)

daśa rātrīraśivenā nava dyūn avanaddhaṃ śnathitamapsvantaḥ | viprutaṃ rebhamudani pravṛktamunninyathuḥ somamiva sruveṇa ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-24)

"In this Ṛk too, the account of the saving of the ṛṣi Rebha — raising him from the well — is told."

Divo napātā — dyotamānasya sūryasya putrau: "the sons of the shining Sun — the Aśvins" is the meaning. Skandasvāmin explains in detail that the Aśvins are the sons of Āditya (the Sun):

दिवो हि पुत्र आदित्यः ऐतरेयब्राह्मणे — प्रजापतिरकामयत [as read] प्रजायेय भूयान्स्यामित्यसृजत [?] — अग्निरेव पृथिव्या अजायत । वायुरन्तरिक्षात् । आदित्यो दिवः । (ऐ. ब्रा. ५-३२-१) इति श्रुतेः ।

divo hi putra ādityaḥ aitareyabrāhmaṇe — prajāpatirakāmayata [as read] prajāyeya bhūyānsyāmityasṛjata [?] — agnireva pṛthivyā ajāyata | vāyurantarikṣāt | ādityo divaḥ | (ai. brā. 5-32-1) iti śruteḥ |

Kannada: "Understanding the Āditya as the son of heaven (the word div meaning the sky, mid-air), [he quotes the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence — that Prajāpati, wishing 'May I be many, may I multiply', — from the earth Agni was born; from mid-air, Vāyu; from heaven, Āditya] — and as evaṃ hi aitihāsikāḥ smaranti, he quotes the Purāṇa passage as the knowers of legend recall it:

दिवः पुत्रो बृहद्भानुश्चक्षुरात्मा विभावसुः । सविता स ऋचीकोऽर्को भानुरागावहो रविः । पुरा विवस्वतः सर्वे तेषां ज्येष्ठस्तथापरः ॥ इति । [as read; last line [?]]

divaḥ putro bṛhadbhānuścakṣurātmā vibhāvasuḥ | savitā sa ṛcīko 'rko bhānurāgāvaho raviḥ | purā vivasvataḥ sarve teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhastathāparaḥ ‖ iti | [as read; last line [?]]

"Bṛhadbhānu, Cakṣus, Ātman, Vibhāvasu, Savitṛ, Ṛcīka, Arka, Bhānu, Āgāvaha, Ravi and Vivasvān — these are sons of heaven; of them Vivasvān alone is the eldest" — so he explains; and:

एवं दिवः पुत्रो विवस्वान् तस्य पुत्रावश्विनौ ।

evaṃ divaḥ putro vivasvān tasya putrāvaśvinau |

"Vivasvān is thus a son of heaven; his sons are the Aśvins."

original p. 361

एवं हीतिहासमाचक्षते — त्वाष्ट्री सरण्यूर्विवस्वतः [?] आदित्यात् यमौ मिथुनं जनयाञ्चकार । सा सवर्णां प्रतिविधायान्यां अश्वं रूपं कृत्वा प्रदुद्राव । विवस्वान् आदित्योऽश्वमेव रूपं कृत्वा तामनुसृत्य तस्यां संबभूव । ततोऽश्विनौ जज्ञाते इति । एवमश्विनौ दिवः पौत्रौ ॥ [as read; small type, some words doubtful [?]]

evaṃ hītihāsamācakṣate — tvāṣṭrī saraṇyūrvivasvataḥ [?] ādityāt yamau mithunaṃ janayāñcakāra | sā savarṇāṃ pratividhāyānyāṃ aśvaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā pradudrāva | vivasvān ādityo 'śvameva rūpaṃ kṛtvā tāmanusṛtya tasyāṃ saṃbabhūva | tato 'śvinau jajñāte iti | evamaśvinau divaḥ pautrau ‖ [as read; small type, some words doubtful [?]]

Kannada: "Saraṇyū, the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, from Vivasvān, called the Āditya, bore Yama and Yamunā [Yamī] — twin children. Because she could not bear the heat of the Āditya, she created another woman in her own likeness, set her in her place (as his wife), took the form of a mare, and fled from the Sun. Then the Āditya too took the form of a horse and followed her; hence the Aśvins were born — so the history is told. Thus the Aśvins are the grandchildren of [Dyaus] Brahmā, who lights all (in heaven)" — so he explains the history.

Kuha yāntā suṣṭutiṃ kāvyasya śayutrā — śayane nivāsasthāne vartamānasya bhārgavasya śobhanāṃ stutiṃ śrotuṃ kuha gacchantau: "[O Aśvins,] where are you two going to hear the fine praise which the Bhārgava — Śukrācārya, who is staying in comfort in his dwelling — utters?" Since the question is asked by one who does not know the Aśvins' dwelling-place, the question here is that of one ignorant of the Aśvins' place:

पुरा खलु उशनसः स्तुतिं गच्छन्तावश्विनौ मार्गमध्ये कूपे पतितं रेभं दृष्ट्वा तं कूपादुदतारयताम् । तदानीमश्विभ्यां गन्तव्यं काव्यस्य निवासस्थानमजानन् ऋषिरश्विनौ पृच्छति ॥

purā khalu uśanasaḥ stutiṃ gacchantāvaśvinau mārgamadhye kūpe patitaṃ rebhaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ kūpādudatārayatām | tadānīmaśvibhyāṃ gantavyaṃ kāvyasya nivāsasthānamajānan ṛṣiraśvinau pṛcchati ‖

Kannada: "Formerly, the Aśvins, going to hear the praise of Śukrācārya, saw the ṛṣi Rebha fallen in a well on the way and lifted him up. Afterwards Rebha, not seeing them (and wishing to learn the place where they were), asked a question" — so Sāyaṇa explains. And for the word śayutrā he explains, as an epithet of the Aśvins, "those who protect one called Śayu".

Hiraṇyasyeva kalaśam — "the word hiraṇyasya is joined to kalaśam, and iva is used in the sense of comparison: as one who knows takes out a jar filled with gold, laid hidden in the earth's hollows where none can find it, so [you lifted out] Rebha who was in the well, …" the sentence continues in the Sāyaṇa quotation: "from the well, with the bhāṣya's hiraṇyapūritaṃ kalaśaṃ bhūmyāṃ nikṣiptaṃ sarvair durjñātaṃ kaścid abhijña uddharati evaṃ rebham avagatya kūpād unnītavantau"; the page ends mid-sentence; continues p. 362

original p. 362

Special Topics of Ṛk 12, concluded "… [Sāyaṇa takes] 'you raised Rebha, who was in the well' as the meaning; and he gives: kāvyasya stutiṃ prati gacchantau yuvāṃ kuha kasmin sthāne rebhaṃ yuvām unninyathuḥ iti praśnaḥ — 'Going towards the praise of Kāvya, where (kuha), in what place, did you two lift up Rebha?' is the question. And he also gives another explanation: 'While going to hear the praise that Śukrācārya speaks regarding you, what was the place from which you lifted the ṛṣi Rebha out of the well?'"

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 12; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Kuha — to the word kim, in the sense of the seventh case, vā hā ca chandasi [as printed vāhaḷa chandasi, Pā. 5-3-13 (numeral list)], the suffix ha; kutihoḥ (Pā. 7-2-4 as the list reads it [?]), ku substituted for the base. Yāntā — root yā prāpaṇe; in the sense of laṭ, suffix śatṛ; in the first dual, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39; the numeral list reads this sūtra as 3-1-39 on pp. 362–363 and 7-1-39 on p. 357 [?]), ā for the case ending; since it is ugit, num; then anusvāra, parasavarṇa. Divo napātā — sup āmantrite parāṅgavat svare (Pā. 2-1-2 as read [?]): divaḥ becomes as if a part of the following vocative; then āmantritasya ca (Pā. 6-1-198), the acute on the first syllable of the group divo napātā; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the eight-fold nighāta does not occur. Napāt means "offspring"; na pātayati iti napāt; nabhrāṇnapān… (Pā. 6-3-75), the n of the naṅ [word] is not elided and the word is irregular; supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā for the case ending (au). So too in vṛṣaṇā, the ā substitution. Śayutrā — root śīṅ svapne; aśitrādibhya itrotrau (Uṇ. sū. 4-612 as the list reads it), the suffix utra; "if so said, pratyayaḥ ādyudāttaś ca (Pā. 3-1-3)" would give the u acute from the suffix's initial acute, so it must be explained otherwise: śayuṃ trāyate iti śayutrā — from trai (root trai pālane), āde ca upadeśe 'śiti (Pā. 6-1-45), ā for the root-vowel; since the root ends in ā, ato 'nupasarge kaḥ (Pā. 3-2-3), suffix ka; since that is kit, ato lopa iṭi ca (Pā. 6-4-64), elision of the root's ā; the form śayutra. Since this derivation is not known, [the Pada-text] makes no avagraha, though in following it an avagraha would be present [?]; dual, au following, as before, ā for it; by the suffix's accent the final acute, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent.

original p. 363

Nikhātam — root khanu avadhāraṇe; niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102), suffix kta; udito vā (Pā. 7-2-56), iṭ is optional with ktvā following, so yasya vibhāṣā (Pā. 7-2-15) prohibits iṭ; janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ (Pā. 6-4-42), ā for the root-vowel; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49), in the compound the gati (ni) keeps its natural accent. Ūpathuḥ — root ḍuvap bījasantāne [as read]; liṭ, second person dual; since it stands after an ajanta, the tiṅanta accent nighāta. Daśame — the word daśan; nāntād asaṅkhyādermaṭ (Pā. 5-2-49), the suffix maṭ in the sense of the ordinal; by the suffix's accent the final acute; locative singular form. Ahan — with the seventh-case singular following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), luk for it; na jasambuddhyoḥ (Pā. 8-2-8), the elision of the n does not occur. ‖ 12 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.13)

युवं च्यवानमश्विना जरन्तं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः । युवो रथं दुहिता सूर्यस्य सह श्रिया नासत्यावृणीत ॥ १३ ॥

yuvaṃ cyavānamaśvinā jarantaṃ punaryuvānaṃ cakrathuḥ śacībhiḥ | yuvo rathaṃ duhitā sūryasya saha śriyā nāsatyāvṛṇīta ‖ 13 ‖

original p. 364

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.13)

युवम् । च्यवानम् । अश्विना । जरन्तम् । पुनरिति । युवानम् । चक्रथुः । शचीभिः । युवोः । रथम् । दुहिता । सूर्यस्य । सह । श्रिया । नासत्या । अवृणीत ॥ १३ ॥

yuvam | cyavānam | aśvinā | jarantam | punariti | yuvānam | cakrathuḥ | śacībhiḥ | yuvoḥ | ratham | duhitā | sūryasya | saha | śriyā | nāsatyā | avṛṇīta ‖ 13 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.13)

हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां शचीभिः रश्मीय्यैः [?] भैषज्यलक्षणैः कर्मभिर्जरन्तं जीर्यन्तं च्यवानं स्तुतीनां च्यावयितारमेतत्संज्ञमृषिं युवानं पुनर्यौवनोपेतं चक्रथुः । कृतवन्तौ । अपि च हे नासत्यावश्विनौ युवोर्युवयो रथं सूर्यस्य दुहिता सूर्याख्या श्रिया सह शुक्लस्वरूपया संपदा [?] कान्त्या [?] सहावृणीत समभजत । आगत्यारूढवतीत्यर्थः । 'आ वां रथं दुहिता सूर्यस्य' (ऋ. १-११६-१७ [as read]) इत्यत्र लिखितमाख्यानमत्रापि द्रष्टव्यम् ॥ जरन्तम् । जृष् वयोहानौ । व्यत्ययेन शप् । युवोः । युष्मच्छब्दात् षष्ठीद्विवचने व्यत्ययेन योचेति यत्वाभावे सति शेषे लोप इति दकारलोपः । अतो गुण इति पररूपत्वम् । एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः । आवृणीत । वृञ् संभक्तौ । क्र्यादिकः ॥

he aśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ śacībhiḥ raśmīyyaiḥ [?] bhaiṣajyalakṣaṇaiḥ karmabhirjarantaṃ jīryantaṃ cyavānaṃ stutīnāṃ cyāvayitārametatsaṃjñamṛṣiṃ yuvānaṃ punaryauvanopetaṃ cakrathuḥ | kṛtavantau | api ca he nāsatyāvaśvinau yuvoryuvayo rathaṃ sūryasya duhitā sūryākhyā śriyā saha śuklasvarūpayā saṃpadā [?] kāntyā [?] sahāvṛṇīta samabhajata | āgatyārūḍhavatītyarthaḥ | 'ā vāṃ rathaṃ duhitā sūryasya ' (ṛ. 1-116-17 [as read]) ityatra likhitamākhyānamatrāpi draṣṭavyam ‖ jarantam | jṛṣ vayohānau | vyatyayena śap | yuvoḥ | yuṣmacchabdāt ṣaṣṭhīdvivacane vyatyayena yoceti yatvābhāve sati śeṣe lopa iti dakāralopaḥ | ato guṇa iti pararūpatvam | ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ | āvṛṇīta | vṛñ saṃbhaktau | kryādikaḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, you two, by your śacībhiḥ — deeds in the form of medical treatment [as read [?]] — made the ṛṣi named Cyavana, jarantam — growing old, cyāvayitāram — the one who makes the praises move (i.e. who brings them forth) — yuvānam — again endowed with youth. And, O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, yuvoḥ — of you two the chariot — Sūryā, the daughter of the Sun (sūryasya duhitā), śriyā saha — together with splendour (in the form of a bright wealth [?], beauty [?]) avṛṇīta — chose, shared in; the meaning is: she came and mounted. The account written at 'ā vāṃ rathaṃ duhitā sūryasya' (Ṛ. 1-116-17 as read) is to be seen here too." Then the bhāṣya's grammar: jarantam (root jṛṣ vayohānau, śap by vyatyaya); yuvoḥ (from yuṣmad, genitive dual: by vyatyaya, [on account of] absence of yatva by the rule yoci, the elision of the d, ato guṇe — pararūpa; ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ); āvṛṇīta (root vṛñ sambhaktau, kryādi) — characterized.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.13) (Kannada, rendered)

He aśvinā — O Aśvins; yuvam — you two; śacībhiḥ — by (your physician's) deeds; jarantam — one who was growing old; cyavānam — Cyavana; punaḥ yuvānam — again endowed with youth; cakrathuḥ — you made (and further); nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; yuvoḥ — of you two; ratham — the chariot; sūryasya duhitā — the daughter of the Sun (the woman Sūryā); śriyā saha — with splendour (with wealth of bright form) united; āvṛṇīta — (mounted) obtained.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.13) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! You made Cyavana, who was growing old, young again by the power of your physician's art; and, O Nāsatyas, Sūryā, the daughter of the Sun, united with splendour (with wealth of bright form), came and chose your chariot."

original p. 365

English Translation (as printed)

"You rendered, by your power, Aswins, the aged Chyavana again young: the daughter of the sun, Nasatyas, invested your chariot with beauty."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 13)

Cyavānaṃ yuvaṃ śacībhiś cakrathuḥ — cyāvayitāraṃ stutīnām etatsaṃjñam ṛṣiṃ punaḥ yauvanopetaṃ aśmīyaiḥ [as read [?]] bhaiṣajyarūpaiḥ karmabhiḥ kṛtavantau: "The Aśvins, by their medical treatment, made the aged ṛṣi Cyavana young, and thereafter he praised them exceedingly" — thus it is described in this Ṛk. Skandasvāmin gives the meaning as Sāyaṇa does, and says this matter is stated in the same way elsewhere, and quotes:

जुजुरुषो नासत्योत वम्रिं प्रामुञ्चतं द्रापिमिव च्यवानात् । प्रातिरतं जहितस्यायुर्दस्रादित्पतिमकृणुतं कनीनाम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१०)

jujuruṣo nāsatyota vamriṃ prāmuñcataṃ drāpimiva cyavānāt | prātirataṃ jahitasyāyurdasrāditpatimakṛṇutaṃ kanīnām ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-10)

Sūryasya duhitā yuvor ratham āvṛṇīta — sūryākhyā sūryasya duhitā yuvāṃ ratham āgatyārūḍhavatī: "Sūryā, the daughter of the Sun, at her self-choice (svayaṃvara) chose you and mounted your chariot. And then it is told in the history here that the Aśvins obtained, with great splendour, a thousand [shining things — printed 'śukla' [?]] and Sūryā herself." Skandasvāmin explains the sense in the same way too:

आ वां रथं दुहिता सूर्यस्य कार्ष्णेवात् [?] अर्वता जयन्ती । [as read; the third and fourth syllables doubtful [?]] विश्वे देवा अन्वमन्यन्त हृद्भिः समु श्रिया नासत्या सचेथे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१७ [as read])

ā vāṃ rathaṃ duhitā sūryasya kārṣṇevāt [?] arvatā jayantī | [as read; the third and fourth syllables doubtful [?]] viśve devā anvamanyanta hṛdbhiḥ samu śriyā nāsatyā sacethe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-17 [as read])

— "in this Ṛk too the same matter is stated," and he quotes it. Yāska:

च्यवनः । ऋषिर्भवति च्यावयिता स्तोमानां च्यवानमित्यपि निगमो भवन्ति (नि. ४-१९ [as read [?]])

cyavanaḥ | ṛṣirbhavati cyāvayitā stomānāṃ cyavānamityapi nigamo bhavanti (ni. 4-19 [as read [?]])

original p. 366

Special Topics of Ṛk 13, continued "Cyavana and cyavāna are two words, both the name of one ṛṣi. He explains the word as meaning 'one who praises' [and quotes]:

युवं च्यवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनर्युवानं चरथाय तक्षथुः । निष्टौग्र्यमूहथुरद्भ्यस्परि विश्वेत्ता वां सवनेषु प्रवाच्या ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-३९-४)

yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ sanayaṃ yathā rathaṃ punaryuvānaṃ carathāya takṣathuḥ | niṣṭaugryamūhathuradbhyaspari viśvettā vāṃ savaneṣu pravācyā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-39-4)

— quoting this Ṛk, in which the word cyavāna is used, he says:

युवां च्यवानं सनयं पुराणं यथा रथं पुनर्युवानं चरणाय तक्षथुः । युवा प्रयौतीकर्माणि । तक्षतिः करोतिकर्मा (नि. ४-१९)

yuvāṃ cyavānaṃ sanayaṃ purāṇaṃ yathā rathaṃ punaryuvānaṃ caraṇāya takṣathuḥ | yuvā prayautīkarmāṇi | takṣatiḥ karotikarmā (ni. 4-19)

"The Aśvins made the old ṛṣi Cyavana, who praises them, a man in youth" — thus [Sāyaṇa] has explained."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 13; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Jarantam — root jṛṣ vayohānau; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85), in the sense of laṭ the suffix śatṛ, then śap vikaraṇa; because of that, guṇa for the root's i-vowel by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; the word jarat; since the lasārvadhātuka has come after upadeśa, tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it anudātta, so the root accent remains; in the second case, when am follows, num because it is ugit. Yuvānam — root yu miśraṇe; kanin yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidhāriṣu… [as printed kanin yukṛṣi…] (Uṇ. sū. 1-157 as the list reads it), the suffix kanin; since the suffix is nit, jñityādir nityam, the initial acute; the i of the kanin [vanishes] and the penultimate is lengthened. Cakrathuḥ — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; liṭ, second person dual; nighāta accent. Yuvoḥ — the word yuṣmad; genitive dual following, vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85), so yatva by yoci (Pā. 7-2-89 as the list reads it) does not come; up to ma [the word is changed], yuvāvau dvivacane (Pā. 7-2-92 as read), the substitute yuva; śeṣe lopaḥ (Pā. 7-2-90 [as read]), elision of the d; ato guṇe (Pā. 6-1-97), pararūpa with the a that remains; as the o-form is guṇa, and follows, again ato guṇe, pararūpa; since an udātta was in place, ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ (Pā. 8-2-5), the acute accent.

original p. 367

Śriyā — sāvekācas tṛtīyādir viḥ (Pā. 6-1-168), the acute on the case ending. Āvṛṇīta — root vṛñ sambhaktau; kryādi; laṅ, third person singular, the suffix ta; kryādibhyaḥ śnā, śnā vikaraṇa; since sārvadhātukam apit (Pā. 1-2-4 as read [?]) makes the suffix ṅit, and it begins with a consonant, ī halyaghoḥ (Pā. 6-4-113), ī for the vikaraṇa; because it stands after an ṛ-sound, ṇatva for the n; the augment aṭ; and since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 13 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.14)

युवं तुग्राय पूर्व्येभिरेवैः पुनर्मन्यावभवतं युवाना । युवं भुज्युमर्णसो निः समुद्राद्विभिरूहथुर्ऋज्रेभिरश्वैः ॥ १४ ॥

yuvaṃ tugrāya pūrvyebhirevaiḥ punarmanyāvabhavataṃ yuvānā | yuvaṃ bhujyumarṇaso niḥ samudrādvibhirūhathurṛjrebhiraśvaiḥ ‖ 14 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.14)

युवम् । तुग्राय । पूर्व्येभिः । एवैः । पुनःऽमन्या । अभवतम् । युवाना । युवम् । भुज्युम् । अर्णसः । निः । समुद्रात् । विऽभिः । ऊहथुः । ऋज्रेभिः । अश्वैः ॥ १४ ॥

yuvam | tugrāya | pūrvyebhiḥ | evaiḥ | punaḥ 'manyā | abhavatam | yuvānā | yuvam | bhujyum | arṇasaḥ | niḥ | samudrāt | vi 'bhiḥ | ūhathuḥ | ṛjrebhiḥ | aśvaiḥ ‖ 14 ‖

original p. 368

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.14)
