हे युवाना दुःखानां यावयितारावश्विनौ युवं युवां पूर्व्येभिः पुराणनामैतत् । पूर्वकालीनैरेवैः [?] गन्तृभिः स्तोत्रैस्तुग्राय भुज्योर्जनकस्य संबन्धिभिः पुनर्मन्या [?] यथा भुज्योः समुद्रगमनात्पूर्वं युवां स्तोतव्यौ तथा पुनरपीदानीं स्तोतव्यावभवतम् । यदा युवां समुद्रमध्ये सेनया सह निमग्नं भुज्युं तुग्रस्य पुत्रमर्णसः उदकयुक्तात्समुद्रादम्बुराशेः सकाशाद्विभिर्गन्तृभिर्नौभिर्ऋज्रेभिः शीघ्रगतियुक्तैरश्वैश्च निरूहथुः । निर्गमय्य पितृसमीपं प्रापितवन्तौ । तदानीं पुनरपि अतिशयेन स्तोतव्यौ जातावित्यर्थः । 'तुग्रो ह भुज्युम्' (ऋ. १-११६-३) इत्यत्रोक्तमाख्यानमत्रानुसंधेयम् ॥ [grammar tail follows in the same small type: evaiḥ (root iṇ gatau, vanu), punarmanyā (mana jñāne, pacādyac, ṭāp), yuvānā (yu miśrāmiśraṇayoḥ, kanin), arṇasaḥ (arṇaśabdād…), ṛjrebhiḥ (ṛja gatisthānārjanopārjaneṣu; ṛjrendrāgra …; bahulaṃ chandasi, bhis aisbhāvaḥ) — characterized, not transcribed]

he yuvānā duḥkhānāṃ yāvayitārāvaśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ pūrvyebhiḥ purāṇanāmaitat | pūrvakālīnairevaiḥ [?] gantṛbhiḥ stotraistugrāya bhujyorjanakasya saṃbandhibhiḥ punarmanyā [?] yathā bhujyoḥ samudragamanātpūrvaṃ yuvāṃ stotavyau tathā punarapīdānīṃ stotavyāvabhavatam | yadā yuvāṃ samudramadhye senayā saha nimagnaṃ bhujyuṃ tugrasya putramarṇasaḥ udakayuktātsamudrādamburāśeḥ sakāśādvibhirgantṛbhirnaubhirṛjrebhiḥ śīghragatiyuktairaśvaiśca nirūhathuḥ | nirgamayya pitṛsamīpaṃ prāpitavantau | tadānīṃ punarapi atiśayena stotavyau jātāvityarthaḥ | 'tugro ha bhujyum ' (ṛ. 1-116-3) ityatroktamākhyānamatrānusaṃdheyam ‖ [grammar tail follows in the same small type: evaiḥ (root iṇ gatau, vanu), punarmanyā (mana jñāne, pacādyac, ṭāp), yuvānā (yu miśrāmiśraṇayoḥ, kanin), arṇasaḥ (arṇaśabdād…), ṛjrebhiḥ (ṛja gatisthānārjanopārjaneṣu; ṛjrendrāgra …; bahulaṃ chandasi, bhis aisbhāvaḥ) — characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Yuvānā, removers of sorrows, Aśvins: you were praised by Tugra — the father of Bhujyu — with ancient praises [?], going…; as you were to be praised before Bhujyu's going to the sea, so you became again, now, worthy of praise. When Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, who had sunk into the middle of the sea together with the army, was brought out of the water-bearing sea (arṇasaḥ), the ocean, with vibhiḥ — fast-going ships — and ṛjrebhiḥ — swift-going horses, you brought him out, took him out, and delivered him to his father's side: then you became still more worthy of praise. The account told at 'tugro ha bhujyum' (Ṛ. 1-116-3) is to be taken up here."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.14) (Kannada, rendered)

Yuvam — you (always); bhujyum — Bhujyu (the son of Tugra); arṇasaḥ — [who was] agitated (in the sea); samudrāt — from the sea; vibhiḥ — by moving (ships); ṛjrebhiḥ — by swift-going; aśvaiḥ (ca) — by horses also; niḥ ūhathuḥ — you carried (him) out and brought him to the side of his father. Yuvānā — O Aśvins, removers of sorrow; yuvam — you two; pūrvyebhiḥ — by ancient; evaiḥ — by praise-words; tugrāya — to one named Tugra; punaḥ manyā — again praised; abhavatam — you became [etc.].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.14) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, removers of sorrows! When you brought Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, who was in the agitated sea, from the middle of the sea by ships and horses and delivered him [to his father] — then that king called Tugra praised you again and again with ancient praise-words."

original p. 369

English Translation (as printed)

"Dissipators of affliction, as you were praised with former praises by Tugra, so were you again adored (by him), when you brought Bhujyu safe from the tossing ocean with swift ships and rapid horses."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 14)

Punarmanyā — mana jñāne atra stutyarthaḥ manyate stutiṃ iti manā | pacādyac | manyā: "Here the root mana (in the sense of knowledge) is used with the meaning 'praise'. Then the suffix ac of the pacādi group comes, and the form manyā arises; the meaning is 'those who are praised'." Skandasvāmin:

पुनश्च स्तोत्र [?] अङ्कर्तेवीप्सार्थः । मन्यते इत्यर्चतिकर्मा कान्तिकर्मा वा । पुनः पुनः स्तुत्या कामया वा । [as read; small type [?]]

punaśca stotra [?] aṅkartevīpsārthaḥ | manyate ityarcatikarmā kāntikarmā vā | punaḥ punaḥ stutyā kāmayā vā | [as read; small type [?]]

"The word punaḥ is used in the sense of repetition. Since the root mana is used in the sense of praise, or of kānti (desire), the Aśvins [are such that] they are praised again and again; or, because they fulfil the wishes of creatures, they are such as to be wished for (abhilaṣaṇīya) by them" — thus he explains.

Pūrvyebhiḥ — purāṇanāmaitat pūrvakālīnaiḥ: "The word pūrva is read among the six names of 'ancient' [pratna, pūrva, pradiva …] (Ni. 3-20 [numeral list]); so the meaning is 'ancient (old)'. The Aśvins have been praised from very ancient times, and are even now described as worthy of exceeding praise."

Bhujyuṃ arṇasaḥ samudrāt ṛjrebhir aśvaiḥ niroohathuḥ — "King Tugra was praising the Aśvins from a very long time. Seeing his son Bhujyu sinking in the middle of the sea, the Aśvins quickly brought swift ships and horses and saved him from the middle of the water and brought him back to the house of his father. For that reason, Tugra praised them again and again — such is the account told here." On this matter:

तुग्रो ह भुज्युमश्विनोदमेघे रयिं न कश्चिन्ममृवाँ अवाहाः । तमूहथुर्नौभिरात्मन्वतीभिरन्तरिक्षप्रुद्भिरपोदकाभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-३)

tugro ha bhujyumaśvinodameghe rayiṃ na kaścinmamṛvā~ avāhāḥ | tamūhathurnaubhirātmanvatībhirantarikṣaprudbhirapodakābhiḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-3)

— "though told in this Ṛk, it is explained here in a different way."

original p. 370

Special Topics of Ṛk 14, concluded Samudrāt — ambu-rāśeḥ sakāśāt. The Nirukta author [explains]:

समुद्रः कस्मात् समुद्द्रवन्त्यस्मादापः समभिद्रवन्त्येनमापः । सम्मोदन्ते अस्मिन् भूतानि समुदको भवति समुनत्तीति वा ॥

samudraḥ kasmāt samuddravantyasmādāpaḥ samabhidravantyenamāpaḥ | sammodante asmin bhūtāni samudako bhavati samunattīti vā ‖

Kannada: "From it, the waters rise upward; or the waters of rivers and the like all run into it and gather; or aquatic creatures, dwelling in this mass of water, rejoice; or, from abundance, the waters are joined together in it; or it wets everything with water" — thus he explains the word samudra with its various meanings. No numeral printed with this Nirukta quotation in the numeral list.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 14; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Pūrvyebhiḥ — pūrve bhavāḥ pūrvyāḥ, suffix yat; in the instrumental plural, bahulaṃ chandasi: bhis does not become ais; bahuvacane jhalyet [as printed; Pā. number illegible in the list [?]], et substituted. Evaiḥ — root iṇ gatau; iṇśīṅbhyāṃ vanaj (Uṇ. sū. 1-150 as the list reads it [?]), the suffix van; guṇa for the i-vowel on that account; since the suffix is nit, jñityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197), the initial acute; instrumental plural form. Punarmanyā — root mana jñāne; since roots have many meanings, here used in the sense of praise; manyate stauti iti manā stutiḥ, since it belongs to the pacādi group, nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (Pā. 3-1-134), suffix ac; to this, in the sense of "worthy of it", chandasi ca (Pā. 5-1-67 as read), suffix ya; yasyeti ca, with it following, elision of the preceding a; by the suffix's accent the final acute; first dual form. Abhavatam — root bhū sattāyām; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Yuvānā — root yu miśrāmiśraṇayoḥ, adādi; kanin yuvṛṣi… (Uṇ. sū. 1-157 as read), suffix kanin; ajiknudhātubhruvām iyuvaṅau (Pā. 6-4-77), uv substituted; with the dual following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā substituted; sarvanāmasthāne ca [as read], lengthening of the penultimate; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19), nighāta. Arṇasaḥ — "arṇo 'smin asti": when the sense of matup is intended, from asanta, the suffix vin [on the model] asmāyāmedrasrajo vini [as read [?]]; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 5-2-122 as read), by the word bahula in that rule, elision [of vin]; the form arṇas remains; ablative singular.

original p. 371

Vibhiḥ — since it is nit, [the accent of the] case ending after it is udātta (as expected), though by the statement sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante here bhis does not get the udātta accent. Ūhathuḥ — root vaha prāpaṇe; liṭ, second person dual; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Ṛjrebhiḥ — root ṛja gatisthānārjanopārjaneṣu; ṛjrendrāgravajra… (Uṇ. sū. 2-28? [as read, partly illegible [?]]), irregularly formed with the suffix ran; since it is nit, jñityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197), the initial acute; in the instrumental plural with bhis following, bahulaṃ chandasi, the substitution ais does not occur; bahuvacane jhalyet, et. ‖ 14 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.15)

अजोहवीदश्विना तौग्र्यो वां प्रोळ्हः समुद्रमव्यथिर्जगन्वान् । निष्टमूहथुः सुयुजा रथेन मनोजवसा वृषणा स्वस्ति ॥ १५ ॥

ajohavīdaśvinā taugryo vāṃ proḷhaḥ samudramavyathirjaganvān | niṣṭamūhathuḥ suyujā rathena manojavasā vṛṣaṇā svasti ‖ 15 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.15)

अजोहवीत् । अश्विना । तौग्र्यः । वाम् । प्रऽऊळ्हः । समुद्रम् । अव्यथिः । जगन्वान् । निः । तम् । ऊहथुः । सुऽयुजा । रथेन । मनःऽजवसा । वृषणा । स्वस्ति ॥ १५ ॥

ajohavīt | aśvinā | taugryaḥ | vām | pra 'ūḷhaḥ | samudram | avyathiḥ | jaganvān | niḥ | tam | ūhathuḥ | su 'yujā | rathena | manaḥ 'javasā | vṛṣaṇā | svasti ‖ 15 ‖

original p. 372

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.15) small type; read with doubts

हे अश्विनौ वां युवां तौग्र्यः तुग्रपुत्रः प्रोळ्हः पित्रा प्रापितः समुद्रेऽम्बुधौ [?] जगन्वान् गतवान् सन् अव्यथिः व्यथारहितः अजोहवीत् । स्तुतिभिराह्वयत् । तमाह्वाकारं [?] हे मनोजवसा मनोवद्वेगयुक्तौ वृषणा कामानां वर्षकावश्विनौ सुयुजा सुष्ठु युक्ताश्वैर्युक्तेन रथेन स्वस्ति क्षेमं यथा भवति तथा निरूहथुः । जलान्निर्गमय्य युवां पितृगृहं प्रापितवन्तौ ॥ [the grammar tail follows: jagan­vān (gamer liṭaḥ kvasuḥ; vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām, optional iṭ), manojavasā (manaso java iva javo yayos tau; supāṃ sulug, ā), nighāta not occurring because of the pādādi [?], etc. — characterized, not transcribed]

he aśvinau vāṃ yuvāṃ taugryaḥ tugraputraḥ proḷhaḥ pitrā prāpitaḥ samudre 'mbudhau [?] jaganvān gatavān san avyathiḥ vyathārahitaḥ ajohavīt | stutibhirāhvayat | tamāhvākāraṃ [?] he manojavasā manovadvegayuktau vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣakāvaśvinau suyujā suṣṭhu yuktāśvairyuktena rathena svasti kṣemaṃ yathā bhavati tathā nirūhathuḥ | jalānnirgamayya yuvāṃ pitṛgṛhaṃ prāpitavantau ‖ [the grammar tail follows: jagan­vān (gamer liṭaḥ kvasuḥ; vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām, optional iṭ), manojavasā (manaso java iva javo yayos tau; supāṃ sulug, ā), nighāta not occurring because of the pādādi [?], etc. — characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, Tugra's son, tauġryaḥ (Bhujyu), prolhaḥ — sent by his father to the sea, the ocean (samudram), going there, avyathiḥ — without distress [though sunk], called (ajohavīt) to you with praises. For that [calling], O swift as thought (manojavasā), showerers of desires, you two brought him out (niroohathuḥ) — with a well-yoked chariot, in such a way that it should be svasti (safe); having brought him out of the water, you delivered him to his father's house."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.15) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; prolhaḥ — sent by his father to the sea's vicinity; taugryaḥ — Bhujyu, the son of Tugra; samudram — to the sea; jagan-vān — having set out; avyathiḥ — (though sunk in the sea) free of distress; vām — you both; ajohavīt — (praising) called; tam — (the praising) him; manojavasā — swift as thought; vṛṣaṇā — showerers of desires (you); suyujā — with well [yoked] horses; rathena — by the chariot; svasti — safely; niḥ ūhathuḥ — you took (out of the sea) and carried [to his father's house].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.15) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! Bhujyu, sent by his father to the sea's vicinity — set out for the voyage, free of anxiety (though sinking in the sea) — praised you; you who are swift as thought and showerers of desires took the praising one out safely on a chariot yoked with excellent horses, and delivered him to his father's house."

English Translation (as printed)

"The son of Tugra, brought back by you, Aswins, (to his father), glorified you when he had crossed the ocean in safety, and you bore him showerers (of benefits), with your well-harnessed car, swift as thought, to safety."

original p. 373

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 15)

Manojavasā — manovad vegayuktau | manaso java iva javo yayos tau: "Those who go with a speed like the mind's; or the meaning is: those who have a speed like the mind's speed."

Svasti — kṣemaṃ yathā bhavati tathā: "Sāyaṇa takes the word svasti as an adverb and construes it with the verb niroohathuḥ, meaning 'safely, or as [it is] comfortable'. Skandasvāmin says that the word svasti here contains an inner causative sense (antarbhāvita-ṇyartha), and explains it as svastimantam — 'one who is well-off, safe'."

"In this Ṛk, too, the greatness of the Aśvins who saved Bhujyu — told earlier at 1-116-3 and 1-117-14 — is described in a different manner."

The Nirukta author, explaining pathyā svastiḥ:

पथ्या स्वस्तिः । पथा अन्तरिक्षं तन्निवासात् । (नि. ११-४५ [numeral list])

pathyā svastiḥ | pathā antarikṣaṃ tannivāsāt | (ni. 11-45 [numeral list])

"Since svasti dwells in mid-air, the word pathyā can be used of it" — so he explains, and quotes:

स्वस्ति नः पथ्यासु धन्वसु स्वस्त्य १ प्सु वृजने स्वर्वति । स्वस्ति नः पुत्रकृथेषु योनिषु स्वस्ति राये मरुतो दधातन ॥ स्वस्तिरिद्धि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्णस्वत्यभि या वाममेति । सा नो अमा सो अरणे नि पातु स्वावेशा भवतु देवगोपा ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-६३-१५ और १६)

svasti naḥ pathyāsu dhanvasu svastya 1 psu vṛjane svarvati | svasti naḥ putrakṛtheṣu yoniṣu svasti rāye maruto dadhātana ‖ svastiriddhi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇasvatyabhi yā vāmameti | sā no amā so araṇe ni pātu svāveśā bhavatu devagopā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-63-15 aura 16)

"Svasti is the one that dwells in mid-air. Worthy of praise by all deities, she is the best; she gives wealth and makes water available — in this manner may svasti protect us at home, in the forest, and in our wanderings. May she protect those who offer oblations with rays. May this goddess shine and protect the gods. May this svasti be of good intent towards us" — thus he explains.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 15; grammar page, noted briefly)

Ajohavīt — root hvej spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; after the yaṅluganta [base], laṅ, third person singular, the suffix tip; the augment īṭ; iteś ca (as read), ī of the suffix elided; abhyastasya ca, saṃprasāraṇa for the root; pūrvarūpa; doubling of the root; kuhoś cuḥ (Pā. 7-4-62 as the list reads it) …

original p. 374

Grammar of Ṛk 15, continued (noted briefly; sūtra numbers from the numeral list where it had them): ajohavīt (continued) — when cutva [comes], guṇo yaṅluk oḥ (Pā. 7-4-82), guṇa for the reduplicative syllable; yaṅo vā (Pā. 7-3-94), the augment īṭ for the unaccented tip; for that reason guṇa of the u of the root, av substituted; the augment aṭ; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not occur; the augment aṭ being udātta, the initial acute. Taugryaḥ — tugrasya apatyaṃ pumān taugryaḥ; it belongs to the gargādi group, suffix yañ; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ, vṛddhi of the initial; yasyeti ca, elision of the a. Jaganvān — root gam̐ḷ gatau; when liṭ has come, kvasuś ca (Pā. 3-2-107), kvasu substituted for it; vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām (Pā. 7-2-68), the augment iṭ is optional, so here no iṭ; the suffix being the cause, doubling of the root; halādiśeṣa for the reduplicative syllable, kuhoś cuḥ, j substituted; mokṣyeti [?] — since a vakāra-initial suffix follows, m of the root becomes n; the word jaganvas; in the first case, atvasantasya cādhātoḥ [as read], lengthening of the penultimate; since the suffix is ugit, num; hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal, [elision of] su; by elision of the cluster-final, elision of the t; since this is asiddha, the elision of the n does not occur; by the suffix's accent, the final acute. Niṣṭam — niḥ + tam, [and by] yuṣmattatakṣuṣvantaḥpādam (Pā. 8-3-103), ṣatva for the visarga, the mūrdhanya. Suyujā — su + yuj, yujir yoge; suffix kvip; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Manojavasā — manaso java iva javo yayos tau manojavasau; supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), ā for the case ending; though it has the name āmantrita, because it stands at the beginning of a pāda the nighāta does not occur; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 6-1-198), the initial acute. Svasti — when su is the upapada, root as bhuvi; to this, in the abstract sense, striyāṃ ktin (Pā. 3-3-94), suffix ktin; chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 [as read; list 3-4-17 [?]]), it gets the sārvadhātuka name; asterbhūḥ (Pā. 2-4-52), bhū substituted for the root does not occur; na subhyām (Pā. 6-2-172), the final acute. ‖ 15 ‖

Sense (editorial and tentative): "What was said in the half-verse 'āsno vṛkasya' (Ṛ. 1-116-14) is set out here by the first half. Vartikā — a female bird like a quail, seized by a wolf (vṛka) [Kannada p. 377 will confirm], O Aśvins, called you (ajohavīt) when you freed (amuñcatam) the vartikā from the mouth (āsnaḥ) of the wolf. And you two (yuvam) went (vi yayathuḥ), by a victorious (jayuṣā) chariot, to the sānu — the high ground — of the mountain (adreḥ), [taking there] the praiser named Jāhuṣa, surrounded by enemies, after bringing him out from the multitude of enemies — to the mountain-top, which none could reach with any helpers. That is said at 'surrounded Jāhuṣa' (Ṛ. 1-116-20). And [you] struck down by poison (viṣeṇa) the offspring of the asura Viṣvāñc, of varied movement…" the sentence continues on p. 376 Bhāṣya of Ṛk 16, continued; small type, read with several doubts

… यद्वा । वर्तते प्रतिदिवसमावर्तत इति वर्तिकोषाः [?] । वृकः [?] इति विवृतज्योतिष्कः [?] सूर्य उच्यते । तेन ग्रस्ता सती सा हे अश्विनौ युवामजोहवीत् आह्वयत् । यदा खलु युवां वृकस्य सूर्यस्यास्य आस्यस्थानीयान्मण्डलादमुञ्चतं आमोचयतम् । सूर्येणैकीभूतामुषसं पृथक्कृत्य एकोदयात्पूर्वं रात्रेरपरभागे स्थापितवन्ताविति अर्थः । तथा च यास्कः । आदित्योऽपि वृक उच्यते यदावृङ्क्ते [?] । अश्वयादुषा अश्विनावादित्येनाभिग्रस्ता तामश्विनौ प्रमुमुचतुरित्याख्यानं (नि. ५-२१ [numeral list]) इति । अपि च जयुषा जयशीलेन रथेनाद्रेर्मेघस्य सानु समुच्छ्रितप्रदेशं वृष्टिचिकीर्षया विशेषेण ययथुः । युवां गतवन्तौ । गत्वा च विष्वाचो विविधगतियुक्तस्य मेघस्य संबन्धिना विषेणोदकेन जातमुत्पन्नं सर्वं भूतजातमहतम् । आगमयेतम् [?] । वृष्टिं कृतवन्तावित्यर्थः ॥

… yadvā | vartate pratidivasamāvartata iti vartikoṣāḥ [?] | vṛkaḥ [?] iti vivṛtajyotiṣkaḥ [?] sūrya ucyate | tena grastā satī sā he aśvinau yuvāmajohavīt āhvayat | yadā khalu yuvāṃ vṛkasya sūryasyāsya āsyasthānīyānmaṇḍalādamuñcataṃ āmocayatam | sūryeṇaikībhūtāmuṣasaṃ pṛthakkṛtya ekodayātpūrvaṃ rātreraparabhāge sthāpitavantāviti arthaḥ | tathā ca yāskaḥ | ādityo 'pi vṛka ucyate yadāvṛṅkte [?] | aśvayāduṣā aśvināvādityenābhigrastā tāmaśvinau pramumucaturityākhyānaṃ (ni. 5-21 [numeral list]) iti | api ca jayuṣā jayaśīlena rathenādrermeghasya sānu samucchritapradeśaṃ vṛṣṭicikīrṣayā viśeṣeṇa yayathuḥ | yuvāṃ gatavantau | gatvā ca viṣvāco vividhagatiyuktasya meghasya saṃbandhinā viṣeṇodakena jātamutpannaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtajātamahatam | āgamayetam [?] | vṛṣṭiṃ kṛtavantāvityarthaḥ ‖

Sense (editorial and tentative): "Or: vartikā — [the dawn] that turns about, recurs every day; vṛka is used for the Sun, whose light is uncovered [?]. Seized by him, she called you, Aśvins, when you freed her from the Sun's disc, that stands in the place of his mouth (āsyasthānīya): having separated the Dawn, who had become one with the Sun, you set her in the latter part of the night, before the rising of the one [sun]. So Yāska [says]: 'the Āditya too is called vṛka, as he turns...' [?] — the story: 'Uṣas, desiring a horse [?], was seized by Āditya; the Aśvins freed her' (Ni. 5-21 as the numeral list reads it). And with a victorious chariot you went to the high ground (sānu) of the cloud (adri), in order to cause rain, going specially; and having gone, you struck [i.e. caused to be struck] all created beings that were born, with the water (viṣa) of the cloud (viṣvāñc) of varied motion; that is, you made rain." The bhāṣya then gives the grammar of ajohavīt, āsnaḥ, jayuṣā, viṣvāco, ahatam (han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, laṅ, luk etc.) — characterized, not transcribed.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.16) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; vartikā — the bird called vartikā (seized by a wolf); vām — you two; yat sīm — when; ajohavīt — [she] praised; tadā — then; vṛkasya — of the wolf; āsnaḥ — from the mouth; amuñcatam — you freed (her); api ca — and; jayuṣā — by the victorious (chariot); adreḥ — of the mountain; sānu — to the top; vi yayathuḥ — you went (with Jāhuṣa); tathā — likewise; viṣvācaḥ — of Viṣvāñca (the asura); jātam — the son; viṣeṇa — by poison; ahatam — you killed. Or: [aśvinā] — O Aśvins; vartikā — the dawn that returns every day; vām — you two; yat sīm — when; ajohavīt — [she], seized by the Sun, praised; — then; vṛkasya — of the Sun (who covers everything); āsnaḥ — from the mouth-like (disc); amuñcatam — you freed [her] (having separated her from him, you placed her in the last part of the night); — and; jayuṣā — on the victorious chariot; adreḥ — of the cloud; sānu — to the top; vi yayathuḥ — you set out (in order to rain) and went; viṣvācaḥ — of the cloud (of varied motion); viṣeṇa — with water; jātam — to all created beings; ahatam — you gave [rain].

original p. 377

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.16) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! When the bird called vartikā praised you, you freed her from the wolf's mouth; on a victorious chariot, with the man called Jāhuṣa, you went to the top of a mountain not reachable by anyone [on foot]; and [thus] you killed with poison the son of the asura named Viṣvāñca. Or: when the Dawn, who had gone along with the Sun, the covering one, praised you, you freed her from the Sun's disc and made her the end of the night; and, seated on a victorious chariot, you went to the top of the clouds in order to rain, and gave the water of the clouds of varied motion to all beings."

English Translation (as printed)

"The quail glorified you, Aswins, when you saved her from the mouth of the wolf; you carried off (Jahusha) to the top of the mountain in our [sic] triumphant chariot; and slew the son of Vishwanch with a poisoned (arrow)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 16)

"In this Ṛk, three wonderful acts of the Aśvins are described: that they released a gubbacci (quail), caught and held by a wolf (the forest dog) and gave life to it; that, seeing the king named Jāhuṣa surrounded by enemies, they helped him, seated him on a splendid chariot and took him to the mountain's peak; and that they gave poison to the son of the asura Viṣvāñca, who harmed the world by wicked ways, and killed him."

आस्नो वृकस्य वर्तिकामभीके युवं नरा नासत्यामुमुक्तम् । उतो कविं पुरुभुजा युवं ह कृपमाणमकृणुतं विचक्षे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१४)

āsno vṛkasya vartikāmabhīke yuvaṃ narā nāsatyāmumuktam | uto kaviṃ purubhujā yuvaṃ ha kṛpamāṇamakṛṇutaṃ vicakṣe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-14)

"In the first half of this Ṛk, the matter of the saving of the quail is explained." Special Topics of Ṛk 16, continued

original p. 378

परिविष्टं जाहुषं विश्वतः सीं सुगेभिर्नक्तमूहथू रजोभिः । विभिष्ट्वा नासत्या रथेन वि पर्वताँ अजरयू अयातम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-२०)

pariviṣṭaṃ jāhuṣaṃ viśvataḥ sīṃ sugebhirnaktamūhathū rajobhiḥ | vibhiṣṭvā nāsatyā rathena vi parvatā~ ajarayū ayātam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-20)

"In this Ṛk, too, the matter of the protection of King Jāhuṣa is stated."

"From the words 'vṛkasya āsno vāṃ vartikām amuñcatam', [Sāyaṇa], seeing that Uṣas had become subject to the sun's disc, explains: 'since the Aśvins freed her from it' — i.e. in the early morning, because the Sun's rising is to occur, they placed Uṣas in the last part of the night, before the Sun's rising; and interpreting so, [Sāyaṇa] says 'sūryeṇa ekībhūtām uṣasaṃ pṛthakkṛtya udayāt pūrvaṃ rātrer aparabhāge sthāpitavantau'. He quotes the Nirukta passage in which Yāska expresses this view — tathā ca yāskaḥ:

आदित्योऽपि वृक उच्यते यदावृङ्क्ते [?] । अह्नयदुषा [?] अश्विना आदित्येनाभिग्रस्ता तामश्विना प्रमुमुचतुरित्याख्यानम् ॥ (नि. ५-२१)

ādityo 'pi vṛka ucyate yadāvṛṅkte [?] | ahnayaduṣā [?] aśvinā ādityenābhigrastā tāmaśvinā pramumucaturityākhyānam ‖ (ni. 5-21)

[Sāyaṇa says] "vivṛtajyotiṣkaḥ sūryaḥ ucyate | vartate pratidivasam āvartate iti vartikā uṣāḥ" — for the words vṛka and vartikā, he gives the meanings 'Uṣas' and 'the Sun'. In this exposition the freeing of a woman who had been seized by force is held praiseworthy. The Nirukta author also says that Uṣas, the woman, seized by the Sun, called the Aśvins and prayed to them. And for the sentence viṣvāco ... jātam ahatam yayathuḥ he gives another meaning: 'the Aśvins, on their victorious chariot, went to the high place where the cloud is, and by pouring the cloud's rain with water saved all beings.'"

Viṣvācaḥ — viṣu nānā abhimukhyena añcati: "[the one] who moves in many contrary directions (towards [different] beings)". Skandasvāmin explains this same meaning of viṣvāk, and quotes:

याभिर्वर्तिकां ग्रसितामुमुञ्चतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विनागतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-८)

yābhirvartikāṃ grasitāmumuñcataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvināgatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-8)

— "quoting also this half-Ṛk."

original p. 379

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 16; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers from the numeral list)

Ajohavīt — root hvej spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; after the yaṅluganta, laṅ, third person singular, suffix tip; iteś ca, elision of ī; yaṅo vā (Pā. 7-3-94 [list]), the augment īṭ; abhyastasya ca (Pā. 6-1-33 [list]), saṃprasāraṇa before the doubling; then doubling, cutva for the reduplicative syllable, guṇa; the augment aṭ; since it is udātta, the initial acute; because it is at the beginning of a pāda, nighāta does not occur. Āsnaḥ — the word āsya; ablative singular following, pad-dan-no-māsa… (Pā. 6-1-63 [list]), āsan substituted for the base; since it has the name bha, alloponaḥ (Pā. 6-4-134 [list]), elision of the a of an; the form āsnaḥ; ūḍidaṃpadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ… (Pā. 6-1-171 [list]), the acute on the case ending. Amuñcatam — root mucḷ mokṣaṇe; laṅ, second person dual; since it is connected with yat [a particle], no nighāta; the augment aṭ is udātta, so the initial acute. Jayuṣā — root ji jaye; the auṇādika suffix usi; guṇa of the i on account of the suffix; ay substituted; ādeśapratyayayoḥ (Pā. 8-3-59), ṣatva of the s of the suffix; by the suffix's accent the u is acute; instrumental singular. Yeyathuḥ [read as yayathuḥ] — root yā prāpaṇe; liṭ, second person dual; after an ajanta, nighāta. Jātam — root janī prādurbhāve; niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 [the list reads 103 here]), suffix kta; janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ (Pā. 6-4-42 [list]), ā for the root-vowel; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Viṣvācaḥ — viṣu nānā abhimukhyena añcati iti vigrahaḥ; ṛtvigdadhṛk… (Pā. 3-2-59 [list]), when a subanta is the upapada, the suffix kvin for the root añcu gatipūjanayoḥ; acaḥ (Pā. 6-4-138 [list]), since it has the name bha, elision of the a of the root; cau (Pā. 6-3-138 [list]), lengthening of the preceding; the case ending being anudātta and the root's a having been elided, anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. 6-1-161 [list]), the acute for the case ending is attained; cau (Pā. 6-1-222 [list]), the acute on the preceding [syllable] …

original p. 380

Grammar of Ṛk 16, concluded (noted briefly): Ahatam — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; adādi; laṅ, second person dual; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtamtāmaḥ, tam substituted; adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. 2-4-72 [list]), luk for śap; since the suffix is jit- [?] [as read: "jid-dvāva"], anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām (Pā. 6-4-37 [list]), elision of the nasal n of the root; the augment aṭ; because it stands after an ajanta, tiṅ atiṅaḥ [as read], the nighāta accent. ‖ 16 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.17)

शतं मेषान्वृक्ये ममहानं तमः प्रणीतमशिवेन पित्रा । आक्षी ऋज्राश्वे अश्विनावधत्तं ज्योतिरन्धाय चक्रथुर्विचक्षे ॥ १७ ॥

śataṃ meṣānvṛkye mamahānaṃ tamaḥ praṇītamaśivena pitrā | ākṣī ṛjrāśve aśvināvadhattaṃ jyotirandhāya cakrathurvicakṣe ‖ 17 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.17)

शतम् । मेषान् । वृक्ये । ममहानम् । तमः । प्रऽनीतम् । अशिवेन । पित्रा । आ । अक्षी इति । ऋज्रऽअश्वे । अश्विनौ । अधत्तम् । ज्योतिः । अन्धाय । चक्रथुः । विऽचक्षे ॥ १७ ॥

śatam | meṣān | vṛkye | mamahānam | tamaḥ | pra 'nītam | aśivena | pitrā | ā | akṣī iti | ṛjra 'aśve | aśvinau | adhattam | jyotiḥ | andhāya | cakrathuḥ | vi 'cakṣe ‖ 17 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.17)

शतं मेषान्वृक्ये चक्षुर्दानम् । (ऋ. १-११६-१६ [as read [?]]) इत्यत्र यदाख्यानमुक्तं तदत्राप्यनुसंधेयम् । शतं शतसंख्याकान्मेषान्वृक्यै वृकीरूपेणावस्थितायै [?] अश्विनोर्वाहनाय रासभाय ममहानं पूजितवन्तं समर्पितवन्तं [?] अशिवेन अशुभकारिणा पित्रा स्वकीयेन जनकेन तमो दृष्टिरहितत्वेन कृतमान्ध्यं प्रणीतं प्रापितमृज्राश्वं चक्षुष्मन्तं कृत्वा अश्विनावकुरुतामिति शेषः । एतदेव विशदयति । हे अश्विनौ आक्षी पित्राशापि [?] चक्षुषी ऋज्राश्वे एतत्संज्ञके राजर्षावधत्तं । पुनर्दर्शनसमर्थे आकुरुतम् । एतेनाह । अन्धाय दृष्टिहीनाय ज्योतिः प्रकाशकं चक्षुः विचक्षे विविधं जगद्द्रष्टुं चक्रथुः । युवां कृतवन्तौ ॥ [grammar tail: mamahānam (maha pūjāyām, liṭ, kānac, the reduplicative syllable lengthened in the Saṃhitā), praṇītam (niṣṭhā, gatir anantaraḥ), pitrā (udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt), akṣī (the dual form with num; ī → ī-kāra, pararūpa)... — characterized, not transcribed]

śataṃ meṣānvṛkye cakṣurdānam | (ṛ. 1-116-16 [as read [?]]) ityatra yadākhyānamuktaṃ tadatrāpyanusaṃdheyam | śataṃ śatasaṃkhyākānmeṣānvṛkyai vṛkīrūpeṇāvasthitāyai [?] aśvinorvāhanāya rāsabhāya mamahānaṃ pūjitavantaṃ samarpitavantaṃ [?] aśivena aśubhakāriṇā pitrā svakīyena janakena tamo dṛṣṭirahitatvena kṛtamāndhyaṃ praṇītaṃ prāpitamṛjrāśvaṃ cakṣuṣmantaṃ kṛtvā aśvināvakurutāmiti śeṣaḥ | etadeva viśadayati | he aśvinau ākṣī pitrāśāpi [?] cakṣuṣī ṛjrāśve etatsaṃjñake rājarṣāvadhattaṃ | punardarśanasamarthe ākurutam | etenāha | andhāya dṛṣṭihīnāya jyotiḥ prakāśakaṃ cakṣuḥ vicakṣe vividhaṃ jagaddraṣṭuṃ cakrathuḥ | yuvāṃ kṛtavantau ‖ [grammar tail: mamahānam (maha pūjāyām, liṭ, kānac, the reduplicative syllable lengthened in the Saṃhitā), praṇītam (niṣṭhā, gatir anantaraḥ), pitrā (udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt), akṣī (the dual form with num; ī → ī-kāra, pararūpa)... — characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "The story told at 'śataṃ meṣān vṛkye' (Ṛ. 1-116-16 as read [?]) is to be taken up here too. Śataṃ — a hundred sheep, to a she-wolf (vṛkye — standing in the form of a female wolf) — who was the vehicle (vāhana) [as read [?]] of the Aśvins — mamahānam: he [Ṛjrāśva] who gave them, offered them (in worship); by the inauspicious (aśivena) father, tamaḥ — blindness, being without sight — praṇītam — brought to — made seeing the Ṛjrāśva who had been blinded: the Aśvins did it — that is the supplement. This he makes clear: O Aśvins, in Ṛjrāśva, the royal sage of that name, you placed (adhattam) akṣī — eyes, [lost through] the father's curse [?]; made him again able to see. Thereby he says: andhāya — to the one without sight, you made jyotiḥ — a light-giving eye, vicakṣe — to see the world in its variety."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.17) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinau — O Aśvins; śatam — a hundred; meṣān — sheep; vṛkye — (to your vehicle) in the form of a she-wolf; mamahānam — (given as food) worshipped [him]; aśivena — by an inauspicious (sorrow-causing) [father]; pitrā — by his father; tamaḥ — [praṇītam] brought to darkness (blindness) — (that is, you made the blinded Ṛjrāśva again able to see); ṛjrāśve — to the king named Ṛjrāśva; akṣī — (eyes lost by his father's curse); ā adhattam — you gave (capable of sight); andhāya — to the blind one; jyotiḥ — light-giving [eyes]; vicakṣe — to see (things clearly); cakrathuḥ — you made.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.17) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! Because he gave a hundred sheep to a she-wolf (your vehicle), his father, made unkind [i.e. cursed him], and Ṛjrāśva became blind; you gave eyes to Ṛjrāśva and made him able to see things clearly."

original p. 382

English Translation (as printed)

"You restored eyes to Rijrashwa, who, on presenting a hundred sheep to the she-wolf, had been condemned [printed "eondemned" — sic] to darkness by his indignant father, and gave light to the blind, wherewith to behold all things."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 17)

In explaining this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa quotes:

शतं मेषान् वृक्ये चक्षदानमृज्राश्वं तं पिताऽन्धं चकार । तस्मा अक्षी नासत्या विचक्ष आधत्तं दस्रा भिषजावनर्वन् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१६ [as read in the image; earlier marked [?]])

śataṃ meṣān vṛkye cakṣadānamṛjrāśvaṃ taṃ pitā 'ndhaṃ cakāra | tasmā akṣī nāsatyā vicakṣa ādhattaṃ dasrā bhiṣajāvanarvan ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-16 [as read in the image; earlier marked [?]])

— "ity atra yad ākhyānam uktaṃ tad atrāpy anusandheyam": "the account told in this Ṛk is to be taken up here too. The meaning explained in the Ṛk 'śataṃ meṣān' is told again here", he says. "A royal sage named Ṛjrāśva gave a hundred sheep, one by one, as food to the vehicle of the Aśvins, who had a she-wolf's form; his father, seeing this, pronounced a curse: 'Let him become unable to see.' Thereby he lost his sight. Ṛjrāśva, being blind, praised the Aśvins. The Aśvins, the physicians of the gods, came, saw him, gave him eyes by which everything could be seen well, and saved him — this account, told in the previous Ṛk [too], is told here again in different words."

Vṛkye — vṛkarūpeṇāvasthitāya aśvinor vāhanāya rāsabhāya: "The Aśvins' vehicle, the power [śakti] that took a wolf's form; that is, for the food of that [she-wolf]."

Mamahānam — pūjitavantam āhārārthaṃ samarpitavantam: "From the root maha, in the sense of worship, [the word] has the meaning 'one who worships exceedingly'; hence it is the idea that giving food to the Aśvins' vehicle, who had taken the form of a wolf, is itself a worship."

Praṇītam — prāpitaṃ ṛjrāśvaṃ cakṣuṣmantam aśvināv akuruta [iti śeṣaḥ]: "The prefix pra, joined with the root nī, gives a different meaning; so the word praṇīta means 'one brought'. Here the sense is: the Aśvins made Ṛjrāśva able to see and gave him eyes."

original p. 383

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 17; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers read from the page — the numeral list has no entry for this page)

Mamahānam — root maha pūjāyām; when liṭ has come, liṭaḥ kānaj vā (Pā. 3-2-106 as read), kānac substituted; on that account, doubling of the root; ādir halśeṣaḥ for the reduplicative syllable; the form mamahāna; in the Saṃhitā the reduplicative syllable is lengthened by Vedic usage; if it is assumed to belong to the tujādi group, then the lengthening would have to be heard in the Pada-text too; since the suffix is cit, ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163 as read) gives the final acute. Praṇītam — root ṇīñ prāpaṇe; with the prefix pra following, in the passive sense niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 as read), suffix kta; since it is kit, guṇa of the root's i-vowel does not occur; ṇatva because of the prefix's cause; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read), the gati (pra) keeps its natural accent. Aśivena — na śivaḥ aśivaḥ, with śena; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 as read), the naṅ [prefix] keeps its natural accent. Pitrā — to the word pitṛ, instrumental singular ṭā following, yaṇ substituted; for the ṛ-vowel that was udātta, yaṇ comes; with the case-ending following it, udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (Pā. 6-1-174 as read), the acute on the case ending. Akṣī — to the word akṣi, dual following, napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ… (Pā. 7-1-72 as read), num is obtained; īcca dvivacane (Pā. 7-1-77 as read), the ī-final substitution is also obtained; then by the maxim vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam [the later rule prevails], since īt-va [?] is enjoined by the later sūtra, the substitution applies; the doubt that num should come after the īt is raised as it is ajanta-… (accent) nighāta; by the maxim sakṛdgatau vipratiṣedhe yad bādhitaṃ tad bādhitam eva, what is once set aside is set aside; hence [num] does not come; udāttaḥ — from the preceding sūtra, by continuation, the ī becomes udātta. Adhattam — root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; laṅ, second person dual; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Vicakṣe — vi the prefix; root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; since roots have many meanings, here used in the sense of seeing; to it, in the sense of the infinitive, tumarthe se-sen-ase… [Pā. 3-4-9 as read [?]] …

original p. 384

Grammar of Ṛk 17, concluded (noted briefly): Vicakṣe (continued) — [the infinitive suffix] se (tumarthe se-sen-ase-asen-kase-kasen-adhyai-…, Pā. 3-4-9 as read); skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca (Pā. 8-2-29 as read), elision of the conjunct's k [of the root]; ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (Pā. 8-2-41 as read), the ṣ → k [for] h; kaṣa-… — the k and then, since a k follows, the suffix's s becomes ṣ; the form cakṣe. Since the suffix is nit, jñityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197 as read), the initial acute. Together with vi, as a gati-compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. ‖ 17 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.18)

शुनमन्धाय भरमह्वयत्सा वृकीरश्विना वृषणा नरेति । जारः कनीन इव चक्षदान ऋज्राश्वः शतमेकं च मेषान् ॥ १८ ॥

śunamandhāya bharamahvayatsā vṛkīraśvinā vṛṣaṇā nareti | jāraḥ kanīna iva cakṣadāna ṛjrāśvaḥ śatamekaṃ ca meṣān ‖ 18 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.18)

शुनम् । अन्धाय । भरम् । अह्वयत् । सा । वृकीः । अश्विना । वृषणा । नरा । इति । जारः । कनीनःऽइव । चक्षदानः । ऋज्रऽअश्वः । शतम् । एकम् । च । मेषान् ॥ १८ ॥

śunam | andhāya | bharam | ahvayat | sā | vṛkīḥ | aśvinā | vṛṣaṇā | narā | iti | jāraḥ | kanīnaḥ 'iva | cakṣadānaḥ | ṛjra 'aśvaḥ | śatam | ekam | ca | meṣān ‖ 18 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.18)

शुनमिति सुखनाम । भरं पोषणहेतुभूतं चक्षुरिन्द्रियेण निष्पाद्यं शुनं सुखमन्धाय दृष्टिहीनाय तस्मै ऋज्राश्वायेच्छन्ती सा वृकी हे अश्विनावह्वयत् । [कृष्णं ? — unreadable [?]] जगद्व्यप्नुवन्तौ वा वृषणा हे वृषणौ कामानां वर्षितारावित्येवं संबोध्य नरा नेतारावश्विनावह्वयत् । अह्वयन्त्यास्तस्याः कोऽभिप्राय इति चेत् तमुच्यते । कनीन इव यथा प्राप्तयौवनः कामुको जारः पारदारिकः सन् परस्त्रियै सर्वं धनं प्रयच्छति एवमृज्राश्वो मह्यं शतमेकं चैकोत्तरशतसंख्याकान्मेषान्पूर्वजननानां [?] स्वभूतानपहृत्य चक्षदानः कर्तनं कुर्वन् प्रादात् । तेनेदृशीं दुर्दशां प्राप्ता इति ॥ कनीनः । युवशब्दस्येष्मयुवल्पयोः कन्यन्यतरस्याम् (पा. ५-३-६४ [as read]) इति युवशब्दस्य कनादेशः । व्यत्ययेनेष्णः [?] आदेशः । यद्वा । कन दीप्तिकान्तिगतिषु । अस्मादौणादिक ईनप्रत्ययः ॥

śunamiti sukhanāma | bharaṃ poṣaṇahetubhūtaṃ cakṣurindriyeṇa niṣpādyaṃ śunaṃ sukhamandhāya dṛṣṭihīnāya tasmai ṛjrāśvāyecchantī sā vṛkī he aśvināvahvayat | [kṛṣṇaṃ ? — unreadable [?]] jagadvyapnuvantau vā vṛṣaṇā he vṛṣaṇau kāmānāṃ varṣitārāvityevaṃ saṃbodhya narā netārāvaśvināvahvayat | ahvayantyāstasyāḥ ko 'bhiprāya iti cet tamucyate | kanīna iva yathā prāptayauvanaḥ kāmuko jāraḥ pāradārikaḥ san parastriyai sarvaṃ dhanaṃ prayacchati evamṛjrāśvo mahyaṃ śatamekaṃ caikottaraśatasaṃkhyākānmeṣānpūrvajananānāṃ [?] svabhūtānapahṛtya cakṣadānaḥ kartanaṃ kurvan prādāt | tenedṛśīṃ durdaśāṃ prāptā iti ‖ kanīnaḥ | yuvaśabdasyeṣmayuvalpayoḥ kanyanyatarasyām (pā. 5-3-64 [as read]) iti yuvaśabdasya kanādeśaḥ | vyatyayeneṣṇaḥ [?] ādeśaḥ | yadvā | kana dīptikāntigatiṣu | asmādauṇādika īnapratyayaḥ ‖

Sense (editorial and tentative): "Śunam is a name for happiness (sukha). Bharam — a cause of nourishment; wishing for that blind Ṛjrāśva śunam — happiness to be produced through the sense of sight — she, the she-wolf (vṛkī), called (ahvayat) the Aśvins, O showerers (vṛṣaṇā) of desires, O leaders (narā), addressing them so. If one asks what was the idea of her who called — this is told: kanīna iva — as a young lover, a jāra, an adulterer, having attained youth, gives all his wealth to another man's wife, so Ṛjrāśva, taking away [from his own family's flock?] a hundred and one sheep belonging to himself, cutting [them] up (cakṣadānaḥ — doing the cutting), gave them to me; and because of that he came to such a wretched plight." Kanīnaḥ — the word yuvan, by the rule yuvālpayoḥ kan anyatarasyām (Pā. 5-3-64 as read), kan is substituted for yuvan; or, from the root kana dīptikāntigatiṣu, an auṇādika suffix īna.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.18) (Kannada, rendered)

Vṛṣaṇā — O givers of desired things; narā — O leaders; aśvinau — O Aśvins; bharam — nourishing; śunam — happiness (to be obtained through the eye); andhāya — for the blind (to give to Ṛjrāśva); sā vṛkī — that she-wolf; ṛjrāśvaḥ — Ṛjrāśva; śatam ekaṃ ca — a hundred and one (belonging to himself and to others); meṣān — sheep; kanīnaḥ — a youthful; jāra iva — like an adulterer (who gives all he has to another man's wife); cakṣadānaḥ — cutting up (for me) gave; iti — thus; ahvayat — called (you).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.18) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, you who are leaders and rainers of desires! Wishing the best happiness — the one attainable through the eye — for the blind Ṛjrāśva, that she-wolf called you: 'Ṛjrāśva, like a young adulterer who gives all his wealth to another man's wife, cut up for me a hundred and one sheep and gave them (and by that he has gotten into this wretched condition).'"

English Translation (as printed)

"(Desiring) that the enjoyment (arising from the perfection) of the senses (should be restored to the blind), the she-wolf invoked you, (saying), 'Aswins, showerers (of benefits), (leaders) of sacrifices), Rijraswa, (lavish) as a youthful gallant, (has given me) a hundred and one sheep, cutting them into fragments.'" The printed English has an unmatched parenthesis at "(leaders) of sacrifices)" [sic].

original p. 386

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 18)

Śunam — śunam iti sukhanāma: "The word śuna is stated among the twenty [as read] names of happiness (Ni. 3-11 [as read [?]]); hence the meaning is 'happiness'."

Bharam — poṣaṇahetubhūtaṃ cakṣurindriyeṇa niṣpādyaṃ sukham: "The word bhara is stated among the forty-six [as read] names of battle (Ni. 2-9 [as read [?]]), so it means 'war'. Here Sāyaṇa gives bhara the meaning 'the cause that gives nourishment'. Hence the word bhara is an adjective of śunam — 'the happiness that comes from the eye'."

Jāraḥ kanīna iva cakṣadānaḥ — yathā prāptayauvanaḥ kāmukaḥ pāradārikaḥ san parastriyai sarvaṃ dhanaṃ prayacchati evaṃ paurajanānāṃ svabhūtānapahṛtya meṣān śakalīkurvan prādāt: "As a lover who has attained youth, in love with another man's wife, gives all his wealth to his beloved, so Ṛjrāśva took the sheep that were the property of the townspeople (nāgarika), cut them up and gave them to the she-wolf, to be used as food." — Skandasvāmin, in explaining the word kanīna, deliberates: "[he first states the construction] jāraḥ kanīna iva vṛkī vṛṣaṇā narety ahvayat: the word kanīna does not mean 'a maiden'; since the word with that sense (kanyā) would not be here the thing to be described, the word kanīna, derived from the root kana which has the sense of kānti (desire, splendour), conveys the idea 'a lover (kāmayitā)'. Just as a paramour calls another man's wife with respect and with love, so the Aśvins' vehicle calls them 'Vṛṣaṇā' — 'givers of the desired things', and 'Narā' — 'proper guides', with respect." And [he adds that] since Ṛjrāśva knew that enmity with enemies would arise, he prepared food for the Aśvins' vehicle so as to have a protector of great power for himself; and that, cursed by his father, he came to blindness, and by the Aśvins' help he got his sight — the reason [for the narrative] is also described, he says; and he quotes the passage:

ऋज्राश्वो ह्योग्रैश्वर्यात् [?] पूर्वमेव ज्ञातेर्वा इयं वृकी अश्विनोः कशा समामाद्धीभूतस्य [?] मृके पितरि शत्रुभिः रुद्धस्य शत्रुजयं करिष्यतीति चक्षदानः । [as read; small type, several words doubtful [?]]

ṛjrāśvo hyograiśvaryāt [?] pūrvameva jñātervā iyaṃ vṛkī aśvinoḥ kaśā samāmāddhībhūtasya [?] mṛke pitari śatrubhiḥ ruddhasya śatrujayaṃ kariṣyatīti cakṣadānaḥ | [as read; small type, several words doubtful [?]]

— "such is the statement he quotes."

original p. 387

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 18; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read — no list entry)

Ahvayat — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, bhvādi; laṅ, third person singular, suffix tip; iteś ca, elision of the ī; śap as the vikaraṇa; vicchoyīvāyoḥ [as read [?]], ay substituted; the augment aṭ; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Narā — root nṛ nayane; ṛdor ap (Pā. 3-3-57 as read), suffix ap; on that account guṇa for the root-vowel; becomes r-final; since the suffix is pit, the root accent remains; with the dual au following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā substituted. Kanīnaḥ — the word yuvan; "very young" is kanīnaḥ: atiśayane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. 5-3-55 as read), the suffix iṣṭhan; it following, yuvālpayoḥ kan anyatarasyām (Pā. 5-3-64 as read), kan for the word yuvan; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85), the suffix's iṣṭhan gets ī-substitution [?]; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghām (Pā. 7-1-2), īn substituted for it; the form kanīna. Or the root kana dīptikāntigatiṣu, with the auṇādika suffix īna; by the suffix's initial acute, the middle acute accent. Cakṣadānaḥ — here the root kṣad [as read; cf. khad] is used in the sense of cutting into pieces; in the sense of laṭ, liṭaḥ kānaj vā (Pā. 3-2-106 as read), suffix kānac; on that account the root is doubled; halādiśeṣa for the reduplicative syllable, kuhoś cuḥ (Pā. 7-4-62), c; since the suffix is cit, ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163), the final acute. ‖ 18 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.19)

मही वामूतिरश्विना मयोभूरुत स्रामं धिष्ण्या सं रिणीथः । अथा युवामिदह्वयत्पुरन्धिरागच्छतं सीं वृषणाववोभिः ॥ १९ ॥

mahī vāmūtiraśvinā mayobhūruta srāmaṃ dhiṣṇyā saṃ riṇīthaḥ | athā yuvāmidahvayatpurandhirāgacchataṃ sīṃ vṛṣaṇāvavobhiḥ ‖ 19 ‖

original p. 388

मही । वाम् । ऊतिः । अश्विना । मयःऽभूः । उत । स्रामम् । धिष्ण्या । सम् । रिणीथः । अथ । युवाम् । इत् । अह्वयत् । पुरम्ऽधिः । आ । अगच्छतम् । सीम् । वृषणौ । अवःऽभिः ॥ १९ ॥

mahī | vām | ūtiḥ | aśvinā | mayaḥ 'bhūḥ | uta | srāmam | dhiṣṇyā | sam | riṇīthaḥ | atha | yuvām | it | ahvayat | puram 'dhiḥ | ā | agacchatam | sīm | vṛṣaṇau | avaḥ 'bhiḥ ‖ 19 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.19)

हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोर्मही महती ऊतिः पालनं मयोभूर्मयसः सुखस्य भावयित्री । उताशि [?] च हे धिष्ण्या । धिषणा स्तुतिलक्षणा वाक् । तयोस्तोतव्यौ [?] स्रामं व्याधिग्रस्तं पुरुषं विश्लिष्टाङ्गमत्र्यादिकं सं रिणीथः । संगतावयवं कुरुथः । अथापि च युवामिद्यवामेन [?] पुरन्धिर्बहुधीर्घोषा विश्पला वाह्वयत् रोगोपशमनार्थमाहूतवती ॥ हे वृषणौ कामानां वर्षितारावश्विनौ अवोभी रक्षणैः सहागच्छतम् । अभिमुख्येन सीमेनां प्राप्तवन्तौ ॥ मही । महती छान्दसो वर्णलोपः । यद्वा । महेरौणादिक इन् । कृदिकारादक्तिन इति ङीष् । मयोभूः । भवतेः क्विप् [?] … रिणीथः । री गतिरेषणयोः । क्र्यादिकः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् ॥

he aśvinau vāṃ yuvayormahī mahatī ūtiḥ pālanaṃ mayobhūrmayasaḥ sukhasya bhāvayitrī | utāśi [?] ca he dhiṣṇyā | dhiṣaṇā stutilakṣaṇā vāk | tayostotavyau [?] srāmaṃ vyādhigrastaṃ puruṣaṃ viśliṣṭāṅgamatryādikaṃ saṃ riṇīthaḥ | saṃgatāvayavaṃ kuruthaḥ | athāpi ca yuvāmidyavāmena [?] purandhirbahudhīrghoṣā viśpalā vāhvayat rogopaśamanārthamāhūtavatī ‖ he vṛṣaṇau kāmānāṃ varṣitārāvaśvinau avobhī rakṣaṇaiḥ sahāgacchatam | abhimukhyena sīmenāṃ prāptavantau ‖ mahī | mahatī chāndaso varṇalopaḥ | yadvā | maherauṇādika in | kṛdikārādaktina iti ṅīṣ | mayobhūḥ | bhavateḥ kvip [?] … riṇīthaḥ | rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ | kryādikaḥ | pvādīnāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam ‖

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, your (vām) great (mahī) protection (ūti) is mayobhūḥ — the producer of happiness (mayas). And, O dhiṣṇyā [possessing, through dhiṣaṇā, the speech of praise, the praise-worthy] — you two put right (saṃ riṇīthaḥ) the man (srāmam) stricken with disease, of dissevered limbs, [one] of the human kind (?) etc.: you make his parts joined. And moreover, purandhiḥ — the woman of many thoughts, Ghoṣā, or Viśpalā, called you for the sake of the cure of disease. O showerers of desires, Aśvins, come with avobhiḥ — with protections; ... [you] coming face-to-face reached her." The bhāṣya adds the grammar of mahī (mahat with Vedic loss of letter; or mahi with ṅīṣ), mayobhūḥ (bhū with kvip), riṇīthaḥ (rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ, kryādi; pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ) — characterized, not transcribed.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.19) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; vām — of you two; mahī — great; ūtiḥ — protection; mayobhūḥ — the maker of happiness; uta — and; dhiṣṇyā — O you who are to be praised with praise-words; srāmam — the one stricken with disease (of dissevered limbs — Atri and others) [as read]; saṃ riṇīthaḥ — you made whole in limbs; atha — and; yuvām it — you only; purandhiḥ — the woman of many thoughts (Ghoṣā, or [she] called Viśpalā); ahvayat — (for the cure of disease) called; vṛṣaṇau — O Aśvins, who give desired things; avobhiḥ — with protective works; sīm — to this Ghoṣā (Viśpalā); ā agacchatam — come.

original p. 389

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.19) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! Your great protection is the maker of happiness; O you who are to be praised with hymns! You made whole the limbs of the man stricken with disease (of dissevered limbs — Atri and others); the wise Ghoṣā (Viśpalā) called you alone (for the cure of disease). O you who give what is desired, to protect her, go to her."

English Translation (as printed)

"Aswins, your powerful protection is the source of happiness, worthy of laudation, you have made whole the maimed; therefore, has the intelligent (Ghosha) called upon you; showerers (of benefits), come hither with your succours"

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 19)

Purandhiḥ — bahudhīḥ ghoṣā viśpalā vā: "The word purandhi, which conveys many meanings, is used here, according to the statement of the Nirukta author — purandhir bahudhīḥ (Ni. 6-13 [as read [?]]) — in the sense of 'one of great knowledge'. The woman called Ghoṣā, and the woman called Viśpalā too, praised the Aśvins for the cure of their disease and obtained their protection; by this it is described here that their power is incomparable."

Vāṃ ūtiḥ mahī mayobhūḥ — "In this Ṛk it is stated that since the Aśvins show favour and protect, great happiness arises. For this reason the protection itself is described as the producer of happiness; and the praise of them too is the producer of health in the sick man."

Sīm — "The Nirukta author has explained the word sīm as 'inclusive' (parigraha) or 'an expletive' (padapūraṇa). He says: parigrahārthīyo vā padapūraṇo vā (Ni. 1-2 [as read])" and quotes:

प्र सीमादित्यो असृजद्विधर्ता ऋतं सिन्धवो वरुणस्य यन्ति । न श्राम्यन्ति न वि मुञ्चन्त्येते वयो न पप्तू रघुया परिज्मन् ॥ (ऋ. सं. २-२८-४ [as read])

pra sīmādityo asṛjadvidhartā ṛtaṃ sindhavo varuṇasya yanti | na śrāmyanti na vi muñcantyete vayo na paptū raghuyā parijman ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 2-28-4 [as read])

— "quoting this Ṛk, he explains sīm with the sense of its being a useless (anarthaka) [filler] … the fifth case [?]… sīmaḥ sīmantaḥ …, sīmā maryādā, visīvyati deśāv iti [as read [?]]" — and gives the explanation. Special Topics of Ṛk 19, continued

original p. 390

ब्रह्म जज्ञानं प्रथमं पुरस्ताद्वि सीमतः सुरुचो वेन आवः । (वा. सं. १३-३ [as read])

brahma jajñānaṃ prathamaṃ purastādvi sīmataḥ suruco vena āvaḥ | (vā. saṃ. 13-3 [as read])

"The word sīm is a word without meaning; it is an indeclinable (avyaya) used to complete the sentence — so he explains, and gives the example of pra sīm ādityaḥ, quoted above. He explains that in the sentence visīmataḥ suruco vena āvaḥ the word sīm too, like the word sīm [in the former], is without meaning, but it indicates 'limit' (maryādā, 'boundary')" — thus Skandasvāmin says:

स्रामशब्दः । द्वाभ्यां स्रामः स्वप्नाय अन्धं अधमाय बधिरम् (वा. सं. ३०-१०) इति पुरुषमेधमन्त्रेषु प्रयोगदर्शनात् काणवचनः । तं कक्षीवन्तं अन्धं त्रिकालविषयसर्वार्थविषयज्ञानप्रदानेन पालयन्तौ वां आहूतवतीं पुरन्धिं वध्रिमतीं हिरण्यहस्तप्रदानेन पालयन्ताविव्यर्थः [?] ॥ [as read; small type]

srāmaśabdaḥ | dvābhyāṃ srāmaḥ svapnāya andhaṃ adhamāya badhiram (vā. saṃ. 30-10) iti puruṣamedhamantreṣu prayogadarśanāt kāṇavacanaḥ | taṃ kakṣīvantaṃ andhaṃ trikālaviṣayasarvārthaviṣayajñānapradānena pālayantau vāṃ āhūtavatīṃ purandhiṃ vadhrimatīṃ hiraṇyahastapradānena pālayantāvivyarthaḥ [?] ‖ [as read; small type]

"The word srāma means 'blind', or 'deaf', for it is seen so used in the Puruṣamedha mantras [Vāj. Saṃ. 30-10]: by this, he gives the Aśvins, who gave the blind Kakṣīvat — to protect him — the eye that is the divine knowledge that sees things of the three times and all matters, which they gave to him; and he explains that they bestowed on Vadhrimatī [Purandhi], who called them, the golden-handed [son]."

"Srāma means blind or deaf; and the Aśvins gave to Kakṣīvat, who was blind, the sight so that he could act in worldly business, and not only that, they graciously gave him also the divine knowledge-producing intellect — an eye that sees what is possible in the three times: past, present and future." And quoting:

युवं नरा स्तुवते पज्रियाय कक्षीवते अरदतं पुरन्धिम् । (ऋ. सं. १-११६-७)

yuvaṃ narā stuvate pajriyāya kakṣīvate aradataṃ purandhim | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-7)

"— he quotes this Ṛk. And purandhi means 'one having much intelligence', Vadhrimatī: to show that she received from the Aśvins a golden-handed (hiraṇyahasta) son, he quotes:"

अजोहवीन्नासत्या करा वां महे यामन्पुरुभुजा पुरन्धिः । श्रुतं तच्छासुरिव वध्रिमत्या हिरण्यहस्तमश्विनावदत्तम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१३)

ajohavīnnāsatyā karā vāṃ mahe yāmanpurubhujā purandhiḥ | śrutaṃ tacchāsuriva vadhrimatyā hiraṇyahastamaśvināvadattam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-13)

"— he quotes this Ṛk."

original p. 391

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 19; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read — no list entry)

Mahī — root maha pūjāyām; in the sense of laṭ, suffix śatṛ; since it is ugit, in the feminine ugitaś ca, ṅīp; with mahat [as base], by Vedic usage the t is elided. Or: from the root maha, in sarvadhātubhyaḥ [as printed in sarvadhātubhya iN; Uṇ. sū. 4-118 as read [?]], the suffix in; with mahi [as base], in the feminine kṛdikārād aktinaḥ, ṅīṣ; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Ūtiḥ — ūtiyūtijūti… (Pā. 3-3-97 as read), the suffix ktin, the acute on the first syllable, formed irregularly. Aśvinā — supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā for the case ending; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19), the nighāta accent. Mayobhūḥ — mayasaḥ bhāvayitrī mayobhūḥ: when the causative sense is included, the root bhū [takes] kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76), the suffix kvip; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Dhiṣṇyā — supāṃ sulug, ā for the dual; the nighāta accent for an āmantrita. Riṇīthaḥ — root rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ, kryādi; laṭ, second person dual, thas; kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. 3-1-81), śnā vikaraṇa; snādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ (Pā. 7-3-80), shortening of the root; the suffix being apit by sārvadhātukam apit, ṅit; since it is hal-initial, ī halyaghoḥ (Pā. 6-4-113), ī for the ā of the śnā suffix; āṭ kuppvāṅ num [as read], ṇatva; the form riṇīthaḥ; since it stands after an ajanta, nighāta. Atha — nipātasya ca (Pā. 6-3-136 as read), in the Saṃhitā lengthening. Purandhiḥ — pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam (Pā. 6-3-109), by which the form is obtained. Agacchatam — root gam̐ḷ gatau; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta. Avobhiḥ — root av rakṣaṇe; sarvadhātubhya asun (Uṇ. sū. 4-188 as read [?]), the suffix asun; since it is nit, the initial acute; instrumental plural. ‖ 19 ‖

original p. 392

अधेनुं दस्रा स्तर्यं विषक्तामपिन्वतं शयवे अश्विना गाम् । युवं शचीभिर्विमदाय जायां न्यूहथुः पुरुमित्रस्य योषाम् ॥ २० ॥

adhenuṃ dasrā staryaṃ viṣaktāmapinvataṃ śayave aśvinā gām | yuvaṃ śacībhirvimadāya jāyāṃ nyūhathuḥ purumitrasya yoṣām ‖ 20 ‖

adhenum | dasrā | staryam | vi 'saktām | apinvatam | śayave | aśvinā | gām | yuvam | śacībhiḥ | vi 'madāya | jāyām | ni | ūhathuḥ | puru 'mitrasya | yoṣām ‖ 20 ‖

हे दस्रा दर्शनीयावश्विनौ विषक्तां विशेषेण सक्ताव यवां [?] कृशावयवामित्यर्थः । अके [?] इव स्तर्यं निवृत्तप्रसवां अधेनुमदोग्ध्रीं [?] एवंभूतां गां शयव एतत्संज्ञायर्षये पिन्वतम् । पयसा पूरयतम् । अपि च पुरुमित्रस्य पुरुमित्रो नाम कश्चिद्राजा । तस्य योषां कुमारीं शचीभिरात्मीयैः कर्मभिर्विमदायैतत्संज्ञायर्षये शत्रुभिः सह योद्धुमशक्ताय युवं न्यूहथुः । विमदस्य गृहं प्रापितवन्तौ ॥ [the grammar tail follows: staryam (stṛñ ācchādane, …, īkāra), viṣaktām (ṣañja saṅge, karmaṇi niṣṭhā, udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ…, nalopaḥ), apinvatam (pivi secane, bhvādi, īditaḥ), purumitrasya (puruṇi mitrāṇi yasya; saṃjñāyāṃ mitrājinayoḥ, Pā. 6-2-165 [as read]), bahuvrīhau pūrvapadāntodāttatvam — characterized, not transcribed]

he dasrā darśanīyāvaśvinau viṣaktāṃ viśeṣeṇa saktāva yavāṃ [?] kṛśāvayavāmityarthaḥ | ake [?] iva staryaṃ nivṛttaprasavāṃ adhenumadogdhrīṃ [?] evaṃbhūtāṃ gāṃ śayava etatsaṃjñāyarṣaye pinvatam | payasā pūrayatam | api ca purumitrasya purumitro nāma kaścidrājā | tasya yoṣāṃ kumārīṃ śacībhirātmīyaiḥ karmabhirvimadāyaitatsaṃjñāyarṣaye śatrubhiḥ saha yoddhumaśaktāya yuvaṃ nyūhathuḥ | vimadasya gṛhaṃ prāpitavantau ‖ [the grammar tail follows: staryam (stṛñ ācchādane, …, īkāra), viṣaktām (ṣañja saṅge, karmaṇi niṣṭhā, udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ…, nalopaḥ), apinvatam (pivi secane, bhvādi, īditaḥ), purumitrasya (puruṇi mitrāṇi yasya; saṃjñāyāṃ mitrājinayoḥ, Pā. 6-2-165 [as read]), bahuvrīhau pūrvapadāntodāttatvam — characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O dasrā, Aśvins worth seeing: viṣaktām — specially attached to [?], i.e. with wasted limbs [?]; staryam — one that had ceased to bear young; adhenum — one that does not give milk, [being] not a milch cow; such a cow (gām), for śayave — the ṛṣi of that name — you filled (apinvatam) with milk. And: Purumitra is the name of a king. His yoṣām — his maiden daughter — by your (śacībhiḥ) deeds, for vimadāya — the ṛṣi of that name, unable to fight with enemies — you two (yuvam) brought (ny ūhathuḥ) [as wife]; you delivered her to Vimada's house."
