॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.20) (Kannada, rendered)

Dasrā — O Aśvins, of beautiful appearance; viṣaktām — much emaciated [?]; staryam — barren (not bearing); adhenum — not giving milk; gām — (a cow's) cow; śayave — for the ṛṣi named Śayu; apinvatam — you made [her] full (with milk; made her like a milch cow); puru-mitrasya — of the king Purumitra; yoṣām — the daughter; yuvam — you two; śacībhiḥ — by your deeds of strength; vimadāya — to the one named Vimada; jāyām — as wife [you made]; ni ūhathuḥ — you joined (to his house).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.20) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Dasras! You made the cow of Śayu — very emaciated (and therefore barren) and not giving milk — one with a full udder; and you made the daughter of the king named Purumitra, by your power, the wife of Vimada."

English Translation (as printed)

"Dasras, you filled the milkless, barren, and emaciated cow of Sayu with milk; you brought, by your powers, the daughter of Purumitra, as a wife, to Vimda [sic]."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 20)

Viṣaktāṃ staryaṃ adhenuṃ gām apinvataṃ — viśeṣeṇa saktāvayavāṃ kṛśāvayavāṃ nivṛttaprasavām adogdhrīṃ gāṃ payasā apūrayatam: "A cow belonging to the one called Śayu was very weak, with thin legs [as read: kai-kāl, 'hands and feet']. Because its bodily condition was not right, it had become very emaciated and bore no young and gave no milk; the Aśvins treated it so that strength came to it, and made it give plenty of milk" — so Sāyaṇa explains. Skandasvāmin explains the same way and quotes:

शयवे चिन्नासत्या शचीभिर्जसुरये स्तर्यं पिप्यथुर्गाम् । (ऋ. सं. १-११६-२२)

śayave cinnāsatyā śacībhirjasuraye staryaṃ pipyathurgām | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-22)

— "he quotes this Ṛk." Special Topics of Ṛk 20, continued

original p. 394

Purumitrasya — puruṇi mitrāṇi yasya: "[Sāyaṇa] explains the meaning as 'one who has many friends (people of affection)'; or, he explains, it is the name of a certain king, Purumitra."

Vimadāya — vimadasaṃjñāya ṛṣaye śatrubhiḥ saha yoddhum aśakyāya: "A ṛṣi named Vimada, seeing that his wife had been carried off by the asuras and that he himself was unable to fight the enemies, was helped by the Aśvins, who brought her back and left her at Vimada's house. In the same way they helped the king named Purumitra and protected his daughter. The same idea is stated in Skandasvāmin's explanation":

यावर्भगाय विमदाय जायां सेनाजुवा न्यूहथू रथेन । (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१ [as read])

yāvarbhagāya vimadāya jāyāṃ senājuvā nyūhathū rathena | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-1 [as read])

"In this Ṛk only the matter of the protection of Vimada is told."

Śacībhiḥ — ātmīyaiḥ karmabhiḥ: "The word śacī is stated among the fifty-one names of speech (Ni. 1-11 [as read]), among the twenty-six names of action (Ni. 2-1 [as read]), and among the fourteen names of knowledge (Ni. 3-9 [as read]) [as read; numerals doubtful [?]]. Since this word has many meanings, here Sāyaṇa quotes:

विश्वमेको अभि चष्टे शचीभिर्भ्राजिरेकस्य ददृशे न रूपम् । (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-४४ [as read])

viśvameko abhi caṣṭe śacībhirbhrājirekasya dadṛśe na rūpam | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-44 [as read])

in which, as the Nirukta author has quoted it, śacībhiḥ is explained as karmabhiḥ — 'by deeds'; so here, too, the meaning for the word śacī is given as 'action'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 20; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Dasrā — supāṃ sulug, ā for the dual; nighāta accent for an āmantrita. Staryam — root stṛñ ācchādane; avitṛstṛtantribhya īḥ (Uṇ. sū. 4-158 as read [?]), the suffix ī; on that account guṇa for the root's ṛ-vowel; the word starī; when am follows, vā chandasi (as read) — the former savarṇa [dīrgha] being optional, here it does not occur; yaṇ substituted; the udātta standing in the place of the semivowel [?]; udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya (Pā. 8-2-4 as read), the svarita accent.

original p. 395

Viṣaktām — root ṣañja saṅge; in the passive sense niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 as read), suffix kta; anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (Pā. 6-4-24 as read), elision of the penultimate nasal; coḥ kuḥ (Pā. 8-2-30 as read), ku for the j when kta follows; khari ca (Pā. 8-4-55 as read), k; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49), the gati (vi) keeps its natural accent; in the feminine ṭāp, since it ends in a. Apinvatam — root pivi secane; idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-58 as read), num; since it belongs to the bhvādi group [and is pit], laṅ, second person dual; śap vikaraṇa; the augment aṭ; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda the nighāta does not occur; because aṭ is udātta, the initial acute. Vimadāya — root madī harṣaglepanayoḥ; since it belongs to the pacādi group, suffix ac; in the compound the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent; dative singular form. Purumitrasya — puruṇi (bahūni) mitrāṇi yasya saḥ purumitraḥ; saṃjñāyāṃ mitrājinayoḥ (Pā. 6-2-165 as read), in the bahuvrīhi compound the last member gets the final acute. Ūhathuḥ — root vaha prāpaṇe; liṭ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. ‖ 20 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.21)

युवं वृकेणाश्विना वपन्तेषं दुहन्ता मनुषाय दस्रा । अभि दस्युं बकुरेणा धमन्तोरु ज्योतिश्चक्रथुरार्याय ॥ २१ ॥

yuvaṃ vṛkeṇāśvinā vapanteṣaṃ duhantā manuṣāya dasrā | abhi dasyuṃ bakureṇā dhamantoru jyotiścakrathurāryāya ‖ 21 ‖

original p. 396

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.21)

युवम् । वृकेण । अश्विना । वपन्ता । इषम् । दुहन्ता । मनुषाय । दस्रा । अभि । दस्युम् । बकुरेण । धमन्ता । उरु । ज्योतिः । चक्रथुः । आर्याय ॥ २१ ॥

yuvam | vṛkeṇa | aśvinā | vapantā | iṣam | duhantā | manuṣāya | dasrā | abhi | dasyum | bakureṇa | dhamantā | uru | jyotiḥ | cakrathuḥ | āryāya ‖ 21 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.21)

आर्याय विदुषे । मनुषशब्दो मनुशब्दपर्यायः । मनुषाय मनवे मनोरर्थं हे दस्रा दर्शनीयावश्विनौ वृकेण लाङ्गलेन कर्षकैः कृष्टदेशे यवं यवाद्युपलक्षितं सर्वं धान्यजातं वपन्ता वापयन्तौ तथेषं अन्ननामैतत् तत्कारणभूतं वृष्ट्युदकं च दुहन्ता मेघात्क्षारयन्तौ तथा दस्युं उपक्षयकारिणमसुरपिशाचादिकं बकुरेण । बकुरो भासमानो वज्रः तेनाभि धमन्ता धमतिर्वधकर्मा अभिघ्नन्तौ एवं त्रिविधं कर्म कुर्वन्तौ युवामुरु विस्तीर्णं ज्योतिः स्वकीयं तेजो माहात्म्यं चक्रथुः । कृतवन्तौ दर्शितवन्तावित्यर्थः । यद्वा । त्रिविधकर्माचरणेनार्याय विदुषे मनवे विस्तीर्णं सूर्याख्यं ज्योतिश्चक्रथुः । कृतवन्तौ । जीवन् हि सूर्यं पश्यति । तदेतद्भूतानि त्रीणि कर्माणि युवाभ्यां कृतानीति भावः । अत्र निरुक्तं बकुरो भास्करो भयंकरो भासमानो द्रवतीति वा [?] । यवमिव वृकेणाश्विना वपन्ता वृको लाङ्गलं भवति विकर्तनात् इति । मनुषाय । मनेरौणादिक उषन्प्रत्ययः । (नि. ६-२६ [as read; compare p. 397]) ॥ [the grammar tail is characterized, not transcribed]

āryāya viduṣe | manuṣaśabdo manuśabdaparyāyaḥ | manuṣāya manave manorarthaṃ he dasrā darśanīyāvaśvinau vṛkeṇa lāṅgalena karṣakaiḥ kṛṣṭadeśe yavaṃ yavādyupalakṣitaṃ sarvaṃ dhānyajātaṃ vapantā vāpayantau tatheṣaṃ annanāmaitat tatkāraṇabhūtaṃ vṛṣṭyudakaṃ ca duhantā meghātkṣārayantau tathā dasyuṃ upakṣayakāriṇamasurapiśācādikaṃ bakureṇa | bakuro bhāsamāno vajraḥ tenābhi dhamantā dhamatirvadhakarmā abhighnantau evaṃ trividhaṃ karma kurvantau yuvāmuru vistīrṇaṃ jyotiḥ svakīyaṃ tejo māhātmyaṃ cakrathuḥ | kṛtavantau darśitavantāvityarthaḥ | yadvā | trividhakarmācaraṇenāryāya viduṣe manave vistīrṇaṃ sūryākhyaṃ jyotiścakrathuḥ | kṛtavantau | jīvan hi sūryaṃ paśyati | tadetadbhūtāni trīṇi karmāṇi yuvābhyāṃ kṛtānīti bhāvaḥ | atra niruktaṃ bakuro bhāskaro bhayaṃkaro bhāsamāno dravatīti vā [?] | yavamiva vṛkeṇāśvinā vapantā vṛko lāṅgalaṃ bhavati vikartanāt iti | manuṣāya | manerauṇādika uṣanpratyayaḥ | (ni. 6-26 [as read; compare p. 397]) ‖ [the grammar tail is characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "Āryāya — for the learned one. The word manuṣa is a synonym of the word manu: manuṣāya — for Manu, for the sake of Manu. O dasrā, Aśvins worth seeing, vṛkeṇa — with the plough (lāṅgala), in the ground ploughed by cultivators, sowing (vapantā) barley and all the kinds of grain indicated by barley; and iṣam (a name for food) — milking (duhantā) from the cloud the rain-water that is its cause; and dasyum — the destroyer, the asuras, piśācas and the like, bakureṇa — with the shining thunderbolt (bakura is the shining vajra), abhi dhamantā (dhamati has the sense of killing) — striking at them. Thus performing a threefold act, you cakrathuḥ made wide light — your own splendour, your greatness — showed it. Or: by the performance of the threefold act you made for the learned Manu the wide light called the Sun; for a living man sees the sun; these three acts have been done by you." On this the Nirukta [says]: "bakuro bhāskaro bhayaṅkaro bhāsamāno dravatīti vā; yavam iva vṛkeṇāśvinā vapantā; vṛko lāṅgalaṃ bhavati vikartanāt."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.21) (Kannada, rendered)

Dasrā aśvinā — O Aśvins, worth seeing; āryāya — for the knowing; manuṣāya — for Manu (for the man); vṛkeṇa — by the plough (in the ploughed earth); yavam — barley and the like grains; vapantā — having sown; iṣam — for [the sake of] food (the cause, the rain); duhantā — milking (from the clouds); dasyum — the cruel one (dasyu, piśāca and the like); bakureṇa — with the shining thunderbolt; abhi dhamantā — killing; uru — wide; jyotiḥ — (your) fame (the glory); cakrathuḥ — you made (you showed).

original p. 397

Pratipadārtha concluded "… abhi dhamantā — killing; uru — wide; jyotiḥ — (your) fame, glory; cakrathuḥ — you made. [Or: the three kinds of action — sowing, milking, and killing the dasyus — as stated above; uru — wide; jyotiḥ — sunlight; manuṣe — for Manu (for the human being); cakrathuḥ — you provided.]"

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.21) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, worth seeing! For the sake of knowing Manu, you sowed barley and other grains in the earth ploughed with the plough (the owner's land), made the rain, the cause of food, fall, and killed their destroyers; thereby you obtained wide fame (made food and killed the dasyus); you provided wide sunlight for the sake of man."

English Translation (as printed)

"Aswins, causing the barley to be sown (in the fields that had been prepared) by the plough; milking (the clouds) for the sake of Manu; destroying the Dasyu with the thunderbolt; you have bestowed brilliant light upon the Arya."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 21)

Manuṣāya — manuṣaśabdo manuśabdaparyāyaḥ | manave manor artham: "The word manuṣa conveys the same meaning as the word manu; hence it is a synonym of the word manu. In the Nirukta: manur mananāt (Ni. 3-48 as read [?]) — one who thinks, 'man'; so it means 'for man'."

Bakureṇa abhi dhamantā — bakuro bhāsamāno vajraḥ: "Here the Nirukta [says]:

बकुरो भास्करो भयङ्करो भासमानो द्रवतीति वा । (नि. ६-३७, ३८ [as read [?]]) यवमिव वृकेणाश्विना वपन्ता वृको लाङ्गलं भवति विकर्तनात् ।

bakuro bhāskaro bhayaṅkaro bhāsamāno dravatīti vā | (ni. 6-37, 38 [as read [?]]) yavamiva vṛkeṇāśvinā vapantā vṛko lāṅgalaṃ bhavati vikartanāt |

In the Nirukta the word bakura is explained with the meanings bhāskara — the sun — [and] bhayaṅkara — the fear-producer; prakāśa, shining; therefore, here Sāyaṇa explains it as 'a shining thunderbolt'. Vikartanāt — the word vṛka means 'the plough', because it tears the earth, or cuts it. The Aśvins did farming in the ground; and with its increase …" the paragraph continues on p. 398

original p. 398

Special Topics of Ṛk 21, continued "… the Aśvins did farming in the ground; and with the growth [of the crops, they caused] rain (the water) to fall; the thieves who steal the crop, and the like, they [struck] with weapons such as the thunderbolt and other fearsome arms, punishing them and protecting the men. By this, they make manifest among men their own supreme, great, and abundant glory — so Sāyaṇa explains. And by performing these three kinds of acts, they make for men the great light called the Sun — the light of both the worldly and the spiritual kind, so that the man may become ārya, 'worthy of worship'. And he gives another meaning: 'The Aśvins perform these three kinds of acts that are the cause of man's life, so that man may live, and, living, see the Sun.' Skandasvāmin, on this matter, quotes:

याभिर्नरा शयवे याभिरत्रये याभिः पुरा मनवे गातुमीषथुः । याभिः शारीराजतं स्यूमरश्मये ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-१६ [as read])

yābhirnarā śayave yābhiratraye yābhiḥ purā manave gātumīṣathuḥ | yābhiḥ śārīrājataṃ syūmaraśmaye tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-16 [as read])

and, having quoted this Ṛk: manuṣaśabdo 'tra manoḥ paryāyaḥ | manunāmno rājño 'ryāya — 'the word manuṣa is here a synonym of manu; for the king named Manu, the ārya': he explains that the second pāda of the Ṛk 1-112-16 also states this meaning. And:

युवामार्यस्यार्थाय वपनवृष्टिदोहनदस्युहननैस्त्रिभिः कर्मभिः महाप्रभावौ युवां साधूनामनुग्रहार्थं जातौ । अथवा अभि दस्युमिति दस्युशब्देन दुर्भिक्षमुच्यते । बकुरशब्देनात्र महान् वृष्ट्युदकसमूहः । ज्योतिश्शब्देनापि सुभिक्षमिति । महत्त्वात् भयंकरेण वृष्ट्युदकसमूहेन अभिघ्नन्तौ विस्तीर्णं सुभिक्षं कृतवन्तौ युवां आर्यस्यार्थाय ॥ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

yuvāmāryasyārthāya vapanavṛṣṭidohanadasyuhananaistribhiḥ karmabhiḥ mahāprabhāvau yuvāṃ sādhūnāmanugrahārthaṃ jātau | athavā abhi dasyumiti dasyuśabdena durbhikṣamucyate | bakuraśabdenātra mahān vṛṣṭyudakasamūhaḥ | jyotiśśabdenāpi subhikṣamiti | mahattvāt bhayaṃkareṇa vṛṣṭyudakasamūhena abhighnantau vistīrṇaṃ subhikṣaṃ kṛtavantau yuvāṃ āryasyārthāya ‖ [as read; small type, partly doubtful [?]]

"The Aśvins, by sowing the seed, by raining so that it grows, and by restraining those who would seize it, performing these three kinds of acts, are [beings] of great glory. They were born to protect the good, and to punish the wicked, and to protect and nourish disciples — for the protection of the Āryas, the venerable — he explains in this one way. And in another: by the word dasyu is meant famine (durbhikṣa, [or] drought); by the word bakura, abundant rain; by the word jyotis, good crops (subhikṣa): so, in times of famine (durbhikṣa), with the rain-water that is abundant, they make the rain fall in order that the rain should check the want of rain, and good crops should come about; and thus the Aśvins perform the work of protecting the good, destroying the famine — he gives yet another meaning."

original p. 399

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 21; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Vapantā — root ḍuvap bījasantāne; since it shows the action of a causer, it must be accepted as having the causative sense included; in the sense of laṭ, suffix śatṛ; śap vikaraṇa; with the dual au following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), ā for it; since it is ugit, num; anusvāra, parasavarṇa; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, by tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186 as read) the root's accent remains. Duhantā — root duha prapūraṇe; adādi; in the sense of laṭ, suffix śatṛ; adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. 2-4-72 as read), luk for śap; since the lasārvadhātuka follows after upadeśa, the nighāta [or anudātta] accent for the lasārvadhātuka does not occur; then the suffix's initial acute remains; since it is apit and so sārvadhātuka [and ṅit], [the root] is jit [?], so guṇa of the light penultimate of the root does not occur; as before, ā for the case ending; num. Manuṣāya — root mana jñāne; the auṇādika suffix uṣan; since it is nit, jñityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197 as read), the initial acute. Dasyum — root dasu upakṣaye, divādi; the auṇādika suffix yun. Dhamantā — the root dhanu [as read; cf. dhmā] is used here in the sense of killing; as before, in the sense of laṭ, śatṛ; case ending with ā; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the root accent remains; num for it, anusvāra, parasavarṇa. Āryāya — root ṛ gatau; ṛhalor ṇyat (Pā. 3-1-124 as read), suffix ṇyat; since it is ṇit, aco ñṇiti (Pā. 7-2-115 as read), vṛddhi of the ṛ-vowel; becoming r-final, the form ārya; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 as read), the initial acute; dative singular form. ‖ 21 ‖

original p. 400

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.22)

आथर्वणायाश्विना दधीचेऽश्व्यं शिरः प्रत्यैरयतम् । स वां मधु प्र वोचदृतायन्त्वाष्ट्रं यद्दस्रावपि कक्ष्यं वाम् ॥ २२ ॥

ātharvaṇāyāśvinā dadhīce 'śvyaṃ śiraḥ pratyairayatam | sa vāṃ madhu pra vocadṛtāyantvāṣṭraṃ yaddasrāvapi kakṣyaṃ vām ‖ 22 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.22)

आथर्वणाय । अश्विना । दधीचे । अश्व्यम् । शिरः । प्रति । ऐरयतम् । सः । वाम् । मधु । प्र । वोचत् । ऋतऽयन् । त्वाष्ट्रम् । यत् । दस्रौ । अपिऽकक्ष्यम् । वाम् ॥ २२ ॥

ātharvaṇāya | aśvinā | dadhīce | aśvyam | śiraḥ | prati | airayatam | saḥ | vām | madhu | pra | vocat | ṛta 'yan | tvāṣṭram | yat | dasrau | api 'kakṣyam | vām ‖ 22 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.22) small type; read with some doubts

तद्वां नरा सनये (ऋ. १-११६-१२ [as read]) इत्यत्रोक्तमाख्यानमिहाप्यनुसंधेयम् । हे अश्विनौ आथर्वणायाथर्वणः पुत्राय दधीचे दध्यञ्नाम्ने [?] महर्षये अश्व्यमश्वसंबन्धि शिरः प्रत्यैरयतम् । प्रत्यधत्तम् । तदीयं मानुषं शिरः प्रच्छिद्यान्यत्र विधायाश्वीयेन शिरसा तमृषिं समयोजयतमित्यर्थः । स च वां युवाभ्यां प्रवर्ग्यविद्यां मधुविद्यां च वक्ष्यामीति पुरा कृतां प्रतिज्ञां ऋतायन् सत्यमात्मन इच्छन् मधु मधुविद्यां त्वाष्ट्रं त्वष्टुरिन्द्राल्लब्धं प्र वोचत् । प्रोक्तवान् । हे दस्रौ दर्शनीयावश्विनौ वां युवयोः संबन्धि यदपि कक्ष्यं छिन्नस्य यज्ञशिरसः कक्षप्रदेशेन पुनःसंधानभूतं प्रवर्ग्यविद्याख्यं रहस्यं तदपि वां युवाभ्यां प्रावोचदित्यर्थः ॥ दधीचे । अञ्चतेरृत्विग्… [grammar tail: dadhīce (añcateḥ … kvin, anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti, nalopaḥ; cau; acaḥ, ī … udāttanivṛtti-svareṇa vibhaktyudāttatve prāpte, tasmāpavādena, añceś chandasi sarvanāmasthānayoḥ) — characterized, not transcribed]

tadvāṃ narā sanaye (ṛ. 1-116-12 [as read]) ityatroktamākhyānamihāpyanusaṃdheyam | he aśvinau ātharvaṇāyātharvaṇaḥ putrāya dadhīce dadhyañnāmne [?] maharṣaye aśvyamaśvasaṃbandhi śiraḥ pratyairayatam | pratyadhattam | tadīyaṃ mānuṣaṃ śiraḥ pracchidyānyatra vidhāyāśvīyena śirasā tamṛṣiṃ samayojayatamityarthaḥ | sa ca vāṃ yuvābhyāṃ pravargyavidyāṃ madhuvidyāṃ ca vakṣyāmīti purā kṛtāṃ pratijñāṃ ṛtāyan satyamātmana icchan madhu madhuvidyāṃ tvāṣṭraṃ tvaṣṭurindrāllabdhaṃ pra vocat | proktavān | he dasrau darśanīyāvaśvinau vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhi yadapi kakṣyaṃ chinnasya yajñaśirasaḥ kakṣapradeśena punaḥsaṃdhānabhūtaṃ pravargyavidyākhyaṃ rahasyaṃ tadapi vāṃ yuvābhyāṃ prāvocadityarthaḥ ‖ dadhīce | añcaterṛtvig… [grammar tail: dadhīce (añcateḥ … kvin, anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti, nalopaḥ; cau; acaḥ, ī … udāttanivṛtti-svareṇa vibhaktyudāttatve prāpte, tasmāpavādena, añceś chandasi sarvanāmasthānayoḥ) — characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "The story told at 'tad vāṃ narā sanaye' (Ṛ. 1-116-12 as read) is to be taken up here too. O Aśvins, to Dadhīca (Dadhyañc), the son of Atharvan, the great ṛṣi, you replaced (pratyairayatam) a horse's head: cutting off his human head and putting it elsewhere, you joined the ṛṣi with a horse's head — that is the meaning. And he, ṛtāyan — wishing truth for himself — spoke (pra vocat) to you the madhu, the honey-knowledge (madhuvidyā) received from Indra, the Tvāṣṭra [teaching], and the Pravargya knowledge — the promise he had made before: 'I shall tell you the Pravargya knowledge and the madhu-knowledge.' And, O dasrau, Aśvins worth seeing, the secret named Pravargya knowledge — which served for re-joining the cut-off head of the sacrifice at the kakṣa region — he told that too to you."

original p. 401

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.22) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; āthavarṇāya — to the son of Atharvan; dadhīce — to the great sage named Dadhyañc; aśvyam — belonging to a horse; śiraḥ — head; prati airayatam — (in the place of his [own head]) you joined; saḥ — he too; ṛtāyan — (to make his promise) true; vām — to you two; tvāṣṭram — received from Tvaṣṭṛ (by Indra); madhu — the knowledge of honey; pra vocat — taught; dasrau — O Aśvins; vām — your; yat — which; āpikakṣyam — [the secret] knowledge of joining the head at the kakṣa region (called Pravargya); (tat) api — that also; vām — to you; pra vocat — taught.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.22) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! You joined a horse's head to the sage Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan; and he, to make true his promise, taught you the honey-knowledge (madhuvidyā) received by him from Tvaṣṭṛ (Indra), and the secret knowledge called Pravargya, which joins the head at the kakṣa region."

English Translation (as printed)

"You replaced, Aswins, with the head of a horse, (the head of) Dadhyanch, the son of Atharvan, and true to his promise, he revealed to you the mystic knowledge which he had learned from Twashtri, and which was as a ligature of the waist to you."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 22)

"In this Ṛk, the account is told again — that the very secret honey-knowledge (madhuvidyā), taught by Indra, was taught to you [Aśvins] by the sage Dadhīca."

तद्वां नरा सनये दंस उग्रमाविष्कृणोमि तन्यतुर्न वृष्टिम् । दध्यङ् ह यन्मध्वाथर्वणो वामश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाच ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१२)

tadvāṃ narā sanaye daṃsa ugramāviṣkṛṇomi tanyaturna vṛṣṭim | dadhyaṅ ha yanmadhvātharvaṇo vāmaśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yadīmuvāca ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-12)

"In this Ṛk what was stated first is stated in a different way." Special Topics of Ṛk 22, continued

original p. 402

इच्छन्नश्वस्य यच्छिरः पर्वतेष्वपश्रितम् । तद्विदच्छर्यणावति ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-८४-१३)

icchannaśvasya yacchiraḥ parvateṣvapaśritam | tadvidaccharyaṇāvati ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-84-13)

"Ātharvaṇāya dadhīce āthavarṇaḥ putrāya dadhyañnāmne maharṣaye aśvasambandhi śiraḥ pratyairayetam pratyadhattam — the story is told thus: the Aśvins, cutting off the human head of the ṛṣi called Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, and joining a horse's head to him, taught him the honey-knowledge (madhuvidyā) given by Indra."

Tvāṣṭram — tvaṣṭur indrāl labdham: "The honey-knowledge was manifested by Indra himself — thus the greatness of the honey-knowledge and the secret of it are told." Skandasvāmin:

त्वष्टेत्यत्र इन्द्र उच्यते । शत्रूणां तनूकर्तृत्वात् । त्वाष्ट्रं यदिति अश्वशिरसो विशेषणं न ब्रह्मणः । युवाभ्यां शर्यणावति निहितं शत्रूणां तनूकर्त्रा इन्द्रेण दृष्टं यच्छिरः गुह्यमसि युवयोः ॥ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

tvaṣṭetyatra indra ucyate | śatrūṇāṃ tanūkartṛtvāt | tvāṣṭraṃ yaditi aśvaśiraso viśeṣaṇaṃ na brahmaṇaḥ | yuvābhyāṃ śaryaṇāvati nihitaṃ śatrūṇāṃ tanūkartrā indreṇa dṛṣṭaṃ yacchiraḥ guhyamasi yuvayoḥ ‖ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

"[He says that] the word tvāṣṭra yat is an adjective of the horse's head, not of brahma. The word tvaṣṭṛ means Indra: he who makes his enemies thin (tanūkaraṇa, destroys). Indra, having cut off the head of the ṛṣi Dadhīca, hid it where none should know (also from the Aśvins), and the Aśvins came to know the secret — so they explain. Sāyaṇa makes the word tvāṣṭram an adjective of the word kakṣyam: tvaṣṭur indrāl labdhaṃ — bhinnasya yajñaśiraḥ kakṣapradeśena punaḥsandhānabhūtaṃ pravargyavidyākhyaṃ rahasyam: 'the secret called the Pravargya knowledge, a re-joining of the cut head of the sacrifice at the kakṣa region; from Tvaṣṭṛ, Indra, [from] Indra, Dadhīca received the honey-knowledge. The Pravargya secret is what makes the broken head of the sacrifice rejoin.'"

Ṛtāyan — pravargyavidyāṃ madhuvidyāṃ ca vakṣyāmīti purā kṛtāṃ pratijñāṃ satyāṃ kartum icchan: "'To make true the promise made before: "I will teach you the Pravargya knowledge and the honey-knowledge"' — so Sāyaṇa takes the word ṛta in the sense of 'truth'. Skandasvāmin [says]: ṛtam ātmana icchan — [formed with] supa ātmanaḥ kyac [Pā. 3-1-8], the suffix kyac; pareccāyām …":

त्वं नस्सोम विश्वतो रक्षा राजन्नघायतः । न रिष्येत्त्वावतः सखा ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-९१-९ [as read [?]])

tvaṃ nassoma viśvato rakṣā rājannaghāyataḥ | na riṣyettvāvataḥ sakhā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-91-9 [as read [?]])

Iti yathā — "ṛtam [means] truth; and he says, tad eva brahma tad vāṃ yor icchan — 'wishing to teach you that very brahma (the knowledge of Brahman)': 'I shall teach you the Brahma-knowledge' — the meaning he explains."

original p. 403

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 22; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Ātharvaṇāya — atharvaṇaḥ apatyaṃ pumān ātharvaṇaḥ; tasyāpatyam (Pā. 4-1-92 as read), the suffix aṇ in the sense of "offspring"; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-117 as read), vṛddhi of the initial; an (Pā. 6-4-167 as read), prakṛtibhāva, so the elision of the ṭi part does not occur; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Dadhīce — dadhi as the upapada, the root añcu gatipūjanayoḥ, to it ṛtvigdadhṛk… (Pā. 3-2-59 as read), the suffix kvin; anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (Pā. 6-4-24 as read), elision of the penultimate nasal; dative singular with a following case ending, it has the name bha, so acaḥ (Pā. 6-4-138 as read), elision of the a of the root; cau (Pā. 6-3-138 as read), the preceding is lengthened when the root's añcu with elided n (an a-ending) follows; the case ending being anudātta, the udātta-vowel of the root having been elided, anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. 6-1-161 as read), the acute on the case ending is attained; this being excepted, cau (Pā. 6-1-222 as read), the acute on the former [syllable] is attained; but by the exception to that, añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam (Pā. 6-1-170 as read), the acute is again on the case ending. Aśvyam — aśvasya sambandhi aśvyam; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110), the suffix yat; yasyeti ca, elision of the a; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 as read), the initial acute. Airayatam — root īra gatau kampane ca; after the ṇijanta, laṅ, second person dual; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Vocat — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; luṅ, third person singular, suffix tip; iteś ca, elision of the ī; asyatiivakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ (Pā. 3-1-52 as read), aṅ substituted for cli; vaca um (Pā. 7-4-20 as read), the augment um …

original p. 404

Grammar of Ṛk 22, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Vocat (continued) — guṇa; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75 as read), the augment aṭ does not occur; the nighāta accent. Ṛtāyan — ṛtaṃ satyam ātmana icchatīti ṛtāyati; supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 as read), the suffix kyac in the sense of wishing; akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ (Pā. 7-4-25 as read), lengthening of the preceding because of kyac; after the kyajanta, in the sense of laṭ, the suffix śatṛ; by kyac's accent, the final acute. Tvāṣṭram — tvaṣṭuḥ labdham tvāṣṭram; tasyedam (Pā. 4-3-120 as read), the suffix aṇ; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-117 as read), vṛddhi of the initial; yaṇ substituted; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Dasrau — āmantritasya ca (Pā. 6-1-198 as read), the nighāta accent. ‖ 22 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.23)

सदा कवी सुमतिमा चके वां विश्वा धियो अश्विना प्रावतं मे । अस्मे रयिं नासत्या बृहन्तमपत्यसाचं श्रुत्यं रराथाम् ॥ २३ ॥

sadā kavī sumatimā cake vāṃ viśvā dhiyo aśvinā prāvataṃ me | asme rayiṃ nāsatyā bṛhantamapatyasācaṃ śrutyaṃ rarāthām ‖ 23 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.23)

सदा । कवी इति । सुऽमतिम् । आ । चके । वाम् । विश्वाः । धियः । अश्विना । प्र । अवतम् । मे । अस्मे इति । रयिम् । नासत्या । बृहन्तम् । अपत्यऽसाचम् । श्रुत्यम् । रराथाम् ॥ २३ ॥

sadā | kavī iti | su 'matim | ā | cake | vām | viśvāḥ | dhiyaḥ | aśvinā | pra | avatam | me | asme iti | rayim | nāsatyā | bṛhantam | apatya 'sācam | śrutyam | rarāthām ‖ 23 ‖

original p. 405

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.23)

हे कवी क्रान्तदर्शिनौ मेधाविनावश्विनौ वां युवयोः सुमतिं कल्याणीमनुग्रहात्मिकां बुद्धिं सदा सर्वदा चके । अभिमुख्येन प्रार्थये । मे मदीयानि विश्वा धियः सर्वाणि कर्माणि युवां प्रावतम् । प्रकर्षेण रक्षतम् । अपि चास्मभ्यं हे नासत्यावश्विनौ बृहन्तं महान्तमपत्यसाचमपत्यैः पुत्रादिभिः समवेतं श्रुत्यं प्रशंसनीयमुत्कृष्टं रयिं धनं रराथां प्रयच्छतम् । चके । कै गै शब्दे । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । लिट्युत्तमैकवचने रूपम् । अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगिति चतुर्थीबहुवचनस्य शेआदेशः । अपत्यसाचम् । अपत्यैः सह सचते संगच्छत इत्यपत्यसाच् । छान्दसो ण्विः । श्रुत्यम् । श्रुतिः स्तुतिः । तत्र भवं श्रुत्यम् । भवे छन्दसीति यत् । यतोऽनावः इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । रराथाम् । रा दाने । लोटि व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः ॥

he kavī krāntadarśinau medhāvināvaśvinau vāṃ yuvayoḥ sumatiṃ kalyāṇīmanugrahātmikāṃ buddhiṃ sadā sarvadā cake | abhimukhyena prārthaye | me madīyāni viśvā dhiyaḥ sarvāṇi karmāṇi yuvāṃ prāvatam | prakarṣeṇa rakṣatam | api cāsmabhyaṃ he nāsatyāvaśvinau bṛhantaṃ mahāntamapatyasācamapatyaiḥ putrādibhiḥ samavetaṃ śrutyaṃ praśaṃsanīyamutkṛṣṭaṃ rayiṃ dhanaṃ rarāthāṃ prayacchatam | cake | kai gai śabde | vyatyayenātmanepadam | liṭyuttamaikavacane rūpam | asme | supāṃ sulugiti caturthībahuvacanasya śeādeśaḥ | apatyasācam | apatyaiḥ saha sacate saṃgacchata ityapatyasāc | chāndaso ṇviḥ | śrutyam | śrutiḥ stutiḥ | tatra bhavaṃ śrutyam | bhave chandasīti yat | yato 'nāvaḥ ityādyudāttatvam | rarāthām | rā dāne | loṭi vyatyayenātmanepadam | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "O sages (kavī — far-seeing, wise Aśvins), I ever (sadā) seek (cake) your sumati — your good, favouring thought, face to face; O Aśvins, protect (prāvatam) all my (viśvā dhiyaḥ) works, strongly. And to us, O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, give (rarāthām) great (bṛhantam) wealth (rayim), accompanied by offspring (apatyasācam), worthy of praise (śrutyam)." Grammar: cake [from the root kai gai śabde, with the middle voice by vyatyaya; the first-person singular of the liṭ]; asme [supāṃ sulug, śe substituted for the dative plural]; apatyasācam [apatyaiḥ saha sacate saṃgacchata ity apatyasāc; Vedic ṇvi]; śrutyam [śrutiḥ stutiḥ; that which exists there; bhave chandasi, yat; yato 'nāvaḥ, initial acute]; rarāthām [root rā dāne; loṭ, middle by vyatyaya; bahulaṃ chandasi, ślu for śap].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.23) (Kannada, rendered)

Kavī — O far-seeing; aśvinā — O Aśvins; vām — your; sumatim — the mind of favour; sadā — always; ā cake — I pray; me — my; viśvā dhiyaḥ — all deeds; prāvatam — (you two) protect well; — and; asme — to us; nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; bṛhantam — great; apatyasācam — accompanied by sons and the like; śrutyam — praiseworthy (excellent); rayim — wealth; rarāthām — graciously give.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.23) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, knowers of the three times! I pray always for your graciously-disposed mind; protect all my works well; and, O Nāsatyas, graciously give us great wealth — accompanied by sons and the like, and praiseworthy."

English Translation (as printed)

"Sapient Aswins, I ever solicit your favour; protect all my religious duties, and grant, Nasatyas, abundant and excellent wealth, together with offspring."

original p. 406

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 23)

Kavī — krāntadarśinau medhāvināv aśvinau: "The word kavi is stated among the twenty-four names of the 'wise one' (medhāvin) (Ni. 3-19 [as read]); and:

विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुञ्चते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । वि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योऽनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥ (ऋ. सं. ५-८१-२)

viśvā rūpāṇi prati muñcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catuṣpade | vi nākamakhyatsavitā vareṇyo 'nu prayāṇamuṣaso vi rājati ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 5-81-2)

in this Ṛk the Nirukta author, [explaining] medhāvī kaviḥ krāntadarśano bhavati kavateḥ vā (Ni. 12-13 [as read]), has set down the word kavi among the synonyms of 'wise one' and so explained that kavi means medhāvin. And in viśvā rūpāṇi prati muñcate kaviḥ too, together with this meaning, he explains that the word kavi, derived from the root kava, conveys the meaning 'far-seeing'. Sāyaṇa also takes the word kavī as an adjective of the word aśvinā, and explains that the Aśvins are wise and thoughtful (vimarśakara)."

Apatyasācam — apatyaiḥ saha sacate saṃgacchate iti apatyasācam | apatyaiḥ putrādibhiḥ samavetam: "'accompanied by offspring, and the like' is the meaning."

"In this [Ṛk], the prayer is described: that the Aśvins, who are far-seeing, wise, and thoughtful, [as] the seer of the mantra, may produce for us favouring thoughts and blessings (maṅgala); that our minds should be so protected as to be right in all works; and that the Aśvins should grant us wealth, [of the kind] to be praised by all, together with sons, grandsons, and so on."

Rayim — dhanam: "The word rayi is stated among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೨-೩೪']) and also among the twenty-eight names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 [as read]). As Yāska explains — rayir iti dhananāma | rāter dānakarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 4-?? [as read]) — it is used here in the sense of wealth."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 23; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Sumatim — root mana jñāne; ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām (Pā. 3-3-174 as read), suffix ktic; the final acute. Cake — root kai gai śabde; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 as read), the middle voice; in the liṭ, first person singular, ṭa; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 as read), e for ṭi …

original p. 407

Grammar of Ṛk 23, continued … doubling of the root on that account; ādeca upadeśe 'śiti (Pā. 6-1-45 as read), since ā has come for the root, shortening of the reduplicative syllable, cutva; ato lopa iṭi ca (Pā. 6-4-64 as read), elision of the root's a; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Dhiyaḥ — root dhyai cintāyām; dhyāyateḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (Pā. 3-2-?? as read), the suffix kvip; on account of that connection, saṃprasāraṇa of the root; lengthening. Avatam — root av rakṣaṇe; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Asme — the word asmad; with the plural of the fourth case following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), śe substituted; since it is śit, anekālśit sarvasya (Pā. 1-1-55 as read), it replaces the whole; śeṣe lopaḥ (Pā. 7-2-90 as read), elision of the part up to ma. Nāsatyā — nabhrāṇnapāt…, irregular; supāṃ sulug, ā for the case ending; the nighāta accent for an āmantrita. Apatyasācam — apatyaiḥ saha sacate saṃgacchate iti apatyasāc; the Vedic ṇvi for the root sac in the group [?]; since it is ñit, ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116 as read), vṛddhi of the penultimate; in the compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent; accusative singular. Śrutyam — root śru śravaṇe; striyāṃ ktin, suffix ktin; śrutiḥ (hearing) is stuti; "what exists there" is śrutyam; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110), the suffix yat; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213), the initial acute. Rarāthām — root rā dāne; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 as read), the middle voice; loṭ, second person dual, āthām; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73 as read), ślu for śap; ślau (Pā. 6-1-10 as read), doubling of the root; hrasvaḥ [rule] shortens the reduplicative syllable; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 23 ‖

original p. 408

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.24)

हिरण्यहस्तमश्विना रराणा पुत्रं नरा वध्रिमत्या अदत्तम् । त्रिधा ह श्यावमश्विना विकस्तमुज्जीवस ऐरयतं सुदानू ॥ २४ ॥

hiraṇyahastamaśvinā rarāṇā putraṃ narā vadhrimatyā adattam | tridhā ha śyāvamaśvinā vikastamujjīvasa airayataṃ sudānū ‖ 24 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.24)

हिरण्यऽहस्तम् । अश्विना । रराणा । पुत्रम् । नरा । वध्रिऽमत्याः । अदत्तम् । त्रिधा । ह । श्यावम् । अश्विना । विऽकस्तम् । उत् । जीवसे । ऐरयतम् । सुदानू इति सुऽदानू ॥ २४ ॥

hiraṇya 'hastam | aśvinā | rarāṇā | putram | narā | vadhri 'matyāḥ | adattam | tridhā | ha | śyāvam | aśvinā | vi 'kastam | ut | jīvase | airayatam | sudānū iti su 'dānū ‖ 24 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.24)

रराणा रममाणौ दातारौ वा नरा नेतारौ हे अश्विनौ हिरण्यहस्तं नाम पुत्रं वध्रिमत्याः एतत्संज्ञायै ब्रह्मवादिन्यै अदत्तम् । प्रायच्छतम् ह । अपि च हे सुदानू शोभनदानावश्विनौ त्रिधा त्रेधा विकस्तं विच्छिन्नं श्यावाख्यमृषिं जीवसे जीवितुमुदैरयतम् । असुरैस्त्रेधा खण्डितं शरीरं पुनरेकीकृत्योदगमयतमित्यर्थः ॥ [grammar tail: rarāṇā (rā dāne, śānac, bahulaṃ chandasi, śapaḥ ślu, vyatyayena makārasyātvam, rāter vā vyatyayena śānac), vadhrimatyāḥ (caturthyarthe bahulaṃ chandasi ṣaṣṭhī), jīvase (jīva prāṇadhāraṇe; tumarthe se-sen-ase… suffix ase) — characterized, not transcribed]

rarāṇā ramamāṇau dātārau vā narā netārau he aśvinau hiraṇyahastaṃ nāma putraṃ vadhrimatyāḥ etatsaṃjñāyai brahmavādinyai adattam | prāyacchatam ha | api ca he sudānū śobhanadānāvaśvinau tridhā tredhā vikastaṃ vicchinnaṃ śyāvākhyamṛṣiṃ jīvase jīvitumudairayatam | asuraistredhā khaṇḍitaṃ śarīraṃ punarekīkṛtyodagamayatamityarthaḥ ‖ [grammar tail: rarāṇā (rā dāne, śānac, bahulaṃ chandasi, śapaḥ ślu, vyatyayena makārasyātvam, rāter vā vyatyayena śānac), vadhrimatyāḥ (caturthyarthe bahulaṃ chandasi ṣaṣṭhī), jīvase (jīva prāṇadhāraṇe; tumarthe se-sen-ase… suffix ase) — characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (mine): "Rarāṇā — rejoicing, or giving; narā — leaders; O Aśvins, to vadhrimatyāḥ — the brahmavādinī of that name — you gave a son called Hiraṇyahasta; and, O sudānū — fine givers, Aśvins, tridhā — in three parts — vikastam — cut up, the ṛṣi called Śyāva, you raised up, to live (jīvase) — that is, you made the body, which the asuras had cut into three parts, one again and raised him."

original p. 409

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.24) (Kannada, rendered)

Rarāṇā — givers (or: those fond of play); narā aśvinā — O leaders, O Aśvins; hiraṇyahastam — [one called] Hiraṇyahasta; putram — a son; vadhrimatyāḥ — to the woman Vadhrimatī; adattam ha — you gave (and); sudānū aśvinā — O Aśvins who give excellently; tridhā — in three parts; vikastam — cut up; śyāvam — the ṛṣi named Śyāva; jīvase — (again) so that he might live; ut airayatam — (joining the three pieces) you roused.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.24) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins who are givers [or: fond of play] and leaders! To Vadhrimatī you graciously gave a son called Hiraṇyahasta; and (in your generosity) you made Śyāva, who had been cut into three, join [together] again and live."

English Translation (as printed)

"Liberal Aswins, leaders (of sacrifices), you gave to Vadhrimathi her son Hiranyahasta; bounteous Aswins, you restored to life the triply-mutilated Syava."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 24)

"In Sāyaṇa's explanation: the woman Vadhrimatī was given by the Aśvins a son named Hiraṇyahasta. Hiraṇyahasta means — hiraṇyayau hastau yasya saḥ hiraṇyahastaḥ: because the hands (arms) wear ornaments of gold, the arm is called hiraṇyahasta; Skandasvāmin's explanation: 'the son with golden-formed hands'."

Vadhrimatyāḥ — "Sāyaṇa explains that the genitive (ṣaṣṭhī) has come in the sense of the dative (caturthī). Skandasvāmin gives the word as vadhrimatyai adhattam, taking it in the dative case itself, and explains it so. And the gift of Hiraṇyahasta is stated in the Ṛk:

श्रुतं तच्छासुरिव वध्रिमत्या हिरण्यहस्तमश्विनावदत्तम् । (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१३)

śrutaṃ tacchāsuriva vadhrimatyā hiraṇyahastamaśvināvadattam | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-13)

— as that is set forth in this Ṛk."

original p. 410

Special Topics of Ṛk 24, concluded Tridhā vikastaṃ śyāvaṃ jīvase udairayetam — "The asuras seized the ṛṣi called Śyāva and cut his body into three pieces; therefore the Aśvins, wishing to protect him, with a noble mind to give life, joined the three pieces of his body, healed him and made him live — this history is told here." Skandasvāmin:

श्यावं कुष्ठित्वात् श्याववर्णमग्नेः पुत्रस्य घोरस्य ज्येष्ठपुत्रं त्रिधा त्रिभिः प्रकारैः जङ्घयोर्मध्ये शिरसि च त्रिभिः प्रकारैः विनिधं [?] छिन्नम् ॥ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

śyāvaṃ kuṣṭhitvāt śyāvavarṇamagneḥ putrasya ghorasya jyeṣṭhaputraṃ tridhā tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ jaṅghayormadhye śirasi ca tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ vinidhaṃ [?] chinnam ‖ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

"The eldest son of Ghora, the son of Agni, was of altered appearance, dark-skinned from leprosy; in order to make him healthy, the Aśvins cut his body variously at the shank and head, treated him, and protected him — so he explains the meaning." And he quotes:

युवं श्यावाय रुशतीमदत्तं महः क्षोणस्याश्विना कण्वाय । प्रवाच्यं तद्वृषणा कृतं वां यन्नार्षदाय श्रवो अध्यधत्तम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११७-८)

yuvaṃ śyāvāya ruśatīmadattaṃ mahaḥ kṣoṇasyāśvinā kaṇvāya | pravācyaṃ tadvṛṣaṇā kṛtaṃ vāṃ yannārṣadāya śravo adhyadhattam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-117-8)

and this Ṛk:

याभिः शचीभिर्वृषणा परावृजं प्रान्धं श्रोणं चक्षस एतवे कृथः । याभिर्वर्तिकां ग्रसितामुमुञ्चतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-८)

yābhiḥ śacībhirvṛṣaṇā parāvṛjaṃ prāndhaṃ śroṇaṃ cakṣasa etave kṛthaḥ | yābhirvartikāṃ grasitāmumuñcataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-8)

"In these the wonderful deeds that the Aśvins perform are stated, and it is described that their power is infinite."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 24; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Hiraṇyahastam — hiraṇyaṃ haste yasya saḥ hiraṇyahastaḥ; in the bahuvrīhi, prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 as read), the former member keeps its natural accent. Rarāṇā — root ramu krīḍāyām; laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe (Pā. 3-2-124 as read), the suffix śānac; bahulaṃ chandasi, ślu for śap; ślau, doubling of the root; rerām + āna — by vyatyaya, a for the m [?]; āṭ kuppvāṅ…, ṇatva for the n — or on the earlier [view]: root rā dāne; vyatyayena śānac; ślu vikaraṇa; doubling of the root; by abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189 as read) the initial acute; supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā for the case ending (au).

original p. 411

Vadhrimatyāḥ — since the sense of the fourth case is meant, bahulaṃ chandasi, the sixth case has come; in the place of the udātta, yaṇ substituted, after which a case ending has come, udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (Pā. 6-1-174 as read), the acute on the case ending. Adattam — root dudāñ dāne; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Tridhā — saṅkhyāyā vidhārthe dhā (Pā. 5-3-42 as read), the suffix dhā in the sense of "kind, manner". Vikastam — root kasa gatau; in the passive sense niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 as read), the suffix kta; gatir anantaraḥ, the gati keeps its natural accent. Jīvase — root jīva prāṇadhāraṇe; since the sense of the infinitive is meant, tumarthe se-sen-ase… (Pā. 3-4-9 as read), the suffix ase; kṛn mejantaḥ (Pā. 1-1-39 as read), because it is a kṛdanta ending in e [?], it is indeclinable; by the suffix's initial acute, the middle-acute form arises. ‖ 24 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.25)

एतानि वामश्विना वीर्याणि प्र पूर्व्याण्यायवो वोचन् । ब्रह्म कृण्वन्तो वृषणा युवभ्यां सुवीरासो विदथमा वदेम ॥ २५ ॥

etāni vāmaśvinā vīryāṇi pra pūrvyāṇyāyavo vocan | brahma kṛṇvanto vṛṣaṇā yuvabhyāṃ suvīrāso vidathamā vadema ‖ 25 ‖

original p. 412

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 117.25) The printed Pada reads "yuvaḥbhyām" with an avagraha — as printed.

एतानि । वाम् । अश्विना । वीर्याणि । प्र । पूर्व्याणि । आयवः । अवोचन् । ब्रह्म । कृण्वन्तः । वृषणा । युवःऽभ्याम् । सुऽवीरासः । विदथम् । आ । वदेम ॥ २५ ॥

etāni | vām | aśvinā | vīryāṇi | pra | pūrvyāṇi | āyavaḥ | avocan | brahma | kṛṇvantaḥ | vṛṣaṇā | yuvaḥ 'bhyām | su 'vīrāsaḥ | vidatham | ā | vadema ‖ 25 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 117.25)

हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोः संबन्धीनि पूर्व्याणि प्रत्नान्येतानीदानीमयोक्तानि [?] वीर्याणि वीरकर्माण्यायवो मनुष्या मदीयाः पित्रादयः प्रावोचन् । उक्तवन्तः । वयं च हे वृषणा कामानामभिवर्षकावश्विनौ युवाभ्यां ब्रह्म मन्त्रात्मकं स्तोत्रं कृण्वन्तः कुर्वन्तः सुवीरासः सुवीराः शोभनवीर्यैः पुत्रादिभिरुपेताः सन्तो विदथं यज्ञमावदेम । अभिमुख्येन स्तुतीरुच्चारयामः । यद्वा । विदथं वेदयन्तमतिथिं तदेवेक्षितप्रदानेना [?] वदेम । अभिमुख्येन प्रियपूर्विकां वाचमुच्चारयामः ॥ कृण्वन्तः । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । इदित्त्वान्नुम् । लटः शतृ । धिन्विकृण्व्योर च (पा. ३-१-८० [as read]) इत्युप्रत्ययः । अकारान्तादेशश्च । अतो लोपे सति स्थानिवद्भावाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । सुवीरासः । शोभना वीरा येषां ते तथोक्ताः । आज्जसेरसुक् । वीरवीर्ये चेत्यादिना [?] क्तपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । विदथम् । विद ज्ञाने । रुविदिभ्यां किदिक्ष्यथप्रत्ययः [?] ॥

he aśvinau vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhīni pūrvyāṇi pratnānyetānīdānīmayoktāni [?] vīryāṇi vīrakarmāṇyāyavo manuṣyā madīyāḥ pitrādayaḥ prāvocan | uktavantaḥ | vayaṃ ca he vṛṣaṇā kāmānāmabhivarṣakāvaśvinau yuvābhyāṃ brahma mantrātmakaṃ stotraṃ kṛṇvantaḥ kurvantaḥ suvīrāsaḥ suvīrāḥ śobhanavīryaiḥ putrādibhirupetāḥ santo vidathaṃ yajñamāvadema | abhimukhyena stutīruccārayāmaḥ | yadvā | vidathaṃ vedayantamatithiṃ tadevekṣitapradānenā [?] vadema | abhimukhyena priyapūrvikāṃ vācamuccārayāmaḥ ‖ kṛṇvantaḥ | kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca | idittvānnum | laṭaḥ śatṛ | dhinvikṛṇvyora ca (pā. 3-1-80 [as read]) ityupratyayaḥ | akārāntādeśaśca | ato lope sati sthānivadbhāvāllaghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ | suvīrāsaḥ | śobhanā vīrā yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ | ājjaserasuk | vīravīrye cetyādinā [?] ktapadādyudāttatvam | vidatham | vida jñāne | ruvidibhyāṃ kidikṣyathapratyayaḥ [?] ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, these (etāni) — your ancient (pūrvyāṇi) heroic deeds (vīryāṇi), just now told, the men (āyavaḥ) — my fathers and others — recounted (pra avocan). And we too, O showerers (vṛṣaṇā) of desires, Aśvins, composing for you a hymn in the form of mantra (brahma), being possessed of good heroes (suvīrāsaḥ) — sons and others of fine valour — would speak (ā vadema) at the sacrifice (vidatham): we utter praises face to face. Or: to the guest who makes known the sacrifice (?) [as read [?]]: we utter words preceded by what is dear, face to face." Grammar: kṛṇvantaḥ (root kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca; since it is it, num; laṭ, śatṛ; dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca, suffix u, and a substituted for the final) …; suvīrāsaḥ (śobhanā vīrā yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ; āj jaser asuk) …; vidatham (vida jñāne; suffix [athan?] [?]) — characterized, not transcribed.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 117.25) (Kannada, rendered)

He aśvinā — O Aśvins; vām — of you two; pūrvyāṇi — ancient; etāni — these (told by me); vīryāṇi — heroic deeds; āyavaḥ — (our fathers and others) men; pra avocan — have described; vayaṃ ca — we too; he vṛṣaṇā — O Aśvins, rainers of desired things; yuvabhyām [as printed] — for you two; brahma — a hymn in the form of mantra; kṛṇvantaḥ — making; suvīrāsaḥ — accompanied by sons and the like, [who are] heroes; vidatham — the sacrifice (in the sacrifice, the guest who is learned); ā vadema — addressing, let us utter (praise-words) (honouring [him], let us speak dear words).

original p. 413

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 117.25) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! These adventurous deeds of yours (told above) have been described by our ancestors; and we too, O Nāsatyas, bestowers of desired things, composing a hymn in the form of mantra, with excellent sons, let us utter these praise-words in the sacrifices (honouring the guests who are learned and speaking dear words)."

English Translation (as printed)

"These, your ancient exploits, Aswins, our forefathers have celebrated, and we offer adoration to you, showerers (of benefits), repeating your praises, accompanied by our dependants."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 25)

Pūrvyāṇi — pratnāni: "The word pūrvya is stated among the six names of 'ancient' (Ni. 3-20 [as in the earlier occurrence]). The meaning is: that which happened a long, long time ago. The deeds that the Aśvins have performed from very ancient times are many; our forefathers have praised them a great deal. They are also fit for us to praise, so it is said here. The Aśvins fulfil the desires of those who praise them. Therefore we, offering mantras in the form of praise to them, with excellent sons and grandsons and so on, uttering exceeding praise for the sake of the Aśvins, pray that we may obtain their favour."

अथवा विदथं वेदयन्तमतिथिं तदेवेक्षितप्रदानेना [?] वदेम अभिमुख्येन प्रियपूर्विकां वाचमुच्चारयामः ।

athavā vidathaṃ vedayantamatithiṃ tadevekṣitapradānenā [?] vadema abhimukhyena priyapūrvikāṃ vācamuccārayāmaḥ |

"To a guest who knows the greatness of the Aśvins, by giving him whatever is desired, or by fulfilling his wishes, we shall ever speak to him words that bring welfare — thus the favour of the Aśvins is wished for here" — so it is described.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 25; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Āvocan [read avocan] — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; luṅ, third person plural, the suffix jhi; jhoʼntaḥ [as printed jhonta; Pā. 7-1-3 as read], ant substituted; iteś ca, elision of the ī; asyatiivakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ (Pā. 3-1-52 as read), aṅ substituted for cli; vaca um (Pā. 7-4-20 as read), the augment um for the root; the augment aṭ; tiṅanta nighāta accent.

original p. 414

Grammar of Ṛk 25, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Kṛṇvantaḥ — root kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca; idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-58 as read), num for the root; in the sense of laṭ, the suffix śatṛ; dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca (Pā. 3-1-80 as read), the suffix u; a is substituted for the root's final; ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48 as read), elision of the a because of u; aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ…, acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau (Pā. 1-1-57 as read), by the sthānivadbhāva the guṇa of the root's light penultimate, on account of u, does not occur; the word kṛṇvat; in the first case, plural, with jas following, since it is ugit, num. Yuvabhyām — since prathamāyāś ca dvivacane bhāṣāyām is stated [for] the common language only, the a substitution does not occur here. Suvīrāsaḥ — śobhanā vīrā yeṣāṃ te suvīrāsaḥ; with jas following, āj jaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50 as read), the augment asuk for it; vīravīryau ca (Pā. 6-2-120 as read), the final member gets the initial acute. Vidatham — root vida jñāne; ruvidibhyāṃ kit [as read; kithat?], the suffix atha; since it is "as kit", guṇa of the root's light penultimate does not occur; by the suffix's initial acute, the middle acute accent. Vadema — root vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci; vidhiliṅ, first person plural; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 25 ‖

Colophon (Kannada, as printed): "nūrahadinēḷaneya sūktavu mugidudu" — "The hundred-and-seventeenth Sūkta is ended."

Sūkta 118 — "ā vāṃ ratho aśvinā śyenapatvā"

original p. 415

Heading (Kannada): "nūrahadineṇṭaneya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-eighteenth Sūkta."

Anukramaṇī (Sanskrit, as printed):

आ वामेकादशर्चं शैतीयं [?] सूक्तं कक्षीवत आर्षं त्रैष्टुभमाश्विनम् । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । आ वामेकादशेति ॥ पूर्वसूक्ताभ्यां सह प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरुक्तो विनियोगः ॥

ā vāmekādaśarcaṃ śaitīyaṃ [?] sūktaṃ kakṣīvata ārṣaṃ traiṣṭubhamāśvinam | tathā cānukrāntam | ā vāmekādaśeti ‖ pūrvasūktābhyāṃ saha prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorukto viniyogaḥ ‖

Sense: "ā vām — a sūkta of eleven Ṛks, the [third (?) — printed śaitīyam [?]] sūkta; of the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān, Triṣṭubh, addressed to the Aśvins. The Anukramaṇī says 'ā vām ekādaśa'. Its application, together with the two preceding sūktas, is stated in the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvina-śastra."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "This sūkta, ā vāṃ rathaḥ, is the third sūkta in the seventeenth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is the one called Kakṣīvān. The deities are the Aśvins. The metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said 'ā vām ekādaśa', beginning thus. At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, the use of this sūkta, together with the preceding sūktas, is for the recitation of the Aśvina-śastra mantras."

सूक्त—११८ (Sūkta 118) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१७ ॥ सूक्त—११८ ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—small numerals; read "19, 20" — as printed [?] ॥ Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Ṛṣi: Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. Devatā: the Aśvins. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.1)

आ वां रथो अश्विना श्येनपत्वा सुमृळीकः स्ववाँ यात्वर्वाङ् । यो मर्त्यस्य मनसो जवीयान्त्रिवन्धुरो वृषणा वातरंहाः ॥ १ ॥

ā vāṃ ratho aśvinā śyenapatvā sumṛḷīkaḥ svavā~ yātvarvāṅ | yo martyasya manaso javīyāntrivandhuro vṛṣaṇā vātaraṃhāḥ ‖ 1 ‖

original p. 416

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.1)

आ । वाम् । रथः । अश्विना । श्येनऽपत्वा । सुऽमृळीकः । स्वऽवान् । यातु । अर्वाक् । यः । मर्त्यस्य । मनसः । जवीयान् । त्रिऽबन्धुरः । वृषणा । वातऽरंहाः ॥ १ ॥

ā | vām | rathaḥ | aśvinā | śyena 'patvā | su 'mṛḷīkaḥ | sva 'vān | yātu | arvāk | yaḥ | martyasya | manasaḥ | javīyān | tri 'bandhuraḥ | vṛṣaṇā | vāta 'raṃhāḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.1) small type; read with some doubts

हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोः स्वभूतो रथोऽर्वाजस्सदभिमुखमा यातु [?] । आगच्छतु । कीदृशो रथः । श्येनपत्वा श्येन इत्येतदश्वनाम [?] शंसनीयगमनैरश्वैः पतन् गच्छन् । यद्वा । श्येनः पक्षी स इव शीघ्रं पतन् । सुमृळीकः शोभनसुखयुक्तः स्ववान् धनवान् । हे वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारावश्विनौ यो युष्मदीयो रथो मर्त्यस्य मनुष्यस्य मनसो जवीयानतिशयेन वेगवान् । तद्यथा वेगेन कृत्स्नं जगद्व्याप्नोति । ततोऽप्यतिशयेन क्षणमात्रादेव सर्वं जगत्पर्येटतीत्यर्थः । त्रिबन्धुरः । बन्धुरं वेष्टितं सारथेः स्थानं । त्रिप्रकारेण बन्धुरेण युक्तः । वातरंहा वातस्य वायो रंहा वेग इव वेगो यस्य स तथोक्तः । अनेनाप्रतिहतगतित्वमुच्यते । स रथ इति पूर्वार्धान्वयः ॥ श्येनपत्वा । पत्लृ गतौ । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति वनिप् । दासीभारादि [?] ॥ [grammar tail: śyenapatvā, javīyān (atiśāyanike īyasun, vinmatorluk, ṭer iti ṭilopaḥ), trivandhuraḥ (bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam), … — characterized, not transcribed]

he aśvinau vāṃ yuvayoḥ svabhūto ratho 'rvājassadabhimukhamā yātu [?] | āgacchatu | kīdṛśo rathaḥ | śyenapatvā śyena ityetadaśvanāma [?] śaṃsanīyagamanairaśvaiḥ patan gacchan | yadvā | śyenaḥ pakṣī sa iva śīghraṃ patan | sumṛḷīkaḥ śobhanasukhayuktaḥ svavān dhanavān | he vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣitārāvaśvinau yo yuṣmadīyo ratho martyasya manuṣyasya manaso javīyānatiśayena vegavān | tadyathā vegena kṛtsnaṃ jagadvyāpnoti | tato 'pyatiśayena kṣaṇamātrādeva sarvaṃ jagatparyeṭatītyarthaḥ | tribandhuraḥ | bandhuraṃ veṣṭitaṃ sāratheḥ sthānaṃ | triprakāreṇa bandhureṇa yuktaḥ | vātaraṃhā vātasya vāyo raṃhā vega iva vego yasya sa tathoktaḥ | anenāpratihatagatitvamucyate | sa ratha iti pūrvārdhānvayaḥ ‖ śyenapatvā | patlṛ gatau | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti vanip | dāsībhārādi [?] ‖ [grammar tail: śyenapatvā, javīyān (atiśāyanike īyasun, vinmatorluk, ṭer iti ṭilopaḥ), trivandhuraḥ (bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam), … — characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, may your own chariot come (ā yātu) arvāk — turned towards us. What kind of chariot? Śyenapatvā — flying, going with praiseworthily-moving horses [as read; the name for horses is śyena [?]]; or, 'flying swiftly like the śyena bird.' Sumṛḷīkaḥ — endowed with fine comfort; svavān — rich. O vṛṣaṇā, rainers of desires, Aśvins, your chariot which is javīyān — swifter than the manas of a mortal (martya, man), exceedingly speedy: as [the mind] pervades the whole world by speed, still more speedily — within a moment — it goes round the world. Trivandhuraḥ — bandhura is the enclosed seat of the charioteer; having it in three forms. Vātaraṃhāḥ — he whose speed (raṃhas) is like the speed of the wind; by this its unobstructed course is told. 'That chariot' is the connection with the first half."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.1) (Kannada, rendered)

He vṛṣaṇā — O Aśvins, rainers of desired things; yaḥ — which your chariot; martyasya — of a man; manasaḥ — than the mind; javīyān — more speedy; trivandhuraḥ — [that] has the three-fold seat of the charioteer; vātaraṃhāḥ — like the wind (of unobstructed) pace; he aśvinā — O Aśvins; saḥ — that [saḥ = sa]; vām — of you two; śyenapatvā — that flies by good horses (like a bird); sumṛḷīkaḥ — comfort-endowed; svavān — wealthy; rathaḥ — that chariot; arvāk — (to us) facing; ā yātu — let it come.

original p. 417

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.1) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, rainers of desires! May your chariot — swifter than the mind's speed, with unobstructed course like the wind, with good horses (flying like a bird), with the three-fold seat of the charioteer — come, endowed with comfort and wealth, face to face with us."

English Translation (as printed)

"May your elegant and rich car, swift as a hawk, come, Ashwins, to our presence, for it is as quick as the mind of man, surmounted, showerers (of benefits), by three columns, and rapid as the wind."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 1)

Śyenapatvā — śaṃsanīyagamanair aśvaiḥ patan gacchan | yadvā śyenaḥ pakṣī sa iva śīghraṃ patan: "The word śyena is stated among the [number as read] names of horses (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೩೨'?]).

नीचायमानं जसुरिं न श्येनं श्रवश्चाच्छा पशुमच्च यूथम् । (ऋ. सं. ४-३९-२ [as read [?]])

nīcāyamānaṃ jasuriṃ na śyenaṃ śravaścācchā paśumacca yūtham | (ṛ. saṃ. 4-39-2 [as read [?]])

In this Ṛk the word śyena means 'a bird (hawk)': śyenaḥ śaṃsanīyaṃ gacchati (Ni. 4-?? [as read]) — it flies very swiftly; like it, a chariot with horses that move quickly is meant. For this reason Sāyaṇa explains the course of this chariot as exceedingly praiseworthy."

Martyasya manaso javīyān — atiśayena vegavān: "Like the mind of a man, that pervades the whole of the world with great speed, [the chariot] with speed greater than that — it travels, he means, round the worlds in a moment."

Vātaraṃhāḥ — vātasya vāyor raṃho vega iva vego yasya: "Its speed is like the speed of the wind: the chariot goes with great speed and pervades everything — that is the meaning."

"In this Ṛk the chariot of the Aśvins is described: moving very fast like birds, yoked with horses fit for that; having the speed of mind; and, by the speed of the wind, going round all worlds in a moment — thus the speed of the chariot is also described."

original p. 418

Special Topics of Ṛk 1, concluded Trivandhuraḥ — bandhuraṃ veṣṭitaṃ sārathe sthānam | triprakāreṇa bandhureṇa yuktaḥ: "The chariot is described as having a charioteer's seat (bandhura) enclosed with [boards of] three kinds. Skandasvāmin explains the meaning: tribandhuraḥ trisārathisthānaḥ — in the chariot of the Aśvins there are three seats for the seating of the charioteer."

Sumṛḷīkaḥ — susukhaḥ: "The meaning is: 'one that gives much comfort'. The Nirukta author quotes:

गामश्वं पोषयित्नु स नो मृळातीदृशे ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-५२-१ [as read [?]]) मधुश्च्युतं घृतमिव सुपूतमृतस्य नः पतयो मृळयन्तु ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-५२-२ [as read [?]])

gāmaśvaṃ poṣayitnu sa no mṛḷātīdṛśe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-52-1 [as read [?]]) madhuścyutaṃ ghṛtamiva supūtamṛtasya naḥ patayo mṛḷayantu ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-52-2 [as read [?]])

— and since in these Ṛks he explains mṛḷātir dānakarmā pūjākarmā vā | mṛḷayatir apy etayor anyatarakarmā pūjākarmā vā (Ni. 10-16 [as read]), the word mṛḷīka, derived from the root mṛḷ, means 'worthy of worship', i.e. 'worthy of worship because it gives comfort'. Here, since the form is from the root mṛḍa sukhe, the meaning is 'comfort-giving'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Śyenapatvā — root patḷ gatau; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-75 as read), the suffix vanip; the word śyenapatvan; since it belongs to dāsībhārādi, the former member keeps its accent, the final acute. Or: in the sūtra mentioned earlier, the mention of api [and the like] being for excluding all qualifiers, the suffix vanip in the abstract sense; then, when it is made a bahuvrīhi compound, bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 as read), the former member keeps its natural accent. Sumṛḷīkaḥ — nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 as read), the final acute of the latter member. Svavān — svaṃ dhanam asya asti, [when] the sense is shown, tad asyāsty asmin (Pā. 5-2-94 as read), the suffix matup; since it follows after an a-ending, mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ (Pā. 8-2-9 as read), v for the m of matup. Yātu — root yā prāpaṇe; loṭ, third person singular; tiṅanta nighāta accent.

original p. 419

Javīyān — javo 'syāsty iti javavān, suffix matup; "very speedy" is javīyān: atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. 5-3-55 as read) continuing, and in the dual-and-plural [rule] dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau (Pā. 5-3-57 as read), the suffix īyasun in the sense of exceeding; with it following, vinmator luk (Pā. 5-3-65 as read), luk for the matup; ṭer (Pā. 6-4-155 as read), elision of the ṭi; since it is su-final [?] and ugit, num; since it is nit, jñityādir nityam, the initial acute. Vātaraṃhāḥ — vātasya raṃha iva raṃho yasya saḥ vātaraṃhāḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1), the former member keeps its natural accent. ‖ 1 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.2)

त्रिबन्धुरेण त्रिवृता रथेन त्रिचक्रेण सुवृता यातमर्वाक् । पिन्वतं गा जिन्वतमर्वतो नो वर्धयतमश्विना वीरमस्मे ॥ २ ॥

tribandhureṇa trivṛtā rathena tricakreṇa suvṛtā yātamarvāk | pinvataṃ gā jinvatamarvato no vardhayatamaśvinā vīramasme ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.2)

त्रिऽबन्धुरेण । त्रिऽवृता । रथेन । त्रिऽचक्रेण । सुऽवृता । आ । यातम् । अर्वाक् । पिन्वतम् । गाः । जिन्वतम् । अर्वतः । नः । वर्धयतम् । अश्विना । वीरम् । अस्मे इति ॥ २ ॥

tri 'bandhureṇa | tri 'vṛtā | rathena | tri 'cakreṇa | su 'vṛtā | ā | yātam | arvāk | pinvatam | gāḥ | jinvatam | arvataḥ | naḥ | vardhayatam | aśvinā | vīram | asme iti ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 420

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.2)

त्रिबन्धुरेण । बन्धुरं सारथिस्थानम् । त्रिप्रकारबन्धुरोपेतेन त्रिवृता त्रिधा वर्तमानेन त्रिचक्रेण चक्रत्रयोपेतेन सुवृता शोभनं गच्छता रथेनार्वाङ्गस्मदभिमुखमा यातम् [?] । आगच्छतम् । आगत्य चास्मदीया गाः पिन्वतम् । पयसा पूरयतम् । नोऽस्माकमर्वतोऽश्वान् जिन्वतम् । प्रीणयतम् । अपि च हे अश्विनौ अस्मे अस्माकं वीरं पुत्रादिकं वर्धयतं [?] । प्रवृद्धं कुरुतम् । त्रिचक्रेण । त्रीणि चक्राणि यस्य स तथोक्तः । त्रिचक्रादीनां छन्दस्युपसंख्यानं (पा. ६-२-१३९-१ [as read [?]]) इत्युक्त्वा पदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

tribandhureṇa | bandhuraṃ sārathisthānam | triprakārabandhuropetena trivṛtā tridhā vartamānena tricakreṇa cakratrayopetena suvṛtā śobhanaṃ gacchatā rathenārvāṅgasmadabhimukhamā yātam [?] | āgacchatam | āgatya cāsmadīyā gāḥ pinvatam | payasā pūrayatam | no 'smākamarvato 'śvān jinvatam | prīṇayatam | api ca he aśvinau asme asmākaṃ vīraṃ putrādikaṃ vardhayataṃ [?] | pravṛddhaṃ kurutam | tricakreṇa | trīṇi cakrāṇi yasya sa tathoktaḥ | tricakrādīnāṃ chandasyupasaṃkhyānaṃ (pā. 6-2-139-1 [as read [?]]) ityuktvā padāntodāttatvam ‖

Sense (mine): "Tribandhureṇa — bandhura is the charioteer's seat; with a chariot having seats of three kinds, trivṛtā — that goes in a threefold manner [triangular], tricakreṇa — with three wheels, suvṛtā — going smoothly; come (ā yātam) arvāk — facing us. Come, and then pinvatam — fill our cows with milk; jinvatam — please our horses (arvataḥ); and, O Aśvins, asme — for us, vardhayatam — increase our vīra — sons and the like. Tricakra — he who has three wheels; having said tricakrādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṅkhyānam, [the accent is] the final acute."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.2) (Kannada, rendered)

He) aśvinā — O Aśvins; tribandhureṇa — with three seats for the charioteer; trivṛtā — of triangular shape; tricakreṇa — with three wheels; suvṛtā — with good motion; rathena — by the chariot; arvāk — (to us) facing; ā yātam — come; gāḥ — (our) cows; pinvatam — fill (with milk); naḥ — our; arvataḥ — horses; jinvatam — fill with vigour; (api ca — and; asme — our; vīram — sons and the like; vardhayatam — cause to flourish.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.2) (Kannada, rendered)

"Come to us face to face, in your chariot — having three seats for the charioteer, triangular, three-wheeled, of good motion; and bestow on our cows milk, on our horses vigour, and on our sons and others increase."

English Translation (as printed)

"Come to us with your tri-columnar, triangular, three-wheeled, and well-constructed car; replenish our cows (with milk), give spirit to our horses, and augment, Aswins, our posterity."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 2)

"The chariot of the Aśvins has three wheels. The seat where the charioteer sits is made of three kinds of boards. In this swift-moving chariot the Aśvins, out of compassion, to grant our wishes … [continues on p. 421]

original p. 421

… to our cows [they give] abundant milk; they make our horses go swiftly; and a prayer is described here that they favour us with sons, grandsons and the like."

Arvataḥ — aśvān: "'Horses'. The word arvan is read among the names of horses (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೨-೩೧']). Arvā — īraṇavān (Ni. 10-?? [as read]): since the word arvan is explained in this way [as 'one who goes with speed'], the sense is 'he who moves swiftly'. Here, according to the context, the meaning 'horse' is given."

Tricakreṇa — trīṇi cakrāṇi yasya saḥ cakratrayopetena: "'with three wheels' is the meaning: provided with three wheels."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Tribandhureṇa — trīṇi bandhurāṇi yasya saḥ tribandhuraḥ, instrumental ṭā; by the statement tricakrādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṅkhyānam, the last member gets the final acute; so too below in tricakreṇa the accent is to be understood: trīṇi cakrāṇi yasya saḥ tricakraḥ, tena tricakreṇa. Yātam — root yā prāpaṇe; loṭ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Pinvatam — root pivi secane, bhvādi; idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-58 as read), num for the root; loṭ, second person dual, thas → tam; śap vikaraṇa; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta does not occur; since it follows after upadeśa, as the lasārvadhātuka has come, tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186 as read) makes it anudātta; then the root accent remains. Jinvatam — root jivi prīṇane; as before, loṭ, second person dual; cādilope vibhāṣā (Pā. 8-1-63 as read), the prohibition of nighāta [from the optionality] comes, so as before the root accent remains. Arvataḥ — root ṛ gatau; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-75 as read), the suffix vanip; on that account guṇa of the root; the word arvan; with śas following, arvaṇas tṛ sāv anañaḥ [as read; Pā. 6-4-127] — tṛ final substitution; since vanip is pit, the root's accent remains.

original p. 422

Grammar of Ṛk 2, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Vardhayatam — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; since it shows the action of a causer, hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26 as read), ṇic; on that account guṇa of the root's light penultimate, becomes r-final; after the ṇijanta, loṭ, second person dual. Asme — the word asmad; with the plural of the sixth case following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), śe substituted; śeṣe lopaḥ, elision of the initial. ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.3) small type; read with several doubts

हे दस्रौ दर्शनीयावश्विनौ प्रवद्यामना प्रकृष्टगमनेन शीघ्रगामिना सुवृता शोभनवर्तनेन रथेनागत्याद्रेरादरं कुर्वतः स्तोतुरिमं श्लोकं स्तुतिलक्षणमिमां वाचं शृणुतम् । अङ्गाश्विना हे अश्विनौ पुराजाः पूर्वजाताः अङ्गिरसो विप्रासो मेधाविनो वां युवामवर्तिं दारिद्र्यं प्रति तत्परिहर्तुं गमिष्ठा गन्तृतमा [?] आहुः । कथयन्ति । किंशब्दः प्रदेशः फलप्रश्ने वर्तते । किं न कथयन्तीत्यर्थः । कथयन्त्येव सर्वे । तथा सत्यागन्तव्यमिति ॥ प्रवद्यामना । [grammar tail: pravadyāmanā (pra- + yā prāpaṇe; ato manin-kvanib-vanipaś ca, bahulavacanād vane manin; bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam), adreḥ (draja ādare, āj-pūrva, auṇādika kip), gamiṣṭhā (gantṛ, tṛś chandasīṣṭhan, turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu, tṛlopaḥ; supāṃ sulug), āhuḥ (suffix accent; no nighāta since pādādi)] — characterized, not transcribed.

he dasrau darśanīyāvaśvinau pravadyāmanā prakṛṣṭagamanena śīghragāminā suvṛtā śobhanavartanena rathenāgatyādrerādaraṃ kurvataḥ stoturimaṃ ślokaṃ stutilakṣaṇamimāṃ vācaṃ śṛṇutam | aṅgāśvinā he aśvinau purājāḥ pūrvajātāḥ aṅgiraso viprāso medhāvino vāṃ yuvāmavartiṃ dāridryaṃ prati tatparihartuṃ gamiṣṭhā gantṛtamā [?] āhuḥ | kathayanti | kiṃśabdaḥ pradeśaḥ phalapraśne vartate | kiṃ na kathayantītyarthaḥ | kathayantyeva sarve | tathā satyāgantavyamiti ‖ pravadyāmanā | [grammar tail: pravadyāmanā (pra- + yā prāpaṇe; ato manin-kvanib-vanipaś ca, bahulavacanād vane manin; bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam), adreḥ (draja ādare, āj-pūrva, auṇādika kip), gamiṣṭhā (gantṛ, tṛś chandasīṣṭhan, turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu, tṛlopaḥ; supāṃ sulug), āhuḥ (suffix accent; no nighāta since pādādi)] — characterized, not transcribed.

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O dasrau — Aśvins worth seeing, coming with your chariot (pravadyāmanā — of excellent motion, swift; suvṛtā — of good turning), hear this śloka — this praise-word — of the praiser who reveres (adreḥ, [with] respect). O Aśvins, purājāḥ — the ancient-born, the wise Aṅgirases, viprāsaḥ, say that you two are the swiftest to go (gamiṣṭhā) to remove poverty (avartim). [The word] kim is used for a question about the fruit: 'Do they not say it?' — all say it indeed. That being so, you should come."
