॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.3) (Kannada, rendered)

He dasrau — O Aśvins worth seeing; pravadyāmanā — fast-going [yāman, going]; suvṛtā — well formed; rathena — with the chariot (coming); adreḥ — one who shows respect; imam ślokam — this hymn, of the form of praise; śṛṇutam — hear; aṅga — O; aśvinā — Aśvins; purājāḥ — the ancient-born; viprāsaḥ — the wise; vām — you two; avartim prati — in order to remove (the praisers') poverty; gamiṣṭhā — [as] the most prompt of those who go; āhuḥ kim — do they not say?

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.3) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Dasras! Coming in your swift and well-formed chariot, hear this praise-word of the one who respects you. O Aśvins! Have not the ancient sages said that you are the foremost among those who go to remove the poverty of the praisers?"

English Translation (as printed)

"Dasras, (having come) with your quickmoving well-constructed car, hear this hymn, (recited by one) who reveres you; do not the ancient sages say that you are most prompt, Aswins, (to avert) poverty from the worshipper?"

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 3)

Pravadyāmanā — prakṛṣṭagamanena śīghragāminā: "'one that goes with excellent motion, swift' — this word, as an adjective of the chariot (ratha) that moves with speed, is explained in different ways by Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin: pravate iti gatikarmā [as read [?]]. Yānti devatā yasmin sa yāmaḥ yajñaḥ [?] — "that in which the deities go is the yāma, the sacrifice; [one who goes to] the sacrifices …" the paragraph continues on p. 424

original p. 424

Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued "Pravadyāmā — thus Skandasvāmin's exposition. The word yāma denotes what pertains to the sacrifice. The chariot is the means that brings the deities (swiftly) to the sacrifice, [hence] he explains [pravadyāmā] as an adjective of the chariot."

Ślokam adreḥ — ādaraṃ kurvataḥ stutilakṣaṇāṃ vācam: "Sāyaṇa gives the meaning 'the speech of one who praises with reverence (viśvāsa, trust)'. Skandasvāmin gives adreḥ the meaning abhiṣavagrāvṇaḥ ('of the pressing-stone') and the word ślokam the meaning śabdam: 'the sound of the stones that press out the soma-juice'."

Viprāsaḥ — medhāvinaḥ: "The word vipra is stated among the twenty-four names of 'wise' (Ni. 3-19 [as read]); hence the meaning 'wise'. The ancient ones: [they say that] the Aśvins, hearing, in the sacrifice, the praises recited by the priests and the sacrificers — those who come with a swift, comfortable chariot — come quickly to remove their poverty; so, [by] praising the Aśvins, they become worthy of their favour, and [we pray]: 'remove our poverty'. Skandasvāmin explains the first half and the second half of this Ṛk as ākṣepa (objection) and samādhāna (reply):

परेणार्धर्चेन उक्तमात्रा [?] अनागच्छन्तौ कुपित इवाह किमङ्गेति । … नैव हि युवां क्षिप्रमुपगन्तारौ यज्ञानां यावस्मद्यज्ञमुक्तमात्रेण नागच्छतम् । [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

pareṇārdharcena uktamātrā [?] anāgacchantau kupita ivāha kimaṅgeti | … naiva hi yuvāṃ kṣipramupagantārau yajñānāṃ yāvasmadyajñamuktamātreṇa nāgacchatam | [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

— 'In the first half, rebuking the Aśvins, as if angry that they were not coming, [the poet] says "kim aṅga" — "is it not so?"; and in the latter half, the objection: "You are not men who come quickly to sacrifices, since you do not come at the mere word of our sacrifice" — you are not of those who come hurriedly; you are of the wise men of old; the ancient ones are praised; but you did not come for our sacrifice' — such is the expression of reproach." The word śloka is stated among the fifty-one names of speech (Ni. 3-5 [as read]); and ślokaḥ śrūyateḥ (Ni. 9-11 [as read]) is explained by the Nirukta author; so it means 'a praise-word'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Pravadyāmanā — here pra, an upasarga joined with su, conveys the sense of the verbal root; after this pra [which has] the sense of the root, upasargāc chandasi dhātvarthe (Pā. 5-1-118 as read), the suffix vati; the form pravat. Root yā prāpaṇe; ato maniṇ-kvanib-vanipaś ca (Pā. 3-2-74 as read), since the word bahulam is understood, the suffix manin in the abstract sense; pravad yāma yasya saḥ pravadyāmā; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1), the former member keeps its natural accent; sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante; in the instrumental singular, the a of an is not elided.

original p. 425

Dasrau — because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the āmantrita nighāta does not occur; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 6-1-198 as read), the initial acute. Śṛṇutam — root śru śravaṇe; loṭ, second person dual; tam substituted; śruvaḥ śṛ ca (Pā. 3-1-74 as read), śṛ substituted for the root; śnu vikaraṇa; since both the vikaraṇa and the suffix are ṅit, guṇa does not occur; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Adreḥ — root dṛñ ādare; the prefix ā before it; auṇādika kip; hrasva for the ā of the āñ; since the i of the suffix remains, yaṇ is substituted on account of it; "one who shows reverence" is the meaning; genitive singular form. Gamiṣṭhā — root gam̐ḷ gatau; the suffix tṛc, the word gantṛ; to it, when the sense of exceeding is meant, tuś chandasi (Pā. 5-3-59 as read), the suffix iṣṭhan; with it following, turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu (Pā. 6-4-154 as read), elision of tṛ; the form gamiṣṭha; with the dual following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā for it. Āhuḥ — root brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; laṭ, third person plural, jhi following; brūvaḥ pañcānām ādita āho brūvaḥ (Pā. 3-4-84 as read), jhi gets ul-substitution; āha substituted for the root; here the h and the r are for pronunciation; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; by the suffix's accent, the final acute. Viprāsaḥ — the word vipra with jas following, āj jaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50 as read), asuk for jas. Purājāḥ — purā jātāḥ purājāḥ; root janī prādurbhāve; anyeṣv api dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-101 as read), when purā is the upapada, the suffix ḍa; since ḍit, ṭi-elision of the root; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. ‖ 3 ‖

original p. 426

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.4)

आ वां श्येनासो अश्विना वहन्तु रथे युक्तास आशवः पतङ्गाः । ये अप्तुरो दिव्यासो न गृध्रा अभि प्रयो नासत्या वहन्ति ॥ ४ ॥

ā vāṃ śyenāso aśvinā vahantu rathe yuktāsa āśavaḥ pataṅgāḥ | ye apturo divyāso na gṛdhrā abhi prayo nāsatyā vahanti ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.4)

आ । वाम् । श्येनासः । अश्विना । वहन्तु । रथे । युक्तासः । आशवः । पतङ्गाः । ये । अप्ऽतुरः । दिव्यासः । न । गृध्राः । अभि । प्रयः । नासत्या । वहन्ति ॥ ४ ॥

ā | vām | śyenāsaḥ | aśvinā | vahantu | rathe | yuktāsaḥ | āśavaḥ | pataṅgāḥ | ye | ap 'turaḥ | divyāsaḥ | na | gṛdhrāḥ | abhi | prayaḥ | nāsatyā | vahanti ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.4)

हे अश्विनौ रथे युक्तासः सारथिना वहनप्रदेशे योजिता आशवो व्याप्नुवन्तः पतङ्गाः पतनसमर्थाः श्येनासः शंसनीयगमना अश्वा वां युवामा वहन्तु । अस्मदभिमुखमानयन्तु । येऽश्वा अप्तुर आप इव त्वरोपेता दिव्यासो न गृध्रा अन्तरिक्षे वर्तमाना गृध्राख्याः पक्षिण इव शीघ्रं गच्छन्तो हे नासत्यौ युवां प्रयो हविर्लक्षणमन्नमभिलक्ष्य वहन्ति प्रापयन्ति । ताद्दशा इति पूर्वत्र संबन्धः ॥ अप्तुरः । तुर त्वरणे । अप्स्वित्युपपदादस्मात्क्विप् चेति क्विप् ॥

he aśvinau rathe yuktāsaḥ sārathinā vahanapradeśe yojitā āśavo vyāpnuvantaḥ pataṅgāḥ patanasamarthāḥ śyenāsaḥ śaṃsanīyagamanā aśvā vāṃ yuvāmā vahantu | asmadabhimukhamānayantu | ye 'śvā aptura āpa iva tvaropetā divyāso na gṛdhrā antarikṣe vartamānā gṛdhrākhyāḥ pakṣiṇa iva śīghraṃ gacchanto he nāsatyau yuvāṃ prayo havirlakṣaṇamannamabhilakṣya vahanti prāpayanti | tāddaśā iti pūrvatra saṃbandhaḥ ‖ apturaḥ | tura tvaraṇe | apsvityupapadādasmātkvip ceti kvip ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, may the horses — yuktāsaḥ yoked to the chariot at the place of drawing by the charioteer; āśavaḥ — quick (all-pervading); pataṅgāḥ — able to fly; śyenāsaḥ — of praiseworthy gait — bring you here (ā vahantu), facing us. Those horses which are apturaḥ — swift like waters; divyāsaḥ na gṛdhrāḥ — going swiftly like the birds called vultures that move in mid-air — convey you, O Nāsatyas, prayaḥ abhi — towards the offering of food (the oblation); 'such [horses]' is the connection with what precedes." Apturaḥ: root tura tvaraṇe, when apsu is the upapada, kvip.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.4) (Kannada, rendered)

Nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; ye — which (your horses); apturaḥ — swift like water; divyāsaḥ — [moving] in the air; gṛdhrāḥ na — like vultures (swift-going); prayaḥ abhi — to the side of the oblation (carrying you two); vahanti — take; aśvinā — O Aśvins; te — those; rathe yuktāsaḥ — harnessed to the chariot; āśavaḥ — swift-going; pataṅgāḥ — flying; śyenāsaḥ — (horses) going like birds; vām — you two; ā vahantu — let them bring (to our neighbourhood).

original p. 427

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.4) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Nāsatyas! Let your horses — swift like flowing water, carrying you through the air like vultures flying there, to the oblation, running, fast-going, with gait like birds — harnessed to the chariot, bring you both to our neighbourhood."

English Translation (as printed)

"May your quick-moving, prancing steeds, rapid as hawks, yoked to your car, bear you, Aswins, (hither), who, quick as (falling) water, like vultures [sic: "vultnres"] flying through the air, convey you, Nasatyas, to the sacrifice."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 4)

Pataṅgāḥ — patanasamarthāḥ: "The word pataṅga is stated among the names of horses (Ni. 3-26 [as read]). 'Those which go swiftly' is Sāyaṇa's [explanation]; 'horses' is Skandasvāmin's meaning."

Prayaḥ — havirlakṣaṇam annam: "The word prayas is stated among the twenty-eight names of food (Ni. 2-5 [as read]); hence the meaning 'food'. May the horses of the chariot, with fine charioteer, in which the Aśvins are seated, come with the swift motion of hawks to our sacrifice; may they bring the Aśvins near us — thus the prayer."

Apturaḥ divyāso na gṛdhrāḥ — āpa iva tvaropetāḥ | antarikṣe vartamānā gṛdhrākhyāḥ pakṣiṇa iva śīghraṃ gacchantaḥ: "The horses of the Aśvins' chariot run with the speed of flowing water; and, like vultures flying in the air, they go swiftly" — so Sāyaṇa; and Skandasvāmin:

आपोऽन्तरिक्षं तत्र त्वरितारौ त्वरयितारौ वा मेघस्य । आपः उदकानि तत्र त्वरितारौ वा [?] मेघस्य । [as read; small type]

āpo 'ntarikṣaṃ tatra tvaritārau tvarayitārau vā meghasya | āpaḥ udakāni tatra tvaritārau vā [?] meghasya | [as read; small type]

"Āpaḥ means mid-air: in mid-air they hasten, or they hasten the clouds in order that rain fall; or [they hasten] the waters (udakāni) to rain" — thus Skandasvāmin explains.

original p. 428

Special Topics of Ṛk 4, concluded "… by giving [them] the waters that rain, [we pray that] the Aśvins favour us with the food in the form of the oblation required for the sacrifices — this prayer is described here."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Śyenāsaḥ — with jas following, āj jaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50 as read), the augment asuk; likewise the asuk comes in these two words of the mantra [yuktāsaḥ, śyenāsaḥ]. Vahantu — root vaha prāpaṇe; loṭ, third person plural; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Āśavaḥ — the prefix āṅ; root aśū vyāptau; the auṇādika suffix u; by the suffix's accent, the final acute; nominative plural form. Pataṅgāḥ — root gam̐ḷ gatau; gameḥ supi vācyam (as read) [gamer ḍaḥ supi?], the suffix khac; khac ḍit [as read], since it is ḍit, the ṭi of the root is elided; the augment mum for the preceding. Apturaḥ — root tura tvaraṇe; when ap is the upapada, kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76 as read), the suffix kvip; the word aptur; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent; nominative plural form. ‖ 4 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.5)

आ वां रथं युवतिस्तिष्ठदत्र जुष्ट्वी नरा दुहिता सूर्यस्य । परि वामश्वा वपुषः पतङ्गा वयो वहन्त्वरुषा अभीके ॥ ५ ॥

ā vāṃ rathaṃ yuvatistiṣṭhadatra juṣṭvī narā duhitā sūryasya | pari vāmaśvā vapuṣaḥ pataṅgā vayo vahantvaruṣā abhīke ‖ 5 ‖

original p. 429

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.5)

आ । वाम् । रथम् । युवतिः । तिष्ठत् । अत्र । जुष्ट्वी । नरा । दुहिता । सूर्यस्य । परि । वाम् । अश्वाः । वपुषः । पतङ्गाः । वयः । वहन्तु । अरुषाः । अभीके ॥ ५ ॥

ā | vām | ratham | yuvatiḥ | tiṣṭhat | atra | juṣṭvī | narā | duhitā | sūryasya | pari | vām | aśvāḥ | vapuṣaḥ | pataṅgāḥ | vayaḥ | vahantu | aruṣāḥ | abhīke ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.5)

हे नरा नेतारावश्विनौ युवतिस्तरुणी सूर्यस्य दुहिता जुष्ट्वी प्रीता सती वां युवयोरत्रेमं रथमा तिष्ठत् । आरूढवती । तया सहितौ वां युवामश्वा अभीके गृहसमीपे तं रथं परि वहन्तु । परिप्रापयन्तु । कीदृशा अश्वाः । वपुषः । वपुरिति रूपस्य शरीरस्य वा नामधेयम् । तद्वन्तः । छान्दसो मत्वर्थीयस्य लोपः । पतङ्गा उत्पतनसमर्थाः वयो गच्छन्तः अरुषा आरोचमाना हिंसकरहिता वा । अत्र । इतराभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति (पा. ५-३-१४ [as read [?]]) दृशिग्रहणादिदमः [?] सप्तम्यन्ताद्विभक्त्यर्थे त्रल्प्रत्ययः । जुष्ट्वी । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । औणादिकः क्त्वप्रत्ययः । वोतो गुणवचनादिति ङीष् ॥ [as read]

he narā netārāvaśvinau yuvatistaruṇī sūryasya duhitā juṣṭvī prītā satī vāṃ yuvayoratremaṃ rathamā tiṣṭhat | ārūḍhavatī | tayā sahitau vāṃ yuvāmaśvā abhīke gṛhasamīpe taṃ rathaṃ pari vahantu | pariprāpayantu | kīdṛśā aśvāḥ | vapuṣaḥ | vapuriti rūpasya śarīrasya vā nāmadheyam | tadvantaḥ | chāndaso matvarthīyasya lopaḥ | pataṅgā utpatanasamarthāḥ vayo gacchantaḥ aruṣā ārocamānā hiṃsakarahitā vā | atra | itarābhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti (pā. 5-3-14 [as read [?]]) dṛśigrahaṇādidamaḥ [?] saptamyantādvibhaktyarthe tralpratyayaḥ | juṣṭvī | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | auṇādikaḥ ktvapratyayaḥ | voto guṇavacanāditi ṅīṣ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O leaders, Aśvins: the young woman (yuvatiḥ) daughter of Sūrya, pleased (juṣṭvī), mounted (ā tiṣṭhat) this chariot of yours. Together with her, may the horses bring your chariot all around (pari vahantu) to near our house (abhīke). What kind of horses? Vapuṣaḥ — having a fine form (vapus is the name for form or for body), [the possessive suffix being dropped in Vedic usage]; pataṅgāḥ — able to spring up; vayaḥ — going; aruṣāḥ — bright, or without harmfulness. Atra — itarābhyo 'pi dṛśyante [Pā. 5-3-14 as read [?]], from the word in the locative [idam], the suffix tral in the sense of the case-ending. Juṣṭvī — juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; an auṇādika suffix ktvā; voto guṇavacanāt, ṅīṣ."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.5) (Kannada, rendered)

He narā — O Aśvins, leaders; yuvatiḥ — the young one; sūryasya duhitā — Sūrya's daughter (the woman Sūryā); juṣṭvī — pleased; vām — your; atra ratham — this chariot; ā tiṣṭhat — mounted (with her, yoked); vapuṣaḥ — [those] of fine bodies (of form); pataṅgāḥ — of the power of flying; vayaḥ — swift-going; aruṣāḥ — free of wrath (non-harmful); vām — your; aśvāḥ — horses; abhīke — to (our) neighbouring house; pari vahantu — let them bring (the chariot).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.5) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! The young daughter of Sūrya, pleased, mounted your chariot. [With her] may your horses, of excellent form, of the power of flying, swift in going, and without harm (without hindrance), bring [your chariot] to the neighbourhood of our house."

original p. 430

English Translation (as printed)

"Leaders (of sacrifice), the youthful daughter of Surya ascended, delighted, this yonr [sic] car; may your strong-bodied prancing fleet, and shining horses, bring you near us."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 5)

Vapuṣaḥ — vapur iti rūpasya śarīrasya vā nāmadheyam | tadvantaḥ: "The word vapus is stated among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೨೪']) and among the sixteen names of form (Ni. 3-?? [as read]). It is an adjective of the horses: 'those with fine bodies'."

Aruṣā — arocamānāḥ hiṃsākarahitā vā: "The word aruṣa is read among the twenty-six [as read] names of horses (Ni. 1-?? [as read]). Sāyaṇa makes this an adjective of the word aśvāḥ and explains: 'those of great lustre, free from harming anyone'."

Abhīke — gṛhasamīpe prapitve: "abhīke … āsannasya (Ni. 3-30 [as read]) is stated in the Nirukta; so the meaning is 'near'. The horses of the Aśvins — having exceedingly fine bodies — [are to bring] their chariot, which Sūryā mounted, along with Sūryā-devī, to the neighbourhood of our house, so it is described." Skandasvāmin:

दुहिता सूर्यस्य सूर्यानाम्नी युवतिः प्राप्तयौवना युवयोः रथमास्थितवत्याजौ जिष्णू [?] आरोढेत्यर्थः । [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

duhitā sūryasya sūryānāmnī yuvatiḥ prāptayauvanā yuvayoḥ rathamāsthitavatyājau jiṣṇū [?] āroḍhetyarthaḥ | [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

"Sūryā, the daughter of the Sun, a young woman who had come of age, praising the victorious Aśvins at the battle, mounted their chariot — thus he explains," and he quotes:

आ वां रथं दुहिता सूर्यस्य काष्ठेवात्स्थादर्वता जयन्ती । विश्वे देवा अन्वमन्यन्त हृद्भिः समु श्रिया नासत्या सचेथे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१७)

ā vāṃ rathaṃ duhitā sūryasya kāṣṭhevātsthādarvatā jayantī | viśve devā anvamanyanta hṛdbhiḥ samu śriyā nāsatyā sacethe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-17)

— "quoting this Ṛk, he explains the word abhīke as yogaśālī. And for the word pataṅgāḥ, since it is formed from the root aśū vyāptau, he gives the meaning 'those who pervade'."

original p. 431

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Yuvatiḥ — the word yuvan; when the feminine is intended, yūnas tiḥ (Pā. 4-1-77 as read), the suffix ti; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya (Pā. 8-2-7 as read), elision of the n; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Tiṣṭhat — root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; luṅ/laṅ, third person singular, suffix tip; iteś ca, elision of the ī; śap vikaraṇa; pāghrādhmāsthā… (Pā. 7-3-78 as read), tiṣṭha substituted; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75 as read), the augment aṭ does not occur; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Atra — the word idam; by the mention of dṛśi in itarābhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 5-3-14 as read), though there is no connection with bhavat and the like, the suffix tral comes to this word in the sense of the second case; iś substituted for idam; since the suffix is lit, liti (Pā. 6-1-193 as read), the acute on the syllable before the suffix. Juṣṭvī — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; the auṇādika suffix ktvā; laśakvataddhite (Pā. 1-3-8 as read), the ś [of kva] gets the name it and is elided; since it is kit, the root's light penultimate does not take guṇa; by ṣṭutva, ṭ for the t; because it is a word denoting quality, when the feminine is intended, oto guṇavacanāt (Pā. 4-1-44 as read), ṅīṣ, and yaṇ substituted; by the suffix's accent, the final acute. Aśvāḥ — root aśū vyāptau; aśūprukṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan [as read; Uṇ. sū. 1-154 as read [?]], the suffix kvan; since it is nit, jñityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197), the initial acute. ‖ 5 ‖

original p. 432

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.6)

उद्वन्दनमैरतं दंसनाभिरुद्रेभं दस्रा वृषणा शचीभिः । निष्टौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात्पुनश्च्यवानं चक्रथुर्युवानम् ॥ ६ ॥

udvandanamairataṃ daṃsanābhirudrebhaṃ dasrā vṛṣaṇā śacībhiḥ | niṣṭaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrātpunaścyavānaṃ cakrathuryuvānam ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.6)

उत् । वन्दनम् । ऐरतम् । दंसनाभिः । उत् । रेभम् । दस्रा । वृषणा । शचीभिः । निः । तौग्र्यम् । पारयथः । समुद्रात् । पुनरिति । च्यवानम् । चक्रथुः । युवानम् ॥ ६ ॥

ut | vandanam | airatam | daṃsanābhiḥ | ut | rebham | dasrā | vṛṣaṇā | śacībhiḥ | niḥ | taugryam | pārayathaḥ | samudrāt | punariti | cyavānam | cakrathuḥ | yuvānam ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.6)

हे अश्विनौ वन्दनमेतत्संज्ञमृषिं दंसनाभिरात्मीयैः कर्मभिः कूपादुदैरतम् । उद्गमयतम् । हे दस्रा दर्शनीयौ वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारावश्विनौ शचीभिः कर्मभी रेभमेतत्संज्ञमृषिं दश रात्रीर्नव वाहानि च कूपे निवसन्तं तस्मादुदैरतम् । उदतारयतम् । तथा तौग्र्यं तुग्रस्य पुत्रं भुज्युं समुद्रे निमग्नमात्मीयैर्नौभिरश्वैश्च समुद्रान्निष्पारयथः । तीरदेशं प्रापितवन्तौ । तथा च्यवानं च्यवनमृषिं जीर्णं पुनर्युवानं यौवनोपेतं चक्रथुः । कृतवन्तौ ॥ ऐरतम् । ईर गतौ कम्पने च । ण्यन्ताल्लङ् । छन्दस्युभयथेति शपः आर्धधातुकत्वात् [?] णेरनिटीति णिलोपः [?] ॥ [rest of the grammar characterized]

he aśvinau vandanametatsaṃjñamṛṣiṃ daṃsanābhirātmīyaiḥ karmabhiḥ kūpādudairatam | udgamayatam | he dasrā darśanīyau vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣitārāvaśvinau śacībhiḥ karmabhī rebhametatsaṃjñamṛṣiṃ daśa rātrīrnava vāhāni ca kūpe nivasantaṃ tasmādudairatam | udatārayatam | tathā taugryaṃ tugrasya putraṃ bhujyuṃ samudre nimagnamātmīyairnaubhiraśvaiśca samudrānniṣpārayathaḥ | tīradeśaṃ prāpitavantau | tathā cyavānaṃ cyavanamṛṣiṃ jīrṇaṃ punaryuvānaṃ yauvanopetaṃ cakrathuḥ | kṛtavantau ‖ airatam | īra gatau kampane ca | ṇyantāllaṅ | chandasyubhayatheti śapaḥ ārdhadhātukatvāt [?] ṇeraniṭīti ṇilopaḥ [?] ‖ [rest of the grammar characterized]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, you lifted the ṛṣi named Vandana out of the well by your own deeds (daṃsanābhiḥ); O dasrā (worth seeing), vṛṣaṇā (showerers of desires), Aśvins, by your śacībhiḥ (deeds) you lifted out the ṛṣi named Rebha, who stayed in the well ten nights and nine days: you brought him up. Likewise Bhujyu, the son of Tugra (taugryam), who had sunk in the sea, you carried across (niḥ pārayathaḥ) from the sea with your own ships and horses, and brought to the shore. And Cyavāna, the ṛṣi Cyavana, old, you made again young (yuvānam): you did."

original p. 433

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.6) (Kannada, rendered)

Dasrā — O Aśvins, worth seeing; vṛṣaṇā — O rainers of desires; vandanam — the ṛṣi Vandana; daṃsanābhiḥ — by (your daring) deeds; ut airatam — you lifted (out of the well); śacībhiḥ — by (your) deeds; rebham — Rebha, the ṛṣi; (ut airatam — you raised up); tathā — likewise; taugryam — Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, (who had sunk in the sea); samudrāt — from the sea; niḥ pārayathaḥ — you carried to the shore; cyavānam — the ṛṣi Cyavana, (who had been brought to old age); punaḥ yuvānam — again a youth; cakrathuḥ — you made.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.6) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, worth seeing and showerers of desires! By your power you lifted out of the well the ṛṣi Vandana and the ṛṣi Rebha; you brought Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, from the middle of the sea to the shore; and you made Cyavana, who had grown old, young again."

English Translation (as printed)

"By your deeds, Dasras, you raised up Vandana, and showerers (of benefits), Rebha; you bore the son of Tugra over the sea, and made Chyavana young."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 6)

"The Aśvins lifted the ṛṣi called Vandana out of the well and saved him. The ṛṣi called Rebha, whom the Rākṣasas bound and threw into a well, lay there for ten nights and nine days; the Aśvins lifted him out of the well and restored him to life. Seeing Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, sunk in the middle of the sea because his ship had been wrecked, and with his retinue sinking in the water, they brought him and all his family to the shore by their ship and by other means, and delivered him to his own house, protected. And, for the ṛṣi Cyavana, who had a body [brought] to extreme (old age) — with wrinkles and grey hairs, having tender-ness [lost] by old age — and who could not see, they made youth appear, and thus saved him. So, in this Ṛk, four wonderful deeds that the Aśvins performed — protecting Vandana, Rebha, Bhujyu and Cyavana — are described, says Sāyaṇa. This matter has been described in the earlier sūktas [also]."

original p. 434

Special Topics of Ṛk 6, concluded Śacībhiḥ — ātmīyābhiḥ karmabhiḥ: "The word śacī is stated among the names of speech (Ni. 3-?? [as read]), among the names of action (Ni. 2-?? [as read]) and among the names of knowledge (Ni. 3-?? [as read]). Sāyaṇa explains it as 'by deeds'; Skandasvāmin explains it as svābhiḥ prajñābhiḥ karmabhir vā — 'by their own intelligence, or by deeds'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Vandanam — root vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ; suffix lyuṭ; yuvoranākau (Pā. 7-1-1 as read), ana substituted; since the root is it, num; liti (Pā. 6-1-193 as read), the acute on the syllable before the suffix. Airatam — root īra gatau kampane ca; here the causative sense is included; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent; or, since it shows the action of a causer, ṇic; after the ṇijanta, laṅ as before; chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 as read), because of the ārdhadhātuka name for śap, ṇer aniṭi (Pā. 6-4-51 as read), elision of ṇi. Pārayathaḥ — root pāra tīrakarmasamāptau; laṭ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Yuvānam — root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ; kanin yuvṛṣi… (Uṇ. sū. 1-156 as read), the suffix kanin; uvaṅ [uv] substituted for the root; since it is nit, jñityādir nityam, the initial acute; with the dual following, sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau (Pā. 6-4-8 as read), lengthening of the penultimate. ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.7)

हे अश्विनौ युवं युवामवनीताय शतद्वारे पीडायन्त्रगृहे [?] अवस्थान्नीताय [?] पीडार्थं प्रक्षिप्तं [?] तुषाग्निं शीतेनोदकेनावारयेथाम् [?] । अपि चास्मा अत्रय ओमानं सुखकरमूर्जं रसवदन्नमधत्तम् । प्रायच्छतम् । तथा सुष्टुतिं शोभनां स्तुतिं जुजुषाणा सेवमानौ युवामपिरिप्तायासुरैः [?] ब्राह्मण्यपरीक्षार्थमिहासीनः सन् वृष्ट्यामुषसं [?] जानीहीत्यन्धकारवति गृहे प्रवेशिताय कण्वायर्षये चक्षुर्वृष्ट्यया उषसः प्रकाशकं वीणाशब्दं प्रत्यधत्तम् [?] । कृतवन्तौ । यद्वा । अपिरिप्तायापिलिप्ताय पटलेन पिहितदृष्टय एवंविधाय कण्वाय चक्षुरिन्द्रियं प्रत्यधत्तं । प्रत्यस्थापयेतम् । ओमानम् । अवतेरौणादिको मनिः । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना वकारस्योपधायाश्च ऊट् गुणः । अपिरिप्ताय । लिप उपदेहे । अस्मात्कर्मणि निष्ठा । … गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जुजुषाणा । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । छान्दसो लिट् । लिटः कानज्वा । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः ॥ [as read]

he aśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāmavanītāya śatadvāre pīḍāyantragṛhe [?] avasthānnītāya [?] pīḍārthaṃ prakṣiptaṃ [?] tuṣāgniṃ śītenodakenāvārayethām [?] | api cāsmā atraya omānaṃ sukhakaramūrjaṃ rasavadannamadhattam | prāyacchatam | tathā suṣṭutiṃ śobhanāṃ stutiṃ jujuṣāṇā sevamānau yuvāmapiriptāyāsuraiḥ [?] brāhmaṇyaparīkṣārthamihāsīnaḥ san vṛṣṭyāmuṣasaṃ [?] jānīhītyandhakāravati gṛhe praveśitāya kaṇvāyarṣaye cakṣurvṛṣṭyayā uṣasaḥ prakāśakaṃ vīṇāśabdaṃ pratyadhattam [?] | kṛtavantau | yadvā | apiriptāyāpiliptāya paṭalena pihitadṛṣṭaya evaṃvidhāya kaṇvāya cakṣurindriyaṃ pratyadhattaṃ | pratyasthāpayetam | omānam | avaterauṇādiko maniḥ | jvaratvaretyādinā vakārasyopadhāyāśca ūṭ guṇaḥ | apiriptāya | lipa upadehe | asmātkarmaṇi niṣṭhā | … gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | jujuṣāṇā | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | chāndaso liṭ | liṭaḥ kānajvā | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterākāraḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, you, for Atri, avanītāya — who was put down (thrown) into a hundred-doored (śatadvāre) pressing-chamber [?] for torture, [who was] taptam — heated, you checked the husk-fire with cold water [?]; and you gave to this Atri omānam — pleasing, comforting — ūrjam — sappy food, [you] gave. And, enjoying (jujuṣāṇā) good praise: apiriptāya — Kaṇva, led by the asuras into a dark house to test his brahmin-hood [with the words] 'while sitting here, know the dawn in the rain [?]'; for him, you gave back (pratyadhattam) sight — the sound of the vīṇā that shows the dawn [?]. Or: apiriptāya — smeared over, with the sight covered by a film: to such a Kaṇva, you gave back the sense of sight." Omānam (auṇādika mani from av), apiriptāya (lipa upadehe, niṣṭhā), jujuṣāṇā (juṣī prītisevanayoḥ, Vedic liṭ, kānac; supāṃ sulug).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.7) (Kannada, rendered; page continues)

He) aśvinā — O Aśvins; yuvam — you two; avanītāya — [for him] who was thrown down below (into a pressing-chamber); atraye — for the ṛṣi named Atri; taptam — [the fire] that was burning him; omānam — comfort-making; ūrjam — nourishing food; adhattam — you gave; (tathā — likewise; suṣṭutim — [the Aśvins'] excellent praise; jujuṣāṇā — you who accepted [it]; apiriptāya — for [him] who was smeared over with a coat (his sight dulled); kaṇvāya — for the ṛṣi named Kaṇva; cakṣuḥ — the light-giving sense of sight; pratyadhattam — you graciously gave.

original p. 436

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.7) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! To the ṛṣi called Atri, who had been thrown into a torture-chamber, you checked the fire that burned him, and gave him comforting and nourishing food; and (likewise), well pleased with excellent praise, you gave back sight to the ṛṣi Kaṇva, who had been put in a dark house (and so had been blind [there])."

English Translation (as printed)

"You (gave relief) to the imprisoned Atri, (quenching the) scorching heat, and fed him with grateful food; solicitous of worthy praise, you gave sight to Kanwa, blinded (by darkness)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 7)

Ūrjam — rasavad annam: "The word ūrja is stated among the twenty-eight names of food, such as andhaḥ, vāja and the like (Ni. 2-7 [as read])."

Avanītāya — avasthān nītāya [as read]: "'one who was put down, with his face downward' is the meaning. The asuras seized the ṛṣi Atri, took him to a house having many openings, with an apparatus (yantra) for inflicting torture, and put him there face downward, [and] burned him with husk-fire. Then the ṛṣi prayed to the Aśvins to ward off the torture. Hearing him, they brought the ṛṣi out of that house, gave him cooling treatment (śaityopacāra), gave him comforting food and drink, and saved him. Hence suṣṭutiṃ jujuṣāṇā — 'taking pleasure in good praise' (śobhanaṃ stutiṃ sevamānau): this is described as: the Aśvins are praised greatly by excellent praise."

Apiriptāya — āsuraiḥ brāhmaṇyaparīkṣārtham ihāsīnaḥ san vṛṣṭyām uṣasaṃ jānīhi iti andhakāragṛhe praveśitāya kaṇvāya ṛṣaye [?] | yadvā apiliptāya pihitadṛṣṭaye: "The asuras put the ṛṣi Kaṇva in a dark house and told him: 'If you are a brāhmaṇa, sit here and know the dawn and tell us.' And, to test his brahminhood, they confined him there. Seeing this, the Aśvins, praised by the ṛṣi Kaṇva who suffered the confinement, said to him, 'When the time of dawn comes, we shall play the vīṇā; hearing its sound, tell the asuras the matter of the dawn,' and they gave him sight by making the vīṇā-sound that announces the dawn, and saved him." And so the matter of the protection of the ṛṣis Atri and Kaṇva is told by this Ṛk.

original p. 437

"This matter has been told in the preceding sūktas as well."

Omānam — sukhakaram: "From the root ava rakṣaṇe (the root with the sense of protection), the word omāna is formed — so Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin explain. The Nirukta author:

ओमासश्चर्षणीधृतो विश्वे देवास आ गत । दाश्वांसो दाशुषः सुतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३-७)

omāsaścarṣaṇīdhṛto viśve devāsa ā gata | dāśvāṃso dāśuṣaḥ sutam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-3-7)

— quoting this Ṛk, he explains: avitāro vā avanīyā vā — 'protectors, or those to be protected'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Avanītāya — root nīñ prāpaṇe; in the passive sense niṣṭhā, the suffix kta; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read), the gati (ava) keeps its natural accent; dative singular form. Taptam — root tapa saṃtāpe; the suffix kta as before; by the suffix's accent, the final acute. Omānam — root ava rakṣaṇe; the auṇādika suffix mani; jvaratvarasrivyaviramavām upadhāyāś ca (Pā. 6-4-20 as read), ūṭ for the v of the root and also for the penultimate; on that account, because of the suffix mani, guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; the word omān; by the suffix's accent, the ā-syllable after the m gets the acute; the accusative with am following, sarvanāmasthāne ca… (as read), lengthening of the penultimate of the nānta. Adhattam — root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Apiriptāya — root lipa upadehe; in the passive sense niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 as read), the suffix kta; since it is kit, guṇa of the light penultimate does not occur; because it belongs to the kapilakādi group, ra-ness of the l occurs; as a gati-compound, gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read), the gati (api) keeps its natural accent; dative singular. Suṣṭutim — root ṣṭuñ stutau; striyāṃ ktin (Pā. 3-3-94 as read), the suffix ktin in the abstract sense; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 as read), the final acute of the latter member; accusative singular.

original p. 438

Grammar of Ṛk 7, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Jujuṣāṇā — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; since the sense of the present is shown, chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6 as read), liṭ; liṭaḥ kānaj vā (Pā. 3-2-106 as read), kānac substituted; on that account doubling of the root; āṭ kuppvāṅnuṃvyavāye 'pi [as read], ṇatva of the suffix's n because of the ṛ-sound; with the dual au, since the case ending follows, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), ā substituted for it. ‖ 7 ‖

yuvam | dhenum | śayave | nādhitāya | apinvatam | aśvinā | pūrvyāya | amuñcatam | vartikām | aṃhasaḥ | niḥ | prati | jaṅghām | viśpalāyāḥ | adhattam ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.8)

अश्विना हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां पूर्व्याय पुरातनाय नाधिताय याचमानाय शयव एतत्संज्ञायर्षये धेनुं निवृत्तप्रसवामदोग्ध्रीमपिन्वतं । पयसासिञ्चतम् । सर्वदा पयस्विनीमकुरुतमित्यर्थः । अपि च वर्तिकां वृकेण ग्रस्तां चटकसदृशीं शकुनिमंहसो वृकास्यलक्षणात्पापान्निरमुञ्चतम् । निरमोचयतम् । यद्वा । पुनःपुनर्वर्तत इति वर्तिकोषाः । कामादित्येन [?] ऽभिग्रस्तां युवामुमोचयतम् । तथा विश्पलायै संग्रामे भिन्नजङ्घायै अगस्त्यपुरोहितस्य खेलस्य संबन्धिन्यै एतत्संज्ञायै स्त्रिया आयसीं जङ्घां प्रत्यधत्तम् । प्रत्यस्थापयेतं समयोजयेतमित्यर्थः ॥ [as read]

aśvinā he aśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ pūrvyāya purātanāya nādhitāya yācamānāya śayava etatsaṃjñāyarṣaye dhenuṃ nivṛttaprasavāmadogdhrīmapinvataṃ | payasāsiñcatam | sarvadā payasvinīmakurutamityarthaḥ | api ca vartikāṃ vṛkeṇa grastāṃ caṭakasadṛśīṃ śakunimaṃhaso vṛkāsyalakṣaṇātpāpānniramuñcatam | niramocayatam | yadvā | punaḥpunarvartata iti vartikoṣāḥ | kāmādityena [?] 'bhigrastāṃ yuvāmumocayatam | tathā viśpalāyai saṃgrāme bhinnajaṅghāyai agastyapurohitasya khelasya saṃbandhinyai etatsaṃjñāyai striyā āyasīṃ jaṅghāṃ pratyadhattam | pratyasthāpayetaṃ samayojayetamityarthaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, for the ancient (pūrvya) Śayu, the ṛṣi of that name, who was entreating (nādhitāya), you filled with milk the cow (dhenum) that had ceased bearing and was not giving milk: you made her always rich in milk. And you freed vartikā — a bird like a quail, seized by the wolf — from aṃhas, the evil in the form of the wolf's mouth. Or: vartikā is uṣas, that returns again and again; you freed her, seized by the Sun [?]. And for Viśpalā, whose shank had been broken in battle — the wife of Khela, the chaplain of Agastya (sic; Khela's chaplain Agastya) — you put back an iron leg."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.8) (Kannada, rendered)

He) aśvinā — O Aśvins; yuvam — you two; pūrvyāya — for the ancient; nādhitāya — [for him] praying; śayave — for the ṛṣi named Śayu; dhenum — the cow (that had no milk); apinvatam — you made [her] full of milk; vartikām — the bird vartikā seized by a wolf; aṃhasaḥ — from the evil (the wolf's mouth); niḥ amuñcatam — you freed [her]. Or: vartikām — the one who returns (the dawn); aṃhasaḥ — from (the sun's) seizure [?]; niḥ amuñcatam — you freed [her]; (tathā — likewise; viśpalāyai — for Viśpalā (who had a broken leg); jaṅghām — an iron-made leg; prati adhattam — you joined.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.8) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! You made the cow of the ancient Śayu, who prayed to you, one rich in milk; you freed the vartikā bird from the mouth of the wolf (or: you freed the Dawn from the Sun); and you joined an iron leg to Viśpalā, whose leg had been broken."

English Translation (as printed)

"You filled his cow with milk, Ashwins, for the ancient Sayu, when imploring (your aid); you liberated the quail from danger; you gave a leg to Vispala."

original p. 440

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 8)

Śayave dhenuṃ apinvatam — etatsaṃjñāya ṛṣaye nivṛttaprasavām adogdhrīṃ payasā āsiñcatam | sarvadā payasvinīm akurutam: "For the word śayu, Sāyaṇa gives 'a ṛṣi named Śayu'; Skandasvāmin explains śayave rājñe — 'for Śayu, a king'. The cow of the one called Śayu was very weak, so that it bore no calves and yielded no milk; by his prayer, the Aśvins perceived this, and made that cow always possess the power to give milk, and so fulfilled the wish of Śayu — thus it is described here."

Vartikām aṃhasaḥ nir amuñcatam — vṛkeṇa grastāṃ caṭakasadṛśīṃ śakuniṃ vṛkāsyalakṣaṇāt pāpān niramocayatam: "Seeing a small bird (caṭaka, quail) caught in the mouth of a wolf and suffering pain, the Aśvins released it and saved it. Or: punaḥ punar vartate — that which returns anew at the beginning of every day is Uṣas, the dawn; this [Dawn] is overcome by the Āditya (the Sun); the Aśvins released her and saved her. That is: since the word uṣas is feminine, it is a woman; since the word āditya is masculine, it is a man; hence the meaning 'a man, a lover, overpowered a woman by force, and they released and saved her'; so, by the words vartikā and vṛka too, the account of the lover is [only] hinted at, while the account of Uṣas and Āditya is the plain one — by both explanations it is thus described."

Viśpalāyāḥ jaṅghām adhattam — saṃgrāme bhinnajaṅghāyai striyai āyasīṃ jaṅghāṃ pratyadhattaṃ samayojayetam: "A king called Khela was fighting a battle; his [wife] named Viśpalā broke a leg on the battlefield. Then Agastya, the chaplain of King Khela, praised the Aśvins; hearing this praise they treated the leg of the woman called Viśpalā and, fitting a rod of iron as a leg, saved her — so it is described."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Śayave — root śīṅ svapne; the auṇādika suffix u; on that account guṇa of the root; ay substituted; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Nādhitāya — root nādha yācñāyām; in the sense of the present, the suffix kta; ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-35 as read), the augment iṭ; by the suffix's accent the final acute; dative singular form.

original p. 441

Apinvatam — root pivi secane, bhvādi; idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-58 as read), num for the root; laṅ, second person dual; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtamtāmaḥ (Pā. 3-4-101 as read), tam substituted; śap vikaraṇa; the augment aṭ; since it is udātta, [the word has] the initial acute; since it stands at the beginning of a pāda, nighāta does not occur. Amuñcatam — root mucḷ mokṣaṇe, tudādi; laṅ, second person dual; śemucādīnām (Pā. 7-1-59 as read; compare 7-1-55 at p. 335 [?]), since the vikaraṇa śa follows, num for the root; as before, since it stands at the beginning of a pāda, nighāta does not occur; the initial acute. ‖ 8 ‖

yuvaṃ śvetaṃ pedava indrajūtamahihanamaśvinādattamaśvam | johūtramaryo abhibhūtimugraṃ sahasrasāṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ vīḍvaṅgam ‖ 9 ‖

yuvam | śvetam | pedave | indra 'jūtam | ahi 'hanam | aśvinā | adattam | aśvam | johūtram | aryaḥ | abhi 'bhūtim | ugram | sahasra 'sām | vṛṣaṇam | vīḷu 'aṅgam ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.9)

अश्विना हे अश्विनौ पेदवे पेदुनाम्ने राज्ञे युवं युवां श्वेतवर्णं कंचिदश्वमदत्तम् । प्रायच्छतम् । कीदृशम् । इन्द्रजूतमिन्द्रेण युवाभ्यां गमितं । दत्तमित्यर्थः । अहिहनं शत्रूणां हन्तारं जोहूत्रमतिशयेन संग्रामेष्वाह्वातारम् । अर्यो वैश्यः [?] शत्रोरभिभूतिमभिभावुकमुग्रमुद्गूर्णं । वीर्यवन्तमित्यर्थः । सहस्रसां सहस्रसंख्याकस्य धनस्य संभक्तारं दातारं वा वृषणं सेक्तारं । युवानमित्यर्थः । वीळ्वङ्गं दृढाङ्गम् ॥ इन्द्रजूतम् । जु इति सौत्रो धातुर्गत्यर्थः । अस्माद्भावविशेषणार्थात्कर्मणि निष्ठा । तृतीया कर्मणेति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जोहूत्रम् । ह्वयतेर्यङ्लुगन्ताद्औणादिकस्त्रप्प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । अर्यः । अरिशब्दात् षष्ठ्येकवचने जसादिषु छन्दसि वावचनमिति ङेर्ज्गुणीति गुणस्य विकल्पितत्वादभावे यणादेशः [?] । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अभिभूतिम् । अभिभवतेः करणे क्तिन् । तादौ च गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सहस्रसाम् । सनोतेः सनतेर्वा जनसनखनेति विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् [?] ॥

aśvinā he aśvinau pedave pedunāmne rājñe yuvaṃ yuvāṃ śvetavarṇaṃ kaṃcidaśvamadattam | prāyacchatam | kīdṛśam | indrajūtamindreṇa yuvābhyāṃ gamitaṃ | dattamityarthaḥ | ahihanaṃ śatrūṇāṃ hantāraṃ johūtramatiśayena saṃgrāmeṣvāhvātāram | aryo vaiśyaḥ [?] śatrorabhibhūtimabhibhāvukamugramudgūrṇaṃ | vīryavantamityarthaḥ | sahasrasāṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākasya dhanasya saṃbhaktāraṃ dātāraṃ vā vṛṣaṇaṃ sektāraṃ | yuvānamityarthaḥ | vīḷvaṅgaṃ dṛḍhāṅgam ‖ indrajūtam | ju iti sautro dhāturgatyarthaḥ | asmādbhāvaviśeṣaṇārthātkarmaṇi niṣṭhā | tṛtīyā karmaṇeti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | johūtram | hvayateryaṅlugantādauṇādikastrappratyayaḥ | pratyayasya pittvādanudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | aryaḥ | ariśabdāt ṣaṣṭhyekavacane jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanamiti ṅerjguṇīti guṇasya vikalpitatvādabhāve yaṇādeśaḥ [?] | udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi vibhakterudāttatvam | abhibhūtim | abhibhavateḥ karaṇe ktin | tādau ca gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | sahasrasām | sanoteḥ sanatervā janasanakhaneti viṭ | viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt [?] ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, to the king named Pedu you gave a white-coloured horse. What kind? Indrajūtam — made to go (given) by Indra to you; ahihanam — slayer of enemies; johūtram — a [horse] that calls out exceedingly in battles; aryaḥ — [for] the enemy of the vaiśya?? [as read [?]] abhibhūtim — the overcomer, ugram — formidable, strong; sahasrasām — dividing, or giving, wealth of a thousand-fold; vṛṣaṇam — a sprinkler [virile]; yuvānam — young; vīḷvaṅgam — of firm limbs."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.9) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; pedave — to the king named Pedu; yuvam — you two; indrajūtam — given [to you] by Indra; ahihanam — slayer of enemies; johūtram — loudly neighing (in battle); aryaḥ — to the enemy; abhibhūtim — causing defeat; ugram — endowed with valour; sahasrasām — bringing a thousand-fold wealth; vṛṣaṇam — youthful; vīḷvaṅgam — firm of limb; śvetam — of white colour; aśvam — a horse; adattam — you gave.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.9) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! You gave to Pedu a horse of white colour — given by Indra to you, a slayer of enemies, neighing loudly in battle, causing defeat to the enemy, endowed with valour, bringing wealth, youthful and firm of limb."

original p. 443

English Translation (as printed)

"You gave to Pedu, Aswins, the white and foe-trampling steed which you had received from Indra, loud-neighing (in battle), defying enemies, high-spirited, the acquirer of a thousand treasures, vigorous, and firm in body."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 9)

Indrajūtam — indreṇa gamitaṃ dattam: "'Given by Indra to the Aśvins' is Sāyaṇa's meaning. Indram iva gantāraṃ kartṛprati [as read]: 'one that goes, like Indra, into battle against enemies' is Skandasvāmin's meaning."

Ahihanam — śatrūṇāṃ hantāram: "'one who destroys enemies' [say] Sāyaṇa; and Skandasvāmin: śauryopetaṃ ca . . . [as read; small type] śatror hinasti ... vā asurasya hantāram — he explains the meaning: 'a destroyer of enemies who rise over him with great strength, or of the asura called Ahi'."

"The king Pedu praised the Aśvins. They, hearing the king's praise, were pleased and, graciously, gave him a horse suited [to him]: it was white-coloured, and it had the power to destroy enemies at the time of battle. Indra had given it long before to the Aśvins, with great respect. It is described as having the nature of regularly winning a thousand kinds of wealth every day."

Sahasrasām — sahasrasaṃkhyākasya dhanasya sambhaktāraṃ dātāraṃ vā: "This horse is one that wins, or gives, a thousandfold of wealth."

Vīḷvaṅgam — dṛḍhāṅgam: "'having firm limbs' is the meaning. The Nirukta author [explains]:

वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः । गोभिः सन्नद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्था ता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-४७-२६)

vanaspate vīḍvaṅgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ | gobhiḥ sannaddho asi vīḷayasvāsthā tā te jayatu jetvāni ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-26)

— quoting this, he explains vīḍvaṅgaḥ dṛḍhāṅgaḥ (Ni. 6-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೯-೧೨']) — 'of firm limbs'."

original p. 444

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Indrajūtam — indreṇa jūtam indrajūtam; jūtam: ju is a sautra root, used in the sense of going; here, because it shows the action of a causer, it must be accepted that the causative sense is included; in the passive sense niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 as read), the suffix kta; since it is kit, guṇa of the root does not occur; since a tatpuruṣa compound has been made with the third case, tṛtīyā karmaṇi (Pā. 6-2-48 as read), the former member keeps its natural accent. Ahihanam — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; in the agent sense, the suffix ap; since it is pit, the root's accent remains; in the compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Adattam — root dudāñ dāne, juhotyādi; laṅ, second person dual; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Johūtram — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; since the sense of exceeding is meant, dhātor eko 'c halāder kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ (Pā. 3-1-22 as read), when yaṅ has come, yaño 'ci ca (Pā. 2-4-74 as read), luk for it; the saṃprasāraṇa and pūrvarūpa on account of yaṅ; sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. 6-1-9 as read), doubling of the root; guṇo yaṅluk oḥ (Pā. 7-4-82 as read), guṇa of the reduplicative syllable; kuhoś cuḥ, c, and jaś [j]; halaḥ (Pā. 6-4-2 as read), lengthening of the u of the saṃprasāraṇa; to this the auṇādika suffix traP; since it is pit, anudātta, [by anudāttau supitau] the root's accent remains. Aryaḥ — the word ari; with the genitive singular following, jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanaṃ prāṅ ṇau caurajasau [as read]; by the statement ghe rṅiti (Pā. 7-3-111 as read) the guṇa is optional, so here guṇa does not occur; then yaṇ substituted; yaṇ standing in the place of an udātta, a consonant before it, a case ending after it — udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (Pā. 6-1-174 as read), the acute on the case ending. Abhibhūtim — root bhū sattāyām; "abhibhūyate anena" gives abhibhūtiḥ, in the sense of the instrument; striyāṃ ktin (Pā. 3-3-94 as read), the suffix ktin; since it is kit, guṇa of the root does not occur; since it is tādi (begins with t), and a nit [is] the final-accented word that follows, tādau ca niti kṛty ataḥ (Pā. 6-2-50 as read), the gati (abhi) keeps its natural accent.

original p. 445

Sahasrasām — root ṣaṇu dāne, or ṣaṇa sambhaktau; janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ (Pā. 3-2-67 as read), the suffix viṭ; since the root ends in a nasal, viḍvanorānunāsikasyāt (Pā. 6-4-41 as read), ā is substituted as the final; in the compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Vīḍvaṅgam — vīḷūni aṅgāni yasya saḥ vīḍvaṅgaḥ, tam; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 as read), the former member keeps its natural accent; since the vowel u was udātta, yaṇ substituted in its place, and a case ending that is anudātta follows, udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya (Pā. 8-2-4 as read), the svarita accent. ‖ 9 ‖

ता वां नरा स्ववसे सुजाता हवामहे अश्विना नाधमानाः । आ न उप वसुमता रथेन गिरो जुषाणा सुविताय यातम् ॥ १० ॥

tā vāṃ narā svavase sujātā havāmahe aśvinā nādhamānāḥ | ā na upa vasumatā rathena giro juṣāṇā suvitāya yātam ‖ 10 ‖

tā | vām | narā | su | avase | su 'jātā | havāmahe | aśvinā | nādhamānāḥ | ā | naḥ | upa | vasu 'matā | rathena | giraḥ | juṣāṇā | suvitāya | yātam ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.10)

नरा नेतारौ हे अश्विना सुजाता शोभनजन्मानौ ता वां तौ युवां नाधमाना धनं याचमाना वयं स्तोतारोऽवसे रक्षणार्थं सु हवामहे । शोभनमाह्वयामहे । गिरः स्तुतीर्जुषाणा सेवमानौ युवां वसुमता धनयुक्तेन रथेन नोऽस्मानुपा यातम् । उपागच्छतम् । किमर्थम् । सुविताय सुष्ठु प्राप्तव्याय धनाय सुखाय वा । सुजाता । शोभनं जातं जन्म ययोस्तौ सुजातौ । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । नाधमानाः । नाध याच्ञायाम् । जुषाणा । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । छान्दसः शानच् । तुदादित्वाच्छः [?] । पूर्ववद्विभक्तेराकारः । सुविताय । सुपूर्वादेतेः कर्मणि निष्ठा । कन्वादित्वादुवङ् [?] । सूपमानात्क्त इत्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥ [as read]

narā netārau he aśvinā sujātā śobhanajanmānau tā vāṃ tau yuvāṃ nādhamānā dhanaṃ yācamānā vayaṃ stotāro 'vase rakṣaṇārthaṃ su havāmahe | śobhanamāhvayāmahe | giraḥ stutīrjuṣāṇā sevamānau yuvāṃ vasumatā dhanayuktena rathena no 'smānupā yātam | upāgacchatam | kimartham | suvitāya suṣṭhu prāptavyāya dhanāya sukhāya vā | sujātā | śobhanaṃ jātaṃ janma yayostau sujātau | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterākāraḥ | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | nādhamānāḥ | nādha yācñāyām | juṣāṇā | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | chāndasaḥ śānac | tudāditvācchaḥ [?] | pūrvavadvibhakterākāraḥ | suvitāya | supūrvādeteḥ karmaṇi niṣṭhā | kanvāditvāduvaṅ [?] | sūpamānātkta ityuttarapadāntodāttatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O leaders, Aśvins, sujātā — of good birth: we, the praisers, begging wealth (nādhamānāḥ), call you well (su havāmahe) for protection (avase). Enjoying (juṣāṇā) our praises, come (yātam) to us (upa) with a wealth-possessing chariot — for what purpose? Suvitāya — for wealth that is to be well attained, or for happiness."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.10) (Kannada, rendered)

Narā — O leaders; aśvinā — O Aśvins; sujātā — of splendid birth; tā — those (such); vām — you two; nādhamānāḥ — we who beg (wealth); avase — for protection; su havāmahe — we call well (by praises); giraḥ — praise-words; juṣāṇā — you who accept; vasumatā — wealth-possessing; rathena — with the chariot; naḥ — to us; suvitāya — for abundant wealth or happiness (to give); upa ā yātam — come to our neighbourhood.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.10) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, leaders, of splendid birth! We who desire wealth call you for protection (you who have such qualities as have been described); come, pleased by the words of praise, in your wealth-bearing chariot, and make us happy (grant us wealth)."

English Translation (as printed)

"Earnestly we call you, leaders (of the sacrifice), such (as you have been described), and who are well born, to our succour, soliciting, Aswins, wealth; contented with our laudations, come to us with your wealthy car, to bring us felicity."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 10)

Sujātā — śobhanaṃ jātaṃ janma yayos tau sujātau | śobhanajanmānau: "'Those of splendid birth' — the meaning is that they were born in order to produce good (maṅgala) for others."

original p. 447

Suvitāya — suṣṭhu prāptavyāya dhanāya sukhāya vā: "'for wealth which we must necessarily obtain, or for happiness' is the meaning. Skandasvāmin: sugatāya yogakarmaṇe prajāyai vā — [he gives the word suvita] the meaning 'for the sake of a good going (a good course)', or 'for the sake of accepting the oblation in the rite of the yoga-work', or 'for the sake of obtaining good offspring for us' — thus he explains."

"We, the sacrificers who perform sacrifices, praise the Aśvins of splendid birth for the sake of obtaining wealth. To protect us, hearing the words of our praise, may the Aśvins fill their chariot with the wealth they give us, and come to our sacrifice and give us good progress, wealth, or offspring — such a prayer is described."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Tā — the word tad; with the dual au following, tyadādīnām aḥ (Pā. 7-2-102 as read), a substituted for the d; ato guṇe (Pā. 6-1-97 as read), pararūpa; supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā for the case ending; since there is single replacement with the preceding, it is udātta. Avase — root ava rakṣaṇe; sarvadhātubhya asun (Uṇ. sū. 4-189 as read), the suffix asun; since it is nit, the initial acute; dative singular. Sujātā — śobhanaṃ jātaṃ janma yayos tau sujātau; root janī prādurbhāve; in the abstract sense kta; janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ (Pā. 6-4-42 as read), ā for the root; the form jāta; with the dual following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39), ā for it; in the compound, nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 as read), the final acute of the latter member. Havāmahe — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, first person plural, mahiṅ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 as read), e for ṭi; bahulaṃ chandasi, saṃprasāraṇa of the root; pūrvarūpa; av substituted on account of śap, guṇa for it; ato dīrgho yañi (Pā. 7-3-101 as read), lengthening of the a-final of the base; since it is at the beginning of a pāda, nighāta does not occur; since the lasārvadhātuka follows after upadeśa, tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186 as read) makes (mahe) anudātta; then the root accent remains.

original p. 448

Grammar of Ṛk 10, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Nādhamānāḥ — root nādha yācñāyām; in the sense of laṭ, śānac; śap vikaraṇa; ānemukh [as read; ānenmuk?] (Pā. 7-2-82 as read), the augment muk for the a-final of the base; as before, since the lasārvadhātuka (āna) follows after upadeśa, it becomes anudātta, so the root's accent remains; nominative plural form. Vasumatā — vasu asmin asti iti vasumān, with it, vasumatā; tad asyāsty asmin (Pā. 5-2-94 as read), the suffix matup; since it is pit, it is anudātta; instrumental singular. Giraḥ — root gṝ nigaraṇe; the suffix kvip; ṛta id dhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-100 as read), i [for ṛ]; becomes r-final; the word gir; accusative plural form. Juṣāṇā — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu cānaś (Pā. 3-2-129 as read), since a habit-sense is meant, the suffix cānaś; tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ (Pā. 3-1-77 as read), śa vikaraṇa; because it is a lasārvadhātuka, anudātta accent does not occur; since it is cit, ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163 as read), the final acute; supāṃ sulug, ā for the dual case ending. Suvitāya — the prefix su; root iṇ gatau; in the passive sense niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 as read), the suffix kta; the form ita; with su + ita, by the statement tanvādīnām upasaṅkhyānam (as read), since it belongs to the tanvādi group, uvaṅ [uv] substitution; sūpamānāt ktaḥ (Pā. 6-2-144 as read), the final acute of the latter member; dative singular form. Yātam — root yā prāpaṇe; loṭ, second person dual; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 10 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.11)

आ श्येनस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमायां उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥ ११ ॥

ā śyenasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | have hi vāmaśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāyāṃ uṣaso vyuṣṭau ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 449

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 118.11) The printed Saṃhitā has "śaśvattamāyā uṣaso"; the Pada's śaśvattamāyāḥ — as printed.

आ । श्येनस्य । जवसा । नूतनेन । अस्मे इति । यातम् । नासत्या । सऽजोषाः । हवे । हि । वाम् । अश्विना । रातऽहव्यः । शश्वत्ऽतमायाः । उषसः । विऽउष्टौ ॥ ११ ॥

ā | śyenasya | javasā | nūtanena | asme iti | yātam | nāsatyā | sa 'joṣāḥ | have | hi | vām | aśvinā | rāta 'havyaḥ | śaśvat 'tamāyāḥ | uṣasaḥ | vi 'uṣṭau ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 118.11)

हे नासत्यावश्विनौ सजोषाः सजोषसौ समानप्रीतियुक्तौ श्येनस्य शंसनीयं गच्छतोऽश्वस्य नूतनेन नवतरेण प्रत्यग्रेण जवसा वेगेन सहितौ युवामस्मे अस्मानायातम् । आगच्छतम् । अश्विना हे अश्विनौ रातहव्यो वां युवाभ्यां दातव्येन हविषा युक्तः सन् शश्वत्तमायाः कालात्मकतया नित्याया उषसो व्युष्टौ विवासनसमये वां युवां हवे । ह्वयामि । हिर्हेतौ । हि यस्माद्धवे तस्मादा यातमित्यर्थः ॥ अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगिति शसः शे आदेशः । सजोषाः । केर्नैव द्विवचनस्य सुलादेशः । हवे । ह्वेञो लटुत्तमैकवचने बहुलं छन्दसेति संप्रसारणं शब्लुगावादेशः । शश्वत्तमायाः । उत्तमशश्वत्तमौ सर्वत्र । (पा. ६-१-१६० [as read]) इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥ [as read]

he nāsatyāvaśvinau sajoṣāḥ sajoṣasau samānaprītiyuktau śyenasya śaṃsanīyaṃ gacchato 'śvasya nūtanena navatareṇa pratyagreṇa javasā vegena sahitau yuvāmasme asmānāyātam | āgacchatam | aśvinā he aśvinau rātahavyo vāṃ yuvābhyāṃ dātavyena haviṣā yuktaḥ san śaśvattamāyāḥ kālātmakatayā nityāyā uṣaso vyuṣṭau vivāsanasamaye vāṃ yuvāṃ have | hvayāmi | hirhetau | hi yasmāddhave tasmādā yātamityarthaḥ ‖ asme | supāṃ sulugiti śasaḥ śe ādeśaḥ | sajoṣāḥ | kernaiva dvivacanasya sulādeśaḥ | have | hveño laṭuttamaikavacane bahulaṃ chandaseti saṃprasāraṇaṃ śablugāvādeśaḥ | śaśvattamāyāḥ | uttamaśaśvattamau sarvatra | (pā. 6-1-160 [as read]) ityantodāttatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, sajoṣāḥ — of the same pleasure, [coming] with the nūtana — newer, fresher — speed (javasā) of a hawk's (śyenasya) — i.e. of a horse of praiseworthy gait — come (ā yātam) to us (asme). O Aśvins, I, rātahavyaḥ — endowed with the oblation to be given to you — call (have) you at the vyuṣṭi — the time of the dawning — of the śaśvattamā Uṣas, who, being time-in-nature, is eternal. Hi is a causal particle: 'because I call, therefore come'."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 118.11) (Kannada, rendered; page continues)

(He) nāsatyā — O Nāsatyas; sajoṣāḥ — [you] of the same pleasure; śyenasya — [like] a hawk's (going); nūtanena — new; javasā — [you] with speed; asme — us; ā yātam — come for [our] sake; he aśvinā — O Aśvins …

original p. 450

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 11, concluded "… vām — you two; rātahavyaḥ — endowed with the oblation to be given; śaśvattamāyāḥ — (being time-in-nature) eternal; uṣasaḥ — of Uṣas; vyuṣṭau — at the time of dawning; have — I call (praising) you."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 118.11) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Nāsatyas! Come to us, being yoked with excellent motion like a hawk and with horses of new speed; O Aśvins, endowed with the oblation to be given to you, I praise you at the dawn of the eternal Uṣas."

English Translation (as printed)

"Come to us, auspicious Nasatyas, with the fresh velocity of a hawk: bearing an oblation, I invoke you, Aswins, at the rising of the ever constant dawn." The printed English reads "Invoke you" with a capital — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 11)

Sajoṣāḥ — samānaprītiyuktau: "'those of the same pleasure' is the meaning; the word is also used in other senses:

आ रुद्रासः इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गन्तन । (ऋ. सं. ३-३२-? [as read [?]])

ā rudrāsaḥ indravantaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gantana | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-32-? [as read [?]])

In this Ṛk sajoṣasaḥ [is explained by] parameśvaryeṇa vithyam āsevitāḥ [as read; small type [?]] — 'those served with supreme lordship in their various dwellings', or 'those who dwell with Indra in joy' — the Nirukta author has explained the meaning (Ni. 11-?? [as read]):

अजुह्वान ईड्यो वन्द्यश्चा याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः । (ऋ. सं. १०-११०-१ [as read])

ajuhvāna īḍyo vandyaścā yāhyagne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-110-1 [as read])

In this Ṛk, vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ means saha joṣaṇaḥ samānaprītiḥ — 'having the same pleasure' (Ni. 9-?? [as read]) — thus the Nirukta author's explanation."

"This Ṛk says: that the Aśvins should come to our sacrifice with a praiseworthy, swift chariot, with the same pleasure; and that we call them in our sacrifice for the sake of the acceptance of the share of the oblation after Uṣas has passed away."

original p. 451

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Javasā — ju is a sautra root, used in the sense of going; from it the suffix asun, which is enjoined for all roots; since it is nit, the initial acute; guṇa of the root's u, av substituted. Nūtanena — "navasya nū ādeśaḥ tanap tanaḥ khalāś ca pratyayau vaktavyau" [as read] — by this statement nū is substituted for nava, and the suffix tanap comes; since the suffix is pit, it is anudātta. Asme — the word asmad; with śas following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), śe substituted; śeṣe lopaḥ, elision of the part [of asmad] that follows up to ma; sāvekācas tṛtīyādir viḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 as read), the acute on the case ending. Sajoṣāḥ — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; the suffix asun enjoined for all roots; samānaṃ joṣaḥ yayos tau sajoṣasau; supāṃ sulug, su substituted for the dual; ru, visarga at the end of the word; in the compound, kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Have — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, first person singular, the suffix iṭ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 as read), e; bahulaṃ chandasi, saṃprasāraṇa of the root; saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa; śap vikaraṇa; on its account guṇa of the u, av; since it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the root accent remains. Rātahavyaḥ — root rā ādāne; the suffix kta; hūyate iti havyam (root hu dānādanayoḥ); aco yat (Pā. 3-1-97 as read), the suffix yat; on its account guṇa of the root's u, av; rātaṃ havyaṃ yasmin saḥ rātahavyaḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 as read), the former member keeps its natural accent. Śaśvattamāyāḥ — since the sense of exceeding is meant, atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. 5-3-55 as read), the suffix tamap; in the feminine, since it ends in a, ṭāp; uttamaśaśvattamau sarvatra (Pā. 6-1-160 [as read; the page reads 6-1-100 [?]]), because it is listed in the uñchādi group, though tamap is pit, the final acute; genitive singular form. ‖ 11 ‖

Colophon (Kannada, as printed): "nūrahadineṇṭaneya sūktavu mugidudu" — "The hundred-and-eighteenth Sūkta is ended."

Sūkta 119 — "ā vāṃ rathaṃ purumāyam"

original p. 452

Heading (Kannada): "nūrahattombhattaneya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-nineteenth Sūkta."

Anukramaṇī (Sanskrit, as printed):

आ वां रथमिति दशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसस्य कक्षीवत आर्षं जागतमाश्विनम् । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । आ वां रथं दश जागतमिति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनक्रतौ जागते छन्दसीदं सूक्तमाश्विनशस्त्रे च । तथा च सूत्रितम् । आ वां रथमभूविदं यो वां परिज्मेति त्रीणि । (आ. ४-१३ [as read]) इति ॥

ā vāṃ rathamiti daśarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasasya kakṣīvata ārṣaṃ jāgatamāśvinam | tathā cānukrāntam | ā vāṃ rathaṃ daśa jāgatamiti ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinakratau jāgate chandasīdaṃ sūktamāśvinaśastre ca | tathā ca sūtritam | ā vāṃ rathamabhūvidaṃ yo vāṃ parijmeti trīṇi | (ā. 4-13 [as read]) iti ‖

Sense: "ā vāṃ ratham — a sūkta of ten Ṛks, the fourth, of Kakṣīvat, of the Dīrghatamas [line]; the ṛṣi's work; Jagatī; addressed to the Aśvins. The Anukramaṇī says 'ā vāṃ rathaṃ daśa jāgatam'. This sūkta is used in the Prātaranuvāka at the Aśvina rite in the Jagatī metre, and in the Aśvina-śastra. As the Sūtra says: 'ā vāṃ ratham abhūvidaṃ yo vāṃ parijmeti trīṇi' (Āśv. 4-13 as read [?])."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "This sūkta, ā vāṃ rathaṃ purumāyam, is the fourth sūkta in the seventeenth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is the one called Kakṣīvān, son of Dīrghatamas. The deities are the Aśvins. The metre is Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said 'ā vāṃ rathaṃ daśa jāgatam'. At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, this sūkta is used for the recitation of the Jagatī Ṛks belonging to the Aśvina rite and for the Aśvina-śastra mantras, as is shown in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra 'ā vāṃ ratham abhūvidam yo vāṃ parijmeti trīṇi' (Āś. 4-13 as read [?])."

सूक्त—११९ (Sūkta 119) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१७ ॥ सूक्त—११९ ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—small numerals; read "20, 21" — as printed [?] ॥ Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Ṛṣi: Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. Devatā: the Aśvins. Chandas: Jagatī.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.1)

आ वां रथं पुरुमायं मनोजुवं जीराश्वं यज्ञियं जीवसे हुवे । सहस्रकेतुं वनिनं शतद्वसुं श्रुष्टीवानं वरिवोधामभि प्रयः ॥ १ ॥

ā vāṃ rathaṃ purumāyaṃ manojuvaṃ jīrāśvaṃ yajñiyaṃ jīvase huve | sahasraketuṃ vaninaṃ śatadvasuṃ śruṣṭīvānaṃ varivodhāmabhi prayaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

original p. 453

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.1)

आ । वाम् । रथम् । पुरुऽमायम् । मनःऽजुवम् । जीरऽअश्वम् । यज्ञियम् । जीवसे । हुवे । सहस्रऽकेतुम् । वनिनम् । शतऽवसुम् । श्रुष्टिऽवानम् । वरिवःऽधाम् । अभि । प्रयः ॥ १ ॥

ā | vām | ratham | puru 'māyam | manaḥ 'juvam | jīra 'aśvam | yajñiyam | jīvase | huve | sahasra 'ketum | vaninam | śata 'vasum | śruṣṭi 'vānam | varivaḥ 'dhām | abhi | prayaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.1) small type; read with some doubts

हे अश्विनौ वां युवयो रथं जीवसे जीवनार्थं प्रयो हविर्लक्षणमन्नमभिलक्ष्य हुवे । ह्वयामि । कीदृशम् । पुरुमायं बहुविधाश्चर्यं बहुविधकर्माणं वा मनोजुवं मन इव शीघ्रं गच्छन्तं जीराश्वं जवदश्वोपेतं यज्ञियं यज्ञेष्वाह्वातुमर्हं सहस्रकेतुमनेकध्वजं सहस्रस्य धनस्य केतयितारं ज्ञापयितारं वा वनिनं वनमित्युदकनाम तद्वन्तं शतद्वसुं शतसंख्यार्थैर्नैर्युक्तं श्रुष्टीवानं श्रुष्टीति क्षिप्रनाम क्षिप्रं संभजमानं । यद्वा सुखवन्तं वरिवोधां वरिव इति धननाम वरिवसो धनस्य दातारम् ॥ पुरुमायं । बहुव्रीहौ त्रिचक्रादित्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा तत्पुरुषे [?] । जीराश्वं । जु इति गत्यर्थः सौत्रो धातुः । जोरी च । (उ. २-२४ [as read]) इति रगीकारान्तादेशश्च । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यज्ञियं । यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञौ विश्वकर्मार्थे [?] घप्रत्ययः । हुवे । ह्वेञो लटि बहुलं छन्दसेति संप्रसारणम् । लुगिति ... बहुलं छन्दसेति शपो लुक् । उवङ् । शतद्वसुं । शतवसुं । छान्दसस्तकारलोपजः [?] ॥ [as read]

he aśvinau vāṃ yuvayo rathaṃ jīvase jīvanārthaṃ prayo havirlakṣaṇamannamabhilakṣya huve | hvayāmi | kīdṛśam | purumāyaṃ bahuvidhāścaryaṃ bahuvidhakarmāṇaṃ vā manojuvaṃ mana iva śīghraṃ gacchantaṃ jīrāśvaṃ javadaśvopetaṃ yajñiyaṃ yajñeṣvāhvātumarhaṃ sahasraketumanekadhvajaṃ sahasrasya dhanasya ketayitāraṃ jñāpayitāraṃ vā vaninaṃ vanamityudakanāma tadvantaṃ śatadvasuṃ śatasaṃkhyārthairnairyuktaṃ śruṣṭīvānaṃ śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma kṣipraṃ saṃbhajamānaṃ | yadvā sukhavantaṃ varivodhāṃ variva iti dhananāma varivaso dhanasya dātāram ‖ purumāyaṃ | bahuvrīhau tricakrāditvādantodāttatvam | yadvā tatpuruṣe [?] | jīrāśvaṃ | ju iti gatyarthaḥ sautro dhātuḥ | jorī ca | (u. 2-24 [as read]) iti ragīkārāntādeśaśca | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | yajñiyaṃ | yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau viśvakarmārthe [?] ghapratyayaḥ | huve | hveño laṭi bahulaṃ chandaseti saṃprasāraṇam | lugiti ... bahulaṃ chandaseti śapo luk | uvaṅ | śatadvasuṃ | śatavasuṃ | chāndasastakāralopajaḥ [?] ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, I invoke (huve) your (vām) chariot for life (jīvase), with a view to the prayaḥ — food in the form of the oblation. What kind of chariot? Purumāyam — of many sorts of wonder, or of many sorts of work; manojuvam — going as swiftly as the mind; jīrāśvam — with swift horses; yajñiyam — fit to be invoked at sacrifices; sahasraketum — of many banners, or making known wealth of a thousand; vaninam — possessing water (vana is a name for water); śatadvasum — joined with wealth of a hundredfold; śruṣṭīvānam — (śruṣṭi is a name for kṣipra, quick) quickly enjoying, or having happiness; varivodhām — the giver of wealth (varivas is a name for wealth)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.1) (Kannada, rendered; page continues)

(He) aśvinā — O Aśvins; purumāyam — of many sorts of wonder (endowed with many sorts of works); manojuvam — swift as the mind; jīrāśvam — with swift-going horses; yajñiyam — fit to be invoked at sacrifices; sahasraketum — with many banners (indicating wealth in thousands); vaninam — endowed with water; śatadvasum — with immense wealth; śruṣṭīvānam — a bringer of happiness; varivodhām — the giver of wealth; vām — your; ratham — chariot …

original p. 454

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 1, concluded "… vām — your; ratham — chariot; jīvase — for (my) life; prayaḥ — to receive the food in the form of the oblation (for the purpose of offering it); ā huve — I call [you]."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.1) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! I call your chariot — wonderful, swift as the mind, with horses of swift gait, worthy of worship at sacrifices, with many banners, water-bringing (rain-bringing), having unlimited wealth, bringing happiness, giving wealth — in order to receive the food in the form of the oblation, and for the sake of (our) life."

English Translation (as printed)

"Desiring food, I invoke, (Aswins), to support my life, your wonderful car, swift as thought, drawn by fleet horses, worthy of veneration, many-bannered, bringing rain, containing wealth, abundantly yielding delight, and conferring riches."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 1)

Purumāyam — "For this word Sāyaṇa gives the meaning 'having many wonders', or 'suited to perform many works'; Skandasvāmin explains bahuprajñam — 'one that produces exceeding knowledge'."

Jīrāśvam — "Since the word jīra is stated among the names of kṣipra ('swift') (Ni. 2-15 [as read]), the meaning is 'speed': 'having horses that run quickly'."

Vaninam — udakavantam: "Since the word vana is stated among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-12 [as read]), vaninam means 'one that has water'."

Śruṣṭīvānam — "śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma (Ni. 6-13 [as read]) — thus Yāska explains; and, since [he] explains śruṣṭīvarī in the sense sukhavatīḥ (Ni. 6-31 [as read]), the intent is that the Aśvins' chariot arrives quickly, or makes for happiness."

Varivodhām — "Since the word varivas is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 [as read]), the meaning is 'having wealth' or 'able to give wealth'."

"In this Ṛk the invocation of the Aśvins is set forth, and the nature and qualities of their chariot are also stated: that the chariot of the Aśvins produces much wonder in all; is fit for accomplishing many tasks; has a speed greater than the mind's; is yoked with swift horses; is able to get excessive wealth from the thousand worlds; gives rain; is fit to give wealth, with rapid movement, to those who sacrifice. For the Aśvins to come seated in such a chariot is described."

original p. 455

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Purumāyam — puru bahudhā māyāḥ yasya saḥ purumāyaḥ, tam; since it belongs to the tricakrādi group, by the statement tricakrādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṅkhyānam, the final acute. Or: "purumāyā asya asti" — when the sense of matup is meant, arśa-ādibhyo 'c (Pā. 5-2-127 as read), the suffix ac; since it is cit, ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163 as read), the final acute. Jīrāśvam — ju is a sautra root, used in the sense of going; the suffix ran by jorī ca (Uṇ. sū. 2-24 as read); by its association [the root takes] ī-ending substitution; jīraḥ aśvaḥ yasya saḥ, tam jīrāśvam; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 as read), the former member keeps its natural accent. Yajñiyam — yajñasya ārham yajñiyaḥ, tam; yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau (Pā. 5-1-71 as read), the suffix gha in the sense of "worthy of"; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghām (Pā. 7-1-2 as read), iy substituted for it; yasyeti ca (Pā. 6-4-148 as read), elision of the a-ending of the base; by the suffix's initial acute, the i gets the acute. Jīvase — root jīva prāṇadhāraṇe; since the infinitive sense is meant, tumarthe se-sen-ase… (Pā. 3-4-9 as read), the suffix ase; by the suffix's initial acute it becomes a middle-acute word; kṛn mejantaḥ (Pā. 1-1-39 as read), since it is a kṛdanta [ending in e] it has the name avyaya; avyayād āpsupaḥ (Pā. 2-4-82 as read), luk of the supa that follows it. Huve — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, first person singular, when the suffix iṭ has come, ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 as read), e; bahulaṃ chandasi, saṃprasāraṇa of the root; saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa; bahulaṃ chandasi, luk for śap; ajiknudhātubhruvām (Pā. 6-4-77 as read), uvaṅ substituted for the u of the root; since by sārvadhātukam apit the suffix is ṅit [-like], guṇa does not occur; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent.

original p. 456

Grammar of Ṛk 1, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Vaninam — vanam udakam asyāsti iti vanī; ata iniṭhanau (Pā. 5-2-115 as read), the suffix ini in the sense of matup; by the suffix's accent the i becomes acute; accusative singular form. Śatadvasum — śataṃ vasu yasya saḥ śatavasuḥ, tam; by Vedic usage the augment t comes; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 as read), the former member keeps its natural accent. Varivodhām — varivasaḥ dātā; root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; the suffix viṭ; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. ‖ 1 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.2)

ऊर्ध्वा धीतिः प्रत्यस्य प्रयाम्यधायि शस्मन्त्सनीयन्त आ दिशः । स्वदामि घर्मं प्रति यन्त्यूतय आ वामूर्जानी रथमश्विनारुहत् ॥ २ ॥

ūrdhvā dhītiḥ pratyasya prayāmyadhāyi śasmantsanīyanta ā diśaḥ | svadāmi gharmaṃ prati yantyūtaya ā vāmūrjānī rathamaśvināruhat ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.2) Printed Saṃhitā "sanīyanta"/Pada "sam ayante": the Saṃhitā as printed reads "śasmantsanyanta ā diśaḥ" [?]; I give the reading of the Pada, which is clearer.

ऊर्ध्वा । धीतिः । प्रति । अस्य । प्रऽयामनि । अधायि । शस्मन् । सम् । अयन्ते । आ । दिशः । स्वदामि । घर्मम् । प्रति । यन्ति । ऊतयः । आ । वाम् । ऊर्जानी । रथम् । अश्विना । अरुहत् ॥ २ ॥

ūrdhvā | dhītiḥ | prati | asya | pra 'yāmani | adhāyi | śasman | sam | ayante | ā | diśaḥ | svadāmi | gharmam | prati | yanti | ūtayaḥ | ā | vām | ūrjānī | ratham | aśvinā | aruhat ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 457

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.2)

अस्य रथस्य प्रयामनि प्रयाणे प्रगमने सति तस्मिन्नश्विनोः शंसने स्तवने धीतिरस्मदीया बुद्धिरूर्ध्वोन्मुखा प्रत्यधायि । प्रत्यस्थायि । तदनन्तरं दिशो देवान्नाः [?] स्तुतयोऽपि समयन्ते । अश्विभ्यां संगच्छन्ते । अकारः समुच्छ्येदः [?] । अहं च स्तोता घर्मं महावीरस्थं [?] यद्वा स्फुरणशीलाज्यादिकं हविः स्वदामि । स्वादु करोमि । ऊतयो रक्षका ऋत्विजश्च प्रति यन्ति । घर्मं प्रति गच्छन्ति संस्कारार्थम् । अपि च हे अश्विनौ वां युवयो रथमूर्जानी सूर्यस्य दुहितारुहत् । आरूढवती ॥ प्रयामनि । या प्रापणे । आतो मनिन्निति कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति बहुलवचनाद्भावे मनिन् । दासीभारादित्वात्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । शस्मन् । शंसु स्तुतौ । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । दृशिग्रहणस्य विध्यन्तलोपसंग्रहार्थत्वादुपधानकारलोपः । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । अयन्ते । अय पय गतौ । भौवादिकोऽनुदात्तेत् । ऊतयः । क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायामित्यवतेः कर्तरि क्तिच् । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना वकारोपधयोरूट् । अरुहत् । कृमृदृरुहिभ्यः इति च्लेरङादेशः ॥ [as read]

asya rathasya prayāmani prayāṇe pragamane sati tasminnaśvinoḥ śaṃsane stavane dhītirasmadīyā buddhirūrdhvonmukhā pratyadhāyi | pratyasthāyi | tadanantaraṃ diśo devānnāḥ [?] stutayo 'pi samayante | aśvibhyāṃ saṃgacchante | akāraḥ samucchyedaḥ [?] | ahaṃ ca stotā gharmaṃ mahāvīrasthaṃ [?] yadvā sphuraṇaśīlājyādikaṃ haviḥ svadāmi | svādu karomi | ūtayo rakṣakā ṛtvijaśca prati yanti | gharmaṃ prati gacchanti saṃskārārtham | api ca he aśvinau vāṃ yuvayo rathamūrjānī sūryasya duhitāruhat | ārūḍhavatī ‖ prayāmani | yā prāpaṇe | āto maninniti kṛtyalyuṭo bahulamiti bahulavacanādbhāve manin | dāsībhārāditvātpūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | śasman | śaṃsu stutau | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | dṛśigrahaṇasya vidhyantalopasaṃgrahārthatvādupadhānakāralopaḥ | supāṃ sulugiti saptamyā luk | ayante | aya paya gatau | bhauvādiko 'nudāttet | ūtayaḥ | kticktau ca saṃjñāyāmityavateḥ kartari ktic | jvaratvaretyādinā vakāropadhayorūṭ | aruhat | kṛmṛdṛruhibhyaḥ iti cleraṅādeśaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "At the prayāman — the setting out, the going — of this chariot, in the praising of the Aśvins, our dhīti — thought — has been set upwards (ūrdhvā, turned up) [adhāyi]. Thereupon the diśaḥ — the directions, [or the] praises — come together (saṃ ayante) with the Aśvins. And I, the praiser, make sweet (svadāmi) the gharma — the mahāvīra vessel [?], or the oblation of quivering ghee and the like. The ūtayaḥ — the protecting priests — go (prati yanti) to the gharma for the sake of consecration. And, O Aśvins, ūrjānī — the daughter of Sūrya — mounted (aruhat) your chariot."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.2) (Kannada, rendered)

Asya — of this chariot; prayāmani — in its moving; dhītiḥ — (our) mind; śasman — in (your) praising; ūrdhvā — turned upwards with zeal; prati adhāyi — is placed (is directed); diśaḥ — (our) praises; ā samayante — join (you); ahaṃ — I; gharmam — the ghee and the like oblation; svadāmi — make sweet (savoury); ūtayaḥ — priests, protectors of the sacrifice; prati yanti — approach (for the sake of consecration of the ghee); (he) aśvinā — O Aśvins; vām — your; ratham — chariot; ūrjānī — Ūrjānī (the daughter of Sūrya); ā aruhat — mounted.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.2) (Kannada, rendered)

"For the going of this your chariot, our mind is absorbed in praising you; our praises also join you; I make the oblation of ghee and the like more delightful; O Aśvins, the priests, protectors of the sacrifice, take up the consecration of the ghee; and Ūrjānī (the daughter of Sūrya) mounts your chariot."

original p. 458

English Translation (as printed)

"Upon its moving, our minds have been raised on high in praise; our hymns reach (the Aswins). I sweeten the oblation: the assistants come nigh: Urjani, (the daughter of the sun), has ascended, Aswins, your car."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 2)

Dhītiḥ — asmadīyā buddhiḥ: "'our mind' is the meaning. The word dhīti is used in two senses: praise (stuti) and knowledge (prajñā). For example:

इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः । पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-६१-२ [as read])

iyaṃ śuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ | pārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 6-61-2 [as read])

In this Ṛk, dhītibhiḥ is explained (Ni. 2-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೨-೩೪']) as supravṛttābhiḥ śobhanābhiḥ stutibhiḥ — 'by well-formed, splendid praises' — the word dhīti is used in the sense of praise.

ऋतस्य हि शुरुधः सन्ति पूर्वीर्ऋतस्य धीतिर्वृजिनानि हन्ति । ऋतस्य श्लोको बधिरा ततर्द कर्णा बुधानः शुचमान आयोः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ४-२३-८ [as read])

ṛtasya hi śurudhaḥ santi pūrvīrṛtasya dhītirvṛjināni hanti | ṛtasya śloko badhirā tatarda karṇā budhānaḥ śucamāna āyoḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 4-23-8 [as read])

Here, in ṛtasya dhītiḥ — prajñā (Ni. 10-?? [as read]) — the word dhīti conveys the meaning 'knowledge'."

Gharmam — mahāvīrasthaṃ | yadvā sphuraṇaśīlājyādikam: "The word gharma is stated among the names of day (Ni. 1-?? [as read]) and among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-?? [as read]). For example:

गौरमीमेदनु वत्सं मिषन्तं मूर्धानं हिङ्ङकृणोन्मातवा उ । सृक्वाणं घर्ममभि वावशाना मिमाति मायुं पयते पयोभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-२८ [as read])

gauramīmedanu vatsaṃ miṣantaṃ mūrdhānaṃ hiṅṅakṛṇonmātavā u | sṛkvāṇaṃ gharmamabhi vāvaśānā mimāti māyuṃ payate payobhiḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-28 [as read])

In this Ṛk the word gharma is explained as gharmadhug iti yājñikāḥ — in the Nirukta (Ni. 11-?? [as read]) — 'the milk-yielding [cow of the gharma rite]', i.e. 'juice' (rasa).

उप ह्वये सुदुघां धेनुमेतां सुहस्तो गोधुगुत दोहदेनाम् । श्रेष्ठं सवं सविता साविषन्नोऽभीद्धो घर्मस्तदु षु प्र वोचम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-२६ [as read])

upa hvaye sudughāṃ dhenumetāṃ suhasto godhuguta dohadenām | śreṣṭhaṃ savaṃ savitā sāviṣanno 'bhīddho gharmastadu ṣu pra vocam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-26 [as read])

original p. 459

Gharmadhug iti yājñikāḥ (Ni. 11-?? "By the chariot's setting out [and their appearing], the minds of the sacrificers become turned upward to praise them. After that, praise of the Aśvins also becomes ready. ॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Dhītiḥ — root dhyai cintāyām; ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām (Pā. 3-3-174 as read), the suffix ktic; saṃprasāraṇa of the root, pūrvarūpa; halaḥ (Pā. 6-4-2 as read), lengthening of the saṃprasāraṇa; ciṭaḥ, the final acute. Prayāmani — root yā prāpaṇe; since the root ends in a, āto maninkvanibvanipaś ca (Pā. 3-2-74 as read), the suffix manin; kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam (Pā. 3-3-113 as read), by the strength of the word bahula this comes in the abstract sense; since it is read in dāsībhārādi, the kṛdanta accent is set aside and the former member keeps its natural accent; with the locative singular following, vibhāṣā ṅiśyoḥ (Pā. 6-4-136 as read), since the elision of the a of an is optional, the elision does not occur here. Adhāyi — root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; in the passive, luṅ, third person singular, the suffix ta; ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ (Pā. 3-1-66 as read), ciṇ for cli; ā …
