Grammar of Ṛk 2, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Adhāyi (continued) — ato yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ (Pā. 7-3-33 as read), the augment yuk for the root; ciṇo luk (Pā. 6-4-104 as read), luk for the ta that follows ciṇ; the augment aṭ; since it is udātta, the initial acute; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta. Śasman — root śaṃsu stutau; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-75 as read), the suffix manin; since the mention of dṛśi in this sūtra is for including other operations, the elision of the penultimate nasal of the root occurs although no cause is there; the form śasman; with the locative singular following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), luk for it. Ayante — root aya paya gatau; bhvādi; anudāttetaḥ, anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam (Pā. 1-3-12 as read), the middle-voice suffix comes; laṭ, third person plural form; because it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Diśaḥ — root diśa atisarjane; kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76 as read), the suffix kvip; nominative plural form. Svadāmi — root svada āsvādane; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. 6-1-64 as read), s for the initial ṣ [as read]; since the causative sense is included, or since the ṇic comes by chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 as read), because śap has the ārdhadhātuka name, ṇer aniṭi (Pā. 6-4-51 as read), elision of the ṇi in the presence of aniṭ; laṭ, first person singular form; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the root accent remains. Ūtayaḥ — root ava rakṣaṇe; ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām (Pā. 3-3-174 as read), the suffix ktic in the agent sense; since it is kit, with it following, jvaratvarasrivyaviramavām upadhāyāś ca (Pā. 6-4-20 as read), ūṭ for the root's v and the penultimate; the form ūti; ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163 as read), the final acute; nominative plural form. Aruhat — root ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca; luṅ, third person singular, the suffix tip; iteś ca, elision of its i; kṛmṛdṛruhibhyaś chandasi (Pā. 3-1-59 as read), aṅ substituted for the cli that is obtained in luṅ; since this is ñit, guṇa of the root's light penultimate does not occur; the augment aṭ; because it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.3)

मखा मखवन्तो यज्ञोपेता अमिता अपरिमिता जायवो जयशीला मनुष्या रणे संग्रामे शुभे शोभनाय धनाय तदर्थं मिथः पस्पृधानासोऽन्योन्यं स्पर्धमाना यद्यदा समग्मत संगच्छन्ते तदानीं हे अश्विना अश्विनौ युवोरह युवयोरेव रथः प्रवणे प्रकर्षेण संभजनीये भूतले चेकिते । ज्ञायते । देवेषु मध्ये युवामेव रक्षणार्थं शीघ्रं रथेनागच्छथ इत्यर्थः । येन रथेन सूरिं स्तोतारं प्रति वरं श्रेष्ठं धनमावहथः प्रापयेथः । स रथ इत्यर्थः ॥ पस्पृधानासः । स्पर्ध संघर्षे । छान्दसो लिट् । तस्य लिटः कानजादेशः । छान्दसं रेफस्य संप्रसारणमकारलोपश्च । अग्मत । गमेश्छान्दसो लङ् । समो … [as read]

makhā makhavanto yajñopetā amitā aparimitā jāyavo jayaśīlā manuṣyā raṇe saṃgrāme śubhe śobhanāya dhanāya tadarthaṃ mithaḥ paspṛdhānāso 'nyonyaṃ spardhamānā yadyadā samagmata saṃgacchante tadānīṃ he aśvinā aśvinau yuvoraha yuvayoreva rathaḥ pravaṇe prakarṣeṇa saṃbhajanīye bhūtale cekite | jñāyate | deveṣu madhye yuvāmeva rakṣaṇārthaṃ śīghraṃ rathenāgacchatha ityarthaḥ | yena rathena sūriṃ stotāraṃ prati varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhanamāvahathaḥ prāpayethaḥ | sa ratha ityarthaḥ ‖ paspṛdhānāsaḥ | spardha saṃgharṣe | chāndaso liṭ | tasya liṭaḥ kānajādeśaḥ | chāndasaṃ rephasya saṃprasāraṇamakāralopaśca | agmata | gameśchāndaso laṅ | samo … [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "The makhāḥ — sacrificers, the amitāḥ — innumerable jāyavaḥ — victorious men: when, in battle (raṇe), for śubhe — good wealth, they come together (sam agmata), striving (paspṛdhānāsaḥ) against one another (mithaḥ), then, O Aśvins, yuvor aha — indeed your chariot is cekite — known [to be] at the pravaṇa — the earth's lowland that is well resorted to; that is: of the gods you alone, for protection, come swiftly with the chariot. With which chariot you bring (vahathaḥ) varam — the best wealth to sūrim — the praiser: that chariot."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.3) (Kannada, rendered)

He) aśvinā — O Aśvins; makhāḥ — those who are endowed with sacrifices (performing sacrifices); amitāḥ — numerous; jāyavaḥ — victorious men; raṇe — in battle; śubhe — for the sake of auspicious wealth; mithaḥ paspṛdhānāsaḥ — contending with one another; yat — when; sam agmata — they meet (then); and yat — by which chariot; yūyam — you; sūrim — the praiser; dveṣe — [looking] for; varam — the excellent wealth; ā vahathaḥ — you bring; (sa — that; yuvoḥ aha — your own; rathaḥ — chariot; pravaṇe — on the earth; cekite — becomes known (is seen by all).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.3) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! In the chariot in which you come bringing wealth to the praiser — numerous men, performers of sacrifices and victorious, meeting in battle for the sake of auspicious wealth, vie with one another; (your chariot alone appears before all, exceeding all others)."

English Translation (as printed)

"When devout and unnumbered (men), victorious in battle, mutually contending for wealth, come together, your car, Aswins, is perceived on its downward course, in which you bear excellent (treasure) to the worshipper,"

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 3)

"Innumerable, ever sure of victory, sacrifice-minded people, for the sake of wealth, in mutual contention, when they fight in battle, [the Aśvins] set out quickly, before all the other gods, to protect them from the misfortunes that arise. You come in readiness. And because you come with your chariot already mounted, your chariot is seen clearly by the one who praises you. And the power of their chariot is described in this Ṛk."

original p. 463

Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued "… is described by this Ṛk, and [it is also said] that the chariot of the Aśvins is visible well to the one who praises."

Makhāḥ — makhavantaḥ yajñopetāḥ: "'those who perform sacrifices'. The word makha is stated among the fifteen names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-17 [as read])."

ये सहांसि सहसा सहन्ते रेजते अग्ने पृथिवी मखेभ्यः । (ऋ. सं. ६-११-? [as read; the numeral doubtful [?]])

ye sahāṃsi sahasā sahante rejate agne pṛthivī makhebhyaḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 6-11-? [as read; the numeral doubtful [?]])

"In this Ṛk the meaning 'the gods who destroy' is stated for the word makha."

Śubhe — śubhaśabdo … udakanāmasu [as read]: "The word śubha is stated among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-12 [as read]); hence the meaning is 'water'. Śobhanāya dhanāya — 'for auspicious wealth': Sāyaṇa explains it as maṅgalakara kāryakkāgi athavā dhanakkāgi — 'for the auspicious cause, or for wealth'; Skandasvāmin explains it as 'for water'. Beyond that, Skandasvāmin gives the meaning in another way: amitāḥ — aparimitāḥ athavā balenāparimitāḥ mahābalāḥ ('measureless, or of measureless strength; of great strength'); jāyavaḥ — jayaśīlāḥ; raṇe — saṃgrāme mithaḥ paspṛdhamānāsaḥ yoddhāraḥ nāśakāḥ — 'in battle, warriors competing with each other, destroyers'; śubhe — śobhārthaṃ jayārthaṃ makhā jāyavaś ca amitāḥ — 'for splendour, for victory, the sacrificers and victors are numerous'. [He explains:] since the word amita conveys 'many', the soldiers who fight in a battle with strength or force are victorious; in order to give victory in battle, in which they fight against each other, your chariot is present."

Pravaṇe cekite — "In [this phrase] Sāyaṇa says prakarṣeṇa saṃbhajanīye bhūtale rathaḥ jñāyate; deveṣu madhye yuvām eva rakṣaṇārthaṃ śīghraṃ rathenāgacchetha — 'on the earth that is best resorted to, [your] chariot is known; among the gods, you alone come swiftly in the chariot to protect'. It is understood that your chariot that moves with great speed remains just over the ground; [and] that you come in a chariot, swiftly, for our protection, more than the other gods — such is the meaning he gives. Skandasvāmin:

प्रवणे निम्ने देशे । चेकिते ज्ञायते लक्ष्यते । अश्वा ह्युच्चा रथो नीचः । उच्चैः श्चादश्वानां तेभ्यो नीचो रथो दृश्यते इत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; small type]

pravaṇe nimne deśe | cekite jñāyate lakṣyate | aśvā hyuccā ratho nīcaḥ | uccaiḥ ścādaśvānāṃ tebhyo nīco ratho dṛśyate ityarthaḥ ‖ [as read; small type]

— the word pravaṇa conveys 'low-lying ground'. Since the horses are tall, the chariot is described as 'low' relative to them, so it is [to be] recognized [as yours]."

Sūrim — stotāram: "The word sūri is stated among the names of praisers (Ni. 3-19 [as read]); the meaning is 'one who praises'."

original p. 464

Special Topics of Ṛk 3, concluded Varam — śreṣṭhaṃ dhanam: "Sāyaṇa's explanation is 'the best wealth'. Skandasvāmin's meaning is varaṇīyaṃ dhanam — 'wealth to be chosen'. Yāska has explained the word vara (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೧-೭']): varo varayitavyo bhavati — 'it is to be chosen', i.e. 'that which is desirable, wanted by all'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Paspṛdhānāsaḥ — root spardha saṃgharṣe; bhvādi; since the sense of the present is meant, chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6 as read), liṭ; liṭaḥ kānaj vā (Pā. 3-2-106 as read), kānac substituted for it; on that account doubling of the root; śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ (Pā. 7-4-61 as read), the p remains in the reduplicative syllable; by Vedic usage saṃprasāraṇa of the r of the root and elision of the a occur; the form paspṛdhāna; ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163 as read), the final acute; with jas following, āj jaser asuk, asuk for jas. Agmata — root gam̐ḷ gatau; since the sense of the present is meant, as before, chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ, laṅ; since the prefix sam is connected, samo gamyṛcchibhyām (Pā. 1-3-29 as read), the middle voice; in the third person plural, jha having come, bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73 as read), luk for śap; since the anakāra [?] has come after it, ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ (Pā. 7-1-5 as read), at substituted [for jha's a]; since sārvadhātukam apit makes the suffix ṅit-like, gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi (Pā. 6-4-98 as read), elision of the penultimate of the root; the augment aṭ; since the particle yat is connected, nipātair yad yadi… (Pā. 8-1-30 as read) prohibits nighāta; the augment aṭ being udātta, the initial acute. Śubhe — root śubha dīptau; kvip ca, suffix kvip; dative singular form; sāvekācas tṛtīyādir viḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 as read), the acute on the case ending. Makhāḥ — makhaḥ yajñaḥ, makhāḥ yeṣāṃ santi; when the sense of matup is meant, arśa ādibhyo 'c (Pā. 5-2-127 as read), the suffix ac; yasyeti ca, elision of the a-ending of the base; the final acute; nominative plural. Amitāḥ — na mitāḥ amitāḥ; kter nañ…, tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 as read), the avyaya former member keeps its natural accent.

original p. 465

Jāyavaḥ — root ji jaye; kṛvāpājimisvidisādhyaśūbhya uṇ (Uṇ. sū. 1-1 as read), the suffix uṇ; since it is ñit, ājoñiti [read aco ñṇiti] (Pā. 7-2-115 as read), vṛddhi for the i; āy substituted; the word jāyu; by the suffix's accent the final acute; nominative plural. Yuvoḥ — the word yuṣmad; with the genitive dual following, sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante, so oṣi ca [yuvāvau dvivacane; compare yuṣmado yuvādeśa] — the a-ending [?]; the yatva does not occur; pararūpa by Vedic usage. Cekite — root kita jñāne; dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ (Pā. 3-1-22 as read), yaṅ [as read: yaj]; since the sense of the present is meant, chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6 as read), after the yaṅanta, liṭ; since yaṅ is ñit, the middle-voice suffix comes; liṭasthaḥ [litaḥ taṅo…] (Pā. 3-4-81 as read), iś substituted for ta; ātaś ca…, tiṅ gets the ārdhadhātuka name; sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. 6-1-9 as read), doubling of the first single-vowel part of the yaṅanta; for the reduplicative syllable, halādiśeṣa; guṇo yaṅluk oḥ (Pā. 7-4-82 as read), guṇa for the reduplicative syllable; cutva; then, in the liṭ, first person singular [as read: cekitthe? [?]], liṭas tajhayor eśirec (Pā. 3-4-81 as read), eśa-substitution; since anabhyāsasya is stated, [with] prohibition of doubling in liṭ, doubling does not occur again; for the sake of that, ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48 as read), elision of the a of yaṅ; yasya halaḥ (Pā. 6-4-49 as read), elision of the y; the form cekite; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Yat — the word yad; with the third case singular following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), luk for it. Vahathaḥ — root vaha prāpaṇe; laṭ, second person dual; since the word yat is connected, nighāta does not occur; as the lasārvadhātuka follows after upadeśa, it is anudātta, so the root's accent remains. ‖ 3 ‖

yuvaṃ bhujyuṃ bhuramāṇaṃ vibhirgataṃ svayuktibhirnivahantā pitṛbhya ā | yāsiṣṭaṃ vartirvṛṣaṇā vijenyaṃ divodāsāya mahi ceti vāmavaḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.4)

युवम् । भुज्युम् । भुरमाणम् । विऽभिः । गतम् । स्वयुक्तिऽभिः । निऽवहन्ता । पितृऽभ्यः । आ । यासिष्टम् । वर्तिः । वृषणा । विऽजेन्यम् । दिवःऽदासाय । महि । चेति । वाम् । अवः ॥ ४ ॥

yuvam | bhujyum | bhuramāṇam | vi 'bhiḥ | gatam | svayukti 'bhiḥ | ni 'vahantā | pitṛ 'bhyaḥ | ā | yāsiṣṭam | vartiḥ | vṛṣaṇā | vi 'jenyam | divaḥ 'dāsāya | mahi | ceti | vām | avaḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.4)

वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारौ हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां भुरमाणं विभिरक्षुण्णैः [?] क्रियमाणं [?] गतं समुद्रे निमग्नं भुज्युं तुग्रपुत्रं स्वयुक्तिभिः स्वयमेव युज्यमानैरश्वैर्नौविशेषैश्च निवहन्ता नितरां वहन्तौ पितृभ्य आ । अज् [?] मर्यादायाम् । यत्र पितरस्तुग्रादेयः असते तावत्पर्यन्तमित्यर्थः । विजेन्यमिति दूरस्थं ब्रुवते । दूरे वर्तमानं वर्तिस्तुग्रस्य गृहं प्रति यासिष्टम् । आगच्छतम् । अपि च दिवोदासाय राज्ञे कृतं युवयोः संबन्धि वो रक्षणं शंबरहननरूपं महि महद्गम्भीरं चेति । अस्माभिर्ज्ञायते ॥ भुरमाणम् । डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः । कर्मणि लटः शानच् । व्यत्ययेन शः । बहुलं छन्दसीत्युत्वम् । पितृभ्य आ । मर्यादायामाङ् कर्मप्रवचनीयसंज्ञा । (पा. १-४-८९ [as read]) पञ्चम्यपाङ्परिभिः । (पा. २-३-१० [as read]) इति पञ्चमी । यासिष्टम् । या प्रापणे । यमरमनमातां सक् च । (पा. ७-२-७३ [as read]) इति सगामः । सिचि इडागमः । विजेन्यम् । विजनो दूरदेशः । तत्र भवं विजेन्यम् । भवे छन्दसीति यत् । तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरितत्वम् ॥ [as read]

vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣitārau he aśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ bhuramāṇaṃ vibhirakṣuṇṇaiḥ [?] kriyamāṇaṃ [?] gataṃ samudre nimagnaṃ bhujyuṃ tugraputraṃ svayuktibhiḥ svayameva yujyamānairaśvairnauviśeṣaiśca nivahantā nitarāṃ vahantau pitṛbhya ā | aj [?] maryādāyām | yatra pitarastugrādeyaḥ asate tāvatparyantamityarthaḥ | vijenyamiti dūrasthaṃ bruvate | dūre vartamānaṃ vartistugrasya gṛhaṃ prati yāsiṣṭam | āgacchatam | api ca divodāsāya rājñe kṛtaṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhi vo rakṣaṇaṃ śaṃbarahananarūpaṃ mahi mahadgambhīraṃ ceti | asmābhirjñāyate ‖ bhuramāṇam | ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ | karmaṇi laṭaḥ śānac | vyatyayena śaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasītyutvam | pitṛbhya ā | maryādāyāmāṅ karmapravacanīyasaṃjñā | (pā. 1-4-89 [as read]) pañcamyapāṅparibhiḥ | (pā. 2-3-10 [as read]) iti pañcamī | yāsiṣṭam | yā prāpaṇe | yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca | (pā. 7-2-73 [as read]) iti sagāmaḥ | sici iḍāgamaḥ | vijenyam | vijano dūradeśaḥ | tatra bhavaṃ vijenyam | bhave chandasīti yat | titsvaritamiti svaritatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O showerers of desires, Aśvins: you, bhuramāṇam — [being] carried, borne (Bhujyu)..., vibhiḥ gatam — who had sunk in the sea, Bhujyu the son of Tugra, with svayuktibhiḥ — horses and special ships that yoke themselves, nivahantā — carrying him down (away), pitṛbhyaḥ ā — as far as his fathers [ā of limit: up to where his fathers, Tugra and the others, were], yāsiṣṭam — you went, to vijenyam — the distant (vijana, solitary place), the vartiḥ — the house of Tugra. And for Divodāsa, the king, mahi — great and deep is your avaḥ — protection, in the form of the killing of Śambara: ceti — it is known by us."

original p. 467

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.4) (Kannada, rendered)

Vṛṣaṇā — O Aśvins, givers of desired things; yuvam — you two; vibhiḥ — by swift-moving (horses); bhuramāṇam — [Bhujyu] being carried; gatam — (who had sunk in the sea); bhujyum — Bhujyu (the son of Tugra); svayuktibhiḥ — by [your] chariots that yoke themselves (by your horses and ships); nivahantā — carrying; pitṛbhyaḥ ā — to (his) father's side; vijenyam — [to the place] far away; vartiḥ — to Tugra's house; yāsiṣṭam — you went; api ca — and; divodāsāya — for the king named Divodāsa; vām — your; avaḥ — protection (the act of killing Śambara); mahi — great; ceti — is known by [us].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.4) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, givers of what is desired! You carried Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, who had sunk in the sea with his own army, by your horses and ships that can yoke themselves, and took him to the house of his father Tugra; and the protection you gave (these acts) to King Divodāsa — we know them to be of great glory."

English Translation (as printed)

"You brought back to his ancestors Bhujyu, who, borne by his own steeds, had perished, (but that you rescued him) with your self-harnessed horses, and went, showerers (of benefits), to his distant dwelling; and great was the succour which it is known you rendered to Divodasa."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 4)

"King Tugra, wishing to destroy the enemies who troubled him, joined [a force] in an island beyond and sent an army with his son Bhujyu. While Bhujyu was going with his army on a ship in the middle of the sea, the ship was wrecked and he sank in the water. Then the Aśvins, hearing the praise he made when he remembered them, quickly brought ships and horses, and themselves brought Bhujyu and his army to the shore, and from there took him to his father King Tugra's house and protected him: [such is] the greatness of the Aśvins. And when the king called Divodāsa began a sacrifice, [and] a rākṣasa called Śambara spoiled his sacrifice and he and his [people] were in danger, the Aśvins, knowing it, protected Divodāsa by killing the asura Śambara — such power of theirs is described in this Ṛk."

"In Skandasvāmin's explanation and in Sāyaṇa's, the sense is the same, though the meaning of some words is differently arranged. For the words pitṛbhyaḥ ā Sāyaṇa …" continues on p. 468

original p. 468

Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued "… for the words pitṛbhyaḥ ā, Sāyaṇa says: yatra pitaras tugrādeyaḥ asate tāvat paryantam — 'as far as the place where his fathers, Tugra and the others, are'. Skandasvāmin explains pitṛbhyaḥ ā thus:

पिक्षणामर्थाय । पितृणामस्य स्वर्गादेः [?] प्रच्युतिहेतोः प्रजासंतानाविच्छेदार्थम् । [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

pikṣaṇāmarthāya | pitṛṇāmasya svargādeḥ [?] pracyutihetoḥ prajāsaṃtānāvicchedārtham | [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

— 'so that the ancestors, [who] fall from heaven, do not fall, the line of offspring is to be continuous, that is, the progeny should go on unbroken' — he explains."

Vibhiḥ — aśvaiḥ: "'by horses' is Sāyaṇa's explanation; Skandasvāmin explains pakṣisadṛśaiḥ aśvaiḥ — 'by horses, swift like birds'."

Bhuramāṇam — bhriyamāṇam: "'one being borne by horses' — so Sāyaṇa; and Skandasvāmin: bhurati gṛsyamāṇam matsyair makarair vā — 'being swallowed by fishes and crocodiles' — since he takes the root bhur to mean 'swallowing'."

Vartiḥ — gṛhaṃ prati vartanyā mārgeṇa: "Sāyaṇa's meaning is 'house'. Skandasvāmin explains the word vartis as 'road'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Bhuramāṇam — root ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; in the passive sense śānac; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 as read), śa vikaraṇa in place of śluḥ [?]; bahulaṃ chandasi, u for the root; uraṇ raparaḥ, [it becomes] r-final; ānemuk (Pā. 7-2-82 as read), the augment muk for the a-ending; the form bhuramāṇa; because the lasārvadhātuka follows after upadeśa, tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186 as read) makes it anudātta, so the śa-vikaraṇa's accent remains; accusative singular form. Gatam — root gam̐ḷ gatau; when kta follows, anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti (Pā. 6-4-37 as read), elision of the nasal m of the root; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Nivahantā — the prefix ni; root vaha prāpaṇe; in the sense of laṭ, śatṛ; śap vikaraṇa; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the root accent remains; in the compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent; with the dual au the case ending, supāṃ sulug, ā for it. Pitṛbhyaḥ ā — the prefix āṅ; āṅ maryādābhividhyoḥ (Pā. 1-4-89 as read), in the sense of maryādā (what is called maryādā when stating a limit [excluded]) it gets the karmapravacanīya name; pañcamy apāṅparibhiḥ (Pā. 2-3-10 as read), the fifth case comes for the word pitṛ connected with it.

original p. 469

Yāsiṣṭam — root yā prāpaṇe; laṅ? [as printed luṅ], second person dual; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtamtāmaḥ, tam substituted; yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca (Pā. 7-2-73 as read), the augment sak for the root; in the luṅ, for the cli that has come the sic, iṭ [augment]; ādeśapratyayayoḥ (Pā. 8-3-59 as read), ṣatva of the s of sic; on that account the ṭ of the suffix becomes ṭh; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75 as read), the augment aṭ does not occur; the form yāsiṣṭam; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Vijenyam — vijana is a distant place; "what exists in vijana" is vijenyam; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110 as read), the suffix yat; by Vedic usage eṇ [for a]; since the suffix is tit, tit svaritam (Pā. 6-1-185 as read), the svarita accent. Divodāsāya — divodāsādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṅkhyānam (as read; Pā. 6-2-?? [?]), the former member's initial acute. ‖ 4 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.5)

युवोरश्विना वपुषे युवायुजं रथं वाणी येमतुरस्य शर्ध्यम् । आ वां पतित्वं सख्याय जग्मुषी योषावृणीत जेन्या युवां पती ॥ ५ ॥

yuvoraśvinā vapuṣe yuvāyujaṃ rathaṃ vāṇī yematurasya śardhyam | ā vāṃ patitvaṃ sakhyāya jagmuṣī yoṣāvṛṇīta jenyā yuvāṃ patī ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.5)

युवोः । अश्विना । वपुषे । युवाऽयुजम् । रथम् । वाणी इति । येमतुः । अस्य । शर्ध्यम् । आ । वाम् । पतित्वम् । सख्याय । जग्मुषी । योषा । अवृणीत । जेन्या । युवाम् । पती इति ॥ ५ ॥

yuvoḥ | aśvinā | vapuṣe | yuvā 'yujam | ratham | vāṇī iti | yematuḥ | asya | śardhyam | ā | vām | patitvam | sakhyāya | jagmuṣī | yoṣā | avṛṇīta | jenyā | yuvām | patī iti ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.5)

अश्विना हे अश्विनौ युवोर्युवयोर्वाणी वननीयौ प्रशस्यावश्वौ युवायुजं युवाभ्यां युज्यमानं रथमाजिधावनसमये [?] अस्य रथस्य यच्छर्ध्यं प्राप्यमादित्याख्यमवधिभूतं लक्ष्यं वपुषे शोभार्थं तद्येमतुः । सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वं प्रापयामासतुः । तदनन्तरं चा जग्मुष्यागतवती जेन्या जेतव्या विजेतव्या जयेन जीयमाना योषा सूर्या सख्याय सवित्रे [?] युवां युवयोः पतित्वमवृणीत । कथमिति । मम युवामेव पती भर्तारावित्यवृणीत ॥ युवोः । षष्ठीद्विवचने योचेति यत्वस्य सर्वविधीनां छन्दसि विकल्पितत्वादभावे शेषे लोप इति दकारलोपः । अतो गुण इति पररूपत्वम् । युवायुजम् । युवावौ द्विवचन इति द्व्यर्थाभिधायकस्य युष्मच्छब्दस्याविभक्तावपि व्यत्ययेन युवादेशः । शर्ध्यम् । कृधु प्रसहने । अस्माण्ण्यन्तादचो यदिति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । जग्मुषी । गमेर्लिटः क्वसुः । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । वसोः संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणम् । गमहनेत्युपधालोपः । जेन्या । जि जये । औणादिक एन्यप्रत्ययः । टिलोपश्च ॥ [as read]

aśvinā he aśvinau yuvoryuvayorvāṇī vananīyau praśasyāvaśvau yuvāyujaṃ yuvābhyāṃ yujyamānaṃ rathamājidhāvanasamaye [?] asya rathasya yacchardhyaṃ prāpyamādityākhyamavadhibhūtaṃ lakṣyaṃ vapuṣe śobhārthaṃ tadyematuḥ | sarvebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ prāpayāmāsatuḥ | tadanantaraṃ cā jagmuṣyāgatavatī jenyā jetavyā vijetavyā jayena jīyamānā yoṣā sūryā sakhyāya savitre [?] yuvāṃ yuvayoḥ patitvamavṛṇīta | kathamiti | mama yuvāmeva patī bhartārāvityavṛṇīta ‖ yuvoḥ | ṣaṣṭhīdvivacane yoceti yatvasya sarvavidhīnāṃ chandasi vikalpitatvādabhāve śeṣe lopa iti dakāralopaḥ | ato guṇa iti pararūpatvam | yuvāyujam | yuvāvau dvivacana iti dvyarthābhidhāyakasya yuṣmacchabdasyāvibhaktāvapi vyatyayena yuvādeśaḥ | śardhyam | kṛdhu prasahane | asmāṇṇyantādaco yaditi yat | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | jagmuṣī | gamerliṭaḥ kvasuḥ | ugitaśceti ṅīp | vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇamiti saṃprasāraṇam | gamahanetyupadhālopaḥ | jenyā | ji jaye | auṇādika enyapratyayaḥ | ṭilopaśca ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, yuvoḥ vāṇī — your two praiseworthy, desirable horses, yuvāyujam — the chariot yoked by you two, at the time of the contest-run, that śardhyam — the goal to be reached, the end-point called the Āditya — vapuṣe — for splendour — yematuḥ — brought [it]: they got the chariot to it before all the gods. After that, jagmuṣī — she who came, jenyā — the one to be won, the prize, yoṣā — Sūryā, sakhyāya — for friendship (for [the sake of] the Sun [?]), āvṛṇīta — chose your two patitvam — lordship: 'you two are my lords (patī)'."

original p. 471

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.5) (Kannada, rendered)

He aśvinā — O Aśvins; yuvoḥ — your; vāṇī — splendid (horses); yuvāyujam — yoked by you; ratham — the chariot; asya — of this chariot; śardhyam — the goal in the race (the Sun); vapuṣe — for the sake of glory (to win glory); yematuḥ — [they] reached (before all others); ā jagmuṣī — who came; jenyā — [she who was] the prize in the race; yoṣā — Sūryā, the daughter of the Sun; sakhyāya — for friendship; yuvām — you two; patī iti — as (my) husbands; vām — your; patitvam — lordship (husbandhood); avṛṇīta — chose (accepted).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.5) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! Your praiseworthy horses brought the chariot yoked by you to the goal in the race (the Sun), before all [others], and made [you] famed; thereafter Sūryā, the daughter of the Sun, who had been the prize [for the race], chose you (out of trust in you) as her husbands."

English Translation (as printed)

"Aswins, your admirable (horses) bore the car which you had harnessed, (first) to the goal, for the sake of honour, and the damsel, who was the prize, came, through affection, to you, and acknowledged your (husbandship), saying 'You are (my) lords'."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 5)

"For the svayaṃvara of Sūryā, the daughter of Sūrya, you yoked horses to your chariot so that it should go faster than the chariots of all the other gods, and in a moment your chariot, set out to win the prize fixed with the gods, reached the goal in the form of the Āditya. Because [the Aśvins] had reached the goal before all the other gods, the goddess Sūryā, pleased with your power, came to your chariot of her own accord and joined it — so the Aśvins' chariot and their power are described. When a dispute arose among the gods to settle who was superior, the greatness of the Aśvins, as exceeding all, has also been described here, as already [described] earlier."

Vāṇī — vananīyau praśasyāv aśvau: "Sāyaṇa explains 'two horses worthy of being praised' [or: desired]. [Also] since the word vāṇī is stated among the names of speech (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೧-೨೩']), [Skandasvāmin takes it as] vāk — 'speech'.

सुगान् पथो अकृणोन्निरजे गाः प्रावन् वाणीः पुरुहूतं धमन्तीः । (ऋ. सं. ३-३०-१० [as read])

sugān patho akṛṇonniraje gāḥ prāvan vāṇīḥ puruhūtaṃ dhamantīḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-30-10 [as read])

Vāṇīr āpaḥ, vahanāt vāṇyaḥ, vadanāt vācaḥ vāṇyaḥ (Ni. 6-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೬-೩']) — since Yāska explains this way, vāṇī means 'waters' (the voices), 'words', so [he gives] the meaning."

original p. 472

Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued "… the Nirukta author explains [the word vāṇī]. Skandasvāmin: vāṇī here — aśitimatam idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī nāmadheyam — 'though this word is not stated among the names of heaven-and-earth, here it is meant to say dyāvāpṛthivī, heaven and earth' — so he explains."

Śardhyam — śardham iti balanāma: "The word śardhya is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 2-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೨-೮']), so it means 'strength'."

"Skandasvāmin tells here a history:

अश्विनौ काष्ठमयेन दुर्बलेन रथेन गच्छन्तौ दृष्ट्वा वृत्रोऽपजहास । तच्छ्रुत्वा अमर्त्येन [?] द्यावापृथिव्यौ कं रथं सुवर्णखचितं बलवन्तं चक्रतुरिति ॥ [as read; small type [?]]

aśvinau kāṣṭhamayena durbalena rathena gacchantau dṛṣṭvā vṛtro 'pajahāsa | tacchrutvā amartyena [?] dyāvāpṛthivyau kaṃ rathaṃ suvarṇakhacitaṃ balavantaṃ cakraturiti ‖ [as read; small type [?]]

— 'Seeing the Aśvins travelling in a chariot made of wood [i.e. of a rough, wooden build], weak, Vṛtra the asura laughed at them. Hearing this, heaven-and-earth made that chariot studded with gold and strong; and, with great strength.' Vāṇī rathaṃ yematuḥ śardhyam — he explains that heaven and earth made the chariot of the Aśvins strong."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Yuvoḥ — the word yuṣmad; with the genitive dual following, in accordance with the statement sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante, yatva [of yoci, Pā. 7-2-89 as read] does not occur even if an ajādi [case ending] follows; yuvāvau dvivacane (Pā. 7-2-92 as read), yuva is substituted up to ma; by pararūpa, śeṣe lopaḥ (Pā. 7-2-90 as read), elision of the d; since a gives guṇa (the o), ato guṇe (Pā. 6-1-97 as read), pararūpa; ru and visarga for the s; the form yuvoḥ. Yuvāyujam — yujyate iti yuk; root yujir yoge; the suffix kvip; yuvābhyāṃ yujyate iti yuvāyuk; vyatyayo bahulam — here, since the word yuṣmad, though a case ending does not follow, has the sense of the dual, yuva is substituted up to ma; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent; accusative singular.

original p. 473

Yematuḥ — root yama uparame; liṭ, second person dual [as printed; atus, third dual], since kit substitution is intended, atas ca … tṛtīya…, ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśādeḥ liṭi (Pā. 6-4-120 as read), et and elision of the reduplicative [syllable] for the root; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Śardhyam — root kṛdhu prasahane; hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26 as read), ṇic; since the word ends in a [with ṇic], aco yat (Pā. 3-1-97 as read), the suffix yat; since ṇic is a cause, guṇa of the root's light penultimate; ṇer aniṭi (Pā. 6-4-51 as read), elision of the ṇic because yat follows; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 as read), the initial acute. Sakhyāya — sakhyur bhāvaḥ sakhyam; sakhyuryaḥ (Pā. 4-1-?? [as read: 'ಪಾ. ೫-೧-೧೩೫']), the suffix ya; yasyeti ca (Pā. 6-4-148 as read), elision of the i; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Jagmuṣī — root gam̐ḷ gatau; when liṭ has come, kvasuś ca (Pā. 3-2-107 as read), the suffix kvasu; for that reason doubling of the root; cutva in the reduplicative syllable; gamahanajana… (Pā. 6-4-98 as read), elision of the penultimate a of the root; when the feminine is meant, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6 as read), ṅīp; since it has the name bha, vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam (Pā. 6-4-131 as read), saṃprasāraṇa of the v of vasu; pūrvarūpa; śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (Pā. 8-3-60 as read), ṣatva of the s of vasu; by the suffix's accent the u gets the acute. Avṛṇīta — root vṛñ varaṇe, kryādi; laṅ, third person singular; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Jenyā — root ji jaye; the suffix enya, formed by the uṇādi rule; on that account elision of the ṭi of the root; the form jenya; by the suffix's initial acute, the e gets the acute; when the feminine is meant, because it ends in a, ṭāp. ‖ 5 ‖

yuvaṃ rebhaṃ pariṣūteruruṣyatho himena gharmaṃ paritaptamatraye | yuvaṃ śayoravasaṃ pipyathurgavi pra dīrgheṇa vandanastāryāyuṣā ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.6)

हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां रेभमृषिं परिसूतेः परितः प्रेरकादुपद्रवात्कूपपतनादेः [?] उरुष्यथः । रक्षथः । उरुष्यतिी रक्षाकर्मेति यास्कः । (नि. ५-२३ [as read]) । तथात्रयऋषये परितप्तं परितस्तप्तं घर्ममसुरैः पीडार्थं प्रक्षिप्तं दीप्यमानं तुषाग्निं हिमेन शीतेनोदकेनावारयेथाम् । यद्वा । हविषामत्रये भक्षयित्र्येऽग्नये परितप्तं सूर्यशिरःसंतप्तं घर्मं [?] अहर्नाम्नेक्तम् [?] अहर्हिमेन वृष्ट्युदकेन हविःसंपादकव्रीह्याद्युत्पत्तिप्रतिबन्धकमावारयेथाम् । अपि च शयोरेतत्संज्ञस्यर्षेर्गवि निवृत्तप्रसवायां धेनावसं रक्षकं पयो युवं युवां पिप्यथुः । प्रवर्धितवन्तौ । तथा जीर्णाङ्गो वन्दनः ऋषिर्दीर्घेणायुषा प्र तारि । युवाभ्यां प्रवर्धितः ॥ [as read]

he aśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ rebhamṛṣiṃ parisūteḥ paritaḥ prerakādupadravātkūpapatanādeḥ [?] uruṣyathaḥ | rakṣathaḥ | uruṣyatiī rakṣākarmeti yāskaḥ | (ni. 5-23 [as read]) | tathātrayaṛṣaye paritaptaṃ paritastaptaṃ gharmamasuraiḥ pīḍārthaṃ prakṣiptaṃ dīpyamānaṃ tuṣāgniṃ himena śītenodakenāvārayethām | yadvā | haviṣāmatraye bhakṣayitrye 'gnaye paritaptaṃ sūryaśiraḥsaṃtaptaṃ gharmaṃ [?] aharnāmnektam [?] aharhimena vṛṣṭyudakena haviḥsaṃpādakavrīhyādyutpattipratibandhakamāvārayethām | api ca śayoretatsaṃjñasyarṣergavi nivṛttaprasavāyāṃ dhenāvasaṃ rakṣakaṃ payo yuvaṃ yuvāṃ pipyathuḥ | pravardhitavantau | tathā jīrṇāṅgo vandanaḥ ṛṣirdīrgheṇāyuṣā pra tāri | yuvābhyāṃ pravardhitaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, you protect (uruṣyathaḥ) the ṛṣi Rebha from pariṣūti — the calamity that pressed on all sides, such as the fall into the well; [Yāska]: uruṣyati is a word for protection (Ni. 5-23 as read). And for the ṛṣi Atri, you kept off the gharma — the blazing husk-fire, put round by the asuras to torment him — taptam, burning all round — with himena — cold water. Or: for Atri — [i.e.] Agni, the eater of oblations — gharma, the heat of the Sun's head, that checks the growth of the rice and the like which produce the oblations, you kept off with hima — rain-water. And for Śayu, in his cow that had ceased bearing, you filled with milk, with avasam — protective milk; and Vandana, the ṛṣi of worn-out limbs, was pra tāri — raised up by you with long life."

original p. 475

Bhāṣya of Ṛk 6, concluded; grammar tail, small type "pra- the prefix tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, with pra: pra tāri; āvasam — avater auṇādiko 'sac; pipyathuḥ — pyāyī vṛddhau [root], vyatyayena parasmaipadam; liṭi dyajjoḥ [as read: liṭy abhyāsasyobhayeṣām?] (Pā. 6-1-?? [as read]) iti ī-bhāvaḥ" — characterized, not transcribed.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.6) (Kannada, rendered)

He) aśvinā — O Aśvins; yuvam — you two; rebham — the ṛṣi Rebha; pariṣūteḥ — from the calamity; uruṣyathaḥ — you protected; atraye — for the ṛṣi Atri (for Agni, the eater of oblations); paritaptam — [which was] burning; gharmam — the fire (the Sun's heat — [heat] that checks the growth of the rice and the like, which sustain the oblations); himena — by cold water (by rain-water) — (you warded off); (and śayoḥ — of the ṛṣi named Śayu; gavi — in the cow; avasam — protecting (milk); yuvam — you two; pipyathuḥ — made grow; tathā — likewise; vandanaḥ — the aged ṛṣi Vandana; dīrgheṇa āyuṣā — with long life; pra tāri — was raised up (by you).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.6) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! You both removed the calamity that had come upon the ṛṣi Rebha; you warded off, with cold water, the fire that tormented Atri (for Agni, who eats the oblations, with rain-water you warded off the heat of the Sun, which destroys the rice and the like); you made the cow of Śayu rich in milk; and to Vandana, the aged ṛṣi, you granted long life."

English Translation (as printed)

"You preserved Rebha from the violence around him; you quenched with snow, for Atri, the scorching heat; you generated milk in the cow of Sayu; and (by you) was Vandana endowed with prolonged life."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 6)

Yuvaṃ rebhaṃ pariṣūter uruṣyathaḥ — yuvāṃ rebhaṃ ṛṣiṃ pariteḥ prerakād upadravāt kūpapatanādyād rakṣathaḥ: "Uruṣyati [is] rakṣākarma (Ni. 3-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೨೩']): since the word uruṣya is stated as a root with the sense 'to protect', the meaning is that the Aśvins saved the ṛṣi Rebha from the calamity that was near him, or from the troubles which the asuras caused him by binding him and throwing him into a well. When the asuras seized the ṛṣi Atri and put him in a husk-fire, the Aśvins, hearing his praise, with cold water from a …" continues on p. 476

original p. 476

Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued "… and saved him — such is the one meaning Sāyaṇa gives; and further, taking atri as meaning Agni, who eats the oblations, he gives another meaning: that [the Aśvins] by means of rain-waters warded off the heat that arose for this Agni — [as] the rice and the like were never produced because of the heat of the sun's rays. Skandasvāmin explains only the account of the protection of the ṛṣi Atri:

हिमेनाग्निं घ्रंसमवारयेथां पितुमतीमूर्जमस्मा अधत्तम् । ऋबीसे अत्रिमश्विनावनीतमुन्निन्यथुः सर्वगणं स्वस्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-८ [as read])

himenāgniṃ ghraṃsamavārayethāṃ pitumatīmūrjamasmā adhattam | ṛbīse atrimaśvināvanītamunninyathuḥ sarvagaṇaṃ svasti ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-8 [as read])

— quoting this Ṛk."

"[Śayu] was a ṛṣi who was aged, and his cow had come to an end of calving; they made her give milk, turning her to the state of youth — thus it is described; and by lifting the ṛṣi Vandana out of the well and giving him strength they saved him: the power of the Aśvins is thus described."

Gharmam — dīptam: "so Skandasvāmin explains. The word gharma is stated among the twelve names of day (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೩೧']) and among the fifteen names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-17 [as read])."

Avasam — rakṣakam: "'that which gives protection' is Sāyaṇa's exposition; Skandasvāmin: avasa is a word denoting pathyodana (suitable cooked food); the pathyodana of Śayu is in the form of milk — so he explains. And Yāska, when explaining the meaning of the word avasa, [quotes]:

मयोभूर्वातो अभि वातूस्रा ऊर्जस्वती रोषधीरा रिशन्ताम् । पीवस्वतीर्जीवधन्याः पिबन्त्ववसाय पद्वते रुद्र मृळ ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१८६-१ [as read])

mayobhūrvāto abhi vātūsrā ūrjasvatī roṣadhīrā riśantām | pīvasvatīrjīvadhanyāḥ pibantvavasāya padvate rudra mṛḷa ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 10-186-1 [as read])

योनिष्ट इन्द्र निषदे अकारि तमा नि षीद स्वानो नार्वा । विमुच्या वयो ऽवसायाश्वान्दोषा वस्तोर्वहीयसः प्रपित्वे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१०४-१ [as read])

yoniṣṭa indra niṣade akāri tamā ni ṣīda svāno nārvā | vimucyā vayo 'vasāyāśvāndoṣā vastorvahīyasaḥ prapitve ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-104-1 [as read])

— quoting these two Ṛks, he explains avasāya padvate rudra mṛḷa thus: pathyedam — avasāya padvate: pathedvā; avasaṃ — gāvaḥ pathyādanam; avater gatyartha …; tasmān nāvagṛhṇanti avasāyārthā … (Ni. 1-?? [as read]). The word avasa conveys 'food [for the cattle] on the way'. From the root av a suffix comes, giving avasāya [as read]."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Pariṣūteḥ — root sūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane; in the feminine, striyāṃ ktin (Pā. 3-3-94 as read), the suffix ktin; since it is tādi and nit, tādau ca niti kṛty ataḥ (Pā. 6-2-50 as read), the gati (pari) keeps its natural accent as an exception to the kṛt accent. Uruṣyathaḥ — the root uruṣya [although it is not listed in the dhātupāṭha], is established by the ākṛtigaṇa; it is used in the sense of protection; laṭ, second person dual; because it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Paritaptam — root tapa saṃtāpe; niṣṭhā, the suffix kta; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read), the gati keeps its natural accent. Avasam — root ava rakṣaṇe; the auṇādika suffix asac; ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163 as read), the final acute; accusative singular. Pipyathuḥ — root pyāyī vṛddhau; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 as read), the parasmaipada; liṭ, second person dual, parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus… (Pā. 3-4-82 as read), athus substituted; liṭy abhyāsasyobhayeṣām [as printed liṭyanyatarasyām] (Pā. 6-1-8 as read), saṃprasāraṇa, ī for the root; its doubling; hrasvaḥ for the reduplicative syllable; ekāco dve prathamasya…, yaṇ; tiṅanta nighāta. Tāri — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; in the passive, luṅ, third person singular, the suffix ta; ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ (Pā. 3-1-66 as read), ciṇ for cli; since it is ñit, aco ñṇiti (Pā. 7-2-115 as read), vṛddhi of the root's ṛ; becomes r-final; ciṇo luk (Pā. 6-4-104 as read), luk for the ta that follows; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75 as read), the augment aṭ does not occur; tiṅanta nighāta. ‖ 6 ‖

yuvam | vandanam | niḥ 'ṛtam | jaraṇyayā | ratham | na | dasrā | karaṇā | sam | invathaḥ | kṣetrāt | ā | vipram | janathaḥ | vipanyayā | pra | vām | atra | vidhate | daṃsanā | bhuvat ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.7)

हे दस्रावश्विनौ युवं युवां जरण्यया जरया निरृतं निःशेषेण प्राप्तं वन्दनमृषिं करणा कर्मणां कर्तारौ शिल्पकुशलौ युवां समिन्वथः । समधत्तम् । पुनर्युवानमकुरुतम् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । रथं न यथा कश्चिच्छिल्पी जीर्णं रथं पुनरभिनवं करोति तद्वत् । अपि च विपन्यया स्तुत्या गर्भस्थेन वामदेवेन स्तुतौ सन्तौ क्षेत्रादा आकारः समुच्चये । मातुरुदरलक्षणाज्जन्मस्थानाद्विप्रं मेधाविनं तमृषिं जनथः । जनयथश्च । तथा वां युवयोर्दंसना रक्षणात्मकं कर्मात्रास्मै विधते परिचरते यजमानाय प्र भुवत् । प्रभवतु । रक्षितुं समर्थं भवतु ॥ निरृतम् । ऋ गतौ । कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जरण्यया । जरणक्रियोर्हा जरण्या । अन्त्यावस्थाच्छन्दसि चेति यः । करणा । करोतेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति (पा. ३-२-७५ [as read]) युच् । इन्वथः । इवि व्याप्तौ । इदित्त्वान्नुम् । … जनथः । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । चिच्छेत्यथावृद्धिः [?] । जनिजॄभ्यां … [as read]

he dasrāvaśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ jaraṇyayā jarayā nirṛtaṃ niḥśeṣeṇa prāptaṃ vandanamṛṣiṃ karaṇā karmaṇāṃ kartārau śilpakuśalau yuvāṃ saminvathaḥ | samadhattam | punaryuvānamakurutam | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | rathaṃ na yathā kaścicchilpī jīrṇaṃ rathaṃ punarabhinavaṃ karoti tadvat | api ca vipanyayā stutyā garbhasthena vāmadevena stutau santau kṣetrādā ākāraḥ samuccaye | māturudaralakṣaṇājjanmasthānādvipraṃ medhāvinaṃ tamṛṣiṃ janathaḥ | janayathaśca | tathā vāṃ yuvayordaṃsanā rakṣaṇātmakaṃ karmātrāsmai vidhate paricarate yajamānāya pra bhuvat | prabhavatu | rakṣituṃ samarthaṃ bhavatu ‖ nirṛtam | ṛ gatau | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | jaraṇyayā | jaraṇakriyorhā jaraṇyā | antyāvasthācchandasi ceti yaḥ | karaṇā | karoteranyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti (pā. 3-2-75 [as read]) yuc | invathaḥ | ivi vyāptau | idittvānnum | … janathaḥ | janī prādurbhāve | cicchetyathāvṛddhiḥ [?] | janijṝbhyāṃ … [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Dasras, Aśvins: you — jaraṇyayā — by old age, nirṛtam — completely overtaken, [the ṛṣi] Vandana — you, karaṇā — makers, skilled in craft, sam invathaḥ — set right; you made him young again. The illustration: ratham na — as some craftsman makes a worn-out chariot new again, so [you did]. And vipanyayā — through praise by Vāmadeva in the womb — when praised, kṣetrāt ā [ā in the sense of 'and'] — from the womb of the mother, the place of birth, you caused the wise ṛṣi (vipra) to be born. And so, vām — your daṃsanā — protecting action, atra — here, for this man who serves (vidhate, the sacrificer), pra bhuvat — may it prevail, may it be able to protect."

original p. 479

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.7) (Kannada, rendered)

Dasrā — O Dasras (Aśvins); yuvam — you two; jaraṇyayā — by old age (decrepitude); nirṛtam — completely wasted; vandanam — the ṛṣi Vandana; karaṇā — you who are skilled in your deeds; rathaṃ na — as a craftsman [repairs] a worn-out chariot, [so]; sam invathaḥ — you made [him] anew (young again); vipanyayā — [by the praise] of Vāmadeva, in the womb; kṣetrāt ā — from the birth-place (the mother's womb); vipram — that wise ṛṣi; janathaḥ — you made to be born; — likewise; vām — your; daṃsanā — action in the form of protection; atra — here; vidhate — [to him] who serves you (to the sacrificer); pra bhuvat — let it be of the power [to protect].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.7) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Dasras (Aśvins)! You, skilled in your deeds, gave youth to the ṛṣi Vandana, who had been reduced by old age, as a craftsman [repairs] a worn-out chariot; and, moved by the praise of Vāmadeva in the womb, you made that ṛṣi to be born from his mother's womb; may your protecting action be able to protect this sacrificer who serves you."

English Translation (as printed)

"Skilful Dasras, you restored Vandana, when debilitated by old age, as a wheelwright repairs a worn-out car; (moved) by his praises, you brought forth the sage (Vamadeva) from the womb: may your (glorious) deeds be (displayed) for him who in this place offers you worship."

original p. 480

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 7)

Jaraṇyayā — jaraṇakriyārhā jaraṇyā: "'softness' [or 'old age-ness'] is the meaning."

Rathaṃ na — yathā kaścit śilpī jīrṇaṃ rathaṃ punar abhinavaṃ karoti tadvat: "As a craftsman makes new again an old chariot that is crumbling, by his skill, so the Aśvins made the body of the aged ṛṣi Vandana like a young body and protected him — thus it is described."

Kṣetrāt vipraṃ vipanyayā ā janathaḥ — vāmadevena stutau mātur udaralakṣaṇāt janmasthānāt medhāvinaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ janayathaḥ: "The ṛṣi Vāmadeva, in the womb of his mother, not knowing how to come out of his mother's womb, praised the Aśvins, and by their favour came out of the womb — the history of the Aśvins' protection of the ṛṣi Vāmadeva is told here. Skandasvāmin:

कश्चिद्दृषिः मृतभार्यो वृद्धश्च पुत्रकामो ऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तस्मा अश्विनावयोनिजं क्षेत्रात्पुत्रं जनयांचक्रतुरिति । तदेतदुच्यते । क्षेत्रात्कृष्टा भूमिः क्षेत्रमुच्यते । ततः विप्रं मेधाविनमजनथः जनितवन्तौ ॥ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

kaściddṛṣiḥ mṛtabhāryo vṛddhaśca putrakāmo 'śvinau tuṣṭāva | tasmā aśvināvayonijaṃ kṣetrātputraṃ janayāṃcakraturiti | tadetaducyate | kṣetrātkṛṣṭā bhūmiḥ kṣetramucyate | tataḥ vipraṃ medhāvinamajanathaḥ janitavantau ‖ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

— 'A certain ṛṣi, whose wife was dead and who was old, wishing for a son, praised the Aśvins; the Aśvins caused a son to be born to him, not from a womb [?], from a field' [as read]; hence 'a field' is the ploughed ground, kṣetra; from it vipra — the wise — was born." He thus explains the story: because the ṛṣi's wife was dead there was no wife; he was very old; but he had a desire for a son; therefore he praised the Aśvins; they made a son who was ayonija [born without a womb?] for him."

Vipram — medhāvinam: "The word vipra is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19 [as read]):

यो अनिध्मो दीदयदप्स्वन्तर्यं विप्रास ईळते अध्वरेषु । (ऋ. सं. १०-३०-४ [as read])

yo anidhmo dīdayadapsvantaryaṃ viprāsa īḷate adhvareṣu | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-30-4 [as read])

In this Ṛk too the word vipra is used in the sense of 'wise'."

Daṃsanā — rakṣaṇātmakaṃ karma: "'Action in the form of protection': so Sāyaṇa explains it as the action that protected the ṛṣi Vāmadeva by bringing him out of the womb. [Skandasvāmin:] daṃsanā darśanīyā pravṛttir yuvor eṣā kṣetrajananalakṣaṇā stutibhiḥ paricaritus tasya ṛṣer arthāya darśanīyā — 'this beautiful act of yours, consisting of the birth [of a son] from the field, is worthy to be seen for the sake of the ṛṣi who served you with praises'. Because [you] procured a son from the field, according to the wish of the ṛṣi, your acts are wonderful, as good for the ṛṣi who served you with praises" — such is Skandasvāmin's exposition. Yuvām …

original p. 481

…concluded "… mukhyatvāt [?] — apart from the Aśvins, no other deity has performed such deeds [as these]; hence it is to be understood that the compassion of these Aśvins is unbounded towards those who praise them."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Nirṛtam — root ṛ gatau; in the passive sense niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 as read), the suffix kta; since it is kit, guṇa does not occur; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read), as an exception to the kṛt accent, the gati (nir) keeps its natural accent. Jaraṇyayā — root jṝṣ vayohānau; in the abstract sense the suffix lyuṭ; yuvoranākau (Pā. 7-1-1 as read), ana substituted; the form jaraṇa; "worthy of old-age" is jaraṇyā: antyāvasthāc chandasi ca [as printed; chandasi ca] the suffix ya; by yasyeti ca, elision of the former a; in the feminine, ṭāp; by the suffix's accent the final acute; instrumental singular form. Karaṇā — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-75 as read), in the agent sense the suffix yuc; yuvoranākau (Pā. 7-1-1 as read), ana; on account of the suffix, guṇa of the root's i-vowel; becomes r-final; since it is cit, ciṭaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163 as read), the final acute; with the dual au following, supāṃ sulug, ā for it. Invathaḥ — root ivi vyāptau; idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-58 as read), num for the root; laṭ, second person dual, thas; kartari śap (Pā. 3-1-68 as read), śap vikaraṇa; because it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Janathaḥ — root janī prādurbhāve; hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26 as read), ṇic; ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116 as read), because of ṇic, vṛddhi of the root's penultimate; jñaniji… [janījṛṣkna… (Pā. 3-1-?? as read)] — because mit is the name it gets, mitāṃ hrasvaḥ (Pā. 6-4-92 as read), shortening of the penultimate; after the ṇijanta, laṭ, second person dual, thas; śap vikaraṇa; chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 as read), since śap has the ārdhadhātuka name, ṇer aniṭi (Pā. 6-4-51 as read), elision of the ṇic on account of it; the form janathaḥ; tiṅanta nighāta accent.

original p. 482

Grammar of Ṛk 7, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Vipanyayā — root pana stutau; aśvāghasyāt [as read; āghasya] (Uṇ. sū. 4-?? [as read: 'ಉ. ಸೂ. ೪-೧೩೫']) — in the abstract sense the suffix yat; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 as read), the initial acute is obtained, but by vyatyaya the final acute occurs; in the compound the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent; in the feminine, ṭāp; instrumental singular form. Vidhate — root vidha vidhāne; tudādi; in the sense of laṭ, śatṛ; tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ (Pā. 3-1-77 as read), śa vikaraṇa; since it is ñit, guṇa of the root's light penultimate does not occur; dative singular form; because śatṛ is numrahita [without num] and the case ending follows it, śaturanumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173 as read), the acute on the case ending. Bhuvat — root bhū sattāyām; leṭ, third person singular, the suffix tip; iteś ca lopaḥ pare [ita ś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu] (Pā. 3-4-97 as read), elision of the i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), the augment aṭ; bahulaṃ chandasi, luk for śap; bhūsuvos tiṅi (Pā. 7-3-88 as read), since the prohibition of guṇa of the root's u occurs, ajiknudhātubhruvām (Pā. 6-4-77 as read), uvaṅ substituted; tiṅanta nighāta accent. ‖ 7 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.8)

अगच्छतं कृपमाणं परावति पितुः स्वस्य त्यजसा निबाधितम् । स्वर्वतीरित ऊतीर्युवोरह चित्रा अभीके अभवन्नभिष्टयः ॥ ८ ॥

agacchataṃ kṛpamāṇaṃ parāvati pituḥ svasya tyajasā nibādhitam | svarvatīrita ūtīryuvoraha citrā abhīke abhavannabhiṣṭayaḥ ‖ 8 ‖

original p. 483

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.8)

अगच्छतम् । कृपमाणम् । परा‍ऽवति । पितुः । स्वस्य । त्यजसा । निऽबाधितम् । स्वःऽवतीः । इतः । ऊतीः । युवोः । अह । चित्राः । अभीके । अभवन् । अभिष्टयः ॥ ८ ॥

agacchatam | kṛpamāṇam | parā 'vati | pituḥ | svasya | tyajasā | ni 'bādhitam | svaḥ 'vatīḥ | itaḥ | ūtīḥ | yuvoḥ | aha | citrāḥ | abhīke | abhavan | abhiṣṭayaḥ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.8)

हे अश्विनौ परावति दूरदेशे समुद्रमध्ये स्वस्य पितुस्तुग्रस्य त्यजसा त्यागेन निबाधितं पीडितं भुज्युं कृपमाणं स्तुवन्तमगच्छतम् । युवां रक्षणार्थं गतवन्तौ । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्धे अश्विनौ स्वर्वतीः स्वर्वत्यः शोभनगमनयुक्ता इते इतोमुखाश्चित्राश्चायनीया युवोरह युवयोरेवोतीरूतयो रक्षा अभीके समीपेऽभिष्टयः सर्वैः प्राणिभिरभ्येषणीया अभवन् । भवन्ति ॥ कृपमाणम् । कृपेः स्तुतिकर्मा । अयं च तुदादिर्द्रष्टव्यः । स्वर्वतीः । सुपूर्वादर्तेर्भावे विच् । ततो मतुप् । छन्दसीर इति मतुपो वत्वम् । अभिष्टयः । इषु इच्छायाम् । भावे क्तिन् । शकन्ध्वादित्वात्परेरूपत्वम् ॥ [as read]

he aśvinau parāvati dūradeśe samudramadhye svasya pitustugrasya tyajasā tyāgena nibādhitaṃ pīḍitaṃ bhujyuṃ kṛpamāṇaṃ stuvantamagacchatam | yuvāṃ rakṣaṇārthaṃ gatavantau | yasmādevaṃ tasmāddhe aśvinau svarvatīḥ svarvatyaḥ śobhanagamanayuktā ite itomukhāścitrāścāyanīyā yuvoraha yuvayorevotīrūtayo rakṣā abhīke samīpe 'bhiṣṭayaḥ sarvaiḥ prāṇibhirabhyeṣaṇīyā abhavan | bhavanti ‖ kṛpamāṇam | kṛpeḥ stutikarmā | ayaṃ ca tudādirdraṣṭavyaḥ | svarvatīḥ | supūrvādarterbhāve vic | tato matup | chandasīra iti matupo vatvam | abhiṣṭayaḥ | iṣu icchāyām | bhāve ktin | śakandhvāditvātparerūpatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, when Bhujyu, afflicted (nibādhitam) by the abandonment (tyajasā) by his own father, Tugra, was parāvati — in a far-off place, in the middle of the sea — kṛpamāṇam — praising [you], you went to him: you went for protection. Since it is so, therefore, O Aśvins, svarvatīḥ — fine-moving, itaḥ — turned toward [us?], wondrous (citrāḥ) ūtīḥ — protections of you two, abhīke — near (at hand), abhiṣṭayaḥ — to be sought by all beings, abhavan — have become."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.8) (Kannada, rendered; page continues)

He aśvinau — O Aśvins; parāvati — in a far-off place (in the middle of the sea); svasya pituḥ — of his own father (Tugra); tyajasā — through his abandonment; nibādhitam — afflicted; kṛpamāṇam — [Bhujyu], who praised you; agacchatam — you went (to protect); he aśvinau — O Aśvins; svarvatīḥ — [which are] of auspicious motion; itaḥ — facing (this way, to us); citrāḥ — wondrous; yuvoḥ aha — your own; ūtīḥ — protecting acts; abhīke — near; abhiṣṭayaḥ — to be desired (by all beings); abhavan — have become.

original p. 484

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.8) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! You set out, in a far-off place (in the middle of the sea), to praise [you] and to protect Bhujyu, who was then in distress, abandoned by his father; therefore (all) of them desire that your wonderful, protective acts, performed by you who move auspiciously, be (always) easy to obtain near at hand."

English Translation (as printed)

"You repaired to him who, afflicted by the abandonment of his own father, praised you from afar: hence your prompt and wonderful succours have been wished to be at hand (by all)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 8)

"Bhujyu, when he was going, abandoned by his father, to subdue enemies, [and] was in the middle of the sea, helpless and in distress — the Aśvins, knowing this, came out of compassion to protect him; and since the protection of all other beings, too, comes about only through the compassion of these Aśvins, it is described [here] that their compassion is desirable to all. In explaining the first half of this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa construes the words with reference to the protection of Bhujyu, the son of Tugra only. Skandasvāmin:

अगच्छतं चक्षुःप्रदानार्थं गतवन्तौ युवां कृपमाणं स्तुवन्तं ऋज्राश्वं प्रति ।

agacchataṃ cakṣuḥpradānārthaṃ gatavantau yuvāṃ kṛpamāṇaṃ stuvantaṃ ṛjrāśvaṃ prati |

— 'you went for the sake of giving sight, to Ṛjrāśva, who was praising [you]': he explains this as the protection of Ṛjrāśva, saying that the Aśvins set out to give eyes to Ṛjrāśva, who was praising them after losing his eyes. According to this, he explains the meanings of the words in each case separately."

Tyajasā — tyāgena bādhitaṃ pīḍitam: "Sāyaṇa takes it in reference to Bhujyu: 'one who was in distress because his father abandoned him'. Pituḥ svasya tyajasā nibādhitam — ātmīyasya pituḥ kopena śāpajanitāndhyena pīḍitam — 'afflicted by blindness produced by his own father's curse out of anger': Skandasvāmin explains it as Ṛjrāśva, who was in distress because of the blindness that arose from it."

Citram — cāyanīyam: "'worthy of worship' is the meaning. In explaining the meaning of the word citra, Yāska has explained citram cāyanīyam maṃhanīyam (Ni. 3-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೨']) in one example, and in another example citraṃ devānām [Ṛ. 1-115-1] he explains the meaning as 'worthy of being worshipped'."

original p. 485

Ūtīḥ — ūtayaḥ rakṣaṇāḥ: "'protections' is Sāyaṇa's [meaning]; and Skandasvāmin also explains yajñān prati gatayaḥ — 'goings to sacrifices'."

Abhīke — samīpe: "'near' is Sāyaṇa's explanation. Skandasvāmin, explaining the latter half of this Ṛk, [construes] citrā abhavan bhīke abhiṣṭayaḥ:

सर्वैः परिचारकैः सह इतः स्थानात् यज्ञान् प्रत्यासन्ने योगकाले युवां गच्छतं तत्र चाभ्येथे । अथवा अभीके इति संग्राममाम सर्वैस्सैन्योर्ध्वभिः सह गच्छथो युवां संग्रामे गत्वा चाभिगच्छथः शत्रूनित्यर्थः ।

sarvaiḥ paricārakaiḥ saha itaḥ sthānāt yajñān pratyāsanne yogakāle yuvāṃ gacchataṃ tatra cābhyethe | athavā abhīke iti saṃgrāmamāma sarvaissainyordhvabhiḥ saha gacchatho yuvāṃ saṃgrāme gatvā cābhigacchathaḥ śatrūnityarthaḥ |

— 'You come from this place with your attendants to the sacrifices, [as the] time of joining [with the oblation] approaches, and there you receive [the worship]. Or: abhīke is the word for 'battle': you go with your warriors to the battlefield to fight, and, going, you face the enemies': so he explains."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Agacchatam — root gam̐ḷ gatau; laṅ, second person dual, tam substituted; śap vikaraṇa; iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ (Pā. 7-3-77 as read), ccha for the root's final; the augment aṭ; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; since the augment aṭ is udātta, the initial acute. Kṛpamāṇam — the root kṛpa is used in the sense of praising; it should be inferred that it is read in the tudādi group; in the sense of laṭ, the suffix śānac; śa vikaraṇa; since it is ñit, guṇa of the light penultimate does not occur; ānemuk (Pā. 7-2-82 as read), the augment muk for the a-ending. Tyajasā — root tyaja hānau; the suffix asun, which comes on account of "all roots"; since it is nit, jñityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197 as read), the initial acute; instrumental singular form. Nibādhitam — root bādha vilodane; in the passive sense niṣṭhā, the suffix kta; ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-35 as read), the augment iṭ; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read), the gati (ni) keeps its natural accent. Svarvatīḥ — the prefix su; root ṛ gatau; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-75 as read), in the abstract sense, the suffix vic; on that account guṇa of the root; becomes r-final …

original p. 486

Grammar of Ṛk 8, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Svarvatīḥ (continued) — becomes r-final; when "svar asya asti" is intended, tad asyāsty asmin (Pā. 5-2-94 as read), the suffix matup; chandasīraḥ (Pā. 8-2-15 as read), v for the m of matup; in the feminine, since it is ugit, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6 as read), ṅīp. Ūtīḥ — root ava rakṣaṇe; in the abstract sense, ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām (Pā. 3-3-174 as read), the suffix ktic; jvaratvarasrivyaviramavām (Pā. 6-4-20 as read), ūṭ for the v and the penultimate; the form ūti; the final acute. Abhiṣṭayaḥ — the prefix abhi; root iṣu icchāyām, tudādi; in the abstract sense, striyāṃ ktin (Pā. 3-3-94 as read), the suffix ktin; since it is kit, guṇa of the root's light penultimate does not occur; by ṣṭutva, ṭa for the t of the suffix; abhi + iṣṭi, since it is read in the śakandhvādi group, śakandhvādiṣu pararūpaṃ vācyam [as read], pararūpa; nominative plural form. ‖ 8 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.9)

उत स्या वां मधुमन्मक्षिकारपन्मदे सोमस्यौशिजो हुवन्यति । युवं दधीचो मन आ विवासथोऽथा शिरः प्रति वामश्व्यं वदत् ॥ ९ ॥

uta syā vāṃ madhumanmakṣikārapanmade somasyauśijo huvanyati | yuvaṃ dadhīco mana ā vivāsatho 'thā śiraḥ prati vāmaśvyaṃ vadat ‖ 9 ‖

original p. 487

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.9)

उत । स्या । वाम् । मधुऽमत् । मक्षिका । अरपत् । मदे । सोमस्य । औशिजः । हुवन्यति । युवम् । दधीचः । मनः । आ । विवासथः । अथ । शिरः । प्रति । वाम् । अश्व्यम् । वदत् ॥ ९ ॥

uta | syā | vām | madhu 'mat | makṣikā | arapat | made | somasya | auśijaḥ | huvanyati | yuvam | dadhīcaḥ | manaḥ | ā | vivāsathaḥ | atha | śiraḥ | prati | vām | aśvyam | vadat ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.9)

उताशि [?] च हे अश्विनौ मधुमन्मधुमन्तौ वां युवां स्या सा मक्षिका सरघा मधुकामा सत्यरपत् [?] । अस्तौत् । तथौशिज उशिजः पुत्रः कक्षीवान् सोमस्य पानेन युवयोर्मदे हर्षे निमित्तभूते सति हुवन्यति । युवामाह्वयतीति । युवं युवां च तस्मै मक्षिकायै मधु दातुं मधुविद्यार्थिनौ सन्तौ दधीचे आथर्वणस्य ऋषेर्मनः शुश्रूषया आ विवासथः । पर्यचरतम् । अथानन्तरं तस्मिन्नृषौ सत्येश्वर्यां युवाभ्यां प्रतिहितमश्वस्य संबन्धि यच्छिरस्तद्वां युवां प्रति मधुविद्यामवदत् । स ऋषिरश्वेन शिरसोपदिष्टवानित्यर्थः ॥ मधुमत् । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्लुक् । अरपत् । रप लप व्यक्तायां वाचि । मदे । मदी हर्षे । मदोऽनुपसर्ग इति भावे ऽप् । हुवन्यति । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । लुटी क्त्वे भावे लुट् । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । हवनमात्मन इच्छति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । अन्त्यलोपश्छान्दसः । वर्णव्यापकोत्वेत्वम् । अश्व्यम् । अश्वे भवमश्व्यम् । भवे छन्दसीति यत् ॥ [as read]

utāśi [?] ca he aśvinau madhumanmadhumantau vāṃ yuvāṃ syā sā makṣikā saraghā madhukāmā satyarapat [?] | astaut | tathauśija uśijaḥ putraḥ kakṣīvān somasya pānena yuvayormade harṣe nimittabhūte sati huvanyati | yuvāmāhvayatīti | yuvaṃ yuvāṃ ca tasmai makṣikāyai madhu dātuṃ madhuvidyārthinau santau dadhīce ātharvaṇasya ṛṣermanaḥ śuśrūṣayā ā vivāsathaḥ | paryacaratam | athānantaraṃ tasminnṛṣau satyeśvaryāṃ yuvābhyāṃ pratihitamaśvasya saṃbandhi yacchirastadvāṃ yuvāṃ prati madhuvidyāmavadat | sa ṛṣiraśvena śirasopadiṣṭavānityarthaḥ ‖ madhumat | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterluk | arapat | rapa lapa vyaktāyāṃ vāci | made | madī harṣe | mado 'nupasarga iti bhāve 'p | huvanyati | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | luṭī ktve bhāve luṭ | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | havanamātmana icchati | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | antyalopaśchāndasaḥ | varṇavyāpakotvetvam | aśvyam | aśve bhavamaśvyam | bhave chandasīti yat ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "And, O Aśvins, that honey-bee (sarghā), honey-loving, madhumat — praised you, honey-possessed; and likewise Auśija, the son of Uśij — Kakṣīvān — hu­vanyati — calls you, when drunk with the soma (somasya made). And you two, wishing [to give] honey to that bee, [and] seeking the honey-knowledge, dadhīcaḥ manaḥ ā vivāsathaḥ — served the mind of Dadhīca, the descendant of Atharvan, with attention. Thereafter, śiraḥ aśvyam — the horse's head that had been set [on him] by you — vām prati madhuvidyām avadat — spoke the honey-knowledge to you: the ṛṣi taught [you] with the horse's head."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.9) (Kannada, rendered; page continues)

Uta — and; aśvinau — O Aśvins; madhumat — [you two] endowed with honey; vām — you two; syā makṣikā — that bee; arapat — praised; auśijaḥ — Kakṣīvān, the son of Uśij; somasya — of the soma-juice; made — in the joy (of drinking, for you two); huvanyati — calls you; yuvam — you two (to give honey to the bee, or to learn the honey-knowledge); dadhīcaḥ — of Atharvan's [son]; …

original p. 488

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 9, concluded "… dadhīcaḥ — of the ṛṣi (Dadhīca, Atharvan's son); manaḥ — the mind; ā vivāsathaḥ — you propitiated (made [him] pleased); atha — thereafter (when he was pleased); aśvyam — belonging to a horse; śiraḥ — the head (that was given to that Dadhyañc by you); vām prati — to you; vadat — [it] told (the honey-knowledge) (taught)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.9) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! The bee praised you, who are endowed with honey (for honey); Kakṣīvān, the son of Uśij, calls you so that you may be pleased by drinking the soma-juice; when you had won the favour of the ṛṣi Atharvan [Dadhīca] (to give honey to the bee), he taught you, with the horse's head that you had given him, the honey-knowledge."

English Translation (as printed)

"That honey-seeking bee also murmured your praise; the son of Usij invokes you to the exhilaration of the Soma Juice: you conciliated the mind of Dadhyanch, so that, provided with the head of a horse, he taught you (the mystic science)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 9)

Makṣikā madhumat arapat — "The history is hinted at in Sāyaṇa's exposition: the bees known as saraghā — [which] when they could not find flowers for their honey, though honey was essential for them — praised the Aśvins and received the honey. Skandasvāmin [says] clearly:

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । सरघानामा मधुकर्यः मक्षिकाः ताः कस्यां चिदनावृष्ट्यां शुष्कासु सर्वपुष्पजातिषु क्षुधा बाध्यमानाः मध्वर्थिन्यो ऽश्विनावाजुहुवुः । ताभ्य उपगम्याश्विनौ मधु ददतुः तत्ताः सपुरिति । [as read; small type [?]]

atretihāsamācakṣate | saraghānāmā madhukaryaḥ makṣikāḥ tāḥ kasyāṃ cidanāvṛṣṭyāṃ śuṣkāsu sarvapuṣpajātiṣu kṣudhā bādhyamānāḥ madhvarthinyo 'śvināvājuhuvuḥ | tābhya upagamyāśvinau madhu dadatuḥ tattāḥ sapuriti | [as read; small type [?]]

— and, explaining this meaning, quoting this Ṛk:

मधु प्रियं भरथो यत्सरड्भ्यस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् । (ऋ. सं. १-११२-२१ [as read])

madhu priyaṃ bharatho yatsaraḍbhyastābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-21 [as read])

and (Sanskrit as printed, small type, continuing on p. 489): The Kannada explanation of this Sanskrit begins at the top of p. 489.

अथवा मक्षिकाशब्देनात्र कुश्चित् मक्षिकासादृश्यात् दधीचो उच्यते । सा युवाभ्यां मधुशब्दसंयुक्तं सरं ब्रह्म व्यक्तमुक्तवती । [as read; small type [?]]

athavā makṣikāśabdenātra kuścit makṣikāsādṛśyāt dadhīco ucyate | sā yuvābhyāṃ madhuśabdasaṃyuktaṃ saraṃ brahma vyaktamuktavatī | [as read; small type [?]]

original p. 489

Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued Kannada exposition of the Sanskrit above: "Taking, as the ground, a certain property of resemblance by which the word makṣikā is applied — [Skandasvāmin] explains dadhīcaḥ; the bee [i.e. Dadhīca], denoted by the word dadhīca, teaches you the supreme brahma that is to be attained through the honey-knowledge. This meaning is not quite appropriate."

Auśijaḥ huvanyati — uśijaḥ putraḥ kakṣīvān yuvām āhvayati: "The ṛṣi called Kakṣīvān, son of Uśij, calls you, in order to make you well pleased by offering the soma-juice" — thus Sāyaṇa's exposition. In explaining the word auśija, Skandasvāmin:

औशिजः उशिजो ऽपत्यभूतः कक्षीवान् । तं उशिजः प्रपौत्रं पौराणिकाः स्मरन्ति । तथा च — उशिजो ब्रह्मदुक्थश्च ऋषिर्दीर्घतमास्तथा । कक्षीवांश्च त्रयस्त्रिंशत् स्मृता ह्यङ्गिरसां वराः ॥ इति ।

auśijaḥ uśijo 'patyabhūtaḥ kakṣīvān | taṃ uśijaḥ prapautraṃ paurāṇikāḥ smaranti | tathā ca — uśijo brahmadukthaśca ṛṣirdīrghatamāstathā | kakṣīvāṃśca trayastriṃśat smṛtā hyaṅgirasāṃ varāḥ ‖ iti |

Saḥ ahaṃ uśijaḥ prapautraḥ kakṣīvān āhvayāmi — the sense is that [the poet] indicates himself in the third person, as if speaking of another (parokṣarūpeṇa nirdeśaḥ). Kannada: "Kakṣīvān, born in the line of Uśij, is the great-grandson (prapautra) of Uśij; Uśij, Brahmaduktha, the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas, Kakṣīvān — thirty-three such persons are famed in the Purāṇas as the best of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis. Here he says that the poet, though Kakṣīvān himself, speaks of himself in the third person." And, in another way:

अथवा उशिक् पुत्रः औशिजः स युवाम् आहूतवान् ।

athavā uśik putraḥ auśijaḥ sa yuvām āhūtavān |

"Or: uśik is a woman; her son is Auśija: that is Dīrghaśravas, who calls you to the sacrifice, to drink the soma-juice and be pleased" — thus he explains in another way, and quotes:

यो भिस्सुदानू औशिजाय वणिजे दीर्घश्रवसे मधु कोशो अक्षरत् । कक्षीवन्तं स्तोतारं याभिरावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११२-११ [as read])

yo bhissudānū auśijāya vaṇije dīrghaśravase madhu kośo akṣarat | kakṣīvantaṃ stotāraṃ yābhirāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-112-11 [as read])

Dadhīcaḥ manaḥ ā vivāsathaḥ — "The Aśvins, both to give honey to the bees and because they needed the honey-knowledge, are described as having satisfied the mind of the ṛṣi Dadhīca by the service they did for him."

original p. 490

Special Topics of Ṛk 9, concluded Aśvyaṃ śiraḥ āvadat — yuvābhyāṃ pratihitam aśvasya sambandhi yat śiraḥ tat madhuvidyāṃ yuvām avadat: "The ṛṣi, by that horse's head which the Aśvins had set in place of Dadhīca's own head, would teach them the honey-knowledge — both [Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin] explain this. Skandasvāmin:

अश्वस्याश्वयवभूतेन मधुब्राह्मणं परं ब्रह्म उक्तवान् ।

aśvasyāśvayavabhūtena madhubrāhmaṇaṃ paraṃ brahma uktavān |

— 'through the horse's head, which is a part of the horse's body, he taught the supreme secret form that is established by the honey-knowledge'; and he quotes:

दध्यङ् ह यन्मध्वाथर्वणो वामश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाच ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११६-१२)"

dadhyaṅ ha yanmadhvātharvaṇo vāmaśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yadīmuvāca ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-116-12)"

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Syā — the word tyad; with su following [as printed], tyadādīnām aḥ (Pā. 7-2-102 as read), a for the d, pararūpa; since it is feminine and ends in a, ṭāp; tado⁠ḥ sa sāvanantyayoḥ (Pā. 7-2-106 as read), s for the t; halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal (Pā. 6-1-68 as read), elision of the su that follows. Madhumat — madhu anayor asti iti madhumantau; tad asyāsty asmin (Pā. 5-2-94 as read), the suffix matup; with the dual au following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), luk for it. Arapat — root rapa lapa vyaktāyāṃ vāci; laṅ, third person singular; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Made — root madī harṣe; mado 'nupasarge (Pā. 3-3-67 as read), in the abstract sense the suffix ap; since it is pit, the root's accent remains; locative singular form. Auśijaḥ — uśijo 'patyaṃ pumān auśijaḥ; tasyāpatyam (Pā. 4-1-92 as read), the suffix aṇ; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-117 as read), vṛddhi of the initial; by the suffix's accent, the final acute.

original p. 491

Huvanyati — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; to it, in the sense of the abstract noun, lyuṭ ca (Pā. 3-3-115 as read), the suffix lyuṭ; bahulaṃ chandasi, saṃprasāraṇa of the root; saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa; yuvoranākau (Pā. 7-1-1 as read), ana for the suffix; ajiknudhātubhruvām (Pā. 6-4-77 as read), uvaṅ for [the u of] the root; "huvanam ātmana icchati" — huvanyati; supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 as read), the suffix kyac in the sense of wishing; by Vedic usage the final (a) is elided; or, when guṇa and av substitution have occurred for the saṃprasāraṇa, havanyati, [by] varṇavyatyaya [interchange of letters] a becomes uv; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Dadhīcaḥ — when dadhi is the upapada, for the root añcu gatipūjanayoḥ, ṛtvigdadhṛk… (Pā. 3-2-59 as read), the suffix kvin; anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (Pā. 6-4-24 as read), elision of the penultimate nasal; with the genitive singular following, since it has the name bha, acaḥ (Pā. 6-4-138 as read), elision of the a of the root; cau (Pā. 6-3-138 as read), because añcu with its a elided follows, lengthening of the preceding [part]; cau (Pā. 6-1-222 as read), though the acute on the earlier member is obtained, by añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam (Pā. 6-1-170 as read), the acute on the case ending that follows. Vivāsathaḥ — the root vivāsa is used in the sense of waiting upon; laṭ, second person dual; nighāta accent. Atha — nipātasya ca (Pā. 6-3-136 as read), lengthening in the Saṃhitā. Aśvyam — aśve bhavam aśvyam; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110 as read), the suffix yat; yasyeti ca, elision of the former a; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 as read), the initial acute. Vadat — root vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci; laṅ, third person singular; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75 as read), the augment aṭ does not occur; nighāta accent. ‖ 9 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 119.10)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 119.10)

अश्विना हे अश्विनौ पेदवे पेदुनाम्ने राज्ञे पुरुवारं बहुभिर्वरणीयं स्पृधां संग्रामे स्पर्धमानानां शत्रूणां तरुतारं तारकं श्वेतं शुभ्रवर्णमिन्द्रलब्धमश्वं युवं युवां दुवस्यथः । दत्त्वन्तौ [?] । पुनरपि कीदृशम् । शर्यैः । शीर्यन्ते इति शर्या योद्धारः । तैः पृतनासु संग्रामेषु दुस्तरं तरीतुमशक्यमभिद्युमभिगतदीप्तिं चर्कृत्यं सर्वेषु कार्येषु पुनःपुनः प्रयोज्यं इन्द्रमिव चर्षणीसहं इन्द्रो यथा शत्रूनभिभवति एवं शत्रुजनानामभिभवितारमित्यर्थः ॥ स्पृधाम् । स्पर्ध संघर्षे । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । चकारेण दृशिग्रहणानुकर्षणात्तस्य च विध्यन्तलोपसंग्रहार्थत्वादेकारस्य लोपो रेफस्य च संप्रसारणम् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । तरुतारम् । तॄ प्लवनतरणयोः । अस्मात्तृचि ग्रसितस्कभितस्तभितेत्यादौ निपातनाद्रुपसिद्धिः । चर्कृत्यम् । करोतेर्यङ्लुगन्ताद्भाषायां कृवृषोरिति क्यप् । ततस्तुक् ॥ [as read]

aśvinā he aśvinau pedave pedunāmne rājñe puruvāraṃ bahubhirvaraṇīyaṃ spṛdhāṃ saṃgrāme spardhamānānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ tarutāraṃ tārakaṃ śvetaṃ śubhravarṇamindralabdhamaśvaṃ yuvaṃ yuvāṃ duvasyathaḥ | dattvantau [?] | punarapi kīdṛśam | śaryaiḥ | śīryante iti śaryā yoddhāraḥ | taiḥ pṛtanāsu saṃgrāmeṣu dustaraṃ tarītumaśakyamabhidyumabhigatadīptiṃ carkṛtyaṃ sarveṣu kāryeṣu punaḥpunaḥ prayojyaṃ indramiva carṣaṇīsahaṃ indro yathā śatrūnabhibhavati evaṃ śatrujanānāmabhibhavitāramityarthaḥ ‖ spṛdhām | spardha saṃgharṣe | kvipceti kvip | cakāreṇa dṛśigrahaṇānukarṣaṇāttasya ca vidhyantalopasaṃgrahārthatvādekārasya lopo rephasya ca saṃprasāraṇam | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | tarutāram | tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ | asmāttṛci grasitaskabhitastabhitetyādau nipātanādrupasiddhiḥ | carkṛtyam | karoteryaṅlugantādbhāṣāyāṃ kṛvṛṣoriti kyap | tatastuk ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, to King Pedu you two duvasyathaḥ — gave [reverently] a śvetam — white-coloured horse received from Indra, puruvāram — desired by many, spṛdhām tarutāram — the bearer-across of enemies who contend in battle; furthermore: śaryaiḥ — [śarya is a warrior, from śṝ] by warriors, pṛtanāsu — in battles, dustaram — impossible to cross over; abhidyum — of radiant lustre; cakṛtyam — to be used again and again in all affairs; indram iva carṣaṇīsaham — as Indra overcomes enemies, so a vanquisher of enemy hosts." Grammar tail of the bhāṣya, small type: tarutāram [tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, suffix tṛc; irregular by grasitaskabhita…], cakṛtyam [from kṛ + yaṅluk; kṛvṛṣoḥ, kyap; augment tuk] — characterized, not transcribed.
