॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 119.10) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; pedave — to the king named Pedu; puruvāram — desired by many; spṛdhām — of enemies who contend (in battle); tarutāram — a bearer-across (the victorious); śaryaiḥ — by warriors; pṛtanāsu — in battles; dustaram — unconquerable; abhidyum — of radiant lustre; cakṛtyam — to be used again and again (in all works); indram iva — like Indra; carṣaṇīsaham — a defeater of enemies; śvetam aśvam — a white horse; yuvam — you two; duvasyathaḥ — gave.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 119.10) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! To Pedu you gave a white-coloured horse — desired by many, a bearer-across of enemies, unconquerable in battle by foes (to be used again and again in all works), like Indra a bringer of defeat to enemies, and of radiant lustre."

English Translation (as printed)

"Aswins, you gave to Pedu the white (horse) desired by many, the breaker-through of combatants, shining, unconquerable by foes in battle, fit for every work; like Indra, the conqueror of men."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 10)

"The Aśvins gave to the king named Pedu a white horse, which Indra had given them as a gift."

Puruvāram — bahubhir varaṇīyam: "'desirable by many people' say Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin, who explain what Sāyaṇa said; śatrūṇāṃ vārayitāraṃ — 'it keeps enemies off; [one who] holds enemies back and protects [its owner] from them' is the meaning."

Spṛdhāṃ tarutāram — saṅgrāmanāmakāṃ nistarītāram: "'one that brings victory in battles' is Skandasvāmin's exposition; since the word spṛdh is stated among the names of battle (Ni. 2-7 [as read]), spṛdh means 'battle' — so the Nirukta author explains: saṅgrāme spardhamānānāṃ śatrūṇām …" continues on p. 494

original p. 494

Special Topics of Ṛk 10, continued "… spṛdhāṃ tarutāram — 'one by which, at the time of battle, enemies who strive to win are conquered': the Aśvins' gift, [the horse,] bestows victory, and gives [the king] the chance to protect himself from them — so Sāyaṇa explains."

Dustaram — taritum aśakyam: "'The horse given by the Aśvins cannot be overcome by anyone, however heroic' is Sāyaṇa's explanation. Skandasvāmin: avatiriti vadhakarmasu pāṭhāt tiratiḥ hiṃsanārthaḥ | tasyaivaṃ rūpam | marhaṇam avatirati iti vadhakarmasu pāṭhād dustaram — 'since the root tṝ is read among the roots with the sense of killing, dustara means one which cannot be killed'."

Cakṛtyam — sarveṣu kāryeṣu punaḥ punaḥ prayojyam: "'one that the Aśvins gave, with favour — a horse fit to be used again and again in all works' is Sāyaṇa's explanation. [Skandasvāmin:] imam api ca kṛnter vadhakarmaṇo rūpam ātmārthaṃ hantāram — 'it is also a form of the root kṛnt [kṛtī chedane], the root with the sense of killing; 'a killer, for the sake of its owner'' — cakṛtyam means 'one that cuts down'; 'one that destroys enemies repeatedly', thus Skandasvāmin explains."

Carṣaṇīsaham — indro yathā śatrūn abhibhavati evaṃ śatrujanān abhibhavitāram: "'the word carṣaṇi is stated among the names of men (Ni. 2-2 [as read])'. The horse given to King Pedu was one that defeats enemy people, as Indra defeats his enemies — such is the meaning."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Spṛdhām — root spardha saṃgharṣe; kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76 as read), to it the suffix kvip; since in this sūtra the ca draws down the mention of dṛśi from the preceding sūtra, which is for including other operations, elision of the root's a-vowel and saṃprasāraṇa of the root's r occur; the word spṛdh; genitive plural form; sāvekācas tṛtīyādir viḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 as read), the acute on the case ending. Śvetam — root śvitā varṇe; since it belongs to the pacādi ākṛtigaṇa, nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (Pā. 3-1-134 as read), the suffix ac; on that account, guṇa of the light penultimate of the root; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Tarutāram — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; when the suffix tṛc comes, the desired form is accomplished by the irregular formation in grasitaskabhitastabhita… (Pā. 7-2-34 as read); gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent.

original p. 495

Duvasyathaḥ — root duvas sandīpane [as read: duvas], kaṇḍvādi; here used in the sense of giving; kaṇḍvādibhyo yak (Pā. 3-1-27 as read), the suffix yak in its own sense; laṭ, second person dual; because it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Śaryaiḥ — root śṝ hiṃsāyām; "śīryante iti śaryāḥ"; aco yat (Pā. 3-1-97 as read), the suffix yat; on that account guṇa of the root's ṛ-vowel; becomes r-final; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 as read), the initial acute. Dustaram — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; "taritum aśakyam dustaram"; īṣaddusuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal (Pā. 3-3-126 as read), the suffix khal in the sense of difficulty; on that account guṇa of the root; becomes r-final; liti (Pā. 6-1-193 as read), the acute on the syllable before the suffix. Cakṛtyam — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; in the sense of frequent repetition, dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ (Pā. 3-1-22 as read), the suffix yaṅ; yaño 'ci ca (Pā. 2-4-74 as read), luk for it; sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. 6-1-9 as read), doubling of the root; guṇo yaṅluk oḥ (Pā. 7-4-82 as read), guṇa for the reduplicative syllable; becomes r-final; after the yaṅluganta, vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ (Pā. 3-1-120 as read), the suffix kyap; since it is pit, hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk (Pā. 6-1-71 as read), the augment tuk; since the suffix is pit, the root's accent remains. ‖ 10 ‖

Colophon (Kannada, as printed): "nūrahattombhattaneya sūktavu mugidudu" — "The hundred-and-nineteenth Sūkta is ended."

Sūkta 120 — "kā rādhaddhotrāśvinā"

Heading (Kannada): "nūra ippattaneya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-twentieth Sūkta."

Anukramaṇī (Sanskrit, as printed; small type, read with several doubts):

का राधद्धोत्रेति द्वादशर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । का राधद्द्वादशान्त्या दुःस्वप्ननाशन्याद्या गायत्री द्वितीया ककुप् तृतीयाचतुर्थ्यौ काविराण्नष्टरूप्यौ पञ्चमी तनुशिरा षष्ठ्युष्णिक् सप्तमी विष्टारबृहती कृतिर्विराट् तिस्रो गायत्र्य इति [as printed and as repeated on p. 496–497; the small type on p. 495 itself was read only in part [?]]

Sense (from the Kannada Anuvāda on p. 496): "This sūkta, kā rādhat, is the fifth sūkta in the seventeenth anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says 'kā rādhat dvādaśa, antyā duḥsvapnanāśanī; ādyā gāyatrī, dvitīyā kakubh, tṛtīyā-caturthyau kāvirāṭ-naṣṭarūpī, pañcamī tanuśirā, ṣaṣṭhy uṣṇik, saptamī viṣṭārabṛhatī, kṛtir virāṭ, tisro gāyatryaḥ'." The details follow on p. 496.

original p. 496

Anukramaṇī of Sūkta 120, concluded; small type "… naṣṭarūpī, [since it has] the character of [the metre named] naṣṭarūpī, according to the lakṣaṇa that is stated at anu. 6-6 [as read]: …; pra yo ghoṣe — this fifth Ṛk is tanuśirā, [having the character of] vikāra-ādeśayoḥ pare ṣaṭkṛṣṇa [as read [?]] tanuśirā (anu. 3-5 [as read]); śrutaṃ gāyatram — this sixth Ṛk, though by the number of its pādas it is a gāyatrī, by the number of its syllables it is uṣṇik; yuvaṃ hi — the seventh, viṣṭārabṛhatī: 'aśvinor marthye daśakau viṣṭārabṛhatī' (anu. 2-5 [as read]); mā kasmai — the eighth, kṛti: 'jāgatāv aṣṭākṣarakā kṛtiḥ' (anu. 6-8 [as read]); duhīyan — the ninth, virāṭ; the last three, from the tenth to the twelfth, are Gāyatrī. By the use of aśvinaṃ vai in the Anukramaṇikā, the deities of the sūkta are the Aśvins; and the last Ṛk, atha svapnasya, is addressed to Duḥsvapnanāśana ('Destroyer of Bad Dreams'): 'ato yā tenocyate sā devatā' (anu. 2-5 [as read]) — the deity is the matter spoken of in the Ṛk itself. The use (viniyoga) of the sūkta is indicated by the liṅga: in the gharma rite the first nine Ṛks are used, as the Śrauta-sūtra says 'kā rādhaddhotrāśvinā vām iti nava bhātṛgnīḥ' (Āś. 4-6 as read [?]); and the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa statement 'kā rādhaddhotrāśvinā vām iti nava vicchandasaḥ' (Ai. Br. 1-?? [as read]) supports it."

Anuvāda (Kannada, as printed): "This sūkta, kā rādhat, is the fifth sūkta in the seventeenth anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says: 'kā rādhad dvādaśa, antyā duḥsvapnanāśanī, ādyā gāyatrī, dvitīyā kakubh, tṛtīyā-caturthyau kāvirāṭ-naṣṭarūpī, pañcamī tanuśirā, ṣaṣṭhī uṣṇik, saptamī viṣṭārabṛhatī, kṛtir virāṭ, tisro gāyatryaḥ'. Its meaning: as in the preceding sūktas, the ṛṣi of this sūkta too is Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. The first Ṛk of this sūkta is Gāyatrī. The second Ṛk, vidvāṃsau, is Kakubh; since the Anukramaṇikā (anu. 2-3 [as read]) states the character of this metre as madhyamapādasya dvādaśākṣaratvāt — 'the middle pāda has twelve syllables' — [this metre is called] Kakubh. The third Ṛk, tā vidvāṃsā, is of the metre called kāvirāṭ; the Anukramaṇikā says 'navakayor madhye jāgataḥ kāvirāṭ' (anu. 6-3 [as read]): one pāda of nine syllables, a middle pāda that is Jagatī (a pāda of twelve), and the others — so the character of the metre called kāvirāṭ is stated. The fourth Ṛk, vi pṛcchāmi, is of the metre naṣṭarūpī; the Anukramaṇikā says 'savavyarājatrayor deśair naṣṭarūpī' (anu. 6-6 [as read]) — that is, the first pāda of nine syllables, the second a virāṭ-pāda of ten syllables, and the third of thirteen syllables: with these, [the metre is] called naṣṭarūpī …"

original p. 497

Anuvāda concluded "… The fifth Ṛk, pra yo ghoṣe, is of the metre tanuśirā: the Anukramaṇikā says 'vikārādeśayoḥ pare ṣaṭkṛṣṇa tanuśirā' [as read] (anu. 3-5 [as read]) — [a metre] with two pādas of eight syllables, and a third pāda of six syllables. The sixth Ṛk, śrutaṃ gāyatram, is Uṣṇik by the number of syllables, though it is Gāyatrī by the number of its pādas. The seventh Ṛk, yuvaṃ hi, is of the metre viṣṭārabṛhatī; the Anukramaṇikā says 'aśvinor marthye daśakau viṣṭārabṛhatī' (anu. 2-5 [as read]) — the metre which has eight syllables in the first and last pādas, and ten and ten in the middle pāda(s). The eighth Ṛk, mā kasmai, is of the metre kṛti; the Anukramaṇikā says 'jāgatāv aṣṭākṣarakā kṛtiḥ' (anu. 6-8 [as read]) — the first two pādas are Jagatī (pādas of twelve syllables) and the last pāda has eight syllables. The ninth Ṛk, duhīyan, is Virāṭ; that is, each pāda of this metre's Ṛks has eleven syllables. The three Ṛks from the tenth to the twelfth are Gāyatrī. We describe the characters of all these metres, with examples, at length in pp. 221–231 of the first part of the Ṛg-saṃhitā [i.e. this edition's first volume]. By the use of the word vaiśvaśabda ['aśvinaṃ vai'] in the Anukramaṇikā, the deities of this sūkta are the Aśvins. The deity of the last Ṛk, atha svapnasya, is said to be duḥsvapnanāśana. In the Anukramaṇikā — 'ato yā tenocyate sā devatā' (anu. 2-5 [as read]), that is, since the statement is that the matter set forth in the Ṛk is the deity of that Ṛk, the destruction of bad dreams, set forth in this last Ṛk, is the deity of the Ṛk. The use of the sūkta is indicated by the liṅga: in the rite called gharma the first nine Ṛks of this sūkta are used, as the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra shows by the sūtra 'kā rādhaddhotrāśvinā vām iti nava bhātṛgnīḥ' (Āś. 4-6 as read [?]); and the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 'kā rādhaddhotrāśvinā vām iti nava vicchandasaḥ' (Ai. Br. 1-?? [as read]) supports this."

original p. 498

सूक्त—१२० (Sūkta 120) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१७ ॥ सूक्त—१२० ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—small numerals; read "22, 23" — as printed [?] ॥ Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12. Ṛṣi: Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. Devatā: Ṛks 1–11 the Aśvins; Ṛk 12 Duḥsvapnanāśana (destruction of bad dreams). Chandas: 1 Gāyatrī; 2 Kakubh; 3 Kāvirāṭ; 4 Naṣṭarūpī; 5 Tanuśirā; 6 (by syllables) Uṣṇik; 7 Viṣṭārabṛhatī; 8 Kṛti; 9 Virāṭ; 10–12 Gāyatrī. The numerals of the head-table were read as printed; those of the chandas list are the ones that match the Anuvāda of p. 496–497.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.1)

का राधद्धोत्राश्विना वां को वां जोष उभयोः । कथा विधात्यप्रचेताः ॥ १ ॥

kā rādhaddhotrāśvinā vāṃ ko vāṃ joṣa ubhayoḥ | kathā vidhātyapracetāḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.1)

का । राधत् । होत्रा । अश्विना । वाम् । कः । वाम् । जोषे । उभयोः । कथा । विधाति । अप्रऽचेताः ॥ १ ॥

kā | rādhat | hotrā | aśvinā | vām | kaḥ | vām | joṣe | ubhayoḥ | kathā | vidhāti | apra 'cetāḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.1)

अश्विना हे अश्विनौ वां युवां का होत्रा । वाङ्नामैतत् । कीदृशी स्तुतिलक्षणा वाग्राधत् । आराधयति । प्रीतान् करोति । युवयोर्माहात्म्यानुरूपा स्तुतिर्नास्तीत्यर्थः । किंच वां युवयोरुभयोर्जोषे जोषणे सेवने प्रीणने वा समर्थः कः स्तोता विद्यते । युष्मद्गुणाभिज्ञः कश्चिदपि नास्तीत्यर्थः । अप्रचेताः युवयोर्माहात्म्यमजानन् कथा केन प्रकारेण विधाति । युवां परिचरति । युष्मद्विषयं परिचरणमपि न कर्तुं शक्नोमीत्यर्थः ॥ राधत् । राध साध संसिद्धौ । लेटि अडागमः । जोषे । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । भावे घञ् । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । कथा । था हेतौ च छन्दसीति किंशब्दात्प्रकारवचने था प्रत्ययः । किमः क इति कादेशः । विधाति । विध विधाने । तौदादिकः । लेट्यडागमः । अप्रचेताः । प्रकृष्टं चेतो यस्यासौ प्रचेताः । नञ्समासे अव्ययपूर्वपदे प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

aśvinā he aśvinau vāṃ yuvāṃ kā hotrā | vāṅnāmaitat | kīdṛśī stutilakṣaṇā vāgrādhat | ārādhayati | prītān karoti | yuvayormāhātmyānurūpā stutirnāstītyarthaḥ | kiṃca vāṃ yuvayorubhayorjoṣe joṣaṇe sevane prīṇane vā samarthaḥ kaḥ stotā vidyate | yuṣmadguṇābhijñaḥ kaścidapi nāstītyarthaḥ | apracetāḥ yuvayormāhātmyamajānan kathā kena prakāreṇa vidhāti | yuvāṃ paricarati | yuṣmadviṣayaṃ paricaraṇamapi na kartuṃ śaknomītyarthaḥ ‖ rādhat | rādha sādha saṃsiddhau | leṭi aḍāgamaḥ | joṣe | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | bhāve ghañ | ñittvādādyudāttatvam | kathā | thā hetau ca chandasīti kiṃśabdātprakāravacane thā pratyayaḥ | kimaḥ ka iti kādeśaḥ | vidhāti | vidha vidhāne | taudādikaḥ | leṭyaḍāgamaḥ | apracetāḥ | prakṛṣṭaṃ ceto yasyāsau pracetāḥ | nañsamāse avyayapūrvapade prakṛtisvaratvam ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, which hotrā — [a name for speech] — which speech in the form of praise could please (rādhat, propitiate) you? The meaning is: there is no praise equal to your greatness. And, who is the praiser able to satisfy you both (joṣe) by service or pleasing? There is none who knows your qualities. Aprācetāḥ — one who does not know your greatness — how (kathā) can he serve (vidhāti) you? I cannot even perform service concerning you."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.1) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinā — O Aśvins; vām — you two; kā hotrā — what praise-word; rādhat — would propitiate (would please)?; vām ubhayoḥ — of both of you; joṣe — in serving; kaḥ — who; (is capable)?; aprācetāḥ — one ignorant of your greatness; kathā — how indeed; vidhāti — would serve you?

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.1) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! What praise-word would please you? (There is no praise-word fit for your greatness.) Who has the capacity to satisfy you? How should one who does not know your greatness satisfy you? (Your service is hard to accomplish.)"

original p. 499

English Translation (as printed)

"What praise may propitiate you, Aswins? who may give satisfaction to you both? how may any ignorant (man) pay fitting homage?"

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 1)

Kā hotā — vāṅnāmaitat kīdṛśī stutilakṣaṇā vāk: "The word hotrā is stated among the names of speech (Ni. 1-11 [as read]). By the question 'which of your (vām) hotrā, praise, is [it]?', although there are many words, it is understood that, because there are no words that adequately express the qualities and the greatness of the Aśvins, it is difficult for [the poet] to praise you. By this it is described that the greatness of the qualities of the Aśvins is beyond words." The Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue past this point on p. 500.

original p. 500

Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued "… 'since there are no words that fully express your greatness, it is difficult to praise you' — such is the idea that is described here; by this it is explained that their greatness is beyond description."

"By the very sentence 'ko vāṃ joṣa ubhayoḥ' — [it is said] that since it is certain that there is no man who, knowing all your qualities, would praise you so that your mind is pleased and satisfied, — and who is he? — [the poet says] that to obtain your favour in that way is not possible. By this it is evident that, just as there is no praise [that expresses] yuvayor māhātmyānurūpā stutir nāsti, there is no one who knows your qualities well — yuṣmadguṇābhijñaḥ kaścid api nāsti."

Kathā — kena prakāreṇa: "'in what way' is the meaning."

कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरयोः कथा जातेकवयः को विवेद । विश्वं त्मना बिभृतो यद्ध नाम वि वर्तेते अहनी चक्रियेव ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१८५-१ [as read])

katarā pūrvā katarāparayoḥ kathā jātekavayaḥ ko viveda | viśvaṃ tmanā bibhṛto yaddha nāma vi vartete ahanī cakriyeva ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-185-1 [as read])

"In this Ṛk the Nirukta author explains the word kathā as katham (Ni. 3-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೨೩'])."

Aprācetāḥ — yuvayor māhātmyam ajānan: "The word pracetas [is used in the Ṛk]:

आ जङ्घन्ति सान्वेषां जघनाँ उप जिघ्नते । अश्वाजनि प्रचेतसोऽश्वान्त्समत्सु चोदय ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-७५-१३ [as read])

ā jaṅghanti sānveṣāṃ jaghanā~ upa jighnate | aśvājani pracetaso 'śvāntsamatsu codaya ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 6-75-13 [as read])

In this Ṛk, pracetasaḥ is explained, since it conveys pravṛddhacetasaḥ — 'those of grown knowledge' (Ni. 9-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೯-೨೦'] — hence apracetas means 'ignorant'. 'How could one who has not known the greatness of the Aśvins perform their service?' — by this question, as in the previous sentence, it is stated that the service of the Aśvins is impossible."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Rādhat — root rādha sādha saṃsiddhau; leṭ, third person singular, the suffix tip; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 3-4-97 as read), elision of the i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), the augment aṭ; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent.

original p. 501

Joṣe — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; in the abstract sense the suffix ghañ; on account of the suffix, puganta-laghūpadhasya ca (Pā. 7-3-86 as read), guṇa of the root's light penultimate; the form joṣa; since the suffix is ñit, ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197 as read), the initial acute; locative singular form. Kathā — the word kim; thā hetau ca chandasi (Pā. 5-3-26 as read), the suffix thā in the sense of manner; prāg diśo vibhaktiḥ (Pā. 5-3-1 as read), the name vibhakti is obtained for it; kimaḥ kaḥ (Pā. 7-2-103 as read), ka substituted for kim; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Vidhāti — root vidha vidhāne; tudādi; leṭ, third person singular, the suffix tip; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), the augment aṭ for it; tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ (Pā. 3-1-77 as read), śa vikaraṇa; since sārvadhātukam apit makes the suffix ṅit, guṇa of the root's light penultimate does not occur; because it stands after an ajanta, tiṅ atiṅaḥ (Pā. 8-1-28 as read), the nighāta accent. Aprācetāḥ — prakṛṣṭaṃ ceto yasya asau pracetāḥ; root citī saṃjñāne; the auṇādika suffix asun; na pracetāḥ aprācetāḥ; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 as read), the avyaya former member keeps its natural accent. ‖ 1 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.2)

विद्वांसाविद्दुरः पृच्छेदविद्वानित्थापरो अचेताः । नू चिन्नु मर्ते अक्रौ ॥ २ ॥

vidvāṃsāvidduraḥ pṛcchedavidvānitthāparo acetāḥ | nū cinnu marte akrau ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.2)

विद्वांसौ । इत् । दुरः । पृच्छेत् । अविद्वान् । इत्था । अपरः । अचेताः । नु । चित् । नु । मर्ते । अक्रौ ॥ २ ॥

vidvāṃsau | it | duraḥ | pṛcchet | avidvān | itthā | aparaḥ | acetāḥ | nu | cit | nu | marte | akrau ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 502

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.2) small type; read with some doubts

इत्थेत्थमनेन पूर्वोक्तप्रकारेणाविद्वानज्ञः स्तोता विद्वांसौ सर्वज्ञावश्विनावेव दुरो द्वाराणि स्तुतिपरिचरणयोरुपायभूतान्मार्गान्पृच्छेत् । प्रष्टुमर्हतीत्यर्थः । अपरोऽश्विभ्यामन्यः सर्वोऽप्यचेताश्चेतसा ज्ञानेन रहितः । तस्मादश्विनावेव पृच्छेदित्यर्थः । तौ चाक्रौ शत्रुभिरनाक्रान्तावश्विनौ नू चित् क्षिप्रमेव मर्ते मनुष्ये स्तोतरि भक्त्यानुग्राहकतया सनिं धत्त इति वाक्यशेषः ॥ इत्था । था हेतौ चेति छन्दसीति थाप्रत्ययः । इदम इश् । एतेतौ रथोः । (पा. ५-३-४ [as read]) इतीद्भावः । यदि था हेतौ चेत्प्रकरणे इदंशब्दस्य सानुवृत्तिस्तदानीमिदमस्थमुः । एतदंशात्परस्या विभक्तेर्व्यत्ययेन सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्डादेशः । अक्रौ । क्रमु पादविक्षेपे । अस्मान्न्यञ्चुपपदे कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति बहुलवचनात्कर्मण्यपि जनिसनखनक्रमगमो विट्विट् [as read; the grammar tail is in small type and characterized only]

itthetthamanena pūrvoktaprakāreṇāvidvānajñaḥ stotā vidvāṃsau sarvajñāvaśvināveva duro dvārāṇi stutiparicaraṇayorupāyabhūtānmārgānpṛcchet | praṣṭumarhatītyarthaḥ | aparo 'śvibhyāmanyaḥ sarvo 'pyacetāścetasā jñānena rahitaḥ | tasmādaśvināveva pṛcchedityarthaḥ | tau cākrau śatrubhiranākrāntāvaśvinau nū cit kṣiprameva marte manuṣye stotari bhaktyānugrāhakatayā saniṃ dhatta iti vākyaśeṣaḥ ‖ itthā | thā hetau ceti chandasīti thāpratyayaḥ | idama iś | etetau rathoḥ | (pā. 5-3-4 [as read]) itīdbhāvaḥ | yadi thā hetau cetprakaraṇe idaṃśabdasya sānuvṛttistadānīmidamasthamuḥ | etadaṃśātparasyā vibhaktervyatyayena supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterḍādeśaḥ | akrau | kramu pādavikṣepe | asmānnyañcupapade kṛtyalyuṭo bahulamiti bahulavacanātkarmaṇyapi janisanakhanakramagamo viṭviṭ [as read; the grammar tail is in small type and characterized only]

Sense (mine): "In this way (itthā), by the manner told above, an ignorant (avidvān) praiser should inquire of the Aśvins alone, the all-knowing (vidvāṃsau), the duraḥ — doors, ways, which are the means of praising and serving. The meaning is: he is entitled to ask. Aparaḥ — any other than the Aśvins is acetāḥ — devoid of understanding, knowledge; therefore he should ask the Aśvins alone. And those two, akrau — not overpowered by enemies — nū cit — quickly — to the man (marte), the praiser, favour [him] (sanim dhatte), out of favour towards devotion: this is the completion of the sentence."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.2) (Kannada, rendered)

Itthā — in this manner; avidvān — one who does not know (the ways of praise); vidvāṃsau — the all-knowing; it — alone; (aśvinau — the Aśvins); duraḥ — the ways (of praise and service); pṛcchet — should ask; aparaḥ — others (than the Aśvins; everyone); acetāḥ — ignorant; akrau — [they, the Aśvins], not overpowered (by enemies); nū cit — quickly; marte — [on] the man (the praiser); nu — favouring [him].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.2) (Kannada, rendered)

"One who does not know, in the manner told above, how to praise and the like, should ask the all-knowing Aśvins themselves the ways of (praise and service); apart from them, everyone else is ignorant; the Aśvins, unconquerable by enemies, quickly favour the one who praises them."

English Translation (as printed)

"Thus may an ignorant man inquire the means of worshipping the all-wise, for every (one) other (then [sic] the Aswins) is unknowing; they, the unconquered, quickly (show favour) to the man (who worships them)."

original p. 503

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 2)

"Both Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin explain the meaning of this Ṛk, in one way and in another. [Sāyaṇa says that] the greatness of the Aśvins is beyond the reach of the mind; hence one who wishes to praise them, and is ignorant of the ways of serving them, asks the Aśvins — who are all-knowing — themselves; there is no other omniscient one than they; and so they favour the ignorant."

"In Skandasvāmin's exposition the meaning is not so clearly seen. Having connected this Ṛk with the Ṛk that follows it, he explains the two Ṛks by the method of a single sentence, [with a construction such as]:

परस्यां ऋचि तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्छब्दोऽध्याहर्तव्यः । तथा चैकवाक्यता — यो विद्वांसौ जानन्तौ स्तोता दुरः स्तुतेर्द्वाराणि उपायः सर्वं पृच्छति । अविद्वानित्था सत्यमेवाजानन् । अशास्येन अपरः न्यनेकः [?] ज्ञातुमसमर्थः स्वयम् । पुराणानेव मर्ते अक्रौ वशीकर्तारौ ।

parasyāṃ ṛci tacchabdaśruteryacchabdo 'dhyāhartavyaḥ | tathā caikavākyatā — yo vidvāṃsau jānantau stotā duraḥ stuterdvārāṇi upāyaḥ sarvaṃ pṛcchati | avidvānitthā satyamevājānan | aśāsyena aparaḥ nyanekaḥ [?] jñātumasamarthaḥ svayam | purāṇāneva marte akrau vaśīkartārau |

— he gives the construction of the words. The words nu and it are fillers (padapūraṇa). The word itthā is stated among the names of truth (Ni. 3-?? [as read]), so he explains it as 'truly'. Because of the word tat in the next Ṛk, the word yat must be supplied here. Thereby: those who are learned know everything; he who wishes to praise asks the ways of praising; the ignorant one, not knowing the truth and falsehood, [and] unable to discern, is ignorant of what he has been taught, as in yathāśrutagrāhī — [a man who takes things only as he hears them]. By the rule of the pareṇa kṛtā [?] those who are learned and [those who are not] are both gracious and protect, by the Aśvins [who are] the ones of greater [knowledge]. It is therefore that, according to Skandasvāmin, those who are praised take under their control mortals who are akrau, [i.e.] who have not been overpowered."

Akrau — śatrubhiḥ anākrāntau: "'not overpowered by enemies' is Sāyaṇa's exposition. āṅpūrvasya krameḥ idaṃ chāndasaṃ rūpam | akramitārau vaśīkartārau — 'this is the Vedic form of the root kram with the prefix āṅ: those who would not be trampled upon, those who bring under control' — so Skandasvāmin says that the word kram, when joined with the prefix āṅ, takes in the Veda the form akra. Yāska [explains]: akraḥ ākramaṇāt (Ni. 6-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೬-೧೭']) — from the sense 'trample' [ākramaṇa] the form akra arises" and he expounds—

original p. 504

Special Topics of Ṛk 2, concluded "… and, quoting a Ṛk in which the word akra is used:

अक्रो न बभ्रिः समिथे महीनां दिदृक्षेयः सूनवे भाऋजीकः । उदुस्रिया जनिता यो जजानापां गर्भो नृतमो यह्वो अग्निः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-१-१३ [as read])

akro na babhriḥ samithe mahīnāṃ didṛkṣeyaḥ sūnave bhāṛjīkaḥ | udusriyā janitā yo jajānāpāṃ garbho nṛtamo yahvo agniḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 3-1-13 [as read])

he explains. Durgācārya (the commentator on the Nirukta) explains it as ākramyate iti arkaḥ prākāraḥ — 'that which is overrun is a rampart'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Vidvāṃsau — root vida jñāne; when laṭ has come, vido laṭo vā; vibher śatur vasuḥ [as printed viderśatur vasuḥ] (Pā. 7-1-36 as read), vasu substituted for śatṛ; the word vidvas; with the dual following, ātve saṃtasya … [upadhādīrgha] (Pā. 6-4-14 as read), lengthening of the penultimate; since it is ugit, the augment num; then anusvāra. Itthā — the word idam; thā hetau ca chandasi (Pā. 5-3-26 as read), the suffix thā in the sense of manner; with it following, idama iś (Pā. 5-3-3 as read), since iś is obtained for the base, etetau rathoḥ (Pā. 5-3-4 as read) as an exception, id is substituted; if in the sūtra thā hetau ca chandasi the word idam is not continued [from the preceding sūtra], then idamas thamuḥ (Pā. 5-3-24 as read), the suffix thamu in the sense of manner; it gets the avyaya name; and by vyatyaya the following case-ending's supāṃ sulug (Pā. 2-4-82 as read), elision by the ḍā-substitution [?]; by the strength of ḍit, elision of the ṭi; the form itthā. Nu, cit — nu śuṣu [as read; Pā. 6-3-136 as read], lengthening of nu in the Saṃhitā. Akrau — root kramu pādavikṣepe; when ā is the upapada [as printed ṅa], janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ (Pā. 3-2-67 as read), the suffix viṭ; kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam (Pā. 3-3-113 as read), because of the word bahula in it, this comes also in the passive sense; viḍvanorānunāsikasyāt (Pā. 6-4-41 as read), when viṭ follows, ā for the root; in the compound with nañ, tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 as read), the avyaya former member keeps its natural accent; nominative dual form. ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 505

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.3)

ता विद्वांसा हवामहे वां ता नो विद्वांसा मन्म वोचेतमद्य । प्रार्चद्दयमानो युवाकुः ॥ ३ ॥

tā vidvāṃsā havāmahe vāṃ tā no vidvāṃsā manma vocetamadya | prārcaddayamāno yuvākuḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.3)

ता । विद्वांसा । हवामहे । वाम् । ता । नः । विद्वांसा । मन्म । वोचेतम् । अद्य । प्र । आर्चत् । दयमानः । युवाकुः ॥ ३ ॥

tā | vidvāṃsā | havāmahe | vām | tā | naḥ | vidvāṃsā | manma | vocetam | adya | pra | ārcat | dayamānaḥ | yuvākuḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.3)

हे अश्विनौ विद्वांसा सर्वज्ञौ ता वां तौ युवां हवामहे । आह्वयामहे । ताना हूतौ [?] विद्वांसावभिज्ञौ युवां नोऽस्मभ्यं मन्म मननीयं ज्ञातव्यं स्तोत्रमद्यास्मिन्काले वोचेतं ब्रुवाणौ भूयास्तम् । स चाहं युवाकुर्युवां कामयमानः स्तुत्या संयोजयन्नादयमानो युवाभ्यां हविः प्रयच्छन् प्रार्चत् । प्रार्चं प्रकर्षेण स्तौमि ॥ ता । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । वोचेतम् । ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि । ब्रुवो वचिः । लिङ्याशिष्यङ् । वच उमित्युमागमः । आर्चत् । अर्च पूजायाम् । भौवादिकः । तिङां तिङो भवन्तीति मिपस्तिबादेशः । दयमानः । दय दानगतिरक्षणहिंसादानेषु । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शानचो लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । युवाकुः । युवां कामयत इति युवाकुः । मितद्र्वादिभ्य उपसंख्यानम् । (पा. ३-२-१८०-१ [as read]) इति डुप्रत्ययः । अभिभक्तावपि व्यत्ययेन युवावौ द्विवचन इति युवादेश आत्त्वं च । यद्वा । यु मिश्रणे । औणादिकः काकुप्रत्ययः ॥ [as read]

he aśvinau vidvāṃsā sarvajñau tā vāṃ tau yuvāṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmahe | tānā hūtau [?] vidvāṃsāvabhijñau yuvāṃ no 'smabhyaṃ manma mananīyaṃ jñātavyaṃ stotramadyāsminkāle vocetaṃ bruvāṇau bhūyāstam | sa cāhaṃ yuvākuryuvāṃ kāmayamānaḥ stutyā saṃyojayannādayamāno yuvābhyāṃ haviḥ prayacchan prārcat | prārcaṃ prakarṣeṇa staumi ‖ tā | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterākāraḥ | vocetam | brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci | bruvo vaciḥ | liṅyāśiṣyaṅ | vaca umityumāgamaḥ | ārcat | arca pūjāyām | bhauvādikaḥ | tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavantīti mipastibādeśaḥ | dayamānaḥ | daya dānagatirakṣaṇahiṃsādāneṣu | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | śānaco lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | yuvākuḥ | yuvāṃ kāmayata iti yuvākuḥ | mitadrvādibhya upasaṃkhyānam | (pā. 3-2-180-1 [as read]) iti ḍupratyayaḥ | abhibhaktāvapi vyatyayena yuvāvau dvivacana iti yuvādeśa āttvaṃ ca | yadvā | yu miśraṇe | auṇādikaḥ kākupratyayaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, vidvāṃsā — omniscient: you two we call (havāmahe). You two, learned, who know, grant to us today a manma — a hymn to be pondered, to be known — may you speak (vocetam) [it]. And I, yuvākuḥ — desirous of you, uniting you by praise, giving you an oblation, pra ārcat — praise exceedingly."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.3) (Kannada, rendered; text on this page as legible)

(He) vidvāṃsā — O omniscient (Aśvins); tā vām — those same two, you; havāmahe — we call; tā vidvāṃsā — those omniscient; naḥ — to us; adya — today; manma — a hymn worthy of pondering; vocetam — may you tell; yuvākuḥ — desirous of you; dayamānaḥ — giving (the oblation); pra ārcat — [I] praise exceedingly.

original p. 506

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.3) (Kannada, rendered; as printed on p. 506, repeating and completing p. 505)

Vidvāṃsā — O omniscient; tā vām — you two; havāmahe — we call; vidvāṃsā — [you], who, being called, know; naḥ — to us; manma — a hymn worthy of knowing; adya — now; vocetam — [you] should tell; (and I) yuvākuḥ — one who desires you, and dayamānaḥ — one who offers (oblations and the like to you); pra ārcat — worship exceedingly.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.3) (Kannada, rendered)

"We call you, who know all (with praise); you, [being] learned [and] called by you, make known to us now the praises that are fit to be known; (we) desire your (favour), and, offering (oblations and the like), we worship you."

English Translation (as printed)

"we invoke you who know all things; may you, who are omniscient, declare to us to-day the praise that is acceptable; desirous of your presence, I reverence you, offering (oblations)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 3)

Yuvākuḥ — yuvāṃ kāmayate iti yuvākuḥ: "'one who desires you (the two)' is the meaning. Skandasvāmin explains the word as yuṣmatkāmaḥ — 'desirous of you'."

Manma — mananīyaṃ jñātavyaṃ stotram: "'a praise that must be known, or that is to be pondered' — thus Sāyaṇa. Yāska quotes:

उप प्रागात्सुमन्मे धायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्ठः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१८७-? [as read; the last numeral doubtful [?]])

upa prāgātsumanme dhāyi manma devānāmāśā upa vītapṛṣṭhaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-187-? [as read; the last numeral doubtful [?]])

and the author of the vṛtti explains manma as mananīyam ṛjujātam [as read [?]]. In this same sense the word is used in several other places:

तमू षु समना गिरा पितॄणां च मन्मभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-४८-२ [as read]; Ni. 10-? [as read])

tamū ṣu samanā girā pitṝṇāṃ ca manmabhiḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 8-48-2 [as read]; Ni. 10-? [as read])

original p. 507

प्र तद्दुःशीमं पृथिवीं भव्यामेन्दवे ... रेजति ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१८६-?) [the Sanskrit as printed is irregular; read only in part [?]]

pra tadduḥśīmaṃ pṛthivīṃ bhavyāmendave ... rejati ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-186-?) [the Sanskrit as printed is irregular; read only in part [?]]

— "here the word manma is explained as mananāni prajñānāni — 'acts of understanding, knowledges'. [The sense:] 'Calling to the omniscient Aśvins, we praise them with the praise-words that [bring] into the range of the mind the intellect they inspire' — thus it is described; and it is also explained that the Aśvins are called by the mantra-seer, who wished to praise them, and, being praised, the oblations are made [by him], and again he pleases them with praises."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Tā — the word tad; with the dual following, tyadādīnām aḥ (Pā. 7-2-102 as read), a substituted; supāṃ sulug, ā for the case ending. Havāmahe — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, first person plural; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Vidvāṃsā — supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), ā for the case ending. Manma — root mana jñāne; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-75 as read), the suffix manin; since it is nit, the initial acute; in the neuter, am [su] following, svamornapuṃsakāt (Pā. 7-1-23 as read), luk for it; then nalopaḥ [elision of the n]. Vocetam — root brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; āśīrliṅ, second person dual, tam substituted; bruvo vaciḥ (Pā. 2-4-53 as read), vac substituted for the root; liṅyāśiṣy aṅ (Pā. 3-1-86 as read), aṅ; by vyatyaya, iy for yāsuṭ; lopo vyor vali (Pā. 6-1-66 as read), elision of the y; vaca um (Pā. 7-4-20 as read), the augment um; guṇa; the form vocetam; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Ārcat — root arca pūjāyām, bhvādi; by the statement tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavantīti [Vedic exchange of person-endings], tip for the mip of the first person; laṅ, first person singular; iteś ca, elision of the i; śap vikaraṇa; the augment aṭ; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Dayamānaḥ — root daya dānagatirakṣaṇahiṃsādāneṣu, bhvādi; in the sense of laṭ, śānac; śap vikaraṇa; ānemuk (Pā. 7-2-82 as read), the augment muk for the a-ending …

original p. 508

Grammar of Ṛk 3, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Dayamānaḥ (continued) — since śap is pit, it is anudātta; since the lasārvadhātuka (śānac) stands after upadeśa, tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186 as read) makes it anudātta, so the root's accent remains. Yuvākuḥ — yuvāṃ kāmayate iti yuvākuḥ; by the statement mitadrvādibhya upasaṅkhyānam (Pā. 3-2-180 vārttika as read), the suffix ḍu; when kam + u [is formed], by the strength of ḍit, elision of the ṭi [of the base]; though a case ending follows, by vyatyaya, yuvāvau dvivacane (Pā. 7-2-92 as read), yuva substituted up to ma, and ā. Or: root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ; the auṇādika suffix kāku; since it is kit, guṇa does not occur; uvaṅ substituted; by the suffix's initial acute the ā of the suffix gets the acute. ‖ 3 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.4)

वि पृच्छामि पाक्या न देवान्वषट्कृतस्याद्भुतस्य दस्रा । पातं च सह्यसो युवं च रभ्यसो नः ॥ ४ ॥

vi pṛcchāmi pākyā na devānvaṣaṭkṛtasyādbhutasya dasrā | pātaṃ ca sahyaso yuvaṃ ca rabhyaso naḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.4)

वि । पृच्छामि । पाक्या । न । देवान् । वषट्ऽकृतस्य । अद्भुतस्य । दस्रा । पातम् । च । सह्यसः । युवम् । च । रभ्यसः । नः ॥ ४ ॥

vi | pṛcchāmi | pākyā | na | devān | vaṣaṭ 'kṛtasya | adbhutasya | dasrā | pātam | ca | sahyasaḥ | yuvam | ca | rabhyasaḥ | naḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.4)

हे अश्विनौ युवां वि पृच्छामि । विशेषेण पृष्ट्वेच्छामि । पाक्या न पक्तव्यप्रज्ञान् स्वपरिपक्वमतीनन्यान्देवान्न पृच्छामि । किंतु युवामेव सर्वज्ञौ पृच्छामीत्यर्थः । हे दस्रा दर्शनीयौ ता युवां वषट्कृतस्य वषट्कारेणाग्नौ हुतस्याद्भुतस्याश्चर्यभूतस्य महतः सह्यसो ऽतिशयेन बलवतो बलोत्पादकस्य सोमस्य स्वांशलक्षणमेकदेशं पातं च । नोऽस्माँश्च रभ्यसोऽतिशयेन रभसो वीर्यवतः प्रोद्यमवतः कुरुतम् ॥ पाक्या । पचेर्बहुलम् । ण्यत् [?] । चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोरिति कुत्वम् । तित्स्वरितः । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्डादेशः । वषट्कृतस्य । वषट्शब्दस्योर्ध्वादिश्चेन गतित्वाद्गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पातम् । पा पाने । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । सह्यसः । सहेर्बहुवचनेनेति सहो बलम् । असुन् । तदस्यास्तीति सहस्विन् । मत्वर्थीयो विनिः । ततः अतिशायनिक ईयसुन् । विन्मतोर्लुक् । छान्दस ईकारलोपः । रभ्यसः । रभ राभस्ये । राभस्यं कार्योत्सुक्यम् । पूर्ववत्प्रक्रिया ॥ [as read]

he aśvinau yuvāṃ vi pṛcchāmi | viśeṣeṇa pṛṣṭvecchāmi | pākyā na paktavyaprajñān svaparipakvamatīnanyāndevānna pṛcchāmi | kiṃtu yuvāmeva sarvajñau pṛcchāmītyarthaḥ | he dasrā darśanīyau tā yuvāṃ vaṣaṭkṛtasya vaṣaṭkāreṇāgnau hutasyādbhutasyāścaryabhūtasya mahataḥ sahyaso 'tiśayena balavato balotpādakasya somasya svāṃśalakṣaṇamekadeśaṃ pātaṃ ca | no 'smā~śca rabhyaso 'tiśayena rabhaso vīryavataḥ prodyamavataḥ kurutam ‖ pākyā | pacerbahulam | ṇyat [?] | cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoriti kutvam | titsvaritaḥ | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterḍādeśaḥ | vaṣaṭkṛtasya | vaṣaṭśabdasyordhvādiścena gatitvādgatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | pātam | pā pāne | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | sahyasaḥ | saherbahuvacaneneti saho balam | asun | tadasyāstīti sahasvin | matvarthīyo viniḥ | tataḥ atiśāyanika īyasun | vinmatorluk | chāndasa īkāralopaḥ | rabhyasaḥ | rabha rābhasye | rābhasyaṃ kāryotsukyam | pūrvavatprakriyā ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, vi pṛcchāmi — I ask you specially. Pākyā na — I do not ask the other gods, [whose minds are] not yet ripened, of immature understanding; but you alone, the omniscient, I ask. O dasrā — worth seeing — [please] drink (pātam) your own share of the vaṣaṭkṛta — the soma that has been offered in the fire by the vaṣaṭ call, adbhuta — wonderful, great, sahyasaḥ — exceedingly strong, strength-producing; and make us rabhyasaḥ — exceedingly vigorous, energetic, enterprising."

original p. 509

Bhāṣya's grammar tail, concluded; small type "rabhyasaḥ — root rabha rābhasye; rābhasya means eagerness for work; the process as before."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.4) (Kannada, rendered)

Aśvinau — O Aśvins; yuvām — [you], the all-knowing; vi pṛcchāmi — I ask intently; pākyā — [those] of ripe knowledge; devān — other gods; na (pṛcchāmi) — I do not ask; he) dasrā — O Aśvins worth seeing; vaṣaṭkṛtasya — [of that] which is offered into the fire with the vaṣaṭ; adbhutasya — wonderful; sahyasaḥ — strength-giving; (somarasasya — of the soma-juice (your share); pātaṃ ca — drink; naḥ ca — and us; rabhyasaḥ — those energetic ([in undertakings]); kuru — make.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.4) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Dasras! I ask you, the all-knowing, with great intentness; I do not ask the other gods, who are of unripe knowledge; drink the wonderful and strength-giving [soma], offered into the fire with the vaṣaṭ call (your share of the soma-juice), and make us foremost [in] undertakings."

English Translation (as printed)

"I invite not the gods immature (in wisdom), but you, Dasras; drink of the wonderful and strength-giving burnt-offering, and make us vigorous."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 4)

Pākyā na devān na pṛcchāmi — na pakvaprajñān sva-paripakvamatīn anyān devān na pṛcchāmi kiṃtu yuvām eva pṛcchāmi sarvajñau: "'I do not ask the other gods, whose understanding is not ripened; I ask only you, the omniscient' — the word pāka is stated among the eight [?] names of 'praiseworthy' (Ni. 3-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೧೩']). 'I will pray that [you], the knowing and wise Aśvins, make our minds greatly knowing, and that we, praising them …'" continues on p. 510

original p. 510

Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued "… we listen to them so that their favour should come to us. By asking them, [we mean that] since the [other] gods are of lesser [capacity] in intellect, and the fruit which we need cannot be got from them, we do not ask them."

"In this Ṛk it is described: that the Aśvins, who are regarded as omniscient because of their greater knowledge, accept the great and nourishing oblations offered into the fire with the vaṣaṭ call, and, drinking the soma-juice, favour us — so that our knowledge, in praising them, grows, our understanding is exceedingly great, and, [that] it may not turn to other gods, whose power is less than theirs."

Adbhutasya — āścaryabhūtasya mahataḥ: "The word adbhuta is stated among the names of 'great' (Ni. 3-13 [as read]). By this word is described the greatness of the substance offered in the fire with the call vaṣaṭ."

Sahyasaḥ — sahate abhibhavati aneneti sahaḥ balam tadasyāsti iti sahasvī: "The strength that enables one to overcome others is called by the word sahas. One who has such strength is called sahasvī; one who has it in excess [is sahyas]; that is the meaning."

Rabhyasaḥ — atiśayena rabhasvinaḥ prodyamānān: "The word rabhasa is stated among the names of 'great' (Ni. 3-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೧೩']). 'The Aśvins are prayed that in us, whose nature includes speed and strength, greatness may arise.' The meaning of the word rabhyas is 'greatness surpassing others'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Pṛcchāmi — root pracchaṃ jñīpsāyāṃ vāci; laṭ, first person singular; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Pākyā — root ḍupacaṣ pāke; ṛhaloṇyat (Pā. 3-1-124 as read), the suffix ṇyat; since it is ṇit, ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116 as read), vṛddhi of the penultimate; cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ (Pā. 7-3-52 as read), k for the c; since the suffix is tit, tit svaritam (Pā. 6-1-185 as read), the svarita accent; accusative [as printed: dual] following with plural [?], supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), ā substituted; the form pākyā.

original p. 511

Vaṣaṭkṛtasya — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; the suffix kta; since vaṣaṭ is read in the ūry-ādi group, ūryādicviḍācaś ca (Pā. 1-4-61 as read), it gets the gati name; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read), the gati keeps its natural accent; the udātta [of the gati] is the initial acute. Pātam — root pā pāne; loṭ, second person dual; bahulaṃ chandasi, luk for śap, so [the substitution] piba does not occur; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Sahyasaḥ — sahate abhibhavati anena iti sahaḥ balam; root ṣaha marṣaṇe; sarvadhātubhya asun (Uṇ. sū. 4-189 as read), the suffix asun; "sahaḥ asya asti iti sahasvī": asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ (Pā. 5-2-121 as read), the suffix vin in the sense of matup; when "one who has it in excess, sahasvī" is intended, dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau (Pā. 5-3-57 as read) [with atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau], the suffix īyasun; vinmator luk (Pā. 5-3-65 as read), luk for vin when īyasun follows; by Vedic usage elision of the ī. Rabhyasaḥ — root rabha rābhasye; rābhasya means readiness to start a work (the start of a task); as before, the suffix asun; by Vedic usage, vṛddhi of the initial; elision of the vin in the sense of matup; elision of the ṭi; elision of the ī of īyasun; since it is nit, the initial acute. ‖ 4 ‖

प्र या घोषे भृगवाणे न शोभे यया वाचा यजति पज्रियो वाम् । प्रैषयुर्न विद्वान् ॥ ५ ॥

pra yā ghoṣe bhṛgavāṇe na śobhe yayā vācā yajati pajriyo vām | praiṣayurna vidvān ‖ 5 ‖

pra | yā | ghoṣe | bhṛgavāṇe | na | śobhe | yayā | vācā | yajati | pajriyaḥ | vām | pra | iṣa 'yuḥ | na | vidvān ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.5)

हे अश्विनौ प्र भवति समर्था भवति सा वाक् या वाक् स्तुतिरूपा घोषे घोषाख्यायाः पुत्रे सुहस्त्याख्ये ऋषौ भृगवाणे न भृगौ च शोभे शोभते । यया च स्तुतिलक्षणया वाचा पज्रियः । पज्रा अङ्गिरसः । तेषां कुलोत्पन्नः कक्षीवानयं वां युवां यजति पूजयति स्तौति । साऽपि शोभते इत्यर्थः । इषयुर्न इषमन्नमात्मनः कामयमानश्च विद्वान् स्तुत्यभिज्ञः कक्षीवानृषिः प्र भवतु । युष्मदनुग्रहात्संपूर्णकामो भवत्वित्यर्थः ॥ घोषे । घोषा नाम काचिद्ब्रह्मवादिनी कक्षीवतः पुत्री । अत्रोपचारात्त्यद्वाचकं प्रातिपदिकं पुत्रे वर्तते । भृगवाणे । चिरंतनो भृगुरिवाचरति । सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्य इति क्विप् । धातुसंज्ञायां व्यत्ययेन लटः शानच् । शबादि । आगमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वान्नुम्गभावः । वृषादिः । शोभे । शुभ दीप्तौ । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः । इषयुः । इष गतौ । इष्यति गच्छतीतीषमन्नं । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । यद्वा । इषु इच्छायाम् । इष्यते सर्वैः प्राणिभिरितीषमन्नम् । व्यत्ययेन कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः । प्रशब्देन संहितायां प्रादूहोढोढ्येषैष्येषु वृद्धिर्वक्तव्या । (पा. ६-१-८९-१ [as read]) इति वृद्धिः ॥

he aśvinau pra bhavati samarthā bhavati sā vāk yā vāk stutirūpā ghoṣe ghoṣākhyāyāḥ putre suhastyākhye ṛṣau bhṛgavāṇe na bhṛgau ca śobhe śobhate | yayā ca stutilakṣaṇayā vācā pajriyaḥ | pajrā aṅgirasaḥ | teṣāṃ kulotpannaḥ kakṣīvānayaṃ vāṃ yuvāṃ yajati pūjayati stauti | sā 'pi śobhate ityarthaḥ | iṣayurna iṣamannamātmanaḥ kāmayamānaśca vidvān stutyabhijñaḥ kakṣīvānṛṣiḥ pra bhavatu | yuṣmadanugrahātsaṃpūrṇakāmo bhavatvityarthaḥ ‖ ghoṣe | ghoṣā nāma kācidbrahmavādinī kakṣīvataḥ putrī | atropacārāttyadvācakaṃ prātipadikaṃ putre vartate | bhṛgavāṇe | ciraṃtano bhṛgurivācarati | sarvaprātipadikebhya iti kvip | dhātusaṃjñāyāṃ vyatyayena laṭaḥ śānac | śabādi | āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvānnumgabhāvaḥ | vṛṣādiḥ | śobhe | śubha dīptau | lopasta ātmanepadeṣviti talopaḥ | iṣayuḥ | iṣa gatau | iṣyati gacchatītīṣamannaṃ | igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ | yadvā | iṣu icchāyām | iṣyate sarvaiḥ prāṇibhiritīṣamannam | vyatyayena karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ | praśabdena saṃhitāyāṃ prādūhoḍhoḍhyeṣaiṣyeṣu vṛddhirvaktavyā | (pā. 6-1-89-1 [as read]) iti vṛddhiḥ ‖

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins, pra bhavati — that speech is capable, the speech in the form of praise which shines (śobhe) ghoṣe — in the son of Ghoṣā, the ṛṣi named Suhastya, and bhṛgavāṇe na — in Bhṛgu; and with which speech in the form of praise pajriyaḥ — Kakṣīvān, born in the family of the Pajras, the Aṅgirases — vāṃ yajati — worships, praises you: that [speech] too shines. Iṣayur na — as one who desires food (iṣam) for himself, and vidvān — knowing how to praise: may the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān prevail (pra bhavatu): may he, by your favour, have all his desires fulfilled."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.5) (Kannada, rendered)

Yā — which (praise-word in your praise); ghoṣe — in the son of the woman Ghoṣā, in Suhastya also; bhṛgavāṇe na — in Bhṛgu also; śobhe — shines (it is prominent); pra (bhavati) — is capable; yayā vācā — by which word; pajriyaḥ — Kakṣīvān, born of the line of Pajra; vām — you; yajati — worships; iṣayuḥ — desirous of food; vidvān na — also one knowing the praise, Kakṣīvān; pra (bhavatu) — may he be fully desirous (may his desires be fulfilled).

original p. 513

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.5) (Kannada, rendered)

"The praise-words used by Kakṣīvān, of the line of Pajra — the son of the woman Ghoṣā, and also Bhṛgu — are full of power. May Kakṣīvān, who desires food and who knows how to praise, obtain his wish by your favour."

English Translation (as printed)

"(Powerful is) the hymn that was repeated by the son of Ghosha, and by Bhrigu, and with which hymn the Angirasas adore you; may the sage (Kakshsivat), desirous (of food), obtain it abundantly."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 5)

"In explaining the meaning of this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin hold somewhat different views. Sāyaṇa, in explaining the word ghoṣe:

घोषे । घोषा नाम काचिद्ब्रह्मवादिनी कक्षीवतः पुत्री । अत्रोपचारात्तद्वाचकं प्रातिपदिकं पुत्रे वर्तते । घोषाख्यायाः पुत्रे सुहस्त्याख्ये ऋषौ ।

ghoṣe | ghoṣā nāma kācidbrahmavādinī kakṣīvataḥ putrī | atropacārāttadvācakaṃ prātipadikaṃ putre vartate | ghoṣākhyāyāḥ putre suhastyākhye ṛṣau |

— 'Ghoṣā was a certain brahmavādinī woman, a daughter of Kakṣīvān; here, by transference of sense, the stem denoting her stands for her son; in the son of the woman named Ghoṣā, in the ṛṣi named Suhastya'. A woman named Ghoṣā, the daughter of the ṛṣi called Kakṣīvān, was a knower of the Self; her son was known by the name Suhastya. He is indicated here by the word ghoṣā; this is held to be a figurative usage (aupacārika) — a usage that accepts a transfer of the mother's name to the son. Skandasvāmin: ghoṣyamāṇatvāt ghoṣaḥ stomaḥ — he explains: 'because it is uttered in a high voice, ghoṣa means praise'."

Bhṛgavāṇe — ciraṃtano bhṛgur ivācarati: "'one who behaves as the ancient Bhṛgu' — Sāyaṇa; and taking the particle na ['like'] in the sense of 'and', he explains bhṛgavāṇe na śobhe as bhṛgau ca śobhate, 'it shines also in the ṛṣi Bhṛgu'. In bhṛgavāṇe na śobhe, the word na is a word of comparison. [Bhṛgavāṇa is a synonym of bhṛgu]: bhṛgavāṇaśabdo bhṛgoḥ paryāyaḥ; sa saptamyarthe ca saptamī; bhṛgor iva pra śobhe prakarṣeṇa śobhate; hence 'as it shines in Bhṛgu'. The word bhṛgavāṇa is a synonym of bhṛgu, so it conveys the meaning of the ṛṣi Bhṛgu: 'as it shines gloriously in the ṛṣi Bhṛgu'."

Pajriyaḥ — "Skandasvāmin: prakarṣeṇa yajati; pājaḥ haviḥlakṣaṇam annam taddārhaḥ pajriyaḥ; athavā pajrā aṅgirasaḥ teṣām apatyabhūtaḥ pajriyaḥ kakṣīvān ātmanā vivāyaṃ [as read [?]]" continues on p. 514

original p. 514

Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued "… [pajriyaḥ is used] parokṣarūpeṇa prathamapuruṣeṇa nirdeśaḥ — 'the statement in the indirect, third-person form'. Yāska, explaining that the word pājas is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [as read]) and pājaḥ pālanāt (Ni. 6-?? [as read]), gives pāja the meaning 'strength'. Since food produces strength, Skandasvāmin, admitting a transfer of sense from effect to cause, explains the word pāja as 'food', and explains pajriyaḥ as one who offers the food in the form of oblation. And [another meaning]: pajrāḥ are the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis; one born in their line is pajriyaḥ. (Here) in this Ṛk, by the third-person form (parokṣa), it is explained that Kakṣīvān himself is pajriyaḥ, born in the family of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis."

"As the words of praise of the ṛṣi Suhastya, son of the woman Ghoṣā, which praise the Aśvins, shine, so the words of praise of Kakṣīvān shine. Kakṣīvān, expert in praising, desirous of food and so on, praises, and, offering oblations, [prays] that the Aśvins' favour should be on him for the fulfilment of his wishes — this is described."

Iṣayurna — annakāma iva kaścit yuṣmanmāhātmyaṃ vā yaṣṭuṃ vā jānan: "'Like one who wishes to obtain food and so on, knowing the greatness of the Aśvins, or acting so that he may offer sacrifice with regard to them' — in this matter too, Skandasvāmin, by giving a comparison (upamāna) and explaining the sense of the sentence, explains that two comparisons are intended by the two sentences here."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Ghoṣe — Ghoṣā is the name of Kakṣīvān's daughter. She was a brahmavādinī. Here, since the usage is figurative (aupacārika), the noun that denotes her is used for her son. Bhṛgavāṇe — ciraṃtano bhṛgur ivācarati bhṛgavati; sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvib vā vaktavyaḥ — by this statement, kvip; since it is read in the sanādi group, sanādyantā dhātavaḥ (Pā. 3-1-32 as read), it gets the dhātu name; in the sense of laṭ, by vyatyaya the suffix śānac; śap vikaraṇa; on that account, guṇa of the u of the base, av; āgamānuśāsanam anityam — by this statement the muk augment does not occur for the a-ending; since the ṛ-sound is the cause, ṇatva of the n; since it is read in the vṛṣādi group, by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (Pā. 6-1-203 as read) the initial acute, though citsvara was obtained. Śobhe — root śubha dīptau; laṭ, third person singular, the suffix ta; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 as read), e; śap vikaraṇa; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. 7-3-86 as read), …

original p. 515

…concluded "… guṇa [of the light penultimate]; lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. 7-1-41 as read), elision of the t of the suffix; since the word yat is connected, no nighāta; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the root's accent remains. Vācā — sāvekācas tṛtīyādir viḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 as read), the acute on the case ending. Iṣayuḥ — root iṣa gatau; "iṣyati gacchati iti iṣam annam"; the root has ik as a penultimate, so igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ (Pā. 3-1-135 as read), the suffix ka; since it is kit, guṇa does not occur. Or: root iṣu icchāyām; "iṣyate sarvaiḥ prāṇibhiḥ iti iṣam annam"; by vyatyaya, the agent suffix in the passive sense; "iṣam ātmana icchati" — iṣayati: supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 as read), the suffix kyac; na cchandasy aputrasya (Pā. 7-4-35 as read), the lengthening etc. do not come; after the kyajanta, in the agent sense, kyāc chandasi (Pā. 3-2-170 as read), the suffix u; ato lopaḥ, elision of the a of kyac; by the suffix's accent the final acute; when pra + iṣayuḥ, in the Saṃhitā, prādūhoḍhodhyeṣaiṣyeṣu vṛddhir vaktavyā (Pā. 6-1-89 vārttika as read), vṛddhi arises. ‖ 5 ‖
