॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.6)

हे अश्विनावश्विनौ गायत्रं गातव्यं गायत्रीच्छन्दोयुक्तं गायत्रसाम्ना निष्पाद्यं वा स्तोत्रं तकवानस्य स्खलद्गतेरन्धस्य ऋज्राश्वस्य संबन्धि श्रुतं । अश्रुणुतम् । अहं चिदहमिव वां युवां स ऋज्राश्वो रिरेभ । स्तुतवान् । किं कुर्वन् । हे शुभस्पती शोभनस्य कर्मणः पालयितारौ जलस्य वा स्वामिनौ । अक्षी युवाभ्यां दत्ते चक्षुषी आ दन् आददानः । तस्मा इव मध्वमुष्मभिमतफलं प्रयच्छतमिति भावः ॥ श्रुतम् । श्रु श्रवणे । लङ् । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । तकवानस्य । तक गतौ । अत्र गतिसामान्यवाचिना तकशब्देन विशेषो मन्दगतिर्लक्ष्यते । औणादिक उप्रत्ययः । भृगवाण इतिवत्प्रक्रियोन्नेया । रिरेभ । रेभृ शब्दे । अक्षी । ई च द्विवचन इत्यक्षिशब्दस्य ईकारान्तादेशः । स चोदात्तः । शुभस्पती । सुबामन्त्रिते परांगवत्स्वर इति पष्ठ्यन्तस्य परांगवद्भावाप्तद्वयसमुदायस्याष्टमिकामन्त्रितानुदात्तत्वम् । दन् । आङ्पूर्वाद्दातेराजो दोऽनास्यविहरणे [?] । (पा. १-३-२० [as read]) इत्यात्मनेपदम् । व्यत्ययेन शतृ । जुहोत्यादित्वात्श्लुः । द्विवचनप्रकरणे छन्दसि वेति वक्तव्यमिति वचनाद्बहुवचनाभावः । छन्दस्युभयथेत्युभयथाश्रयणात् शतुः सार्वधातुकत्वेन ङित्त्वम् । अर्धधातुकत्वादातो लोप इटि चेत्याकारलोपः ॥ [as read]

he aśvināvaśvinau gāyatraṃ gātavyaṃ gāyatrīcchandoyuktaṃ gāyatrasāmnā niṣpādyaṃ vā stotraṃ takavānasya skhaladgaterandhasya ṛjrāśvasya saṃbandhi śrutaṃ | aśruṇutam | ahaṃ cidahamiva vāṃ yuvāṃ sa ṛjrāśvo rirebha | stutavān | kiṃ kurvan | he śubhaspatī śobhanasya karmaṇaḥ pālayitārau jalasya vā svāminau | akṣī yuvābhyāṃ datte cakṣuṣī ā dan ādadānaḥ | tasmā iva madhvamuṣmabhimataphalaṃ prayacchatamiti bhāvaḥ ‖ śrutam | śru śravaṇe | laṅ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | takavānasya | taka gatau | atra gatisāmānyavācinā takaśabdena viśeṣo mandagatirlakṣyate | auṇādika upratyayaḥ | bhṛgavāṇa itivatprakriyonneyā | rirebha | rebhṛ śabde | akṣī | ī ca dvivacana ityakṣiśabdasya īkārāntādeśaḥ | sa codāttaḥ | śubhaspatī | subāmantrite parāṃgavatsvara iti paṣṭhyantasya parāṃgavadbhāvāptadvayasamudāyasyāṣṭamikāmantritānudāttatvam | dan | āṅpūrvāddāterājo do 'nāsyaviharaṇe [?] | (pā. 1-3-20 [as read]) ityātmanepadam | vyatyayena śatṛ | juhotyāditvātśluḥ | dvivacanaprakaraṇe chandasi veti vaktavyamiti vacanādbahuvacanābhāvaḥ | chandasyubhayathetyubhayathāśrayaṇāt śatuḥ sārvadhātukatvena ṅittvam | ardhadhātukatvādāto lopa iṭi cetyākāralopaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Aśvins: gāyatram — the song to be sung, the hymn that is of the Gāyatrī metre or accomplished by the Gāyatra-sāman — śrutam — you heard, [the song] belonging to Ṛjrāśva, who was takavānasya — of the stumbling gait, [i.e. the blind]. Ahaṃ cid — like me, he, Ṛjrāśva, rirebha — praised you two. What does he do? Śubhaspatī — O protectors of good works, or lords of water, ā dan — taking back the akṣī — the two eyes you gave him [or: taking, receiving] — to him, as to me, give (prayacchatam) the sweet [oblation, and] the fruit that is wished — such is the meaning."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.6) (Kannada, rendered)

He) aśvinau — O Aśvins; gāyatram — [the hymn] of Gāyatrī metre (fit to be sung); takavānasya — [of him who is] stumbling (because of blindness) — Ṛjrāśva's praise; śrutam — you heard; aham cit — like me; vām — you two; śubhaspatī — O Aśvins who are protectors of good deeds (lords of water); ā akṣī — the eyes given by you; ā dan — having got; (saḥ — he, Ṛjrāśva; rireba hi — praised, indeed.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.6) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins, protectors of good deeds (lords of water)! You heard the praise, in Gāyatrī metre, of Ṛjrāśva, who stumbled [in blindness]; having got the eyes you gave, he praised you just as I have. (Therefore favour me too as you favoured him.)"

English Translation (as printed)

"Hear the song of the stumbling (blind man), for verily, Aswins, I gorify [sic] you, recovering my eyes (through you), who are protectors of good works."

original p. 517

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 6)

Takavānasya — skhaladgateḥ andhasya ṛjrāśvasya sambandhi: "Here the word taka, which in general indicates going, is used specially for slow, stumbling going: 'for one whose gait has stumbled, the blind Ṛjrāśva — [who,] being blind and unable to see, walks stumbling' is the meaning. The root taka has the sense of going, and here a stumbling gait is meant."

Gāyatram — gātavyaṃ gāyatrīcchandoyuktam | gāyatrasāmnā niṣpādyaṃ vā stotram: "'What is to be sung, or [that] which is of Gāyatrī metre', or 'the hymn performed by the Gāyatra-sāman' is Sāyaṇa's explanation. Skandasvāmin: gāyatrīty arcatikarmasu (Ni. 3-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೧೯']) pāṭhāt arcatikarmāyam — since the root gai is read among roots of the sense 'to worship', [it means worship]; gīyate anena iti gāyatraṃ stotram — 'that by which it is sung is the gāyatra, a hymn'; and since the statement gāyatraṃ gāyateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೧-೮']) is made in explaining the word gāyatra, the word gāyatra means 'a collection of hymns'."

Śubhaspatī — śobhanasya karmaṇaḥ pālayitārau jalasya vā svāminau: "'those who protect auspicious acts, [or] lords of waters' is the meaning. Since the word śubh is stated among the names of water (Ni. 1-12 [as read]), Skandasvāmin explains śubhaspatī as 'lords of the rain and of the waters that fall'."

"Because the Aśvins graciously gave Ṛjrāśva eyes, as [he had] before, he praised the Aśvins. 'May the Aśvins, who produce good, hearing the praise of the seer of the mantra, fulfil his desired objects' — so the prayer is described."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Śrutam — root śru śravaṇe; laṅ, second person dual, tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtamtāmaḥ (Pā. 3-4-101 as read), tam substituted; bahulaṃ chandasi, luk for the vikaraṇa; since it is jit [śnu removed], guṇa of the root's u does not occur; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75 as read), the augment aṭ does not occur; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; by the suffix's accent the final acute.

original p. 518

Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Takavānasya — root taka gatau; though it is a general word for going, here it is used for the specific slow going; the auṇādika suffix u; as was said in bhṛgavāṇe, here too, in the sense of conduct (ācāra), kvip; since it gets the dhātu name, by vyatyaya śānac is substituted for laṭ; since vṛṣādi is an ākṛtigaṇa, vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (Pā. 6-1-203 as read), the initial acute. Rirebhe — the root rebhṛ śabde; liṭ, third person singular; since hi is connected, the nighāta accent has the prohibition by hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34 as read); since ṇal is lit, liti (Pā. 6-1-193 as read), the acute on the syllable before the suffix, so it becomes a middle-acute word. Akṣī — with the dual following, īcca dvivacane (Pā. 7-1-77 as read), ī is substituted for the final; it is udātta. Śubhaspatī — subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare (Pā. 2-1-2 as read), the word ending in the genitive becomes as a part of the following āmantrita; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19 as read), the nighāta accent for the group of two words. Dan — root dudāñ dāne; since āṅ is the prefix, āṅo 'nāsyavihṛtyam [āṅo dośāsyavihṛtye?] (Pā. 1-3-20 as read), the middle-voice; vyatyayo bahulam, in the sense of laṭ the suffix śatṛ; since it is juhotyādi, ślu vikaraṇa; by the statement dvivacane prakaraṇe chandasi vetivaktavyam, here no doubling of the root occurs by ślau [Pā. 6-1-10]; by chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 as read), since it has the name sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, sārvadhātukam apit gives [the ṅit-like state], and by ato lopa iṭi ca (Pā. 6-4-64 as read), elision of the ā; the word dat; with the nominative following, since it is ugit, num; halṅyābbhyo…, elision of su; saṃyogāntalopa, elision of the t; since this is asiddha, the elision of the n does not occur. ‖ 6 ‖

original p. 519

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.7)

युवं ह्यास्तं महो रन्युवं वा यन्निरततंसतम् । ता नो वसू सुगोपा स्यातं पातं नो वृकादघायोः ॥ ७ ॥

yuvaṃ hyāstaṃ maho ranyuvaṃ vā yanniratataṃsatam | tā no vasū sugopā syātaṃ pātaṃ no vṛkādaghāyoḥ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.7) The printed Pada reads "ranyuvam" with a stray avagraha and "niḥatatamsatam" — as printed; I give the evident words.

युवम् । हि । आस्तम् । महः । रन् । युवम् । वा । यत् । निःऽअततंसतम् । ता । नः । वसू इति । सुऽगोपा । स्यातम् । पातम् । नः । वृकात् । अघऽयोः ॥ ७ ॥

yuvam | hi | āstam | mahaḥ | ran | yuvam | vā | yat | niḥ 'atataṃsatam | tā | naḥ | vasū iti | su 'gopā | syātam | pātam | naḥ | vṛkāt | agha 'yoḥ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.7)

हे अश्विनौ महो महतो धनस्य रन् रातारौ दातारौ युवं युवां किंचनास्तं ... निरततंसतं धनानि निरगमयतम् । रक्षकौ विनाशकावसि युवमेवेत्येवार्थः । हे वसू वासयितारावश्विनौ ता तादृशौ युवां नोऽस्माकं सुगोपा सुष्ठु गोपायितारौ रक्षितारौ स्यातं । भवतं । अपि च नोऽस्मानघायोरघमस्माकमिच्छतो वृकात्स्तेनात्पातं । रक्षतम् ॥ महः । महतः । छान्दसो वर्णलोपः । रन् । रन्नित्यवत्प्रक्रियोन्नेया । व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । निरततंसतम् । तसि अलंकारे । अस्मान्ण्यन्ताल्लङि निरिप्रसृस्तुभ्य इति च्लेरङ् द्विर्वचनादि च । गरुसंज्ञाया लघुसंज्ञाया बाधितत्वात्तस्य द्वाभावः । सुगोपा । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्लुक् । अघायोः । अघं परेषामिच्छति । छन्दसि परेच्छायामिति क्यच् । अश्वाघस्यादित्वम् । क्याच्छन्दसीत्युप्रत्ययः ॥ [as read]

he aśvinau maho mahato dhanasya ran rātārau dātārau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ kiṃcanāstaṃ ... niratataṃsataṃ dhanāni niragamayatam | rakṣakau vināśakāvasi yuvamevetyevārthaḥ | he vasū vāsayitārāvaśvinau tā tādṛśau yuvāṃ no 'smākaṃ sugopā suṣṭhu gopāyitārau rakṣitārau syātaṃ | bhavataṃ | api ca no 'smānaghāyoraghamasmākamicchato vṛkātstenātpātaṃ | rakṣatam ‖ mahaḥ | mahataḥ | chāndaso varṇalopaḥ | ran | rannityavatprakriyonneyā | vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ | niratataṃsatam | tasi alaṃkāre | asmānṇyantāllaṅi niriprasṛstubhya iti cleraṅ dvirvacanādi ca | garusaṃjñāyā laghusaṃjñāyā bādhitatvāttasya dvābhāvaḥ | sugopā | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterluk | aghāyoḥ | aghaṃ pareṣāmicchati | chandasi parecchāyāmiti kyac | aśvāghasyāditvam | kyācchandasītyupratyayaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, raṇ — givers (rātārau) of mahaḥ — great wealth: you who (yat) nirata-taṃsatam — sent forth the riches (dhanāni): you alone are protectors and destroyers. O vasū — makers of dwelling, Aśvins: be to us (asmākam) sugopā — good guardians; and pātam — protect us from vṛkāt — the thief, [from] aghāyoḥ — one who wishes us evil."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.7) (Kannada, rendered; text partly legible)

He) vasū — O Aśvins; mahaḥ — of great wealth; ran — givers; yuvam hi — you two indeed; āstam — are; (yat — when; yuvam vā — you two; niḥ atataṃsatam — sent forth riches; tā yuvām — you two, such; naḥ — our; sugopā — good protectors; syātam — be; aghāyoḥ — [from] the one who wishes evil (from the thief); vṛkāt — from the wolf (from the evil [creature]); naḥ pātam — protect us.

original p. 520

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.7) (Kannada, rendered; as printed on p. 520, complete)

(He) aśvinau — O Aśvins; yuvam — you two; mahaḥ — great wealth; ran — those who give; āstam — are; yuvam — you two; nirataṃsatam — [wealth] ruined (made to disappear); (he) vasū — O Aśvins, givers of dwellings; tā — such; naḥ — to us; sugopā — good protectors; syātam — be; (and) naḥ — us; aghāyoḥ — [from] one who wishes the fruit of sin (to us); vṛkāt — from the thief; pātam — protect.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.7) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! It is you who give great wealth; it is you who destroy it. You, givers of dwelling, be our good protectors; and protect us from the thief who would harm us."

English Translation (as printed)

"You have been givers of great riches; you have again caused them to disappear; do you, who are donors of dwellings, become our preservers; protect us from the felonious robber."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 7)

Mahaḥ — mahato dhanasya: "The word mahas is stated among the names of water (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೧-೩೧']); here it means 'wealth'."

"Skandasvāmin: nirataṃsatam — tasu upakṣaye ity asya idaṃ rūpam; na kaṃnoteḥ yuvām [?] arthamupakṣayathaḥ | yasmai deyaṃ dhanaṃ tasmai ca dhanaṃ dhattam | ya upakṣayitavyas tam upakṣayatha ity arthaḥ [as read; small type [?]] — 'the form nirataṃsatam comes from the root tasu upakṣaye ('to waste away'), with the prefix niḥ; the sense is nāśa, 'ruining'. The Aśvins give wealth, with favour, to those for whom it is to be given; to those who are to be restrained, they ruin their wealth. Therefore they are described as capable of both restraining (nigraha) and favouring (anugraha)."

Vasū — vāsayitārāv aśvinau: "'The Aśvins make [us] live in comfort' — Sāyaṇa; Skandasvāmin explains: 'they are worthy of praise [vasu], or they are possessors of wealth'."

Vṛkāt — stenāt: "'from a thief, [one] who plunders' — Sāyaṇa. The word vṛka conveys the sense 'thunderbolt' (Ni. 6-11 [as read]), and is stated among the names of thunderbolts (Ni. 2-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೨-೧೯']) and vṛkaś candramā bhavati (Ni. 5-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೫-೩೧']), vṛko lāṅgalaṃ bhavati vikartanāt (Ni. 6-26 [as read]) — by these statements, the word vṛka means moon, plough, thief, thunderbolt," says Yāska. (Continues on p. 521)

original p. 521

"… Skandasvāmin, together with these meanings, [says] bhakṣitum icchataḥ prāṇiviśeṣāt athavā adātuḥ pāpakāmāt — 'from an animal [a wolf] that wishes to eat, or from one who does not give, who wishes evil' — i.e. 'one who takes what is in our hands'. In this Ṛk it is prayed that the Aśvins, who exercise restraint and favour, should protect us, and that we may have protection from those who wish to rob us of our wealth and to hurt us."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Āstam — root asa bhuvi; laṅ, second person dual; the prohibition [of the aṭ] by hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34 as read) does not [apply]; the augment aṭ being udātta, the initial acute. Mahaḥ — the word mahat; with the genitive singular following, the form mahataḥ; by Vedic usage the elision of the ati [?] occurs. Or: root maha pūjāyām; kvip ca, the suffix kvip; genitive singular, the form mahaḥ. Ran — root rā ādāne; in the sense of laṭ, the suffix śatṛ; for śap, adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. 2-4-72 as read), luk; by sārvadhātukam apit, since it has jit-like state, and by chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 as read), since it has the ārdhadhātuka name, ato lopa iṭi ca (Pā. 6-4-64 as read), elision of the ā of the root; with su following, since it is ugit, num; elision of su; saṃyogāntalopa; by the suffix's accent the acute; by vyatyayo bahulam the singular suffix has come for the dual. Nirataṃsatam — root tasu alaṅkāre; hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26 as read), ṇic; after the ṇijanta, laṅ, second person dual, tam substituted; ṇiśrisrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ (Pā. 3-1-48 as read), caṅ for cli; caṅi (Pā. 6-1-11 as read), doubling of the root; since it is idit, the augment num for the root; ādihalśeṣa for the reduplicative syllable; since num has come, by guru the laghu name is set aside, sanvallaghuni (Pā. 7-4-93 as read), the sanvad bhāva does not occur; therefore i [etc.] do not occur for the reduplicative syllable; the augment aṭ; since the word yat is connected, nipātair yad yadi… (Pā. 8-1-30 as read), the prohibition of nighāta …

original p. 522

Grammar of Ṛk 7, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Nirataṃsatam (continued) — since it is udātta [the augment aṭ], it has the initial acute; since it stands after udātta at the end of a finite verb, tiṅo gotrādīni … [as read: tiṅ ca udāttavati (Pā. 8-1-71 as read)], the nighāta accent for the gati (nir). Tā — supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), ā for the case ending. Sugopā — root gupū rakṣaṇe; since it is in the pacādi group, the suffix ac; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca, guṇa of the root's light penultimate; as before, ā for the case ending; the final acute. Syātam — root asa bhuvi; vidhiliṅ, second person dual, tam substituted; śnasor allopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-111 as read), elision of the a of the root; nighāta accent. Pātam — root pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; loṭ, second person dual; since tiṅ atiṅaḥ (Pā. 8-1-28 as read), the [rule says] atiṅaḥ is a prohibition [? as printed], and since it comes after a finite verb, the nighāta does not occur; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Aghāyoḥ — when "agham pareṣām icchati" is meant, by the statement chandasi pareccāyām api [as read], the suffix kyac also in the sense of "wishing for others"; aśvāghasyāt (Pā. 7-4-37 as read), ā for the a before kyac; the kyac-final aghāya gets the dhātu name; kyāc chandasi (Pā. 3-2-170 as read), the suffix u after it; ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48 as read), elision of the a of kyac; by the suffix's accent the final acute; fifth singular form. ‖ 7 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.8)

मा कस्मै धातमभ्यमित्रिणे नो माकुत्रा नो गृहेभ्यो धेनवो गुः । स्तनाभुजो अशिश्वीः ॥ ८ ॥

mā kasmai dhātamabhyamitriṇe no mākutrā no gṛhebhyo dhenavo guḥ | stanābhujo aśiśvīḥ ‖ 8 ‖

original p. 523

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.8)

मा । कस्मै । धातम् । अभि । अमित्रिणे । नः । मा । अकुत्र । नः । गृहेभ्यः । धेनवः । गुः । स्तनऽभुजः । अशिश्वीः ॥ ८ ॥

mā | kasmai | dhātam | abhi | amitriṇe | naḥ | mā | akutra | naḥ | gṛhebhyaḥ | dhenavaḥ | guḥ | stana 'bhujaḥ | aśiśvīḥ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.8)

हे अश्विनौ अमित्रिणे । अमित्रं मित्रराहित्यम् । तद्वते कस्मै चिदपि शत्रवे नोऽस्माना भि धातम् । अभिमुख्येन मा स्थापयेतम् । अपि च नोऽस्माकं गृहेभ्यः सकाशात्स्तनाभुजः स्तनैर्वत्सानुष्ठ्यांश्च [?] पालयन्त्यो धेनवो गावोऽशिश्वीः शिशुना वत्सेन विरहिता अस्मदीये गृहेऽशयाना वा सत्योऽकुत्र चिदस्माभिरगम्ये प्रदेशे मा गुः । मा गच्छन्तु ॥ धातम् । धाञो माजः लुङि गातिस्थेति सिचो लुक् । न माङ्योग इत्यडभावः । अकुत्र । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । गुः । इण् गतौ । इणो गा लुङीति गादेशः । गातिस्थेति सिचो लुक् । आत इति झेर्जुस् । स्तनाभुजः । भुज पालनाभ्यवहारयोः । स्तनैर्भुञ्जन्ति पालयन्तीति स्तनाभुजः । क्विप् । अस्येषामपि दृश्यत इति सांहितिको दीर्घः । अशिश्वीः । सख्यशिश्वीति भाषायां । (पा. ४-१-८ [as read]) इति छन्दसि ऽपि व्यत्ययेन निपातनं द्रष्टव्यम् । यद्वा । शिशुरस्यास्तीति शिश्वी । छन्दसीवनिपावति मत्वर्थीय ईकारः । नञ्समासे ऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । अथवा शीङ् स्वप्ने । उत्सर्गश्छन्दसीति किप्प्रत्ययः । द्विर्वचनप्रश्लेषे । ... [as read]

he aśvinau amitriṇe | amitraṃ mitrarāhityam | tadvate kasmai cidapi śatrave no 'smānā bhi dhātam | abhimukhyena mā sthāpayetam | api ca no 'smākaṃ gṛhebhyaḥ sakāśātstanābhujaḥ stanairvatsānuṣṭhyāṃśca [?] pālayantyo dhenavo gāvo 'śiśvīḥ śiśunā vatsena virahitā asmadīye gṛhe 'śayānā vā satyo 'kutra cidasmābhiragamye pradeśe mā guḥ | mā gacchantu ‖ dhātam | dhāño mājaḥ luṅi gātistheti sico luk | na māṅyoga ityaḍabhāvaḥ | akutra | parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | guḥ | iṇ gatau | iṇo gā luṅīti gādeśaḥ | gātistheti sico luk | āta iti jherjus | stanābhujaḥ | bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ | stanairbhuñjanti pālayantīti stanābhujaḥ | kvip | asyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti sāṃhitiko dīrghaḥ | aśiśvīḥ | sakhyaśiśvīti bhāṣāyāṃ | (pā. 4-1-8 [as read]) iti chandasi 'pi vyatyayena nipātanaṃ draṣṭavyam | yadvā | śiśurasyāstīti śiśvī | chandasīvanipāvati matvarthīya īkāraḥ | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vā chandasīti pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ | athavā śīṅ svapne | utsargaśchandasīti kippratyayaḥ | dvirvacanapraśleṣe | ... [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins: amitriṇe — amitra is 'the state of lacking friends'; to any enemy who has it, naḥ — us — mā abhi dhātam — do not hand us over [in the sense of facing]. And, from our homes, may the cows (dhenavaḥ), stanābhujaḥ — that nourish [the calves] with their udders, aśiśvīḥ — without a calf, or [without] sleeping calves in our house, akutra — to a place unreachable by us — mā guḥ — not go."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.8) (Kannada, rendered)

— O Aśvins; amitriṇe — [to one who is] our enemy; kasmai — to anyone; naḥ — us; mā abhidhātam — do not hand over; stanābhujaḥ — protecting by their udders (the calves and men); dhenavaḥ — cows; aśiśvīḥ — [cows] not afflicted by [troubles], [lying] in our houses; akutra — to any place (not accessible to us); naḥ — our; gṛhebhyaḥ — from the houses; mā guḥ — let them not go.

original p. 524

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.8) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! Do not hand us over to (our) enemies; may our cows, which nourish us with their milk, not leave their calves and go anywhere."

English Translation (as printed)

"Deliver us not, Aswins, to our enemies; never may our cows, who nourish us with their udders, stray from our houses, separated from their calves."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 8)

Stanābhujaḥ — stanaiḥ vatsān manuṣyāṃś ca pālayantyaḥ: "Sāyaṇa explains: 'cows which protect, by their udders, calves and men by giving them milk'. Skandasvāmin: stanaiḥ bhujyante yāsāṃ tāḥ stanābhujaḥ — 'cows whose udders are enjoyed [i.e. milked] by calves' — he describes [them] as such [creatures whose udders are enjoyed by calves].

Skandasvāmin gives a meaning somewhat different from what Sāyaṇa says:

द्वितीयपादे धेनूनामुपादानात् तत्सन्निध्यात् धेनूर्वा । धनं वा मा कस्मै चित् अभ्यमित्रिणे अमित्राय दत्तम् ॥

dvitīyapāde dhenūnāmupādānāt tatsannidhyāt dhenūrvā | dhanaṃ vā mā kasmai cit abhyamitriṇe amitrāya dattam ‖

— In the second pāda of this Ṛk, by the word 'cows' [dhenavaḥ]; and also, [as] 'us and:

अस्माकं संबन्धिभ्यो गृहेभ्यो युवाभ्यां दत्ताः धेनवः दुह्यन्ते याः गावः ताः ॥

asmākaṃ saṃbandhibhyo gṛhebhyo yuvābhyāṃ dattāḥ dhenavaḥ duhyante yāḥ gāvaḥ tāḥ ‖

— "the cows given by you to us, which are being milked, and do not lead them to our enemies [i.e. do not let them go astray], but protect them" — such a prayer is described here. And that our wealth should not fall into enemies' hands, and that the cows, along with their calves, which give milk, should remain in our houses constantly, without going elsewhere — so [the poet] prays to the Aśvins."

Akutra — asmābhir agamye pradeśe: "'in a place not reachable by us' — Sāyaṇa; Skandasvāmin: yatra na jñāyate kiṃcid iti tadakiṃ corasthānam | tatra akutra | ajñeye corasthāne — 'the place where nothing is known, [that is,] a thieves' hide-out; there, akutra: in an unknowable thieves' lair'. He explains that the place that is not known [to us] is called akutra; it is a thieves' hide-out, hard to know."

original p. 525

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Dhātam — root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; luṅ, second person dual, tam substituted; since cli has sic substituted, gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 2-4-77 as read), luk for it; since māṅ is connected, na māṅyoge (Pā. 6-4-74 as read), the augment aṭ is prohibited. Amitriṇe — "na vidyate mitraṃ yasya is amitraḥ; amitram asya asti iti amitrī; to him, amitriṇe": ata iniṭhanau (Pā. 5-2-115 as read), the suffix ini in the sense of matup; by the suffix's accent; āṭ kuppvāṅnum…, ṇatva of the n. Akutra — parādiś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-2-199 as read), the latter member's initial acute; nipātasya ca (Pā. 6-3-136 as read), lengthening in the Saṃhitā. Guḥ — root iṇ gatau; luṅ, third person plural, the suffix jhi; iṇo gā luṅi (Pā. 2-4-45 as read), gā substituted for the root, since luṅ is the cause; since cli has sic substituted, gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 2-4-77 as read), luk for sic; āto 'ntaḥ … (Pā. 3-4-110 as read), since sic has been elided and jhi follows an ā-ending, jus is substituted for jhi; uṣyapadāntāt (Pā. 6-1-96 as read), pararūpa; na māṅyoge (Pā. 6-4-74 as read), prohibition of the augment aṭ; tiṅanta nighāta accent. Stanābhujaḥ — root bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ; "stanyena bhuñjanti pālayanti iti stanābhujaḥ" (those that protect [calves and men] with their milk); kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76 as read), the suffix kvip; anyeṣām api dṛśyate (Pā. 6-3-137 as read), lengthening of the former member; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read), the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent; nominative plural form. Aśiśvīḥ — sakhyaśiśvī iti bhāṣāyām (Pā. 4-1-62 as read): [a form] enjoined for the common language by the sūtra, but by vyatyaya the irregular formation must also be admitted in the Veda. Or: "śiśur asya asti iti śiśvī" — chandasīvanipau [chandasīvanipāv…] (Pā. 5-2-109 as read), the suffix ī in the sense of matup; na śiśvī aśiśvī; in the nañ compound, tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 as read), the avyaya former member keeps its natural accent; with jas following, vā chandasi (Pā. 6-1-106 as read), pūrvasavarṇadīrgha …

original p. 526

Grammar of Ṛk 8, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Aśiśvīḥ (continued) — Or: root śīṅ svapne; utsargaś chandasi [as read; Pā. 3-2-171 vārttika? [?]], the suffix kvi (kvin); on that account doubling of the root; hrasvaḥ (Pā. 7-4-59 as read), shortening of the reduplicative syllable; erānekācaḥ asaṃyogapūrvasya (Pā. 6-4-82 as read), yaṇ substituted; by Vedic usage vatva [for the anekāc …]; as before, since it is a nañ-compound, the nañ-compound accent. ‖ 8 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.9)

दुहीयन्मित्रधितये युवाकु राये च नो मिमीतं वाजवत्यै । इषे च नो मिमीतं धेनुमत्यै ॥ ९ ॥

duhīyanmitradhitaye yuvāku rāye ca no mimītaṃ vājavatyai | iṣe ca no mimītaṃ dhenumatyai ‖ 9 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.9)

दुहीयन् । मित्रऽधितये । युवाकु । राये । च । नः । मिमीतम् । वाजऽवत्यै । इषे । च । नः । मिमीतम् । धेनुऽमत्यै ॥ ९ ॥

duhīyan | mitra 'dhitaye | yuvāku | rāye | ca | naḥ | mimītam | vāja 'vatyai | iṣe | ca | naḥ | mimītam | dhenu 'matyai ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.9)

हे अश्विनौ युवाकु युवां कामयमानाः स्तुतिभिर्यावयितारः संयोजयितारो वा स्तोतारो मित्रधितये मित्राणां बन्धुजनानां धारणार्थं दुहीयन् । युष्मत्सकाशाद्धनानि दुहन्ति प्राप्नुवन्ति । अतो नोऽस्मानपि वाजवत्यै वाजयुक्ताय च रायै धनाय मिमीतम् । कुरुतम् । तथा धेनुमत्यै धेनुभिर्युक्तायेषे ऽन्नाय च नोऽस्मभ्यं मिमीतम् । कुरुतम् । अस्मभ्यं स्तोतृभ्यो बलयुक्तं धनं गोयुक्तमन्नं च प्रयच्छतमित्यर्थः ॥ दुहीयन् । दुह प्रपूरणे । दुहेर्दोहः । इगुपधात्कित् । (उ. ४-११६ [as read]) इति भाव इप्रत्ययः । दुहिमात्मन इच्छति दुहीयति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । दुहीयतेर्लेटि अडागमः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । यद्वा । दुहेर्लिङि ऋत्विज्ञ रन् । (पा. ३-४-१०५ [as read]) इति व्यत्ययेन रनादेशाभावे रूपमेतत् । छान्दसोऽन्तलोपः ॥ [as read; part of the grammar tail characterized only] मिमीतम् । माङ् माने शब्दे च । जौहोत्यादिकः । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदम् । भृञामित्यभ्यासस्येत्वम् । चवायोगे प्रथमेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥

he aśvinau yuvāku yuvāṃ kāmayamānāḥ stutibhiryāvayitāraḥ saṃyojayitāro vā stotāro mitradhitaye mitrāṇāṃ bandhujanānāṃ dhāraṇārthaṃ duhīyan | yuṣmatsakāśāddhanāni duhanti prāpnuvanti | ato no 'smānapi vājavatyai vājayuktāya ca rāyai dhanāya mimītam | kurutam | tathā dhenumatyai dhenubhiryuktāyeṣe 'nnāya ca no 'smabhyaṃ mimītam | kurutam | asmabhyaṃ stotṛbhyo balayuktaṃ dhanaṃ goyuktamannaṃ ca prayacchatamityarthaḥ ‖ duhīyan | duha prapūraṇe | duherdohaḥ | igupadhātkit | (u. 4-116 [as read]) iti bhāva ipratyayaḥ | duhimātmana icchati duhīyati | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | duhīyaterleṭi aḍāgamaḥ | itaśca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | yadvā | duherliṅi ṛtvijña ran | (pā. 3-4-105 [as read]) iti vyatyayena ranādeśābhāve rūpametat | chāndaso 'ntalopaḥ ‖ [as read; part of the grammar tail characterized only] mimītam | māṅ māne śabde ca | jauhotyādikaḥ | vyatyayena parasmaipadam | bhṛñāmityabhyāsasyetvam | cavāyoge prathameti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ ‖

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Aśvins, yuvāku — desirous of you, the praisers — who make [you] come by praises [or who unite]: for mitradhitaye — for the support of friends and kinsmen — they duhīyan — milk wealth from you, they obtain. Therefore, for us too, mimītam — make [for] vājavatyai rāye — wealth endowed with strength; and dhenumatyai iṣe — food endowed with cows — grant to us, the praisers — [that is:] give wealth endowed with strength and food together with cows."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.9) (Kannada, rendered)

He aśvinau — O Aśvins; yuvāku — those who desire you (the praisers); mitradhitaye — for the support of [their] friends; duhīyan — [from you] obtain wealth and the like; ataḥ — therefore; naḥ — us; vājavatyai — [endowed with] strength; rāye ca — and for wealth; mimītam — make (in a worthy manner); tathā — likewise; dhenumatyai — endowed with cows; iṣe ca — and for food; naḥ — to us; mimītam — do favour.

original p. 527

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.9) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Aśvins! Those who praise you obtain (from you) wealth and the like for the support of their friends; (therefore) favour us also with strength, wealth, cows and food (such as can be) enjoyed."

English Translation (as printed)

"Those who adore you obtain (wealth) for the support of their friends; direct us to opulence, bestowing food; direct us to food, associatted [sic] with cows."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 9)

Yuvākuḥ — yuvāṃ kāmayamānāḥ stutibhir yāvayitāro vā stotāraḥ: "'we call the Aśvins, desiring them, [praising] to protect [us]; or we praise [them]; or those who desire them, who wish to please them by praises' — such is the meaning that Sāyaṇa's exposition conveys: the ones who desire; who wish to win favour; or who praise."

original p. 528

Special Topics of Ṛk 9, concluded "… yu miśraṇe miśraṇīyaṃ payaḥ pānārham ity arthaḥ | yuṣmatkāmaṃ vāṃ yuvākuḥ | yuvayor yogyam ity arthaḥ [Sāyaṇa as quoted: the root yu in the sense of miśraṇa; 'milk fit for drinking' is the meaning; or 'one who desires you (the two)', 'fit for you (the two)']. Skandasvāmin: 'From the root yu, which has the sense of mixing, the word yuvāku is derived — (to drink) milk fit for drinking, or water; or one who looks to the Aśvins for protection, i.e. one who is fit for protection by the Aśvins' — he also explains this meaning."

Mitradhitaye — mitrāṇāṃ bandhujanānāṃ dhāraṇārtham: "'for the support of friends and kinsmen' — Sāyaṇa: for protecting affectionate friends and relatives. Skandasvāmin:

धेट् पाने इत्यस्य दधातेर्वा दानार्थस्य इदं रूपम् । मित्राणां पानार्थं मित्रेभ्यो वा दानार्थम् ।

dheṭ pāne ityasya dadhātervā dānārthasya idaṃ rūpam | mitrāṇāṃ pānārthaṃ mitrebhyo vā dānārtham |

— 'The word dhiti is formed either from the root dheṭ (dhe pāne), which has the sense of drinking, or from the root dadha [dudhāñ], which has the sense of giving: [it means] for the drinking of friends, or for the giving to friends.' He explains the meaning: 'for the drinking of the friends, and for the giving to friends'."

"By praising the Aśvins, and by getting wealth, food and favour for protecting [their] kinsmen and friends, those praisers prosper; therefore the prayer is described that the Aśvins should favour us with food, wealth, strength and the cow-form wealth."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Duhīyan — root muha prasrāvaṇe [as printed; duha prapūraṇe]; duher dohaḥ, igupadhāt kit (Uṇ. sū. 4-116 as read), the suffix i in the abstract sense; since the suffix is kit, [as if] guṇa of the light penultimate does not occur; when "duhim ātmana icchati" is intended, supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 as read), the suffix kyac after duhi; by vyatyaya lengthening of the former [vowel]; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ (Pā. 3-1-32 as read), the dhātu name for duhīya; to it leṭ, third person plural, the suffix jhi; jho 'ntaḥ (Pā. 7-1-3 as read), ant substituted for jh; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 3-4-97 as read), elision of the i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), the augment aṭ; ato guṇe (Pā. 6-1-97 as read), pararūpa. Or: to the root muha [duha], liṅ, third person plural, ṛtvijñuraṃ [jhasya ran] (Pā. 3-4-105 as read), the ran substitution does not occur by vyatyaya; then, by Vedic usage, the y for the r and elision of the final; or, since ran [jhasya ran] is [taken], [by] vyatyaya, yaṇ for the r; the …

original p. 529

"… the variety of formations, because of their not being determined, the avagraha was not made at the time of the Pada-text; because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, no nighāta; by the suffix's accent the final acute. Yuvākuḥ — "yuvāṃ kāmayante iti yuvākavaḥ", root kamu kāntau; mitadrvādibhya upasaṅkhyānam (Pā. 3-2-180 vārttika as read), the suffix ḍu; since it is ḍit, elision of the ṭi of the root; though a case ending follows, by vyatyaya, yuva for yuṣmad up to ma; ā for the a; or: root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ, the auṇādika suffix kāku; uvaṅ substituted; with jas following, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 as read), luk for it. Rāye — the word rai; with the dative singular following, ā for it (rāyo halyam — āy); ūḍidaṃpadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ (Pā. 6-1-171 as read), the acute on the case ending. Mimītam — root māṅ māne śabde ca; juhotyādi; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 as read), the parasmaipada; loṭ, second person dual, since laṅ … tam is substituted; ślu vikaraṇa; ślau (Pā. 6-1-10 as read), doubling of the root; bhṛñām it (Pā. 7-4-76 as read), i for the reduplicative syllable; īhalyaghoḥ (Pā. 6-4-113 as read), ī for the root's ā; cavāyoge prathamā (Pā. 8-1-59 as read), prohibition of nighāta, so by the suffix's accent the final acute. Iṣe — sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 as read), the acute on the case ending. ‖ 9 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.10)

अश्विनोरसनं रथमनश्वं वाजिनीवतोः । तेनाहं भूरि चाकन ॥ १० ॥

aśvinorasanaṃ rathamanaśvaṃ vājinīvatoḥ | tenāhaṃ bhūri cākana ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.10)

अश्विनोः । असनम् । रथम् । अनश्वम् । वाजिनीऽवतोः । तेन । अहम् । भूरि । चाकन ॥ १० ॥

aśvinoḥ | asanam | ratham | anaśvam | vājinī 'vatoḥ | tena | aham | bhūri | cākana ‖ 10 ‖

original p. 530

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.10)

वाजिनीवतोः । वाजोऽन्नं बलं वा । तद्वत्योः क्रियावतोरश्विनोरनश्वमश्वरहितमप्यश्वराहित्येऽपि सामर्थ्यातिशयेन गच्छन्तं रथमसनं । अहं स्तोता समभजम् । तेन च रथेन भूरि प्रभूतं श्रेयश्चाकन । कामये । असनं । वन षण संभक्तौ । लङ् । चाकन । कन दीप्तिकान्तिगतिषु । छान्दसो लिट् । तलुत्तमो वा । पा. ३-४-८१ [as read] इति तस्य विकल्पान्नैद्भावः । तुजादित्वाद्भ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् ॥ [as read]

vājinīvatoḥ | vājo 'nnaṃ balaṃ vā | tadvatyoḥ kriyāvatoraśvinoranaśvamaśvarahitamapyaśvarāhitye 'pi sāmarthyātiśayena gacchantaṃ rathamasanaṃ | ahaṃ stotā samabhajam | tena ca rathena bhūri prabhūtaṃ śreyaścākana | kāmaye | asanaṃ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | laṅ | cākana | kana dīptikāntigatiṣu | chāndaso liṭ | taluttamo vā | pā. 3-4-81 [as read] iti tasya vikalpānnaidbhāvaḥ | tujāditvādbhyāsasya dīrghatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "Vājinīvatoḥ — vāja is food or strength; of the two Aśvins, who possess this (vājinīvatoḥ, those who possess strength and food): their chariot, anaśvam — though it has no horses — goes, by excess of power, in spite of the absence of horses: that chariot (asanam) I, the praiser, have shared [in]; and by that chariot I long for (cākana) much good (bhūri śreyaḥ)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.10) (Kannada, rendered)

Vājinīvatoḥ — of those who have deeds that produce strength (food); aśvinoḥ — of the Aśvins; anaśvam — without horses (capable of going); ratham — the chariot; aham — I; asanam — praised; tena — by that chariot; bhūri — much (good); cākana — I desire, I pray.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.10) (Kannada, rendered)

"The chariot of the Aśvins, whose deeds produce strength (food), is able to go though it has no horses. I have praised such a chariot, and by it I desire to obtain much good."

English Translation (as printed)

"I have obtained, without horses, the car of the food-bestowing Aswins, and expect (to gain) by it much (wealth)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 10)

Vājinīvatoḥ — vājo 'nnaṃ balaṃ vā tadvatoḥ: "The word vāja conveys the meaning 'food' or 'strength'. Because the Aśvins are the ones who favour these [two] (those for whom the word is the object), [the sense is:] vājinīvantau means 'those who possess food and strength' — so Sāyaṇa explains. Skandasvāmin:

वाजो बलं तद्वती सेना वाजिनी । अन्नं वा हविर्लक्षणं वाजम् । तद्वती । सत्रादीनां [?] यागसंकेताद्वाजिनी । तद्वतोः । बलवतोरन्नवतोर्वा ॥

vājo balaṃ tadvatī senā vājinī | annaṃ vā havirlakṣaṇaṃ vājam | tadvatī | satrādīnāṃ [?] yāgasaṃketādvājinī | tadvatoḥ | balavatorannavatorvā ‖

— 'The word vāja means strength; an army possessing it is vājinī; or the food in the form of the oblation is vāja. For this, to the sacrifices such as the satra, [and] the āhavanīya [?] etc. — which have much of the food in the form of oblation — [the name] vājinī is also given; therefore the Aśvins are possessors of strength, and of the food which is in the form of oblation' — he explains."

original p. 531

"Yāska states the word vājinīvatī in the list of synonyms for uṣas (Ni. 2-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೨-೧೯']):

उषस्तच्चित्रमा भराऽस्मभ्यं वाजिनीवति । (ऋ. सं. १-४८-१२ [as read])

uṣastaccitramā bharā 'smabhyaṃ vājinīvati | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-48-12 [as read])

पावकानः सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३-१० [as read])

pāvakānaḥ sarasvatī vājebhirvājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-3-10 [as read])

In these [passages] he explains the word vāja as 'food' and the word vājinīvatī as 'one with food'."

"Though the Aśvins' chariot has no horses, it moves with great speed by its own power, and it is capable of giving food and strength; therefore the seer of the mantra praises that chariot and prays for the Aśvins' favour — thus it is described here."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Asanam — root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. 6-1-64 as read), s for the initial ṣ; laṅ, first person singular, am substituted; śap vikaraṇa, pararūpa; the augment aṭ; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Anaśvam — "na vidyate aśvo yasya saḥ anaśvaḥ"; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 as read), the final acute of the latter member; accusative singular. Vājinīvatoḥ — "vājinī balakriyā anayoḥ asti iti vājinīvantau, of them": tad asyāsty asmin (Pā. 5-2-94 as read), the suffix matup; chandasīraḥ (Pā. 8-2-15 as read), v for the m of matup; since it is pit it is anudātta. Cākana — root kana dīptikāntigatiṣu; in the sense of the present, chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6 as read), liṭ; first person singular, parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus… (Pā. 3-4-82 as read), ṇal for mip; on that account doubling of the root; ādihalśeṣa for the reduplicative syllable; tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya (Pā. 6-1-7 as read), lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; kuhoś cuḥ, c; ṇal uttamo vā (Pā. 7-1-91 as read), ṇitva of the suffix; since it is optional, [the suffix is not ṇit], so vṛddhi of the penultimate of the root, by ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116 as read), does not occur; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 10 ‖

अयं समह मा तनूह्यते जनाँ अनु । सोमपेयं सुखो रथः ॥ ११ ॥

ayaṃ samaha mā tanūhyate janā~ anu | somapeyaṃ sukho rathaḥ ‖ 11 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.11)

अयम् । समह । मा । तनु । ऊह्यते । जनान् । अनु । सोमऽपेयम् । सुऽखः । रथः ॥ ११ ॥

ayam | samaha | mā | tanu | ūhyate | janān | anu | soma 'peyam | su 'khaḥ | rathaḥ ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.11)

हे समह धनेन सहित हे रथ अयमयं पुरोवर्ती त्वं मा मां तनु । विस्तारय । पुत्रपौत्रधनादिभिः समृद्धं कुरु । यद्वा । अयमयमानं त्वां प्राप्नुवन्तं मां मिमीते योज्यम् [?] । स च सुखः शोभनावकाशः सुखहेतुर्वा रथो जनाननु स्तोतृजनेषु सोमपेयं सोमपासनं प्रत्यूह्यते । ऊह्यते । अश्विभ्यां नीयते । अश्विभ्यां यद्दीयते तत्स्ववं रथ इव पदादिति रथं संबोध्य प्रार्थना ॥ अयम् । इदोऽयन्पुंसि । (पा. ७-२-१११ [as read]) । यद्वा । अय पय गतौ । पचाद्यच् । समह । मह इति धननाम । मघेन सह वर्तते इति समघः । छान्दसो वर्णविकारः । यद्वा । मह पूजायाम् । महयति पूजयतीति महः धनं । पचाद्यच् । ऊह्यते । वह प्रापणे । कर्मणि लेट्यडागमः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । तस्य छान्दसो दीर्घः । आदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे यक इव स्वरः शिष्यते । सोमपेयम् । पा पाने । अचो यदिति भावे यत् । ईद्यतीति ईकारादेशः । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ [as read]

he samaha dhanena sahita he ratha ayamayaṃ purovartī tvaṃ mā māṃ tanu | vistāraya | putrapautradhanādibhiḥ samṛddhaṃ kuru | yadvā | ayamayamānaṃ tvāṃ prāpnuvantaṃ māṃ mimīte yojyam [?] | sa ca sukhaḥ śobhanāvakāśaḥ sukhaheturvā ratho janānanu stotṛjaneṣu somapeyaṃ somapāsanaṃ pratyūhyate | ūhyate | aśvibhyāṃ nīyate | aśvibhyāṃ yaddīyate tatsvavaṃ ratha iva padāditi rathaṃ saṃbodhya prārthanā ‖ ayam | ido 'yanpuṃsi | (pā. 7-2-111 [as read]) | yadvā | aya paya gatau | pacādyac | samaha | maha iti dhananāma | maghena saha vartate iti samaghaḥ | chāndaso varṇavikāraḥ | yadvā | maha pūjāyām | mahayati pūjayatīti mahaḥ dhanaṃ | pacādyac | ūhyate | vaha prāpaṇe | karmaṇi leṭyaḍāgamaḥ | yajāditvātsaṃprasāraṇaṃ | tasya chāndaso dīrghaḥ | ādupadeśāllasārvadhātukānudāttatve yaka iva svaraḥ śiṣyate | somapeyam | pā pāne | aco yaditi bhāve yat | īdyatīti īkārādeśaḥ | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O samaha — O [chariot] associated with wealth, O chariot, ayam — this, standing before [me], you tanu — spread (make wide) mā — me: make me prosperous with sons, grandsons, wealth and the like. Or: you measure out (join) me who am approaching you. And that sukhaḥ — comfortable (having a fine space, a cause of comfort) chariot, janān anu — towards the praisers, somapeyam — for the drinking of soma — is borne (ūhyate) — carried by the Aśvins. What is given by the Aśvins [is] their own. Addressing the chariot, he prays."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.11) (Kannada, rendered)

(He) samaha — O chariot endowed with wealth; āyam — [you] who come towards me (standing before me); mā — me; tanu — make wide (make prosperous with sons and the like); sukhaḥ — comfort-giving; rathaḥ — the chariot; janān anu — towards the praisers; somapeyam — for the drinking of soma; ūhyate — is carried (by the Aśvins).

original p. 533

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.11) (Kannada, rendered)

"O chariot, endowed with wealth! Make me, who have come towards you, prosperous with sons, wealth and the like; that chariot, bringing comfort, is carried (by the Aśvins) near the praisers for the sake of drinking the soma. (Therefore everything the Aśvins have given is given by the chariot — such is the notion; hence the prayer is addressed to the chariot.)"

English Translation (as printed)

"This (is he who has obtained you), wealth-bearing (car): augment (my prosperity); may the delightful car bear the Soma beverage of men (to the Aswins)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 11)

"The seer of the mantra, praising the chariot itself — which, as it comes to the sacrifices of the Aśvins for the drinking of soma, has an abundance of their presence and so is powerful — prays to it for the attainment of his wishes; so it is described here."

Samaha — mahayati pūjayatīti mahaḥ dhanam | maghaṃ iti dhananāma maghena saha vartate iti samahaḥ chāndaso varṇavikāraḥ: "'one who honours (mahayati, 'worships') is mahaḥ: wealth'. The word magha is stated among the twenty-eight [?] names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 [as read]); so it means wealth. The words magha and maha — by Vedic usage the sense is one, but the letter h has come in place of the letter gh. And since the word maha derived from the root maha of the sense 'worship' has the sense 'that which is to be worshipped', it means 'wealth'. By this derivation Sāyaṇa gives the word samaha the meaning 'with wealth'. Skandasvāmin:

हे समह — महः उत्सवः पूजा वा सहितो महेन समहः निर्मोत्सवयुक्तः पूज्यो वा । व्यत्ययेन चात्र एकवचनम् । समहौ पूज्यौ चेत्यर्थः ॥

he samaha — mahaḥ utsavaḥ pūjā vā sahito mahena samahaḥ nirmotsavayuktaḥ pūjyo vā | vyatyayena cātra ekavacanam | samahau pūjyau cetyarthaḥ ‖

— 'the word maha is [a word] of festival or of worship; one who is always manifest in a festival or worship [is samaha]. Since this word is for the Aśvins in particular, it should be dual; but, because it is used in the Veda, the singular has come in place of it; so he explains the meaning of addressing the Aśvins by samaha, instead of samahau."

original p. 534

Special Topics of Ṛk 11, concluded Ūhyate — uhyate aśvibhyāṃ nīyate: "'It is carried by the Aśvins.' The meaning is: since people who praise the Aśvins call them to the sacrifices for the drinking of soma, [the Aśvins] come on their chariot; or, in order to restrain enemies and to favour the praisers, the chariot is borne by the Aśvins."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Ayam — the word idam; with su following, ido 'y puṃsi (Pā. 7-2-111 as read), iy for id; halṅyābbhyo…, elision of su. Or: root aya paya gatau; since it is read in the pacādi group, nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (Pā. 3-1-134 as read), the suffix ac; the final acute. Samaha — magha is a name for wealth; "maghena saha vartate iti samaghaḥ"; by Vedic usage a change of letter, h for the gh, occurs. Or: root maha pūjāyām; "mahayati pūjayati iti mahaḥ" — wealth (a cause of worship); as before, by being read in the pacādi group, the suffix ac; "mahena saha vartate iti samahaḥ"; in the vocative, since it gets the āmantrita name, āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19 as read), the nighāta accent. Tanu — root tanu vistāre; loṭ, second person singular; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Ūhyate — root vaha prāpaṇe; in the passive, leṭ, third person singular, the suffix ta; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 as read), e; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), the augment aṭ; sārvadhātuke yak (Pā. 3-1-67 as read), yak; since vaha is in the yajādi group, since the suffix yak is not kit, [saṃprasāraṇa] by vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti (Pā. 6-1-15 as read) of the root — saṃprasāraṇa; saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa; by Vedic usage lengthening for it; since the lasārvadhātuka stands after upadeśa, tāsyanudāttetṅidadupadeśāl (Pā. 6-1-186 as read) makes it anudātta, so the yak accent remains. Somapeyam — root pā pāne; aco yat (Pā. 3-1-97 as read), the suffix yat; īdyati (Pā. 6-4-65 as read), ī for the root's ā when yat follows; guṇa; the form peya; yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 as read), the initial acute; in the compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Sukhaḥ — "śobhanaṃ khaṃ (avakāśaḥ) yasya saḥ sukhaḥ"; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 as read), the final acute of the latter member. ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 535

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.12)

अध स्वप्नस्य निर्विदेऽभुञ्जतश्च रेवतः । उभा ता बस्रि नश्यतः ॥ १२ ॥

adha svapnasya nirvide 'bhuñjataśca revataḥ | ubhā tā basri naśyataḥ ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 120.12)

अध । स्वप्नस्य । निः । विदे । अभुञ्जतः । च । रेवतः । उभा । ता । बस्रि । नश्यतः ॥ १२ ॥

adha | svapnasya | niḥ | vide | abhuñjataḥ | ca | revataḥ | ubhā | tā | basri | naśyataḥ ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 120.12)

अधेदानीं प्रभातसमये स्वप्नस्य स्वप्नं प्रति निर्विदे । निर्विण्णोऽस्मि । तथा भुञ्जतः परानरक्षतो धनवतश्च पुरुषस्य यं नभूतं पुरुषं प्रत्यपि निर्विण्णोऽस्मि । यतस्वप्नदृष्टम् बस्रि क्षिप्रं नश्यतः नाशं प्राप्नुतः । स्वप्नदृष्टः पदार्थः प्रातर्नोपलभ्यते कदर्येण धनमभुक्तमन्वत्वं सत् क्षिप्रमेव नश्यति । तदुभयविषयो निर्वेदो मां बाधत इत्यर्थः । अत्र स्वप्नमात्रस्यासत्त्वप्रतिपादनेन दुःस्वप्नस्य सद्भावः प्रतिपादितः । अत एषा दुःस्वप्ननाशनीति युज्यते ॥ स्वप्नस्य । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी । विदे । विद्लृ लाभे । आगमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वान्नुमभावः । रेवतः । रयेश्छान्दस्मतुप् । रयेर्मतौ बहुलमिति संप्रसारणम् । छन्दसीर इति मतुपो वत्वम् । देशचाच्छे मतुपस उदात्तत्वमिति तस्योदात्तत्वम् । उभा ता उभयत्र सुपां सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः ॥ [as read]

adhedānīṃ prabhātasamaye svapnasya svapnaṃ prati nirvide | nirviṇṇo 'smi | tathā bhuñjataḥ parānarakṣato dhanavataśca puruṣasya yaṃ nabhūtaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyapi nirviṇṇo 'smi | yatasvapnadṛṣṭam basri kṣipraṃ naśyataḥ nāśaṃ prāpnutaḥ | svapnadṛṣṭaḥ padārthaḥ prātarnopalabhyate kadaryeṇa dhanamabhuktamanvatvaṃ sat kṣiprameva naśyati | tadubhayaviṣayo nirvedo māṃ bādhata ityarthaḥ | atra svapnamātrasyāsattvapratipādanena duḥsvapnasya sadbhāvaḥ pratipāditaḥ | ata eṣā duḥsvapnanāśanīti yujyate ‖ svapnasya | kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyamiti karmaṇaḥ saṃpradānatvāccaturthyarthe ṣaṣṭhī | vide | vidlṛ lābhe | āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvānnumabhāvaḥ | revataḥ | rayeśchāndasmatup | rayermatau bahulamiti saṃprasāraṇam | chandasīra iti matupo vatvam | deśacācche matupasa udāttatvamiti tasyodāttatvam | ubhā tā ubhayatra supāṃ supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "Adha — now, at the time of dawn, svapnasya nirvide — I am weary of [that which belongs to] a dream. And likewise [I am weary] of a man who abhuñjataḥ — does not enjoy, who does not protect others, though rich: I am weary even of him. Both of these — what is seen in a dream (svapnadṛṣṭaḥ) and the wealth that is not enjoyed — basri (quickly) naśyataḥ — perish. A thing seen in a dream is not found in the morning; and wealth, [held by the] miser, not used, though real, perishes quickly. A weariness regarding both of these troubles me." (Bhāṣya adds: since the unreality of dreams is thereby declared, the existence of bad dreams is [also] set forth; therefore this Ṛk is rightly called duḥsvapnanāśanī.)

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 120.12) (Kannada, rendered)

Adha — now (at the time of dawn); svapnasya — with regard to dreams; nirvide — I have become weary; — likewise; abhuñjataḥ — [with regard to him who] does no good to others; revataḥ ca — and with regard to a rich man; nirvide — I have become weary; tā ubhā — both of these (dream, and the wealth of a miser); basri — quickly; naśyataḥ — perish.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 120.12) (Kannada, rendered)

"Now I am weary both of the dream and of the wealth of the miser — both of which perish quickly."

original p. 536

English Translation (as printed)

"Now am I disdainful of sleep, and of the rich man who benefits not others, for both (the morinng [sic] sleep and the selfish rich man) quickly perish."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 12)

"Now (at dawn) I am weary of what concerns dreams; and likewise I am weary of the rich man who does no good to others. The principal idea is: may the evil dream and the selfish rich man, both, quickly come to destruction."

"The state of being weary (nirvedabhāva) of the seer of the mantra is described here. A mean person earns wealth, but neither enjoys comfort himself nor protects others. Like him, a bad dream too gives pain only when seen; wealth earned by a mean man, [kept] without enjoyment and giving, is lost; a bad dream appears only at the time [of sleeping] and then is not seen in that very moment. When the word svapna itself denotes something unreal, the word duḥsvapna is said [here] to be of the same unreal sense, with the example of the wealth [of the miser]. And Sāyaṇa explains that by the mere recitation of this Ṛk a bad dream is destroyed." Skandasvāmin:

उत्तमा स्वप्ननाशिनी । पञ्चानामाश्विनानां सूक्तानामुत्तमा यो चुक् [?] विषा स्वप्ननाशनार्थम् । स्वप्नशब्देनात्र यः कश्चित् दुःस्वप्नः इष्यते स उच्यते न स्वप्नमात्रम् । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । दुःस्वप्नं निर्विदे । विद सत्तायामित्यस्य रूपं निर्वेदयामि निःस्वत्तां करोमि नाशयामीत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

uttamā svapnanāśinī | pañcānāmāśvinānāṃ sūktānāmuttamā yo cuk [?] viṣā svapnanāśanārtham | svapnaśabdenātra yaḥ kaścit duḥsvapnaḥ iṣyate sa ucyate na svapnamātram | dvitīyārthe ṣaṣṭhī | duḥsvapnaṃ nirvide | vida sattāyāmityasya rūpaṃ nirvedayāmi niḥsvattāṃ karomi nāśayāmītyarthaḥ ‖ [as read; small type, doubtful [?]]

"In these five sūktas that speak of the glory (mahimā) of the Aśvins, this mantra is famous as duḥsvapnanāśinī, since it has the power to destroy bad dreams. It does not destroy all dreams that occur to the sleeper; it destroys only bad dreams. A bad dream has no existence, [being] like things having existence (stability); this is stated here with the example of [the wealth of the miser], as well as [in] the sentence containing a comparison (dṛṣṭāntavākya) used in this very mantra."

No grammar page is printed for Ṛk 12 here; the page ends with an ornament, and the next page begins Sūkta 121. No Sanskrit colophon is printed at the end of Sūkta 120 — only the ornament at the foot of p. 536.

Sūkta 121 — "kad itthā nṝḥ pātram"

original p. 537

Heading (Kannada): "nūra ippattombhanaya sūktavu" — "the hundred-and-twenty-first Sūkta." The page also carries, above it, the start of the eighteenth anuvāka.

Anukramaṇī (Sanskrit, as printed):

अष्टादशेऽनुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्र कदित्थेति पञ्चदशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रम्यते । कदित्था पञ्चोना वैश्वदेवं वेति । अनुवर्तमानः कक्षीवानृषिः । अनादेशपरिभाषया त्रिष्टुप् । विश्वे देवा इन्द्रो वा देवता ॥ विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

aṣṭādaśe 'nuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatra kadittheti pañcadaśarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktam | atrānukramyate | kaditthā pañconā vaiśvadevaṃ veti | anuvartamānaḥ kakṣīvānṛṣiḥ | anādeśaparibhāṣayā triṣṭup | viśve devā indro vā devatā ‖ viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖

Sense: "In the eighteenth anuvāka there are six sūktas. Of these, kad itthā — of fifteen Ṛks — is the first. The Anukramaṇī says: 'kad itthā pañconā vaiśvadevaṃ veti'. The ṛṣi, by continuation, is Kakṣīvān. By the rule of no assignment, the metre is Triṣṭubh. The deities are the Viśvedevas, or Indra. The application (viniyoga) is by liṅga."

Anuvāda (Kannada): "With the sūkta kad itthā the eighteenth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala begins. This anuvāka has six sūktas (121–126 [as read]). Of them kad itthā is the first; it has fifteen Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says 'kadityā pañconā vaiśvadevaṃ vā'. As for the preceding sūktas, the ṛṣi of this sūkta too is Kakṣīvān. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The deities are the Viśvedevas, or Indra. The application is by liṅga."

सूक्त—१२१ (Sūkta 121) ॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—१८ ॥ सूक्त—१२१ ॥ ॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय ८ ॥ वर्ग—small numerals; read "24, 25, 26" — as printed [?] ॥ Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 15 printed "१५". Ṛṣi: Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. Devatā: the Viśvedevas or Indra. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

कदित्था नॄः पात्रं देवयतां श्रवद्गिरो अङ्गिरसां तुरण्यन् । प्र यदानड्विश आ हर्म्यस्योरु क्रंसते अध्वरे यजत्रः ॥ १ ॥

kaditthā nṝḥ pātraṃ devayatāṃ śravadgiro aṅgirasāṃ turaṇyan | pra yadānaḍviśa ā harmyasyoru kraṃsate adhvare yajatraḥ ‖ 1 ‖

original p. 538

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.1)

कत् । इत्था । नॄन् । पात्रम् । देवऽयताम् । श्रवत् । गिरः । अङ्गिरसाम् । तुरण्यन् । प्र । यत् । आनट् । विशः । आ । हर्म्यस्य । उरु । क्रंसते । अध्वरे । यजत्रः ॥ १ ॥

kat | itthā | nṝn | pātram | deva 'yatām | śravat | giraḥ | aṅgirasām | turaṇyan | pra | yat | ānaṭ | viśaḥ | ā | harmyasya | uru | kraṃsate | adhvare | yajatraḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.1) small type; read with some doubts

नॄन्पात्रं नृणां स्तुतेर्नेतॄणां पुरुषाणां रक्षणशीलः इन्द्रस्तुरण्यन् गोरूपधनं प्रेरयन् देवयतां देवं द्योतमानं दानादिगुणयुक्तं वेन्द्रमात्मन इच्छतामङ्गिरसां स्मभ्यां [?] अस्माकमित्थमित्थं प्रयुज्यमाना गिरः स्तुतीः कत् कदा कस्मिन्काले श्रवत् । शृणुयात् । यद्यदा स इन्द्रो हर्म्यस्य हर्म्योपलक्षितेन गृहेण युक्तस्य यजमानस्य संबन्धिनो विश ऋत्विजः क्षणानुष्ट्यान [?] अभिमुख्येन प्रानट् । प्राप्नोति तदानीमध्वरेऽस्मदीये यज्ञे यजत्रो यष्टव्यः सन्नुरु बहुलं क्रंसते । क्रमते । स्वयमेवोत्सहत इत्यर्थः ॥ कत् । कदा । अन्त्यलोपश्छान्दसः । नॄन् । पात्रम् । नृन्से । पा. ८-३-१० इति संहितायां नकारस्य रुत्वम् । … पात्रम् । पा रक्षणे । ताच्छीलिकस्त्रन् । … देवयताम् । … श्रवत् । श्रु श्रवणे । लेट्यडागमः । … तुरण्यन् । तुरण त्वरायाम् । कण्ड्वादिः । … आनट् । अशू व्याप्तौ । … हर्म्यस्य । हर्म्यशब्दादर्शआदित्वादच् । क्रंसते । क्रमु पादविक्षेपे । … यजत्रः । अमिनक्षियजिवधि [?] … [the grammar tail is in small type; characterized, not transcribed]

nṝnpātraṃ nṛṇāṃ stuternetṝṇāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ rakṣaṇaśīlaḥ indrasturaṇyan gorūpadhanaṃ prerayan devayatāṃ devaṃ dyotamānaṃ dānādiguṇayuktaṃ vendramātmana icchatāmaṅgirasāṃ smabhyāṃ [?] asmākamitthamitthaṃ prayujyamānā giraḥ stutīḥ kat kadā kasminkāle śravat | śṛṇuyāt | yadyadā sa indro harmyasya harmyopalakṣitena gṛheṇa yuktasya yajamānasya saṃbandhino viśa ṛtvijaḥ kṣaṇānuṣṭyāna [?] abhimukhyena prānaṭ | prāpnoti tadānīmadhvare 'smadīye yajñe yajatro yaṣṭavyaḥ sannuru bahulaṃ kraṃsate | kramate | svayamevotsahata ityarthaḥ ‖ kat | kadā | antyalopaśchāndasaḥ | nṝn | pātram | nṛnse | pā. 8-3-10 iti saṃhitāyāṃ nakārasya rutvam | … pātram | pā rakṣaṇe | tācchīlikastran | … devayatām | … śravat | śru śravaṇe | leṭyaḍāgamaḥ | … turaṇyan | turaṇa tvarāyām | kaṇḍvādiḥ | … ānaṭ | aśū vyāptau | … harmyasya | harmyaśabdādarśaāditvādac | kraṃsate | kramu pādavikṣepe | … yajatraḥ | aminakṣiyajivadhi [?] … [the grammar tail is in small type; characterized, not transcribed]

Sense (mine): "Nṝn pātram — Indra, the guardian of men, the leaders [who praise]; turaṇyan — urging on wealth in the form of cows; for us Aṅgirases, who desire (devayatām) a shining Indra who has the qualities of generosity, kat — when — will he listen (śravat) to our praise-words thus (itthā) uttered? Yat — when that Indra reaches (ānaṭ) face to face the viśaḥ — the priests belonging to the sacrificer who owns a house (harmya) — then, at our adhvara, our sacrifice, being the one to be worshipped (yajatraḥ), he kraṃsate — strides (comes), [it is meant] he exerts himself spontaneously."

original p. 539

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.1) (Kannada, rendered)

Nṝn — of men (of men's praises); pātram — the protector; turaṇyan — the impeller of cows and the like (Indra); devayatām — desirous of a shining Indra, or of a god endowed with generosity and the like; aṅgirasām — of us, the Aṅgirases; itthā — thus (uttered); giraḥ — praise-words; kat — when; śravat — will he hear? yat — when (Indra); harmyasya — of the sacrificer who has a house; viśaḥ — [of] the priests (men); ā pra ānaṭ — [being] face to face, comes; adhvare — in (our) sacrifice; yajatraḥ — worthy of worship; uru — greatly; kraṃsate — steps (becomes eager).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.1) (Kannada, rendered)

"When Indra, worthy of worship, comes in the sacrifice face to face with the priests, the men [belonging] to the householder-sacrificer, he becomes greatly eager; therefore, when will Indra, protector of men and impeller of the cattle-wealth, hear these praise-words (to be uttered presently) of us Aṅgirases, who desire him?"

English Translation (as printed)

"When will Indra, the protector of men and granter of riches, listen to the praises thus (recited) of the Angirasas, who are devoted to the gods? When he perceives the ministers of the master of the mansion, and is to be the object of worship in the sacrifice, he greatly exults."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 1)

Kat — kadā: "'when' is the meaning."

Pātram — "from the root pā, which has the sense of protection, the word pātra conveys 'one who protects'."

Devayatām — devaṃ dyotamānaṃ dānādiguṇayuktaṃ vā indram ātmana icchatām: "'those who desire a shining Indra, or an Indra endowed with the quality of giving' — i.e. those who look to him for protection."

"Sāyaṇa: when the cows of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis were carried off, they called Indra for protection, and he, hearing their praise, restrained the rākṣasas who had carried off the cows …" continues on p. 540

original p. 540

Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued "… he suggests, by the words nṝn pātraṃ devayatām aṅgirasāṃ turaṇyan, that [Indra] is the impeller of the cow-wealth of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis, who look to the deity for protection. Skandasvāmin: as in the Ṛk

कद्ध नूनं कधप्रियः पिता पुत्रं न हस्तयोः । (ऋ. सं. १-३८-१ [as read])

kaddha nūnaṃ kadhapriyaḥ pitā putraṃ na hastayoḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-38-1 [as read])

the word kat conveys 'when'. Nṝn = manuṣyāṇām asmākaṃ manuṣyāṇām — 'to us, the men'; pātram — 'the vessel called graha or camasa, by which the oblation is offered in the sacrifice'; devayatām — of the Aṅgirases who desire the god; [he adds that the word pitṛ in a similar Ṛk is used of the sacrificers who are 'sons' of the Aṅgirases]; 'giraḥ śravat — he will hear the praise-words of the sages born in the line of the Aṅgirases, and, quickly, drink the soma-juice' — such is the sense he gives. In their expositions the two commentators differ."

Harmyasya — harater idaṃ rūpam harturaḥ śatrudhanānām indrasya uru kraṃsate bahu karoti: "'[Indra,] the seizer of enemies' wealth [is called to the sacrifice]; the sacrificer calls him in many ways and praises' — or, harmyam iti gṛhanāma ('house'): 'yajñagṛhe yo 'dhvaraḥ tasmin bahu kramate indraḥ' — 'Indra comes many times to the sacrifice in the sacrificial hall' — so Skandasvāmin. Sāyaṇa: uru kraṃsate bahulaṃ kramate svayam evotsahate — 'Indra, worthy of worship, is greatly eager to come to the sacrificial hall'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Kat — the word kadā; by Vedic usage the final ā is elided. Nṝn pātram — nṝn + pātram: nṝn pe (Pā. 8-3-10 as read), ru for the n in the Saṃhitā because p follows; atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā (Pā. 8-3-2 as read), the preceding ṛ … becomes nasal; kupvoḥ… , visarga.

original p. 541

Pātram — root pā rakṣaṇe; tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu (Pā. 3-2-129 as read), the suffix tṛn in the sense of habit; the word pātṛ; by vyatyaya, tra substituted when su follows; since by the maxim saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ the guṇa is not obtained, yaṇ; by the suffix's nit, the initial acute. Devayatām — "devam ātmana icchanti": supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 as read), kyac after deva; the form devayati; na cchandasy aputrasya (Pā. 7-4-35 as read), the lengthening etc. do not occur; after the kyajanta deva-ya, in the sense of laṭ, śatṛ; the word devayat; genitive plural, since śatṛ is numrahita, śaturanumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173 as read), the acute on the case ending. Śravat — root śru śravaṇe; leṭ, third person singular, tip; itaś ca lopaḥ (Pā. 3-4-97 as read), elision of i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), aṭ; bahulaṃ chandasi, luk for the vikaraṇa; guṇa of the u, av; at the beginning of a pāda no nighāta; since tip is pit, anudātta, so the root's accent remains. Turaṇyan — root turaṇa tvarāyām; kaṇḍvādi; kaṇḍvādibhyo yak (Pā. 3-1-27 as read), yak in its own sense; in the sense of laṭ, śatṛ; first singular, [yak accent remains]. Ānaṭ — root aśū vyāptau; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 as read), the parasmaipada; laṅ, third person singular, tip; itaś ca, elision of i; by vyatyaya śnu as vikaraṇa [instead of śap]; …; halṅyābbhyo…, elision of tip; vraśca… (Pā. 8-2-36 as read), ṣatva of the ś; jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte (Pā. 8-2-39 as read), ḍ for the ṣ; vāvasāne (Pā. 8-4-56 as read), ṭ; āḍ ajādīnām (Pā. 6-4-72 as read), the augment āṭ; the form ānaṭ; since yat is connected, no nighāta; the augment being udātta, the initial acute. Harmyasya — "harmyam asya asti" — harmya ... arśa ādibhyo 'c (Pā. 5-2-127 as read), the suffix ac in the sense of matup; yasyeti ca, elision of the preceding a …

original p. 542

Grammar of Ṛk 1, concluded (noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read): Kraṃsate — root kramu pādavikṣepe; vṛttisargatāyaneṣu kramaḥ (Pā. 1-3-38 as read), here, since the sense is exertion, the middle voice; leṭ, third person singular; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), aṭ; sib bahulaṃ leṭi (Pā. 3-1-34 as read), sip; naśchā… anusvāra for the m; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. Yajatraḥ — root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; aminakṣiyajidhi… (Uṇ. sū. 3-?? as read), the suffix atra; since it is nit, the initial acute. ‖ 1 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.2)

स्तम्भीद्ध द्यां स धरुणं प्रुषायदृभुर्वाजाय द्रविणं नरो गोः । अनु स्वजां महिषश्चक्षत व्रां मेनामश्वस्य परि मातरं गोः ॥ २ ॥

stambhīddha dyāṃ sa dharuṇaṃ pruṣāyadṛbhurvājāya draviṇaṃ naro goḥ | anu svajāṃ mahiṣaścakṣata vrāṃ menāmaśvasya pari mātaraṃ goḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.2) Printed Saṃhitā "prṣāyat"/Pada "puṣāyat"; I give the Pada's reading.

स्तम्भीत् । ह । द्याम् । सः । धरुणम् । पुषायत् । ऋभुः । वाजाय । द्रविणम् । नरः । गोः । अनु । स्वऽजाम् । महिषः । चक्षत । व्राम् । मेनाम् । अश्वस्य । परि । मातरम् । गोः ॥ २ ॥

stambhīt | ha | dyām | saḥ | dharuṇam | puṣāyat | ṛbhuḥ | vājāya | draviṇam | naraḥ | goḥ | anu | sva 'jām | mahiṣaḥ | cakṣata | vrām | menām | aśvasya | pari | mātaram | goḥ ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 543

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.2)

स इन्द्रो द्यां द्युलोकं स्तम्भीत् । स्तभ्नाति खलु । तथा गोः पणिभिरपहृतस्य गोसमूहस्य वज्रस्योदकस्य किरणसमूहस्य वा नरो नेता । स इन्द्र ऋभुः सूर्यात्मनोरुविस्तीर्णं भासमानः सन् द्रविणं सर्वैः प्राणिभिरद्रवणीयं धरुणं उदकनामैतत् । सर्वस्य धारकं वृष्ट्युदकं वाजाय अन्नार्थं बलार्थं वा प्रुषायत् । प्रुष्णाति सिञ्चति प्रवर्षतीत्यर्थः । अपि च महिषः महान्नामैतत् । महान्सूर्यरूपीन्द्रः स्वजां स्वसकाशादुत्पन्नां व्रां वृणोति तमसा सर्वमाच्छादयतीति व्रा रात्रिः । यद्वा प्रकाशेन वृणोतीति व्रा उषाः । कामनु चक्षत । चष्टिः पश्यतिकर्मा । अनुपश्यति प्रकाशते । स्वयं प्रौढप्रकाशोऽपि स्वगत्या निष्पादितायां रात्रेरुषसश्च पश्चादुदेतीत्यर्थः । अपि चेदमुपरमाश्चर्यं यदयमश्वस्य मेनां स्त्रीमन्नामैतत् स्त्रियं वडवां गोर्मातरं जननीं परिवृणक्ति [?] विपरीतमकरोत् । कदाचिदिन्द्रो लीलयाश्वायां गामुत्पादयामास । तदेत्र प्रतिपाद्यते मन्त्रान्तरे चेन्द्रवाक्यरूप एतद्वृत्तान्तमवगम्यते । धरुणम् । धारेर्णित् ...उन्प्रत्ययः । प्रुषायत् । प्रुष प्लुष स्नेहनसेचनपूरणेषु । क्र्यादिकः । लेट्यडागमः । छन्दसि शायजपीत्यादिना शप् ... नरः । नृ नये । चक्षत । चक्षिङ् व्यक्तायां वाचि । छान्दसो लङ् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः ॥ [as read]

sa indro dyāṃ dyulokaṃ stambhīt | stabhnāti khalu | tathā goḥ paṇibhirapahṛtasya gosamūhasya vajrasyodakasya kiraṇasamūhasya vā naro netā | sa indra ṛbhuḥ sūryātmanoruvistīrṇaṃ bhāsamānaḥ san draviṇaṃ sarvaiḥ prāṇibhiradravaṇīyaṃ dharuṇaṃ udakanāmaitat | sarvasya dhārakaṃ vṛṣṭyudakaṃ vājāya annārthaṃ balārthaṃ vā pruṣāyat | pruṣṇāti siñcati pravarṣatītyarthaḥ | api ca mahiṣaḥ mahānnāmaitat | mahānsūryarūpīndraḥ svajāṃ svasakāśādutpannāṃ vrāṃ vṛṇoti tamasā sarvamācchādayatīti vrā rātriḥ | yadvā prakāśena vṛṇotīti vrā uṣāḥ | kāmanu cakṣata | caṣṭiḥ paśyatikarmā | anupaśyati prakāśate | svayaṃ prauḍhaprakāśo 'pi svagatyā niṣpāditāyāṃ rātreruṣasaśca paścādudetītyarthaḥ | api cedamuparamāścaryaṃ yadayamaśvasya menāṃ strīmannāmaitat striyaṃ vaḍavāṃ gormātaraṃ jananīṃ parivṛṇakti [?] viparītamakarot | kadācidindro līlayāśvāyāṃ gāmutpādayāmāsa | tadetra pratipādyate mantrāntare cendravākyarūpa etadvṛttāntamavagamyate | dharuṇam | dhārerṇit ...unpratyayaḥ | pruṣāyat | pruṣa pluṣa snehanasecanapūraṇeṣu | kryādikaḥ | leṭyaḍāgamaḥ | chandasi śāyajapītyādinā śap ... naraḥ | nṛ naye | cakṣata | cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci | chāndaso laṅ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "That Indra stambhīt — propped up dyām — the heaven; he indeed props. And he is the leader (naraḥ) of the herd of cows (goḥ) carried off by the Paṇis, [or] of the thunderbolt, of the water, of the mass of rays. That Indra, ṛbhuḥ — shining widely in the form of the Sun — pruṣāyat — drenches, rains down, the dhruṇa [as printed dharuṇa] — the water that supports everything, [the] draviṇam — [wealth] flowing, that is the rain-water — vājāya — for food or strength. And mahiṣaḥ — the great (mahiṣa is a name for 'great') Indra in the form of the Sun — anu cakṣata — follows and sees vrām — Night, who covers everything with darkness; or Dawn, who covers by light — svajām — born from himself. Though himself fully radiant, he rises after Night and Dawn, which are produced by his own motion. And this is a further wonder: he made the mare (aśvasya menām, the female) the mother of the cow — he once made it so in sport; that account is told here and is understood in another mantra in the form of Indra's own words."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.2) (Kannada, rendered)

Saḥ — that Indra; dyām — the heavenly world; stambhīt ha — held fixed; goḥ — of the cows (of water, of rays); naraḥ — the leader (Indra); ṛbhuḥ — shining widely, in the form of the Sun; draviṇam — flowing; dharuṇam — the supporter of all (rain-water); vājāya — for food, or for strength; pruṣāyat — made fat (rained); api ca — and; mahiṣaḥ — the very great Indra (in the Sun's form); svajām — born of himself; vrām — covering (Night, or Dawn); anu cakṣata — follows and shines; aśvasya menām — the female of the horse; goḥ mātaram — as the mother of the cow; pari (cakṣata) — he made (against nature).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.2) (Kannada, rendered)

"Indra holds the sky still; Indra, the leader of the cows (of waters, of rays), shining widely in the form of the Sun, gives to the world, as rain, the flowing, all-supporting water, for food and strength; the great Indra, in the form of the Sun, follows and illumines the Night — or the Dawn — born from himself; and by his own greatness, against nature, he made a mare the mother of a cow."

original p. 544

English Translation (as printed) page head printed "Englih Translation" — sic

"He verily upholds the heaven; he, the brilliant, the leader of the (stolen) herd, pours forth the flowing (water) for the sake of food: the mighty Indra manifests himself after his own daughter, (the dawn); he made the female of horse unnaturally the mother of the cow."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 2)

Goḥ — paṇibhir apahṛtasya gosamūhasya vajrasya udakasya kiraṇasamūhasya vā: "nareḥ [naraḥ] netā indraḥ. Since the word gau is stated among the twenty-one [?] names of the earth (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೧-೩']), [it means] 'the earth'; and in the Nirukta:

येन गौरभिप्रवृत्ता मिमाति मायुं ध्वसनौ [?] । शब्दं करोति मायुमिवादित्यमिति । वागेषा माध्यमिका ध्वंसने मेघे अधिश्रिता ॥

yena gaurabhipravṛttā mimāti māyuṃ dhvasanau [?] | śabdaṃ karoti māyumivādityamiti | vāgeṣā mādhyamikā dhvaṃsane meghe adhiśritā ‖

(Ni. 2-9 [as read]) — hence, [in the Nirukta] it also means 'speech' (vāk, Ni. 1-11 [as read]), among the common names; and since the word dyauḥ is stated as āditya among the synonyms of 'ray' (Ni. 1-?? [as read]), 'ray'; since it is in the list of the names of speech [vāk] (Ni. 1-11 [as read]), 'speech'; and, since it is stated among the names of praise [stotra], 'praise'. Since the word go has many senses, it is explained that Indra brought back the cows stolen from the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis by the asuras, that he uses the thunderbolt properly, that he makes the rain-waters come to the earth, that he holds a mass of rays."

Ṛbhuḥ — sūryātmanā viṣṭīrṇaṃ bhāsamānaḥ: "'shining widely in the form of the Sun'. Yāska: ṛbhavaḥ — uru bhāntīti vā, ṛtena bhāntīti vā, ṛtena bhavantīti vā (Ni. 11-?? [as read]) — 'those who shine widely, or by truth, or [who] come into being by truth'; or, 'those who are exceedingly truthful, of the form of truth':

विष्ट्वी शमी तरणित्वेन वाघतो मर्तासः सन्तो अमृतत्वमानशुः । सौधन्वना ऋभवः सूरचक्षसः संवत्सरे समपृच्यन्त धीतिभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११०-४ [as read])

viṣṭvī śamī taraṇitvena vāghato martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvamānaśuḥ | saudhanvanā ṛbhavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ saṃvatsare samapṛcyanta dhītibhiḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-110-4 [as read])

— quoting this Ṛk he explains the word ṛbhu, and in ādit sūryarmaśmayo ṛbhavaḥ (Ni. 11-?? [as read]) shows that the rays of the Sun, too, are called ṛbhu."

original p. 545

Dharuṇam — sarvasya dhārakaṃ vṛṣṭyudakam: "The word dharuṇa is stated among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-12 [as read]); hence 'water' — Indra gives to the world, as rain, the rain-water that supports everything, for food and for the growth of strength."

Mahiṣaḥ — mahannāmaitat; mahān sūryarūpī indraḥ: "The word mahiṣa is stated among the names of 'great' (Ni. 3-?? [as read])."

Svajāṃ vrāṃ anu cakṣata — svasakāśād utpannāṃ vṛṇoti tamasā sarvam ācchādayatīti vrā rātriḥ | yadvā prakāśena vṛṇotīti vrā uṣāḥ tām anu paścāt paśyati prakāśate: "'Being of the form of the Sun, Indra follows the Night, which covers everything with darkness and is born of his own motion; and shines after her. Or: vrā means 'dawn', which covers (makes everything desirable) by its light. The Sun, being exceedingly bright, rises after the time of dawn, and rises to protect what is born from him: this is the behaviour of the world. Hence Sūryā is said to follow dawn, and the Sun is said to rise after the dawn.' — so Sāyaṇa."

"Skandasvāmin: svajām anu cakṣate — stute iva prajāpateḥ yā jātā sā svajā tāṃ mahān indraḥ anupūrveṇa sarvataḥ paśyati — 'the great Indra, completely filled, knows fully the matter of the woman (Uṣas) who was born of Prajāpati, the Brahmā'' — thus he explains."

original p. 546

Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued Aśvasya menāṃ vaḍavāṃ gomātaraṃ akarot — "'Once Indra, in sport, caused a cow to be born from a mare; that is the matter set forth here, and in another mantra, which is in the form of Indra's own speech, it is told clearly' — thus Sāyaṇa: this wonderful act of the playful Indra, who made a cow be born of a mare, is told here."

Skandasvāmin: "vrāṃ varaṇīyāṃ menāṃ striyaṃ bhāryām aśvasya vyāpteḥ prajāpateḥ mātaraṃ mātṛbhūtāṃ gantṛtvāt indro 'traiva gauruccyate ātmane vivety arthaḥ — 'he understood that his own mother, designated by the word go, was the wife of Prajāpati, the pervading Brahmā' — and he gives another explanation:

अथवा व्रा इति रात्रिनाम । उक्तं हि शाकपूणिना । व्रा इति रात्रिरप्युच्यत इति । स्वजा चासौ स्वयमेव जायमानत्वात् । स्वयं जनयित्रीं महानिन्द्रो जानाति रात्रिं नाम स्त्रियमश्वस्य मातरं । अश्वग्रहणमत्रोपलक्षणं प्राणिमात्रस्य अश्वादेः । सम्यगाहारपरिणामादिकरणेन मातृभूतां गोरुपत्वात् ॥

athavā vrā iti rātrināma | uktaṃ hi śākapūṇinā | vrā iti rātrirapyucyata iti | svajā cāsau svayameva jāyamānatvāt | svayaṃ janayitrīṃ mahānindro jānāti rātriṃ nāma striyamaśvasya mātaraṃ | aśvagrahaṇamatropalakṣaṇaṃ prāṇimātrasya aśvādeḥ | samyagāhārapariṇāmādikaraṇena mātṛbhūtāṃ gorupatvāt ‖

— 'or, vrā is a name for Night; for Śākapūṇi has said so: "vrā is also called night". She is svajā, born of herself. The great Indra knows Night — the woman, the mother of the horse; the word aśva here is a general indication [of all beings, horses and the rest]: by providing right food and its digestion and the like, she is as a mother, in the form of a cow'. The ṛṣi Śākapūṇi says that the word vrā means 'night': so the meaning of vrā is 'night'. [Skandasvāmin takes it] that Night is self-born, that she protects all beings, horses and the rest, by the digestion of food and so on, as a mother, and that he understands the Dawn, who comes at the end of the night, as the mother [of all]."

"Though Indra is holding the sky steady, he restored to the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis the cows carried off by the asuras, having destroyed them; being in the form of the Sun, he makes rain, which gives food and strength for the beings that are in his control; he fixes time, making day and night — two kinds of activity — suitable [for creatures]; in the day, which is luminous, he shines in the form of the Sun; by destroying the darkness of night and by rising after the dawn — all these are his extraordinary protection of the world; and they are works fit for a mother."

original p. 547

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Dharuṇam — root dhṛñ avasthāne; dhārer ṇiluk ca [as read; Uṇ. sū. 3-?? [?]], the suffix unan after the ṇijanta; the n arising when r follows, āṭ kuppvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi (Pā. 8-4-2 as read), ṇatva; by the suffix's accent the u is acute. Pruṣāyat — root pruṣa pluṣa snehanasecanapūraṇeṣu, kryādi; leṭ, third person singular, tip; itaś ca lopaḥ (Pā. 3-4-97 as read), elision of the i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 as read), aṭ; chandasi śāyajapi [as read; Pā. 3-1-84], though hi does not follow, śāyaj [for śnā]; the form pruṣāyat; since it stands after an ajanta, tiṅ atiṅaḥ (Pā. 8-1-28 as read), the nighāta accent. Naraḥ — root nṛ nayane; ṛdor ap (Pā. 3-3-57 as read), the suffix ap; since it is from the word bahula, this occurs in the agent sense; guṇa of the ṛ, becomes r-final; since it is pit, anudātta, so the root's accent remains. Svajām — "svasmāt jātā svajā, [accusative] tām"; root janī prādurbhāve; the suffix ḍa; since it is ḍit, elision of the ṭi of the root; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt, the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent. Cakṣata — root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci, adādi; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6 as read), laṅ in the sense of the present; third person singular, ta; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73 as read), luk for śap does not occur; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75 as read), the augment aṭ does not occur; the roots have many senses, so here it is used in the sense of seeing; since it stands after an ajanta, the nighāta accent. ‖ 2 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.3) begins at the foot of p. 547, concluded on p. 548

नक्षद्धवमरुणीः पूर्व्यं राट् तुरो विशामङ्गिरसामनु द्यून् । तक्षद्वज्रं नियुतं तस्तम्भद्द्यां चतुष्पदे नर्याय द्विपादे ॥ ३ ॥

nakṣaddhavamaruṇīḥ pūrvyaṃ rāṭ turo viśāmaṅgirasāmanu dyūn | takṣadvajraṃ niyutaṃ tastambhaddyāṃ catuṣpade naryāya dvipāde ‖ 3 ‖

original p. 548

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.3)

नक्षत् । हवम् । अरुणीः । पूर्व्यम् । राट् । तुरः । विशाम् । अङ्गिरसाम् । अनु । द्यून् । तक्षत् । वज्रम् । निऽयुतम् । तस्तम्भत् । द्याम् । चतुःऽपदे । नर्याय । द्विऽपादे ॥ ३ ॥
