॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.3)

अरुणीररुणवर्णा आरोचमाना उषसो राट् राजयन्स्प्रकाशयन्सूर्यात्मेन्द्रः पूर्व्यं पूर्वैर्ऋषिभिः प्रयुक्तं हवमिदानीमस्माभिः क्रियमाणमाह्वानं नक्षत् । नक्षतु । शृणोतु । कीदृशः । अनु द्यून् अनुदिवसं विशां मनुष्याणामङ्गिरसां मृषीणां स्तोत्रॄणां तुरो धनस्य प्रेरयिता । अपि च स इन्द्रो वज्रं स्वकीयमायुधं नियुतं हन्तव्येन सह नितरां युक्तं तक्षत् । अकरोत् । तथा द्यां द्युलोकं तस्तम्भत् । अस्तम्भयत् । यथाधो न पतति तथाकरोदित्यर्थः । किमर्थम् । नर्याय नृभ्यो हिताय चतुष्पदे गवाश्वादये द्विपादे मनुष्याय च । एतमुभयार्थमित्यर्थः ॥ नक्षत् । नक्ष गतौ । लेट्यडागमः । पूर्व्यम् । पूर्वैः कृतमिनौ च । पा. ४-४-१३३ [as read] इति यप्रत्ययः । राट् । राज दीप्तौ । आस्मात्क्विप् … तुरः । तुर त्वरणे । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । तक्षत् । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । तस्तम्भत् । स्तभि स्तम्भे । स्तम्भु [?] । अस्माण्ण्यन्ताल्लङि [?] चङि चङ्‌न्यतरस्या … [as read] चतुष्पदे । चत्वारः पादा अस्य । संख्यासुपूर्वस्येति पादशब्दस्यान्तलोपः समासान्तः । चतुर्थ्येकवचने भसंज्ञायां … पादः पदित्यद्द्वाः । द्विपादे । पूर्ववत्प्रक्रिया । अयं तु विशेषः । अयेस्मीयादित्वेन [?] पदत्वाभावे सद्भावाभावः । द्वित्रिभ्यां पाद्दन्मूर्धसु बहुव्रीहावित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥ [as read]

aruṇīraruṇavarṇā ārocamānā uṣaso rāṭ rājayansprakāśayansūryātmendraḥ pūrvyaṃ pūrvairṛṣibhiḥ prayuktaṃ havamidānīmasmābhiḥ kriyamāṇamāhvānaṃ nakṣat | nakṣatu | śṛṇotu | kīdṛśaḥ | anu dyūn anudivasaṃ viśāṃ manuṣyāṇāmaṅgirasāṃ mṛṣīṇāṃ stotrṝṇāṃ turo dhanasya prerayitā | api ca sa indro vajraṃ svakīyamāyudhaṃ niyutaṃ hantavyena saha nitarāṃ yuktaṃ takṣat | akarot | tathā dyāṃ dyulokaṃ tastambhat | astambhayat | yathādho na patati tathākarodityarthaḥ | kimartham | naryāya nṛbhyo hitāya catuṣpade gavāśvādaye dvipāde manuṣyāya ca | etamubhayārthamityarthaḥ ‖ nakṣat | nakṣa gatau | leṭyaḍāgamaḥ | pūrvyam | pūrvaiḥ kṛtaminau ca | pā. 4-4-133 [as read] iti yapratyayaḥ | rāṭ | rāja dīptau | āsmātkvip … turaḥ | tura tvaraṇe | igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ | takṣat | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge 'pītyaḍabhāvaḥ | tastambhat | stabhi stambhe | stambhu [?] | asmāṇṇyantāllaṅi [?] caṅi caṅnyatarasyā … [as read] catuṣpade | catvāraḥ pādā asya | saṃkhyāsupūrvasyeti pādaśabdasyāntalopaḥ samāsāntaḥ | caturthyekavacane bhasaṃjñāyāṃ … pādaḥ padityaddvāḥ | dvipāde | pūrvavatprakriyā | ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ | ayesmīyāditvena [?] padatvābhāve sadbhāvābhāvaḥ | dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrdhasu bahuvrīhāvityuttarapadāntodāttatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "Indra, in the form of the Sun, illuminating the aruṇīḥ — the ruddy, shining dawns — nakṣat — may he come to, hear, havam — the invocation, pūrvyam — used by the ancient ṛṣis, now being made by us. What kind of one? Anu dyūn — every day, turaḥ — impeller of wealth to the viśām — the men, the Aṅgirases, the seers who are praisers. And that Indra takṣat — fashioned his thunderbolt, his own weapon, niyutam — constantly joined to the one to be struck; and he tastambhat — held up dyām — heaven, so that it does not fall below; for whom? Naryāya — for the benefit of men, catuṣpade — quadrupeds, cows, horses and the like, dvipāde — for bipeds, men: for both." Bhāṣya's grammar tail concluded: catuṣpade, dvipāde [the pād of the word becomes pad], accent by dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrdhasu bahuvrīhau — characterized, not transcribed.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.3) (Kannada, rendered)

Aruṇīḥ — of ruddy colour (the dawns); rāṭ — Indra in the form of the Sun, who makes them shine; pūrvyam — used by the ancient ṛṣis; havam — the invocation (now being made by us); anu dyūn — every day; aṅgirasām — of the Aṅgirases; viśām — (to the men) praisers; turaḥ — the giver of wealth; nakṣat — may he hear; — and; vajram — the thunderbolt; niyutam — (being sharp) always joined to the man to be slain; takṣat — made; tathā — so; naryāya — for the happiness of men; catuṣpade — and of four-footed creatures; dvipāde — of two-footed creatures; dyām — the sky; tastambhat — held up, like a post.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.3) (Kannada, rendered)

"May Indra, who in the form of the Sun gives light to the ruddy dawns, and who gives wealth to the Aṅgirases, hear the invocation, used by the ancient ṛṣis and now made by us; he makes his thunderbolt always sharp, ready for the man to be slain; and he holds the sky steadily like a post, for the sake of men, and of two-footed and four-footed creatures."

English Translation (as printed) page marks "English Translation`"

"May he, illuminating the purple (dawn), listen to the invocation (addressed to him) of old, daily bestowing wealth upon the race of Angiras: he has sharpned [sic] his fatel [sic] shaft; he has supported the heaven for the good of men, of quadrupeds, and bipeds."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 3)

"In explaining the meaning of this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin construe the words in different ways."

Rāṭ — rājayañ prakāśayan sūryātmā indraḥ: "Indra makes the ruddy time of dawn shine, in the form of the Sun. Havaṃ nakṣat — asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇam āhvānaṃ …" continues on p. 550

original p. 550

Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued "Havaṃ nakṣat — āhvānaṃ nakṣatu śṛṇotu: 'may Indra come to the sacrifice which we perform, and hear [it]', is Sāyaṇa's meaning. And anu dyūn turaḥ — 'he who impels wealth, giving it in increasing measure every day'. Skandasvāmin: because nakṣ is a root of the sense 'going', [it means] 'he hears the invocation of the sacrificer and goes to sacrifices'. Aruṇīḥ pūrvyaṃ rājate: 'at the moment of the dawn's rising he shines in the form of the Sun'. For turaḥ he gives turvitā tvarayitā vā śatrūṇām — 'one who hurries [the destruction of] enemies, who wakes [Indra] to fight'; for anu dyūn he gives ahany ahani ('day by day'): vajraṃ anu dyūn takṣati — 'he sharpens the thunderbolt every day'; and for niyutam — śatruśarīreṣu praveṣṭāraṃ — 'one that enters [and] makes the body of the enemy quickly pierced' (Skandasvāmin's meaning)."

Naryāya — nṛbhyo hitāya: "nareṣu bhavaṃ naryam — 'for the good of men'. Yāska:

विद्मा हि ते पतयः [?] … जनिष्ठो अपो नर्यः सुजातः प्रोर्वशी तिरत दीर्घमायुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३१-१० [as read; the first pāda doubtful [?]])

vidmā hi te patayaḥ [?] … janiṣṭho apo naryaḥ sujātaḥ prorvaśī tirata dīrghamāyuḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-31-10 [as read; the first pāda doubtful [?]])

naryo manuṣyo nṛbhyo hito narasaṃmitaḥ (Ni. 5-?? [as read]) — 'in this Ṛk narya means man, or food beneficial to man, or wealth that gives much of the [things desired]; or he explains: one who is born of man (in a history-related sense)'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Nakṣat (nakṣa gatau; leṭ, tip; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu, Pā. 3-4-97; leṭo 'ṭāṭau, Pā. 3-4-94; no nighāta at the beginning of a pāda) · pūrvyam (pūrvaiḥ kṛtam; pūrvaiḥ kṛtam inayau ca, Pā. 4-4-133, suffix ya; yasyeti ca) · rāṭ (rāja dīptau; kvip ca; vraścabhrasja…, Pā. 8-2-36, ṣatva, jaś, car) · turaḥ (tura tvaraṇe; igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ, Pā. 3-1-135) · viśām (genitive plural; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ, Pā. 6-1-168) · takṣat (takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe, laṅ; no augment, Pā. 6-4-75) · tastambhat (stabhi stambhe; hetumati ca, ṇic; ṇiśrisrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ, Pā. 3-1-48; doubling by Pā. 6-1-11) · catuṣpade (saṅkhyāsupūrvasya, Pā. 5-4-140, final elision; pādaḥ pat, Pā. 6-4-130) · naryāya (nṛbhyo hitam; yat) — sūtra numbers as read.

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.4) Printed Saṃhitā "driyāṇām"; the Pada "usriyāṇām" is the clear reading.

asya | made | svaryam | dāḥ | ṛtāya | api 'vṛtam | usriyāṇām | anīkam | yat | ha | pra 'sarge | tri 'kakup | ni 'vartat | apa | druhaḥ | mānuṣasya | duraḥ | variti | vaḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.4) small type

हे इन्द्र अस्य सोमस्य पानेन मदे हर्षे सति ऋताय यज्ञार्थं स्वर्यं स्तुत्यमपीवृतं पणिभिर्गुहासु निगूढमुस्रियाणां गवामनीकं सङ्घं दाः । अङ्गिरोभ्यो दत्तवानसि । उत्तरार्धः परोक्षकृतः । यद्ध यदा खलु प्रसर्गे युद्धे त्रिककुप् त्रिषु लोकेषूच्छ्रित इन्द्रो निवर्तत् नितरां वर्तेत तदानीं स इन्द्रो द्रुहो द्रोग्धुर्मानुषस्य मनोः संबन्धिनोऽसुरस्य पणेः संबन्धिनीर्दुरो द्वाराणि गवामनिर्गमनाय पिहितान्यप वः । अपवृणोति । उद्घाटयतीत्यर्थः ॥ [grammar tail characterized only]

he indra asya somasya pānena made harṣe sati ṛtāya yajñārthaṃ svaryaṃ stutyamapīvṛtaṃ paṇibhirguhāsu nigūḍhamusriyāṇāṃ gavāmanīkaṃ saṅghaṃ dāḥ | aṅgirobhyo dattavānasi | uttarārdhaḥ parokṣakṛtaḥ | yaddha yadā khalu prasarge yuddhe trikakup triṣu lokeṣūcchrita indro nivartat nitarāṃ varteta tadānīṃ sa indro druho drogdhurmānuṣasya manoḥ saṃbandhino 'surasya paṇeḥ saṃbandhinīrduro dvārāṇi gavāmanirgamanāya pihitānyapa vaḥ | apavṛṇoti | udghāṭayatītyarthaḥ ‖ [grammar tail characterized only]

Sense (mine): "O Indra, being exhilarated (made) by drinking this soma, ṛtāya — for the sacrifice — you gave to [the Aṅgirases] the svaryam — praiseworthy — apīvṛtam — concealed by the Paṇis in caves — anīkam — host — of cows (usriyāṇām). The latter half is in the third person: yat ha — when, in the prasarga (battle), Indra, trikakut — exalted in the three worlds — turns, then he opens (apa vaḥ) the doors, closed so that the cows cannot come out, belonging to the Paṇi, the asura, the injurer, the descendant of man [mānuṣasya, or of Manu]."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.4) (Kannada, rendered)

(He) indra — O Indra; asya — of this soma (drinking); made — when [you were] pleased; svaryam — praiseworthy; apīvṛtam — hidden (by the asura called Paṇi); usriyāṇām — of cows; anīkam — the herd; ṛtāya — for the sake of sacrificial acts; dāḥ — you gave (to the Aṅgirases, making a way); yat ha — when; prasarge — in battle; trikakut — [Indra] exalted in the three worlds; nivartat — turns; tadā — then; druhaḥ — of the injurer; mānuṣasya — belonging to man (of the Paṇi); duraḥ — the doors [that bar the cows]; apa vaḥ — he opens.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.4) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra! Pleased by drinking this soma, you gave to the Aṅgirases, for their sacrificial acts, the herd of cows, which was praiseworthy and had been hidden by the asura called Paṇi; when, in battle, Indra, unrivalled in the three worlds, turns, he breaks open the doors, [barring] the cows, of the hostile asura."

English Translation (as printed)

"In the exhilaration of this Soma juice, you have restored the celebrated herd of cattle, hidden (in the cave), for the sake of sacrifice, (to the Angirasas): when, Indra, the threefold crest engages in combat, he opens the doors of the tyrannical descendants of Manu;"

original p. 554

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 4)

Ṛtāya — yajñārtham: "The word ṛta is stated among the names of water (Ni. 1-12 [as read]) and among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-17 [as read]):

स सर्धदर्थो विषुणस्य जन्तोर्नृणां शिश्नं देवा अपि गुर्वृतं नः । (ऋ. सं. ४-३१-? [as read; doubtful [?]])

sa sardhadartho viṣuṇasya jantornṛṇāṃ śiśnaṃ devā api gurvṛtaṃ naḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 4-31-? [as read; doubtful [?]])

Since satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā is explained (Ni. 4-?? [as read]), the word ṛta here means 'sacrifice'."

Usriyāṇām — gavām: "The word usriyā is read among the nine names of cows (Ni. 2-?? [as read]):

उत वां विक्षु मद्यास्वन्धो गावा आपश्च पीपयन्त देवीः । उतो नो अस्य पूर्व्यः पतिर्दन्वीतं पातं पयसा उस्रियायाः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१५३-४ [as read])

uta vāṃ vikṣu madyāsvandho gāvā āpaśca pīpayanta devīḥ | uto no asya pūrvyaḥ patirdanvītaṃ pātaṃ payasā usriyāyāḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-153-4 [as read])

usriyeti gonāma, usraviṇo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ, usreti ca (Ni. 4-?? [as read]) — in this way the word usriyā is explained as 'a word for the cow'."

Trikakup — triṣu lokeṣu ucchritaḥ: "'exalted in the three worlds' — Sāyaṇa's exposition; Skandasvāmin explains that Indra is 'foremost' (śreṣṭha) because he has prowess in a family (kula) that is of high birth, and is renowned."

Druhaḥ mānuṣasya duraḥ apa vaḥ — "Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin explain this sentence differently. Sāyaṇa: the asura Paṇi, who injures men, hid the cows in places where others could not find them; Indra found out those places, rescued the cows, and gave them to the Aṅgirases. Skandasvāmin:

द्रुहः द्रोग्धुर्मेघस्य मनुष्यजातस्य सर्वस्य । मेघो ह्युदकं निरुध्य सर्वं मनुष्यजातं द्रोग्धि । तस्य दुरः द्वाराणि उदकनिर्गमनद्वाराणि अपावृणोति ॥

druhaḥ drogdhurmeghasya manuṣyajātasya sarvasya | megho hyudakaṃ nirudhya sarvaṃ manuṣyajātaṃ drogdhi | tasya duraḥ dvārāṇi udakanirgamanadvārāṇi apāvṛṇoti ‖

— 'the cloud, [being] the injurer of all mankind, shuts up the water and so injures all men; Indra opens its duraḥ — the doors, the openings by which the water comes out'. That is: the cloud, with the intention of harming all men, held back the water and withheld the rain; Indra, destroying the injuring intent of those clouds, opens the water's doors — so that the waters may come from the clouds, in order that rain may fall — so it is described. Sāyaṇa explains the latter half of the Ṛk as in the third person (parokṣakṛta); he explains the word prasarga as 'time of battle'. Skandasvāmin:

original p. 555

continuing "prasarge — prasṛjyate yasmin sa prasargo dānakālaḥ — 'the time of giving, a time of exceeding bounty': 'at the time when the giver of the offering is ready for giving, Indra comes face to face with the giver'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Made (mada tṛptiyoge; mado 'nupasarge, Pā. 3-3-67 as read, suffix ap; locative) · svaryam (svara + ṇyat; ṛhaloṇyat, Pā. 3-1-124; tit svaritam, Pā. 6-1-185) · dāḥ (dudāñ dāne, luṅ, sip; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu, Pā. 2-4-77, luk; no augment, Pā. 6-4-75) · apīvṛtam (api + vṛñ varaṇe; kta; nipātasya ca, Pā. 6-3-136, lengthening of api) · prasarge (pra + sṛja visarge; ghañ in the locative sense; ñnityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197) · nivartat (vṛtu vartane; leṭ, tip; parasmaipada by vyatyaya) · vaḥ (vṛñ varaṇe; luṅ … mantre ghasahvara…, Pā. 2-4-80, luk for cli; guṇa; halṅyābbhyaḥ; visarga) — sūtra numbers as read. ‖ 4 ‖ The rest of the grammar of nivartat and vaḥ — leṭ, the augment aṭ, guṇa, luk of cli, nighāta — is completed on this page; no further word is treated.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.5)

हे इन्द्र तुरणे क्षिप्रकारिणे तुभ्यं भुरण्यू कृत्स्नं जगत्पोषयन्त्यौ पितरावुत्पादयन्त्यौ द्यावापृथिव्यौ यदा पयः सान्नाय्यलक्षणं हविरनीतां गोष्ठ्रं [?] नयतां … कीदृशं पयः । राधो राधकं समृद्धिकरं सुरेतः शोभनरेतस्कं कृत्स्नजगदुत्पादनसमर्थमित्यर्थः । हविषः सकाशाद्धि जगदुत्पद्यते । अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः । (मनु. ३-७६ [as read]) इति । यद्वा यदा च द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां गोष्ठ्रानीतं शुचि शुद्धं सबर्दुघायाः क्षीरस्य दोग्ध्र्याः उस्रियाया गोः पयो रेक्णः धननामैतत् । धनवदतिप्रियं । यद्वा । आतिरिक्तं प्रवृद्धं । एवंविधं हविस्तुभ्यमायजन्त । अभिमुख्येन यजमानाः प्रायच्छन् । तदानीं द्रुहो मानुषस्य द्वाराण्यपवृणोतीति पूर्वत्रा सम्बन्धः । आनीताम् । णीञ् प्राप्तणे । लङ् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । सुरेतः । सोमनस्से ... तुरणे । तुरण त्वरायाम् । कण्ड्वादिः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । आतोलोपयलोपौ । भुरण्या । भुरण धारणपोषणयोः । अयमपि कण्ड्वादिः । औणादिक उप्रत्ययः ॥ [as read]

he indra turaṇe kṣiprakāriṇe tubhyaṃ bhuraṇyū kṛtsnaṃ jagatpoṣayantyau pitarāvutpādayantyau dyāvāpṛthivyau yadā payaḥ sānnāyyalakṣaṇaṃ haviranītāṃ goṣṭhraṃ [?] nayatāṃ … kīdṛśaṃ payaḥ | rādho rādhakaṃ samṛddhikaraṃ suretaḥ śobhanaretaskaṃ kṛtsnajagadutpādanasamarthamityarthaḥ | haviṣaḥ sakāśāddhi jagadutpadyate | agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate | ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ | (manu. 3-76 [as read]) iti | yadvā yadā ca dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ goṣṭhrānītaṃ śuci śuddhaṃ sabardughāyāḥ kṣīrasya dogdhryāḥ usriyāyā goḥ payo rekṇaḥ dhananāmaitat | dhanavadatipriyaṃ | yadvā | ātiriktaṃ pravṛddhaṃ | evaṃvidhaṃ havistubhyamāyajanta | abhimukhyena yajamānāḥ prāyacchan | tadānīṃ druho mānuṣasya dvārāṇyapavṛṇotīti pūrvatrā sambandhaḥ | ānītām | ṇīñ prāptaṇe | laṅ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | suretaḥ | somanasse ... turaṇe | turaṇa tvarāyām | kaṇḍvādiḥ | kvipceti kvip | ātolopayalopau | bhuraṇyā | bhuraṇa dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ | ayamapi kaṇḍvādiḥ | auṇādika upratyayaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "O Indra — turaṇe — swift in action — when for you the two bhuraṇyū — heaven and earth, the two parents, nourishing the whole world, begetting it — brought payas — the sāṃnāyya oblation of milk — [that is] rādhaḥ — fulfilling, causing prosperity — suretaḥ — of fine seed, able to beget the whole world (for from the oblation the world arises: 'the offering cast into the fire reaches the Sun; from the Sun comes rain, from rain food, from food creatures' — Manu 3-76 as read); or when, brought by heaven and earth, [or by the sacrificers,] śuci — pure — rekṇaḥ — [the word rekṇas is a name for wealth: wealth-like, very dear]; the milk of the cow usriyā, sabardughā, the yielding of the milk: this oblation (ayajanta) the sacrificers offered to you face to face — then you open the doors of the injurer."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.5) (Kannada, rendered)

He) indra — O Indra; turaṇe — swift in action; tubhyam — to you; bhuraṇyū — [the two parents] nourishing the world (heaven and earth); yat — when; rādhaḥ — prosperity-giving; suretaḥ — [the oblation] having the seed that produces the world; payaḥ — the sāṃnāyya oblation; anītām — brought; yat — when; sabardughāyāḥ — of the milk-yielding; usriyāyāḥ — cow; śuci — pure (placed in the cows by heaven and earth); rekṇaḥ — [like wealth] very dear, abundant; payaḥ — [the oblation] in the form of milk; te — to you; ā ayajanta — [the sacrificers] offered and worshipped; (tadā — then you break the doors that bar the cows.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.5) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra, swift in action! When heaven and earth, the nourishing parents of the world, brought you the prosperity-giving oblation of the seed that produces the world (the sāṃnāyya oblation), and when the sacrificers, [the doers of rites], offered you the pure milk of the milk-yielding cow, in abundance, [then] you broke open the doors, [made] to bar the cows, of the asura called Paṇi."

original p. 558

English Translation (as printed)

"When your parents, (heaven and earth), the protectors (of the world), brought the nutritious and invigorating oblation to you who are quick in act, and when they offered you the pure and precious milk of the milch-cow."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 5)

"Skandasvāmin gives a meaning somewhat different from what Sāyaṇa has explained in this Ṛk."

Bhuraṇyū — kṛtsnaṃ jagat poṣayantyau: "The word bhuraṇyu is stated among the twenty-six names of 'swift' (Ni. 2-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೨-೯']), but Sāyaṇa explains that, though it is in the Nirukta's list, [here] they nourish the whole world."

"Heaven and earth, producers and nourishers of the whole world, make the sāṃnāyya oblation — [the oblation] which gives Indra the power, chief means for producing the world — to be produced by the cows. Milk, produced from the cows, and the oblation in the form of ghee are the means of the world's production, as is said in Manu-smṛti:

अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः ॥ (मनुस्मृति ३-७६ [as read])

agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate | ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ ‖ (manusmṛti 3-76 [as read])

(The sense is: 'the offering cast into the fire reaches the Sun; from the Sun comes rain, and from the rain, food; and from that, creatures arise'.) Such an oblation is as dear to the gods as wealth. Indra accepts the oblation offered by the sacrificers and protects them, restraining those who injure men — so Sāyaṇa explains."

"Skandasvāmin: since the word payas is explained by the Nirukta author as having many senses, it is stated among the names of night (Ni. 1-?? [as read: 'ನಿ. ೩-೯']), of water (Ni. 1-?? [as read]) and of food (Ni. 2-?? [as read]); the word retas is stated among the names of water (Ni. 1-?? [as read])."

original p. 559

भुरण्यू श्रेष्ठे पितरौ सर्वस्य पित्रृभूते द्यावापृथिव्यौ सर्वस्य धनभूतं सुरेतः पयः शोभनमुदकं त्वरणाय तुर्वित्रे वा शत्रूणां तुभ्यमायजन्ते अभिमुख्येन दत्तवन्तः । पय इत्यनेन तोयेदकत्वमुक्तं । सुरेत इत्यनेन तु तस्य शोभनत्वमुच्यते इति नास्ति पौनरुक्त्यम् ॥ [as read]

bhuraṇyū śreṣṭhe pitarau sarvasya pitrṛbhūte dyāvāpṛthivyau sarvasya dhanabhūtaṃ suretaḥ payaḥ śobhanamudakaṃ tvaraṇāya turvitre vā śatrūṇāṃ tubhyamāyajante abhimukhyena dattavantaḥ | paya ityanena toyedakatvamuktaṃ | sureta ityanena tu tasya śobhanatvamucyate iti nāsti paunaruktyam ‖ [as read]

"Heaven and earth, the swift parents who protect everything, offer to Indra, who works swiftly [or: who is eager to destroy enemies], water as an oblation — water which is [fine] seed: since by the word retas and by the word payas water is meant, and the word su (śobhana, 'fine') is used here as an adjective, a repetition is not a fault. The oblation of this kind is śuci — pure — and rekṇaḥ — wealth-like — pure; and, for the gods, [dear] as wealth. Moreover:

प्रजापतिप्रभृतयः सर्वे देवाः सबर्दुघायाः अमृतमयदोग्ध्र्याः उस्रियायाः गोः क्षीरं तुभ्यं तव पानार्थं दत्तवन्तः ।

prajāpatiprabhṛtayaḥ sarve devāḥ sabardughāyāḥ amṛtamayadogdhryāḥ usriyāyāḥ goḥ kṣīraṃ tubhyaṃ tava pānārthaṃ dattavantaḥ |

— 'Prajāpati and all the gods offer the milk of the cow, which yields nectar (sabardughā), for Indra's drinking'. And:

अथवैवमन्यथास्या ऋचो ऽर्थयोजना । तुभ्यं पय इत्यत्र पय दधि उच्यते । पितरावपि स्वेषामपत्यानां पित्रृत्वात् पालयित्रृत्वाद्वा दंपती यजमानौ दर्शपूर्णमासयोर्यद्दधि यजमानौ वेदिं प्रति नयेते तत्तवार्थाय । यच्च धनं पुरोडाशाख्यं शोभनं प्रणीताकालक्षणं संस्कारकमुदकं यस्मै तत् सुरेतः यच्च ते तुभ्यमायजन्ते । मर्यादया वत्सैर्मृज्य पयः उस्रियायाः तदेव तवार्थाय ।

athavaivamanyathāsyā ṛco 'rthayojanā | tubhyaṃ paya ityatra paya dadhi ucyate | pitarāvapi sveṣāmapatyānāṃ pitrṛtvāt pālayitrṛtvādvā daṃpatī yajamānau darśapūrṇamāsayoryaddadhi yajamānau vediṃ prati nayete tattavārthāya | yacca dhanaṃ puroḍāśākhyaṃ śobhanaṃ praṇītākālakṣaṇaṃ saṃskārakamudakaṃ yasmai tat suretaḥ yacca te tubhyamāyajante | maryādayā vatsairmṛjya payaḥ usriyāyāḥ tadeva tavārthāya |

"Or, [Skandasvāmin] explains the Ṛk in a different way: In tubhyaṃ payaḥ, the word payas means curds (dadhi); by pitarau he means the couple who, as parents of their own offspring or as their protectors, are the sacrificers; the curds that the couple bring to the altar at the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices is for you [Indra]; the wealth called purodāśa, which is fine, [and] the consecrating water called praṇītā, with that suretaḥ — they offer to you; and the milk of the cow usriyā that has been milked [after] removing the calves — all this is for you. In this way [the sacrificers] offer the curds in the fire for Indra alone; knowing the purodāśa as dear to the gods, as wealth, they offer [it] to Indra; with the vessel called praṇītā, the priests offer the sanctified water, called suretas, to Indra alone; and so, with reverence, they offer in the fire the nectar-like cow-product only to Indra — so he explains."

original p. 560

"Indra, accepting this, restrains the asuras who trouble the Śiśnas [?] and the like; and the asuras' hidden wealth, in inaccessible places, he finds and destroys them — so it is described here."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.6)

अधेदानीमयमिन्द्रः स्तुतिभिः प्रीयमाणः सन् प्र जज्ञे । प्रकर्षेण प्रादुर्बभूव । स तरणिः शत्रूणां तारकोऽस्माभिर्ममत्तु । मादयतु । स च प्र रोचि प्रकृष्टं रोचते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अस्या अस्माभिर्दृश्यमानाया उषसः समीपे वर्तमानः सूरो न सूर्य इव । जरणा जरणीयः स्तोतव्य इन्दुः सोमो धामाहवनीयलक्षणं स्थानमभिलक्ष्य स्रुवेण सिञ्चन् सिच्यमानः सन् स्वेदुहव्यैः स्वभूतसंपद्दविष्क्रियोर्येभिरस्माभिराष्ट आश्रीत आसीत् । तानस्माभिरायेत्यर्थः । जज्ञे । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । लिटि गमहनेत्युपधालोपः । मममत्तु । मदी हर्षे । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः । रोचि । रुच दीप्तौ । छान्दसो वर्तमाने लुङ् । वृत्त्यायेन चिण्भावादेशः । आष्ट । अश भोजने । कर्मणि लङ् । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । व्रश्चादिषत्वे ष्टुत्वम् । आडागमः ॥ [as read]

adhedānīmayamindraḥ stutibhiḥ prīyamāṇaḥ san pra jajñe | prakarṣeṇa prādurbabhūva | sa taraṇiḥ śatrūṇāṃ tārako 'smābhirmamattu | mādayatu | sa ca pra roci prakṛṣṭaṃ rocate | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | asyā asmābhirdṛśyamānāyā uṣasaḥ samīpe vartamānaḥ sūro na sūrya iva | jaraṇā jaraṇīyaḥ stotavya induḥ somo dhāmāhavanīyalakṣaṇaṃ sthānamabhilakṣya sruveṇa siñcan sicyamānaḥ san sveduhavyaiḥ svabhūtasaṃpaddaviṣkriyoryebhirasmābhirāṣṭa āśrīta āsīt | tānasmābhirāyetyarthaḥ | jajñe | janī prādurbhāve | liṭi gamahanetyupadhālopaḥ | mamamattu | madī harṣe | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya śluḥ | roci | ruca dīptau | chāndaso vartamāne luṅ | vṛttyāyena ciṇbhāvādeśaḥ | āṣṭa | aśa bhojane | karmaṇi laṅ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | vraścādiṣatve ṣṭutvam | āḍāgamaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative): "Now (adha) this Indra, being pleased by praises, pra jajñe — has appeared. He, taraṇiḥ — the crosser (the saviour) from enemies — may he rejoice (mamattu) with us. And pra roci — he shines forth, sūro na — like the Sun, standing near asyāḥ uṣasaḥ — this Dawn seen by us. Induḥ — the soma, to be praised, being poured by the ladle (sruva) into the dhāman — the place called the āhavanīya — svedūhavyaiḥ — with those offerings made with the sacrificer's own wealth — āṣṭa — which was eaten (consumed) by us — those [offerings] are brought by us." Bhāṣya's grammar tail of Ṛk 6 concluded: svedūhavyaiḥ — sva + idū + havya, or iṃdhī dīptau, auṇādika suffix u; siñcan — ṣica kṣaraṇe, kartṛ suffix by vyatyaya, śe muñcādīnām num; jaraṇā — jṛṣ / jṝ stutikarma, lyuṭ in the passive; supāṃ sulug, ā — characterized, not transcribed.

original p. 562

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.6) (Kannada, rendered)

Adha — now (pleased by our praises); pra jajñe — Indra appeared; jaraṇā — praiseworthy (excellent); induḥ — soma-juice; dhāma abhi — at the place of the āhavanīya fire; sruveṇa — with the ladle; siñcan — being sprinkled; svedūhavyaiḥ — [by those] who have their own and abundant oblations; yebhiḥ — by whom (by us); āṣṭa — was partaken of; tā — such; naḥ — us; taraṇiḥ — Indra, the breaker of enemies; mamattu — let him gladden; asyāḥ — of this (visible to us); uṣasaḥ — of the dawn (nearby); sūro na — like the Sun; pra roci — [he] shines specially.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.6) (Kannada, rendered)

"Now Indra, pleased by our praises, has appeared. After we, who have prepared abundant oblations, have sprinkled the excellent soma-juice with the ladle at the place of the āhavanīya fire and partaken of it, may Indra, who shines like the Sun that stands near the dawn, give us delight."

English Translation (as printed)

"Now is Indra manifested; may he, the overcomer (of his foes), grant us happiness, he, who shines brightly, like the sun of this dawn: may the excellent Soma, being sprinkled upon the place of sacrifice with a ladle, (exhilarate us), by whom, presenting the oblations we had prepared, it was imbibed."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 6)

Svedūhavyaiḥ — imāni prabhūtāni ca tāni havyāni svabhūtāni ca havyāni yeṣāṃ; yadvā iṃdhī dīptau svāyattāni indūni iddhāni havyāni yeṣāṃ; athavā svabhūtam idaṃ purovarti havyaṃ havir yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ: "'those who have these abundant and their own oblations'; or, from the root iṃdhī (to shine) — [those] whose oblations, within their own control, are kindled; or, 'those who have this oblation, present before them, as their own' — [the meaning is] sacrificers who have oblations of their own, abundant, and prepared for the sake of the gods. Skandasvāmin: svedūhavyaiḥ — [analysis] sva + indu + havya: sva means 'one's own', indu means soma — i.e. 'those who have, for the sacrifice, their own soma as the oblation'; the n-letter is dropped by the speed of the pronunciation; and 'the soma prepared for the god āyāya' — in this sense the sacrificers who have prepared soma for the gods, as the oblation, offer it in the fire. And, as [the sacrificers are] the friends of Indra, the Aṅgirases, in this Ṛk the word svedūhavya is used as a description of the sacrificers who offer with the gladness of their friends."

original p. 563

Taraṇiḥ — śatrūṇāṃ tārakaḥ: "'one who saves from the calamities caused by enemies, by destroying them'."

Asyāḥ uṣaso na sūraḥ — asmābhir dṛśyamānāyā uṣasaḥ samīpe vartamānaḥ sūrya iva: "'like the Sun that stands near the dawn which we see' — Sāyaṇa explains that Indra follows the soma, as the Sun follows the dawn visible to us. Skandasvāmin, explaining the simile in the same way: naśabdo 'tra purastād upacāro 'pi upamāsthānīyaḥ sūryasyoṣasaḥ putratvena sambandhaḥ — 'the word na here is indicated as [a particle of] comparison, in the figurative manner; and the relation of Sun and Dawn is that of a son [to a mother]': 'ruśadvatsā ruśatī śvetyāgāt' (Ṛ. 1-113-2) — this is said as a word of comparison: the Sun and Dawn have the relation of begetter and begotten; so he elaborates from the Ṛk ruśadvatsā."

Induḥ — somaḥ somalatā: "'the soma-plant'. The word indu is stated among the names of drops (Ni. 1-?? [as read]) and among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 4-?? [as read]): indur indheḥ undater vā, indheḥ dīptikarmaṇaḥ, unater klendanakarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 10-?? [as read]) — 'derived from the root iṃdhī, of the sense of brightness, or from und, of the sense of wetting; hence indu means the moon or the soma-creeper' — two meanings. Skandasvāmin:

एकवाक्यतार्थं यत्तच्छब्दावध्याहार्यौ । यः वृत्रवधादिषु यशसा शौर्येण च परिवृद्धः । यज्ञेषु प्रकर्षेण आमादयत् [?] यथा यस्या उषसः संबन्धी सूर्यः तद्वत् दीप्यते । यैरस्माभिर्देवैः सह सोमं पिबति स्तूयते च तैः स्वसखैरङ्गिरोभिः सह तृप्यतु ॥

ekavākyatārthaṃ yattacchabdāvadhyāhāryau | yaḥ vṛtravadhādiṣu yaśasā śauryeṇa ca parivṛddhaḥ | yajñeṣu prakarṣeṇa āmādayat [?] yathā yasyā uṣasaḥ saṃbandhī sūryaḥ tadvat dīpyate | yairasmābhirdevaiḥ saha somaṃ pibati stūyate ca taiḥ svasakhairaṅgirobhiḥ saha tṛpyatu ‖

— 'for the sake of a single sentence, [the words] yat and tat are to be supplied. [Indra], who has grown great in fame and valour by such deeds as the killing of Vṛtra, [who] delights exceedingly at sacrifices, shines like the Sun that belongs to the dawn; with the gods, by whom, together with the Aṅgirases, he drinks the soma and is praised, with those friends of his, may he be satisfied'."

original p. 564

"— he explains the sense: that Indra, grown by deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra, is greatly in fame and valour; he is, in the sacrifices, exceedingly delighted by the shares of oblation; he shines near the dawn like the Sun; he, being together with the gods, and being all-pervading in the gods, drinks the soma, with the gods, and is praised by those gods — thus Indra's nature, qualities and deeds are described; and, being thus, he, being satisfied and exhilarated through receiving the shares of the oblations together with his friends the Aṅgirases, should favour the sacrificers, so that they too become satisfied and exhilarated — such is the prayer described."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly)

Adha (atha, with dh for th by Vedic usage) · jajñe (janī prādurbhāve, liṭ, ta → eś; doubling; gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi, Pā. 6-4-98, elision of the penultimate; nighāta) · mamattu (madī harṣe, loṭ, tu; ślu for śap, Pā. 2-4-75 as read; doubling by ślau, Pā. 6-1-10; khari ca, c → t) · roci (ruca dīptau; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ, Pā. 3-4-6, luṅ; cleś cili → ciṇ by vyatyaya; ciṇo luk, Pā. 6-4-104; no augment) · yebhiḥ (bahulaṃ chandasi, no ais-substitution) · āṣṭa (aśa bhojane, passive laṅ, ta; luk of the vikaraṇa; vraścabhrasja…, ṣatva, ṣṭutva; augment āṭ; no nighāta by yaddhṛttānnityam, Pā. 8-1-66) — sūtra numbers as read.

original p. 565

Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded Svedūhavyaiḥ (iduḥ / iṃdhī dīptau, suffix u, the num does not arise by āgamaśāstram anityam, Pā. [vārttika]; the form idu; the compound analysed idū prabhūtāni ca tāni havyāni svabhūtāni ca havyāni yeṣāṃ te svedūhavyāḥ; by pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam) · siñcan (ṣiṣic kṣaraṇe; kartṛ suffix in the passive by vyatyaya; śatṛ; śe muñcādīnām, Pā. 7-1-59, num; accent of śap) · jaraṇā (jṝ stutyarthe, lyuṭ in the passive, yuvoranākau, Pā. 7-1-1, ana; supāṃ sulug, Pā. 7-1-39, ā; liti, Pā. 6-1-193, accent by vyatyaya on the suffix's first). ‖ 6 ‖

स्विध्मा यद्वनधितिरपस्यात्सूरो अध्वरे परि रोधना गोः । यद्ध प्रभासि कृत्व्याँ अनु द्यूननर्विशे पश्विषे तुराय ॥ ७ ॥

svidhmā yadvanadhitirapasyātsūro adhvare pari rodhanā goḥ | yaddha prabhāsi kṛtvyā~ anu dyūnanarviśe paśviṣe turāya ‖ 7 ‖

सुऽइध्मा । यत् । वनऽधितिः । अपस्यात् । सूरः । अध्वरे । परि । रोधना । गोः । यत् । ह । प्रऽभासि । कृत्व्यान् । अनु । द्यून् । अनर्विशे । पशुऽइषे । तुराय ॥ ७ ॥

su 'idhmā | yat | vana 'dhitiḥ | apasyāt | sūraḥ | adhvare | pari | rodhanā | goḥ | yat | ha | pra 'bhāsi | kṛtvyān | anu | dyūn | anarviśe | paśu 'iṣe | turāya ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.7)

यदि स्विध्मा सुदीप्ता अस्या वनधितिर्वने छेत्तव्ये वृक्षसमूहे निधातव्या शस्त्र-रूपः स्वधितिः । अपस्यात् विशसनात्मकं स्वकीयं कर्म कर्तुमिच्छेत् तदानीं सूरः प्रेरकोऽध्वर्युरध्वरे यज्ञे गोः पशोः रोधना रोधनाय यूपे नियोजनाय परि भवति । समर्थो भवति । यद्वा । स्विध्मा सूर्यकिरणैः सुदीप्ता वनधितिः वनमुदकमस्यां धीयते इति वनधितिर्मेघमाला । सा यद्यदापस्यात् अपः प्रवर्षणलक्षणं कर्म करोति तदानीं सूरः प्रेरक इन्द्रो ऽध्वरे यज्ञस्य निमित्तभूते ऽहिंसितव्ये ऽन्तरिक्षे वर्तमानः सन् गोर्वृष्ट्युदकस्य रोधना रोधनान्यावरणानि परि परितो निवारयतीति शेषः । उत्तरार्धः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे इन्द्र सूर्यात्मना वर्तमानस्त्वं कृत्व्यान् । कृत्वीति कर्मनाम । कर्मसु साधून् द्यून् दिवसानुलक्ष्य यद्ध यदा खलु प्रभासि प्रकर्षेण दीप्यसे तदानीमनर्विशे [?] अनसा शकटेनेन्धनार्थं [?] प्रविशते । यद्वा गन्तव्यं स्थलं प्रति गन्तुमशक्ताय पुरुषाय पश्विषे पशून् प्रेरयते तुराय त्वरमाणाय गोपालाय च सिद्धेऽभिमतमिति वाक्यशेषः ॥ स्विध्मा । शोभनमिध्मं दीप्तमास्यं दीप्तिर्वा यस्याः सा तथोक्ता । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । अपस्यात् । अपःशब्दात्सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । लेट्यडागमः । रोधना । रुधिर् आवरणे । ल्युट्चेति भावे ल्युट् । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । अनर्विशे । अनसा विशते प्राप्नोतीत्यनर्विट् । विशतेः क्विप् । अहरादीनां पत्यादिष्पसङ्ख्यानम् । (म. ८-२-२०-१ [as read]) इति सकारस्य रेफादेशः । यद्वा । अर्तेः कर्मणि विच् । अरं गन्तव्यं प्रति विशते प्राप्नोतीत्यर्विट् । न अर्विट् अनर्विट् । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अत एव वृत्प्त्यैनवधारणेनावग्रहः । पश्विषे । इष गतौ । अस्मादन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात् क्विप्चेति क्विप् ॥ [as read]

yadi svidhmā sudīptā asyā vanadhitirvane chettavye vṛkṣasamūhe nidhātavyā śastra-rūpaḥ svadhitiḥ | apasyāt viśasanātmakaṃ svakīyaṃ karma kartumicchet tadānīṃ sūraḥ prerako 'dhvaryuradhvare yajñe goḥ paśoḥ rodhanā rodhanāya yūpe niyojanāya pari bhavati | samartho bhavati | yadvā | svidhmā sūryakiraṇaiḥ sudīptā vanadhitiḥ vanamudakamasyāṃ dhīyate iti vanadhitirmeghamālā | sā yadyadāpasyāt apaḥ pravarṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ karma karoti tadānīṃ sūraḥ preraka indro 'dhvare yajñasya nimittabhūte 'hiṃsitavye 'ntarikṣe vartamānaḥ san gorvṛṣṭyudakasya rodhanā rodhanānyāvaraṇāni pari parito nivārayatīti śeṣaḥ | uttarārdhaḥ pratyakṣakṛtaḥ | he indra sūryātmanā vartamānastvaṃ kṛtvyān | kṛtvīti karmanāma | karmasu sādhūn dyūn divasānulakṣya yaddha yadā khalu prabhāsi prakarṣeṇa dīpyase tadānīmanarviśe [?] anasā śakaṭenendhanārthaṃ [?] praviśate | yadvā gantavyaṃ sthalaṃ prati gantumaśaktāya puruṣāya paśviṣe paśūn prerayate turāya tvaramāṇāya gopālāya ca siddhe 'bhimatamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ ‖ svidhmā | śobhanamidhmaṃ dīptamāsyaṃ dīptirvā yasyāḥ sā tathoktā | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | apasyāt | apaḥśabdātsupa ātmanaḥ kyac | leṭyaḍāgamaḥ | rodhanā | rudhir āvaraṇe | lyuṭceti bhāve lyuṭ | śeśchandasi bahulamiti śerlopaḥ | anarviśe | anasā viśate prāpnotītyanarviṭ | viśateḥ kvip | aharādīnāṃ patyādiṣpasaṅkhyānam | (ma. 8-2-20-1 [as read]) iti sakārasya rephādeśaḥ | yadvā | arteḥ karmaṇi vic | araṃ gantavyaṃ prati viśate prāpnotītyarviṭ | na arviṭ anarviṭ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | ata eva vṛtptyainavadhāraṇenāvagrahaḥ | paśviṣe | iṣa gatau | asmādantarbhāvitaṇyarthāt kvipceti kvip ‖ [as read]

Sense (editorial and tentative; two explanations): (1) "If the vanadhiti — the hatchet (svadhiti, an axe-like weapon) svidhmā — of bright edge, to be placed in the forest on the group of trees to be cut — should wish apasyāt to do its own cutting work (apas), then sūraḥ — the impelling adhvaryu, at the adhvara (sacrifice), rodhanā goḥ — for the binding of the victim — is able pari bhavati — competent to have it bound to the sacrificial post. (2) Or: svidhmā — brilliantly lit by the Sun's rays; vanadhiti — a cloud (vana is water; that in which water is stored, [a cloud]) — when it does the work of raining: then sūraḥ — Indra the impeller, remaining in mid-air for the sake of the sacrifice, to be free from harm — rodhanā goḥ — the obstructions of the rain-water — wards off all around. The second half is in the second person: O Indra, abiding in the Sun's form, yat ha — when you shine forth anu dyūn kṛtvyān — on the days fit for rites, then [success attends] anarviśe — one who enters [the forest] with a cart (for fuel); or a man unable to go to the place he must reach; paśviṣe — one who urges cattle, turāya — the hasty herdsman: their desire is fulfilled." Grammar tail of the bhāṣya concluded — svidhmā, apasyāt [kyac from apas], rodhanā [rudhir āvaraṇe, lyuṭ], anarviśe [anasā viśate, kvip; ahar-ādīnāṃ patyādiṣūpasaṅkhyānam, s → r], paśviṣe [iṣa gatau, kvip] — characterized, not transcribed.

original p. 567

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.7) (Kannada, rendered)

Svidhmā — shining brightly (edged); vanadhitiḥ — the axe, the cutter of the forest; yat — when; apasyāt — is ready to do its work; tat — then; sūraḥ — the impelling adhvaryu; adhvare — in the sacrifice; goḥ — the animal; rodhanā — for binding (to the post); pari bhavati — is capable. Or: svidhmā — brightly shining through the rays of the Sun; vanadhitiḥ — the rain-cloud; yat — when; apasyāt — rains; tat — then; sūraḥ — Indra, the impeller; antarikṣe — in mid-air; goḥ rodhanā — the obstacles of the rain-water; pari (nivārayati) — keeps away. He) indra — O Indra; kṛtvyān — fit for rites; anu dyūn — on days; yat ha — when; prabhāsi — you shine; (tadā — then; anarviśe — one who goes on a cart [to the forest] for fuel; turāya — the one who hastens; paśviṣe — one who urges cattle, the herdsman: iṣṭārtha siddhyati — his desire is fulfilled.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.7) (Kannada, rendered)

"When the bright-edged axe that cuts the forest is ready, the adhvaryu, the impeller, is able to bind the animal to the sacrificial post; [or:] when the cloud, brilliantly lit by the Sun's rays, is ready to rain, Indra, in mid-air, ward off the obstacles to the rain; O Indra, in the form of the Sun, when you shine on the days fit for rites, the man who goes into the forest with a cart for fuel, and the herdsman who hastens driving his cattle, obtain their wish."

English Translation (as printed) spelling as printed

"When the bright-edged hatchet is ready for its work, the directing prieet [sic] is able to have the victim bound in the sacrifice: when, Indra, you shine upon the days that are appropriated to sacred rites, then (success attends) upon tha [sic] man who goes with his cart (for fuel), the driver (of cattle), or the active (shepherd)"

original p. 568

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 7)

"Sāyaṇa explains the first half of this Ṛk in two ways. In the first way: at the time of the sacrifice, the adhvaryu is ready to bind the animals to the sacrificial post, with the sharp axe (svadhiti) fit for cutting the trees in the forest, a weapon prepared for the dissection of animals — this is a matter related to the sacrifice. The word svidhmā he explains as 'rays of the Sun'; vanadhiti, vanam asyāṃ dhīyate iti vanadhitiḥ meghamālā — 'vana means water; since it holds water, vanadhiti is a row of clouds':

वनधितिर्मेघमाला यदा अपस्यात् अपः प्रवर्षणलक्षणं कर्म करोति तदानीं सूरः प्रेरकः इन्द्रः अध्वरे यज्ञस्य निमित्तभूते अहिंसितव्ये अन्तरिक्षे वर्तमानः सन् गोः वृष्ट्युदकस्य रोधना रोधनान्यावरणानि परि परितो निवारयति ।

vanadhitirmeghamālā yadā apasyāt apaḥ pravarṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ karma karoti tadānīṃ sūraḥ prerakaḥ indraḥ adhvare yajñasya nimittabhūte ahiṃsitavye antarikṣe vartamānaḥ san goḥ vṛṣṭyudakasya rodhanā rodhanānyāvaraṇāni pari parito nivārayati |

— 'When the row of clouds, lit by the Sun's rays, [is ready] to rain, the impelling Indra, in mid-air, to see that the work which is the cause of the sacrifice goes properly, removes the obstructions that withhold the rain.' These are the two ways. In both, Indra's concern for the protection of the sacrifice is described. Also it is described that Indra, shining in the form of the Sun, fixes the time for rites, and protects the man who has entered the forest and cannot reach the place he goes to."

Turāyetthaṃ ramaṇāya — tvaramāṇāya: "'to one who hurries' is the meaning."

original p. 569

Svidhmā — śobhanam idhmaṃ dīptam āsyaṃ dīptir vā yasyāḥ sā: "'that which has excellent fire-wood [i.e. a bright face, or bright edge]' — 'having a face of fine lustre'."

"Skandasvāmin takes the meaning of this Ṛk together with that of the next Ṛk as one sentence. In some words his explanation differs from Sāyaṇa's:

अनर्विशे पश्विषे तुराय — ऋ गतौ । आगता विशो यस्य सो ऽनर्विट् । यस्य मित्रादयो वा मनुष्याः यस्य स्वत्वान्नरकं न गताः परिचारका वा सर्वे पशून् इच्छति स पश्विट् । देवान् वा परिचरितुं यस्वरते स तुरः ।

anarviśe paśviṣe turāya — ṛ gatau | āgatā viśo yasya so 'narviṭ | yasya mitrādayo vā manuṣyāḥ yasya svatvānnarakaṃ na gatāḥ paricārakā vā sarve paśūn icchati sa paśviṭ | devān vā paricarituṃ yasvarate sa turaḥ |

— 'the one whose subjects (viśaḥ) have come [to him]; or, friends and others, who because of his [generosity] have not gone to hell; or, who has attendants; he who desires cattle for them all; or, who hastens to serve the gods'. For those who are of sacrificial disposition, [such as] friends and others, who by their own [rites] do not go to the hells, who are attached to the service of the deities and are desirous of cattle, and are in haste to serve the gods and the like — in this way Indra is ready to carry out without hindrance the sacrifices of such sacrificers. And Sāyaṇa:

अनर्विशे — अनसा शकटेन इन्धनाद्याहरणाय अरण्यं प्रविशते । यद्वा गन्तव्यं प्रति गन्तुमशक्ताय पुरुषाय । पशूर् प्रेरयते तुराय त्वरमाणाय गोपालाय ।

anarviśe — anasā śakaṭena indhanādyāharaṇāya araṇyaṃ praviśate | yadvā gantavyaṃ prati gantumaśaktāya puruṣāya | paśūr prerayate turāya tvaramāṇāya gopālāya |

— 'for one who enters the forest with a cart to fetch fuel and the like, or, for a man not able to go to the place he must reach; and for the shepherd who hastens, driving [his] cattle — Indra fulfils the wishes of these also'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly)

Svidhmā (śobhanam idhmaṃ dīptam asyāṃ…; nañsubhyām, Pā. 6-2-172, final acute of the latter member) · apasyāt (apas + kyac, supa ātmanaḥ kyac, Pā. 3-1-8; the kyajanta gets the dhātu name, sanādyantā dhātavaḥ, Pā. 3-1-32; leṭ, tip; itaś ca lopaḥ, Pā. 3-4-97; leṭo 'ṭāṭau, Pā. 3-4-94; no nighāta by yaddhṛttānnityam, Pā. 8-1-66; final acute by kyac) — sūtra numbers as read.

Grammar of Ṛk 7, concluded (noted briefly): rodhanā (rudhir āvaraṇe, lyuṭ ca, Pā. 3-3-115; yuvoranākau, Pā. 7-1-1; neuter plural, śer lopaḥ by Pā. 6-1-70 as read) · prabhāsi (bhā dīptau, laṭ, sip; no nighāta because yat is connected) · anarviśe (anasā viśati prāpnoti iti anarviṭ; viśa praveśane, kvip ca, Pā. 3-2-76; aharādīnāṃ patyādiṣūpasaṅkhyānam, the s of anas becomes r; or ṛ gatau, vic in the passive; na arviṭ; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…, Pā. 6-2-2, the avyaya former member keeps its accent; no avagraha in the Pada because the derivation is not clear) · paśviṣe (iṣa gatau, with the causative included; kvip ca; the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent) — sūtra numbers as read. ‖ 7 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.8)

अष्टा महो दिव आदो हरी इह द्युम्नासाहमभि योधान उत्सम् । हरिं यत्ते मन्दिनं दुक्षन्वृधे गोरभसमद्रिभिर्वातापयम् ॥ ८ ॥

aṣṭā maho diva ādo harī iha dyumnāsāhamabhi yodhāna utsam | hariṃ yatte mandinaṃ dukṣanvṛdhe gorabhasamadribhirvātāpayam ‖ 8 ‖

original p. 571

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.8)

अष्टा । महः । दिवः । आदः । हरी इति । इह । द्युम्नऽसहम् । अभि । योधानः । उत्सम् । हरिम् । यत् । ते । मन्दिनम् । दुक्षन् । वृधे । गोऽरभसम् । अद्रिऽभिः । वातऽआप्यम् ॥ ८ ॥

aṣṭā | mahaḥ | divaḥ | ādaḥ | harī iti | iha | dyumna 'saham | abhi | yodhānaḥ | utsam | harim | yat | te | mandinam | dukṣan | vṛdhe | go 'rabhasam | adri 'bhiḥ | vāta 'āpyam ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.8)

हे इन्द्र महो महतो दिवो मदकरस्य सोमस्याष्टा भोक्तारौ पातारौ हरी स्वकीयावश्वाविहास्मिन्कर्मण्यादः । पीतशेषं सोमं पाययेत्यर्थः । तथा द्युम्नासाहं द्युम्नस्यास्मदीयस्य धनस्याभिभवितारमुत्सं सोतारं [?] क्षयितारं शत्रुं योधानो योधनशीलस्त्वमभि भव । यद्यदा ते तव वृधे वर्धनाय हरिं मनोहरं मन्दिनं मदकरं गोरभसं । अत्र गोशब्दः पयसि वर्तते । पयो बलं । तद्वेगवन्तं । वीर्यवन्तमित्यर्थः । वाताप्यं वातेन प्राप्तव्यम् । वाततुल्यवेगशीघ्रकारिणा त्वया पातव्यमित्यर्थः । एवंविधं सोममद्रिभिर्ग्रावभिर्दुक्षन् दुहन्ति ऋत्विजोऽभिषुण्वन्ति तदानीमाद इति पूर्वत्र संबन्धः ॥ अष्टा । अश भोजने तृच् । आगमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वादिडभावः । दुक्षन् । पदकालीनो भप्‍ [?] … [as read]

he indra maho mahato divo madakarasya somasyāṣṭā bhoktārau pātārau harī svakīyāvaśvāvihāsminkarmaṇyādaḥ | pītaśeṣaṃ somaṃ pāyayetyarthaḥ | tathā dyumnāsāhaṃ dyumnasyāsmadīyasya dhanasyābhibhavitāramutsaṃ sotāraṃ [?] kṣayitāraṃ śatruṃ yodhāno yodhanaśīlastvamabhi bhava | yadyadā te tava vṛdhe vardhanāya hariṃ manoharaṃ mandinaṃ madakaraṃ gorabhasaṃ | atra gośabdaḥ payasi vartate | payo balaṃ | tadvegavantaṃ | vīryavantamityarthaḥ | vātāpyaṃ vātena prāptavyam | vātatulyavegaśīghrakāriṇā tvayā pātavyamityarthaḥ | evaṃvidhaṃ somamadribhirgrāvabhirdukṣan duhanti ṛtvijo 'bhiṣuṇvanti tadānīmāda iti pūrvatra saṃbandhaḥ ‖ aṣṭā | aśa bhojane tṛc | āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvādiḍabhāvaḥ | dukṣan | padakālīno bhap [?] … [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Indra, ādaḥ — [please] make hari — your two own horses, the aṣṭā — the partakers, drinkers — maho divaḥ — of the great div, i.e. of the exhilarating soma — drink here (iha), in this rite, [the soma that remains after drinking]; and you, yodhānaḥ — one who delights to fight — overcome (abhi bhava) the enemy utsam — the destroyer who is dyumnāsāham — the overpowerer of our wealth. Yat — when for your increase (vṛdhe) the priests milk (dukṣan) with the stones the soma — harim — delightful, mandinam — exhilarating, gorabhasam — (go here means milk; milk is strength), possessing the vigour of milk, vātāpyam — to be reached by the wind — to be drunk by you who are as swift as the wind."

original p. 572

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.8) (Kannada, rendered)

Yat — when; te — your; vṛdhe — for increase; hariṃ — delightful; mandinam — exhilarating; gorabhasam — strengthening like milk; vātāpyam — fit to be drunk by you, swift as wind; adribhiḥ — with stones; dukṣan — the priests milk out; tadā — then; he indra — O Indra; maho divaḥ — of the great (excellent, exhilarating) [soma]; aṣṭā — drinking; hari — your two horses; iha — in this rite; ādaḥ — [make them] drink (the remaining soma); — likewise; dyumnāsāham — one who carries off our wealth; utsam — the enemy; yodhānaḥ — you, the warrior; abhi (bhava) — overpower.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.8) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra! For your increase the priests prepare, with stones, the soma-juice — delightful, exhilarating, strengthening like milk, fit to be drunk by you who are swift as wind; make your horses drink such excellent and exhilarating soma (the remaining part of your drinking); and you, the warrior, overpower our enemy who plunders our wealth."

English Translation (as printed) page head "Englih" — sic

"Send hither your horses, the quaffers of the exhilarating libation; overcome, warrior, the adversary plundering us of our treasure; when they express with stones, for the increase (of your strength), the delightful, exhilarating, invigorating (juice), to be overtaken by you who are swifter than the wind."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 8)

Hari — svakīyau aśvau: "hari indrasya (Ni. 1-?? [as read]) — because the horses of Indra's chariot are famous by the name hari, Indra, having drunk, prays that the remaining soma be given to his horses."

Dyumnāsāham — dyumnasya asmadīyasya dhanasya abhibhavitāram: "The word dyumna is stated among the twenty-eight names of wealth, magha, rekṇas and so on (Ni. 2-?? [as read]). It is described that Indra should restrain him who destroys our wealth."

Utsam — utsrāvayitāram: "The word utsa is stated among the names of a well (Ni. 3-?? [as read]): utsaḥ utsaraṇāt vā utsadanāt vā utsyandanāt vā unatter vā (Ni. 10-?? [as read]) — this word is formed either from the root sad with the sense of going, or from the root sad with the sense of 'ending (destroying)', or from the root syand with the sense of 'flowing', or from undī with the sense of 'wetting'. By this, [it is said] that Indra should destroy those who plunder our wealth."

original p. 573

Vātāpyam — vātena prāptavyaṃ vātatulyavegaśīghrakāriṇā tvayā pātavyam: "'to be drunk by you who are swift as wind' — Sāyaṇa explains that the soma prepared by the priests is for Indra's drinking. Skandasvāmin explains the meaning of this Ṛk differently:

महः महतः द्युलोकस्य अष्टा व्याप्ता हरी हरिभ्याम् उत्सं मेघं अभियोधानः द्युम्नासाहं द्युम्नमन्नं मांसमण्डादि यद्यत्त्वत्पृत्वेनाभिमतं तत्सर्वं विवाभिभवति । आदः अभक्षयः ।

mahaḥ mahataḥ dyulokasya aṣṭā vyāptā harī haribhyām utsaṃ meghaṃ abhiyodhānaḥ dyumnāsāhaṃ dyumnamannaṃ māṃsamaṇḍādi yadyattvatpṛtvenābhimataṃ tatsarvaṃ vivābhibhavati | ādaḥ abhakṣayaḥ |

— 'Indra pervades the heavenly world and mid-air; he consumes the oblations pleasing in our sacrifice — meat, cooked rice etc.; he, fighting with his horses the gathering of clouds, causes rain.' And:

गोरभसं गावः स्तुतयः आपो वा । रभस इति महन्नाम । गावो रभयोत्त्रो [?] यस्य स गोरभसः गोभिर्वा महत्कृत इत्यर्थः । वातापयं उदकरूपं अथवा वातं प्राणं तस्य आप्यायितारं प्राणकरं ।

gorabhasaṃ gāvaḥ stutayaḥ āpo vā | rabhasa iti mahannāma | gāvo rabhayottro [?] yasya sa gorabhasaḥ gobhirvā mahatkṛta ityarthaḥ | vātāpayaṃ udakarūpaṃ athavā vātaṃ prāṇaṃ tasya āpyāyitāraṃ prāṇakaraṃ |

— 'gorabhasa — go is praise or water; rabhasa is a name for great (Ni. 3-?? [as read]): the soma, which has been made great by oblations and by praises, or by the waters; vātāpya — water-formed; or, one who strengthens breath, the life: [the soma] that makes breath strong; or [the oblation] in the form of water that is beneficial to life' — so he explains."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly)

Aṣṭā (aśa bhojane; suffix tṛc; no iṭ by āgamānuśāsanam anityam; vraścabhrasja…, Pā. 8-2-36, ṣatva, ṣṭutva; dual; final acute from nit) · mahaḥ (mahataḥ, loss of t) · divaḥ (ūḍidaṃpadādi, Pā. 6-1-171, acute on the case ending) · dyumnāsāham (saha abhibhave; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, Pā. 6-1-64; suffix ṇvi; upadhāvṛddhi; lengthening of the former member by anyeṣām api dṛśyate, Pā. 6-3-137; the kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent) — sūtra numbers as read.

tvamāyasaṃ prati vartayo gordivo aśmānamupanītamṛbhvā | kutsāya yatra puruhūta vanvañchuṣṇamanantaiḥ pariyāsi vadhaiḥ ‖ 9 ‖

tvam | āyasam | prati | vartayaḥ | goḥ | divaḥ | aśmānam | upa 'nītam | ṛbhvā | kutsāya | yatra | puru 'hūta | vanvan | śuṣṇam | anantaiḥ | pari 'yāsi | vadhaiḥ ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.9)

हे इन्द्र त्वं गोर्गन्तुः शुष्णस्यासुरस्य वधार्थमायसमयोमयं वज्रं प्रति वर्तयः । अभिमुख्येन व्यसृजः । कीदृशं वज्रम् । दिवो द्युलोकादृभ्वा दीप्तेन त्वष्ट्रोपनीतमानीतमश्मानं क्षिप्रं शत्रोर्व्यापकम् । यत्र यदा हे पुरुहूत पुरुभिर्बहुभिः स्तोतृभिराहूतेन्द्र कुत्साय कुत्सनामकायर्षये शुष्णं शोषकमसुरमनन्तैर्निरवधिकैर्वधैर्हननसाधनैरायुधैर्वन्वन् हिंसन् परियासि परितो गच्छसि तदानीं तद्वधार्थं वज्रं प्रत्यवर्तय इत्यर्थः ॥ अश्मानम् । अशू व्याप्तौ । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । ऋभ्वा । जसादिषु छन्दसि वावचनमिति नाभावस्य विकल्पितत्वादभावे यणादेशः । वन्वन् । वनु याचने । अत्र हिंसार्थः । तथा च यास्कः । वनुष्यतिर्हन्तिकर्मा नवगतसंस्कारो भवति । (नि. ५-३ [as read]) इति । वध्यैः । हननङ्क्ष वध इति हन्तेः करणेऽप् । तत्संनियोगेन वधादेशश्च । सचादन्तोऽन्तोदात्तः । तस्मातो लोपे सत्वुदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण प्रत्ययस्योदात्तत्वम् ॥ [as read]

he indra tvaṃ gorgantuḥ śuṣṇasyāsurasya vadhārthamāyasamayomayaṃ vajraṃ prati vartayaḥ | abhimukhyena vyasṛjaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ vajram | divo dyulokādṛbhvā dīptena tvaṣṭropanītamānītamaśmānaṃ kṣipraṃ śatrorvyāpakam | yatra yadā he puruhūta purubhirbahubhiḥ stotṛbhirāhūtendra kutsāya kutsanāmakāyarṣaye śuṣṇaṃ śoṣakamasuramanantairniravadhikairvadhairhananasādhanairāyudhairvanvan hiṃsan pariyāsi parito gacchasi tadānīṃ tadvadhārthaṃ vajraṃ pratyavartaya ityarthaḥ ‖ aśmānam | aśū vyāptau | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | ṛbhvā | jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanamiti nābhāvasya vikalpitatvādabhāve yaṇādeśaḥ | vanvan | vanu yācane | atra hiṃsārthaḥ | tathā ca yāskaḥ | vanuṣyatirhantikarmā navagatasaṃskāro bhavati | (ni. 5-3 [as read]) iti | vadhyaiḥ | hananaṅkṣa vadha iti hanteḥ karaṇe 'p | tatsaṃniyogena vadhādeśaśca | sacādanto 'ntodāttaḥ | tasmāto lope satvudāttanivṛttisvareṇa pratyayasyodāttatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Indra, you prati vartayaḥ — hurled forth the āyasam — iron thunderbolt, to kill the asura Śuṣṇa, goḥ — the swift [goer] — the aśmānam — swift, pervading the enemy [stone-like], brought upanītam by Tvaṣṭṛ ṛbhvā — the shining, divaḥ — from heaven. Yatra — when, O puruhūta — called by many praisers — you, for Kutsa, the ṛṣi, go all around (pari yāsi) vanvan — slaying — Śuṣṇa, the withering asura, with anantaiḥ vadhaiḥ — countless weapons, instruments of killing — then, for his killing, you hurled the bolt."

original p. 576

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.9) (Kannada, rendered)

Yatra — when; puruhūta — O Indra called by many [praisers]; kutsāya — for the ṛṣi Kutsa; śuṣṇam — [against] the injuring asura; anantaiḥ — numberless; vadhaiḥ — with killing weapons; vanvan — slaying; pariyāsi — you go around; — then; tvam — you; goḥ — [of] the swift-moving (asura); divaḥ — from heaven; ṛbhvā — [by] the shining (Ṛbhu); upanītam — brought; aśmānam — swiftly (against the enemy); āyasam — made of iron (thunderbolt); prati vartayaḥ — you hurled.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.9) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra, called by many! For the ṛṣi Kutsa, when you went, with numberless weapons, against the injuring asura Śuṣṇa, you hurled upon that swiftly moving one the iron thunderbolt that Ṛbhu brought from heaven."

English Translation (as printed)

"You hurled your iron bolt upon the quick-moving (Asura), the swift destroyer of foes, that was brought (to you) by Ribhu from heaven; when you, who are worshipped by many, striking Sushna for the sake of Kutsa, encompassed him with numberless fatal (weapons)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 9)

Ṛbhvā — dīptena tvaṣṭrā: "The word ṛbhu is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19 [as read]), and Yāska, explaining the Nirukta word ṛbhu as uru bhāntīti vā (Ni. 11-?? [as read]), [shows that it means] 'one who shines much'; hence Sāyaṇa explains it as 'Tvaṣṭṛ, the shining one'; Skandasvāmin as 'Indra, the wise'."

Vanvan pariyāsi — hiṃsan parito gacchasi: "'Going around, killing Śuṣṇa — for the sake of Kutsa' is Sāyaṇa's explanation. Vanvan (from vanu yācane) kutsasyābhimataṃ prārthyamānaḥ śuṣṇaṃ nāmāsuraṃ pariyāsi — Skandasvāmin: 'the meaning of vanu is 'asking'; Indra, asked by Kutsa to fulfil his wish, killed the asura named Śuṣṇa'; and he explains the prefix pari with the sense of vadha, from the roots read among those with the sense of 'killing' (yā, vadhārtha):

यो वज्रिवः परियास्मंहो मा ... धृष्णो वेयसे वि सूरीन् । (ऋ. सं. २-३२-? [as read; read only in part [?]])

yo vajrivaḥ pariyāsmaṃho mā ... dhṛṣṇo veyase vi sūrīn | (ṛ. saṃ. 2-32-? [as read; read only in part [?]])

original p. 577

Vadhaiḥ — prahāraiḥ: "'vadha means a blow' — Sāyaṇa: vadhyaiḥ hananasādhanair āyudhaiḥ — 'with weapons, the instruments of killing'. Yāska: vanuṣyatir hantikarmā anavagatasaṃskāro bhavati (Ni. 5-3 [as read]) — he explains that the root vanu conveys the sense of killing."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar page, noted briefly)

Āyasam (ayaso vikāraḥ; aṇ in the sense of modification; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ, Pā. 7-2-117, vṛddhi; final acute) · vartayaḥ (vṛtu vartane; hetumati ca, Pā. 3-1-26, ṇic; guṇa; laṭ, second singular) · goḥ (gamḷ gatau; gamer ḍoḥ, Uṇ. sū. 2-67 as read, suffix ḍo; the form go; genitive) · divaḥ (divu; diver ḍivaḥ, suffix ḍivi; div; ūḍidaṃpadādi, Pā. 6-1-171) · aśmānam (aśū vyāptau; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante, Pā. 3-2-75, manin; ñnityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197) · upanītam (ṇīñ prāpaṇe, niṣṭhā; gatir anantaraḥ, Pā. 6-2-49) · ṛbhvā (jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam, the nā-forms optional, so yaṇ) · vanvan (vanu yācane, here in the sense of killing — so Yāska; śatṛ) — sūtra numbers as read.

original p. 578

Grammar of Ṛk 9, concluded (noted briefly): anantaiḥ (na vidyate antaḥ yeṣāṃ; nañsubhyām, Pā. 6-2-172, final acute) · pariyāsi (yā prāpaṇe, laṭ, second singular; no nighāta because yatra is connected, Pā. 8-1-30; tiṅ ca udāttavati, Pā. 8-1-71, the gati pari is wholly anudātta) · vadhaiḥ (hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ; hanaś ca vadhaḥ, Pā. 3-3-76, ap in the instrument sense with vadha substituted; ato lopaḥ; anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ, Pā. 6-1-161; instrumental plural). ‖ 9 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.10)

पुरा यत्सूरस्तमसोऽपीतेस्तमद्रिवः फलिगं हेतिमस्य । शुष्णस्य चित्परिहितं यदोजो दिवस्परि सुग्रथितं तदादः ॥ १० ॥

purā yatsūrastamaso 'pītestamadrivaḥ phaligaṃ hetimasya | śuṣṇasya citparihitaṃ yadojo divaspari sugrathitaṃ tadādaḥ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.10)

पुरा । यत् । सूरः । तमसः । अपिऽइतेः । तम् । अद्रिऽवः । फलिऽगम् । हेतिम् । अस्य । शुष्णस्य । चित् । परिऽहितम् । यत् । ओजः । दिवः । परि । सुऽग्रथितम् । तत् । आ । अदः ॥ १० ॥

purā | yat | sūraḥ | tamasaḥ | api 'iteḥ | tam | adri 'vaḥ | phali 'gam | hetim | asya | śuṣṇasya | cit | pari 'hitam | yat | ojaḥ | divaḥ | pari | su 'grathitam | tat | ā | adaḥ ‖ 10 ‖

original p. 579

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.10)

पुरा यद्यदा सूरः सूर्यस्तमसस्तमोरूपस्य शुष्णस्यासुरस्यापीतेः संग्रामान्मुक्तो भवदिति शेषः । तदानीं हे अद्रिवः आदृहृत्यनेनेत्यद्रिर्वज्रः । तद्वन्निन्द्र तं फलिगं मेघनामैतत् । मेघरूपेणावृण्वन्तं हेतिं हन्तारं शुष्णमसुरमस्य निरसितवानसि । यद्वा । अस्य शुष्णस्यासुरस्य हेतिं हननसाधनमायुधं फलिगं मेघलक्षणं प्राभाङ्क्षीरिति शेषः । तथा शुष्णस्य चित् शोषयितुरसुरस्य चेयदोज आच्छादकं बलं दिवस्परि द्योतमानस्य सूर्यस्योपरि परिहितमाच्छादितं सुग्रथितं सुष्ठु सूर्ये सक्तं तदोजस्तत्सूर्यादादः । आदद्यनः । विश्लिष्टं कृतवानसीत्यर्थः ॥ अद्रिवः । छन्दसीर इति मतुपो वत्वम् । मतुवसोरुरिति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । हेतिम् । कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति बहुलवचनाद्धन्तेः कर्तरि क्तिन् । ऊतियूतीत्यादौ निपातनाद्रूपसिद्धिरन्तोदात्तत्वं च । अस्य । असु क्षेपणे । लटः सिप् । तस्य व्यत्ययेन ह्यादेशः । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । दिवस्परि । पञ्चम्याः परावध्यर्थ इति विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वम् । आदः । दो विदारणे । लङि सिपि बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । गुणे हल्ङ्याब्भ्य इति सिलोपः ॥ [as read]

purā yadyadā sūraḥ sūryastamasastamorūpasya śuṣṇasyāsurasyāpīteḥ saṃgrāmānmukto bhavaditi śeṣaḥ | tadānīṃ he adrivaḥ ādṛhṛtyanenetyadrirvajraḥ | tadvannindra taṃ phaligaṃ meghanāmaitat | megharūpeṇāvṛṇvantaṃ hetiṃ hantāraṃ śuṣṇamasuramasya nirasitavānasi | yadvā | asya śuṣṇasyāsurasya hetiṃ hananasādhanamāyudhaṃ phaligaṃ meghalakṣaṇaṃ prābhāṅkṣīriti śeṣaḥ | tathā śuṣṇasya cit śoṣayiturasurasya ceyadoja ācchādakaṃ balaṃ divaspari dyotamānasya sūryasyopari parihitamācchāditaṃ sugrathitaṃ suṣṭhu sūrye saktaṃ tadojastatsūryādādaḥ | ādadyanaḥ | viśliṣṭaṃ kṛtavānasītyarthaḥ ‖ adrivaḥ | chandasīra iti matupo vatvam | matuvasoruriti nakārasya rutvam | hetim | kṛtyalyuṭo bahulamiti bahulavacanāddhanteḥ kartari ktin | ūtiyūtītyādau nipātanādrūpasiddhirantodāttatvaṃ ca | asya | asu kṣepaṇe | laṭaḥ sip | tasya vyatyayena hyādeśaḥ | ato heriti herluk | divaspari | pañcamyāḥ parāvadhyartha iti visarjanīyasya satvam | ādaḥ | do vidāraṇe | laṅi sipi bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | guṇe halṅyābbhya iti silopaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "Formerly, when Sūrya (the Sun) was freed from the battle with tamas — the asura Śuṣṇa, who is of the form of darkness (apīteḥ — from the battle) — then, O adrivaḥ — wielder of the adri (thunderbolt: that by which one rends) — Indra, you cleft phaligam — [a name for the cloud] — the cloud that covers, the slayer (hetim), of this Śuṣṇa. Or: you broke this Śuṣṇa's weapon, the hetiṃ, in the form of a cloud. Also śuṣṇasya cit — of the withering asura — the covering strength (ojaḥ) placed over (parihitam) the shining Sun, firmly (sugrathitam) fastened on the Sun — you ādaḥ — split from the Sun: you separated it."

original p. 580

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.10) (Kannada, rendered; p. 579 and 580)

Pura — formerly; yat — when; sūraḥ — the Sun; tamasaḥ — [freed] from darkness (from the asura of the form of darkness); apīteḥ — [freed] from battle (liberated); — then; he) adrivaḥ — O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt; tam phaligam — that covering cloud; hetim — the slayer; asya — (of Śuṣṇa) you split; (tathā — likewise; śuṣṇasya cit — of the asura Śuṣṇa; yat ojaḥ — whatever strength; divaḥ pari — over the shining Sun; parihitam — placed; sugrathitam — well fastened; tat — that strength (of the asura); ādaḥ — you cut off.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.10) (Kannada, rendered)

"When the Sun was released after a battle from the covering darkness (the asura who is of the form of darkness), you, wielder of the thunderbolt, split the cloud, [Śuṣṇa's] weapon, that stood in the way of the Sun; you broke, releasing the Sun, the strength, firmly seized, of the asura Śuṣṇa that covered him."

English Translation (as printed)

"When the sun (had emerged) from the stuggle [sic] with darkness, you broke, wielder of the thunderbolt, the cloud that had been his annoyance, and sunderred [sic] the well-fastened covering in which Sushna had enveloped him."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 10)

"In explaining this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa describes that one named Śuṣṇa was an asura and fought Indra, like Vṛtra. The word phaliga also he says is a name of the asura, as the word Śuṣṇa [is]. Besides explaining it so, he also explains the meaning of the cloud-form."

Adrivaḥ — ādṛṇāti anena iti adriḥ vajraḥ tadvān indraḥ: "'The word adri is stated among the names of cloud (Ni. 1-?? [as read]); ādṛṇāty aneneti (Ni. 4-4 [as read]): adrir ādṛṇāteḥ — 'the thunderbolt, with which [the cloud] is rent', so thunderbolt is adri; tadvān — Indra. Or: because it is the stone by which soma is pressed, adri is also the pressing stone: somābhiṣavagrāvabhir… adriḥ. Or, because of te somādaḥ: [the sentence] te somādo harī indrasya niṃśatīr aṃśum duhanto adhyāsate gavi (Ṛ. 10-94-? [as read]) — in this Ṛk, the word adri in the mantra is explained by Yāska (asmin mantre atter adrisyād iti, Ni. ?-?? [as read]): because adri is formed also from the root ad, 'to eat', adriḥ means 'one who eats' — Indra."

Sūraḥ — sūryaḥ tamasaḥ tamorūpasya śuṣṇasya apīteḥ saṅgrāmāt mukto 'bhavat: "'The Sun, the Indra who stands in the form of the Sun, covers [by] the asura Śuṣṇa in the form of darkness, [and] winning victories in the battles with Śuṣṇa, who causes affliction to the world, he shone in the form of the Sun.'"

original p. 581

Taṃ phaligaṃ hetim asya — meghānām etat; meghe rūpeṇāvṛṇvantaṃ hantāraṃ śuṣṇam asuraṃ nirasitavān asi: "'the phaliga is a name for cloud' (Ni. 1-?? [as read]); 'Śuṣṇa, when covering the Sun, took the shape of a cloud to be his helper; hence Indra destroyed the cloud which was like a weapon of Śuṣṇa'."

Śuṣṇasya — śoṣayitur asurasya: "'of the asura named Śuṣṇa, who dries up water'. The word śuṣṇa is stated among the names of cloud (Ni. 3-?? [as read]):

न्याविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दृळ्हा वि शृङ्गिणमभिनच्छुष्णमिन्द्रः । यावत्तरो मघवन्यावदोजो वज्रेण शत्रुमवधीः पृतन्युम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३३-१२ [as read])

nyāvidhyadilībiśasya dṛḷhā vi śṛṅgiṇamabhinacchuṣṇamindraḥ | yāvattaro maghavanyāvadojo vajreṇa śatrumavadhīḥ pṛtanyum ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-33-12 [as read])

In this Ṛk the word śuṣṇa means 'cloud' (Ni. 6-?? [as read]).

नि यद्वृणक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्णस्य चिद्व्रन्दिनो रोरुवद्वना । (ऋ. सं. १-५४-५ [as read])

ni yadvṛṇakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣṇasya cidvrandino roruvadvanā | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-54-5 [as read])

Śuṣṇasyādityasya śoṣayituḥ (Ni. ?-?? [as read]) — 'Yāska explains [the word as] the Sun, who dries up water'. Skandasvāmin explains the Ṛk in the same way as Sāyaṇa and tells the history connected with it:

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । वृत्रः किल सूर्यरोधनसमर्थं तमस्तुस्तान । तं हत्वेन्द्रः तमसो ऽपसनोदनार्थं सूर्यं दिवि आरोहयां चकार । तदेतदत्र सम्यगुक्तम् । त्वमपामपिधानावृणोरपाधारयः पर्वते दानुमद्वसु । वृत्रं यदिन्द्र शवसावधीरहिमादित्सूर्यं दिव्यारोहयो दृशे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५२-६ [as read])

atretihāsamācakṣate | vṛtraḥ kila sūryarodhanasamarthaṃ tamastustāna | taṃ hatvendraḥ tamaso 'pasanodanārthaṃ sūryaṃ divi ārohayāṃ cakāra | tadetadatra samyaguktam | tvamapāmapidhānāvṛṇorapādhārayaḥ parvate dānumadvasu | vṛtraṃ yadindra śavasāvadhīrahimāditsūryaṃ divyārohayo dṛśe ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-52-6 [as read])

— 'In this history: Vṛtra covered the Sun with darkness; Indra, having killed him, set the Sun in the sky to drive away the darkness.' Here, along with the darkness-bearing Vṛtra, the phaliga, too, became a helper of Śuṣṇa in [darkening the Sun]. Or, in another way [the meaning of the Ṛk is organized]: phaliga is a name for cloud; to the cloud which, stopping the water, stood [blocking] the Sun's rays, formerly [and to the darkness] you hurled the thunderbolt, and the strength, covering all around the Sun's [light], of Śuṣṇa, the withering, you …" the page ends; continues p. 582

original p. 582

Special Topics of Ṛk 10, concluded "The word ojas is stated among the names of water (Ni. 1-?? [as read]), so it conveys the sense of 'water'. [Skandasvāmin] tells a history on the subject of Indra's restraining of Vṛtra: the asura Vṛtra, able to hold back the Sun's brightness, made darkness; Indra destroyed that darkness, and, to destroy the grime that remained in the part connected with the darkness, entered the Sun's disc in the sky and shone in the form of the Sun. This matter is stated in the Ṛk vṛtraṃ yad indra (Ṛ. 1-52-6 as read). In this way, Śuṣṇa — who was making darkness and protecting it — Indra killed, and the phaliga helping him. Or: phaliga is a word for cloud, and [Sāyaṇa] says that in the form of a cloud, Śuṣṇa, covering the Sun and holding back the light, increased the darkness; Indra struck the cloud with the thunderbolt, destroyed the darkness, and made the light; and he saved the world, producing rain in the places suited [for it], by the rays connected with the Sun."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.11)

हे इन्द्र मही महत्यौ पाजसी बलवत्यावचक्रे अचङ्क्रमाणे सर्वत्र व्याप्ते वर्तमाने द्यावाक्षामा द्यावापृथिव्यौ कर्मन् वृत्रवधादिलक्षणे कर्मणि प्रवृत्तं त्वामनुमदतां । हृष्टमकुरुताम् । अनुमन्येतां वा । तथा च तैत्तिरीयकं । स आभ्यामेव प्रसूते इन्द्रो वृत्रमहन्निति । तदनन्तरं त्वमाशयानं समन्ताद्व्याप्य वर्तमानं वराहुं वराहारं वृत्रमसुरं सिरासु सरणशीलासु अप्सु महो महता वज्रेण सिष्वपः । अस्वापयः । वज्रेण हत्वा पातितवानसीत्यर्थः ॥ मही । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । पाजसी । पाजःशब्दो बलवाचको लक्षणयात्र तद्वति वर्तते । ईयोडियाजीकाराणामुपसंख्यानमिति विभक्तेरीकारादेशः । द्यावाक्षामा । द्यौश्च क्षामा च दिवो द्यावेति द्यावादेशः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेरालुक् । मदताम् । मदी हर्षे । व्यत्ययेन शप् । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । महः । महतः । करणे [?] शेषत्वेन विवक्षिते षष्ठी । अश्च्बुपोलोपश्छान्दसः । सिष्वपः । ञिष्वप् शये । अस्माण्ण्यन्ताल्लङि चङि । चङ्न्यतरस्या … सम्प्रसारणं न क्रियते ॥ [as read]

he indra mahī mahatyau pājasī balavatyāvacakre acaṅkramāṇe sarvatra vyāpte vartamāne dyāvākṣāmā dyāvāpṛthivyau karman vṛtravadhādilakṣaṇe karmaṇi pravṛttaṃ tvāmanumadatāṃ | hṛṣṭamakurutām | anumanyetāṃ vā | tathā ca taittirīyakaṃ | sa ābhyāmeva prasūte indro vṛtramahanniti | tadanantaraṃ tvamāśayānaṃ samantādvyāpya vartamānaṃ varāhuṃ varāhāraṃ vṛtramasuraṃ sirāsu saraṇaśīlāsu apsu maho mahatā vajreṇa siṣvapaḥ | asvāpayaḥ | vajreṇa hatvā pātitavānasītyarthaḥ ‖ mahī | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakteḥ pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ | pājasī | pājaḥśabdo balavācako lakṣaṇayātra tadvati vartate | īyoḍiyājīkārāṇāmupasaṃkhyānamiti vibhakterīkārādeśaḥ | dyāvākṣāmā | dyauśca kṣāmā ca divo dyāveti dyāvādeśaḥ | devatādvandve cetyubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterāluk | madatām | madī harṣe | vyatyayena śap | bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge 'pītyaḍabhāvaḥ | mahaḥ | mahataḥ | karaṇe [?] śeṣatvena vivakṣite ṣaṣṭhī | aścbupolopaśchāndasaḥ | siṣvapaḥ | ñiṣvap śaye | asmāṇṇyantāllaṅi caṅi | caṅnyatarasyā … samprasāraṇaṃ na kriyate ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Indra, mahī — the great — pājasī — strong — acakre — unmoving, pervading everywhere — dyāvākṣāmā — heaven and earth: anu madatām — gladdened [applauded] you, who were engaged in the work (karman) of killing Vṛtra and the like; or: approved [it]. As the Taittirīya says: 'by these two he was impelled; Indra slew Vṛtra' (Tai. Saṃ. 2-3-2-6 as read). Thereafter you siṣvapaḥ — laid asleep, vajreṇa mahaḥ — with the great thunderbolt, vṛtram — the asura Vṛtra, āśayānam — lying pervading everywhere, varāhum — the eater of good food, sirāsu — in the flowing waters: you cast him down, killing him with the bolt."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.11) (Kannada, rendered)

(He) indra — O Indra; mahī — great; pājasī — strong; acakre — all-pervading, unmoving; dyāvākṣāmā — heaven and earth; karman anu — [after] your work [the killing of Vṛtra]; tvā — you; madatām — made glad; anantaram — afterwards; tvam — you; āśayānam — lying pervading everywhere; varāhum — the eater of good food; vṛtram — Vṛtra, the asura; sirāsu — in the waters; mahaḥ vajreṇa — with the great thunderbolt; siṣvapaḥ — cast down (laid to sleep).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.11) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra! Heaven and earth, vast, powerful and all-pervading, were glad at your deed of killing Vṛtra. Afterwards you, with your great thunderbolt, killed the all-pervading Vṛtra, the eater of good food, and cast him into the waters."

original p. 585

English Translation (as printed)

"Then the vast, powerful, and immoveable earth and heaven animated you, Indra, to glorious deeds, and you hurled down into the waters, with your mighty thunderbolt, the everywhere-spreading and destroying Vritra."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 11)

Dyāvākṣāmā karmann anu madatām — dyāvāpṛthivyau vṛtravadhādilakṣaṇe karmaṇi pravṛttaṃ tvāṃ hṛṣṭam akurutām anumanyetāṃ vā; tathā ca taittirīyakam — sa ābhyām eva prasūte indro vṛtram ahann iti: "'Heaven and earth were pleased at your deeds, or approved' — that is, when Indra engaged in the fighting of Vṛtra, heaven and earth, from joy, approved; seeing it, Indra was pleased too. The Taittirīya Saṃhitā too says that Indra, born of heaven and earth, slew Vṛtra; this Sāyaṇa states, and Skandasvāmin says the same."

Pājasī — balavatī: "The word pājas is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [as read]); 'possessing strength'." Mahī — "mahat; the word mahī is stated among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-?? [as read])."

Sirāsu āśayānaṃ varāhuṃ vṛtraṃ vajreṇa siṣvapaḥ — saraṇaśīlāsv apsu ā samantād vyāpya vartamānaṃ varāhāraṃ vṛtrāsuraṃ vajreṇa asvāpayaḥ vajreṇa hatvā pātitavān: "'The word vṛtra is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-?? [as read]) and among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-?? [as read]): tat ko vṛtraḥ? megha iti nairuktāḥ; tvāṣṭro 'suraḥ iti aitihāsikāḥ (Ni. 2-16 [as read]) — Yāska explains the meaning of the word vṛtra: 'the Nairuktas, [the students of the meaning of the Vedas], say that Vṛtra is the cloud; the Aitihāsikas [the students of history], that he is an asura, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ'. Indra, with his mighty thunderbolt, strikes down upon the earth Vṛtra, who is all-pervading in the flowing rivers, eater of the best food." Skandasvāmin:

शेरतेऽत्र स्थानार्थः आमाशयो जलाशय इति यथा । सिरा इति नदीनाम । नदीभिः क्वेदेया आपो लक्ष्यन्ते । अन्तरिक्षे या नद्यः तदप्सु गूहितम् । वराहुं वराहाकारम् ॥

śerate 'tra sthānārthaḥ āmāśayo jalāśaya iti yathā | sirā iti nadīnāma | nadībhiḥ kvedeyā āpo lakṣyante | antarikṣe yā nadyaḥ tadapsu gūhitam | varāhuṃ varāhākāram ‖

— 'āśayāna — one who lies down, like āmāśaya, jalāśaya; sirā is a name for rivers; by rivers, waters are meant; "the waters that are the rivers in the sky": Vṛtra was hidden in those waters; varāhu — of the form of a boar' …" continues on p. 586

original p. 586

Special Topics of Ṛk 11, concluded "… the root śīṅ here indicates a place; so āśayāna [means] 'lying in' — like jalāśaya, āmāśaya. Sirā means 'rivers'; by the word nadī [Skandasvāmin means] the waters connected with rivers. He explains that the asura Vṛtra lay covered in river-waters; and he is described as having the form of a boar (varāha). The ṛṣi Hiraṇyastūpa has told this matter, and he quotes the Ṛk:

अतिष्ठन्तीनामनिवेशनानां काष्ठानां मध्ये निहितं शरीरम् । वृत्रस्य निण्यं वि चरन्त्यापो दीर्घं तम आशयदिन्द्रशत्रुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३२-१० [as read])"

atiṣṭhantīnāmaniveśanānāṃ kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye nihitaṃ śarīram | vṛtrasya niṇyaṃ vi carantyāpo dīrghaṃ tama āśayadindraśatruḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-32-10 [as read])"

Mahī (mahatī, loss of t by Vedic usage; mahī + au, supāṃ sulug, Pā. 7-1-39, pūrvasavarṇadīrgha) · pājasī (pājas conveys strength; here, by transference, 'possessing it'; with the dual au, īyoḍiyājīkārāṇām upasaṅkhyānam, ī substituted) · acakre (nañsubhyām, Pā. 6-2-172, final acute) · dyāvākṣāmā (dyauś ca kṣamā ca; divo dyāvā, Pā. 6-3-29, dyāvā substituted; devatādvandve ca, Pā. 6-2-141, both members keep their accent; supāṃ sulug) · madatām (madī harṣe, laṅ, second dual, tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtamtāmaḥ, tām by Pā. 3-4-101; by vyatyaya śap in place of śnu; no augment) · karman (locative singular, supāṃ sulug, luk) · āśayānam (śīṅ svapne; cānaś in the sense of the present; śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ, Pā. 7-4-21, guṇa, ay; the kṛdanta keeps natural accent) · mahaḥ (mahataḥ; or maha pūjāyām, kvip ca, Pā. 3-2-76; genitive [for the instrument], ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe, Pā. 2-3-50) · siṣvapaḥ (ṣiṣvapa śaye; hetumati ca, ṇic; laṅ, sip; ṇiśrisrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ, Pā. 3-1-48; by saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ no saṃprasāraṇa; doubling ślau, Pā. 6-1-10, sanvallaghuni, Pā. 7-4-93, the reduplicative a → i; ṇer aniṭi, Pā. 6-4-51; ru, visarga; nighāta). ‖ 11 ‖
