॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.12)

हे इन्द्र नर्यो नृभ्यो हितस्त्वं यान्नॄन्नेतॄनश्वानवः अवसि रक्षसि तान्नॄनश्वांस्तिष्ठ । वातस्य तुल्यान् तद्वद्वेगं गच्छतः सुयुजः शोभनं रथेन युज्यमानान् वहिष्ठान् अतिशयेन वोढॄनश्वान् ऽआतिष्ठ । आरोहेत्यर्थः । काव्यः कवेः पुत्र उशना मन्दिनं मदकरं यं वज्रं ते तुभ्यं दात् दत्तवान् तं वज्रं वृत्रहणं वृत्रस्यासुरस्य घातकं पार्यं शत्रूणां पारणे अतिक्रमणे समर्थं च ततक्ष । कृतवानसि ॥ अवः । अवतेर्लेट्यडागमः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । वहिष्ठान् । वोढृशब्दात्तृश्छन्दसीष्ठन् । तुरिष्ठेमेयःसु इति तृलोपः । पार्यम् । पार तीर कर्मसमाप्तौ । अस्माण्ण्यन्तादयो यदिति यत् । ततक्ष । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ [as read]

he indra naryo nṛbhyo hitastvaṃ yānnṝnnetṝnaśvānavaḥ avasi rakṣasi tānnṝnaśvāṃstiṣṭha | vātasya tulyān tadvadvegaṃ gacchataḥ suyujaḥ śobhanaṃ rathena yujyamānān vahiṣṭhān atiśayena voḍhṝnaśvān 'ātiṣṭha | ārohetyarthaḥ | kāvyaḥ kaveḥ putra uśanā mandinaṃ madakaraṃ yaṃ vajraṃ te tubhyaṃ dāt dattavān taṃ vajraṃ vṛtrahaṇaṃ vṛtrasyāsurasya ghātakaṃ pāryaṃ śatrūṇāṃ pāraṇe atikramaṇe samarthaṃ ca tatakṣa | kṛtavānasi ‖ avaḥ | avaterleṭyaḍāgamaḥ | itaśca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | vahiṣṭhān | voḍhṛśabdāttṛśchandasīṣṭhan | turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu iti tṛlopaḥ | pāryam | pāra tīra karmasamāptau | asmāṇṇyantādayo yaditi yat | tatakṣa | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | puruṣavyatyayaḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Indra, beneficial to men, nṝn — the leaders, the horses [or: men] whom you protect, mount (tiṣṭha) those horses, vātasya — swift as the wind, suyujaḥ — easily yoked to the chariot, vahiṣṭhān — the best bearers. Kāvya Uśanā — Uśanas, the son of Kavi — gave (dāt) you the mandinam — exhilarating (vṛtrahaṇam, slayer of Vṛtra) pāryam — able to cross over and overcome enemies — vajram, the thunderbolt, which you sharpened (tataksa)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.12) (Kannada, rendered)

He) indra — O Indra; naryaḥ — beneficial to men; tvam — you; yān nṝn — which leaders (horses); avaḥ — protect; vātasya — [swift] as the wind; suyujaḥ — easily yoked (to the chariot); vahiṣṭhān — (best) bearers of the burden; tiṣṭha — mount; kāvyaḥ — the son of Kavi; uśanā — Uśanas; mandinam — exhilarating; yam — which thunderbolt; te — to you; dāt — gave; (tam — that; vajram — thunderbolt; vṛtrahaṇam — slayer of Vṛtra; pāryam — breaker of enemies (capable); tataksa — you made.

original p. 589

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.12) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra, beneficial to men! Mount the horses swift as the wind, easily yoked [to the chariot], best bearers of burdens, whom you [yourself] protect; and make the thunderbolt — which Uśanas, the son of Kavi, gave you — the killer of Vṛtra and the breaker of enemies."

English Translation (as printed)

"Indra, friend of man, mount the horses whom you cherish, who are fleet as the wind, are easily yoked, and who bear (their burden) well; you have sharpened the foe-destroying thunderbolt, the slayer of vritra, which inspiring (weapon) Usanas, the son of Kavi, gave you."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 12)

Pāryam — śatrūṇāṃ pāraṇe atikramaṇe samarthaṃ ca: "'able to overcome and destroy enemies, or able to be superior to enemies' — Sāyaṇa; and Skandasvāmin explains pālayitāraṃ stotṝṇām — 'one who protects those who praise' [the sense of the root pṝ in pālana-pūraṇayoḥ, 'to protect' and 'to fill'], taking Indra as the protector of the praisers."

Kāvya uśanā vajraṃ dāt — kaveḥ putra uśanā vajraṃ dattavān: "'Śukra, the son of the ṛṣi Kavi (Bhṛgu), gave the thunderbolt to Indra' — so Sāyaṇa. Skandasvāmin:

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । त्वष्टा इन्द्रार्थं वज्रं चकारेति तद्धिरण्यस्तूपेनोक्तम् ।

atretihāsamācakṣate | tvaṣṭā indrārthaṃ vajraṃ cakāreti taddhiraṇyastūpenoktam |

— quoting the history, and saying that Hiraṇyastūpa has stated the story of how the thunderbolt came to Indra: 'Tvaṣṭṛ the brahmā made the thunderbolt for Indra':

अहन्नहिं पर्वते शिश्रियाणं त्वष्टास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष । वाश्रा इव धेनवः स्यन्दमाना अञ्जः समुद्रमव जग्मुरापः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३२-२ [as read])

ahannahiṃ parvate śiśriyāṇaṃ tvaṣṭāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa | vāśrā iva dhenavaḥ syandamānā añjaḥ samudramava jagmurāpaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-32-2 [as read])

— quoting this Ṛk, he says that Uśanas took [the weapon] made by Tvaṣṭṛ the brahmā and gave it to Indra: tvaṣṭṛkṛtaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ dattavān — 'he gave [it, being] fashioned by Tvaṣṭṛ'. And:

original p. 590

Special Topics of Ṛk 12, concluded "Taṃ tatakṣva — takṣatiḥ karotikarmā; loḍarthe liṭ prathamapuruṣo madhyamapuruṣasya sthāne; asmadīyaśatruvadhārthaṃ saṃskuru vajram: 'the root takṣ is used here in the sense of "doing" (making). The perfect (liṭ) in the sense of the imperative (loṭ), and the third person for the second. [The sense:] make the thunderbolt ready for the killing of our enemies' — so [Sāyaṇa] explains. The Ṛk describes that Indra should use the thunderbolt for the killing of our enemies."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 12; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Indra (āmantritasya ca, Pā. 6-1-198, nighāta) · naryaḥ (nṛbhyo hitaḥ; tasmai hitam, Pā. 5-1-5, yat; yasyeti ca; yato 'nāvaḥ, Pā. 6-1-213, initial acute) · yān + avaḥ (dīrghād aṭi samānapāde, Pā. 8-3-9, ru; ato roṭ … anunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā, Pā. 8-3-2) · avaḥ (ava rakṣaṇe, leṭ, sip; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu, Pā. 3-4-97; leṭo 'ṭāṭau, Pā. 3-4-94; ru, visarga; no nighāta because yat is connected, yaddhṛttānnityam, Pā. 8-1-66) · tiṣṭha (ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau, loṭ, second singular, hi → …; pāghrādhmāsthāmnādānadṛśyarti…, Pā. 7-3-78, tiṣṭha; ato het, Pā. 6-4-105; dyaujośasi ca, Pā. 8-?? [as read], lengthening in the Saṃhitā; no nighāta at the beginning of a pāda) · suyujaḥ (yujir yoge, kvip; kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent).

Grammar of Ṛk 12, continued, noted briefly vahiṣṭhān (vaha prāpaṇe, suffix tṛc; hoḍhaḥ, Pā. 8-2-31, ḍha; ṣṭutva, lopa; sahivahor odavarṇasya, Pā. 6-3-112, o for the root's a; ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ, Pā. 8-3-13, the former ḍh dropped; the word voḍhṛ; with the sense of exceeding, tuśchandasi, Pā. 5-3-59, iṣṭhan; turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu, Pā. 6-4-154, tṛ elided; the form vahiṣṭha; ñnityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197, initial acute) · mandinam (madi harṣe; idito num dhātoḥ, Pā. 7-1-58; ṇini in the habit-sense; accent on i) · dāt (dudāñ dāne, luṅ, tip; itaś ca lopaḥ; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu, Pā. 2-4-77, luk of sic; no augment by Pā. 6-4-75; no nighāta because yat is connected) · vṛtrahaṇam (hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ; brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip, Pā. 3-2-87, kvip; iṇ-han-…, Pā. 6-4-12 as read, no lengthening) · pāryam (pāra tīra karmasamāptau; hetumati ca, ṇic; aco yat, Pā. 3-1-97; yato 'nāvaḥ, Pā. 6-1-213) · tataksa (takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe; by vyatyaya a liṭ [first-person] ending tha in the second-person sense; tiṅanta nighāta). ‖ 12 ‖

original p. 592

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.13)

त्वं सूरो हरितो रामयो नॄन्भरच्चक्रमेतशो नायमिन्द्र । प्रास्य पारं नवतिं नाव्यानामपि कर्तमवर्तयोऽयज्यून् ॥ १३ ॥

tvaṃ sūro harito rāmayo nṝnbharaccakrametaśo nāyamindra | prāsya pāraṃ navatiṃ nāvyānāmapi kartamavartayo 'yajyūn ‖ 13 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.13)

त्वम् । सूरः । हरितः । रमयः । नॄन् । भरत् । चक्रम् । एतशः । न । अयम् । इन्द्र । प्र । अस्य । पारम् । नवतिम् । नाव्यानाम् । अपि । कर्तम् । अवर्तयः । अयज्यून् ॥ १३ ॥

tvam | sūraḥ | haritaḥ | ramayaḥ | nṝn | bharat | cakram | etaśaḥ | na | ayam | indra | pra | asya | pāram | navatim | nāvyānām | api | kartam | avartayaḥ | ayajyūn ‖ 13 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.13)

हे इन्द्र सूरः सूर्यात्मना वर्तमानस्त्वं हरितो हरिद्वर्णान्नॄन्नेतॄनश्वान् यद्वा रसहरणशीलान् रश्मीन् रमयः । उपारमयः । एतशो न । एतश इति सूर्याश्वस्याख्या । तथा च श्रूयते । एतशेनैत्वा सूर्यो देवतां गमयेत्तीति । नशब्दश्चार्थे । एतशश्च रथस्य चक्रं भरत् प्रावहत् । अपि च त्वं नाव्यानां नावा तार्याणां नदीनां नवतिं नवतिसंख्यामतीत्य वर्तमानं पारं तीरदेशं यज्ञहीनानसुरादीन् प्रास्य प्रक्षिप्य तत्र कर्तमवर्तयः । कर्तव्यमपि कृत्वा तानयजमानानवर्तयः । प्रापयः ॥ रमयः । लङ् । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति सांहितिको दीर्घः । प्रास्य । असु क्षेपणे । अस्मात्क्त्वो ल्यबादेशः । नाव्यानाम् । नौवयोधर्मेत्यादिना यत् । तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरितत्वम् ॥ [as read]

he indra sūraḥ sūryātmanā vartamānastvaṃ harito haridvarṇānnṝnnetṝnaśvān yadvā rasaharaṇaśīlān raśmīn ramayaḥ | upāramayaḥ | etaśo na | etaśa iti sūryāśvasyākhyā | tathā ca śrūyate | etaśenaitvā sūryo devatāṃ gamayettīti | naśabdaścārthe | etaśaśca rathasya cakraṃ bharat prāvahat | api ca tvaṃ nāvyānāṃ nāvā tāryāṇāṃ nadīnāṃ navatiṃ navatisaṃkhyāmatītya vartamānaṃ pāraṃ tīradeśaṃ yajñahīnānasurādīn prāsya prakṣipya tatra kartamavartayaḥ | kartavyamapi kṛtvā tānayajamānānavartayaḥ | prāpayaḥ ‖ ramayaḥ | laṅ | bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge 'pītyaḍabhāvaḥ | anyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti sāṃhitiko dīrghaḥ | prāsya | asu kṣepaṇe | asmātktvo lyabādeśaḥ | nāvyānām | nauvayodharmetyādinā yat | titsvaritamiti svaritatvam ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O Indra, you, being in the form of the Sun (sūraḥ), made harita — the yellow-hued, leading horses, or the rays that carry away the juices (rasa) — ramayaḥ — rest (stop). Etaśo na — as the Sun's horse, named Etaśa, [drags the wheel]: as is heard, 'Sūrya, bringing [by] Etaśa, makes the deity reach' — the word na is in the sense of 'and' — and Etaśa bharat — bore (drew) the wheel of the chariot. And, tvam — you — prāsya — having cast across pāram — to the further bank — of the ninety (navatim) rivers nāvyānām — to be crossed by boat — those who perform no sacrifices, the asuras and the like, — there you kartam avartayaḥ — made them turn to what is to be done: that is, you made the non-sacrificers do their duty."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.13) (Kannada, rendered)

He) indra — O Indra; sūraḥ — in the form of the Sun; tvam — you; haritaḥ — yellow-hued; nṝn — the leading horses (rays); ramayaḥ — made stop; etaśaḥ na — [like] the Sun's horse Etaśa; cakram — the wheel; bharat — bore; (api ca — and; nāvyānām — of the rivers that must be crossed by boat; navatim — the ninety; pāram — at the bank beyond; ayajyūn — the non-sacrificers (asuras); prāsya — having cast; kartam — to the duty (the sacrifices to be done by men); avartayaḥ — you made them turn.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.13) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra in the form of the Sun! You made the yellow-hued horses (rays) stand still; Etaśa, the Sun's horse, bore the chariot's wheel; and you, having cast the asuras who perform no sacrifices to the bank beyond the ninety rivers that must be crossed by boat, made them do the sacrifices and other duties to be performed by men there."

original p. 593

English Translation (as printed)

"Stop, Sura [sic], your yellow horses, for this Etasa, Indra, drags the wheel: having driven those who offer no sacrifices to the opposite bank of the ninety rivers, you compel them (to do) what is to be done."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 13)

"Here Indra's fighting, in the form of the Sun, shining in the Sun's chariot, with asuras who trouble the world, is described."

Haritaḥ nṝn ramayaḥ etaśo na bharat — haritavarṇān netṝn aśvān yadvā rasaharaṇaśīlān raśmīn upāramayaḥ; etaśa iti sūryāśvasyākhyā; tathā ca śrūyate — etaśena tvā sūryo devatāṃ gamayatu (Tai. Saṃ. 1-?-?-? [as read]) iti etaśaś ca rathasya cakraṃ prāvahat: "'He makes the yellow-hued horses stand still' — the horses, though they are yellowish, go swiftly; or, the rays that carry away the water (the juices) of the earth; Indra stays them in his chariot. The name of the Sun's horse is Etaśa. This matter is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, so Sāyaṇa explains. Skandasvāmin:

सूर्यस्य स्वभूतान् हरितः हरितवर्णानश्वान् मनुष्याभ्यः …

sūryasya svabhūtān haritaḥ haritavarṇānaśvān manuṣyābhyaḥ …

[— 'the green-hued horses that belong to the Sun…' the paragraph runs on to p. 594]

original p. 594

Special Topics of Ṛk 13, concluded "… 'for the good of men, he yokes the Sun's horses to the chariot, and Indra is in the form of the Sun' — thus he explains.

Bharat — asuraiḥ bhajyamānaṃ dhārayan rakṣan sūryarathasya cakram aśvaṃ cāsuraiḥ apahriyamāṇam: 'while fighting the asuras, [Indra] protected the wheels of the Sun's chariot that were being broken, and fixed his own chariot's horses to the Sun-chariot's horses that the asuras had carried off' — and he quotes the Ṛks:

त्वमाविथ नर्यं तुर्वशं यदुं त्वं तुर्वीतिं वय्यं शतक्रतो । त्वं रथमेतशं कृत्व्ये धने त्वं पुरो नवतिं दम्भयो नव ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५४-६ [as read])

tvamāvitha naryaṃ turvaśaṃ yaduṃ tvaṃ turvītiṃ vayyaṃ śatakrato | tvaṃ rathametaśaṃ kṛtvye dhane tvaṃ puro navatiṃ dambhayo nava ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-54-6 [as read])

अस्मा इदु त्यदनु दायि एषामेको यद्वव्ने भूरेरीशानः । प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं सौवश्व्ये सुष्विमावदिन्द्रः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-६१-१५ [as read])

asmā idu tyadanu dāyi eṣāmeko yadvavne bhūrerīśānaḥ | praitaśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ sauvaśvye suṣvimāvadindraḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-61-15 [as read])

Ayajyūn — ayajanaśīlān agādhāpagānāṃ nadīnāṃ navater garte kūpe prāvartayaḥ: 'those who by nature perform no sacrifices — Indra casts them into the deep waters, into the pits, wells, hollows of the many rivers' — so he explains."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 13; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Ramayaḥ (ramu krīḍāyām; with the causative included, hetumati ca, Pā. 3-1-26, ṇic; ata upadhāyāḥ, Pā. 7-2-116, vṛddhi; being mit, mitāṃ hrasvaḥ, Pā. 6-4-92, shortened; laṅ, sip; itaś ca lopaḥ; śap; guṇa, ay; no augment by Pā. 6-4-75; ru, visarga; nighāta) · bharat (bhṛñ bharaṇe, bhvādi; laṅ, tip; itaś ca lopaḥ; śap; guṇa; uraṇ raparaḥ, Pā. 1-1-51; no augment; no nighāta at the beginning of a pāda; root accent remains)

original p. 595

Grammar of Ṛk 13, concluded prāsya (pra + asu kṣepaṇe; ktvā → lyap by samāse 'nañpūrve ktvo lyap, Pā. 7-1-37; root accent remains) · nāvyānām (nāvā tāryam nāvyam; naudvayodharmavisamūlamūlasīta…, Pā. 4-4-91, yat in the sense 'to be crossed'; vānto yi pratyaye, Pā. 6-1-79, āv; tit svaritam, Pā. 6-1-185; genitive plural) · avartayaḥ (vṛtu vartane; hetumati ca, ṇic; puganta-laghūpadhasya ca, Pā. 7-3-86, guṇa; laṅ, sip; augment aṭ; nighāta) · ayajyūn (yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; auṇādika suffix yus; na yajyuḥ ayajyuḥ; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…, Pā. 6-2-2, the avyaya former member keeps its accent). ‖ 13 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.14)

त्वं नो अस्या इन्द्र दुर्हणायाः पाहि वज्रिवो दुरिताद्भीके । प्र नो वाजान्रथ्योऽअश्वबुध्यानिषे यन्धि श्रवसे सूनृतायै ॥ १४ ॥

tvaṃ no asyā indra durhaṇāyāḥ pāhi vajrivo duritādbhīke | pra no vājānrathyo 'aśvabudhyāniṣe yandhi śravase sūnṛtāyai ‖ 14 ‖

original p. 596

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.14)

त्वम् । नः । अस्याः । इन्द्र । दुःऽहनायाः । पाहि । वज्रिवः । दुःऽइतात् । अभीके । प्र । नः । वाजान् । रथ्यः । अश्वऽबुध्यान् । इषे । यन्धि । श्रवसे । सूनृतायै ॥ १४ ॥

tvam | naḥ | asyāḥ | indra | duḥ 'hanāyāḥ | pāhi | vajrivaḥ | duḥ 'itāt | abhīke | pra | naḥ | vājān | rathyaḥ | aśva 'budhyān | iṣe | yandhi | śravase | sūnṛtāyai ‖ 14 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.14)

हे वज्रिवो वज्रवन्निन्द्र त्वं दुर्हणायाः दुःखेन हन्तव्यायाः अस्या अवर्तमानायाः [?] दारिद्र्यात् नोऽस्मान्पाहि । रक्ष । तथा दुरितात्पापादभीके अभिप्राप्ते समीपवर्तिनि संग्रामे सत्यस्मान्पाहि । अपि च नोऽस्मभ्यं रथ्यो रथयुक्तान् अश्वबुध्यान् अश्वानां बोधकान् अश्वप्रमुखान् इमान्वाजान् धनानि प्र यन्धि । प्रयच्छ । किमर्थम् । इषे अन्नार्थं श्रवसे कीर्त्यर्थं सूनृतायै प्रियसत्यात्मिका वाक् तदर्थं च ॥ दुर्हणायाः । ईषद्दुःसुषु कृच्छ्राकृच्छ्रार्थेषु खल् । पाहि । पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । वज्रिवः । वज्रो ऽस्यास्तीति वज्री हस्तः । तद्वान् वज्रिवान् । छन्दसीर इति मतुपो वत्वम् । सम्बुद्धौ मतुवसोरुरिति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । रथ्यः । छन्दसीवनिपाविति रथशब्दान्मत्वर्थीय ईकारः । यन्धि । यम उपरमे । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । वा छन्दसीति हेर्धिः ॥ [as read]

he vajrivo vajravannindra tvaṃ durhaṇāyāḥ duḥkhena hantavyāyāḥ asyā avartamānāyāḥ [?] dāridryāt no 'smānpāhi | rakṣa | tathā duritātpāpādabhīke abhiprāpte samīpavartini saṃgrāme satyasmānpāhi | api ca no 'smabhyaṃ rathyo rathayuktān aśvabudhyān aśvānāṃ bodhakān aśvapramukhān imānvājān dhanāni pra yandhi | prayaccha | kimartham | iṣe annārthaṃ śravase kīrtyarthaṃ sūnṛtāyai priyasatyātmikā vāk tadarthaṃ ca ‖ durhaṇāyāḥ | īṣadduḥsuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal | pāhi | pādāditvānnighātābhāvaḥ | vajrivaḥ | vajro 'syāstīti vajrī hastaḥ | tadvān vajrivān | chandasīra iti matupo vatvam | sambuddhau matuvasoruriti nakārasya rutvam | rathyaḥ | chandasīvanipāviti rathaśabdānmatvarthīya īkāraḥ | yandhi | yama uparame | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | vā chandasīti herdhiḥ ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O thunderbolt-bearer (vajrivaḥ), Indra: protect (pāhi) us from this durhaṇā — hard to be destroyed [poverty], and from durita — evil — abhīke — when battle is near. And, rathyaḥ — [you] who have a chariot — bestow (pra yandhi) on us these vājān — riches, aśvabudhyān — such as awaken horses (that is, headed by horses), for iṣe — food, śravase — fame, sūnṛtāyai — pleasant, truthful speech."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.14) (Kannada, rendered)

Vajrivaḥ indra — O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt; tvam — you; durhaṇāyāḥ — hard to be got rid of; asyāḥ — this (poverty); naḥ — us; pāhi — protect; abhīke — in a battle that is near; durītāt — from evil (misfortune); pāhi — protect; — and; naḥ — to us; rathyaḥ — [you] who have a chariot; aśvabudhyān — [riches] rooted in horses, [headed by horses]; vājān — wealth; iṣe — for food; śravase — for fame; sūnṛtāyai — for pleasant, true speech; pra yandhi — grant.

original p. 597

Pratipadārtha concluded "aśvabudhyān — [rooted in horses, i.e. horse-based] … vājān — wealth; iṣe — for food; śravase — for fame; sūnṛtāyai — for pleasant, true speech; pra yandhi — grant favour."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.14) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt! Take us across the poverty that is hard to remove, and the misfortune that comes in war; and grant us riches with chariots and horses, for the sake of food, fame, and pleasant, truthful speech."

English Translation (as printed)

"Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, preserve us from this (poverty) that is so difficult to be destroyed, and from misfortune in war; grant us riches conspicuous for chariots, remarkable for horses, for the sake of food, of fame, and of truth."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 14)

Aśvabudhyān — aśvānāṃ bodhakān aśvapramukhān; sarvaṃ hi dhanam aśvamūlam dāsapravargam; aśvā budhyāḥ bodhayitavyā yena dhanena tādṛśam: "'[Riches] which wake the horses, headed by horses; all wealth has the horse as its root, [as also] the group of servants; the wealth by which horses are to be awakened (looked after) is of such a kind' — he explains that horses are the principal [part] of the wealth gained, and that servants who do work are also counted as wealth; Sāyaṇa quotes the Ṛk:

उपस्तुतिमश्व्यं पार्थिवं सुवीरं दासप्रवर्गं रयिमश्वबुध्यम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३८-? [as read; the last numeral doubtful [?]])

upastutimaśvyaṃ pārthivaṃ suvīraṃ dāsapravargaṃ rayimaśvabudhyam ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-38-? [as read; the last numeral doubtful [?]])

— the prayer is: 'O Indra, protect us from poverty that is hard to remove and destroys us, and from sinners who cause evil to happen to us, and, when war has come, protect us by them; grant us riches rich in horses, chariots and many servants'; and that we may have food, fame, and kind, truthful speech."

Vajrivaḥ — vajro 'syāsti iti vajrī hastaḥ; tadvān vajrivān: "'one who has a hand holding the thunderbolt' is the meaning." (The word vajrin is formed with matup and the Vedic v.)

original p. 598

Special Topics of Ṛk 14, concluded Śravase — kīrtyartham: "The word śravas is stated among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 [as read]); hence 'wealth' — so the meaning.

यो मे सहस्रममिमीत सवानतो राजा श्रव इच्छमानः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१२६-१ [as read])

yo me sahasramamimīta savānato rājā śrava icchamānaḥ ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-126-1 [as read])

śrava icchamānaḥ is explained (Ni. 7-11 [as read]) as praśaṃsām icchamānaḥ — so it means 'fame'. Yāska explains śrava ity annanāma (Ni. 10-3 [as read]) — so, 'food'."

Vājān — dhanāni: "'wealth'. The word vāja is stated among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 [as read]) and also read in the sense of 'battle' (Ni. 2-17 [as read]); and vāja is the name of Ṛbhu (Ni. 11-?? [as read]). Sāyaṇa here explains it as 'wealth'."

Sūnṛtāyai — priyasatyātmikā vāk tadarthaṃ ca: "'speech that is both pleasant and true' is the meaning. The word sūnṛta is stated among the names of uṣas (Ni. 1-?? [as read]) and also among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 [as read]). Here Sāyaṇa adopts the sense 'speech'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 14; grammar pages, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read)

Asyāḥ (ūḍidaṃpadādi, Pā. 6-1-171, acute on the case ending) · durhaṇāyāḥ (hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ; with dus as upapada, īṣaddussuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal, Pā. 3-3-126, khal in the passive; liti, Pā. 6-1-193; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; genitive) · pāhi (pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; loṭ, second singular, hi; adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ, Pā. 2-4-72, luk; no nighāta at the beginning of a pāda; hi is apit by hi cāpitvavidhānam, the acute) · vajrivaḥ (vajraḥ asya asti iti vajrī haste; ata iniṭhanau, Pā. 5-2-115, ini; vajrimat; chandasīraḥ, Pā. 8-2-15, v for m; vocative, matuvasoru sambuddhau, Pā. 8-3-1, ru; kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ, Pā. 8-3-15; āmantritasya ca, Pā. 8-1-19, nighāta)

Grammar of Ṛk 14, concluded durītāt (dus + iṇ gatau; niṣṭhā, kta; final acute; fifth singular; kṛdanta hind-part keeps its natural accent in the compound) · rathyaḥ (rathaḥ asya asti iti rathī; chandasīvanipau, Pā. 5-2-109, ī in the sense of matup; yaṇ in the plural; the case ending ā following, udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya, Pā. 8-2-4, svarita) · iṣe (sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ, Pā. 6-1-168) · yandhi (yama uparame; loṭ, second singular, sip; serhyapicca, Pā. 3-4-87, hi for sip; bahulaṃ chandasi, luk of the vikaraṇa; vā chandasi, Pā. 6-4-88? as read, hi not apit; since it is pit, sārvadhātukam apit does not make it ṅit, and ajiknuṃ … by anusvāra and parasavarṇa the m becomes n; nighāta) · śravase (śru śravaṇe; sarvadhātubhya asun; ñnityādir nityam, Pā. 6-1-197; dative singular). ‖ 14 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.15 — the last Ṛk of the sūkta)

मा ते अस्मत्सुमतिर्वि दसद्वाजप्रमहः समिषो वरन्त । आ नो भज मघवन्गोष्वर्यो मंहिष्ठास्ते सधमादः स्याम ॥ १५ ॥

mā te asmatsumatirvi dasadvājapramahaḥ samiṣo varanta | ā no bhaja maghavangoṣvaryo maṃhiṣṭhāste sadhamādaḥ syāma ‖ 15 ‖

original p. 600

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Ṛk 121.15)

मा । सा । ते । अस्मत् । सुऽमतिः । वि । दसत् । वाजऽप्रमहः । सम् । इषः । वरन्त । आ । नः । भज । मघऽवन् । गोषु । अर्यः । मंहिष्ठाः । ते । सधऽमादः । स्याम ॥ १५ ॥

mā | sā | te | asmat | su 'matiḥ | vi | dasat | vāja 'pramahaḥ | sam | iṣaḥ | varanta | ā | naḥ | bhaja | magha 'van | goṣu | aryaḥ | maṃhiṣṭhāḥ | te | sadha 'mādaḥ | syāma ‖ 15 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Ṛk 121.15)

हे वाजप्रमहो वाजैर्धनैः प्रमहनीयेन्द्र ते त्वदीया सा सुमतिः शोभनानुग्रहरूपा बुद्धिरस्मदस्मासु मा वि दसत् । मा विनश्यतु । तथेषोऽन्नान्यस्मान् सं वरन्त । संवृण्वन्तु । हे मघवन् धनवन्निन्द्र अर्यो धनपतिस्त्वं नोऽस्मान्गोष्वा भज । प्रापय । ते तव मंहिष्ठा अतिशयेन स्तुतिभिः प्रवर्धयितारो वयं सधमादः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः सह मादयन्तो भवेम ॥ अस्मत् । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । दसत् । दसु उपक्षये । माङ् लुङ्पुषादित्वादङ् । वाजप्रमहः । वाजैर्धनैः प्रकृष्टं महस्तेजो यस्य स तथोक्तः । पादादित्वादाष्टमिको निघाताभावः । षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रितादुदात्तत्वम् । वरन्त । वृञ् वरणे । व्यत्ययेन शप् । गोषु सावेकाचेति प्राप्तस्य विभक्त्युदात्तत्वस्य न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधः । अर्यः । अर्यः स्वामिवैश्ययोरिति निपात्यते । अर्यः स्वाम्याख्याचेत् । फि. १-१४ [as read] इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । मंहिष्ठाः । मही वृद्धौ । इदितो नुम् । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्तृच् । तुश्छन्दसीतीष्ठन् । तुरिष्ठेमेयःसुस्वितितृलोपः । सधमादः । मद तृप्तियोगे । चुरादिकः । सह मादयन्ते तृप्ताः भवन्तीति सधमादः । क्विप् च । जस् ॥ [as read]

he vājapramaho vājairdhanaiḥ pramahanīyendra te tvadīyā sā sumatiḥ śobhanānugraharūpā buddhirasmadasmāsu mā vi dasat | mā vinaśyatu | tatheṣo 'nnānyasmān saṃ varanta | saṃvṛṇvantu | he maghavan dhanavannindra aryo dhanapatistvaṃ no 'smāngoṣvā bhaja | prāpaya | te tava maṃhiṣṭhā atiśayena stutibhiḥ pravardhayitāro vayaṃ sadhamādaḥ putrapautrādibhiḥ saha mādayanto bhavema ‖ asmat | supāṃ sulugiti saptamyā luk | dasat | dasu upakṣaye | māṅ luṅpuṣāditvādaṅ | vājapramahaḥ | vājairdhanaiḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ mahastejo yasya sa tathoktaḥ | pādāditvādāṣṭamiko nighātābhāvaḥ | ṣāṣṭhikamāmantritādudāttatvam | varanta | vṛñ varaṇe | vyatyayena śap | goṣu sāvekāceti prāptasya vibhaktyudāttatvasya na gośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaḥ | aryaḥ | aryaḥ svāmivaiśyayoriti nipātyate | aryaḥ svāmyākhyācet | phi. 1-14 [as read] ityantodāttatvam | maṃhiṣṭhāḥ | mahī vṛddhau | idito num | antarbhāvitaṇyarthāttṛc | tuśchandasītīṣṭhan | turiṣṭhemeyaḥsusvititṛlopaḥ | sadhamādaḥ | mada tṛptiyoge | curādikaḥ | saha mādayante tṛptāḥ bhavantīti sadhamādaḥ | kvip ca | jas ‖ [as read]

Sense (mine): "O vājapramahaḥ — O Indra, to be honoured with riches (vāja): may that sumati — your good, favourable thought — never vi dasat — fail, be lost, from us. May iṣaḥ — food [and the like] — sam varanta — come to us together. O maghavan — wealthy Indra, aryaḥ — lord of wealth — ā bhaja — bring us to [goṣu] — [the possession of] cows. Maṃhiṣṭhāḥ — we who most exceedingly magnify you by praise, sadhamādaḥ — may we be happy, together with sons, grandsons and the like."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 121.15) (Kannada, rendered)

(He) vājapramahaḥ — O Indra, famous for wealth; te — your; sā sumatiḥ — that gracious thought; asmat — in us; mā vi dasat — may it not decay (not be lost); iṣaḥ — food; saṃ varanta — may it come to us (make us prosperous); (he) maghavan — O lord of wealth; aryaḥ — [you], the master of wealth; naḥ — us; goṣu — in cows (to give cows); ā bhaja — favour us; te — you; maṃhiṣṭhāḥ — we who magnify you with praises; sadhamādaḥ — happy together with sons, grandsons and others; syāma — may we be.

original p. 601

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 121.15) (Kannada, rendered)

"O Indra, famous for wealth (lordship)! May your favour towards us be complete; O Indra, lord of wealth, grant us, who magnify you by praises, food, cows, and the happiness [that comes] with sons, grandsons and the like."

English Translation (as printed)

"Famous for affluence, Indra, never may your favour be withdrawn from us; may food ever sustain us; opulent Maghavan, make us possessors of cattle, and may we, most assiduous in your adoration, be happy, together (with our families)."

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu, Ṛk 15)

Vājapramahaḥ — vājair dhanaiḥ pramahanīya indra: "'one to be exceedingly honoured with riches' — Sāyaṇa; the word vāja conveys wealth. Skandasvāmin: vājaṃ balaṃ prakarṣeṇa mahayasya saḥ vājapramahāḥ — 'one who is honoured by exceeding strength'. The prayer is that this favourable thought of Indra be in us; that Indra, lord of wealth, grant us cows; that our understanding may be such that we praise Indra with exceeding praise; and that we may be happy together with sons, grandsons and the rest."

Aryaḥ — dhanapatiḥ: "The word arya is stated among the names of the Lord (Ni. 3-?? [as read]). Sāyaṇa explains 'master of wealth'. Skandasvāmin says in his commentary:

गोषु इति सप्तमीनिर्देशात् स्थिता इति वाक्यशेषः । अर्यः स्वाम्यर्थे वा । अथवा अर्यशब्दो ऽत्र षष्ठ्यन्तः । अरेः स्वभूतासु गोषु स्थितान् । शत्रोः या गावः ताः अस्मभ्यं दत्त्वा अस्मान् भजेत्यर्थः ॥

goṣu iti saptamīnirdeśāt sthitā iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | aryaḥ svāmyarthe vā | athavā aryaśabdo 'tra ṣaṣṭhyantaḥ | areḥ svabhūtāsu goṣu sthitān | śatroḥ yā gāvaḥ tāḥ asmabhyaṃ dattvā asmān bhajetyarthaḥ ‖

— 'because of the locative goṣu, the sentence is completed by "standing"; arya is in the sense of master; or the word arya here is in the genitive: "those standing in the cows that are the enemy's: whatever cows belong to the enemy, give those to us and favour us". Because goṣu is in the locative, [the meaning is that] Indra, being master over cows, should protect us; he prays that, giving us the cows of the enemy, [Indra] protect us."

original p. 602

Special Topics concluded "Sadhamādaḥ syāma — te tubhyaṃ saha ca mādayitāraḥ saha somasya pātāraḥ nityaṃ bhavema ity āśāsmahe: 'we pray that we may always be those who, together with you, delight, and together drink soma, offering Indra the soma-juice that gives delight, and that you favour us so that we may stay drinking the soma with you' — so he explains."

Verse of benediction (Sanskrit, as printed at the close of the Adhyāya):

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥

vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃścaturo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖

Sense: "May Vidyātīrtha Maheśvara, dispelling the darkness of the heart by the illumination of the meaning of the Veda, grant the four human ends (puruṣārtha)."

Colophon (Sanskrit, as printed):

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरन्धरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये प्रथमाष्टके अष्टमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ ॐ तत्सत् ॥

iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhurandhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye prathamāṣṭake aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖ oṃ tatsat ‖

Sense: "Thus, in the Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa, the commentary on the Ṛk-saṃhitā composed by Sāyaṇācārya, the bearer of the burden of the empire of the illustrious King Vīra Bukka, the promoter of the Vedic path — in the first Aṣṭaka, the Eighth Adhyāya is concluded. Om tat sat."

Kannada closing lines (as printed): "illige śrī sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitavū karnāṭakabhāṣānuvādayutavū āda ṛgvēdasaṃhiteya prathamāṣṭakadalli eṇṭaneya adhyāyavu samāptavādudu." — "Here, in the first Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and the Kannada translation, the eighth Adhyāya has come to its end."

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥

yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖

Sense: "Whatever is faulty in letter or word, or lacking in measure — may all that be forgiven, O God, Lord of Speech; salutation to you."

Then, as printed: "śubhaṃ bhūyāt" — "May it be auspicious." "maṅgalam" — "Auspiciousness."

12. The first sentence of this bhāṣya, begun on p. 232, was: "Here this story. The ṛṣi named Cyavana, whose limbs were aged, full of wrinkles and grey hair, deserted by his sons and others, praised the Aśvins; being praised, they removed the old age of that ṛṣi and made him young again. This is what is said: O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, from the aged Cyavana — the ṛṣi called Cyavana — the vavri, the dark covering of the body, [that is] the old age, you pra amuñcatam, released completely. An illustration: as one wearing a mail-coat covering the whole body, then discards it; and O Dasras — the two beautiful ones named Dasra — you prātiratam, increased, the āyuḥ, life, of the ṛṣi deserted by sons and others; and immediately you made him, now young,... husband of maidens."
